summary: Claude Code sessions that run on Anthropic-managed VMs (Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise premium / Chat + Claude Code seats) rather than on the developer's machine. The VM clones the GitHub repository, works on a branch, and can open pull requests; a GitHub proxy carries git traffic on a scoped credential so the user's GitHub token never enters the sandbox, and MCP connector traffic goes through Anthropic's servers. Sessions persist after the browser closes, can be driven from the mobile app, Slack (Claude Tag) or the CLI, and are reclaimed after inactivity. Organisations that need execution on their own network run self-hosted environments; inference still goes to api.anthropic.com with a session-scoped OAuth token.

Admin control is server-side only: device managed-settings files and MDM policies do not reach cloud sessions, so policy comes from server-managed settings (claude.ai Admin Settings > Claude Code > Managed settings), organisation-shared cloud environments (network access level, environment variables, setup script), the Claude Code admin toggles (Cloud sessions — the allow_remote_sessions policy — Quick setup, Remote Control) and the Scheduled tasks toggle under Capabilities. Prompts, code and outputs follow the account's retention policy; ZDR organisations cannot use cloud sessions at all, and the Compliance API does not return Claude Code web transcripts.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Pro, Max and Team; Enterprise with premium or Chat + Claude Code seats (scheduled tasks and Code Review are research previews; self-hosted environments are a public beta). Not available through Console API keys, Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry or ZDR organisations. Repositories must be on GitHub (GHES supported on Team/Enterprise); non-GitHub repos can be sent as a bundle but cannot push back.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Anthropic API from Anthropic-managed infrastructure (so organisation IP allowlists block it unless Anthropic-hosted services are exempted); self-hosted environments call the API from your network with a session-scoped OAuth token and cannot route through a cloud provider or gateway.

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: The repository is cloned into an isolated VM; all outbound traffic passes a security proxy for audit logging; GitHub credentials stay outside the sandbox; with network access "No access" the VM can still reach the Anthropic API, which the docs note may allow data to exit.

facts.label: Retention & training
facts.value: Same commercial policy as local Claude Code (no training on Team/Enterprise/API, 30-day retention); session event data is deleted when a user deletes the session; ZDR organisations have cloud sessions disabled at the backend.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: code.claude.com/docs (Claude Code on the web, Cloud environments, Self-hosted environments)

riskNotes.note: Through the Claude GitHub App a cloud session reaches public repositories and private ones the App is installed on; through /web-setup (Quick setup) it reaches every repository the member's gh token can; restrict at GitHub. Shared environments' variables are readable by every member's sessions, so secrets must not go there; keys belong in network secrets, which the agent proxy attaches outside the sandbox on every plan.

Auto-fix replies to PR comments and pushes fixes under the user's GitHub account and can trigger comment-driven automation such as Atlantis; the GitHub proxy rejects branch deletions and tag pushes but doesn't limit which branches a push updates, so protected branches need GitHub rulesets.

Sessions started from Slack read the whole thread as context; the earlier Claude Code in Slack docs warn Claude may follow directions from other messages. Network egress in Anthropic-hosted environments defaults to Trusted (package registries and GitHub), which bounds exfiltration.
Any member with a seat can start cloud sessions once "Cloud sessions" is on; scheduled tasks run unattended. Admin toggles and organisation-default environments are the inventory levers.

controls.mechanism: Owner toggles at claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-code (Cloud sessions — the allow_remote_sessions policy — Quick setup, Remote Control), Scheduled tasks (Was Routines) under Organization settings > Capabilities > Remote sessions, Allow self-hosted environments on the Cloud environments page, the GitHub connector at Admin settings > Connectors, and the Cloud sessions and Scheduled tasks capabilities in Enterprise custom roles; who or what may trigger a session is not an admin policy

steps.title: Decide whether cloud sessions exist
body: An Owner turns cloud sessions on or off for the organisation with the allow_remote_sessions policy (the Cloud sessions toggle) at claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-code, and leaves Quick setup off so members can't hand a personal gh token to cloud sessions with /web-setup.

steps.title: Grant cloud sessions by role
body: On Enterprise, grant the Cloud sessions capability (under Claude Code on a role's Capabilities tab, Organization settings > Roles) only to the groups that should run them; roles that already granted Claude Code have it on until you turn it off.

steps.title: Keep unattended runs owned
body: Turn the Scheduled tasks (Was Routines) toggle off at Organization settings > Capabilities > Remote sessions unless someone owns scheduled, API and GitHub-triggered runs (on Enterprise, grant the role capability instead); turning it off stops existing tasks and blocks new ones.

steps.title: Keep self-hosted execution off until owned
body: Leave Allow self-hosted environments off on the Cloud environments admin page until a team owns the runners.

controls.note: Partial on the rule: enablement is per role only on Enterprise (Team plans have only the organisation-wide Cloud sessions and Scheduled tasks toggles), and trigger policy is not an admin setting: a scheduled task's GitHub trigger fires on pull-request and release events in any repository where the Claude GitHub App is installed, narrowed only by filters its owner sets (such as Author); auto-fix acts on any reviewer comment or CI failure on a watched PR; an API trigger admits whoever holds the task's token. The widening switches are admin-controlled and off by default on Team and Enterprise: Quick setup, Remote Control, self-hosted environments and the GitHub connector itself.

original.mechanism: claude.ai organisation login with SSO/SCIM; per-role Claude Code capability on Enterprise; Owner-only admin toggles at claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-code

steps.title: Gate cloud sessions by seat and role
body: Assign Claude Code seats and, on Enterprise, grant the Claude Code capability to custom roles under Organization settings > Roles; sessions always use the subscription login (API keys cannot start them).

steps.title: Decide whether the web surface exists
body: Owners turn "Code in the web", the allow_remote_sessions policy, Remote Control and Quick web setup on or off at claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-code.

controls.mechanism: Owner-managed organisation-shared and self-hosted environments on the Cloud environments admin page; scheduled tasks kept per user at claude.ai/code/routines; Compliance API Activity Feed events for cloud sessions, session shares and managed-settings changes; the Scheduled tasks toggle and role capability as the only enforcement

steps.title: Centralise environments
body: Create organisation-shared environments on the Cloud environments admin page and set the organisation default at claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-code, so sessions run in an Owner-managed list.

steps.title: Reconcile sessions from the Activity Feed
body: Query the Compliance API Activity Feed for ccr_session_created, session_share_created and claude_code_managed_settings activities to see who runs cloud sessions and what changed.

controls.note: Partial: environments have an Owner and a list, but scheduled tasks belong to individual accounts and aren't shared (no admin listing is documented), members' personal environments are approved by no one, and nothing denies an unregistered task or environment short of the Scheduled tasks and Cloud sessions switches. Sessions and GitHub App installations have no owner or approval record beyond who created them.

original.mechanism: Session list at claude.ai/code with Team visibility on Team/Enterprise; organisation-shared and self-hosted environments managed by Owners on the Cloud environments admin page; Routines listed per user

steps.title: Centralise environments
body: Owners create organisation-shared environments and set the organisation default on the Cloud environments page; Admins cannot open it. Members' own environments are personal to their account.

original.note: There is no approval workflow or owner record for sessions or routines beyond the user who created them.

controls.mechanism: Server-managed permissions.deny / ask / allow with allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly and disableAutoMode (Bypass isn't offered in cloud sessions); allowedMcpServers / deniedMcpServers and connector tool controls filter delivered connectors; the GitHub proxy blocks branch deletions and tag pushes and limits API calls to attached repositories; network access is set per environment

steps.title: Deliver the permission policy from the console
body: Under Admin Settings > Claude Code > Managed settings, deliver permissions.deny rules, disableBypassPermissionsMode and allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly true; device MDM files don't reach Anthropic-hosted sessions.

steps.title: Remove Auto from the mode picker
body: Set permissions.disableAutoMode "disable" in server-managed settings; cloud sessions then offer only Accept edits and Plan.

steps.title: Filter the connectors a session receives
body: Deliver allowedMcpServers and deniedMcpServers through server-managed settings (the session's proxy rewrites connector URLs, so match accordingly) and set unneeded connector tools to blocked.

steps.title: Standardise the environment
body: Give sessions an Owner-managed shared environment with Custom network access and make it the organisation default.

controls.note: Partial: tool rules are admin-locked (Bypass isn't offered, Auto is removable), but the rest of the locked environment isn't: members can create personal environments with Full network access and pick them, and the docs say there is no organisation-level allowlist admins can push. The GitHub proxy limits API calls to attached repositories and rejects branch deletions and tag pushes, but doesn't limit which branches a push updates (that is GitHub branch protection), and nothing documents that the session's GitHub grant can't merge, approve or mark a PR ready; with Quick setup on, /web-setup reaches every repository a member's gh token can; scheduled tasks run with no permission-mode picker; a single-repository session loads the repository's hooks and .mcp.json servers without asking unless managed settings say otherwise.

original.mechanism: Server-managed settings (permissions.allow/ask/deny, allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly, disableAutoMode) apply to cloud sessions; permission mode is chosen per session from the web UI; connectors filtered by allowedMcpServers / deniedMcpServers

steps.title: Deliver the same permission policy as the desktop fleet
body: Configure permissions.deny, disableBypassPermissionsMode and allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly under Admin Settings > Claude Code > Managed settings; endpoint-managed files do not reach Anthropic-hosted sessions.

steps.title: Filter connectors in cloud sessions
body: Connectors are passed to the cloud VM and filtered by the organisation's allowedMcpServers / deniedMcpServers patterns; disableSideloadFlags drops servers the server delivered through --mcp-config.

original.note: Server-managed deny hides, allow pre-approves, specifiers limit arguments; the per-session mode picker can still choose Auto unless disableAutoMode is set. Connector tools follow the org's ask/blocked settings.

original.mechanism: Server-managed settings permissions.deny / ask and allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly apply to cloud sessions; command hooks committed in the repository run inside the VM

steps.title: Deliver deny rules through server-managed settings
body: Configure permissions.deny and allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly under Admin settings > Claude Code; deny rules run before every permission mode in the session, and endpoint-managed files never reach Anthropic-hosted sessions.

original.note: Deny rules are deterministic and organisation-owned. Hooks are repository code, writable by anyone with push access, so they are not enterprise policy. Connector tools follow the organisation's ask or blocked settings; a connector's own actions are outside the rules.

original.mechanism: Organisation allowedMcpServers / deniedMcpServers patterns filter the connectors passed to the cloud VM; disableSideloadFlags; organisation connector ask / blocked settings

steps.title: Filter connectors organisation-wide
body: Deliver allowedMcpServers and deniedMcpServers through server-managed settings so only matching connectors reach cloud sessions; disableSideloadFlags drops servers a session tried to add itself.

original.note: Rated native on the same rule as Claude Code: admission by identity, organisation-wide. Admission is not integrity — nothing pins the tool descriptions a connector returns or detects a changed implementation. Connector traffic runs through Anthropic's servers and never passes the environment's network policy.

controls.mechanism: Server-managed permissions.ask rules and connector tools set to ask stop an interactive cloud session for the user's approval; for everything else the gate is the draft branch or pull request a person reviews

steps.title: Force prompts on named actions
body: Add permissions.ask rules such as Bash(git push *) in server-managed settings; an ask rule prompts even in Auto, and the prompt appears in claude.ai or the mobile app.

steps.title: Keep auto-fix off where comments deploy
body: Leave the per-PR Auto-fix toggle off on repositories where an issue_comment can run Atlantis, Terraform Cloud or privileged Actions; auto-fix pushes and replies under the user's GitHub account.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: a merge gate approves the output, not the actions. Cloud sessions pre-approve file edits in every mode and Accept edits pushes the branch without stopping; ask rules and connector ask settings do make a person approve named actions in interactive sessions, but scheduled tasks and GitHub-triggered runs have no permission-mode picker and run without stopping for approval, so no one is present. The auto-mode classifier and Code Review are not human approval; the reviewer's merge on GitHub comes after the actions ran.

original.mechanism: Per-session permission mode picker (Accept edits, Plan, Auto; Bypass unavailable in cloud sessions), permissions.ask rules from server-managed settings, MCP connector tool approvals that pause the session

steps.title: Force prompts on named actions
body: Add permissions.ask rules such as Bash(git push *) in server-managed settings; the session waits for the user (and expires if it waits too long) rather than auto-approving.

steps.title: Review before merge
body: Sessions produce a diff and a PR rather than merging; auto-fix acts only on PRs where the toggle is on, and the docs recommend disabling it where a PR comment can deploy infrastructure. The PR gates the output, not actions taken during the session — use permissions.ask for those.

controls.mechanism: Organisation, group, per-user and pooled monthly spend limits under Organization settings > Usage (Enterprise); a monthly spend limit on usage credits (Team and seat-based Enterprise); vendor-fixed seat limits and scheduled-task hourly run and GitHub-event caps

steps.title: Set group, user and organisation spend limits
body: Under Organization settings > Usage > Spend limits, set group limits (By group/tier), per-user limits and, if needed, a pooled monthly budget; members stop at whichever limit runs out first.

steps.title: Cap usage credits on seat-based plans
body: On Team and seat-based Enterprise, set the monthly spend limit on usage credits under Organization settings > Usage, or leave credits off so members stop at the seat's included usage.

controls.note: Native on the rule: admin-set spend limits stop usage when exhausted — the consumption guide says members at their limit are blocked mid-task and usage can go slightly over before it pauses — and scheduled runs past the limit are rejected without usage credits. Not admin-settable: session duration, concurrency, fan-out or a per-session budget; the scheduled-task hourly run limits, per-task GitHub event caps and the VM ceilings (about 4 vCPUs, 16 GB RAM, 30 GB disk) are vendor-fixed, and Team seats carry fixed included usage. Cloud sessions share the account's rate limits with all other Claude usage.

original.mechanism: Cloud sessions share the account's rate limits; organisation and per-user spend limits in the admin console; no per-session budget or time cap

steps.title: Set organisation, group and user spend limits
body: Configure limits under Organization settings > Usage (org default, by group, per user); Claude Code, Cowork and chat draw from the same consumption pool.

original.note: Sessions stop only when the account's limits are exhausted; there is no turn or wall-clock cap for a cloud session. Sub-limits present: account rate limits and organisation or per-user spend limits (hard at the account). Absent: turn, wall-clock and per-session spend caps.

controls.mechanism: Enterprise Inference hooks send each governed request's transcript, tool results included, to the organisation's AI security server before inference; server-managed PostToolUse hooks run in cloud sessions and can replace a tool's output; built-in safeguards are not configurable

steps.title: Deny poisoned requests before inference
body: Allow Inference hooks for the organisation; they govern Claude Code sessions on the web, so your AI security server can deny a request carrying injected issue text, file content or tool output.

steps.title: Replace suspect tool output
body: Deliver a PostToolUse hook through server-managed settings that classifies WebFetch, Bash and MCP results and returns updatedToolOutput with a quarantine notice.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: both are attach points for the organisation's own classifier. Nothing in the product classifies issue text, review comments, repository files or fetched pages for injection, and no hidden-character or HTML-comment filtering is documented; the auto-mode classifier judges actions, not inputs; the Trusted network level is containment. CODEOWNERS on .claude/, CLAUDE.md and the environment's setup script is the process control.

original.mechanism: Same built-in safeguards as local Claude Code plus the auto-mode classifier and a default-limited network egress; Enterprise Inference hooks apply to Claude Code sessions

steps.title: Keep egress at Trusted or Custom
body: Set the environment's network access level to Trusted (default) or a Custom allowlist so an injected instruction cannot reach arbitrary hosts.

steps.title: Add inline prompt inspection (Enterprise, beta)
body: Configure Inference hooks so every governed Claude Code prompt is sent to your AI security server for an allow/deny verdict before inference.

original.note: The built-in safeguards detect a subset of injected commands and web content; the egress limit and auto-mode classifier contain the rest. Nothing detects injection in repository files or MCP results as such.

controls.mechanism: GitHub proxy (a scoped credential in the VM swapped for the user's token; no branch deletions or tag pushes; API calls to attached repositories; GraphQL refused); network secrets attached per host by the agent proxy (every plan); any key the proxy can't attach an environment variable the session can read

steps.title: Let the GitHub proxy hold the repository credential
body: Leave GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN unset so both read proxy-injected and the proxy substitutes the real credential outside the VM; a token you set is an ordinary variable everyone using the environment can read.

steps.title: Keep other keys out of the VM
body: Store keys as network secrets with their hosts (Owners do it for shared environments from the Cloud environments admin page) so the agent proxy attaches them after the request leaves the VM.

steps.title: Supply git credentials per session when self-hosting
body: Start runners with --use-anthropic-git-proxy, or mint a short-lived per-session token in the wrapper script, instead of baking credentials into the runner image.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: the repository credential and network secrets stay outside the sandbox, but a network secret is attached in every session in the environment, whoever started it, and never to setup-script requests, package registries or the Anthropic API, so any key those need is an environment variable that the setup script, every command and — through tool output — the model can read, as can every member sharing the environment; setup-phase secrets aren't removed before the agent runs. Connector credentials stay on Anthropic's side. The session exercises the user's GitHub grant; there is no on-behalf-of exchange.

original.mechanism: GitHub proxy keeps git credentials and signing keys outside the VM (a scoped credential swapped at the proxy, push limited to the working branch, API requests scoped to attached repositories); API credentials attached per host by the agent proxy on Pro and Max only; environment variables readable by the session

steps.title: Rely on the GitHub proxy, not tokens in the environment
body: Leave GitHub access to the proxy: the git client holds a scoped credential the proxy swaps for your token, push works only against the session's branch, and GitHub API calls reach only attached repositories. A GH_TOKEN you set gets the same restrictions.

original.note: Rated partial on the same rule as the Claude Agent SDK: the GitHub path is isolated by default, but on Team and Enterprise every other credential a session needs is an environment variable readable by commands and, through tool output, by the model — per-host API credentials exist on Pro and Max only. No on-behalf-of exchange: sessions act as the connecting user's GitHub identity.

original.mechanism: GitHub proxy keeps git credentials and signing keys outside the sandbox; API credentials attached by the agent proxy per host (Pro/Max only); environment variables are readable by the session

steps.title: Never put secrets in environment variables
body: Every session in a shared environment can read its variables and setup script; on Pro/Max store keys as API credentials with allowed hosts instead. Team and Enterprise do not have API credentials yet.

steps.title: Supply git credentials from your own store in self-hosted environments
body: Configure per-session minted credentials or the Anthropic git proxy in the runner deployment rather than baking tokens into the runner image.

original.note: Git credentials and signing keys are held by the proxy and never enter the sandbox; environment variables set on the environment are readable by every command in the session and by the model through tool output. Per-host API credential injection is a Pro/Max feature, not an Enterprise one.

controls.mechanism: Transcripts kept under the account's retention and restored on reopen (the owner deletes them); per-session Team or Public sharing chosen by the user; environment cache snapshots of setup-script output; repository CLAUDE.md and .claude/ loaded from the clone; server-managed claudeMd and strictPluginOnlyCustomization

steps.title: Lock what the repository can add
body: Deliver strictPluginOnlyCustomization in server-managed settings so repository skills, agents, hooks and MCP servers can't add instructions that run with tool access.

steps.title: Put organisation instructions above the repository's
body: Set the managed claudeMd key in server-managed settings; it loads before project CLAUDE.md files and can't be excluded.

steps.title: Review the cached environment
body: Treat a shared environment's setup script as reviewed code; editing it rebuilds the snapshot every member's sessions start from.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: what persists is set by the vendor and the user, not admin policy. Transcripts follow the plan's retention and only their owner deletes them; sharing is a per-session user toggle (Team visibility on Team and Enterprise, with repository access verification on by default; Public on Pro and Max), and Claude-in-Slack sessions are shared with Team visibility automatically; the environment cache keeps setup output for later sessions for about seven days; auto memory is machine-local and doesn't carry across cloud environments. Instruction files and hooks arrive with the clone, writable by anyone with push access, and nothing validates them.

original.mechanism: Session VMs are reclaimed after inactivity and conversation history is restored on reopen; users can delete sessions permanently; auto memory follows the repository's settings

steps.title: Delete sessions and bound the VM lifetime
body: Users delete sessions (event data removed permanently) from the sidebar; VMs are automatically reclaimed after inactivity and background work is not restored.

original.note: Retention and deletion only: transcripts are restored on reopen and deletable. Transcript retention is not poisoning detection; auto memory in the repository is the same plain-file store as local Claude Code, with no validation or rollback.

controls.mechanism: Anthropic Trust Center artifacts feed the organisation's TPRM platform

evidence.title: Anthropic Trust Center (compliance table and Request access)
Claude Code security page, cloud execution security

controls.note: External: assessed in the organisation's TPRM platform. The Trust Center lists SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, ISO 42001, CSA STAR, HIPAA and NIST 800-171 for Claude Enterprise (Claude Team: all but HIPAA), with reports behind Request access; the security page's cloud execution section states the isolation, credential-proxy, push-restriction and audit-logging claims to assess. Re-assess when the defaults move: network level, network-secret availability, and Compliance API coverage of cloud sessions.

original.mechanism: Anthropic Trust Center artifacts (SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001) into the buyer's TPRM platform
original.note: Vendor evidence is published; cadence and reassessment are the organisation's own TPRM process.

steps.title: Attach vendor evidence
body: Pull the Trust Center reports linked from the Claude Code security page into the vendor record; the cloud execution section documents the isolation claims to assess.

original.mechanism: Compliance API organisation settings endpoint and Activity Feed expose effective settings and admin actions to posture tooling; server-managed settings are readable by Owners

steps.title: Read effective settings programmatically
body: Use the Compliance API directory endpoints (organizations, users, roles, groups and each organisation's effective settings) with a Compliance Access Key to evidence the configuration.

original.note: Readback only: the Compliance API exposes effective settings for an SSPM product to compare against policy; the product ships no baseline comparison, drift detection or remediation.

controls.mechanism: A fresh, isolated Anthropic-managed VM per cloud session, reclaimed after inactivity; sessions routed to a self-hosted environment run on the organisation's own runners

steps.title: Keep sessions in isolated environments
body: Each cloud session runs in an isolated, Anthropic-managed VM; a session routed to a self-hosted environment runs on your runners, where isolation is your deployment's responsibility.

steps.title: Give each self-hosted session its own container
body: Run self-hosted runners at --capacity 1 with an ephemeral container per session, or use on-demand runners, and keep the environment secret off hosts that run sessions.

controls.note: Native: each Anthropic-hosted session gets a fresh VM (Ubuntu 24.04, x86_64) that is reclaimed after inactivity; background work isn't restored. Shared across sessions: only the environment cache, a filesystem snapshot of the setup script's output that later sessions start from. Inside: shell, file tools, Docker and the setup script, which runs as root. Outside: the model, MCP connectors (through Anthropic's servers) and the GitHub proxy. In a self-hosted environment isolation is the operator's.

original.mechanism: Isolated Anthropic-managed VM per session; sessions routed to a self-hosted environment run on the organisation's own runners

steps.title: Keep sessions in isolated environments
body: Each cloud session runs in an isolated, Anthropic-managed VM; a session routed to a self-hosted environment runs on your runners, where isolation is your deployment's responsibility.

steps.title: Harden self-hosted runners yourself
body: Build the runner image, default-deny egress and git credential supply into the deployment; Anthropic's boundary stops at the session it hands the runner.

original.note: Inside the boundary: the shell, file tools, Docker and the setup script. Outside: the model, MCP connectors (their traffic runs through Anthropic's servers) and the GitHub proxy. The VM is reclaimed after inactivity and background work is not restored.

controls.mechanism: Environment network access level (None, Trusted, Full, Custom with Allowed domains) enforced by the security proxy in Anthropic-hosted environments; default Trusted; Owner-managed shared environments and an organisation default

steps.title: Author the allowlist on a shared environment
body: On the Cloud environments admin page, create a shared environment with Network access set to Custom and your Allowed domains; members see it read-only.

steps.title: Make it the organisation default
body: Choose that environment as the organisation's default at claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-code so sessions members start without picking one use it.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: an Owner authors a Custom allowlist on shared environments, but it isn't locked — members can create personal environments at Full and select them, and the docs say there is no organisation-level allowlist admins can push. Setup and agent phases share one network policy. Bypassing the allowlist at every level, None included: GitHub through its proxy, MCP connectors through Anthropic's servers, network-secret hosts and the Anthropic API. The Trusted defaults include write-capable hosts such as gist.github.com, npm and PyPI. In a self-hosted environment egress is your own boundary.

original.mechanism: Environment Network access level (None, Trusted, Full, Custom with Allowed domains) enforced by the security proxy in Anthropic-hosted environments; default Trusted; organisation-shared environments with an organisation default

steps.title: Set the environment's network access level
body: In the environment dialog choose None, Trusted (package registries, GitHub, cloud SDKs) or Custom with your own Allowed domains; Full allows any domain. The security proxy carries every outbound request and keeps a DNS-level audit trail.

steps.title: Share a locked-down environment organisation-wide
body: Owners create organisation-shared environments on the Cloud environments admin page and set an organisation default so members' sessions inherit it; do not put secrets in its variables, every member's session reads them.

original.note: Paths the allowlist never sees, at every level including None: GitHub through its proxy, MCP connectors through Anthropic's servers, hosts listed on API credentials, and the Anthropic API itself. In a self-hosted environment egress is your own firewall.

controls.mechanism: Transcript and diff at claude.ai/code with Claude-Session commit trailers; Activity Feed control-plane events (ccr_session_created, session_share_created, managed-settings changes); Inference hooks push each governed request's transcript (Enterprise); OpenTelemetry from the server-managed env block, which reaches Anthropic-hosted sessions, and self-hosted runners' pinned OTLP destination

steps.title: Link every commit to its session
body: Keep attribution.sessionUrl at its default so commits carry a Claude-Session trailer and PR bodies link the transcript.

steps.title: Pull control-plane events
body: Read ccr_session_created, ccr_session_updated, session_share_created and claude_code_managed_settings activities from the Compliance API Activity Feed.

steps.title: Archive transcripts as they happen
body: Have your Inference hooks server store each governed request's transcript and return allow.

steps.title: Export OpenTelemetry from cloud sessions
body: Set CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY and the OTEL_* exporter variables in the server-managed settings env block, and add the collector's domain to each shared environment's allowlist; filter on ccr.session.id. On self-hosted runners, name the endpoint in the runner's environment.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: nothing exports the Anthropic-hosted session record itself. The Compliance API session endpoints exclude Claude Code cloud sessions (the remote endpoints return Cowork only); the Activity Feed is control-plane; the Inference hooks feed is a beta pre-inference policy hook (prompt event only, so a session's final response isn't sent, and ancillary requests are skipped), not a session export; OpenTelemetry from server-managed settings reaches Anthropic-hosted sessions but leaves through the session's network, so it arrives only where the environment's allowlist admits the collector, and a member's personal environment can leave it out (Claude Tag sessions don't receive server-managed settings). The security page says cloud operations are logged for compliance; customer access to those logs isn't documented.

original.mechanism: Session transcript and diff view at claude.ai/code; all outbound traffic through the security proxy is logged for audit; self-hosted runners expose metrics and a health endpoint and forward OTel from sessions

steps.title: Read the session record
body: Each session keeps the full conversation, tool activity and per-file diffs, visible to the user and (with Team visibility) the organisation.

steps.title: Export runner and session telemetry when self-hosting
body: The runner honours the OpenTelemetry variables from network-config and sessions inherit them; the reference lists runner metrics and the health endpoint.

original.note: Anthropic-hosted sessions do not expose an OTLP export to the organisation's collector and the Compliance API does not return Claude Code web transcripts.

original.mechanism: Anthropic logs all cloud-session operations and proxy traffic for compliance; admin console changes appear in the Enterprise audit log / Compliance API Activity Feed; session transcripts are not exported

steps.title: Export admin and settings events
body: Enterprise Owners export audit logs (180 days) from Organization settings > Data and privacy or query the Compliance API Activity Feed; server-managed settings changes are audited there.

original.note: The Compliance API session endpoints explicitly exclude Claude Code on the web; the vendor's own operation logs are not customer-accessible.

controls.mechanism: Owner toggles (Cloud sessions, Scheduled tasks), archiving a shared environment, seat removal, owner-only session archive and delete; for self-hosted environments, environment-secret revocation and runner drain

steps.title: Turn cloud sessions off
body: Turn the Cloud sessions toggle (the allow_remote_sessions policy) off at claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-code; new cloud sessions and CLI follow-ups then fail with a policy error.

steps.title: Stop scheduled tasks
body: Turn the Scheduled tasks (Was Routines) toggle off at Organization settings > Capabilities > Remote sessions; existing tasks stop running and members can't create new ones.

steps.title: Retire an environment
body: Archive a shared environment on the Cloud environments page so no new session starts in it; sessions already running continue.

steps.title: Cut off self-hosted runners
body: Revoke the environment secret on the environment's Configuration tab; runners holding it fail their next poll and exit.

controls.note: Partial: no documented admin stop for a running Anthropic-hosted session — archive and delete are the session owner's actions, and the VM is reclaimed only after an unstated idle period. Turning cloud sessions off, archiving an environment or removing a seat blocks new sessions; whether a running session stops is not documented (delay not documented). Revoking a self-hosted environment secret stops runners at their next poll, while issued session JWTs stay valid until they expire.

original.mechanism: Owner toggles (Code in the web, allow_remote_sessions, Remote Control, Allow self-hosted environments), seat removal, session archive/delete, runner --retire-at and SIGTERM drain

steps.title: Turn the surface off
body: Owners disable "Code in the web" and allow_remote_sessions at claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-code; new cloud sessions then fail with a policy error.

steps.title: Stop runners cleanly
body: Self-hosted runners drain on SIGTERM or at --retire-at, releasing sessions so they resume elsewhere; revoking the environment key stops new claims.

original.note: Running Anthropic-hosted sessions are not remotely terminable by an admin; they end at inactivity.

controls.mechanism: Write-only network secrets on every plan (unreadable after saving, attached by the agent proxy, Owner-managed on shared environments); plain environment variables for anything else; the user's GitHub token held by the GitHub proxy, with /web-setup tokens stored encrypted with the account; for self-hosted environments a rotatable environment secret and short-lived session tokens

steps.title: Keep secrets out of environment variables
body: Don't put secrets in an environment's variables or setup script, which everyone using the environment can read; use network secrets, which can't be viewed after saving.

steps.title: Remove a stored GitHub token
body: Disconnect GitHub at claude.ai/customize/connectors to delete the stored /web-setup token, and revoke it on GitHub to invalidate it.

steps.title: Rotate the self-hosted environment secret
body: Create a new secret on the environment's Configuration tab, roll it out to runners and revoke the old one; each secret expires 365 days after creation.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: network secrets are a write-only store on every plan, but they rotate only by delete and re-add and never reach setup-script requests, package registries or the Anthropic API, so keys for those stay plain variables readable by every member sharing the environment, every command and the model through tool output. The repository credential sits outside the VM, but its lifetime is the connected GitHub grant — a /web-setup gh token is long-lived — and no shorter-lived repository credential is documented for Anthropic-hosted sessions. Tunnel: Anthropic offers no private-network tunnel for Anthropic-hosted sessions; connectors reach your servers from Anthropic's side. Self-hosted environments are the private-network option: the environment secret is shown once, expires after 365 days and is rotated and revoked per environment (the orchestrator's SCM connector tunnel to GitHub Enterprise Server authenticates with it), runner inference tokens last about 30 minutes, and session JWTs four hours with no revocation feed.

settings.name: Require SSO for Claude
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Organization and access › Authentication
settings.recommended: On, with MFA enforced on the Claude app in your IdP
settings.why: Every claude.ai login — the only credential cloud sessions accept — goes through the corporate IdP and its MFA.

settings.name: User provisioning (SCIM)
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Organization and access › User provisioning
settings.recommended: SCIM, driven by the IdP group that grants Claude Code
settings.why: Removing someone in the IdP removes their seat, so a leaver can no longer start, steer or schedule cloud sessions.

settings.name: Restrict organization creation
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Organization and access › Security
settings.recommended: On
settings.why: Stops staff creating side Claude organisations on your domains whose cloud sessions run outside your managed settings and environments.

settings.name: Cloud sessions
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Claude Code (the allow_remote_sessions policy)
settings.recommended: On, once the organisation default environment and server-managed settings are in place
settings.why: The organisation-wide switch for every cloud session, CLI handoff and scheduled task; off, new sessions fail with a policy error.

settings.name: Cloud sessions (custom role capability)
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Roles › role › Capabilities › Claude Code
settings.default: On for roles that already granted Claude Code
settings.recommended: Granted only to the engineering groups' roles
settings.why: Members whose role lacks it can't run sessions on Anthropic's infrastructure or use Remote Control, so the surface follows the IdP group.

settings.name: Quick setup
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Claude Code
settings.recommended: Off
settings.why: Keeps /web-setup hidden, so no member hands a personal gh token to cloud sessions that then reach every repository it can.

settings.name: Repository access (Claude GitHub App installation)
settings.where: GitHub › organization Settings › GitHub Apps › Claude › Repository access
settings.recommended: Only select repositories — those teams have approved for cloud sessions
settings.why: A browser-connected session reaches private repositories only where the App's installation includes them, so the App scope is the repository allowlist.

settings.name: Connected GitHub accounts
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Git providers › GitHub
settings.recommended: Only the firm's GitHub organisations linked; personal accounts unlinked
settings.why: Members' own GitHub accounts with the App installed link to the organisation automatically; reviewing the list keeps code sources inventoried.

settings.name: Allow self-hosted environments
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Cloud environments
settings.recommended: Off, unless a team owns and hardens the runners
settings.why: Keeps sessions in Anthropic's per-session VMs; a self-hosted runner's isolation, egress and git credentials become yours to build.

settings.name: Default environment
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Claude Code
settings.default: The member's own Default environment (Trusted network access)
settings.recommended: An Owner-managed organisation-shared environment with Custom network access
settings.why: Sessions members start without picking an environment run on the organisation's network policy and setup script, not one each person made.

settings.name: Network access
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Cloud environments › shared environment › Network access
settings.recommended: Custom — your source control, package mirror and approved domains in Allowed domains
settings.why: Trusted is Anthropic's list and includes write-capable hosts such as gist.github.com; members can still pick personal Full environments, which no setting locks.

settings.name: Network secrets
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Cloud environments › shared environment › Network secrets
settings.default: None (Environment variables readable by every session)
settings.recommended: Every API key a shared environment needs, scoped to its hosts; no secrets in Environment variables or the setup script
settings.why: The agent proxy attaches the key after the request leaves the VM, so neither the model nor a command can read it, as they can a variable.

settings.name: Scheduled tasks (Was Routines)
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Capabilities › Remote sessions (on Enterprise also the role's Remote sessions capability)
settings.recommended: On only for the roles that own unattended runs; off for everyone else
settings.why: Scheduled, API and GitHub-triggered runs act with nobody present; off, existing tasks stop and none can be created. On Team the toggle is organisation-wide, so leave it off until someone owns them.

settings.name: permissions.deny
settings.where: Organization settings › Claude Code › Managed settings → permissions.deny
settings.recommended: Deny reads of secret paths — Read(./.env*), Read(./secrets/**)
settings.why: Server-managed deny rules are the only permission policy that reaches a cloud session, and they win over every mode.

settings.name: disableAutoMode
settings.where: Organization settings › Claude Code › Managed settings → disableAutoMode
settings.default: Unset (Auto offered where the model supports it)
settings.recommended: Unset — Auto stays available; deny and ask rules still precede it
settings.why: Cloud sessions already pre-approve edits and never offer Bypass; regulated teams set "disable" so sessions run only in Accept edits or Plan.

settings.name: allowManagedHooksOnly
settings.where: Organization settings › Claude Code › Managed settings → allowManagedHooksOnly
settings.recommended: true
settings.why: Hooks committed to the repository otherwise run in the VM with the environment's network and variables; move dependency installs to the environment's setup script.

settings.name: strictPluginOnlyCustomization
settings.where: Organization settings › Claude Code › Managed settings → strictPluginOnlyCustomization
settings.recommended: ["hooks", "mcp"]
settings.why: A cloned repository's .mcp.json servers and hooks don't load in the session; project skills and agents stay available.

settings.name: claudeMd
settings.where: Organization settings › Claude Code › Managed settings → claudeMd
settings.recommended: The organisation's standing rules (no secrets in commits, no pushes to protected branches)
settings.why: Loads ahead of the repository's CLAUDE.md, so organisation instructions sit above anything a contributor commits.

settings.name: Organization-wide tool policy
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Connectors › connector › tool (Always allow / Needs approval / Blocked)
settings.recommended: Write and send tools set to Needs approval; tools no one uses Blocked
settings.why: A tool set to ask prompts on every call even in Auto, and a blocked tool never reaches the session; connector traffic bypasses the environment allowlist.

settings.name: Inference hooks
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Data and privacy › Inference hooks
settings.recommended: On, connected to your DLP or AI-security service, enforcing after a monitor-only period
settings.why: Each governed request from a cloud session, tool results included, is checked by your own service before inference, so injected issue text or secrets can be stopped centrally.

settings.name: Member limit
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Usage › By group/tier › Edit limits
settings.recommended: A monthly per-member limit on each group that runs Claude Code
settings.why: A runaway or looping cloud session stops when its owner's limit is spent, rather than drawing on the organisation's whole pool.

settings.name: Compliance API (Activity Feed)
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › API, then a Compliance Access Key
settings.recommended: On, pulled into your SIEM
settings.why: Session creation, deletion and sharing and managed-settings changes (ccr_session_created, session_share_created) reach the SIEM; cloud-session transcripts are not in the Compliance API.

settings.name: CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY with OTEL exporters
settings.where: Organization settings › Claude Code › Managed settings → env.CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY, OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT
settings.recommended: "1", exporting OTLP logs and metrics to your collector, with its domain in every shared environment's Allowed domains
settings.why: Tool decisions and API requests from cloud sessions reach the SIEM keyed by ccr.session.id; the export leaves through the session's network, so an environment that can't reach the collector sends nothing.

settings.name: attribution.sessionUrl
settings.where: Organization settings › Claude Code › Managed settings → attribution.sessionUrl
settings.recommended: true — don't turn it off
settings.why: Every commit carries a Claude-Session trailer and every pull request links the transcript, so a reviewer can trace the run that produced it.

settings.name: Remote Control
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Claude Code
settings.default: Off on Team and Enterprise until an Owner enables it
settings.recommended: Off, unless a team needs to drive local sessions from claude.ai or a phone
settings.why: Stops a developer's local session — with their files and credentials — being steered from claude.ai/code alongside the cloud sessions.

tools.name: Claude Cowork

variants.name: Cowork in Claude Desktop (local session in the Cowork VM sandbox)
Cowork in the cloud (web, mobile, Chrome side panel; sessions on Anthropic servers)
variants.note: Announced 7 July 2026 (beta, Max first). "Run Cowork in the cloud" is on by default on Team and off by default on Enterprise, where an owner turns it on and grants the "Cowork in the cloud" capability through custom roles. Device managed settings do not reach these sessions.

variants.name: Dispatch (background tasks) and scheduled tasks
variants.note: Dispatch runs its tasks on the desktop (Pro and Max, not offered to new users); scheduled tasks run in the cloud with no device online.

summary: Cowork is Anthropic's agentic workspace for non-developers: the Claude Code architecture inside Claude Desktop, working on the user's own files, connectors, skills and plugins, with sub-agents, browser use (Claude in Chrome or a built-in browser) and computer use. Local sessions run shell and document tools in a hardened VM on the device with file access scoped to connected folders and shell traffic held to the organisation's egress policy; cloud sessions (web, mobile, Chrome side panel) run on Anthropic's servers, save sessions and files to the account, keep working with every device offline, and can only touch local folders while the desktop app is open. Inference is the Anthropic API on first-party plans, or the organisation's provider on Claude Desktop on 3P.

Modelled as a third-party coding and desktop agent: it is the Claude Code runtime inside a vendor desktop app, driven by a present user who connects folders and approves tool calls, and administered through the same two planes as Claude Code (the claude.ai console and device managed configuration). It is not the self-hosted autonomous personal-agent class; the cloud variant stretches towards a managed agent runtime and is noted on the variant. Admin control is in the claude.ai console at Organization settings > Cowork: "Enable for your organization", "Run Cowork in the cloud", the built-in browser toggle, "Allow 'Always allow' for connector tools" and an OTLP collector for session events; under Organization settings > Capabilities, "Allow 'Automatically approve' mode" and "Start new tasks in 'Automatically approve' mode"; and curated plugin marketplaces (Installed by default / Available / Required / Not available), with role-based access on Enterprise; on the device, Claude Desktop's enterprise policy (com.anthropic.claudefordesktop, HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Claude) adds allowedWorkspaceFolders, secureVmFeaturesEnabled, isLocalDevMcpEnabled, isDesktopExtensionEnabled and forceLoginOrgUUID, and local sessions read Claude Code managed settings deployed on the device; the wider key set (coworkEgressAllowedHosts, disabledBuiltinTools, disableBypassPermissionsMode, coworkTabEnabled) is documented for Claude Desktop on 3P. Cowork sessions never fetch Claude Code server-managed settings. No behavioural baseline or drift detection is offered; the OTLP event stream is the raw material if one is built.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise in Claude Desktop; web and mobile in beta for Pro, Max and Team and for Enterprise where admins enable it; Claude Desktop on 3P runs Cowork on Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry or a gateway.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Anthropic API (first-party) or the provider configured in Claude Desktop managed configuration (inferenceProvider gateway / bedrock / vertex / foundry / anthropic) on 3P deployments.

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: Prompts, the contents of files in connected folders that Claude reads, tool outputs, browser page content and connector data go to the model provider; cloud sessions store sessions and files in the account; the OTLP exporter (inside the VM, subject to egress rules) sends events to the organisation's collector.

facts.label: Retention & training
facts.value: Local conversation history stays on the device outside standard retention (Compliance API captures local sessions server-side for 6 years or the custom period); cloud sessions are saved to the account (remote transcripts 6 years unless deleted). Cowork is not covered by ZDR. Commercial terms: no training.

facts.label: Usage limits & models
facts.value: Organisation, group and per-user usage limits (Organization settings > Usage) are shared across Cowork, Claude Code and chat, with no per-task budget; model access and effort caps under Organization settings > Models are enforced across most Claude products including Cowork.

facts.label: Network path
facts.value: TLS to the provider; on Claude Desktop on 3P, egressProxyUrl / egressProxyPacUrl in managed configuration route app and agent traffic; HTTPS_PROXY, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS and CLAUDE_CODE_CLIENT_CERT/KEY are read from managed and user settings only in app-managed sessions, never from repository settings.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: claude.com/docs/cowork plus the Help Center Cowork on Team and Enterprise article

riskNotes.note: Cowork reads documents, web pages (via the built-in browser or Claude in Chrome) and connector results as instructions, with the "Automatically approve" mode offered to members by default on Team and Enterprise; the egress policy and connector tool approvals are the containment.

"Always allow" for connector tools is off by default because it removes the per-tool prompt; bypass ("Skip all approvals") can be removed with disableBypassPermissionsMode only on Claude Desktop on 3P.

Users can attach home folders, Documents, AppData and whole drives (4 September 2026; SSH keys and cloud credentials inside them stay off-limits); allowedWorkspaceFolders in the enterprise policy is the fence. OTLP events carry metadata only on current Desktop versions unless the otlpContentCapture device key adds content (some older versions send it when the key is unset, so deploy it as []); connected folder paths are always included, so filter at the collector.

Cloud sessions and scheduled tasks run unattended without a device; the Enterprise console can enable cloud capability per group, and the Compliance API lists remote Cowork sessions including agent-owned scheduled runs.

Users can add plugin marketplaces and upload plugins; admins curate marketplaces (Installed by default, Available, Required, Not available), claude.ai applies the admin console's strictKnownMarketplaces and blockedMarketplaces to marketplaces added from Cowork, and turning off user marketplaces and uploads is a Claude Desktop on 3P key.

controls.mechanism: Anthropic's content classifiers scan untrusted content entering Claude's context (no administrator setting); Inference hooks (Enterprise) hold every governed Cowork prompt and returned tool result for an allow or deny verdict from the organisation's AI security server

steps.title: Put an inspector on returned tool content (Enterprise)
body: At Organization settings > Data and privacy > Inference hooks turn on "Allow for your organization", register your AI security server, set Failure handling to "Block the request" and turn on "Enforce verdicts" so Cowork prompts and tool results wait for its verdict.

steps.title: Know what the vendor screening covers
body: The Cowork safety page states that content classifiers scan all untrusted content entering Claude's context and flag potential injections; there is no setting, threshold or event export for them.

controls.note: Partial on the rule applied to every vendor: vendor-internal screening that is not admin-configurable, plus an inline hook that is an attach point until the organisation's server does the classifying. Inference hooks govern Cowork on web, desktop and mobile, including tool results, but return only allow or deny (no strip or quarantine), are an Enterprise beta, never send system prompts or tool definitions, and are not available on Bedrock or Google Cloud deployments. The "Automatically approve" safety check judges proposed actions, which is action policy, not input screening.

original.mechanism: Auto-mode classifier ("Automatically approve"), browser safety classifiers, egress allowlist; Enterprise Inference hooks govern Cowork prompts

steps.title: Keep tool approvals in the loop
body: Leave "Allow 'Always allow' for connector tools" off and consider turning off "Allow 'Automatically approve' mode" under Organization settings > Cowork > Permissions for sensitive teams.

steps.title: Inspect prompts inline (Enterprise, beta)
body: Inference hooks send every governed Cowork prompt, including tool results, to your AI security server for an allow/deny verdict before inference.

original.note: The auto-mode and browser classifiers screen proposed actions; the egress allowlist contains. Document and connector content is not classified for injected instructions.

controls.mechanism: Inference hooks (Enterprise) hand every governed Cowork prompt, tool result and uploaded file text to the organisation's DLP server for allow or deny; allowedWorkspaceFolders, the built-in exclusion of credential locations and a Blocked or read-only connector tool policy minimise what can be read

steps.title: Inspect prompts and tool results inline (Enterprise)
body: At Organization settings > Data and privacy > Inference hooks connect your DLP or AI security server and turn on "Enforce verdicts"; it denies requests carrying regulated content, since rewriting or redacting a prompt is not supported.

steps.title: Fence the folders Cowork can mount
body: Set allowedWorkspaceFolders in com.anthropic.claudefordesktop or HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Claude to the folders users may connect (unset is unrestricted).

steps.title: Keep sensitive connectors read-only
body: Set write tools to Blocked at Organization settings > Connectors, or per custom role on the Connectors tab under Organization settings > Roles (Enterprise).

controls.note: Partial by the rule: an inline hook that can block is an attach point, and nothing in the product masks or tokenises a value. Folder allowlists, the exclusion of SSH keys, AWS and Google Cloud credentials and shell profiles from attached home folders (changelog, 4 September 2026) and read-only connector policy are data minimisation, not detection. Hooks see what reaches the model (browser pages and file contents only as far as they enter the conversation); the Compliance API supports DLP after the fact.

original.mechanism: allowedWorkspaceFolders and Read deny rules limit what can be read; connector write permissions can be removed; Inference hooks (Enterprise) inspect prompts inline; coworkEgressAllowedHosts limits where data can go

steps.title: Fence data paths
body: Combine allowedWorkspaceFolders, disabledBuiltinTools Read rules for secret paths and connector read-only permissions; add Inference hooks for inline DLP on Enterprise.

original.note: Folder scoping, deny rules and the egress allowlist restrict paths; Inference hooks are the only content-inspection path and only for prompts the organisation's server governs. File contents read inside the VM are not scanned.

controls.mechanism: "Require SSO for Claude" (Organization settings > Organization and access > Authentication) sends every interactive sign-in through the IdP, whose MFA policy applies; forceLoginOrgUUID pins Claude Desktop to the organisation; "Shortened session length" bounds how long a sign-in lasts (Enterprise)

steps.title: Enforce SSO
body: After domain verification and IdP setup, toggle on "Require SSO for Claude" under Organization settings > Organization and access > Authentication, and require MFA in the IdP.

steps.title: Pin the desktop app to your organisation
body: Deploy forceLoginOrgUUID in com.anthropic.claudefordesktop or HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Claude; login fails for any account outside the listed organisations.

steps.title: Bound session lifetime (Enterprise)
body: At Organization settings > Organization and access > Session security enable "Shortened session length" (1, 7, 14 or 28 days) so users sign in, and meet the IdP's MFA, again.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: MFA is configured in the IdP, not in Claude, which documents no second-factor requirement of its own. Paths that skip a fresh challenge: the desktop's signed-in session (kept while the user stays active unless Shortened session length is set), cloud sessions and scheduled tasks that keep running on that sign-in with no device present ("Require trusted devices" under Organization settings > Capabilities > Remote sessions adds an enrolled-device and 18-hour sign-in check to reaching a device from those sessions), and personal accounts on unmanaged devices, which the tenant-restriction header or Enterprise domain capture address. Claude Desktop on 3P has no Anthropic identity; sign-in is the provider's or the organisation's IdP.

original.mechanism: "Enable for your organization" toggle at Organization settings > Cowork; Enterprise custom roles and groups gate Cowork and cloud capability; SSO/SCIM at the organisation; forceLoginOrgUUID in Claude Desktop managed configuration

steps.title: Enable Cowork for the right people
body: Turn on "Enable for your organization" at Organization settings > Cowork and, on Enterprise, grant Cowork and cloud sessions to specific groups through custom roles.

steps.title: Pin the desktop app to your organisation
body: Deploy forceLoginOrgUUID in the com.anthropic.claudefordesktop profile or HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Claude so the app only accepts your organisation's logins.

steps.title: Attach the Cowork architecture evidence
body: Record the architecture overview (a sandbox per cloud session, a mandatory egress proxy, connector tokens never entering the sandbox) and request the desktop security architecture overview it points to on the Trust Center.

steps.title: Collect certifications and the 3P data path

controls.mechanism: Organisation-wide connector tool policy and custom-role grants (Always allow / Needs approval / Blocked per connector or tool) enforced on Anthropic's servers for local and cloud sessions; Claude Code managed settings on the device (permissions.deny / ask, allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly) for local sessions; the "Automatically approve" safety check is a classifier

steps.title: Set the connector tool policy
body: At Organization settings > Connectors set each connector's tools to Always allow, Needs approval or Blocked, and on Enterprise narrow them per role on the Connectors tab under Organization settings > Roles.

steps.title: Deny tools in local sessions from device policy
body: Deploy permissions.deny rules in Claude Code managed settings (MDM or managed-settings.json); a whole-tool Bash or WebFetch deny also stops Cowork's mcp__workspace__bash and mcp__workspace__web_fetch, but allow rules and argument-scoped Bash rules do not carry over.

steps.title: Know which sessions read device policy
body: Local Cowork sessions read the MDM policy and managed-settings file on the device and never fetch server-managed settings; cloud sessions read neither.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: deterministic rules exist, but connector tools are matched by name only (no arguments or target), shell commands in local sessions only as a whole tool, and cloud sessions get the connector policy and console toggles alone. The Automatically approve check is a model, not a policy decision point. Browser actions follow the site allowlist and blocklist at Organization settings > Claude in Chrome. Decisions reach the OTLP export as tool_decision events (source "config"). Claude Desktop on 3P adds disabledBuiltinTools and builtinToolPolicy with argument-scoped rules, of which Cowork's own sandboxed shell honours bare tool names only.

original.mechanism: Managed configuration disabledBuiltinTools (tool or argument-scoped rules such as Read(**/.env)) and builtinToolPolicy (ask / allow per tool); Claude Code managed deny rules apply to Cowork's mcp__workspace__bash and web_fetch tools in local sessions

steps.title: Deny tools by policy on the device
body: Set disabledBuiltinTools (for example Bash, Read(**/.env)) and builtinToolPolicy ask entries in Claude Desktop managed configuration; managed Bash and WebFetch deny rules in Claude Code policy also stop Cowork's workspace tools.

original.note: Cloud sessions do not read device policy; only the console toggles and connector tool settings reach them.

controls.mechanism: Account memory is off by default on Team and Enterprise and turned on at Organization settings > Capabilities (local sessions do not use it); skills and plugins locked to reviewed sources at Organization settings > Plugins & skills > Policy; organisation instructions; desktopSessionCleanupPeriodDays for local transcripts; folder and project instructions have no admin control

steps.title: Decide on memory
body: Leave memory off or turn it on at Organization settings > Capabilities (and grant the Memory capability per role on Enterprise); users can view, edit and delete what is saved.

steps.title: Lock instruction sources to reviewed skills and plugins
body: At Organization settings > Plugins & skills > Policy turn off "User-created skills" and set Publishing to "Requires review", and deliver standing skills in plugins set to Required.

body: Enter them under Organization settings > Organization and access > Organization instructions (up to 3,000 characters, up to an hour to apply); they are prompt-level guidance, not enforcement.

steps.title: Bound local transcripts
body: Set desktopSessionCleanupPeriodDays in Claude Code managed settings on the device; Desktop and Cowork transcripts are otherwise kept at any age.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: memory can be disabled and instruction sources partly locked, but nothing validates what is written. Folder instructions, which Claude "can also update on its own during a session", and project instructions and project memory have no admin control ("owners cannot restrict project creation"). Local conversation history sits outside standard retention and cannot be deleted centrally. Claude Desktop on 3P adds coworkSessionRetentionDays, which deletes idle local tasks but keeps memory.

original.mechanism: desktopSessionCleanupPeriodDays for local transcripts; cloud sessions deletable by users; Compliance API retention follows custom periods; skills and memory managed in Customize

steps.title: Bound local transcripts
body: Set desktopSessionCleanupPeriodDays in managed settings; Desktop and Cowork transcripts are otherwise exempt from cleanupPeriodDays.

original.note: Retention only: cleanup periods and deletion bound how long transcripts and memory persist. Nothing validates memory writes or restores a known-good state.

original.mechanism: organizationInstructions in Claude Desktop managed configuration (MDM + bootstrap; appended to the system prompt in Chat, Cowork and Code, up to 3,000 characters, guidance not enforcement); skills and plugins locked to admin sources (skillCreationEnabled, userPluginMarketplacesEnabled, userPluginUploadsEnabled false; required marketplaces); Enterprise skill scanning; project instructions are user-authored and local

steps.title: Append organisation instructions
body: Set organizationInstructions in the com.anthropic.claudefordesktop profile or HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Claude; the docs state it is guidance the model follows, not an enforced control.

body: Set skillCreationEnabled, userPluginMarketplacesEnabled and userPluginUploadsEnabled false and deliver skills and hooks through allowedPluginMarketplaces or org-plugins/ so only reviewed instructions load.

steps.title: Scan skills and plugins (Enterprise)
body: Turn on skill scanning so skills and plugins are checked for malicious content; classifiers separately flag injections in untrusted content entering context.

original.note: Cowork does not read the Claude Code CLI's ~/.claude directory, and whether a managed claudeMd policy reaches Cowork sessions is not documented; Cowork project instructions live on the device and are not admin-controlled.

controls.mechanism: Shell commands and code run in a dedicated Linux VM isolated by the hypervisor (Apple Virtualization.framework, Hyper-V) with its own egress filtering, syscall restrictions and per-session user isolation, with no user switch to turn it off; allowedWorkspaceFolders limits what the VM mounts; requireCoworkFullVmSandbox (3P) is deprecated. Credential paths: Connector tokens stay on Anthropic's servers and never enter the VM; the VM sees only connected folders, and Claude's own configuration, SSH keys, AWS and Google Cloud credentials and shell profiles stay off-limits inside attached folders; Enterprise-managed connector authorisation issues IdP-scoped grants; Claude in Chrome acts in the user's signed-in browser

steps.title: Restrict which folders Cowork can mount
body: Set allowedWorkspaceFolders in com.anthropic.claudefordesktop or HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Claude (unset is unrestricted; home folders and whole drives can be attached since 4 September 2026).

steps.title: Keep host-side MCP servers off where not needed
body: Set isLocalDevMcpEnabled and isDesktopExtensionEnabled false on managed devices, because plugin-bundled MCP servers and desktop extensions run on the host outside the VM.

steps.title: Fence the folders Cowork can mount
body: Set allowedWorkspaceFolders in com.anthropic.claudefordesktop or HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Claude so home folders and whole drives cannot be attached.

steps.title: Issue connector access through the IdP
body: At Organization settings > Connectors open a connector, select "Set up" next to Managed authorization on the Configuration tab, choose Applied roles and Scopes; deprovisioning in the IdP removes the access.

steps.title: Keep Claude out of signed-in browsers where not needed
body: Turn off Claude in Chrome at Organization settings > Claude in Chrome and use the built-in browser, which does not see users' logins unless they import them.

controls.note: Native: the VM is not a user option, and when it cannot start, shell commands and code execution report "workspace unavailable" instead of running on the host. Outside it: the agent loop itself, file reads and writes in connected folders and web fetches (host-side, gated by an application-layer permission system), plugin MCP servers and desktop extensions (the user's own permissions), the built-in browser and Claude in Chrome, and computer use (Pro and Max beta, no sandbox). Cloud sessions run in Anthropic's per-session sandbox (toolClaudeCoworkCloud). Credential paths: Partial by the rule: the credential-location exclusion is built in (changelog, 4 September 2026) but its enforcement layer is not documented, and file tools on the host are gated by an application-layer permission system rather than the OS. What the agent still acts with: the user's full connector OAuth grant (no on-behalf-of exchange; managed authorisation narrows scopes for the listed connectors, Okta only), the user's Chrome sessions through Claude in Chrome, and plugin MCP servers running with the user's own permissions. On Claude Desktop on 3P, Bedrock and Vertex credential files are written into the session working directory mounted into the VM.

original.mechanism: Local tools run in the hardened Cowork VM with file access scoped to connected folders (allowedWorkspaceFolders) and web fetches to coworkEgressAllowedHosts; cloud sessions run on Anthropic-managed servers; requireCoworkFullVmSandbox is deprecated

steps.title: Restrict which folders Cowork can mount
body: Set allowedWorkspaceFolders in Claude Desktop managed configuration (unset means unrestricted); September 2026 builds let users attach home folders and whole drives otherwise.

steps.title: Note the VM policy gap
body: In a full VM sandbox the device's MDM policy and managed-settings.json are not present, and Cowork never fetches server-managed settings; deliver Cowork controls through Claude Desktop managed configuration instead.

original.note: Inside the boundary: local tools in the Cowork VM, scoped to connected folders. Outside: connector calls, which run through Anthropic's MCP proxy, and cloud sessions, which run on Anthropic-managed servers under Anthropic's isolation.

original.mechanism: Enterprise-managed connector authorisation through the IdP with per-role permission scoping; otherwise Claude acts with the user's own connector and browser sessions

steps.title: Provision connectors centrally with scoped permissions

original.note: Enterprise-managed connector authorisation scopes what a connector may reach per role; otherwise Claude acts with the user's own connector and browser sessions, and files in connected folders are readable in the VM. No on-behalf-of exchange — the connector call carries the user's authority.

controls.mechanism: Connector tool policy per connector and tool (Always allow / Needs approval / Blocked), organisation-wide and per custom role, enforced on Anthropic's servers; "Allow 'Automatically approve' mode" under Organization settings > Capabilities and the built-in browser and Claude in Chrome toggles; Claude Code managed Read / Edit rules reach local sessions

steps.title: Decide on browsers

steps.title: Path-scope local file tools

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: connector tools are allowed or denied by name with no argument or resource scoping, shell commands only as a whole tool, and the "Skip all approvals" mode has no documented console switch on Team. The 3P feature table says neither Automatically approve nor Skip is offered to Claude Enterprise, while the Help Center documents the Automatically approve setting as on by default for Team and Enterprise, so set it explicitly. Device rules never reach cloud sessions. Claude Desktop on 3P adds argument-scoped disabledBuiltinTools and builtinToolPolicy and removes bypass with disableBypassPermissionsMode.

steps.title: Limit connector actions organisation-wide
body: At Organization settings > Connectors restrict each connector's tools (for example search but not send) and keep "Allow 'Always allow' for connector tools" off so each call still prompts.

steps.title: Decide on browsers
body: Toggle the built-in browser at Organization settings > Cowork and Claude in Chrome at Organization settings > Claude in Chrome (both turn on by default on Enterprise starting 10 September 2026 unless already turned off).

controls.mechanism: Standard deployments hold no static keys: the claude.ai sign-in follows the IdP and "Shortened session length", connector OAuth tokens stay on Anthropic's servers (lifetime set by the connector's authorisation server under managed authorisation) and OTLP headers are encrypted at rest; on 3P, inferenceCredentialHelper with inferenceCredentialHelperTtlSec, OAuth tokens in Keychain or DPAPI

steps.title: Bound the sign-in lifetime (Enterprise)
body: Enable "Shortened session length" under Organization settings > Organization and access > Session security.

steps.title: Use a credential helper on third-party deployments
body: Set inferenceCredentialHelper with inferenceCredentialHelperTtlSec instead of a static inferenceAnthropicApiKey or inferenceGatewayApiKey in Claude Desktop on 3P managed configuration.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: custody of the desktop app's own claude.ai sign-in token is not documented for standard deployments (the 3P data-storage page documents Keychain or DPAPI for OAuth tokens and owner-only transient credential files), and on 3P nothing forbids a static managed key. Secrets out of model context: credential locations inside attached folders are excluded, but any other secret file in a connected folder is readable by the model.
