steps.title: Use a credential helper on third-party deployments
body: Set inferenceCredentialHelper (with inferenceCredentialHelperTtlSec) instead of a static inferenceAnthropicApiKey / inferenceGatewayApiKey in managed configuration.

original.note: Connector tokens stay on the platform; files in connected folders, including any .env the user connected, are readable by tools in the VM and so by the model. Credential-helper TTLs on third-party deployments are the only ephemeral issuance.

controls.mechanism: Admission only: Owners alone add connectors (Organization settings > Connectors), the desktop extension allowlist, isLocalDevMcpEnabled and isDesktopExtensionEnabled on the device, curated plugin marketplaces and the admin console's strictKnownMarketplaces / blockedMarketplaces; skill and plugin scanning does not cover MCP servers; 3P can pin plugin content by commit SHA or manifestSha256

steps.title: Admit connectors and extensions by allowlist
body: Keep connectors owner-added at Organization settings > Connectors and turn on Allowlist on its Desktop tab so only approved .mcpb extensions install.

steps.title: Stop host-side MCP servers on managed devices
body: Set isLocalDevMcpEnabled false (plugin-bundled and locally configured servers) and isDesktopExtensionEnabled false in com.anthropic.claudefordesktop or HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Claude.

steps.title: Restrict marketplace sources
body: Set strictKnownMarketplaces and blockedMarketplaces in the admin console's Claude Code managed settings; claude.ai applies them when anyone adds a marketplace from Customize in Cowork.

steps.title: Pin plugin content (Claude Desktop on 3P)
body: In allowedPluginMarketplaces set ref to a 40-character commit SHA, or manifestSha256 with a sha256 per archive, and set isDesktopExtensionSignatureRequired true.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: an allowlist admits servers but pins nothing they serve. Remote connectors' tool definitions are neither hashed nor re-gated when they change; the extension allowlist "does not guard against individuals tampering with local MCP file contents after installation"; skill and plugin scanning excludes MCP servers and hooks. Digest pinning exists only on Claude Desktop on 3P and covers plugin content, not remote servers.

original.mechanism: Org-enabled connectors only (Organization settings > Connectors), desktop extension allowlist, isLocalDevMcpEnabled, managedMcpServers, admin-curated plugin marketplaces (Installed by default / Available / Required / Not available), userPluginMarketplacesEnabled and userPluginUploadsEnabled

steps.title: Curate plugins and marketplaces
body: Configure organisation plugin marketplaces with installation tiers under Organization settings and, on the device, set userPluginMarketplacesEnabled and userPluginUploadsEnabled false to stop users adding sources.

steps.title: Control local MCP and extensions
body: Set isLocalDevMcpEnabled false and turn on the desktop extension allowlist (Organization settings > Connectors > Desktop) so only approved .mcpb extensions load.

original.note: Admission by source: connectors the organisation enables, extensions on the allowlist and plugins from curated marketplaces. Admission is not integrity — nothing pins the tool descriptions a connector returns or detects a changed implementation.

controls.mechanism: Manually approve mode; connector tools capped at "Needs approval" ask before every call and lose "Always allow"; "Allow 'Always allow' for connector tools" (off by default) keeps write-capable connector tools on per-task approval; "Start new tasks in 'Automatically approve' mode" off keeps Manually approve as the default and "Allow 'Automatically approve' mode" off removes the classifier mode (both under Organization settings > Capabilities); permanent file deletion always asks

steps.title: Force approval on named connector tools
body: Set the tools to Needs approval at Organization settings > Connectors or on a custom role's Connectors tab; members then confirm each call and cannot choose Always allow.

steps.title: Keep persistent approval and the classifier mode off
body: Leave "Allow 'Always allow' for connector tools" off under Organization settings > Cowork > Permissions, turn off "Start new tasks in 'Automatically approve' mode" under Organization settings > Capabilities (on by default for Team), and turn off "Allow 'Automatically approve' mode" there for groups whose every task must be approved manually.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: a present person approves connector actions with the tool in front of them and an admin can force that for named tools, but with "Always allow" off write tools are approved per task, not per call, unless capped at Needs approval; "Skip all approvals" has no documented console switch on Team (disableBypassPermissionsMode is a 3P key); shell commands in the VM are not individually approved ("you shouldn't expect to validate every individual command"); and scheduled tasks run with an approval mode chosen at creation and nobody present. The Automatically approve reviewer is a model and never counts as human approval.

original.mechanism: Per-tool approval prompts for connector tools, "Automatically approve" (classifier) and manual modes, browser Manually approve mode, disableBypassPermissionsMode on the device

steps.title: Remove bypass and keep prompts
body: Set disableBypassPermissionsMode true in Claude Desktop managed configuration and leave "Allow 'Always allow' for connector tools" off in the console.

controls.mechanism: OpenTelemetry export set by an Owner at Organization settings > Cowork (OTLP endpoint, protocol, headers) for local and cloud sessions: user_prompt, assistant_response, tool_result (tool_name, decision_type, decision_source, tool_parameters), tool_decision, api_request and api_error events correlated by prompt.id and session.id; Compliance API local (cowork) and remote (cowork_remote) session transcripts on Enterprise

steps.title: Stream Cowork events to the SIEM
body: At Organization settings > Cowork enter the OTLP endpoint, protocol and headers; new sessions export events, and the headers are encrypted at rest on Anthropic's servers.

steps.title: Retrieve transcripts after the fact (Enterprise)
body: Use a Compliance Access Key with read:compliance_user_data on /v1/compliance/apps/sessions/local and /v1/compliance/apps/sessions/remote for prompts, responses, tool calls and results.

controls.note: Native: capture is set by an administrator, carries tool calls and permission decisions to a sink the organisation runs, and no user off switch is documented. Content is a device key on first-party and 3P deployments alike: current Claude Desktop versions send metadata only unless otlpContentCapture adds prompts, responses or tool details, and some older first-party versions send content when it is unset, so deploy it as [] for metadata only. user.email and connected folder paths are always present on standard deployments. Settings load at session start. Integrity and retention are the collector's; audit logs record no Cowork session events, and the Compliance API skips local sessions in HIPAA-ready organisations.

original.mechanism: OpenTelemetry export configured at Admin settings > Cowork (OTLP endpoint, protocol, headers) with user_prompt, tool_result (decision_type, decision_source), api_request and tool_decision events carrying user.email by default (metadata only unless otlpContentCapture is enabled); Compliance API local and remote Cowork session transcripts (Enterprise)

steps.title: Stream Cowork events to the SIEM
body: At Admin settings > Cowork set the OTLP endpoint, protocol and headers; events carry metadata only until otlpContentCapture is enabled for userPrompts, assistantResponses or toolDetails, so turn those on deliberately rather than assuming prompt content is already flowing.

steps.title: Retrieve transcripts after the fact
body: Enterprise Compliance Access Keys with read:compliance_user_data list cowork and cowork_remote sessions and return prompts, responses, tool calls and results.

original.note: Native event emission to the organisation's OTLP endpoint; retention, integrity and tamper evidence are what that endpoint provides. Content is metadata only unless content capture is enabled.

controls.mechanism: "Enable for your organization" off at Organization settings > Cowork, the Claude Cowork capability removed from a custom role (up to 15 minutes), secureVmFeaturesEnabled false on managed devices; Inference hooks can deny an account's next request (Enterprise); no administrator stop of a running session is documented

steps.title: Switch Cowork off
body: Turn off "Enable for your organization" at Organization settings > Cowork, or remove the Claude Cowork capability from the member's custom role (role changes take up to 15 minutes).

steps.title: Remove Cowork from managed devices
body: Set secureVmFeaturesEnabled false in com.anthropic.claudefordesktop or HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Claude.

steps.title: Refuse inference for an account (Enterprise)
body: With Inference hooks enforcing, have your AI security server deny that user's requests; turning enforcement on or off reaches every Anthropic server in about a minute.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: the console blocks new use, but whether a running session stops is not documented (delay not documented for the organisation toggle; up to 15 minutes for role changes), network changes apply only to new sessions, and an Inference hooks deny refuses the next request without terminating the session or its scheduled runs. Cloud sessions and scheduled tasks keep running with every device offline, so an EDR process kill, the external complement, reaches only local sessions, and host EDR cannot see inside the VM. Pausing another member's scheduled task is not an admin action.

steps.title: Block personal accounts on the corporate network
body: Inject anthropic-allowed-org-ids at the TLS-inspecting proxy for claude.ai, api.anthropic.com, claude.com and anthropic.com.

steps.title: Block personal-account Cowork on the corporate network
body: Inject anthropic-allowed-org-ids at the TLS-inspecting proxy for claude.ai and api.anthropic.com.

body: Review Organization settings > Plugins & skills > Inventory, and approve submissions on its Requests tab with Publishing set to "Requires review".

body: Query /v1/compliance/apps/sessions/remote; agent-owned sessions carry agent_id and started_by_user for scheduled tasks.

settings.recommended: 7 days
settings.why: The desktop sign-in that Cowork acts with expires weekly, so a stolen or stale session meets the IdP's MFA again.

settings.name: User provisioning (SCIM)
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Organization and access › User provisioning
settings.recommended: SCIM, driven by the IdP group that grants Claude
settings.why: Removing someone in the IdP removes their seat, so a leaver's Cowork access ends with their account rather than with a ticket.

settings.name: Restrict organization creation
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Organization and access › Security
settings.recommended: On
settings.why: Stops staff creating personal or side Claude organisations on your verified domains, which no admin can see.

settings.name: Migrate accounts using your domain
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Organization and access › Security
settings.recommended: On, after reviewing the personal accounts listed on your domain
settings.why: No Free, Pro or Max account can exist on the verified domain, so staff can't run Cowork on a personal plan with work files; it can't be reversed.

settings.name: forceLoginOrgUUID
settings.where: Claude Desktop policy (com.anthropic.claudefordesktop / HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Claude) → forceLoginOrgUUID
settings.recommended: Your organisation's UUID
settings.why: On managed devices Claude Desktop refuses a login to any other organisation, personal accounts included.

settings.name: Tenant Restrictions (anthropic-allowed-org-ids)
settings.where: Corporate TLS-inspecting proxy → anthropic-allowed-org-ids header on Claude traffic
settings.recommended: Your organisation's UUID, injected for every managed device
settings.why: Personal and other organisations' Claude accounts can't sign in from the corporate network, on any device or browser.

settings.name: Enable for your organization
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Cowork
settings.recommended: On, scoped by custom role to the groups rolled out
settings.why: The organisation-wide off switch for Cowork; on Enterprise the role's Cowork capability limits who gets it.

settings.name: secureVmFeaturesEnabled
settings.where: Claude Desktop policy → secureVmFeaturesEnabled
settings.recommended: true; false on devices that must not run Cowork
settings.why: The per-device switch that removes Cowork from Claude Desktop, independent of the console.

settings.name: allowedWorkspaceFolders
settings.where: Claude Desktop policy → allowedWorkspaceFolders
settings.recommended: The folders staff work in (for example ~/Documents and ~/Desktop), not home folders or whole drives
settings.why: Cowork can mount only the listed paths, so the VM and the model never see the rest of the disk.

settings.name: desktopSessionCleanupPeriodDays
settings.where: Claude Code managed settings on the device → desktopSessionCleanupPeriodDays
settings.why: Local Cowork transcripts sit on the device outside standard retention and admins can't delete them; this bounds how long client material stays there.

settings.name: Inference hooks
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Data and privacy › Inference hooks
settings.recommended: On, connected to your DLP or AI-security service, enforcing after a monitor-only period
settings.why: Each Cowork request, tool results and file text included, is checked by your own service before inference, so secrets and injected content can be stopped centrally.

settings.name: Organization-wide tool policy
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Connectors › connector › tool (Always allow / Needs approval / Blocked)
settings.recommended: Write and send tools set to Needs approval; tools no one uses Blocked
settings.why: The ceiling no role or member can widen — Needs approval removes Always allow, Blocked hides the tool from Claude.

settings.name: Allow "Always allow" for connector tools
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Cowork › Permissions
settings.recommended: Off
settings.why: Members approve write-capable connector tools in every task instead of saving a standing approval.

settings.name: Allow "Automatically approve" mode
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Capabilities
settings.recommended: On — members may switch to it; a safety check reviews each action
settings.why: Keeps the mode for long tasks while connector Needs approval caps still prompt; regulated teams turn it off so every task runs on Manually approve.

settings.name: Start new tasks in "Automatically approve" mode
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Capabilities
settings.default: On for Team, off for Enterprise
settings.recommended: Off
settings.why: Every new task starts on Manually approve, so skipping prompts is a choice the member makes for that task.

settings.name: Managed authorization
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Connectors › connector › Configuration
settings.default: Not set up (each member authorises with their own OAuth grant)
settings.recommended: Set up for every supported connector, with the Scopes your roles need
settings.why: The IdP issues and revokes connector access by group, so scopes are chosen centrally and de-provisioning ends it.

settings.name: isLocalDevMcpEnabled
settings.where: Claude Desktop policy → isLocalDevMcpEnabled
settings.recommended: false
settings.why: Locally configured and plugin-bundled MCP servers run on the host with the user's permissions, outside the VM and any allowlist; it also stops Claude in Chrome driving the browser from the desktop app.

settings.name: Allowlist (desktop extensions)
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Connectors › Desktop
settings.default: Off (every extension in the registry installable)
settings.recommended: On, with only approved extensions added; leave isDesktopExtensionEnabled unset so the list populates
settings.why: Desktop extensions are blocked by default and members install only the .mcpb servers you list.

settings.name: strictKnownMarketplaces
settings.where: Organization settings › Claude Code › Managed settings → strictKnownMarketplaces
settings.recommended: Your organisation's marketplace(s) only
settings.why: claude.ai applies the list itself when anyone adds a marketplace from Customize in Cowork, so plugins come only from sources you curate.

settings.name: Publishing
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Plugins & skills › Policy
settings.default: Open on Team; Requires review on Enterprise (moving to Open where scanning is on)
settings.recommended: Requires review
settings.why: An Owner approves every skill and plugin, and each new version, before it reaches colleagues' sessions; set it explicitly so the default change doesn't apply.

settings.name: Skill and plugin security scanning
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Plugins & skills › Policy
settings.default: On for Enterprise organisations that hadn't chosen before 2 October 2026
settings.recommended: On
settings.why: Every skill and plugin uploaded or edited is scanned before it is installed, and a failing one is blocked.

settings.name: Blocklist
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Claude in Chrome
settings.recommended: Banking and payment sites, HR and payroll systems, and your admin consoles
settings.why: Claude can't navigate to or act on those sites in Claude in Chrome or the Cowork built-in browser, where it works with the user's sign-ins.

settings.name: Allow network egress
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Capabilities › Code execution and file creation
settings.default: Package managers only (off for new Enterprise organisations)
settings.recommended: Package managers and specific domains — your package mirror and the hosts tasks need
settings.why: Shell commands in the Cowork VM reach only the listed hosts; web fetch, web search and connectors are outside this policy.

settings.name: OTLP endpoint
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Cowork (OTLP endpoint, protocol, headers)
settings.recommended: Your OpenTelemetry collector, forwarding to the SIEM
settings.why: Tool calls, file access and approval decisions from every new session land in the SIEM, keyed by user and session.

settings.name: otlpContentCapture
settings.where: Claude Desktop policy → otlpContentCapture
settings.default: Unset (metadata only on current versions; some older versions send content)
settings.recommended: [] — metadata only
settings.why: Events carry tool decisions without prompt, response or tool-input text, keeping client material out of the SIEM on every Desktop version.

settings.name: Compliance API (session transcripts)
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › API, then a Compliance Access Key with read:compliance_user_data
settings.recommended: On, pulled into your eDiscovery or SIEM
settings.why: Local Cowork transcripts, which otherwise exist only on the laptop, are retrievable centrally after the fact.

settings.name: disableAutoUpdates
settings.where: Claude Desktop policy → disableAutoUpdates, autoUpdaterEnforcementHours
settings.recommended: false, unless MDM pins and ships versions itself / 72
settings.why: Security fixes to Claude Desktop and the Cowork VM reach every device, restarting it within three days of a prepared update.

tools.name: Claude Cowork in the cloud

variants.name: Cowork on web, mobile and the Chrome side panel (sessions on Anthropic servers)
The same cloud session started from Claude Desktop with "Cloud" selected; the local client is toolClaudeCowork
Scheduled tasks
variants.note: Unattended runs on the same cloud runtime, owned by the person who scheduled them. Dispatch, listed here before 2026-09-25, runs its tasks on the desktop and belongs to the desktop entity.

summary: The Cowork engine run on Anthropic's servers instead of the device: the agent loop and code execution run in a per-session ephemeral sandbox, sessions and files are saved to the account and keep working with every device offline, and the session can only touch local folders while the desktop app on that device is open, over an Anthropic-brokered connection. Every byte leaving the sandbox passes a mandatory proxy the sandbox cannot reconfigure; the network policy is the organisation's existing network-access setting ("no access" by default on Enterprise). Connector tokens never enter the sandbox — calls are made server-side.

Modelled as a vendor-hosted agent session because the loop has left the machine: the doors are the web and mobile apps, the Chrome side panel, the desktop app and the scheduler, and the admin plane is the claude.ai console only — device managed configuration (allowedWorkspaceFolders, coworkEgressAllowedHosts, disabledBuiltinTools) reaches local sessions and not these. Organisation settings > Cowork carries "Run Cowork in the cloud" (Team on by default; Enterprise off by default and granted through custom roles), "Allow 'Always allow' for connector tools" and the OTLP collector; Organization settings > Capabilities carries the network-access policy, the two "Automatically approve" settings, "Require trusted devices" and the Scheduled tasks (Was Routines) toggle; the Compliance API captures remote Cowork sessions, including agent-owned scheduled runs. Cowork is not covered by zero data retention.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Web and mobile in beta for Pro, Max and Team, and for Enterprise where an owner or a custom role enables it; the desktop Cloud option follows the same setting.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Anthropic API only. Cloud sessions run on Anthropic infrastructure and are not available when Claude Desktop is configured for Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry or a gateway.

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: Prompts, connector data, browser page content and the session's files live in the account; a device's local folders are reachable only while the desktop app is open on it, through the brokered connection.

facts.label: Retention & training
facts.value: Cloud sessions are saved to the account (remote transcripts 6 years unless deleted) and captured by the Compliance API; Cowork is not covered by ZDR. Commercial terms: no training.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: claude.com/docs/cowork plus the Help Center architecture overview and Team/Enterprise admin article

items.title: Enable cloud sessions per role, not per organisation
body: Organization settings > Cowork > "Run Cowork in the cloud" is off by default on Enterprise; grant it through custom roles to the groups that need unattended or device-independent sessions, and leave "Enable for your organization" scoped the same way.

links.title: Use Claude Cowork on Team and Enterprise plans

items.title: Set the network-access policy before the first session
body: Cloud sandboxes inherit the organisation's network-access setting under Organization settings > Capabilities; the Enterprise default is no access. Device keys such as coworkEgressAllowedHosts do not reach cloud sessions.

riskNotes.note: Documents, connector results and browser pages enter an unattended session as instruction; the network-access policy and the connector approval toggles are the containment, and "Automatically approve" removes the per-tool prompt.
Scheduled tasks run with no device and no person present; the Compliance API's list of remote sessions, including agent-owned scheduled runs, is the inventory.
Sessions and their files are saved to the account and retained for years unless deleted; the session can reach a device's folders whenever the desktop app is open there.

controls.mechanism: "Run Cowork in the cloud" at Organization settings > Cowork plus the "Cowork in the cloud" custom-role capability on Enterprise; Scheduled tasks (Was Routines) at Organization settings > Capabilities > Remote sessions and as a role capability; only the signed-in account owner starts or steers a session; "Require trusted devices" for reaching devices from cloud sessions; the built-in browser and Claude in Chrome toggles govern the reach-back into devices

steps.title: Gate cloud sessions by role
body: On Enterprise turn on "Run Cowork in the cloud" at Organization settings > Cowork and grant the Cowork in the cloud capability to groups through custom roles; on Team it is on by default, so turn it off there deliberately.

steps.title: Keep unattended runs owned
body: Turn the Scheduled tasks (Was Routines) toggle off at Organization settings > Capabilities > Remote sessions, or on Enterprise grant the Scheduled tasks capability only to the roles that own unattended runs; turning it off also stops Cowork's cloud scheduled tasks.

steps.title: Require trusted devices for cloud sessions
body: Turn on "Require trusted devices" at Organization settings > Capabilities > Remote sessions; members then need an enrolled device and a sign-in under 18 hours old, and it applies to every cloud session in the organisation.

steps.title: Decide the reach-back into devices
body: Toggle the built-in browser at Organization settings > Cowork and Claude in Chrome at Organization settings > Claude in Chrome.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: enablement is per role on Enterprise (organisation-wide only on Team) and there is no repository, bot or channel trigger, but the trigger condition is fixed by the vendor (the account owner, from any of their devices), and scheduled tasks, which start sessions with nobody present, are switched on or off per organisation or per role, not per task or trigger. Sessions cannot be shared with other members.

original.mechanism: "Run Cowork in the cloud" per custom role; trusted-device enrolment; SSO at the account layer

steps.title: Gate cloud sessions by role
body: On Enterprise the cloud toggle is off by default and granted through custom roles; Team turns it on by default, so turn it off there deliberately.

controls.mechanism: An isolated, temporary sandbox per session on Anthropic-managed infrastructure, created when the session starts and destroyed when it ends, sharing no state with other sessions or organisations and unable to reach private, internal, link-local or cloud-metadata addresses; always on

steps.title: Record the isolation claim
body: The architecture overview states one sandbox per session, destroyed at the end, with no state shared across sessions or organisations; there is no setting to change.

controls.note: Native by the rule: one sandbox per session, reclaimed after it, documented by the vendor, with assurance through assessment rather than a setting. Outside it: the reach-back to a member's device (local files, the built-in browser and Claude in Chrome run there, only while the desktop app is online and only for connected folders), connector calls and web fetch or web search, which run on Anthropic's servers.

original.mechanism: Per-session ephemeral sandbox on Anthropic servers; always on, no toggle
original.note: Vendor-internal isolation with no administrator setting; the architecture overview is the claim, assurance is the evidence.

steps.title: Read the architecture overview
body: Each cloud session runs in its own ephemeral sandbox with no access to the organisation's network by default; local folders are reachable only through the desktop app's brokered connection.

controls.mechanism: The organisation's network-access policy (Organization settings > Capabilities, Code execution and file creation, "Allow network egress") enforced by a mandatory proxy outside the sandbox that it cannot reconfigure or bypass; no network access by default on Enterprise; applied when a session is created

steps.title: Choose the network-access level
body: At Organization settings > Capabilities keep "Allow network egress" off or choose package managers and specific domains, listing only the hosts sessions need.

steps.title: Confirm cloud sessions inherit it
body: Cloud sessions use the same network-access setting as local Cowork and chat, enforced by the mandatory egress proxy.

controls.note: Native by the rule: an admin-authored allowlist members cannot change, enforced around the sandbox. The setup and agent phases are not separated, every allowlist preset keeps public package managers, and changes reach new sessions only. Outside it: connector calls and web fetch or web search (server side; web search can be turned off at Organization settings > Capabilities), the built-in browser and Claude in Chrome on the member's device, and the inference API. Device egress keys do not apply.

original.mechanism: Organisation network-access policy enforced by a mandatory sandbox proxy
original.note: The policy is set at Organization settings > Capabilities and applies to every cloud session; device egress keys do not apply.

steps.title: Choose the network-access level
body: Enterprise defaults to no access; widen to an allowlist only for the groups whose sessions need the web.

controls.mechanism: Connector authorisation tokens never enter the sandbox and connector calls are made on the server side; the sandbox holds only session-scoped tokens that expire within hours; there is no repository credential

steps.title: Record the credential boundary
body: The architecture overview states the sandbox holds only session-scoped tokens that expire within hours and that connector tokens never enter it; nothing is configured.

steps.title: Narrow what connector grants reach
body: At Organization settings > Connectors set up Managed authorization for supported connectors with chosen Scopes and Applied roles, so the IdP issues and revokes the grant.

controls.note: Native by the rule: the credentials that matter stay outside the sandbox and what is inside is session-scoped and short-lived. What remains in the member's authority: connector calls carry the member's full grant (no on-behalf-of exchange; managed authorisation narrows scopes for the listed connectors, Okta only), a session that reaches the member's desktop acts in their Chrome sessions through Claude in Chrome, and files saved to the account, secrets included, are readable by the model.

original.mechanism: Connector tokens held server-side; never present in the sandbox

steps.title: Confirm connector calls are server-side
body: The architecture overview states connector tokens never enter sandboxes and calls are made server-side; no per-session credential is exposed to the model.

controls.mechanism: Manually approve mode and connector tools capped at "Needs approval" ask the owner before each call; "Allow 'Always allow' for connector tools" (off by default) at Organization settings > Cowork > Permissions; "Allow 'Automatically approve' mode" and "Start new tasks in 'Automatically approve' mode" at Organization settings > Capabilities

steps.title: Force approval on named connector tools
body: Set the tools to Needs approval at Organization settings > Connectors or on a custom role's Connectors tab; members confirm each call and lose the Always allow option.

steps.title: Keep persistent approval and the classifier mode off
body: Leave "Allow 'Always allow' for connector tools" off under Organization settings > Cowork > Permissions, turn off "Start new tasks in 'Automatically approve' mode" under Organization settings > Capabilities, and turn off "Allow 'Automatically approve' mode" there for groups whose every task must be approved manually.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: the owner approves connector calls before they run and an admin can force that for named tools, but scheduled tasks run with an approval mode chosen at creation and nobody present (runs are reviewed afterwards on the Scheduled page), code in the sandbox is not approved per command, "Skip all approvals" has no documented console switch on Team, and the Automatically approve reviewer is a model that never counts. There is no merge-style gate on output.

original.mechanism: "Automatically approve" and "Always allow for connector tools" toggles
original.note: The toggles govern per-tool prompts in attended sessions; Dispatch and scheduled runs have no prompt to answer, and there is no merge-style gate on their output.

steps.title: Keep connector approvals in the loop
body: Leave "Allow 'Always allow' for connector tools" off and consider turning off "Allow 'Automatically approve' mode" for sensitive groups.

controls.mechanism: Connector tool policy per tool (Always allow / Needs approval / Blocked), organisation-wide and per custom role, enforced on Anthropic's servers for cloud sessions; the network-access level; code execution, web search, built-in browser and Claude in Chrome toggles; the Automatically approve toggle

steps.title: Scope connector tools by role
body: Set each tool's ceiling at Organization settings > Connectors and narrow it per group on the Connectors tab of each custom role under Organization settings > Roles (Enterprise).

steps.title: Switch off built-in tools a session does not need
body: Turn off web search at Organization settings > Capabilities and the built-in browser at Organization settings > Cowork.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: tools are allowed or denied by name with no argument or resource scoping, "Skip all approvals" has no documented console switch on Team, and device managed settings never reach cloud sessions. No repository token exists, so the branch and repository scoping half of the pin does not apply.

original.mechanism: Connector enablement per organisation; curated plugin marketplaces; built-in browser toggle

steps.title: Curate what a cloud session may call
body: Connectors and plugin marketplaces are admitted at Organization settings > Cowork; the built-in browser can be disabled for the organisation.

controls.mechanism: The Compliance API remote session list, with agent-owned scheduled runs (agent_id, started_by_user); Organization settings > Plugins & skills > Inventory for distributed skills and plugins; owner-added connectors

steps.title: Export the session list
body: Query /v1/compliance/apps/sessions/remote; agent-owned sessions carry agent_id and started_by_user.

steps.title: Review the plugin and skill inventory
body: Organization settings > Plugins & skills > Inventory lists source, version, capabilities, audience and 30-day use for each governed item.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: there is no admin view of members' scheduled tasks and no way to deny one short of the organisation or role Scheduled tasks switch, runs appear only after they happen, and each task is owned by whoever created it; the inventory covers what the organisation distributes, not what members build for themselves.

original.mechanism: Compliance API listing of remote Cowork sessions, including scheduled runs
original.note: A list of sessions, not a registry with owners and approval; scheduled tasks are owned by whoever created them.

steps.title: Export the session list
body: Remote Cowork sessions, including agent-owned scheduled runs, are available through the Compliance API sessions endpoint.

controls.mechanism: Account memory shared with chat, off by default on Team and Enterprise (Organization settings > Capabilities and the Memory role capability); project memory scoped to each project; sessions and files saved to the account; organisation instructions; admin-curated skills and plugins

steps.title: Decide on memory
body: Leave memory off or turn it on at Organization settings > Capabilities (per role with the Memory capability on Enterprise); members can view, edit and delete entries.

steps.title: Lock instruction sources to reviewed skills and plugins
body: At Organization settings > Plugins & skills > Policy turn off "User-created skills" and set Publishing to "Requires review".

steps.title: Set the retention decision
body: Remote transcripts are kept 6 years unless the member deletes the session, and the Compliance API cannot delete them, so decide the deletion process before enabling cloud sessions.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: memory can be kept off and instruction sources partly locked, but memory writes are not validated (members review and edit their own), project instructions and project memory have no admin control, and projects can be shared under the Share projects capability. Sessions cannot be shared. A deleted task leaves history immediately and backend storage within 30 days.

original.mechanism: Account-level session and file retention; deletion by the user or through the Compliance API
original.note: Retention is administered, not scoped; what a later session may read from an earlier one is not a setting.

steps.title: Set the retention decision
body: Remote transcripts are retained for 6 years unless deleted; decide the deletion policy before enabling cloud sessions.

controls.mechanism: "Run Cowork in the cloud" or "Enable for your organization" off at Organization settings > Cowork, the Cowork in the cloud capability removed from a role (up to 15 minutes), an Inference hooks deny for an account (Enterprise, beta); the Scheduled tasks (Was Routines) toggle or role capability; the owner stops, pauses or deletes their own tasks

steps.title: Disable cloud sessions
body: Turn off "Run Cowork in the cloud", or "Enable for your organization" for the whole product, at Organization settings > Cowork.

steps.title: Refuse inference for an account (Enterprise)
body: With Inference hooks enforcing, have your AI security server deny that user's requests; turning enforcement on or off reaches every Anthropic server in about a minute.

steps.title: Stop every scheduled task
body: Turn off Scheduled tasks (Was Routines) at Organization settings > Capabilities > Remote sessions, or the Scheduled tasks capability on a role; turning it off also turns off Cowork's cloud scheduled tasks.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: whether switching cloud sessions off stops a running session is not documented (delay not documented; role changes take up to 15 minutes; network changes reach new sessions only). The Scheduled tasks switch stops all scheduled tasks at once, but only the owner can stop one task or pause and delete a single scheduled one. An Inference hooks deny refuses the next request without terminating the session or cancelling queued runs, and setting a group's pooled budget to $0 freezes its usage on usage-based Enterprise. No EDR complement exists, because the sessions run off every endpoint.

original.mechanism: Turning off "Run Cowork in the cloud" or the organisation toggle
original.note: Prevents new cloud sessions; the delay before a running Dispatch or scheduled task stops is not documented.

steps.title: Disable cloud sessions
body: Organization settings > Cowork > "Run Cowork in the cloud" off, or "Enable for your organization" off for the whole product.

controls.mechanism: Compliance API remote session endpoints (product_surface cowork_remote) return prompts, responses, tool calls and tool results; the OTLP export set at Organization settings > Cowork covers cloud sessions with events correlated by prompt.id and session.id

steps.title: Pull cloud-session transcripts (Enterprise)
body: Use a Compliance Access Key with read:compliance_user_data on /v1/compliance/apps/sessions/remote and its messages endpoint.

steps.title: Stream session events to your collector
body: At Organization settings > Cowork enter the OTLP endpoint, protocol and headers; the stream covers cloud sessions as well as local ones.

controls.note: Native by the rule: programmatic export covering this hosted surface. The OTLP push is the copy the session cannot alter; the Compliance API pull is not, because a member's deletion removes a remote session from it. Tool inputs and results are truncated to 10,000 bytes by default, thinking is left out of the OTLP response event, the OTLP prompt-content default is documented both ways, and Team plans get OTLP only (the Compliance API is Enterprise).

original.mechanism: Compliance API capture of cloud sessions; OTLP session events to the organisation's collector

steps.title: Stream session events
body: Configure the OTLP collector under Organization settings > Cowork; metadata by default, content capture opt-in.

controls.mechanism: Spend limits at Organization settings > Usage (organisation, group per-user, seat tier and individual) and pooled monthly group budgets (Enterprise, beta) that pause every member when exhausted; Team usage-credit spend limits

steps.title: Set group spend limits (Enterprise)
body: At Organization settings > Usage open the "By group/tier" tab, choose "Edit limits" on a group and set a Member limit; individual limits override group limits.

steps.title: Cap a team with a pooled budget (Enterprise, beta)
body: In the same "Edit limits" dialog set a Pooled monthly budget; when it runs out usage pauses for every member of the group, and $0 freezes the group.

steps.title: Cap usage credits (Team and seat-based Enterprise)
body: At Organization settings > Usage set the organisation-wide monthly spend limit and per-user limits on usage credits.

controls.note: Native by the rule: admin-set spend caps stop use when exhausted ("usage can go slightly over a limit before it pauses"). Not offered: a per-session or per-task budget, session duration or concurrency limits, or a cap on scheduled tasks; the pool is shared with chat and Claude Code, seat usage limits are vendor-fixed, and pooled budgets cannot be managed through the Admin API.

controls.mechanism: Anthropic's content classifiers scan untrusted content entering context (no administrator setting); Inference hooks (Enterprise) hold each governed prompt and returned tool result, connector calls included, for an allow or deny verdict from the organisation's AI security server

steps.title: Put an inspector on returned tool content (Enterprise)
body: At Organization settings > Data and privacy > Inference hooks turn on "Allow for your organization", register your AI security server, choose Failure handling and turn on "Enforce verdicts".

steps.title: Know what the vendor screening covers
body: Content classifiers scan all untrusted content entering Claude's context and flag potential injections; there is no setting or event export for them.

controls.note: Partial on the rule applied to every vendor: vendor-internal screening that is not admin-configurable, and an inline hook that is an attach point until the organisation's server classifies. Hook verdicts are allow or deny only (no strip or quarantine) and system prompts and tool definitions are never sent. Connector content returning through the organisation's AI gateway on the tunnel path can be classified there as well.

controls.mechanism: The Anthropic Trust Center (SOC 2 Type 2 and CSA STAR L2 report, ISO 27001 and ISO 42001 certificates, 2025 annual penetration testing reports, SIG Lite and CAIQ questionnaires, Cowork security documents) and the Help Center architecture overview of cloud sessions feed the organisation's TPRM platform

evidence.title: Anthropic Trust Center (compliance scope table and resources, read 2026-09-25)
Claude Cowork architecture overview (cloud session architecture)
What Certifications has Anthropic obtained?

controls.note: External by the rule applied to every vendor: the TPRM platform holds the questionnaire, evidence expiry and reassessment trigger. The Trust Center lists SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001:2022, ISO/IEC 42001:2023, HIPAA and CSA STAR for Claude Enterprise and Claude Team; its Cowork document is the desktop security architecture, so request the cloud-sandbox, egress-proxy and tenant-isolation claims explicitly. Reassess on the moving defaults: cloud sessions on by default for Team and the default execution place where allowed, Cowork not covered by zero data retention, a beta surface.

controls.mechanism: Session-scoped sandbox tokens that expire within hours; connector tokens held server-side and, under managed authorisation, issued and revoked by the IdP; MCP tunnels (Enterprise research preview) with a rotatable, revocable tunnel token and a CA the organisation holds; no store for secrets a task needs

steps.title: Rotate and revoke the tunnel credentials
body: Revoke the Tunnels API key at Organization settings > Tunnels > Tunnels API after setup, rotate the tunnel token by incrementing tunnel.tokenVersion (Helm) or --token-version (Compose), and archive the tunnel to invalidate its token.

steps.title: Issue connector credentials through the IdP
body: Set up Managed authorization on supported connectors at Organization settings > Connectors so the IdP sets token lifetime and deprovisioning revokes access.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: a vendor tunnel exists and its credentials are scoped, rotatable and revocable (outbound-only cloudflared plus proxy, inner TLS with a CA generated in your environment, a server certificate valid 90 days and renewed locally, rotation that does not sever established connections), and sandbox tokens are short-lived, but Cowork offers no encrypted, write-only store for secrets a task needs, so anything a member pastes or saves to the account is readable by the model. Tunnels are an Enterprise research preview by request, with Cloudflare as subprocessor.

settings.name: Require SSO for Claude
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Organization and access › Authentication
settings.recommended: On, with MFA enforced on the Claude app in your IdP
settings.why: Every claude.ai login that starts or steers a cloud session goes through the corporate IdP and its MFA.

settings.name: Shortened session length
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Organization and access › Session security
settings.default: Not enabled (sign-in kept while the user stays active)
settings.recommended: 7 days
settings.why: The web and mobile sign-ins that steer cloud sessions expire weekly, so a stolen browser session meets the IdP's MFA again.

settings.name: User provisioning (SCIM)
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Organization and access › User provisioning
settings.recommended: SCIM, driven by the IdP group that grants Claude
settings.why: Removing someone in the IdP removes their seat, so a leaver's cloud sessions and scheduled tasks lose their owner's access with the account.

settings.name: Restrict organization creation
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Organization and access › Security
settings.recommended: On
settings.why: Stops staff creating side Claude organisations on your domains whose cloud sessions no admin can see or switch off.

settings.name: Run Cowork in the cloud
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Cowork
settings.default: On for Team, off for Enterprise
settings.recommended: On, once the network policy and connector tool policy are set
settings.why: The organisation-wide switch for sessions on Anthropic's servers; off, members' Cowork runs only on their own devices.

settings.name: Cowork in the cloud (custom role capability)
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Roles › role › Capabilities
settings.recommended: Granted only to the groups that need device-independent or scheduled work
settings.why: On Enterprise the organisation toggle only makes cloud sessions possible; the role grant decides who runs them, following the IdP group.

settings.name: Scheduled tasks (Was Routines)
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Capabilities › Remote sessions (on Enterprise also the role's Remote sessions capability)
settings.recommended: On only for the roles that own unattended runs; off for everyone else
settings.why: Scheduled tasks run with nobody present on the approval mode chosen at creation; turning the capability off also turns off Cowork's cloud scheduled tasks. On Team the toggle is organisation-wide.

settings.name: Require trusted devices
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Capabilities › Remote sessions
settings.recommended: On
settings.why: Reaching back into a member's computer from a cloud session needs an enrolled device and a sign-in under 18 hours old, not just a signed-in account.

settings.name: Allow network egress
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Capabilities › Code execution and file creation
settings.default: Off for new Enterprise organisations; package managers only otherwise
settings.recommended: Package managers and specific domains — your package mirror and the hosts tasks need
settings.why: The mandatory proxy outside the sandbox holds every session to that list; connectors, web fetch and web search run server-side and are outside it.

settings.name: Organization-wide tool policy
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Connectors › connector › tool (Always allow / Needs approval / Blocked)
settings.recommended: Write and send tools set to Needs approval; tools no one uses Blocked
settings.why: The ceiling no role or member can widen — Needs approval removes Always allow, Blocked hides the tool from Claude.

settings.name: Allow "Always allow" for connector tools
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Cowork › Permissions
settings.recommended: Off
settings.why: Members approve write-capable connector tools in every task instead of saving a standing approval a later unattended run inherits.

settings.name: Allow "Automatically approve" mode
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Capabilities
settings.recommended: On — members may switch to it; a safety check reviews each action
settings.why: Keeps the mode for long tasks while connector Needs approval caps still prompt; regulated teams turn it off so every task runs on Manually approve.

settings.name: Start new tasks in "Automatically approve" mode
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Capabilities
settings.default: On for Team, off for Enterprise
settings.recommended: Off
settings.why: Every new task starts on Manually approve, so skipping prompts is a choice the member makes for that task.

settings.name: Managed authorization
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Connectors › connector › Configuration
settings.default: Not set up (each member authorises with their own OAuth grant)
settings.recommended: Set up for every supported connector, with the Scopes your roles need
settings.why: Connector calls run server-side on a grant the IdP issues and revokes by group, so scopes are chosen centrally and de-provisioning ends it.

settings.name: Blocklist
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Claude in Chrome
settings.recommended: Banking and payment sites, HR and payroll systems, and your admin consoles
settings.why: A cloud session that drives a member's Chrome or built-in browser can't navigate to or act on those sites with the member's sign-ins.

settings.name: Memory
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Capabilities
settings.default: Off (each member opts in once an Owner allows it)
settings.recommended: Off; projects keep their own context
settings.why: Account memory is shared between chat and cloud Cowork, so one engagement's details could resurface in another client's task; teams that want it turn it on per role.

settings.name: Publishing
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Plugins & skills › Policy
settings.default: Open on Team; Requires review on Enterprise (moving to Open where scanning is on)
settings.recommended: Requires review
settings.why: An Owner approves every skill and plugin, and each new version, before it reaches colleagues' cloud sessions; set it explicitly so the default change doesn't apply.

settings.name: Inference hooks
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Data and privacy › Inference hooks
settings.recommended: On, connected to your DLP or AI-security service, enforcing after a monitor-only period
settings.why: Each request from a cloud session, connector results included, is checked by your own service before inference, so injected content and secrets can be stopped centrally.

settings.name: Member limit
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Usage › By group/tier › Edit limits
settings.recommended: A monthly per-member limit on each group that runs Cowork
settings.why: A runaway task or scheduled run stops when its owner's limit is spent, rather than drawing on the organisation's whole pool.

settings.name: OTLP endpoint
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Cowork (OTLP endpoint, protocol, headers)
settings.recommended: Your OpenTelemetry collector, forwarding to the SIEM
settings.why: Tool calls and approval decisions from cloud sessions are pushed to a store the session can't alter; cloud scheduled tasks send metadata only.

settings.name: Compliance API (session transcripts)
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › API, then a Compliance Access Key with read:compliance_user_data
settings.recommended: On, pulled into your eDiscovery or SIEM
settings.why: Remote Cowork transcripts, scheduled runs included, are retrievable centrally — before a member deletes the session.
