tools.name: Claude (claude.ai)

variants.name: claude.ai in the browser
The same synced chats in Claude Desktop and the iOS / Android apps
variants.note: Standard Claude Desktop loads the claude.ai web application and stores conversations on Anthropic's backend, and connectors added on the web or desktop follow the account to the mobile apps, so as a chat client each app is this product. What the desktop app runs or reaches on the device is toolClaudeDesktop.

summary: Anthropic's chat product, claude.ai in the browser. Chat runs on the Anthropic API under the user's organisation login; connectors (MCP) reach Google Drive, Microsoft 365, GitHub, Slack and custom remote servers through mcp-proxy.anthropic.com. Prompts, uploads and connector results go to Anthropic; Team and Enterprise data is not used for training and follows the organisation's retention setting (indefinite by default until a custom period is set). Claude Desktop and the mobile apps show the same synced chats; the desktop app's local reach (local MCP servers, desktop extensions, device policy) is the endpoint record toolClaudeDesktop.

Team and Enterprise administration is in the claude.ai console: SSO (SAML/OIDC via WorkOS) with domain verification and "Require SSO for Claude", JIT or SCIM provisioning with group-to-role mapping, custom roles and groups gating Claude Code, Cowork, Chrome, connectors, Claude Tag and models, connector enablement and per-tool read/write restrictions, enterprise-managed connector authorisation through the IdP, audit logs (180-day export) and the Compliance API (Activity Feed, chats, files, projects, session transcripts, effective settings), custom retention, spend limits, IP allowlisting, CMEK and US-only inference.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Free, Pro, Max (consumer terms); Team (SSO, server-managed settings, analytics); Enterprise (SCIM, custom roles, Compliance API, audit logs, custom retention, CMEK, IP allowlisting, ZDR for Claude Code, HIPAA-ready option, US-only inference).

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Anthropic API, with conversations stored on Anthropic's backend for the web, desktop and mobile apps alike. Claude Desktop on 3P, which routes to a cloud provider and keeps history on the device, is a variant of toolClaudeDesktop.

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: Prompts, attachments, artifact content and connector retrievals to Anthropic; remote connectors are reached from Anthropic's cloud, not from the device; the tenant-restrictions header (web, desktop, API-key and OAuth access) and the IP allowlist are the network-side gates.

facts.label: Retention & training
facts.value: Commercial plans: no training; chat and project retention indefinite by default, configurable from 30 days at Organization settings > Data and privacy; audit logs 180 days; Compliance API local/remote session transcripts 6 years or the custom period.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: support.claude.com Team and Enterprise plans collection plus platform.claude.com manage-claude (Compliance API, inference hooks)

items.title: Managed connector authorization
body: Enterprise-managed connector authorization (GA) lets admins provision MCP connectors org-wide through the IdP (Okta today), assign them by role and scope the permissions Claude may request; Owners can also restrict each connector's tools to read-only and block verified-domain services from connecting to outside accounts. Connector permissions govern the connectors added under Organization settings > Connectors, not servers a member runs locally in Claude Desktop (the desktop extension allowlist and device policy for those are on toolClaudeDesktop).

links.title: Manage custom roles on Enterprise plans (where connector permissions apply)

items.title: Identity, audit and compliance for the organisation
body: SSO via WorkOS (Okta, Entra ID, Google, OneLogin, JumpCloud, Duo SAML) with "Require SSO for Claude", JIT or SCIM provisioning with group-to-role mapping and automatic removal; Enterprise custom roles and groups; IP allowlisting (CIDR ranges enabled by Anthropic support); tenant restrictions via the proxy-injected anthropic-allowed-org-ids header.

Audit logs (Enterprise, 180 days, emailed download link) from Organization settings > Data and privacy; the Compliance API for the Activity Feed, chats, files, projects, directory, effective settings and Cowork / Claude Code / M365 session transcripts; custom data retention from 30 days; Inference hooks for inline allow/deny of every governed prompt across claude.ai, Cowork, Claude Code, Claude for Microsoft 365, Claude Tag and Claude in Chrome.

links.title: Set up JIT or SCIM provisioning

riskNotes.note: Chat and project retention is indefinite until an Owner sets a period; uploads, connector results and artifacts persist with the chat. Custom retention and the Compliance API delete endpoints are the levers.

Connectors act with the user's granted scopes; org-wide tool restrictions (read vs write) and managed authorisation scoping keep Claude from sending mail or writing tickets when only reading is intended.
Personal accounts on the corporate network are blocked only by tenant restrictions or IP allowlisting; domain capture and SSO enforcement pull verified-domain users into the organisation.

controls.mechanism: Enterprise custom roles and groups (Organization settings > Roles, Groups) grant capabilities, each connector and connector tool (Always allow / Needs approval / Blocked) and admin permissions, with "View effective role"; target-tenant consent for the connector apps is documented: Microsoft Entra admin consent for the two Microsoft 365 connector apps (client IDs 08ad6f98-a4f8-4635-bb8d-f1a3044760f0 and 07c030f6-5743-41b7-ba00-0a6e85f37c17) and Google Workspace API controls trust for Claude

steps.title: Authorise features and connectors by role
body: At Organization settings > Roles create custom roles, choose their groups, toggle capabilities and set each connector or tool on the Connectors tab; check a member with View effective role.

steps.title: Decide in Microsoft Entra whether the connector may be granted
body: A Global Administrator grants admin consent through the adminconsent URLs for both client IDs, requires assignment on the M365 MCP Server for Claude and M365 MCP Client for Claude enterprise apps, and revokes Graph permissions the organisation does not want.

steps.title: Decide in Google Workspace
body: In admin.google.com under Security > Access and data control > API controls > Manage third-party app access, set Claude to Trusted, or leave it blocked.

steps.title: Pull personal accounts on your domain into the tenant (Enterprise)
body: With Restrict organization creation, SSO enforcement and JIT or SCIM in place, turn on Migrate accounts using your domain under Organization settings > Organization and access > Security.

controls.note: Native on Enterprise by the rule: the console administers role and group authorisation over connectors, tools and features, enforced on Anthropic's servers and failing toward deny, and the vendor documents the target-tenant consent path with the app IDs. Team plans have organisation-wide connector and tool policy only, which is partial. Connector permissions apply only to members on the Custom role (User, Admin and Owner see every organisation connector under the organisation-wide policy), grants are additive across roles, and role changes take up to 15 minutes. The consent itself is the target tenant's control, not Anthropic's. Domain capture (Enterprise) keeps employees in the corporate tenant; Team plans can verify a domain but not claim existing accounts. Pinning the desktop app's sign-in to the organisation (forceLoginOrgUUID) is device policy, recorded on toolClaudeDesktop.

original.mechanism: SSO (SAML/OIDC) with Require SSO for Claude, domain verification and capture, JIT or SCIM provisioning with group-to-role mapping, custom roles and groups (Enterprise)

steps.title: Enforce SSO
body: Verify domains at claude.ai/admin-settings/organization, configure the IdP through WorkOS, then toggle "Require SSO for Claude" in Authentication settings.

steps.title: Provision and deprovision from the directory
body: Enable SCIM with group-to-role mapping (Enterprise / Console); users removed from all mapped groups are removed at the next sync.

steps.title: Gate features by role
body: Create custom roles and groups at Organization settings > Roles and Groups to gate Claude Code, Cowork, Chrome, connectors, Claude Tag, models and admin scopes.

original.mechanism: Connectors retrieve as the authenticated user (OAuth) or as the scoped managed authorisation; verified-domain restriction stops org services connecting to outside accounts

steps.title: Keep retrieval per user
body: Prefer user OAuth or role-scoped managed authorisation over shared service accounts and turn on the verified-domain connector restriction on Enterprise.

original.note: Delegated when the connector runs as the user (the source system enforces the user's permissions, oversharing included); service-owned when enterprise-managed authorisation is used, in which case the managed scope, not the user's entitlements, bounds retrieval for everyone.

controls.mechanism: anthropic-allowed-org-ids tenant-restriction header (Enterprise and Console) injected by the organisation's TLS-inspecting proxy and enforced by Anthropic for claude.ai web, desktop, API-key and OAuth traffic; IP allowlisting (Enterprise, CIDR ranges enabled by Anthropic support); the code execution sandbox's own egress set at Organization settings > Capabilities

steps.title: Block other tenants at the proxy
body: Inject anthropic-allowed-org-ids with your organisation UUIDs (numbered continuation headers, up to 500 UUIDs) for claude.ai, api.anthropic.com, claude.com and anthropic.com, overwriting the header on every request.

steps.title: Restrict where your tenant can be used from (Enterprise)
body: Send Anthropic support your office and VPN CIDR ranges; every authenticated request from another address is then denied.

steps.title: Set the sandbox's own egress
body: At Organization settings > Capabilities under Code execution and file creation, leave Allow network egress off or limit it to package managers and named domains.

controls.note: Partial on the D3-OTF rule: Anthropic honours a documented tenant-restriction header that the organisation's SSE injects (TLS inspection required; other organisations get a 403 tenant_restriction_violation), so personal and foreign tenants are blocked on managed networks. A customer proxy does not control the vendor's own egress: remote connectors reach MCP servers from Anthropic's cloud, web search runs on Anthropic's servers, and the code execution sandbox is governed only by the Capabilities network setting (off for new Enterprise organisations, package managers only on Team; connector traffic stays possible whatever it says). Off-network and unmanaged devices bypass the header; IP allowlisting gates only the organisation's own tenant. Local MCP servers and desktop extensions in Claude Desktop use the device's network; that local reach is toolClaudeDesktop.

original.mechanism: IP allowlisting (Enterprise, CIDR ranges enabled by Anthropic support) and tenant restrictions (anthropic-allowed-org-ids header injected by a TLS-inspecting proxy)

steps.title: Restrict where Claude can be used from
body: Compile CIDR ranges and have Anthropic enable IP allowlisting; every authenticated request outside the ranges is denied (Anthropic-hosted cloud sessions then need an exemption).

steps.title: Block other tenants at the proxy
body: Inject anthropic-allowed-org-ids with your org UUIDs for claude.ai, api.anthropic.com, claude.com and anthropic.com (up to 500 UUIDs across numbered headers).

original.note: IP allowlisting is enforced by Anthropic; the tenant-restriction header is enforced by a TLS-inspecting proxy the organisation operates. Neither is an SSE service: inline inspection of prompts and uploads is the customer's SSE, and its completeness depends on which paths it sees.

original.mechanism: Documented host allowlist for Claude Desktop and claude.ai; egressProxyUrl / PAC keys on 3P; connector traffic through mcp-proxy.anthropic.com; custom connectors reachable only via allowlisted Anthropic IPs

steps.title: Allowlist the documented hosts
body: Permit anthropic.com, claude.ai, claude.com, platform.claude.com, downloads.claude.ai, *.claudeusercontent.com and *.claudemcpcontent.com (plus optional CDN hosts for artifacts) and route through egressProxyUrl on managed devices.

original.note: The product documents its destinations and offers proxy keys; it enforces no destination policy of its own. Connector traffic egresses from Anthropic's MCP proxy, outside the organisation's network.

controls.mechanism: Inference hooks (Enterprise) hold every governed claude.ai request on web, desktop and mobile, with its tool calls, tool results and extracted attachment text, for an allow or deny verdict from the organisation's DLP or AI security server; the Compliance API supports detection after the fact

steps.title: Put your DLP inline (Enterprise)
body: At Organization settings > Data and privacy > Inference hooks turn on Allow for your organization, register the endpoint and signing secret, set Failure handling to Block the request, Requests inspected to 100 and turn on Enforce verdicts.

steps.title: Scan stored content after the fact
body: Give your DLP or DSPM product a Compliance Access Key with read:compliance_user_data to page through /v1/compliance/apps/chats, messages and files, and delete:compliance_user_data only on a separate key.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: an inline hook that hands prompts to the organisation's DLP with a block verdict is an attach point, and Claude classifies nothing itself. The hook allows or denies only (no masking or redaction), never receives image bytes (a screenshot of a document is not inspected), has no response-side event yet, skips voice mode, members of excluded custom roles and requests outside the rollout percentage, and falls back to the failure-handling choice when the server errs or the circuit breaker trips. A blocked message stays in the conversation. It is not available on Bedrock or Google Cloud, nor on Team plans. Blocking connector write tools and custom retention are minimisation and lifecycle, not detection; Compliance API scanning finds content after it reached Anthropic.

original.mechanism: Inference hooks (Enterprise, beta) route every governed prompt to your AI security server for allow/deny; connector tool restrictions limit outbound actions; no built-in content classifier

steps.title: Enable Inference hooks
body: Configure the AI security server endpoint and signing secret, run shadow mode, then enforce; denied requests never reach the model and are recorded in the Activity Feed. Not available on Bedrock or Google Cloud.

original.note: Inference hooks route governed prompts to the organisation's scanner; the product itself classifies nothing, and uploads, connector results and outputs are outside the hook unless the hook contract says otherwise.

original.mechanism: claude.ai is a browser SaaS; paste and upload inspection is the organisation's browser-security tooling
original.note: Anthropic offers no in-page inspection; pair the tenant-restriction header with browser D&R or SSE inline controls.

steps.title: Instrument the browser session
body: Apply your browser-security policy to claude.ai and *.claudeusercontent.com and use the tenant-restriction header to keep sessions in the corporate tenant.

controls.mechanism: Anthropic's model-layer defenses against injected instructions (no administrator setting); Inference hooks (Enterprise) hand each governed request, including connector tool calls and the results they return, to the organisation's AI security server before the next inference step

steps.title: Put a screen on returned connector content (Enterprise)
body: At Organization settings > Data and privacy > Inference hooks register an AI security server that classifies tool results for injection, set Failure handling to Block the request and turn on Enforce verdicts.

steps.title: Know what the vendor screening covers
body: The connector verification page tells members to stay aware of prompt injection "even though Claude has built-in protections"; Verified and Community labels are not a security audit of what a connector returns.

controls.note: Partial on the rule applied to every vendor: vendor-internal defenses documented only in general terms (no setting, threshold, quarantine or event an administrator can see), plus an inline hook that is an attach point until the organisation's server does the classifying. The hook returns allow or deny (no strip or quarantine), never receives system prompts or tool definitions, so a poisoned connector description is not seen, and ignores images. Claude.ai has no action classifier to lean on; restricting write tools limits what an injection can do, which is AML.M0028, not screening.

original.mechanism: Anthropic model-side safeguards and web-fetch isolation; connector tool restrictions; Inference hooks for inline policy

steps.title: Limit what an injected instruction can do
body: Restrict connectors to read-only tools and enable only vetted connectors; use Inference hooks to deny prompts carrying policy-violating content.

original.note: No admin-configurable injection classifier is exposed for chat.

controls.mechanism: The Anthropic Trust Center (compliance scope table, SOC 2 Type 2 and CSA STAR L2 report, ISO 27001 and ISO 42001 certificates, HIPAA reports, SIG Lite, CAIQ, VSA and HECVAT questionnaires, infrastructure diagram, security advisories) and the Compliance API effective-settings endpoint feed the organisation's TPRM platform

evidence.title: Anthropic Trust Center (compliance scope table and resources, read 2026-09-25)
Compliance API — organizations, users, roles, groups and effective settings

controls.note: External by the rule applied to every vendor: the questionnaire, evidence expiry and reassessment trigger live in the organisation's TPRM platform. The Trust Center scope table lists SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, ISO 42001, CSA STAR, HIPAA and NIST 800-171 for Claude Enterprise, and all but HIPAA for Claude Team; the reports and questionnaires sit behind Request access. Advisories for the desktop app's installer are on toolClaudeDesktop. Re-assess the tenant on a clock by reading each organisation's effective settings through the Compliance API (Enterprise); a readback is evidence for the assessment, not the assessment.

original.mechanism: Trust Center artifacts (SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA implementation guide, architecture overviews) feed the buyer's TPRM platform

steps.title: Collect artifacts
body: Request the Trust Center resources referenced across the docs, including the Cowork desktop security architecture overview and the M365 architecture diagrams.

original.mechanism: Compliance API directory and settings endpoints, Enterprise Analytics API and usage exports feed the organisation's governance platform

steps.title: Mirror organisation state
body: Pull organizations, users, roles, groups and effective settings from the Compliance API and per-user engagement from the Enterprise Analytics API.

original.mechanism: Compliance API effective-settings and Activity Feed endpoints, audit log export, and admin console readback let posture tooling verify training opt-out, retention, connectors and roles

steps.title: Evidence configuration continuously
body: Poll each organisation's effective settings and the Activity Feed with a Compliance Access Key; use the audit log export (180 days) for point-in-time evidence.

original.note: The Compliance API effective-settings and Activity Feed endpoints are the readback an SSPM product polls; nothing in the product compares settings to a baseline, detects drift or remediates. The same rule applies to every vendor with a readback API.

controls.mechanism: Connector tool policy per connector and tool (Always allow / Needs approval / Blocked) at Organization settings > Connectors and, on Enterprise, on each custom role's Connectors tab; a Needs approval ceiling makes Claude ask before each call and removes the member's "Always allow"

steps.title: Cap write tools at Needs approval
body: Set send, create, update and delete tools to Needs approval (or Blocked) in the organisation-wide tool policy at Organization settings > Connectors and on each role's Connectors tab; members then confirm every call and cannot choose Always allow.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: a present person approves each call of an organisation connector's tool and an administrator can force that per tool, non-overridably and enforced on Anthropic's servers for web, desktop and mobile, but the docs do not say the prompt shows the tool's arguments, so approval bound to the exact action is not documented. Outside the policy: code execution with network egress, which acts without per-action approval; roles or organisations left at Always allow, where members keep persistent approval; and servers a member runs locally in Claude Desktop, which connector permissions do not govern (toolClaudeDesktop). Team plans set the policy organisation-wide only.

original.mechanism: Connector tool calls prompt per tool unless the user chooses always allow; Owners can set connector tools to ask or blocked org-wide; no approval workflow for chat outputs

steps.title: Force approval on connector actions
body: At Organization settings > Connectors set tools that write (send message, create issue) to ask or remove them; these settings are enforced in Claude Code and Cowork sessions too.

controls.mechanism: The Compliance API enumerates every chat, file, project and project attachment, and chat messages name the integration and MCP server behind each tool call; Organization settings > Connectors lists the organisation's connectors; the Activity Feed records which member connected which integration

steps.title: Enumerate what Claude holds (Enterprise)
body: Page /v1/compliance/apps/chats with order_by=updated_at, then each chat's messages, files and artifacts, and the projects and project attachments, with a read:compliance_user_data key.

steps.title: List the sources behind the connectors
body: Export the connectors at Organization settings > Connectors and the integration_user_connected events, then run your data-classification tooling over those sources before enabling them.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: the product lists what it stores and which sources are connected, without classification or an oversharing report on the drives, mailboxes, sites and channels behind the connectors (the Microsoft 365 connector retrieves on demand and caches no file content, so there is no index to inspect). Custom retention and deletion are lifecycle controls, not inventory. Knowing what the connectors reach is a DSPM or data-classification product, which can consume the Compliance API.

original.mechanism: Custom data retention (30 days to indefinite) for chats and projects, Compliance API retrieve and delete for chats, files and projects, organisation data export

steps.title: Set retention and delete on demand
body: Configure retention at Organization settings > Data and privacy (Owner) and use the Compliance API content endpoints to retrieve or delete chats, files and projects.

original.note: Retention, deletion and export are data lifecycle controls. They do not discover or classify sensitive content in chats, files or projects, nor assess exposure; a DSPM product consumes the Compliance API content endpoints to do that.

controls.mechanism: Connector OAuth tokens encrypted in Anthropic's backend and never shown to the model, their lifetime set by the source or, under managed authorisation, the IdP; MCP tunnels (Enterprise research preview) with a tunnel token rotated by re-running setup and revoked by archiving; Compliance Access Keys scoped at creation and deleted at Organization settings > API

steps.title: Rotate and revoke the tunnel credentials
body: Revoke the Tunnels API key at Organization settings > Tunnels > Tunnels API after every setup run, rotate the tunnel token by incrementing tunnel.tokenVersion (Helm) or --token-version (Compose) and re-running setup, and archive a tunnel to invalidate it.

steps.title: Scope and rotate compliance keys
body: Create separate read and delete Compliance Access Keys at Organization settings > API and rotate them yourself; they never expire and a deleted key fails on the next request.

steps.title: Issue connector credentials through the IdP
body: Set up Managed authorization on supported connectors so the IdP and the connector's authorisation server set token lifetime and deprovisioning revokes access.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: a vendor tunnel exists and its credentials are scoped and revocable, but rotating the tunnel token means re-running setup and restarting cloudflared (a redeploy of the tunnel stack), the token and TLS private keys are stored in your environment (Helm release Secrets are not encrypted at rest by default), and the preview carries no uptime or support commitment. Compliance Access Keys do not expire, and individually authorised connector tokens live as long as the source allows. Credentials held on the device by Claude Desktop (its sign-in, desktop extension settings, local MCP server configuration) are toolClaudeDesktop.

original.mechanism: Connector OAuth tokens held by the platform; enterprise-managed authorisation replaces per-user grants; API and compliance keys are scoped and revocable in the console

steps.title: Centralise connector credentials
body: Use enterprise-managed authorisation so connector access is inherited from IdP roles on first login instead of users pasting tokens.

original.note: Connector tokens are held by the platform and never shown to the model; the API and compliance keys are long-lived until rotated in the console. Enterprise-managed authorisation replaces per-user grants — it does not make the underlying credential ephemeral.

controls.mechanism: Only Owners add connectors (Organization settings > Connectors) and members can connect only those; per-tool Always allow / Needs approval / Blocked as an organisation-wide ceiling and, on Enterprise, per custom role, enforced on Anthropic's servers

steps.title: Set the organisation-wide tool policy
body: At Organization settings > Connectors open each connector's tool permissions and set every tool or category to Always allow, Needs approval or Blocked; members cannot widen it.

steps.title: Narrow it per group (Enterprise)
body: On each custom role's Connectors tab under Organization settings > Roles set All connectors, each connector or each tool; new roles default to Needs approval, and the stricter of role and organisation policy applies.

controls.note: Native on Enterprise by the rule: an administrator allowlist of connectors plus per-tool (read versus write) scoping per group, locked against members and enforced outside the model; when permissions cannot load, access fails toward deny. Boundaries: no argument or resource scoping (which folder, which channel) beyond the source system's own permissions; Team plans scope organisation-wide only; members on built-in roles get every organisation connector under the organisation-wide policy. Connector permissions "don't govern connectors a member runs locally on their own machine": local MCP servers and desktop extensions are Claude Desktop's own reach, recorded on toolClaudeDesktop.

original.mechanism: Connector enablement per organisation, per-tool read/write restrictions, role-based connector access, desktop extension allowlist, isLocalDevMcpEnabled, isDesktopExtensionEnabled

steps.title: Enable and scope connectors
body: Enable connectors at Organization settings > Connectors > Browse connectors and restrict each connector's tools (for example search but not send) for the whole organisation.

steps.title: Lock down device-side tools
body: Turn on the desktop extension allowlist and set isLocalDevMcpEnabled or isDesktopExtensionEnabled false in device policy where local tools are not wanted.

original.note: Connector enablement and per-tool read/write restrictions hide or limit connector tools org-wide; there is no argument-level scoping (which folder, which channel) beyond what the connector's own authorisation grants.

controls.mechanism: Connectors retrieve with each member's own permissions at the source (per-user OAuth, or the IdP's assertion under managed authorisation); administrators choose which connectors and tools exist, narrow Microsoft Graph permissions in Entra, and stop verified-domain services connecting to outside Claude accounts; no site, drive or mailbox scoping in Claude

steps.title: Keep retrieval on the member's own entitlements
body: Add only the connectors you govern at Organization settings > Connectors; each member then authenticates individually and reaches only what their source account can.

steps.title: Narrow what the Microsoft 365 connector may read
body: In Entra under Enterprise applications > M365 MCP Server for Claude > Permissions revoke Graph permissions such as Sites.Read.All or Mail.Read that the organisation does not want reached.

steps.title: Keep work data out of personal Claude accounts (Enterprise)
body: At Organization settings > Organization and access > Connector domain restriction turn on Restrict verified-domain connectors to your enterprise.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: retrieval runs with the requesting member's entitlements, so the source enforces them (oversharing included, and Microsoft 365 DLP applies to delegated calls), but administrators can only include or exclude whole connectors, tools or Graph permission scopes, not choose which sites, drives or mailboxes the assistant may search; the Ask Your Org enterprise search project uses the same per-member connectors. Under managed authorisation the Owner-chosen scopes bound every member of the roles selected. Oversharing remediation is the source's.

original.mechanism: Connectors retrieve as the authenticated user (OAuth) or as the scoped managed authorisation; verified-domain restriction stops org services connecting to outside accounts

steps.title: Keep retrieval per user
body: Prefer user OAuth or role-scoped managed authorisation over shared service accounts and turn on the verified-domain connector restriction on Enterprise.

original.note: Delegated when the connector runs as the user (the source system enforces the user's permissions, oversharing included); service-owned when enterprise-managed authorisation is used, in which case the managed scope, not the user's entitlements, bounds retrieval for everyone.

controls.mechanism: Organization settings > Connectors lists every organisation connector (only Owners add them, members connect only those); Organization settings > Plugins & skills Inventory and Requests tabs list governed plugins and skills and the approval queue for member submissions

steps.title: Treat the connector list as the enforced register
body: Keep custom connectors Owner-added at Organization settings > Connectors and remove any that have no owner in your inventory.

steps.title: Approve plugins and skills before they spread
body: Review the Inventory and approve or deny member submissions on the Requests tab of Organization settings > Plugins & skills.

steps.title: Inventory grants from the Activity Feed (Enterprise)
body: Query /v1/compliance/activities with activity_types[] integration_user_connected and integration_user_disconnected to keep a per-member register of connector grants.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: the connector list is an enforced register, but it carries no owner or approval record per connector, and members with the Create skills capability add their own skills. Reconciliation against actual use is the organisation's inventory; no console page or API lists each member's live connector grants, so that register is rebuilt from Activity Feed events. Desktop extensions and local MCP servers, which this list does not show, are registered (or not) on toolClaudeDesktop.

original.mechanism: Organisation connector catalogue, extension allowlist and role assignments in the console; Compliance API session listings for Cowork and Claude Code

steps.title: Treat the connector catalogue as the registry
body: Only Owner-enabled connectors and allowlisted extensions are available to members; review them under Organization settings > Connectors.

original.note: The connector catalogue and extension allowlist are approved configuration; session listings are use. There is no owner or approval record per connector and no reconciliation — the organisation's inventory holds those.

controls.mechanism: Enterprise domain claiming lists every personal Free, Pro and Max account on a verified domain (email, plan, created, last active; CSV export) and "Migrate accounts using your domain" moves or closes them; Restrict organization creation and the anthropic-allowed-org-ids header prevent new personal use

steps.title: Review personal accounts on your domain (Enterprise)
body: After domain verification, SSO enforcement and JIT or SCIM, review and export the personal accounts on the domain, then turn on Migrate accounts using your domain under Organization settings > Organization and access > Security.

steps.title: Stop new personal organisations on the domain
body: Turn on Restrict organization creation under Security on the Organization and access page once the domain shows Verified.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: the vendor lists personal accounts on the verified domains, not what they do, accounts on personal addresses, Claude on unmanaged devices, or connectors members attach, which remain for SSE/CASB and endpoint inventory. Domain capture is one-way and has a fixed 30-day window; Team plans can verify a domain and block new personal accounts but not list or claim existing ones. The header prevents rather than discovers, as does forceLoginOrgUUID on managed devices (toolClaudeDesktop).

original.mechanism: Domain capture pulls verified-domain accounts into the organisation; tenant restrictions and IP allowlisting block personal accounts on corporate networks

steps.title: Capture and block
body: Verify domains for account claiming and deploy the tenant-restriction header so personal claude.ai use from managed networks is refused.

original.note: Domain capture is a genuine discovery signal: it finds personal accounts on verified domains and pulls them into the organisation. Its scope is accounts on your domains — personal accounts on other addresses and unmanaged devices are found by proxy or endpoint inventory.

controls.mechanism: Compliance API (Enterprise): /v1/compliance/apps/chats and each chat's messages return prompts, responses and tool_use blocks (tool name, JSON input, integration name, mcp_server_url) with tool_result text, files and artifacts; /v1/compliance/activities returns control-plane and connector events such as integration_user_connected, mcp_tool_policy_updated and inference_hooks_request_denied; a 180-day audit-log CSV export

steps.title: Create a Compliance Access Key (Enterprise)
body: The primary owner enables the Compliance API at Organization settings > API and creates a key with read:compliance_activities and read:compliance_user_data only.

steps.title: Pull conversations with their tool calls
body: Walk /v1/compliance/apps/chats with order_by=updated_at and fetch each chat's messages with tool_result_max_chars and tool_use_input_max_chars set to -1 so inputs and results are not cut at 10,000 characters.

steps.title: Stream the Activity Feed to the SIEM
body: Poll /v1/compliance/activities from the last saved cursor and correlate its events with your gateway's records.

controls.note: Native by the rule: an administrator exports conversation content with each connector call's tool, arguments, server and result, plus connector and policy events, programmatically. Boundaries: Enterprise only (Team has neither the API nor audit logs); pull-based, so a chat a member deletes before the next poll comes back with deleted_at and no content, and retention deletions are final; non-text tool results are omitted; transcripts of Cowork and Claude Code sessions are separate endpoints; integrity and retention beyond Anthropic's are the SIEM's. Inference hooks can push each governed transcript in real time as an archival alternative.

original.mechanism: Enterprise audit logs (30+ event types, 180-day export) and the Compliance API Activity Feed with actor, IP, user agent and device; session transcripts for Cowork, Claude Code, M365 and Science

steps.title: Export or stream audit events
body: Owners export logs from Organization settings > Data and privacy, or query GET /v1/compliance/activities continuously into the SIEM.

original.note: Vendor-held audit log with a 180-day export window and the Activity Feed; durable retention and tamper evidence beyond that window are the organisation's archive. Events are attributed, not signed.

controls.mechanism: Member removal (Organization settings > Members > Remove from team, or SCIM) ends access immediately; an Owner removes a connector for everyone at Organization settings > Connectors or sets its tools to Blocked; the Chat capability off on custom roles (up to 15 minutes); an Inference hooks deny for an account (Enterprise)

steps.title: Cut a member off
body: Select Remove from team at Organization settings > Members, or remove the person from the IdP app with SCIM; they lose access to the organisation immediately.

steps.title: Remove a connector for everyone
body: At Organization settings > Connectors click Remove (or the three dots) on the connector, or set all of its tools to Blocked, then revoke the app's grant at the source (Entra, Google, your IdP).

steps.title: Refuse inference for an account (Enterprise)
body: With Enforce verdicts on, have your AI security server deny that member's requests; turning enforcement on or off reaches every Anthropic server in about a minute.

steps.title: Issue connector grants from the IdP
body: On a supported connector click Set up next to Managed authorization, confirm the Okta connection, choose the roles and the scopes Claude may request, then Save & turn on.

steps.title: End grants with the person
body: Use SCIM directory sync so members removed from the IdP app are removed from the organisation, which ends their access immediately.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: there is no organisation-wide switch for claude.ai chat (the Chat capability can be turned off only on custom roles, and built-in roles keep it); removing a connector disables it for every member, but revocation of the grants at the source is not documented, so revoke them there; and the effect of either on a research run or tool loop already in progress is not documented (delay not documented; role changes up to 15 minutes). Member removal is documented as immediate. An Inference hooks deny refuses the next inference request, which halts a running tool loop at its next step, but only on Enterprise and only while the hook is enforcing. Managed authorisation binds connector grants to the IdP lifecycle but covers ten listed connectors and Okta only; individually authorised grants live as long as the source allows.

original.mechanism: SCIM deprovisioning, member removal, connector disable (revokes for all), extension allowlist force-delete, device keys (isClaudeCodeForDesktopEnabled, secureVmFeaturesEnabled, isDesktopExtensionEnabled), Compliance API delete

steps.title: Cut access and remove data
body: Remove the member or SCIM group, disable the connector at Organization settings > Connectors, and delete chats, files or projects through the Compliance API.

original.note: Seat removal and connector disable apply at the next request; a connector call in flight completes. The docs state no propagation delay, so measure it.

settings.name: Require SSO for Claude
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Organization and access › Authentication
settings.recommended: On, with MFA enforced on the Claude app in your IdP
settings.why: Every claude.ai, Claude Desktop and mobile login goes through the corporate IdP and its MFA; personal email logins on your domain stop working.

settings.name: Shortened session length
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Organization and access › Session security
settings.default: Not enabled (sign-in kept while the user stays active)
settings.recommended: 7 days
settings.why: Web, desktop and mobile sign-ins expire weekly, so a stolen or stale session meets the IdP's MFA again.

settings.name: User provisioning (SCIM)
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Organization and access › User provisioning
settings.recommended: SCIM, driven by the IdP group that grants Claude
settings.why: Removing someone in the IdP removes their seat, so a leaver's access ends with their account rather than with a ticket.

settings.name: Restrict organization creation
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Organization and access › Security
settings.recommended: On
settings.why: Stops staff creating personal or side Claude organisations on your verified domains, which no admin can see.

settings.name: Migrate accounts using your domain
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Organization and access › Security
settings.recommended: On, after reviewing the personal accounts listed on your domain
settings.why: No Free, Pro or Max account can exist on the verified domain, so work chats can't sit in personal plans no admin sees; it can't be reversed.

settings.name: Tenant Restrictions (anthropic-allowed-org-ids)
settings.where: Corporate TLS-inspecting proxy → anthropic-allowed-org-ids header on claude.ai, api.anthropic.com, claude.com and anthropic.com
settings.recommended: Your organisation's UUID, injected and overwritten on every request from managed devices
settings.why: Personal and other organisations' Claude accounts can't be used from the corporate network in any browser or the desktop app.

settings.name: Chat (custom role capability)
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Roles › role › Capabilities
settings.recommended: Granted on the roles of the groups rolled out to Claude
settings.why: Chat on web, desktop and mobile follows IdP group membership, and withholding it on a role stops that group's use; built-in roles keep it.

settings.name: Custom data retention controls
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Data and privacy
settings.recommended: 30 days for chats; projects and artifacts on your records-retention schedule, never indefinite
settings.why: Uploaded client files, connector results and artifacts otherwise stay with the chat forever; the minimum is 30 days, and a shorter period deletes at the next daily run.

settings.name: Memory
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Capabilities
settings.default: Off (each member opts in once an Owner allows it)
settings.recommended: Off; projects keep their own context
settings.why: Account memory carries details across chats, so one engagement's material could resurface in another client's work; teams that want it get it per role.

settings.name: Inference hooks
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Data and privacy › Inference hooks
settings.recommended: On, connected to your DLP or AI-security service, enforcing after a monitor-only period
settings.why: Each chat request on web, desktop and mobile, connector results and extracted attachment text included, is checked by your own service before inference, so secrets and injected content can be stopped centrally.

settings.name: Restrict verified-domain connectors to your enterprise
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Organization and access › Connector domain restriction
settings.recommended: On
settings.why: A work Gmail, Slack or Microsoft 365 account on your domain can be connected only from your organisation's Claude accounts, not a personal one.

settings.name: Organization-wide tool policy
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Connectors › connector › tool (Always allow / Needs approval / Blocked)
settings.recommended: Write and send tools set to Needs approval; tools no one uses Blocked
settings.why: The ceiling no role or member can widen — Needs approval removes Always allow, so every send, create or delete is confirmed; Blocked hides the tool from Claude.

settings.name: Connector permissions (custom role Connectors tab)
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Roles › role › Connectors
settings.recommended: Each group's role granted only the connectors and tools its work needs
settings.why: Connector reach follows IdP groups, and the stricter of role and organisation policy applies; members on built-in roles see every organisation connector.

settings.name: Managed authorization
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Connectors › connector › Configuration
settings.default: Not set up (each member authorises with their own OAuth grant)
settings.recommended: Set up for every supported connector, with the Scopes your roles need
settings.why: The IdP issues and revokes connector access by group, so scopes are chosen centrally and de-provisioning ends it.

settings.name: Assignment required? (M365 MCP Server for Claude and M365 MCP Client for Claude)
settings.where: Microsoft Entra admin center › Enterprise applications › each app › Properties, then Users and groups
settings.recommended: Yes on both apps, assigned to the same Claude user group
settings.why: Only the people you assign can authenticate the Microsoft 365 connector; revoke Graph permissions on the server app that no group needs.

settings.name: Manage third-party app access (Claude set to Trusted)
settings.where: Google Admin console › Security › Access and data control › API controls › Manage third-party app access
settings.recommended: Claude Trusted only once Google Workspace connectors are approved; blocked until then
settings.why: Google Workspace decides whether the connectors may reach Drive, Gmail and Calendar at all, independently of Claude's own connector list.

settings.name: Publishing
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Plugins & skills › Policy
settings.default: Open on Team; Requires review on Enterprise (moving to Open where scanning is on)
settings.recommended: Requires review
settings.why: An Owner approves every skill and plugin, and each new version, before it reaches colleagues; set it explicitly so the default change doesn't apply.

settings.name: User-created skills
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Plugins & skills › Policy
settings.recommended: On, with Skill and plugin security scanning on
settings.why: Members keep their own skills for personal use while uploads are scanned; regulated teams turn it off so only provisioned skills run.

settings.name: Skill and plugin security scanning
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Plugins & skills › Policy
settings.default: On for Enterprise organisations that hadn't chosen before 2 October 2026
settings.recommended: On
settings.why: Every third-party skill and plugin uploaded or edited is scanned before it runs, and a failing one is blocked.

settings.name: Allow network egress
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Capabilities › Code execution and file creation
settings.default: Package managers only on Team; off for new Enterprise organisations
settings.recommended: Package managers and specific domains — your package mirror and the hosts analysis needs
settings.why: Code Claude runs in the chat sandbox reaches only the listed hosts; connector traffic and web search are outside this setting.

settings.name: External sharing and Email invitations outside your organization
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Artifacts
settings.recommended: Both off; allow external sharing for a single artifact when a team asks
settings.why: Artifacts open to anyone with the link, or to outside invitees, fall outside your IP allowlist and tenant; turning sharing off also stops existing public links.

settings.name: Compliance API
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › API, then a Compliance Access Key with read:compliance_activities and read:compliance_user_data
settings.recommended: On, pulled into your SIEM and eDiscovery; delete scope on a separate key
settings.why: Chats with each connector call's tool, arguments and result, files, projects and the Activity Feed reach your own store; while it is off nothing is recorded.

tools.name: Claude Desktop (local MCP servers, desktop extensions and device policy)

variants.name: Claude Desktop (macOS PKG/DMG, Windows MSIX, Linux beta) signed in to claude.ai
variants.note: Its chats are claude.ai chats (toolClaudeWeb); this entity covers what the app runs and reaches on the device. The Code tab is a variant of toolClaudeCode and the Cowork tab is toolClaudeCowork.

variants.name: Claude Desktop on 3P (inference via Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry, a gateway or the Claude API; local history)
variants.note: Configured through an MDM profile, a bootstrap server or the Enterprise Admin Console for Desktop 3P (Organization settings on claude.ai, generally available); conversation content goes only to your endpoint and is stored on the device; users have a local device identity only unless the deployment is managed from the admin console.

summary: The Claude desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux (beta), as a program on the managed endpoint. As a chat client it shows the same synced claude.ai chats as the browser (toolClaudeWeb), and its Code and Cowork tabs are toolClaudeCode and toolClaudeCowork. What it adds on the device is its own reach: local MCP servers from claude_desktop_config.json and desktop extensions (.mcpb) that run as host processes with the user's permissions and feed tool results into chat, Quick Entry screenshots and window sharing on macOS, the connection through which the app drives Claude in Chrome, the bridge through which cloud sessions reach the computer's files and browser while the app is online, and the app binary and its updater. Standard deployments load the web application from claude.ai and send inference to the Anthropic API; Claude Desktop on 3P bundles the web application, routes inference to the organisation's provider and keeps history on the device.

Administration is split across two planes. Device policy, deployed by MDM to the macOS domain com.anthropic.claudefordesktop, the Windows key HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Claude or the root-owned Linux file /etc/claude-desktop/managed-settings.json, turns local MCP servers, desktop extensions and the extension directory on or off, pins sign-in to the organisation (forceLoginOrgUUID), turns the Code and Cowork tabs off, and governs auto-update; device policy overrides the in-app allowlist. The claude.ai console holds the desktop extension allowlist (Organization settings > Connectors > Desktop), the Computer access capability on Enterprise custom roles and Require trusted devices. Connector permissions "don't govern connectors a member runs locally on their own machine", so a local server's tools have no administrator policy on standard deployments. Claude Desktop on 3P adds per-tool policy for managed MCP servers, signed-extension enforcement, an OTLP export covering Chat, Cowork and Code, local retention periods and proxy keys.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Every plan for Chat; Code and Cowork on Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise; device policies and the desktop extension allowlist for Team and Enterprise administrators; on Claude Desktop on 3P inference is billed by the configured provider.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Standard: Anthropic API, web application loaded from claude.ai, conversations stored on Anthropic's backend. 3P: the configured provider (gateway, anthropic, bedrock, mantle, vertex or foundry), web application bundled in the app, conversations on local disk.

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: Prompts, attachments, Quick Entry screenshots and the results of local MCP and extension tool calls go to the inference provider with the chat; the app loads code and user content from Anthropic hosts (claude.ai, *.claude.com, *.claudeusercontent.com, *.claudemcpcontent.com and others); local MCP servers and extensions make their own network calls from the device.

facts.label: Retention & training
facts.value: Standard: chats follow the claude.ai organisation's retention (toolClaudeWeb). 3P: conversations, projects and memory stay on the device, unencrypted (sign-in tokens and saved keys are encrypted with the OS secure storage), until chatSessionRetentionDays deletes idle chats.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: support.claude.com Claude Desktop collection (Enterprise configuration, deploy for macOS and Windows, desktop extensions) plus claude.com/docs/third-party/claude-desktop for 3P and code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop for the Code tab and network requirements

facts.label: Updates
facts.value: macOS and Windows builds update themselves (Windows checks about every four hours) unless disableAutoUpdates is set; a downloaded update forces a restart after autoUpdaterEnforcementHours (72 by default); Linux updates arrive through Anthropic's apt repository and the app does not update itself.

items.title: Device policy
body: Standard deployments read the keys on the Help Center's Enterprise configuration page from the macOS configuration-profile domain com.anthropic.claudefordesktop, the Windows HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Claude registry key (machine-level settings take priority over HKCU when both are configured) or the root-owned Linux file /etc/claude-desktop/managed-settings.json: isLocalDevMcpEnabled (local MCP servers), isDesktopExtensionEnabled and isDesktopExtensionDirectoryEnabled (extensions and the directory), forceLoginOrgUUID (one UUID or a JSON array), isClaudeCodeForDesktopEnabled (the Code tab), secureVmFeaturesEnabled (Cowork), allowedWorkspaceFolders (Cowork folders), effortLevel, disableAutoUpdates and autoUpdaterEnforcementHours. The app reads them at launch, so a change needs a quit and reopen; device policy overrides the in-app allowlist.

Claude Desktop on 3P reads a wider key set from the same stores, a bootstrap server or the Enterprise Admin Console: managedMcpServers with a per-tool toolPolicy (allow, ask, blocked) enforced in the desktop host process, mcpPersistentAlwaysAllowEnabled, allowedPluginMcpServers and deniedPluginMcpServers, isDesktopExtensionSignatureRequired, developerModeEnabled (unpacked extensions), quickEntryScreenshotsEnabled and quickEntryFileSharingEnabled, disableDeploymentModeChooser, disableDeepLinkRegistration, egressProxyUrl (a route, not an access control), otlpEndpoint and otlpContentCapture, chatSessionRetentionDays and the telemetry and update keys.

links.title: Device management policies (Claude Code Desktop docs)

items.title: Local MCP servers and desktop extensions
body: A server defined in claude_desktop_config.json is available in Desktop chat and local Code tab sessions; desktop extensions are .mcpb packages installed from the Anthropic-reviewed directory or from a file, run locally with a built-in Node.js runtime, and are available only in Claude Desktop and Claude Code, not on the web or mobile. Extension settings marked sensitive are encrypted with the OS secure storage, and directory extensions update automatically by default.

The desktop extension allowlist (Team and Enterprise Owners, Organization settings > Connectors > Desktop) ships off, so every directory extension is installable until an Owner turns it on; turning it on force-deletes installed extensions that are not listed, stops drag-and-drop installs and lets Owners upload org-scoped custom .mcpb extensions. It does not guard against tampering with local MCP files after installation, and it does not see servers in claude_desktop_config.json.

items.title: What reaches the computer through the app
body: Cloud sessions reach a member's local files or browser only through Claude Desktop on that device, only for connected folders and only while the app is online; the device keys govern that reach as well. On Enterprise the Computer access capability on custom roles decides who may reach their computer from scheduled tasks, Claude on the web or Claude Mobile (sessions started in Claude Desktop itself are not affected), and Require trusted devices asks for an enrolled device and a recent sign-in. isLocalDevMcpEnabled false also skips the setup that connects the app to Claude in Chrome.

Quick Entry on macOS captures screenshots and other apps' windows with Screen Recording and Accessibility permissions; claude:// links can open the app with a prefilled prompt that the user still sends, and a folder passed in a link is always confirmed before use. Computer use in the Code tab is a Pro, Max and Ultra research preview, not offered on Team or Enterprise.

links.title: Claude Cowork architecture overview (cloud sessions reach devices through the app)
