riskNotes.note: Servers a user adds to claude_desktop_config.json run on the device and appear in no console list; the extension allowlist does not see them. isLocalDevMcpEnabled false is the only administrator control on standard deployments, and EDR or MDM inventory is how they are found.

Until an Owner turns on the allowlist every directory extension is installable, directory extensions update themselves, and a .mcpb can be installed from a file; signed-extension enforcement (isDesktopExtensionSignatureRequired) is a 3P key.

Local servers and extensions read local files and internal systems with the user's own access and return the results into a chat that goes to the inference provider; Quick Entry adds screenshots and other apps' windows. Inference hooks see the text that reaches the model, not image bytes.

A personal claude.ai account in the desktop app on a managed device carries the same local reach; forceLoginOrgUUID pins sign-in to the organisation, and on 3P disableDeploymentModeChooser stops users leaving the managed configuration by signing in to claude.ai.

Tool results from local servers and extensions, and pages reached through Claude in Chrome, enter the conversation as content Claude may follow; claude:// links only prefill a prompt and folders passed in a link are confirmed before use.

controls.mechanism: "Require SSO for Claude" sends every interactive sign-in, the desktop app's included, through the IdP, whose MFA policy applies; forceLoginOrgUUID pins Claude Desktop to the organisation on managed devices; "Shortened session length" bounds how long a sign-in lasts (Enterprise); "Require trusted devices" asks for an enrolled device and a sign-in under 18 hours old before remote sessions reach a computer

steps.title: Enforce SSO
body: After domain verification and IdP setup, toggle on "Require SSO for Claude" under Organization settings > Organization and access > Authentication, and require MFA in the IdP.

steps.title: Pin the desktop app to your organisation
body: Deploy forceLoginOrgUUID in com.anthropic.claudefordesktop, HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Claude or /etc/claude-desktop/managed-settings.json; login fails for any account outside the listed organisations.

steps.title: Bound session lifetime (Enterprise)
body: At Organization settings > Organization and access > Session security enable "Shortened session length" so users sign in, and meet the IdP's MFA, again.

steps.title: Require trusted devices for reaching the computer
body: Turn on "Require trusted devices" at Organization settings > Capabilities > Remote sessions.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to toolClaudeCowork: MFA is configured in the IdP, not in Claude, which documents no second-factor requirement of its own. Paths that skip a fresh challenge: the desktop's signed-in session (kept while the user stays active unless Shortened session length is set) and personal accounts on unmanaged devices. Trusted Devices is a beta and applies only to sessions started after it is turned on. Claude Desktop on 3P has no Anthropic identity unless managed from the admin console; sign-in is the provider's or the organisation's IdP.

controls.mechanism: Standard deployments: on/off device keys for local MCP servers (isLocalDevMcpEnabled) and desktop extensions (isDesktopExtensionEnabled) and the extension allowlist, with no per-tool rule for a local server; Claude Desktop on 3P: managedMcpServers toolPolicy (allow / ask / blocked per tool name, with wildcards) enforced in the desktop host process, plus allowedPluginMcpServers and deniedPluginMcpServers

steps.title: Remove local tools where they are not needed
body: Set isLocalDevMcpEnabled false and, unless you govern extensions with the allowlist, isDesktopExtensionEnabled false in the Claude Desktop policy.

steps.title: Write per-tool policy for managed servers (Claude Desktop on 3P)
body: Give each managedMcpServers entry a toolPolicy, for example "*": "blocked" with exact "allow" entries for approved tools; when isLocalDevMcpEnabled false comes from the same MDM profile, only that profile's local managed servers start.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: on standard deployments the decision is whole-server or whole-extension, because connector permissions "don't govern connectors a member runs locally on their own machine", and nothing matches a local tool's arguments. The 3P toolPolicy is a deterministic per-tool decision enforced outside the prompt UI, but it matches tool names only and covers only servers listed in managedMcpServers; Claude Code's own managed settings take priority in Code sessions. Policy for the Code and Cowork tabs is on toolClaudeCode and toolClaudeCowork.

controls.mechanism: The Anthropic Trust Center (certifications, the Claude Cowork Desktop Security Architecture Overview and the Claude Desktop Security Overview for third-party platforms) and the Help Center certifications list feed the organisation's TPRM platform

evidence.title: Claude Desktop on 3P overview (Trust Center security overviews for the desktop app)
What Certifications has Anthropic obtained?
Legal and compliance (Claude Desktop on 3P)

controls.note: External by the rule applied to every vendor: the questionnaire, evidence expiry and reassessment trigger live in the organisation's TPRM platform. The Help Center lists the HIPAA-ready configuration, ISO 27001:2022, ISO/IEC 42001:2023 and SOC 2 Type I and Type II; the two desktop security overviews are behind a Trust Center access request. Assess the installer and updater as endpoint software (CVE-2026-22561 below); on Claude Desktop on 3P the compliance posture of inference follows the configured provider.

controls.mechanism: Inference hooks (Enterprise) hold each governed Claude Desktop chat request, including the results of local MCP and extension tool calls, for an allow or deny verdict from the organisation's DLP server; isLocalDevMcpEnabled and isDesktopExtensionEnabled remove the local sources; on 3P, quickEntryScreenshotsEnabled and quickEntryFileSharingEnabled stop Quick Entry capturing the screen or other apps' files

steps.title: Put your DLP inline (Enterprise)
body: At Organization settings > Data and privacy > Inference hooks turn on Allow for your organization, register the endpoint and signing secret, set Failure handling to Block the request and turn on Enforce verdicts.

steps.title: Turn off screen capture in Quick Entry (Claude Desktop on 3P)
body: Set quickEntryScreenshotsEnabled false (and quickEntryFileSharingEnabled false) where screenshots of other apps must not reach the model.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to toolClaudeWeb: the hook that can block is an attach point, and nothing in the app masks or tokenises a value. The hook never receives image bytes, so a Quick Entry screenshot is not inspected, and it is not available on Bedrock or Google Cloud. Removing local servers or capture is minimisation, not detection; quickEntryScreenshotsEnabled leaves a local server or extension that captures the screen untouched. Standard deployments have no Quick Entry key.

controls.mechanism: isLocalDevMcpEnabled, isDesktopExtensionEnabled and isDesktopExtensionDirectoryEnabled on the device, the desktop extension allowlist (Organization settings > Connectors > Desktop), the Computer access capability on Enterprise custom roles, and isClaudeCodeForDesktopEnabled for the Code tab; on 3P, managedMcpServers toolPolicy and allowedPluginMcpServers

steps.title: Admit only the extensions you approve
body: Toggle Allowlist on under Organization settings > Connectors > Desktop and add only approved extensions; leave isDesktopExtensionEnabled and isDesktopExtensionDirectoryEnabled unset so the list populates.

steps.title: Turn off locally configured servers
body: Set isLocalDevMcpEnabled false in the Claude Desktop policy.

steps.title: Decide who may reach their computer remotely (Enterprise)
body: Turn Computer access off under Remote sessions on the Capabilities tab of each custom role whose members do not need to reach their computer from the web, mobile or scheduled tasks.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: administrators admit or remove whole extensions and servers, but a local server's tools cannot be scoped per tool or per argument on standard deployments, and an admitted extension acts with whatever the user's account can reach on the device. Per-tool scoping exists only in the 3P managedMcpServers toolPolicy. The Code and Cowork tabs scope their own tools (toolClaudeCode, toolClaudeCowork).

controls.mechanism: Local MCP servers and desktop extensions run as ordinary host processes with the user's permissions; the app offers no sandbox for them, only their removal

evidence.title: Claude Cowork architecture overview (local plugin MCP servers run natively on the device)
Deploying enterprise-grade MCP servers with desktop extensions (direct filesystem and OS access)
Enterprise configuration for Claude Desktop

controls.note: None: Anthropic describes desktop extensions as giving "direct filesystem access", control of desktop applications and access to systems behind the firewall with the user's own authenticated context, and local plugin MCP servers run natively on the device. The organisation's choices are to remove them (isLocalDevMcpEnabled, isDesktopExtensionEnabled), to deliver tools as remote connectors instead, or to run the work in Cowork, whose VM is the isolation boundary (toolClaudeCowork). Cloud sessions reaching the device get only the folder-limited desktop file tools once local servers are off, which is an application-layer scope, not isolation.

controls.mechanism: Account memory, which Desktop chats share with claude.ai, is available on Team and Enterprise only where an Owner allows it at Organization settings > Capabilities, and off for each member until they turn it on; on 3P, history, projects and memory stay on the device and chatSessionRetentionDays deletes idle chats

steps.title: Decide on memory
body: Leave memory off or turn it on at Organization settings > Capabilities (and grant the Memory capability per role on Enterprise).

steps.title: Bound local history (Claude Desktop on 3P)
body: Set chatSessionRetentionDays so idle chats and their files are deleted from the device.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to toolClaudeCowork: memory can be disabled and local history bounded, but nothing validates what is written. On 3P, chatSessionRetentionDays keeps projects and memory, skips open or running sessions, and conversations on disk are not encrypted. Local servers and extensions keep whatever state they write on the device, outside every Claude setting.

controls.mechanism: Anthropic's model-layer defenses (no administrator setting); Inference hooks (Enterprise) hand each governed Desktop chat request, including returned local tool results, to the organisation's AI security server before the next inference step

steps.title: Put a screen on returned tool content (Enterprise)
body: At Organization settings > Data and privacy > Inference hooks register an AI security server that classifies tool results for injection, set Failure handling to Block the request and turn on Enforce verdicts.

controls.note: Partial on the rule applied to every vendor: vendor-internal defenses documented only in general terms, plus an inline hook that is an attach point until the organisation's server does the classifying. The hook returns allow or deny only, never receives tool definitions, so a poisoned local server description is not seen, and ignores images.

controls.mechanism: Desktop extension settings marked sensitive are encrypted with Keychain, Windows Credential Manager or the Linux keyring; "Shortened session length" bounds the sign-in (Enterprise); on 3P, sign-in tokens and OAuth tokens are encrypted with Keychain or DPAPI, transient credential files are owner-only, and inferenceCredentialHelper with inferenceCredentialHelperTtlSec replaces static keys

steps.title: Bound the sign-in lifetime (Enterprise)
body: Enable "Shortened session length" under Organization settings > Organization and access > Session security.

steps.title: Use a credential helper on third-party deployments
body: Set inferenceCredentialHelper with inferenceCredentialHelperTtlSec instead of a static inferenceAnthropicApiKey or inferenceGatewayApiKey.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: credential custody is documented for extension settings and for 3P, but not for the standard app's own claude.ai sign-in token, and a developer-added server's credentials sit in the env block of claude_desktop_config.json with no documented protection. On 3P nothing forbids a static managed key, and Bedrock and Vertex credential files are written into Code and Cowork session directories.

controls.mechanism: Admission only: the desktop extension allowlist and isDesktopExtensionDirectoryEnabled for the Anthropic-reviewed directory, isLocalDevMcpEnabled for locally configured servers; on 3P, isDesktopExtensionSignatureRequired rejects unsigned extensions

steps.title: Admit extensions by allowlist
body: Turn on Allowlist under Organization settings > Connectors > Desktop so only listed .mcpb extensions install.

steps.title: Require signed extensions (Claude Desktop on 3P)
body: Set isDesktopExtensionSignatureRequired true.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: an allowlist admits extensions but pins nothing they serve. The allowlist "does not guard against individuals tampering with local MCP file contents after installation", directory extensions update automatically, an updated custom extension is a new upload of the same name, and signature enforcement is a 3P key. Locally configured servers have no integrity check at all.

controls.mechanism: Local MCP and extension tool calls prompt the user, who can approve once or save an "Always allow"; on 3P, mcpPersistentAlwaysAllowEnabled false removes persistent approvals and a managedMcpServers toolPolicy of "ask" requires approval of every call

steps.title: Keep approvals per call (Claude Desktop on 3P)
body: Set mcpPersistentAlwaysAllowEnabled false, and set "ask" in the toolPolicy of managed servers whose tools write or send.

steps.title: Remove the tools nobody approves centrally (standard deployments)
body: Set isLocalDevMcpEnabled false where local servers are not wanted, since no console setting reaches their approval prompts.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: a present person approves local tool calls, but on standard deployments the user decides whether to keep approving (no administrator switch removes Always allow for local servers, and connector permissions do not reach them). On 3P, "ask" forces per-call approval and managed policy takes precedence over user grants, but mcpPersistentAlwaysAllowEnabled false leaves allow rules already saved in a user's Claude Code settings in force for Code sessions. Computer use in the Code tab, which acts within an app once the app is approved, is offered only on Pro, Max and Ultra plans.

controls.mechanism: The desktop extension allowlist at Organization settings > Connectors > Desktop, with org-scoped custom extensions under Custom team extensions; on 3P, managedMcpServers is the pushed server list

steps.title: Treat the allowlist as the extension register
body: Turn on Allowlist under Organization settings > Connectors > Desktop, add approved extensions and upload custom ones with "Add custom extension".

steps.title: Stop servers that no register lists
body: Set isLocalDevMcpEnabled false so servers in claude_desktop_config.json do not run.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: the allowlist is an enforced register of extensions, but it ships off, carries no owner or approval record, and does not list servers in claude_desktop_config.json, which no console or API shows; EDR or MDM inventory finds them. Plugins and skills are registered on toolClaudeWeb and toolClaudeCowork.

controls.mechanism: Standard: Desktop chats are claude.ai chats, so the Compliance API (Enterprise) returns them with their tool_use and tool_result blocks; 3P: otlpEndpoint exports Chat, Cowork and Code session events to the organisation's collector (metadata only unless otlpContentCapture adds content)

steps.title: Pull Desktop chats with their tool calls (Enterprise)
body: Create a Compliance Access Key with read:compliance_user_data at Organization settings > API and page /v1/compliance/apps/chats and each chat's messages.

steps.title: Export to your collector (Claude Desktop on 3P)
body: Set otlpEndpoint to your OpenTelemetry collector; add otlpContentCapture categories only where you need content.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: on standard deployments the chat export carries tool calls, but the messages endpoint documents integration_name and mcp_server_url without saying what they hold for a local server, nothing records what the local server process did on the device, and Team has no export. On 3P the OTLP export is administrator-set but metadata only by default, and integrity and retention are the collector's. Code and Cowork tab telemetry is on toolClaudeCode and toolClaudeCowork.

controls.mechanism: Enterprise domain claiming lists every personal Free, Pro and Max account on the verified domain and "Migrate accounts using your domain" moves or closes them; forceLoginOrgUUID and the anthropic-allowed-org-ids header prevent personal-account use on managed devices and networks

steps.title: Pin the desktop app to your organisation
body: Deploy forceLoginOrgUUID in the Claude Desktop policy on every managed device.

steps.title: Review personal accounts on your domain (Enterprise)
body: After domain verification and SSO enforcement, review the personal accounts on the domain and turn on "Migrate accounts using your domain" under Organization settings > Organization and access > Security.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to toolClaudeCowork: the vendor discovers personal accounts on the verified domain, not Claude Desktop installs, accounts on personal addresses or the local servers and extensions running on devices, which remain for EDR or MDM inventory and SSE/CASB. forceLoginOrgUUID prevents rather than discovers.

controls.mechanism: isLocalDevMcpEnabled and isDesktopExtensionEnabled false on managed devices (read at launch); turning on the allowlist force-deletes unlisted extensions; Computer access off on a custom role; member removal or SCIM ends the sign-in's access

steps.title: Remove local tools from managed devices
body: Set isLocalDevMcpEnabled and isDesktopExtensionEnabled false in com.anthropic.claudefordesktop or HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Claude, then have the app restarted.

steps.title: Withdraw an extension
body: Remove it from the allowlist at Organization settings > Connectors > Desktop with "Remove from allowlist".

steps.title: Cut a member off
body: Remove the person from the IdP app with SCIM so their seat, and the app's sign-in, end.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: device keys apply when Claude Desktop launches, so a running server stops only after a restart, and the delay for an allowlist removal or a role change (up to 15 minutes) to stop a server already running is not documented. An EDR process kill is the external complement for a local server; cloud sessions and the Code and Cowork tabs have their own switches (toolClaudeCodeWeb, toolClaudeCode, toolClaudeCowork).

controls.mechanism: Host EDR sees Claude Desktop and the local MCP servers and extensions it starts as host processes (extensions run on the app's built-in Node.js runtime); the app analyses no process behaviour

evidence.title: Getting started with local MCP servers on Claude Desktop (built-in Node.js runtime, logs)
Claude Cowork architecture overview (what runs natively on the device)
Deploy Claude Desktop for Windows (MSIX, AppLocker)

controls.note: External (EDR) by the rule applied to every endpoint product: integration points are the MDM-deployed app (PKG, MSIX or the apt package), the server and extension processes it spawns, which the host sensor can see, and the per-server logs in the app's Extensions settings. The Cowork VM is opaque to host sensors (toolClaudeCowork).

controls.mechanism: Local MCP servers and extensions use the device's network with no destination policy in the app; the documented Anthropic host list and, on 3P, egressProxyUrl ("a route, not a network access control") are the integration points for the organisation's SSE or host firewall

evidence.title: Claude Code Desktop docs — network access requirements
Claude Desktop on 3P configuration reference (egressProxyUrl)
Deploying enterprise-grade MCP servers with desktop extensions (no firewall rules needed)

controls.note: External (SSE, host firewall) by the rule: Anthropic presents desktop extensions as reaching internal systems "without requiring additional firewall rules or VPN configurations", and the app applies no egress allowlist to them. Cowork's VM egress policy (toolClaudeCowork) and the Code tab's sandbox (toolClaudeCode) do not cover local servers started by the app.

controls.mechanism: Directory extensions are Anthropic-reviewed and installable only from the sanctioned registry once the allowlist is on; on 3P, isDesktopExtensionSignatureRequired rejects extensions not signed by a trusted publisher

steps.title: Require signed extensions (Claude Desktop on 3P)
body: Set isDesktopExtensionSignatureRequired true in the managed configuration.

steps.title: Keep installs to the reviewed registry
body: Turn on the allowlist so users can no longer drag or click to install .mcpb files.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: the product checks where an extension comes from (review, allowlist, signature on 3P) but scans no .mcpb content, and skill and plugin scanning does not cover MCP servers. Custom extensions uploaded by Owners and servers in claude_desktop_config.json are not analysed; an endpoint anti-malware product scans the files on disk.

settings.name: Require SSO for Claude
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Organization and access › Authentication
settings.recommended: On, with MFA enforced on the Claude app in your IdP
settings.why: Every interactive claude.ai and Claude Desktop login goes through the corporate IdP and its MFA; personal email logins on your domain stop working.

settings.name: Shortened session length
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Organization and access › Session security
settings.default: Not enabled (sign-in kept while the user stays active)
settings.recommended: 7 days
settings.why: The Claude Desktop sign-in expires weekly, so a stolen or stale session meets the IdP's MFA again.

settings.name: forceLoginOrgUUID
settings.where: Claude Desktop policy (com.anthropic.claudefordesktop / HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Claude) → forceLoginOrgUUID
settings.recommended: Your organisation's UUID
settings.why: On managed devices Claude Desktop refuses a login to any other organisation, personal accounts included.

settings.name: Migrate accounts using your domain
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Organization and access › Security
settings.recommended: On, after reviewing the personal accounts listed on your domain
settings.why: No Free, Pro or Max account can exist on the verified domain, so work chats can't sit in personal plans no admin sees; it can't be reversed.

settings.name: Tenant Restrictions (anthropic-allowed-org-ids)
settings.where: Corporate TLS-inspecting proxy → anthropic-allowed-org-ids header on Claude traffic
settings.recommended: Your organisation's UUID, injected for every managed device
settings.why: Personal and other organisations' Claude accounts can't sign in from the corporate network, on any device or browser.

settings.name: Require trusted devices
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Capabilities › Remote sessions
settings.recommended: On
settings.why: Reaching back into a member's computer from a cloud session needs an enrolled device and a sign-in under 18 hours old, not just a signed-in account.

settings.name: Computer access (custom role capability)
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Roles › role › Capabilities › Remote sessions
settings.default: On for roles that include Chat, Claude Code, Cowork or Claude in Chrome while it is on for the organisation
settings.recommended: Granted only on the roles of groups that need to reach their own computer from the web, mobile or scheduled tasks
settings.why: Scheduled tasks, Claude on the web and Claude Mobile reach a member's files, apps and browser through the desktop app only for those groups; sessions started in Claude Desktop itself are unaffected.

settings.name: isLocalDevMcpEnabled
settings.where: Claude Desktop policy → isLocalDevMcpEnabled
settings.recommended: false
settings.why: Local MCP servers from claude_desktop_config.json and plugins run on the device with the user's permissions, outside the connector list and tool policy; off also stops the app connecting to Claude in Chrome.

settings.name: isDesktopExtensionEnabled
settings.where: Claude Desktop policy → isDesktopExtensionEnabled, isDesktopExtensionDirectoryEnabled
settings.recommended: Unset, so the allowlist decides which extensions load
settings.why: isDesktopExtensionEnabled false stops installed extensions loading and blocks new installs, and either key set to false overrides the in-app allowlist; keep them as the off switch for machines that must run no extensions.

settings.name: Allowlist (desktop extensions)
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Connectors › Desktop
settings.default: Off (every extension in the registry installable)
settings.recommended: On, with only approved extensions added; leave isDesktopExtensionEnabled unset so the list populates
settings.why: Desktop extensions are blocked by default, installed ones outside the list are removed, and members install only the .mcpb servers you list.

settings.name: isClaudeCodeForDesktopEnabled
settings.where: Claude Desktop policy → isClaudeCodeForDesktopEnabled
settings.recommended: false, except on devices of the groups that hold Claude Code
settings.why: The Code tab runs commands and edits files on the device; off, chat users don't get a coding agent their role was never meant to have.

settings.name: Inference hooks
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Data and privacy › Inference hooks
settings.recommended: On, connected to your DLP or AI-security service, enforcing after a monitor-only period
settings.why: Each Claude Desktop chat request, results from local MCP servers and extensions included, is checked by your own service before inference, so secrets and injected content can be stopped centrally.

settings.name: Memory
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Capabilities
settings.default: Off (each member opts in once an Owner allows it)
settings.recommended: Off; projects keep their own context
settings.why: Account memory carries details across chats, so one engagement's material could resurface in another client's work; teams that want it get it per role.

settings.name: Compliance API
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › API, then a Compliance Access Key with read:compliance_user_data
settings.recommended: On, pulled into your SIEM and eDiscovery; delete scope on a separate key
settings.why: Desktop chats are claude.ai chats, so their tool calls and results reach your own store with the rest; while it is off nothing is exported.

settings.name: disableAutoUpdates
settings.where: Claude Desktop policy → disableAutoUpdates, autoUpdaterEnforcementHours
settings.recommended: false, unless MDM pins and ships versions itself / 72
settings.why: Security fixes to Claude Desktop reach every device, restarting it within three days of a prepared update.

settings.name: Managed MCP servers (managedMcpServers)
settings.where: Claude Desktop on 3P configuration (MDM profile, bootstrap server or Enterprise Admin Console) → managedMcpServers, each entry's toolPolicy
settings.default: Unset (no servers pushed; users' own tools user-controlled)
settings.recommended: The approved servers, each with a toolPolicy of "*": "blocked" plus exact "allow" or "ask" entries
settings.why: Approved servers reach every device with unlisted tools removed, and the policy is enforced in the desktop host process, not only in the prompt.

settings.name: Allow persistent tool approvals (mcpPersistentAlwaysAllowEnabled)
settings.where: Claude Desktop on 3P configuration → mcpPersistentAlwaysAllowEnabled
settings.recommended: false
settings.why: MCP tool approvals stay per call or per task, and standing approvals users saved earlier in Chat and Cowork stop applying.

settings.name: Require signed extensions (isDesktopExtensionSignatureRequired)
settings.where: Claude Desktop on 3P configuration → isDesktopExtensionSignatureRequired
settings.recommended: true
settings.why: Desktop extensions not signed by a trusted publisher are rejected, so an unsigned or home-made .mcpb can't load.

settings.name: Disable Claude.ai sign-in (disableDeploymentModeChooser)
settings.where: Claude Desktop on 3P MDM profile → disableDeploymentModeChooser
settings.recommended: true
settings.why: Users see only your provider at sign-in and can't leave the managed configuration by signing in to claude.ai, personal accounts included.
settings.requires: Claude Desktop on 3P (not settable from the Enterprise Admin Console)

settings.name: Chat retention period (chatSessionRetentionDays)
settings.where: Claude Desktop on 3P configuration → chatSessionRetentionDays
settings.why: Chats and their files, stored unencrypted on the device in 3P mode, are deleted after 30 idle days instead of staying on laptops indefinitely; projects and memory stay.

settings.name: OTLP endpoint (otlpEndpoint)
settings.where: Claude Desktop on 3P configuration → otlpEndpoint, otlpContentCapture
settings.recommended: Your OpenTelemetry collector, forwarding to the SIEM; otlpContentCapture left unset (metadata only)
settings.why: Chat, Cowork and Code session events from every device land in the SIEM with the signed-in user, without prompt or tool content unless you add it.

tools.name: Claude Duet

variants.name: Claude Duet app (iOS and Android)
variants.note: Standalone app, separate from the Claude app; one ongoing thread plus side channels that share memory.

variants.name: Claude Duet on claude.ai

summary: A proactive personal agent operated by Anthropic. It works on its own computer in the cloud with its own browser, keeps one persistent thread, and carries the person's Claude memory, skills and connectors from the first message, and supports plugins. It sends a morning brief, checks connected accounts at set intervals and keeps working after the app is closed, asking before it sends, pays, signs or deletes anything.

It is a consumer research preview for US Pro and Max accounts by waitlist. Nothing about it is administered by an organisation: the risk for an enterprise is an employee connecting a work mailbox, calendar or Slack to it from a personal plan, which a Claude Enterprise organisation can now block for supported connectors on its verified domains.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Research preview by waitlist for Pro and Max accounts in the US, included in the plan and sharing its usage limits. Not available on Team or Enterprise.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Anthropic operates the agent and its cloud computer. It runs on Claude Opus 5.5 and sets its own effort per job; the model cannot be chosen.

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: Connected-app content, Claude memory and skills, and Claude chats outside projects reach the hosted agent. Passwords are typed into a separate form on the device and sent to the cloud browser.

facts.label: Retention & training
facts.value: The Duet documentation states no retention period or training rule; it runs on the account's settings, so training follows Help Improve our AI models (Settings > Privacy) under the Privacy Policy and Consumer Terms. Disconnecting an app keeps what Duet already learned.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: Get started with Claude Duet (support centre); product page and announcement.

facts.label: Purchases
facts.value: Link by Stripe and Shop Pay, connected inside Duet; each purchase uses a one-time card. Trading securities and moving money between accounts are refused even with approval.

items.title: Decide whether work accounts may connect to it
body: Duet has no organisation plan. A Claude Enterprise organisation can turn on Restrict verified-domain connectors to your enterprise so personal accounts cannot connect supported work connectors on its domains; for everything else, use the identity provider's or each SaaS admin console's third-party app consent controls to decide whether Claude connectors may reach work mail, calendars, drives and Slack from a personal account.

links.title: Restrict verified-domain connectors to your enterprise
Use connectors to extend Claude's capabilities

items.title: Treat the approval prompt as a bounded safeguard
body: Duet asks before sending, paying, signing or deleting, and finishes the rest of a task while an approval waits. Reading and drafting are not gated, and its cloud browser cannot be watched or taken over, so what it read on the way to a proposed action is not visible.

riskNotes.note: A personal-plan agent with standing access to a work mailbox or Slack is invisible to every admin console.
Email and web pages it reads on its own schedule can steer later work; the vendor says no defence is perfect.
Memory, connected content and Claude chats outside projects all reach the hosted agent and outlive a disconnect.
It acts with the owner's connector grants and saved browser sessions, including on items others sent.

controls.mechanism: No Duet plan or admin switch; a Claude Enterprise organisation's Restrict verified-domain connectors to your enterprise blocks personal accounts connecting supported work connectors, and the connected services' third-party app consent controls decide the rest.

evidence.title: Plan availability (not on Team or Enterprise)
Restrict verified-domain connectors to your enterprise
Connectors and where they are managed

controls.note: External: Duet runs only on individual Pro and Max accounts, so no organisation can turn it on or off. Govern it at the destination — the firm's Claude Enterprise connector domain restriction (new connections only, on services that share the account's identity), the identity provider's or Google Workspace, Microsoft 365 and Slack admins' OAuth app approval for the Claude connectors — and in acceptable-use policy for personal AI plans.

controls.mechanism: The person starts every connection and manages it in Customize > Connectors; vendor-fixed limits refuse trading securities, moving money between accounts and using someone else's account.

steps.title: Connect only what it needs
body: In Customize > Connectors, disconnect any service Duet should not reach and, per connector, set write and delete tool groups to Needs approval or Blocked under Tool permissions.

controls.note: Partial on the consumer rule: the person sets it and no organisation can require it. The Duet article does not say whether Duet honours the per-tool permissions set for Claude; verify before relying on them. Sites without a connector are reached through its cloud browser, with no per-site setting.

controls.mechanism: Approval in the Duet app before sending a message, making a payment, signing a document or deleting anything; deferred approvals return later.

steps.title: Review each approval request
body: Read the exact action Duet shows before approving; it may finish the rest of a task first, so check the draft and what it read, and mark tasks complete yourself in the Tasks tab.

controls.note: Partial on the same rule as toolOpenaiDots: the categories are vendor-defined, an auto-mode classifier decides which actions count, and the person approves in the app; nothing is configurable by an organisation and reading or drafting is never gated.

controls.mechanism: Sign-in is the person's own Claude account; no organisation SSO or MFA policy applies.

evidence.title: Plan availability and account requirements

controls.note: None for an organisation: Duet is not on Team or Enterprise, so no SSO, conditional access or MFA requirement reaches it. Any second factor is whatever the person's own sign-in method provides.

controls.mechanism: Passwords are typed into a separate on-device form and sent straight to the cloud browser, kept out of the chat; Link and Shop Pay pay with a one-time card, and Duet never receives the full card or account number.

summary: Office add-ins served from pivot.claude.ai inside Excel, PowerPoint, Word and Outlook that read and write the open file or mail thread, with connectors, skills and an optional cross-app mode. Users sign in with their Claude account (Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise) and requests go to Anthropic, or the add-in is pointed at the organisation's Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry or gateway endpoint. Chat history, uploaded skills, connector registrations and the sign-in credential live in the Office webview's browser storage on each device; Anthropic deletes inputs and outputs from its backend within 30 days.

Admins deploy and gate the add-ins through the Microsoft 365 Admin Center and toggle "Let Claude work across apps" at Organization settings > Office agents. Governance gaps are explicit in the docs: the add-ins do not inherit custom data retention and activity is not in Enterprise audit logs or data exports. Enterprise organisations with the Compliance API get add-in session transcripts (office_agents/* local sessions), which the add-in pages label public beta and the Compliance API reference calls stable. A custom OpenTelemetry collector receives the full unfiltered audit trail (prompts, tool inputs and outputs, document references) from each user's browser and must support CORS.

controls.mechanism: Microsoft 365 admin center Settings > Integrated apps assigns the add-ins to everyone, users or groups, with self-install closed by Let users access the Office Store (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and the My Marketplace Apps / My Custom Apps / My ReadWriteMailbox Apps user roles (Outlook); a documented tenant-wide Microsoft Graph admin consent to Anthropic's Claude for Office Entra app (c2995f31-11e7-4882-b7a7-ef9def0a0266) or your own single-tenant app via graph_client_id; per-user disabled_features / access_policies through Entra extension attributes or a bootstrap endpoint in custom-manifest deployments; claude.ai Organization settings > Office agents is org-wide only

steps.title: Assign the add-ins to groups
body: In the Microsoft 365 admin center go to Settings > Integrated apps > Add-ins > Deploy Add-in, choose the Claude listing or upload the manifest, and assign Specific users/groups; group membership then grants and removes access.

steps.title: Close the self-install paths
body: Clear Let users access the Office Store at Settings > Org settings > Services > User owned apps and services, and for Outlook remove My Marketplace Apps, My Custom Apps and My ReadWriteMailbox Apps from the default role assignment policy in the Exchange admin center.

steps.title: Decide the Graph consent
body: Have a Global Administrator open the documented admin-consent link for Claude for Office (Mail.ReadWrite, Calendars.Read, User.Read, offline_access), or register a single-tenant app with those delegated permissions and set graph_client_id on the manifest URL instead.

steps.title: Set per-user feature policy
body: In custom-manifest deployments deliver disabled_features (comma-separated) through Entra ID extension attributes, or access_policies statements through the manifest or a bootstrap endpoint, so features vary by user.

steps.title: Consolidate accounts on your domain
body: On Enterprise, turn on Migrate accounts using your domain under Organization settings > Organization and access > Security, so new accounts on the domain go straight through SSO into the workspace instead of becoming personal accounts.

steps.title: Put Conditional Access on the Entra sign-in
body: Target an MFA Conditional Access policy at the Claude for Office enterprise application (c2995f31-11e7-4882-b7a7-ef9def0a0266), or at your own single-tenant app set with graph_client_id, which governs the Outlook Graph token and Entra sign-in on Bedrock direct, keyless Foundry and gateway_auth_source=entra deployments.

controls.note: Native by the rule, with the add-in's authorization plane split across two consoles. The Microsoft side decides who may run the add-in (group assignment; unassigned users are blocked only once the Office Store setting and the Exchange add-in user roles, both on by default, are closed) and whether the Graph grant exists at all: Anthropic documents the consent URL, the app ID, the verified publisher (Anthropic, PBC), the redirect URIs and the delegated scopes, plus a single-tenant alternative whose approval and Conditional Access the organisation owns (the setup plugin's manifest command also lists People.Read for that app; the Outlook page lists four scopes). That consent is the Microsoft 365 tenant's own control. The claude.ai side is coarse: Organization settings > Office agents switches cross-app mode for everyone, Enterprise custom roles do not list the add-ins, and model access follows the member's role. Per-user feature policy exists only where configuration keys are delivered, which the docs describe for third-party-platform deployments. Personal Pro and Max accounts can sign in to the same AppSource add-in; domain capture covers only verified domains.

original.mechanism: Claude account sign-in (SSO/SCIM at the organisation) plus Microsoft 365 Admin Center add-in assignment; Entra ID identity in third-party mode

steps.title: Assign the add-ins to users
body: Manage member access to the Excel, PowerPoint, Word and Outlook add-ins through the Microsoft 365 Admin Center and grant the one-time Microsoft Graph consent for Outlook.

steps.title: Enforce the Claude organisation
body: Require SSO for Claude and use domain capture so the add-in sign-in lands in the managed organisation.

original.mechanism: The add-in reads only the currently open file or the open email; Outlook access is bounded by the Graph consent granted by the admin

steps.title: Scope Graph consent
body: Grant only the Microsoft Graph permissions the Outlook add-in documents during the one-time admin consent.

original.note: Delegated: the open document is what the user already has; Outlook retrieval carries the Graph consent the admin granted, so that consent, not the user's mailbox permissions, is the ceiling.

controls.mechanism: The anthropic-allowed-org-ids tenant-restriction header, injected by the organisation's proxy on claude.ai, api.anthropic.com, claude.com and anthropic.com (Enterprise), covers the add-in's Claude-account sign-in and inference; the per-path domain allowlist; disabled_features web_search removes Anthropic-served web search and fetch in custom-manifest deployments

steps.title: Inject the tenant-restriction header
body: Have your proxy add anthropic-allowed-org-ids with your organisation UUIDs on claude.ai, api.anthropic.com, claude.com and anthropic.com; a request for any other organisation fails with 403 tenant_restriction_violation.

steps.title: Allow only the documented destinations
body: Permit pivot.claude.ai, claude.ai, api.anthropic.com, appsforoffice.microsoft.com and, when used, login.microsoftonline.com, graph.microsoft.com, mcp-proxy.anthropic.com and bridge.claudeusercontent.com (Claude account), or your gateway and cloud endpoints (third-party platform).

steps.title: Keep web search inside your network
body: In custom-manifest deployments set disabled_features=web_search and attach an in-network search tool with mcp_servers, so search queries stop going to Anthropic's search provider.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: Anthropic enforces the tenant block server-side and the organisation's SSE injects the header. The header article lists web, desktop, API-key and OAuth-token access but does not name the Office add-ins, so confirm with a personal-organisation sign-in through the proxy. A customer proxy does not control egress Anthropic performs for the add-in: built-in web search and web fetch (Anthropic's search provider), code-execution containers and MCP connector calls through mcp-proxy.anthropic.com leave from Anthropic's cloud. On third-party platforms inference goes only to the organisation's gateway or cloud endpoint, so the header is moot there and the gateway is the egress point.

original.mechanism: pivot.claude.ai and the model endpoint are ordinary HTTPS from the Office webview; tenant-restriction header and IP allowlisting apply to claude.ai traffic

steps.title: Keep add-in traffic in the corporate tenant
body: Inject anthropic-allowed-org-ids at the proxy for claude.ai and api.anthropic.com so the add-in cannot sign in to a personal organisation.

original.note: The add-in itself offers nothing; the vendor-side tenant restriction is credited on the Claude chat entity, and the proxy that enforces the header is the organisation's SSE. Confirm the Office webview honours the proxy before relying on it.

original.mechanism: Only pivot.claude.ai, the model endpoint, the identity provider and the configured OTel collector are contacted; third-party mode keeps content inside your endpoint

steps.title: Allowlist the documented destinations
body: Permit pivot.claude.ai plus your model endpoint and collector; in third-party mode conversation content goes only to your Vertex, Bedrock, Azure or gateway endpoint.

original.note: The add-in documents a small fixed destination set; it enforces no policy of its own, and the Office webview's traffic must be bounded by the proxy or SSE.

controls.mechanism: access_policies statements that deny addin.access on an open document, or file.upload of an attached file, by Microsoft Purview sensitivity label GUID (mip_label_guid), label name or file path, with an allow-list mode and fail-closed handling of unreadable labels (manifest or bootstrap); Microsoft's Allow programmatic access = false label option keeps Outlook add-ins off encrypted mail; Inference hooks (Enterprise, Claude-account sign-in) hold each add-in request, tool results and extracted attachment text included, for an allow or deny verdict from the organisation's DLP server; nothing in the add-in detects content itself

steps.title: Put your DLP inline (Enterprise)
body: At claude.ai Organization settings > Data and privacy > Inference hooks turn on Allow for your organization, register your DLP server, set Failure handling to Block the request and turn on Enforce verdicts; one hook governs Claude for Microsoft 365 with the organisation's other Claude products.

steps.title: Block the add-in on labelled content
body: Add access_policies deny statements for addin.access with an open_file resource matching your restricted sublabel GUIDs, and for file.upload with an uploaded_file resource on the same labels, and deliver the array in the manifest or bootstrap response.

steps.title: Keep Outlook add-ins off encrypted mail
body: For sensitivity labels that encrypt mail, set the Allow programmatic access custom policy option to false; Outlook add-ins do not activate on those items.

steps.title: Scan transcripts after the fact
body: Pull office_agents/* local session transcripts from the Compliance API into your DLP scanner; this detects after the prompt was sent and cannot block it.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: label-based restriction without content detection. access_policies reads the label, not the content — an unlabelled document carrying card numbers passes unless labels are allow-listed (the first allow flips that scope to default-deny, and exists: false refuses unlabelled files). It gates only the open document and uploaded attachments: text the user types or pastes, mail read through Graph (thread retrieval, search, attachments read inline), connector results and cross-app context are not documented as label-checked, and the key is documented for manifest and bootstrap delivery, not the AppSource install with Claude sign-in. Microsoft Purview lists DLP and sensitivity labels as unsupported for Anthropic Claude interactions. Anthropic's Inference hooks now name Claude for Microsoft 365 among the products one hook governs, so an Enterprise organisation's DLP server can deny a request carrying typed, pasted or document content before inference — an attach point that allows or denies only (no masking), never sees image bytes, and does not reach third-party-platform deployments, where the organisation's gateway is the inline point. The OpenTelemetry collector and Compliance API see prompts only after they were sent.

original.mechanism: Custom OpenTelemetry collector receives prompts and document references for detection; no inline blocking; Inference hooks are documented for claude.ai, Cowork and Claude Code, not M365

steps.title: Route the audit trail to your DLP pipeline
body: Configure a custom collector endpoint (CORS-enabled, forwarding to your backend) so spans with prompt content and tool inputs reach your inspection tooling.

original.note: The telemetry collector sees prompts after the fact; it cannot block. Preventive DLP on document and mail content is the endpoint DLP or SSE product, and Inference hooks are not documented for the add-ins.

original.mechanism: The add-in is a web page in the Office webview (WebView2 / macOS container); browser and endpoint tooling see it as pivot.claude.ai traffic
original.note: No vendor inspection point; Office on the web places the add-in in a third-party frame that browsers partition.

steps.title: Treat pivot.claude.ai as a governed SaaS origin
body: Apply your web-content policy to https://pivot.claude.ai and the configured model endpoint.

controls.mechanism: No documented screening of document, mail, attachment or connector content by the add-in itself; Inference hooks (Enterprise, Claude-account sign-in) hand each governed request, tool calls and tool results included, to the organisation's AI security server before the next inference step; on third-party platforms every model request passes the organisation's LLM gateway (gateway_url, or azure_base_url for Foundry), the inline point for an AI gateway's injection classifier

steps.title: Put a screen on document, mail and tool content (Enterprise)
body: At claude.ai Organization settings > Data and privacy > Inference hooks register an AI security server that classifies tool results for injection, set Failure handling to Block the request and turn on Enforce verdicts.

steps.title: Screen at your gateway on third-party platforms
body: Point gateway_url (or azure_base_url for Foundry) at a gateway that runs your injection classifier; every /v1/messages request from the add-in passes it.

steps.title: Know what the user is told to check
body: The Outlook page tells users to review drafts from untrusted senders; there is no screening setting in the add-in.

controls.note: Partial on the rule applied to every vendor, raised from external on 2026-10-30: the Inference hooks page now names Claude for Microsoft 365 among the products one hook governs, an inline attach point that is partial until the organisation's server does the classifying. It returns allow or deny only (no strip or quarantine), never receives system prompts, tool definitions or image bytes, covers only Enterprise organisations signed in with Claude accounts, and is not available on Bedrock or Google Cloud. An AI gateway placed on the third-party gateway path sees every /v1/messages request — open-document content, email bodies and tool results included — and can block it. The Excel, PowerPoint and Word pages say risky operations ask for confirmation and the Outlook page tells users to review drafts from untrusted senders; confirmation gates the action, not the input, and is credited under human approval. Turning off Let Claude work across apps (Organization settings > Office agents) stops an email's instructions steering an edit in another app — containment, not screening.

original.mechanism: Anthropic model-side safeguards only; document and email content is the untrusted input
original.note: No admin-tunable detector; the vendor documents no add-in-specific injection controls.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: a present human confirms, and in custom-manifest deployments the administrator can keep users in "Ask before edits" and remove "Dangerously always allow", but connector "Always allow" choices are unaffected by those slugs, and with a Claude-account install from AppSource the administrator cannot require approval and users can hold a standing approval (auto_accept). The add-in decides which operations count as risky; Word's tracked-changes mode is one the user enters, not a policy; Outlook's move and flag operations run through Graph under Mail.ReadWrite and whether they prompt is not documented. Connector Tool permissions are documented for claude.ai connectors; the add-in pages say connectors are enabled in Claude settings but do not state that Needs approval is enforced in the add-ins. On third-party platforms connectors are "coming soon" and admin-attached mcp_servers carry no approval setting.

controls.mechanism: No inventory or classification in the product: the add-in keeps no index and reaches the open file, the user's own mailbox and calendar through Graph (Outlook) and user-connected connectors; OpenTelemetry document.url per turn and Compliance API transcripts record which documents were sent, and the data-storage page maps the device-side stores

Configure a custom OpenTelemetry collector (document.url on agent.query spans)
