controls.note: External: inventory and oversharing discovery of the SharePoint, OneDrive and Exchange content the add-in can reach belong to the DSPM / data-classification product (Microsoft Purview DSPM, for example); the add-in reaches whatever the user opens or their delegated Graph scope allows. It contributes a use record, not an inventory: document.url on every agent.query span, and file contents in Compliance API transcripts (Enterprise). Purview's Anthropic Claude connector (preview) imports the activity feed and chat conversations through the Compliance API; session transcripts, where add-in activity sits, are not among its listed data types. The device-side stores (claude-chat-history holds attached file contents) are an endpoint data store for the organisation's own inventory; the 30-day backend deletion and the 50-conversation cap are retention, not inventory.

original.mechanism: Backend deletion within 30 days; local store bounded to 50 conversations per user/org/app; users can delete all history; export scripts before reimaging; no admin retention setting

steps.title: Manage the device-side store
body: Use the claude-for-msft-365-install plugin export scripts before rebuilds and treat exports as secrets (they contain credentials); control lifetime through profile cleanup rather than an add-in setting.

original.note: Lifecycle only: nothing here discovers or classifies sensitive content in the local store; that is the endpoint DLP or DSPM product's job.

controls.mechanism: Graph and cloud-provider tokens are obtained and used on the device and never reach Anthropic or the model; Claude sign-in, connector and gateway credentials sit unencrypted in the webview's localStorage; keyless options (gateway_auth_source=entra, Bedrock via Entra-to-STS, keyless Foundry) and a bootstrap_url that re-issues the gateway token about five minutes before its declared expiry let the administrator bound credential lifetime; no tunnel

steps.title: Replace static keys with Entra-issued tokens
body: Set entra_sso=1, graph_client_id, entra_scope and gateway_auth_source=entra so the add-in sends each user's short-lived Entra access token to your gateway or Foundry resource and ignores any gateway_token or azure_api_key.

steps.title: Issue gateway tokens from a bootstrap endpoint
body: Serve the gateway token from bootstrap_url with an expiry; the add-in calls the endpoint again about five minutes before expiry and once on a 401, so tokens rotate without users signing out.

steps.title: Keep secrets out of the manifest query string
body: Put gateway_token, azure_api_key, google_client_secret, otlp_headers, inference_headers and mcp_servers after # in the manifest URL; the add-in ignores them in the query string from October 19, 2026.

steps.title: Issue connector credentials from your own endpoint
body: In custom-manifest deployments provision connectors per user with mcp_servers from a bootstrap endpoint, so the credential is one your endpoint issues and expires rather than a user's OAuth grant on the device.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: the administrator can bound lifetime and rotation for the gateway credential (Entra or bootstrap), but the Claude-account access and refresh tokens and MCP connector tokens are held unencrypted in the add-in's localStorage — the OS account is the only boundary — with no admin lifetime or rotation setting, and a static gateway token or API key is a shared secret on every device, held until changed and copied into data exports. Custody is otherwise sound where documented: the Graph token stays in the MSAL cache and goes only to graph.microsoft.com, and the redirect through pivot.claude.ai carries only a code or a consent outcome. Anthropic offers no tunnel for the add-ins; admin-attached mcp_servers are called directly from the user's browser. Shared OS accounts share uploaded skills and connector registrations.

original.mechanism: Cloud-provider sign-ins use short-lived tokens renewed on device; a centrally issued gateway token or API key is a shared secret on every device

steps.title: Prefer per-user sign-in over a shared key
body: Use Entra ID / cloud-provider sign-in in third-party mode instead of distributing a gateway API key in the manifest.

original.note: Cloud sign-ins are short-lived; a centrally issued gateway token or API key is a long-lived shared secret on every device, readable from the add-in's local storage by anyone with the user's OS session.

controls.mechanism: Organization settings > Connectors enablement and per-tool Always allow / Needs approval / Blocked on claude.ai (enforcement in the add-ins not stated); Organization settings > Office agents "Let Claude work across apps" plus the per-device "Let Claude work across files"; disabled_features (web_search, file.upload, skills.authoring, permission_mode.accept_all_edits, permission_mode.dangerously_always_allow) and admin-provisioned mcp_servers in custom-manifest deployments; a fixed Graph scope set for Outlook

steps.title: Enable only vetted connectors
body: An Owner adds connectors at Organization settings > Connectors and sets each connector's Tool permissions; the add-ins offer only connectors enabled in Claude settings.

steps.title: Turn cross-app mode off where it is not needed
body: At Organization settings > Office agents turn off Let Claude work across apps; the per-device Let Claude work across files setting is off by default on Team and Enterprise.

steps.title: Remove tools in custom-manifest deployments
body: Set disabled_features (or access_policies deny statements) for web_search, file.upload and skills.authoring, and give each user only the in-network servers listed in mcp_servers.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: connector-level admission and feature switches exist, but no per-tool or read/write scoping per group is documented for the add-ins. Tool permissions are documented for claude.ai connectors, and Enterprise custom roles gate connectors per tool, yet neither page names the Office add-ins. The built-in Office tools (cell and document writes, execute_office_js) have no admin scoping, and Outlook's Graph scope is a fixed delegated set (Mail.ReadWrite, Calendars.Read, User.Read, offline_access), all-or-nothing at consent. disabled_features applies per user through Entra extension attributes or a bootstrap endpoint; access_policies only through the manifest or bootstrap.

original.mechanism: "Let Claude work across apps" org toggle at Organization settings > Office agents (no published default); a separate per-add-in, per-device "Let Claude work across files" setting is on by default for Pro/Max and off by default for Team/Enterprise; connector and skill availability follows organisation connector settings; Graph consent scopes for Outlook

steps.title: Turn cross-app mode on or off
body: At Organization settings > Office agents toggle "Let Claude work across apps"; each user's add-in also has its own "Let Claude work across files" setting in Settings, on by default on Pro/Max and off by default on Team/Enterprise.

controls.mechanism: Retrieval runs as the user: Office.js reads only the open file or the open mail item, and Outlook's Graph calls use the user's own delegated token; access_policies addin.access statements keyed on sensitivity label or file path restrict which open documents the add-in will run on (manifest or bootstrap); no admin scoping of mailboxes, folders or connector corpora

steps.title: Restrict the add-in to approved documents
body: Add an access_policies allow statement for addin.access listing your General and Public label GUIDs (default-deny for everything else), or deny statements for restricted labels and file_path prefixes such as a restricted share.

steps.title: Own the Graph application
body: Register a single-tenant app with the delegated Graph permissions and set graph_client_id, so approval and Conditional Access for mailbox access sit under your own application.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: identity-scoped retrieval holds — the open document is one the user already opened, and Graph delegated access is bounded by both the consented scopes and the user's own mailbox and calendar permissions, so whatever the user can already reach, oversharing included, is reachable. The admin restriction covers only the open document (label or path), is documented for manifest and bootstrap delivery, and does not scope mailbox search, thread retrieval or connectors. Oversharing analysis of SharePoint, OneDrive and Exchange is the DSPM product's.

original.mechanism: The add-in reads only the currently open file or the open email; Outlook access is bounded by the Graph consent granted by the admin

steps.title: Scope Graph consent
body: Grant only the Microsoft Graph permissions the Outlook add-in documents during the one-time admin consent.

original.note: Delegated: the open document is what the user already has; Outlook retrieval carries the Graph consent the admin granted, so that consent, not the user's mailbox permissions, is the ceiling.

controls.mechanism: Microsoft 365 admin center Integrated apps lists the add-ins the organisation deployed, and closing the Office Store and the Exchange add-in user roles blocks others; Organization settings > Connectors is the approved connector catalogue; Compliance API local sessions (product_surface office_agents/*) record use

steps.title: Hold the deployment record in Integrated apps
body: Deploy the Claude add-ins from Settings > Integrated apps and clear Let users access the Office Store, so users run only centrally deployed add-ins.

steps.title: Close Outlook self-install
body: Remove My Marketplace Apps, My Custom Apps and My ReadWriteMailbox Apps from the default role assignment policy under Roles > User roles in the Exchange admin center.

steps.title: Reconcile use against the record
body: List local sessions whose product_surface is office_agents/excel, office_agents/powerpoint, office_agents/word or office_agents/outlook from the Compliance API.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: enforcement exists (only deployed add-ins once self-install is closed; only Owner-enabled connectors) but there is no owner or approval record per add-in or connector. Integrated apps shows what administrators deployed, not copies users installed from AppSource while the store was open or a third-party manifest pointing the add-in at another gateway; connectors a user authorised live only on that user's device. Compliance API session listings cover Claude-account Enterprise use only.

original.mechanism: Microsoft 365 Admin Center integrated-apps inventory of deployed Claude add-ins; Compliance API local sessions with office_agents/* product_surface (beta)

steps.title: Inventory deployments and sessions
body: List deployed add-ins in the M365 Admin Center and, on Enterprise, query local sessions with product_surface office_agents/excel and similar.

original.note: The Admin Center inventory records deployment, not ownership or approval of what the add-ins may do; treat it as an input to the organisation's inventory.

controls.mechanism: Enterprise domain claiming (Organization settings > Organization and access > Security, Migrate accounts using your domain) lists personal Free, Pro and Max accounts on verified domains with plan and last-active date and a CSV export; the add-ins' Claude-account sign-in uses those same accounts

steps.title: Review personal accounts on your domains
body: Turn on Migrate accounts using your domain and review the list of existing personal accounts (email, plan, creation and last active dates), exported as CSV, before claiming them.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: the domain-claim list is a genuine discovery signal for personal Claude accounts on verified domains — the accounts a user would sign in to the add-in with — though not for which of them used the add-in. Personal accounts on other addresses, add-ins users installed themselves (Integrated apps does not list them) and third-party manifests pointed at an unsanctioned gateway are found by SSE, CASB or endpoint inventory. The tenant-restriction header and closing the Office Store are prevention, credited here only in this note.

original.mechanism: M365 Admin Center controls whether users can acquire AppSource add-ins; tenant restrictions block personal Claude organisations

steps.title: Control add-in acquisition
body: Manage which users can install the Claude add-ins through the Microsoft 365 Admin Center and enforce the tenant-restriction header for claude.ai.

controls.mechanism: Compliance API local session endpoints (GET /v1/compliance/apps/sessions/local and /{session_id}/messages, product_surface office_agents/*, scope read:compliance_user_data) return Enterprise add-in transcripts with prompts, responses, tool calls and results; a custom OpenTelemetry collector (otlp_endpoint and otlp_headers at Organization settings > Office agents, or the same keys in the manifest, Entra attributes or bootstrap) receives agent.query, agent.stream and agent.tool_execution spans

steps.title: Pull add-in transcripts from the Compliance API
body: With a Compliance Access Key holding read:compliance_user_data, list GET /v1/compliance/apps/sessions/local with updated_at.gte, keep sessions whose product_surface starts with office_agents, and fetch each session's /messages transcript.

steps.title: Stream spans to a collector you run
body: Set otlp_endpoint (and otlp_headers) at Organization settings > Office agents on Enterprise, or as a configuration key on third-party platforms, pointing at an OpenTelemetry Collector with a CORS-enabled OTLP/HTTP receiver; raise otlp_attr_max_chars if 4,000-character truncation loses evidence.

controls.note: Native by the rule: programmatic export of conversation content and tool events. Boundaries: the Compliance API covers Claude-account Enterprise sign-in only (the add-in pages call this coverage public beta, the Compliance API reference calls it stable), not Pro, Max, Team or third-party-platform deployments, and HIPAA-ready or ZDR organisations capture no local sessions. Add-in activity is not in Enterprise audit logs or data exports, and deleting a conversation in the add-in does not remove the session. OpenTelemetry spans are posted from each user's browser, so a user who controls the client can suppress them — telemetry, not tamper resistance; they omit assistant response text, record connector tools as mcp_tool, and on third-party platforms carry no user identity (correlate session.id with Entra or gateway logs). On the third-party path the organisation's gateway log is the record to fuse with. History is keyed to a Claude account or a hashed Entra object ID; Office builds without nested app authentication fall back to a per-installation identifier shared by everyone on the device.

original.mechanism: Custom OpenTelemetry collector receives the full span trail per user (CORS required); Compliance API M365 session transcripts (beta); excluded from Enterprise audit logs and data exports

steps.title: Configure a custom collector
body: Point the add-in at an OpenTelemetry Collector you run with a CORS-enabled OTLP HTTP receiver; the collector, not the browser, authenticates to your backend.

controls.mechanism: Remove the add-in (or its assignment) in Integrated apps; deny addin.access through access_policies or disabled_features ("Kill switch: the add-in refuses to run") in custom-manifest or bootstrap deployments; disable the Claude for Office enterprise app (Enabled for users to sign-in? = No) and revoke its admin consent in Entra; an Inference hooks deny (Enterprise, Claude-account sign-in) refuses a member's next governed request; no claude.ai switch disables the add-ins

steps.title: Refuse inference for an account (Enterprise)
body: With Enforce verdicts on at Organization settings > Data and privacy > Inference hooks, have your AI security server deny that member's requests from the add-ins.

steps.title: Remove the add-in deployment
body: In Settings > Integrated apps select the Claude add-in and remove it (or remove users under Users); a removed add-in is not accessible to any user.

steps.title: Make the add-in refuse to run
body: Deliver disabled_features=addin.access, or an access_policies deny for addin.access, through the manifest, Entra extension attributes or a bootstrap endpoint; the add-in reads it when it loads.

steps.title: Stop token issuance in Entra
body: In Entra ID > Enterprise apps > Claude for Office > Properties set Enabled for users to sign-in? to No, which prevents all tokens being issued for the app, and revoke its admin-consented permissions.

steps.title: Review and revoke the Graph grant
body: In Entra ID > Enterprise apps > All applications open Claude for Office (c2995f31-11e7-4882-b7a7-ef9def0a0266), review Permissions > Admin consent, and revoke there or with Remove-MgOauth2PermissionGrant.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: each stop blocks the next load or the next token, not a task pane already running, and the delay is not documented (Microsoft gives 24 to 72 hours for deployments to appear; removal timing is not stated). Configuration keys are read when the add-in loads — only served settings, which are re-read while it runs, are documented as applying mid-session, and they are preview. Disabling the Entra app stops new tokens; cached Graph access tokens run to expiry. Connector grants on each device cannot be revoked in bulk, and copies users installed themselves from AppSource are not removed by Integrated apps. No claude.ai switch disables the add-ins; an Inference hooks deny refuses the next governed request, which halts a running task at its next step, but only on Enterprise with Claude-account sign-in and only while the hook is enforcing. Otherwise removing a member's seat or revoking the gateway token at your gateway is the practical stop for inference, though the add-in pages do not document its effect. Local history, skills and credentials persist until the device profile is wiped.

original.mechanism: Remove the add-in deployment in the M365 Admin Center, disable cross-app mode, remove the user's Claude seat; local data persists until the profile is wiped

steps.title: Withdraw the add-in
body: Remove or block the add-ins in the M365 Admin Center and turn off "Let Claude work across apps"; wipe the device profile to remove local history and credentials.

original.note: Withdrawing the add-in applies at the client's next add-in catalogue refresh, and seat removal at the next request; the docs state no delay, so measure it.

settings.name: Deploy Add-in (Specific users/groups)
settings.where: Microsoft 365 admin center › Settings › Integrated apps › Add-ins › Deploy Add-in
settings.recommended: Specific users/groups — the Entra groups rolled out to Claude
settings.why: Who gets the Excel, PowerPoint, Word and Outlook add-ins is a group decision you can audit and reverse, not everyone at once.

settings.name: Let users access the Office Store
settings.where: Microsoft 365 admin center › Settings › Org settings › Services › User owned apps and services
settings.recommended: Off
settings.why: Users can't install the Claude add-ins (or any other) from AppSource themselves, so only centrally deployed copies run in Word, Excel and PowerPoint.

settings.name: My Custom Apps, My Marketplace Apps and My ReadWriteMailbox Apps
settings.where: Exchange admin center › Roles › User roles › Default Role Assignment Policy › Other roles
settings.recommended: All three removed from the default role assignment policy
settings.why: The Office Store setting doesn't reach Outlook; this stops users installing an Outlook add-in that reads and writes their mailbox on their own.

settings.name: Grant Microsoft Graph consent
settings.where: Microsoft Entra admin consent link for Claude for Outlook (client ID c2995f31-11e7-4882-b7a7-ef9def0a0266), or your own single-tenant app via graph_client_id
settings.recommended: Granted by a Global Administrator once Outlook is approved — to your own single-tenant app where policy forbids multi-tenant consent
settings.why: Outlook reads mail and calendar only through this delegated grant (Mail.ReadWrite, Calendars.Read, User.Read, offline_access, no Mail.Send), so drafts land unsent and the tenant owns the decision.

settings.name: Assignment required
settings.where: Microsoft Entra admin center › Enterprise apps › the add-in's app (c2995f31-11e7-4882-b7a7-ef9def0a0266, or your own) › Properties
settings.recommended: Yes, assigned to the same groups as the add-in deployment
settings.why: Only assigned users can get a Graph token for the add-in, so a user who installed it outside the deployment can't reach mail.

settings.name: Enabled for users to sign-in?
settings.where: Microsoft Entra admin center › Enterprise apps › the add-in's app (c2995f31-11e7-4882-b7a7-ef9def0a0266, or your own) › Properties
settings.recommended: Yes — set No to stop the add-in's Graph access in an incident
settings.why: No issues no further tokens for the app to anyone, which cuts Outlook's mailbox access without touching each device.

settings.name: Require SSO for Claude
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Organization and access › Authentication
settings.recommended: On, with MFA enforced on the Claude app in your IdP
settings.why: The Claude account each add-in signs in with goes through the corporate IdP and its MFA; personal email logins on your domain stop working.

settings.name: User provisioning (SCIM)
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Organization and access › User provisioning
settings.recommended: SCIM, driven by the IdP group that grants Claude
settings.why: Removing someone in the IdP removes their seat, so a leaver's add-in sign-in stops working with their account rather than with a ticket.

settings.name: Restrict organization creation
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Organization and access › Security
settings.recommended: On
settings.why: Stops staff creating personal or side Claude organisations on your verified domains, which no admin can see.

settings.name: Migrate accounts using your domain
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Organization and access › Security
settings.recommended: On, after reviewing the personal accounts listed on your domain
settings.why: No Free, Pro or Max account can exist on the verified domain, so nobody signs the add-in in to a personal plan with client workbooks; it can't be reversed.

settings.name: Tenant Restrictions (anthropic-allowed-org-ids)
settings.where: Corporate TLS-inspecting proxy → anthropic-allowed-org-ids header on claude.ai, api.anthropic.com, claude.com and anthropic.com
settings.recommended: Your organisation's UUID, injected and overwritten on every request from managed devices
settings.why: A personal or other organisation's Claude account fails with tenant_restriction_violation on the corporate network; test it with an add-in sign-in, which the page doesn't name.

settings.name: Let Claude work across apps
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Office agents
settings.recommended: Off, until a team's workflow needs one task to span Outlook and the other apps
settings.why: Off, an email's instructions can't steer an edit in an open workbook or deck; the per-device "Let Claude work across files" already starts off on Team and Enterprise.

settings.name: Organization-wide tool policy
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Connectors › connector › tool (Always allow / Needs approval / Blocked)
settings.recommended: Write and send tools set to Needs approval; tools no one uses Blocked
settings.why: The add-ins offer only connectors enabled in Claude settings, and this is the ceiling no member can widen; confirm Needs approval prompts in the add-in, which the pages don't state.

settings.name: Inference hooks
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Data and privacy › Inference hooks
settings.recommended: On, connected to your DLP or AI-security service, enforcing after a monitor-only period
settings.why: One hook now governs Claude for Microsoft 365 with the rest of the organisation, so prompts carrying document or mail content, and tool results, can be denied before inference.

settings.name: access_policies
settings.where: Custom manifest, Entra ID extension attribute or bootstrap endpoint → access_policies
settings.recommended: A deny statement for addin.access on files carrying your most restricted sensitivity labels
settings.why: The add-in won't run on a document carrying those labels; it keys on the label, so an unlabelled file with the same content still passes.

settings.name: disabled_features
settings.where: Custom manifest, Entra ID extension attribute or bootstrap endpoint → disabled_features
settings.recommended: permission_mode.dangerously_always_allow
settings.why: Removes "Dangerously always allow", so no user can switch approvals off; addin.access in the same key is the per-user kill switch.

settings.name: gateway_auth_source
settings.where: Custom manifest → gateway_auth_source (with entra_sso and graph_client_id), or bootstrap_url
settings.recommended: "entra" — or a bootstrap_url that issues expiring tokens
settings.why: Each user sends their own short-lived Entra token to your gateway or Foundry resource instead of a shared key sitting in every device's browser storage.

settings.name: otlp_endpoint
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Office agents (otlp_endpoint, otlp_headers), or the same configuration keys
settings.recommended: An OpenTelemetry Collector you run, with CORS for pivot.claude.ai, forwarding to the SIEM
settings.why: Add-in activity is not in Enterprise audit logs or data exports; spans carry prompts, tool inputs and outputs and document references unfiltered, so scope access to the collector as for client content.

settings.name: Compliance API (session transcripts)
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › API, then a Compliance Access Key with read:compliance_user_data
settings.recommended: On, pulled into your eDiscovery or SIEM
settings.why: Add-in sessions (product_surface office_agents/*) are retrievable centrally after the fact, though deleting a conversation in the add-in doesn't remove them.

tools.name: Claude Managed Agents

variants.name: Managed Agents API (agents, environments, sessions, vaults) on api.anthropic.com
Self-hosted sandboxes (your worker polls the environment work queue)
variants.note: Control plane stays with Anthropic; sandbox image, egress, service-key custody and session-content retention are yours. Environment-variable vault credentials are not yet supported here.

summary: Anthropic's hosted agent harness (beta, enabled by default for API accounts; Managed Agents endpoints take the managed-agents-2026-04-01 beta header, memory store endpoints agent-memory-2026-07-22): you define an agent (model, system prompt, toolset, MCP servers, skills), an environment (Anthropic cloud sandbox — an isolated Ubuntu container, up to 8 GB / 10 GB — or a self-hosted sandbox), then run sessions that stream events over SSE. The sandbox runs bash, file tools and code; web_search and web_fetch run on Anthropic's servers. Sessions are stateful: event history persists until you delete the session and sandbox state is checkpointed for 30 days, so Managed Agents is not ZDR- or HIPAA-BAA-eligible.

Governance is API-native and workspace-scoped: permission_policy always_allow / always_ask / auto per toolset or per tool (MCP toolsets default to always_ask), tool enable flags, per-tool allowed_domains / blocked_domains, environment networking unrestricted / limited with allowed_hosts, vault credentials injected at egress so the agent never sees the secret, hard dollar session budgets, versioned agent definitions, memory stores with immutable version history and redaction, signed webhooks and a persisted event stream. Also available on Claude Platform on AWS and Claude Models on Google Cloud (Anthropic managed) with differences.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Any Claude API organisation (beta, on by default); MCP tunnels and dreaming are a limited research preview. Billed per model token, $10 per 1,000 web searches and $0.08 per session hour at list rates.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Anthropic API, Claude Platform on AWS and Claude Models on Google Cloud (Anthropic managed); model pinned per agent with optional inference_geo "us" or "global", validated against the workspace's allowed_inference_geos when the agent is saved, when a session is created and on every turn.

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: Everything runs on Anthropic infrastructure: conversation, tool inputs/outputs, files and sandbox state; self-hosted sandboxes keep tool execution and files on your side while the transcript still passes through Anthropic.

facts.label: Retention & training
facts.value: Commercial terms (no training). Session transcripts persist until you delete the session; sandbox checkpoints 30 days; memory versions retained 30 days (recent versions longer); not eligible for ZDR or HIPAA BAA.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents (overview through reference)

riskNotes.note: Vaults and credentials are workspace-scoped: any API key with workspace access can reference any user's vault at session creation, so a session can act on a grant its caller does not own. The docs recommend separate workspaces and environments per trust boundary for self-hosted sandboxes.

Memory stores attach read_write by default and the docs warn a successful injection can write content later sessions read as trusted; use read_only for reference stores and limited networking with allowed_hosts for production.

The built-in agent toolset defaults to always_allow, including bash with unrestricted egress on API-created environments; the vendor's guidance is limited networking, auto on bash, write, edit and web_fetch, and always_ask on tools whose changes cannot be undone, on bash where end-user text is relayed, and on MCP tools that write.

MCP servers are declared by URL with no workspace allowlist; in a limited environment with allow_mcp_servers false, a session whose agent declares a host outside allowed_hosts fails to start. MCP toolsets default to always_ask so newly added server tools do not run unapproved, and per-tool enabled flags can pin the set.

Custom tool results, uploaded files and outputs are stored server-side until deleted; OAuth exchanges performed inside the sandbox return tokens unredacted, so perform exchanges outside and store the result in the vault.

controls.mechanism: Vault credential values are write-only, never returned and stored under Anthropic-managed encryption (outside workspace CMEK), rotated in place with running sessions re-resolving; Workload Identity Federation tokens (token_lifetime_seconds 60 to 86400, default 3600) and API key expirations for the API itself; the MCP tunnel token (Rotate token, archive) and up to two CA certificates (Revoke), provisioned over a workspace:manage_tunnels federation rule

steps.title: Register credentials in a vault and rotate in place
body: Add mcp_oauth (with a refresh block), static_bearer or environment_variable credentials; update the secret to rotate (running sessions re-resolve without a restart) and archive to purge it while keeping the record.

steps.title: Federate the API credential
body: Connect the workload under Settings → Workload identity with a workspace:developer rule and a short token_lifetime_seconds, unset ANTHROPIC_API_KEY wherever it runs (it shadows federation), and delete the old key.

steps.title: Provision the tunnel over federation
body: Create the tunnel with programmatic access so the setup component fetches the tunnel token and registers a locally generated CA over a workspace:manage_tunnels rule; the private key never leaves your environment.

steps.title: Rotate and revoke tunnel credentials
body: Use Rotate token on the tunnel's detail page, register a new CA certificate beside the old one and Revoke the old, and archive the tunnel to invalidate its token; every reveal and rotation is recorded in the Compliance API activity log.

controls.note: Native by the credential-hardening rule: an encrypted write-only store for tool credentials, federated short-lived credentials for the API, and a scoped, rotatable, revocable tunnel credential. Boundaries: nothing refuses static API keys — any Workspace Developer can create one and Never is offered unless an organisation maximum expiration policy is set (where that policy is set is not documented); static_bearer credentials live as long as the upstream token; an OAuth exchange run inside the sandbox leaves the returned token there unredacted. Tunnel (research preview, request access): rotating the token does not sever established cloudflared connections, so cutting a compromised host means stopping the stack or archiving the tunnel; the tunnel token and TLS private key sit on the organisation's host and in its secrets manager.

original.mechanism: Vault credentials (mcp_oauth with managed refresh, static_bearer, environment_variable with networking.allowed_hosts and injection_location) substituted at egress; secret values are write-only; rotate via update, archive purges the secret

steps.title: Register credentials in a vault
body: Add mcp_oauth or static_bearer credentials keyed by mcp_server_url, or environment_variable credentials keyed by secret_name with networking type limited and allowed_hosts; the agent sees only an opaque placeholder.

steps.title: Rotate and revoke
body: Update the credential's secret (running sessions re-resolve without restart), archive to purge the secret while keeping the audit record (vaults page), and subscribe to vault_credential.refresh_failed on the webhooks page (platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks) for the notification.

original.note: Vault substitution keeps values out of the sandbox and the model; it does not scope them per requesting user. A credential in a vault is presented for every session that vault is attached to, so tenant-scoped delegation — one user's authority, not a shared credential's — is the application's to arrange through per-user vaults or mcp_oauth per user. Where no credential matches, the connection is attempted unauthenticated.

controls.mechanism: Agents, environments, vaults, memory stores and deployments are listable workspace resources (id, name, description, metadata, immutable agent version history, archived_at); agent.created / updated / archived webhooks and the Compliance API Activity Feed's platform_agent_created / updated / archived records; the only gate on writing a definition is workspace membership and role

steps.title: Treat the agent resource as the register
body: Create each agent once with owner and approval metadata, list its versions, and archive retired agents so new sessions cannot reference them.

steps.title: Record who changed each definition
body: Turn on the Compliance API (claude.ai Organization settings › API for an Enterprise parent, or the Compliance API toggle on the Console's Compliance page for a standalone Console organisation) and pull platform_agent_created, platform_agent_updated and platform_agent_archived from the Activity Feed, alongside the agent.* webhooks.

steps.title: Limit who can write definitions
body: Give Workspace Developer only to the authors and the pipeline's service account and Workspace User to everyone else, since any role that can use the API can create, update and override agents.

controls.note: Partial by the registry rule: the inventory, version history and change record exist, but nothing gates a definition before it runs. Any key or token with workspace:developer — the only non-admin scope; finer-grained scopes "per resource, or read versus write" are not available — can create or update an agent (omitting version makes the update unconditional), and a session created with agent_with_overrides replaces model, system, tools, mcp_servers and skills without creating a version, so a session can run a configuration the register never saw. Environments are not versioned. There is no approval state; ownership is metadata the organisation writes, and reconciliation is its pipeline.

original.mechanism: Agents are first-class workspace resources with id, name, description, metadata, version history, archive; environments, vaults, memory stores and deployments likewise; list endpoints and lifecycle webhooks

steps.title: Treat the agent resource as the registry

controls.mechanism: Immutable agent versions (version increments on every change; optimistic concurrency through the version field, 409 on mismatch; full version history); sessions and scheduled deployments pin agent {id, version}; coordinator rosters keep the version pinned when last updated; user.define_outcome runs a grader inside one session

controls.mechanism: permission_policy always_ask pauses the session (session.status_idle, stop_reason requires_action with the blocking event_ids) until a user.tool_confirmation naming that tool_use_id with result allow or deny (optional deny_message); a confirmation for a call not at ask is rejected with 400; subagent requests are cross-posted to the primary thread; webhook session.status_idled

controls.note: Native by the approval rule: the runtime pauses on the configured tool and runs it only on a confirmation bound to that call's event id, whose input is fixed; the model cannot send it and the session waits indefinitely. Boundaries: the runtime cannot tell a person's confirmation from the application's — any holder of a workspace key can send one — so that a human decides is the front end's to guarantee; auto is not a human checkpoint ("the call runs before anyone sees it"); custom tools are never paused by policy and are the application's to gate; the policy is definition content that an update or a session override can loosen. On this drawing the organisation's gateway owns the gate and this is the second, configured layer.

body: Managed Agents is stateful and not ZDR- or HIPAA-eligible; capture this from the retention page in the vendor assessment.

original.mechanism: Every configuration is readable through the API (agents, environments, vaults minus secrets, memory stores, deployments) for posture checks

steps.title: Check posture from the API
body: Enumerate environments for networking type unrestricted, agents for always_allow bash or missing domain lists, and sessions without budgets; treat these as findings.

original.note: Every configuration is readable through the API, which is the input an SSPM product needs; the checks listed in the step are ones the customer writes, not ones the product runs.

controls.mechanism: Persisted session event history (agent.tool_use / tool_result and agent.mcp_tool_use / mcp_tool_result with inputs and results, agent.custom_tool_use, agent.message, span.model_request_start / end with model_usage, thread and compaction events, session.error, session.usage) streamed over SSE and listable in full per session and per thread; lifecycle webhooks; Compliance API Activity Feed session and agent lifecycle records

steps.title: Stream and archive every session's events
body: Open the stream before sending, list the full history (GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/events, and each thread's in multiagent sessions) to reconcile, and store events in your own system keyed by id and processed_at.

steps.title: Do not treat webhooks as the log
body: Webhooks make three attempts and then drop the event with no signal; reconcile by listing session events, and export memory versions before their 30-day window.

steps.title: Correlate with the lifecycle record
body: Enable the Compliance API and pull platform_agent_session_created, platform_agent_session_deleted and platform_agent_updated activities (retained six years) to tie sessions to definition changes and their actors.

controls.note: Native by the tracing rule: every persisted event — tool calls with inputs and results, MCP calls, model requests with usage, thread handoffs, compaction and errors — is retrievable by API for export to the organisation's store, and memory reads and writes appear as ordinary tool events. Not included: thinking content (agent.thinking is a progress signal) and event deltas. There is no OTLP export or log sink: the stream is pulled, and any workspace key can delete a session and its history, so tamper resistance is the organisation's archive. Detection runs in the consumer.

original.mechanism: Persisted session event stream (agent.tool_use / tool_result / mcp_tool_use / message, span.model_request_start/end with usage, session.error, thread events) over SSE and list endpoints; session.usage snapshots

steps.title: Consume and archive the event stream
body: Stream events per session (open the stream before sending), and list past events by type for reconstruction; every persisted event has an id and processed_at.

original.note: Events cover tool use, model requests with usage, errors and thread events, correlated by session; there is no model chain-of-thought and no OTLP export — the stream is pulled through the API. Observability is not detection; that logic runs in the consumer.

original.mechanism: Full event history persisted with the session until deletion; memory version history attributed to sessions; vault archive keeps records after purging secrets; signed webhooks (webhook-signature, 5-minute freshness)

steps.title: Keep an off-platform copy
body: Webhooks are not a durable log (three attempts, then dropped); reconcile by listing session events and export memory versions before the 30-day window expires.

original.note: The event history is customer-deletable and not tamper-evident in the Five Eyes sense; your archive is the record.

controls.mechanism: Memory stores (agent-memory-2026-07-22) are workspace-scoped and absent unless attached in a session's resources at creation (up to 8), with access read_write (default) or read_only enforced at the filesystem; every write is an immutable version attributed to the session, listable and redactable, retained 30 days (recent versions of a live memory longer); memories and stores editable, archivable and deletable by API; session history deleted with the session

steps.title: Scope stores and attach them deliberately
body: Use one store per end user, team or project and attach shared reference stores with access read_only; nothing is shared unless your application attaches it.

steps.title: Audit, roll back and scrub memory
body: List memory versions, restore by writing an earlier version's content back with memories.update, redact versions that captured secrets or PII, and export versions you need beyond 30 days.

steps.title: Delete conversation state you no longer need
body: Delete sessions to remove their event history and sandbox; transcripts otherwise persist.

controls.note: Native on this drawing's memory rule: scope is set per attachment and writes are controllable (read_only, delete and redact by API, a version per write). Content validation, the rule's other write control, is absent: nothing checks what a read_write session writes, and the docs warn an injection can plant content later sessions read as trusted. Separation between users is the application's attachment choice, since any workspace key can attach any store. On self-hosted sandboxes read_only protects the store from upload, not the local copy, which bash, custom tools and sandbox MCP servers can still change. Sandbox state lasts 30 days from creation.

original.mechanism: Memory stores are workspace-scoped resources attached per session with access read_write or read_only, capped at 8 per session; every write creates an immutable version; versions can be redacted; stores can be archived or deleted

steps.title: Segment and scope stores
body: Use one store per user, team or project, attach shared reference stores read_only, and pass instructions per attachment.

steps.title: Audit and roll back memory
body: List memory versions, restore prior content by writing it back, and redact versions that captured secrets or PII while keeping the audit trail.

original.note: Integrity and recovery are real here: read_only stops sessions writing, every write is an immutable version, and recovery is re-pointing to an earlier version. What can still write: any session attached read_write, and the API. Writes are trusted as the session's — nothing scans content for poisoning before it is versioned.

controls.mechanism: user.interrupt per session or thread, then session archive or delete; agent archive (read-only, no new sessions, its scheduled deployments archived); vault and credential archive or delete, propagated at periodic re-resolution; deployment pause (future runs only); environment key revocation for self-hosted workers; tunnel archive

steps.title: Interrupt the agent's running sessions
body: List sessions with agent_id and status running, send user.interrupt without session_thread_id to stop every thread, then archive or delete each session once it is idle.

steps.title: Archive the agent
body: Archive the agent so no new session can reference it; existing sessions keep running until you stop them.

steps.title: Revoke its credentials
body: Archive the vaults or credentials its sessions used (secrets purged, records kept) or delete them; running sessions pick the change up at their next re-resolution.

steps.title: Cut self-hosted workers
body: Revoke ANTHROPIC_ENVIRONMENT_KEY and generate a replacement; revocation takes effect on the worker's next call.

controls.note: Partial by the kill-switch rule: all three actions exist, but the delays are not documented. user.interrupt stops a model response immediately but "can take longer to apply while tool calls are running", and a running session can be neither archived nor deleted until it applies (delay not documented). Archiving the agent leaves existing sessions running. Vault revocation reaches running sessions at a periodic re-resolution whose interval is not documented. There is no single per-agent stop: it is a loop over the agent's sessions, which any holder of a workspace key can run.

original.mechanism: user.interrupt, session archive and delete (removes events and sandbox), agent archive (blocks new sessions), vault or credential archive/delete (purges secrets, propagates to running sessions), environment key revocation, deployment pause

steps.title: Stop and decommission
body: Send user.interrupt, then archive or delete the session; archive the agent so no new sessions start; archive vault credentials to revoke access (running sessions re-resolve credentials periodically).

original.note: user.interrupt stops the active session; archiving credentials propagates at the sessions' next periodic re-resolution, so that interval is the revocation delay for delegated work.

controls.mechanism: One isolated Linux container per session on Anthropic infrastructure (Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, up to 8 GB memory and 10 GB disk), never shared between sessions even when they share an environment; checkpointed while idle, kept 30 days from creation and removed when the session is deleted; self-hosted sandboxes run on a worker you operate

body: Build a per-session image around the worker and have the poller's spawn script start a fresh sandbox for each claimed work item, rather than one handler running every item on one host.

Outside: the loop, inference, web_search and web_fetch (Anthropic's servers) and the MCP connector, which connects from Anthropic's side. The container technology and its escape testing are not documented beyond "isolated Linux containers". In a multiagent session every agent shares the one sandbox and filesystem. A self-hosted sandbox moves the boundary to the deployer, including how tools are isolated from each other inside it.

controls.mechanism: Environment networking type limited with allowed_hosts (bare hostnames or wildcard patterns), allow_mcp_servers and allow_package_managers (an Anthropic-maintained registry list), enforced around the cloud sandbox and, in a limited environment, applied to web_search and web_fetch too; unrestricted (a general safety blocklist only) is the default for an API request that omits networking; allowed_domains on each web tool and the Console's organisation web settings narrow those tools further

controls.mechanism: permission_policy (always_allow, always_ask, auto) per toolset in default_config and per tool in configs, evaluated server-side before each built-in or MCP tool call; enabled false removes a tool; auto is a server-side model evaluation; evaluated_permission and evaluation recorded on every agent.tool_use and agent.mcp_tool_use event

steps.title: Gate consequential tools with always_ask
body: Set permission_policy always_ask on bash (a configs entry) and keep it on every mcp_toolset (the default), so each call pauses with requires_action until your application answers.

steps.title: Keep the evaluation in your audit record
body: Store evaluated_permission and the evaluation object (policy type, reason_code) from each agent.tool_use and agent.mcp_tool_use event; a call denied under auto carries reason_code high_risk and cannot be re-allowed.

steps.title: Decide custom tools in your application

body: Set permission_policy always_ask on bash and on every MCP toolset (their default) so the session pauses with requires_action until a user.tool_confirmation arrives; always_ask is the deterministic gate, auto is the server's own reviewer.

steps.title: Keep the evaluation in your audit record
body: Store evaluated_permission and the evaluation object (policy type, reason_code) from each agent.tool_use and agent.mcp_tool_use event; a call denied under auto carries reason_code high_risk and cannot be re-allowed.

controls.mechanism: Vault credentials substituted at egress: mcp_oauth and static_bearer keyed to an mcp_server_url (normalised exact match), environment_variable keyed by secret_name with networking.allowed_hosts and injection_location header / body; values are write-only and the sandbox holds an opaque placeholder; vault_ids chosen per session, one vault per end user

steps.title: Hold one user's credentials in one vault
body: Create a vault per end user, add mcp_oauth (with refresh) or static_bearer credentials keyed by mcp_server_url, and pass only that user's vault in vault_ids when you create the session.

steps.title: Bind environment secrets to named hosts and headers
body: Create environment_variable credentials with networking type limited, the exact allowed_hosts, and injection_location {"header": true}, so the secret is substituted only into request headers to those hosts.

steps.title: Run token exchanges outside the sandbox
body: Perform OAuth client-credentials and other exchange flows in your application and store the resulting token in the vault, because a token returned into the sandbox arrives unredacted.

controls.note: Native by the credential-scoping rule: credentials stay out of the sandbox and the model's context and are presented only to the destination they are keyed to, and per-user vaults are the documented model ("the collection of credentials associated with an end user"). Boundaries: vaults are workspace-scoped, so which user's vault a session gets is the application's binding — any key with workspace access can attach any vault; in a multiagent session the vaults apply to every thread whose definition declares the matching server; the first matching vault wins; with no match the connection is attempted unauthenticated; an environment_variable credential set to unrestricted is substituted for any host, and that type is not supported on self-hosted sandboxes. The tunnel carries traffic without authenticating to the upstream.

original.mechanism: Vault credentials substituted at egress (the sandbox holds a placeholder; values are write-only); per-session secret for self-hosted workers; the environment service key scoped to one environment's work queue

steps.title: Attach credentials through vaults, never the environment
body: Register mcp_oauth, static_bearer or environment_variable credentials in a vault and pass vault_ids at session creation; the agent sees only an opaque placeholder and the proxy substitutes the value for matching hosts.

steps.title: Scope self-hosted credentials per session
body: Pass the per-session secret only into the sandbox serving that session, keep the environment key in a secrets manager and out of images, and give each trust boundary its own workspace and environment.

original.note: A vault credential is presented for every session the vault is attached to, so tenant- scoped delegation — one user's authority rather than a shared credential — is your arrangement through per-user vaults or per-user mcp_oauth, not the runtime's default. Where no credential matches a server, the connection is attempted unauthenticated.

controls.mechanism: Workspace roles (Workspace User, Workspace Limited Developer, Workspace Developer, Workspace Admin) assigned per workspace in the Claude Console; Require SSO for Console and SCIM provisioning through a parent organisation; Restrict organization creation on verified domains; Workload Identity Federation rules scoped by oauth_scope to the workspaces they are enabled in; API keys bound to one workspace

steps.title: Assign workspace roles deliberately
body: In Claude Console › Settings › Workspaces › workspace › Members give Workspace Developer only to the agent's authors and the pipeline's service account, Workspace User to everyone else, and Workspace Admin to a named few.

steps.title: Federate Console sign-in and membership
body: Turn on Require SSO for Console under Organization and access › Authentication and drive membership with SCIM from the IdP group that grants Console access.

steps.title: Keep staff inside your organisation
body: Turn on Restrict organization creation under Organization and access › Security so nobody opens a separate Console organisation on your verified domains.

steps.title: Bind each workload to one workspace
body: Connect each agent workload under Settings › Workload identity with its own federation rule, enabled in one workspace only, instead of a shared API key.

controls.note: Native on the authorisation rule (as on toolVertexAgentEngine): the organisation administers who can use the API, create keys and define agents, environments and vaults, and Anthropic enforces it per workspace. Boundary: the workspace is the smallest unit. No per-agent, per-vault or read-versus-write permission is documented, so any key or token with workspace access can run, update or override every agent and attach any vault in that workspace, and separate trust boundaries need separate workspaces. Workspace Limited Developer limits only the Console, not the API; organisation admins hold Workspace Admin in every workspace. Which end user a session acts for is the application's to authorise.

controls.mechanism: Session budget (budget.max_list_cost, a hard dollar cap priced at list rates over model tokens, web searches and session hours) set at session or deployment creation, which pauses every thread when reached; workspace monthly spend limits and per-model rate limits set by Console administrators below the organisation's; cloud sandbox capped at 8 GB memory and 10 GB disk

steps.title: Budget every session
body: Pass budget {type limit, max_list_cost {amount, currency USD}} on every session and deployment create; a budget cannot be added to a session created without one.

steps.title: Cap the agent workspace
body: On the Console's Workspaces page select the agent workspace, open Spend limits and set a monthly cap and alerts; set requests and tokens per minute under Rate limits for its models.

controls.note: Native on the resource-consumption rule (unlike toolVertexAgentEngine, which has no per-session budget): the runtime enforces a per-session spend ceiling across every thread, including subagents, and the workspace caps total spend and request rate. Boundaries: the budget is optional and set by whoever creates the session, and it can be changed or removed at any time; it is checked between model requests, so each thread can overshoot by one request and the tool calls it returns; it compares list price, not contracted price; a session at its budget pauses idle rather than terminating. No turn count or wall-clock limit is documented apart from the cost of session hours. Spend limits cannot be set on the Default Workspace.

settings.name: Require SSO for Console
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Organization and access › Authentication (or Claude Console › Settings › Identity and access)
settings.recommended: On, with MFA enforced on the Claude app in your IdP
settings.why: Every Console sign-in — the people who create keys, agents, environments and vaults — goes through the corporate IdP and its MFA.
settings.requires: SSO set up through a parent organisation (Enterprise, or arranged with Sales)

settings.name: User provisioning (SCIM)
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Organization and access › User provisioning (or the Console's Identity and access page)
settings.recommended: SCIM, driven by the IdP group that grants Console access
settings.why: Removing someone in the IdP removes their Console membership, and their personal API keys stop working with it.
settings.requires: Enterprise or a Console organisation with its own parent organisation

settings.name: Restrict organization creation
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Organization and access › Security
settings.recommended: On
settings.why: Stops staff opening their own Console organisations on your verified domains, where agents would run outside your workspaces, roles and audit.

settings.name: Workspace roles
settings.where: Claude Console › Settings › Workspaces › workspace › Members
settings.recommended: Workspace Developer only for the agent's authors and its pipeline service account; Workspace User for everyone else; Workspace Admin for a named few
settings.why: Any role that can use the API can create, update or override agents and attach any vault in the workspace; Workspace Limited Developer limits only the Console, not the API.

settings.name: Federation rule (Connect workload)
settings.where: Claude Console › Settings › Workload identity › Connect workload (oauth_scope, token_lifetime_seconds), then ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_RULE_ID in the workload
settings.recommended: One rule per agent workload, enabled in one workspace only, with token_lifetime_seconds 600
settings.why: No long-lived Claude API key sits in the deployment, and archiving the rule refuses the next token exchange, so the token lifetime is the revocation delay.

settings.name: Key expiration
settings.where: Claude Console › API keys › Create key (expiration and Linked account)
settings.default: Chosen per key; Never is offered unless an organisation maximum expiration policy is set
settings.recommended: 30 days or less, linked to a service account scoped to one workspace — never a legacy workspace key or Never
settings.why: A key that leaks from a pipeline stops working on its own, and an identity-backed key dies with its service account.

settings.name: allowed_inference_geos
settings.where: Claude Console › workspace settings → allowed_inference_geos, default_inference_geo
settings.recommended: The geos your data-handling policy approves for that workspace (["us"] where client contracts require US processing)
settings.why: An agent or session whose inference_geo is outside the list is rejected when it is saved, when a session starts and on every turn.

settings.name: Cloud or self-hosted sandbox
settings.where: Environment › config.type (cloud or self_hosted)
settings.recommended: Cloud, unless tools must run on infrastructure you control
settings.why: Keeps each session in Anthropic's per-session container; a self-hosted sandbox makes isolation, hardening and egress the firm's to build.

settings.name: networking (limited, allowed_hosts)
settings.where: Environment › config.networking.type, config.networking.allowed_hosts
settings.default: unrestricted when an API request omits it; the Console form starts at Limited with nothing allowed
settings.recommended: limited, with only the hosts the agent needs — set explicitly in every create request
settings.why: Sandbox traffic, and in a limited environment web_search and web_fetch too, reaches only listed hosts; unrestricted lets an injected command post anything anywhere.

settings.name: allow_package_managers and allow_mcp_servers
settings.where: Environment › config.networking.allow_package_managers, allow_mcp_servers
settings.recommended: false / false — list package mirrors and MCP hosts in allowed_hosts instead
settings.why: allow_package_managers opens github.com and the public registries on a list Anthropic can change; with allow_mcp_servers false a session whose agent declares an unlisted MCP host fails to start.

settings.name: allowed_domains (web_search, web_fetch)
settings.where: Agent › tools › agent_toolset_20260401 › configs entry for web_fetch and web_search → allowed_domains
settings.recommended: On web_fetch, the sites the agent needs; on web_search, the sites you want results from
settings.why: Any URL the agent fetches can carry data to that site; blocked_domains is not a security control, and the lists apply in every environment type.

settings.name: Web search and web fetch (organization settings)
settings.where: Claude Console › Settings › Capabilities
settings.recommended: On, with organisation-wide blocked domains only where a policy covers every workspace
settings.why: The one web-tool floor no agent definition can lower — a search result or fetched URL must pass both the organisation's lists and the tool's own.

settings.name: default_config.enabled (agent toolset)
settings.where: Agent › tools › agent_toolset_20260401 › default_config.enabled, then configs per tool
settings.recommended: false, then enable only the tools the agent needs
settings.why: An agent that never needed bash or the web tools does not hold them when untrusted input tells it to use them.

settings.name: permission_policy (agent toolset)
settings.where: Agent › tools › agent_toolset_20260401 › default_config.permission_policy and configs[].permission_policy
settings.recommended: auto on bash, write, edit and web_fetch; always_allow on read, glob and grep; always_ask on bash where the agent relays end-user text
settings.why: The server evaluates each consequential call instead of running all of them unreviewed; regulated teams set always_ask so a person approves every call.

settings.name: default_config.enabled (MCP toolset)
settings.where: Agent › tools › mcp_toolset › default_config.enabled, then configs per tool
settings.recommended: false, with each reviewed tool enabled by name
settings.why: A tool the server operator adds later stays off until someone reviews it, instead of appearing in every session.

settings.name: permission_policy (MCP toolset)
settings.where: Agent › tools › mcp_toolset › default_config.permission_policy and configs[].permission_policy
settings.recommended: always_ask for tools that change data — keep the default; auto per tool for read-only tools
settings.why: A write to a connected system pauses for your application's approval, and a newly added server tool still waits.

settings.name: injection_location and networking (environment variable credential)
settings.where: Vault › credential (environment_variable) › injection_location, networking
settings.default: Both locations when an API create omits it (Console-created: header only)
settings.recommended: {"header": true, "body": false}, with limited networking naming the exact hosts the key is for
settings.why: The real secret is substituted only into request headers to those hosts; a body location or unrestricted networking hands it to whatever the agent builds.

settings.name: vault_ids
settings.where: Session or deployment create → vault_ids
settings.recommended: One vault per end user or workload, and only that one passed to its sessions; vaults of different trust levels in separate workspaces
settings.why: A session presents only its caller's credentials, since anyone who can start sessions in a workspace can reference its vaults.

settings.name: authorization_token (github_repository resource)
settings.where: Session resources › github_repository › authorization_token
settings.recommended: A fine-grained token for that repository with the minimum permissions — write only if the agent must push
settings.why: Code in the sandbox can fetch from and push to the mounted repository with the token for the whole session.

settings.name: access (memory store attachment)
settings.where: Session resources › memory_store › access
settings.recommended: read_only, unless the agent must write to that store
settings.why: An injected instruction cannot plant text that later sessions read as trusted memory; the filesystem rejects writes.

settings.name: agent (pinned version)
settings.where: Session or deployment create → agent {type agent, id, version}
settings.default: Latest version when the agent ID is passed as a string
settings.recommended: A pinned version on every session and deployment; no agent_with_overrides outside testing
settings.why: A newly saved definition runs only where the pipeline points a session at it, and rolling back is changing that number.

settings.name: budget (max_list_cost)
settings.where: Session or deployment create → budget.max_list_cost
settings.default: No budget (cannot be added to a session created without one)
settings.recommended: A cap sized to what you expect one run to cost
settings.why: A looping or hijacked session pauses every thread at the cap instead of running on; spend can pass it by the requests already in flight.

settings.name: Spend limits
settings.where: Claude Console › Settings › Workspaces › workspace › Spend limits
settings.recommended: A monthly cap and alert on each agent workspace
settings.why: A session created without a budget, or many of them, stop at the workspace's cap rather than the organisation's.

settings.name: Webhooks (event types)
settings.where: Claude Console › Settings › Workspaces › workspace › Webhooks
settings.recommended: An endpoint subscribed to session.status_idled, session.budget_reached, session.status_terminated and the agent.*, environment.* and vault_credential.* events
settings.why: Idle, capped and failed sessions and every definition change raise an alert; webhooks drop after three attempts, so reconcile against the event list.

settings.name: Compliance API (Activity Feed)
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › API (Enterprise parent), or Claude Console › Settings › Compliance › Compliance API (standalone Console organisation), then a key with read:compliance_activities
settings.recommended: On, pulled into your SIEM
settings.why: Agent, session, vault and memory-store changes with their actors (platform_agent_updated, platform_agent_session_created) reach the SIEM, retained six years; nothing is recorded while it is off.
settings.requires: Enterprise, or an eligible standalone Console organisation
