tools.name: Claude Tag (Claude in Slack)

variants.name: @Claude in Slack channels (organisation agent identity)
@Claude direct messages (runs on the member's own claude.ai account)
variants.note: DMs use the member's personal connectors and seat; Owners can disable DMs organisation-wide.

variants.name: Claude Code in Slack (earlier per-user version; Pro/Max, retiring on Team/Enterprise)

summary: Claude Tag is Anthropic's organisation-managed @Claude for Slack (public beta on Team and Enterprise, first-party service only, not for ZDR or CMEK organisations). In channels Claude acts under its own service accounts that an Owner provisions, not as the person who tagged it; each thread runs in an ephemeral sandbox on the same infrastructure as Claude Code on the web (or in a self-hosted environment, where the connectors an admin adds don't apply), and in an Anthropic-hosted environment every outbound request crosses Agent Proxy, which injects credentials from a write-only store and blocks hosts no allow layer covers. Direct messages instead run on the sender's own claude.ai account with their personal connectors.

Admin control lives at claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-tag (Owner role, or the Enterprise Claude Tag Admin permission): pairing workspaces, connectors and bundles of credentials (the Connectors and Bundles tabs under Claude's access), repository grants, domains, plugins and instructions attached per scope (the Slack page for the whole organisation, a workspace or a channel), the "Enable Claude Tag in Slack" switch, per-scope enable switches and New / Legacy version, member, guest and Slack Connect restrictions (Slack page › Advanced › Access), blocked channel patterns, the DM toggle, auto-mode allow rules, and spend limits at claude.ai/admin-settings/usage/claude-tag. Channel work bills to the organisation's usage balance. Session transcripts, channel and workspace memory, routines and artifacts are stored by Anthropic with no automatic retention period during the beta and are not yet in the Compliance API session endpoints.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Team and Enterprise only; not on Free, Pro, Max, third-party deployments, or ZDR or CMEK organisations; not covered by Anthropic's BAA. Routines must be enabled at Admin settings > Capabilities > Remote sessions > Routines. Slack Connect (externally shared) channels are off by default (Restrict) and answer only where an Owner or Claude Tag admin sets How should Claude work in channels with guests to Channel only (or an Owner to Full access), with access capped at channel-only either way.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Anthropic first-party API from Anthropic-managed sandboxes; self-hosted environments run the sandbox on your runners but still call api.anthropic.com.

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: Slack messages Claude is shown (including other people's and guests'), attached files, Slack search results, data retrieved from connected tools and everything Claude did are held as session transcripts on Anthropic's side; web search runs on Anthropic's servers outside Agent Proxy rules.

facts.label: Retention & training
facts.value: No automatic retention period during the beta; custom organisation retention does not apply to transcripts or memory (it does to artifacts); deletion is by disconnecting a workspace, removing a channel scope, deleting memory files or routines, or uninstalling the app. Commercial terms (no training).

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: claude.com/docs/claude-tag (concepts, admins, users)

riskNotes.note: Anyone in a channel under a bundle's scope can make Claude act with that bundle's credentials; the docs say to connect a dedicated service account per tool, attach narrow bundles to private channels, and never a personal login.

Claude reads whole threads and can respond without being tagged; guests' and other members' messages become instructions and transcript content. Auto-mode allow rules pre-approve actions per scope, and there is no per-thread deny list.

Public-channel memory is shared workspace-wide and survives a channel going private; Claude can keyword-search public channels without being added to them; artifacts are readable by anyone with access to the source channel.
Routines and channel watches run unattended with the channel's credentials and are created by any channel member; the Activity page's Scheduled work tab is the inventory.

controls.mechanism: Enterprise custom roles with the "Claude Tag in Slack" capability (effective once "Restrict to roles with Claude Tag access" is on), channel managers through a custom role holding only "Claude Tag channel setup", Owner-only pairing, bundles and scopes; target-tenant consent documented: a Slack workspace admin approves the Claude app and its bot scopes, a GitHub organisation owner installs the Claude GitHub App and approves its permissions, and each other tool's service account is created in that tool

steps.title: Authorise use by role (Enterprise)
body: Turn on Restrict to roles with Claude Tag access at claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-tag, create groups at claude.ai/admin-settings/groups and a custom role with the Claude Tag in Slack capability at claude.ai/admin-settings/roles.

steps.title: Let the Slack administrator decide the install
body: A Slack workspace admin reviews the scopes on Slack's consent screen (or under Manage apps > App requests) before approving the Claude app; uninstalling it later deletes the workspace's Claude data.

steps.title: Let the GitHub organisation owner decide the app
body: At claude.ai/admin-settings/github link or install the Claude GitHub App; a Needs permissions status sends an owner to github.com to approve the request.

steps.title: Limit account linking to your domains (Enterprise)
body: In the Member access dialog at claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-tag turn on Restrict to your verified domains so Slack users whose profile email is off your verified domains cannot link a Claude account, and turn on Require SSO for Claude at claude.ai/admin-settings/organization.

controls.note: Native on Enterprise by the rule: the console administers role- and group-based authorisation over who may use Claude Tag and who may configure which channel, enforced by Anthropic (a restricted member's mentions get a private notice and their thread replies are withheld), and the vendor documents the target-tenant approval for its Slack and GitHub apps. Team plans have the organisation-wide toggle only, which is partial. Built-in roles always grant the capability, and any grant wins across roles. The Slack and GitHub approvals are those tenants' controls, and Enterprise Grid pairings to several Claude organisations are governed by one organisation's settings. Without the restriction toggle anyone in a paired Slack workspace can use Claude even without a Claude account, authenticated only by Slack; with it, each request is still authenticated by the member's Slack session.

original.mechanism: Owner-only setup and configuration; "Restrict to roles with Claude Tag access" (Enterprise custom roles with the Claude Tag in Slack capability) or "Restrict to your organization" (Team); "Restrict to your verified domains" for account linking; channel managers via custom roles

steps.title: Restrict who can invoke Claude
body: At claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-tag > Where Claude Tag works > Member access, turn on "Restrict to roles with Claude Tag access" (Enterprise) or "Restrict to your organization" (Team); the toggle covers channels and DMs.

steps.title: Gate by custom role
body: Create groups at claude.ai/admin-settings/groups and a custom role at claude.ai/admin-settings/roles with the "Claude Tag in Slack" capability; built-in roles always grant it.

original.mechanism: Reach inside a tool equals what the service account can access; account-level scoping is the control; DMs run as the user

steps.title: Scope the service account, not just the connection
body: Share only the folders, spaces or projects Claude should see with its dedicated account; host and path rules limit endpoints, not records.

original.note: Service-owned in channels: retrieval carries the service account's access, so every member of a scope reaches what that account can, regardless of their own entitlements. Delegated in DMs, which run as the member.

controls.mechanism: No Claude Tag tenant-restriction header: the anthropic-allowed-org-ids header reaches only the claude.ai sign-in used to link accounts, and which Slack workspaces are reachable is Slack's control; the sandbox's egress is Anthropic's Agent Proxy (default-deny, admin-set allow layers), which no customer proxy sees

evidence.title: Enforce network-level access control with Tenant Restrictions
Security and data handling (Agent Proxy network egress)

controls.note: External on the D3-OTF rule: Claude Tag is used inside Slack and runs server-side, so the browser-side lever is the organisation's SSE admitting the corporate Slack workspace (a Slack-side control) and injecting anthropic-allowed-org-ids on claude.ai so members link only to the corporate organisation. A customer proxy does not control the agent's egress: every channel request leaves Anthropic's sandbox through Agent Proxy, which blocks hosts no connection, bundle Domains entry or environment network level allows (Trusted by default; allow-all is an Anthropic-enabled opt-in; private ranges and cloud metadata always blocked), while web search runs on Anthropic's servers outside those rules. Those allow layers are recorded under AML.M0028.

original.mechanism: Corporate proxy tenant-restriction header for claude.ai; Slack-side app approval and Enterprise Grid distribution controls
original.note: Claude Tag runs server-side, so the only network-layer levers are the Slack admin's app approval and the anthropic-allowed-org-ids header on claude.ai traffic for the account linking flow.

steps.title: Control the Slack side
body: Slack workspace admins decide whether the Claude app is installed; on Enterprise Grid, org admins choose which workspaces get it; removing the app revokes access immediately.

original.mechanism: Agent Proxy allow layers: connection allowed websites (credentialed), bundle Domains tab (uncredentialed, wildcard leftmost label, ports), and the scope's environment network access level (Trusted default, Custom, Full, No access); private ranges and cloud metadata always blocked; HTTP/HTTPS only

steps.title: Allow hosts per bundle
body: On the bundle's Domains tab add each hostname (and non-443 ports); requests to unlisted hosts are blocked and Claude names the blocked host in the thread.

steps.title: Pin a stricter environment on the scope
body: Create an organisation-shared cloud environment with No access or a Custom list and choose it under the scope's Advanced > Environment.

original.note: Enforced server-side by the Agent Proxy for the sandbox; artifact publishing and Slack posting are separate egress paths governed by scope settings, not the domain lists.

controls.mechanism: Inference hooks (Enterprise) govern Claude Tag sessions: each governed request, with the Slack thread, tool calls and tool results, waits for an allow or deny verdict from the organisation's DLP server; for tasks run with a member's personal connectors (limited availability) a vendor sensitive-content check holds flagged results for the requester's review, and on Enterprise an admin can require review of every result organisation-wide

steps.title: Put your DLP inline (Enterprise)
body: At claude.ai Organization settings > Data and privacy > Inference hooks turn on Allow for your organization, register your DLP server, set Failure handling to Block the request and turn on Enforce verdicts.

steps.title: Require review of every personal-connector result (Enterprise)
body: At claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-tag select Edit on the Personal connectors row and turn on Require human review of every message; it applies to every workspace and channel.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: the hook is an attach point that can block (allow or deny only, no masking; a denied message must be edited or deleted in Slack before `@Claude !restart`), and the vendor check holds rather than masks, covers only results of personal-connector tasks, and "is a screen, not a guarantee". Nothing inspects what the service accounts retrieve or what Claude posts in ordinary channel work, and artifacts are readable by everyone with access to the source channel. Default-deny egress through Agent Proxy limits where data can go but is not detection. Claude Tag is not covered by Anthropic's BAA.

original.mechanism: Default-deny egress through Agent Proxy (data leaves only to allowed hosts); credentials never enter the sandbox; Enterprise Inference hooks are not documented for Claude Tag

steps.title: Keep egress default-deny
body: Leave the environment at Trusted or pin a No access environment on the scope, list only needed hosts on the bundle's Domains tab, and do not request allow-all egress unless required.

original.note: No content inspection of prompts or outputs is offered; artifact publishing and Slack posting are the visible egress paths.
Not applicable: the surface is Slack and a server-side sandbox, not a browser session the organisation instruments.

evidence.title: Vendor docs index, reviewed for applicability (2026-09-10)

controls.mechanism: No administrator-configurable screening of Slack messages or tool results; restricted members' and guests' messages are withheld or reach Claude only as context, and personal-connector tasks take direction only from the requester; Inference hooks (Enterprise) hand each governed request, thread and tool results included, to the organisation's AI security server

steps.title: Put a screen on thread and tool content (Enterprise)
body: Register an AI security server under Organization settings > Data and privacy > Inference hooks that classifies Slack messages and tool results for injection, and turn on Enforce verdicts.

steps.title: Keep untrusted authors out of Claude's input
body: Turn on Restrict to roles with Claude Tag access (Restrict to your organization on Team) so other members' thread replies reach Claude only as context, and keep How should Claude work in channels with guests at Restrict or Channel only under Claude's access > Channels > Slack > Advanced > Access.

controls.note: Partial on the rule applied to every vendor: the vendor's measures are structural (who Claude reads, whose instructions it takes) rather than content screening an administrator can switch on and see events from, and the hook is an attach point returning allow or deny only. The auto-mode permission checker judges proposed actions, which is action policy, not input screening. Claude reads whole threads and may reply untagged while Respond automatically is on; the credential-free sandbox and default-deny egress contain an injection rather than detect it.

original.mechanism: Auto-mode classifier plus structural containment (credential-free sandbox, default-deny egress, service-account scoping)

steps.title: Contain rather than detect
body: Attach bundles holding sensitive credentials only to private channels, keep guest channels Restricted, and rely on Agent Proxy blocking unlisted hosts.

original.note: The auto-mode classifier screens proposed actions; the sandbox and default-deny egress contain. Slack messages and connector results are not classified for injected instructions.

controls.mechanism: The Anthropic Trust Center plus Claude Tag's security, data-lifecycle and healthcare pages feed the organisation's TPRM platform

evidence.title: Anthropic Trust Center (compliance scope table and resources, read 2026-09-25)
Claude Tag data lifecycle and deletion
Use Claude Tag in healthcare (not covered by the BAA)

controls.note: External by the rule applied to every vendor: the TPRM platform holds the questionnaire, evidence expiry and reassessment trigger. The Trust Center scope table lists Claude Enterprise and Claude Team (SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, ISO 42001, CSA STAR, NIST 800-171; HIPAA for Enterprise only) and does not name Claude Tag. Record the beta-specific gaps: public beta; transcripts and memory kept with no automatic retention period and excluded from data exports and the Compliance API; not available to ZDR or CMEK organisations; not covered by Anthropic's BAA; web search outside Agent Proxy rules. Reassess when it reaches general availability.

original.mechanism: Anthropic Trust Center artifacts plus the security-and-data and data-lifecycle pages feed the buyer's vendor assessment

steps.title: Record beta-specific gaps
body: Note in the vendor record that transcripts and memory have no retention period, are excluded from data exports and Compliance API sessions during the beta, and that ZDR organisations are excluded.

original.mechanism: Audit page (Scheduled work, Memory, Network events export), Access bundles page with per-connection status, analytics at claude.ai/analytics/claude-tag

steps.title: Inventory what Claude can do and does
body: Review the Access bundles page (Active / Never used per credential), the Audit page tabs at claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-tag/audit, and the per-channel Access summary.

original.note: The Audit page, Access bundles and analytics are inputs to governance; there is no intake, risk decision, ownership or lifecycle workflow in the product. Rated external on the same rule as every other vendor.

original.mechanism: Admin console readback (Access bundles, scopes, Access summary), audit log entries for channel-manager and deletion actions via the Compliance API Activity Feed

steps.title: Evidence the configuration
body: Export the channel Access summary and bundle listings, and read channel-manager credential changes and scope removals from the organisation audit log through the Compliance API.

original.note: Console readback and audit entries are the inputs an SSPM product consumes; nothing in the product compares configuration to policy or detects drift.

controls.mechanism: Channel sessions run in auto mode: Claude's permission checker (a model) reviews each action and Owners pre-approve actions per scope with Auto mode allow rules; no per-action human prompt. Personal-connector tasks ask the requester before starting and, under Allow with review or the Enterprise Require human review of every message switch, hold each result for approval before it posts; Claude's pull requests wait for a human merge

steps.title: Keep allow rules narrow
body: Add Auto mode allow rules only on the narrowest scope (scope > Advanced > Auto mode allow rules) and name the tool, action and environment; rules on a workspace or the Slack page reach every channel beneath.

steps.title: Require review of every personal-connector result (Enterprise)
body: Turn on Require human review of every message in the Personal connectors dialog at claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-tag so the requester approves every result before it posts.

steps.title: Require a second approval on Claude's pull requests
body: Require two approving reviews, or a status check only claude[bot] pull requests must pass, with stale approvals dismissed on new commits.

steps.title: Stop proactive work where it is not wanted
body: Turn off a channel's Respond automatically setting so Claude only starts work when tagged.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: no person approves an individual channel action; the permission checker is a model and never counts as human approval, and allow rules pre-approve actions with nobody present. Result review approves what posts to the channel, and a pull-request merge approves the output, not the actions taken to produce them. Guests can never approve. Routines and channel watches run unattended.

original.mechanism: Sessions run in auto mode (classifier); Owners add narrow auto-mode allow rules per scope; pull requests are drafts for humans to merge; "Respond automatically" per channel

steps.title: Keep allow rules narrow
body: Add auto-mode allow rules only on the narrowest scope (up to 50 per scope, 1,024 characters each) and name the tool, action and environment; everything else stays under the classifier.

steps.title: Stop proactive work where it is not wanted
body: Turn off a channel's Respond automatically setting so Claude only works when tagged; proactive sessions bill under Proactive.

original.note: There is no per-action approval prompt in a channel; the classifier and deny-by-egress are the gates.

controls.mechanism: No inventory or classification setting: each scope's page on the Channels tab lists the Connectors, Repositories and Plugins a channel gets, with origin lines, and the Activity page Memory tab (or a scope's View memory files) shows what Claude saved, as read-only views; what sits behind each service account is classified by the organisation's DSPM

evidence.title: Configure per-channel access (Check or remove what a place has)
Review what Claude Tag has done (Activity page Memory tab)
Data lifecycle and deletion (transcripts not in data exports or the Compliance API)

controls.note: External, lowered from partial on 2026-10-30 when the settings table was written: no Claude Tag setting delivers data inventory. The per-scope access lists and memory views are pages an Owner reads, not a control an administrator switches on, and they carry no classification or oversharing view of the drives, projects or repositories behind each service account. Transcripts are kept with no automatic retention period during the beta and are excluded from data exports and the Compliance API, so no DSPM product can consume them; deletion (scope removal, workspace disconnect) is lifecycle, not inventory. Inventory and classification of the sources behind the connections is the organisation's DSPM.

original.mechanism: Memory files viewable, editable and deletable per scope by Owners; data lifecycle table for every deletion action; no retention window during beta

steps.title: Review and prune memory
body: Open a scope's View memory files (or the Audit page Memory tab) to read, edit or delete what Claude saved; workspace memory from public channels is shared workspace-wide.

steps.title: Delete data deliberately
body: Removing a channel scope deletes its sessions, memory, routines and artifacts; disconnecting the workspace deletes everything for that workspace; version Off deletes nothing.

original.note: Memory review and deletion are lifecycle controls; nothing classifies what was saved or assesses who can read it beyond the scope model, so discovery and posture assessment remain the customer's DSPM.

controls.mechanism: Connector credentials (on the Connectors tab, or held by a bundle) sit in a write-only store and Agent Proxy injects them at the network boundary, only to the credential's allowed websites (narrowable by path and HTTP method), so neither the sandbox nor the model holds them; Rotate secret and Remove credential per credential; "Copy setup link for another admin" with approval on the Notifications Requests tab; Federated agent access replaces stored secrets with 10-minute Anthropic-signed tokens; no tunnel

steps.title: Store credentials only as connections
body: On the Connectors tab add each service with its Allowed websites, then Edit the credential in the connector's Access from table to restrict it to a path prefix and read-only methods; never put a credential in an environment variable.

steps.title: Rotate or remove a credential
body: Use Rotate secret or Remove credential from the row's menu in the connector's Access from table; have the secret's owner submit it through Copy setup link for another admin and approve it with Review on the Approval needed row of the Notifications Requests tab.

steps.title: Replace stored keys with federated tokens
body: Connect your gateway, AWS role, Google Cloud identity or authorisation server under Federated agent access so Claude presents a short-lived signed token and Anthropic stores no key.

controls.note: Native by the rule: custody is outside the sandbox and model, each credential is scoped to named hosts and methods, the administrator rotates or revokes it in the console, and lifetime is bounded where the target accepts federated tokens. Boundaries: static SaaS keys are long-lived until rotated (no expiry or rotation schedule in the product); environment variables on a scope's pinned cloud environment are readable by every session and by Claude, which is why the docs say credentials never go there; running sessions may keep a revoked credential for a short, unbounded window. Tunnel: none; a connected service must accept internet traffic from Anthropic's egress range 160.79.104.0/21 (PrivateLink and VPC peering unsupported), and sessions in self-hosted environments can't use the connectors an admin adds.

original.mechanism: Access bundle credentials (Bearer, Basic, AWS SigV4, GCP service account, OAuth client credentials, MCP Connector sign-in) injected by Agent Proxy; rotate secret and setup links for another admin to submit a secret

steps.title: Add and rotate credentials in bundles
body: On the bundle's Credentials tab connect each service, set Allowed hosts, restrict by HTTP method or path, and use Rotate secret; use "Copy link for another admin" so the secret owner submits it directly.

original.note: Bundle credentials are injected at the proxy and never reach the sandbox or the model. They are the bundle's shared credentials, presented for every session in the scope, not per-requester; rotation is manual through the rotate flow.

controls.mechanism: Per-scope bundles (the Slack page, a workspace, a channel) that only Owners and Claude Tag admins, or a channel's managers for its own bundle, fill with connectors, domains, repositories and plugins; each credential limited to allowed websites, a path prefix and HTTP methods; Agent Proxy blocks every other host; Channel only strips inherited access while a guest is present

steps.title: Attach access per channel
body: Create bundles such as data-readonly or github-write and attach each to the narrowest scope that needs it, keeping sensitive bundles on private channels only.

steps.title: Narrow each connection to read where reading is enough
body: In the connector's Access from table (or under What's in it on the bundle's page) choose Edit on a credential and restrict it to specific hosts, a path prefix and GET-only methods.

steps.title: Confirm what a channel ends up with
body: Open the channel's page from the Channels tab under Claude's access and check its Claude's access table, which shows what it inherits.

controls.note: Native by the rule: an administrator allowlist of connections with read/write (method) scoping per channel scope, locked against channel members and enforced by Agent Proxy outside the model. Boundaries: scoping is per channel or workspace, not per requesting person, so everyone in a scope gets the same reach; an MCP Connector connection is one endpoint, so path and method rules cannot pick its individual tools; a bundle on the Slack page reaches every channel; auto-mode allow rules pre-approve actions; DMs and personal-connector tasks use the member's claude.ai connectors, outside the bundles.

original.mechanism: Per-scope Access bundles (credentials, repositories, plugins, instructions) with inheritance from Default Slack to workspace to channel; connection host/path/method restrictions; plugin enable toggles per bundle

steps.title: Compose access by capability and channel
body: Create bundles such as data-readonly, github-write and monitoring, attach only what a channel needs, and keep sensitive bundles on private channels.

steps.title: Narrow each connection
body: Edit a connection to restrict it to specific hosts, a path prefix and read-only methods, and scope the underlying service account to the projects it needs.

original.note: Bundles decide which credentials, repositories and plugins a scope has (hiding); host, path and method restrictions on connections limit arguments; auto-mode allow rules pre-approve. Inheritance means a broad Default Slack bundle reaches every channel unless overridden.

controls.mechanism: In channels, retrieval uses the service account's access, scoped by what the organisation shares with that account and by the connection's hosts and paths; "Channels Claude can search" narrows Slack search to channels Claude is in; guest channels lose workspace search; DMs and personal-connector tasks run with the member's own permissions

steps.title: Scope the service account, not just the connection
body: Share only the folders, spaces or projects Claude should see with its dedicated account; host and path rules limit endpoints, not records.

steps.title: Limit Slack search to channels Claude is in
body: At claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-tag > Claude's access > Channels > the Slack page (or a workspace or channel) > Advanced set Channels Claude can search to Only channels Claude is in.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: the administrator scopes the corpus (what the service account can open, which Slack channels search covers), but channel retrieval does not carry the requester's entitlements — every member of a scope reaches what the account can, and by default Claude searches every public channel, including ones it has not been added to. Requester entitlements apply only in DMs and in personal-connector tasks, which are available to a limited number of organisations.

original.mechanism: Reach inside a tool equals what the service account can access; account-level scoping is the control; DMs run as the user

steps.title: Scope the service account, not just the connection
body: Share only the folders, spaces or projects Claude should see with its dedicated account; host and path rules limit endpoints, not records.

original.note: Service-owned in channels: retrieval carries the service account's access, so every member of a scope reaches what that account can, regardless of their own entitlements. Delegated in DMs, which run as the member.

controls.mechanism: The Connectors and Bundles tabs under Claude's access list every connector and bundle, each connector's credentials in its Access from table, and credentials submitted by setup link wait as Approval needed on the Notifications Requests tab; each scope's page lists what a channel gets; the Activity page Scheduled work tab lists every routine with Created by, Pause/Resume and Delete; a session can use only the bundles and connectors that apply to its scope

steps.title: Use the Connectors and Bundles tabs as the register
body: Review the Connectors and Bundles tabs, and approve or reject credentials a teammate submitted through a setup link on the Notifications Requests tab before they become active.

steps.title: Review unattended work
body: On the Scheduled work tab at claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-tag/audit filter by scope and pause or delete routines nobody owns.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: connections are an enforced register with an approval state for link-submitted credentials, but they carry no owner field, and routines, which run unattended with the channel's credentials, are created by any channel member without approval and appear only after creation. Personal connectors used in DMs and channel tasks are the member's and are not listed; a Claude app installed in another Slack workspace is found in Slack's app management. Channel sessions act as an Owner-provisioned identity per tool — a dedicated service account, the Claude Slack or GitHub app, or a federated identity — so the register lists non-human principals rather than people's logins.

original.mechanism: Scopes and bundles are the registry of where Claude runs and with what; Scheduled work tab lists every routine with Created by

steps.title: List where Claude operates and what is scheduled
body: The Slack tab under Claude Tag's access lists workspaces and channels with their bundles; the Audit page Scheduled work tab lists routines with pause and delete.

original.note: Scopes, bundles and the routine list are approved configuration and use within Slack; there is no owner or approval record per routine beyond Created by.

controls.mechanism: Claude Tag lists no personal accounts or unsanctioned installs; Slack's app management (Manage apps, App requests), the claude.ai organisation's domain claiming and SSE/CASB find them; "Restrict to your verified domains" and blocked channel patterns prevent rather than discover

evidence.title: What the Claude Slack app can access (Slack administrator's view)
Restrict where Claude Tag operates

controls.note: External by the rule: the product has no view of Claude used outside the organisation's pairing — a workspace paired to another Claude organisation, personal claude.ai accounts, or members' own connectors. Slack administration (app installs and approval requests), the claude.ai organisation's Enterprise domain claiming (recorded on toolClaudeWeb) and SSE/CASB find those. Inside the sanctioned deployment the Scheduled work tab inventories member-created routines, and Restrict to your verified domains stops verified-domain Slack users linking to outside organisations — prevention, credited here only.

original.mechanism: Blocked and auto-join channel name patterns; Claude responds only where added; per-scope version Off; Slack app inventory

steps.title: Fence channels by name
body: Add Blocked channel patterns (for example *-confidential-*) under Default Slack access > Advanced so Claude stays silent even if invited.

original.note: Channel patterns and version Off are prevention; the Slack app inventory that would reveal an unsanctioned Claude install belongs to Slack administration, not this product.

controls.mechanism: The Compliance API Activity Feed records control-plane events (ccr_agent_* bindings and Slack access scopes, Agent Proxy credential creation, rotation and deletion, proxy rules, channel managers, workspace pairings); the Activity page Network events tab exports hourly JSON of Agent Proxy calls (no git or MCP traffic); Inference hooks (Enterprise) can push each governed transcript to an organisation endpoint; session transcripts are not in the Compliance API or data exports during the beta

steps.title: Stream control-plane events (Enterprise)
body: Poll /v1/compliance/activities with a read:compliance_activities key and keep the ccr_agent_*, slack_workspace_* and inference_hooks_* events in the SIEM.

steps.title: Download network events
body: Export each hour's Network events JSON from claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-tag/audit and correlate with the service accounts' entries in each tool's audit log.

steps.title: Archive transcripts through a hook (Enterprise, beta)
body: Point Inference hooks at an endpoint that stores each transcript and always returns allow.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: the vendor's exports are control-plane events and network metadata; conversation content and tool calls leave only through an archival hook the organisation builds, which misses requests while the circuit breaker is tripped, those outside the rollout percentage and system prompts, or not at all on Team. The network export is a per-hour console download without git or MCP traffic, there is no per-action log of who asked, and a member's Home tab Disconnect or a deletion started in Slack is not in the audit log.

original.mechanism: Audit page (routines, memory, hourly Network events JSON export of Agent Proxy calls, excluding git and MCP), attribution under service accounts in each tool's logs, organisation audit log via Compliance API for channel-manager and deletion events

steps.title: Download network events and read tool-side logs
body: Export hourly Network events from claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-tag/audit and correlate with the service account's entries in GitHub, Datadog and other tools.

original.note: Session transcripts are not exportable and the Compliance API does not list Claude Tag sessions during the beta.

controls.mechanism: "Enable Claude Tag in Slack" switch (top of claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-tag, turns off DMs too), per-scope Enable Claude Tag in this workspace / channel switches and Respond in all channels (Respond in channels on Team), Allow direct messages, Delete bundle (revokes its credentials everywhere, running sessions included), federated connection removal, Scheduled work Pause/Delete, spend limits, workspace Disconnect or app uninstall

steps.title: Turn Claude Tag off for the organisation
body: Turn off Enable Claude Tag in Slack at the top of claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-tag; it stops channels and direct messages and deletes nothing.

steps.title: Revoke the credentials in bulk
body: Choose Delete bundle on each bundle's page, which revokes its credentials everywhere it applied, and remove federated connections under Federated agent access.

steps.title: Stop unattended work
body: Pause or delete routines on the Scheduled work tab at claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-tag/audit.

steps.title: Decommission a workspace
body: Select Disconnect on the workspace in Connected workspaces to delete its sessions, memory, routines, artifacts, scopes and account links.

controls.note: Native by the rule: an Owner can disable the product organisation-wide, revoke every credential a bundle holds in one action per bundle, and the docs say running sessions lose a revoked credential after "a short window" (no bound published) and that a removed federated gateway stops at once and a removed cloud role or authorisation server within about a minute, with tokens already issued valid up to 10 minutes (exchanged AWS credentials up to an hour). Not documented: whether the organisation switch or a scope's enable switch ends a thread already running, so work that needs no credential may continue until it finishes (delay not documented). Members removed from the organisation lose access within minutes; personal connectors are revoked per member (Home tab Disconnect) or with the workspace disconnect; the Claude GitHub App is uninstalled at GitHub.

original.mechanism: Enable Claude Tag for your organization toggle, per-scope Claude Tag version Off, Allow direct messages off, /remove @Claude, bundle deletion (revokes credentials everywhere), workspace disconnect, app uninstall, spend limit reached

steps.title: Stop responding and revoke credentials
body: Set the scope's version to Off (or the org toggle), then delete the bundle to revoke its credentials; running sessions may hold a revoked credential briefly.

steps.title: Decommission the data
body: Disconnect the workspace at claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-tag to delete its sessions, memory, routines, artifacts and account links.

original.note: Setting a scope Off stops new sessions; a running session may hold a revoked credential briefly, and the docs give no bound for that window — measure it.

settings.name: Require SSO for Claude
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Organization and access › Authentication
settings.recommended: On, with MFA enforced on the Claude app in your IdP
settings.why: The Claude account a member links from Slack, and runs direct messages on, signs in through the corporate IdP and its MFA.

settings.name: User provisioning (SCIM)
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Organization and access › User provisioning
settings.recommended: SCIM, driven by the IdP group that grants Claude
settings.why: A member removed in the IdP leaves the organisation and loses Claude Tag within minutes, and the routines they set up in direct messages are turned off.

settings.name: Require approved apps (Only allow pre-approved apps)
settings.where: Slack › Admin › Apps and workflows › App Management Settings
settings.recommended: On, with the Claude app approved only for the workspaces your Claude organisation pairs
settings.why: A member can't install Claude into another workspace and pair it with a different Claude organisation; installs go through a Slack admin who reviews the scopes.

settings.name: Enable Claude Tag in Slack
settings.where: claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-tag (top of the page)
settings.recommended: On, once access restriction, bundles and blocked channel patterns are in place
settings.why: The organisation-wide off switch for every channel and direct message; turning it off deletes nothing, so it is safe to use in an incident.

settings.name: Restrict to roles with Claude Tag access (Restrict to your organization on Team)
settings.where: claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-tag › Claude's access › Channels › Slack › Advanced › Access
settings.default: Off (anyone in the paired Slack workspace can use Claude, even without a Claude account)
settings.recommended: On, with a custom role granting the Claude Tag in Slack capability to the groups rolled out
settings.why: Only members with a seat can direct Claude; others' mentions get a private notice and their thread replies reach Claude as context, not requests.

settings.name: Restrict to your verified domains
settings.where: claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-tag › Claude's access › Channels › Slack › Advanced › Access
settings.recommended: On
settings.why: Slack users off your verified domains can't link a Claude account, and users on them can't link to an organisation outside your enterprise.

settings.name: Claude Tag Admin
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Roles › role › Admin permissions › Product admin
settings.recommended: Can manage for a named few on the team that owns Claude Tag; channel managers for single channels
settings.why: Bundles, credentials, domains and guest settings stay with people you chose, without making them organisation Owners.

settings.name: How should Claude work in channels with guests
settings.where: claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-tag › Claude's access › Channels › Slack (or a workspace or channel) › Advanced › Access
settings.recommended: Restrict on the Slack page; Channel only on a client channel whose team asks, with nothing sensitive attached to it
settings.why: Guests and Slack Connect partners can read what Claude posts and direct it; Restrict keeps them away, and Channel only drops inherited bundles, memory and search.

settings.name: Blocked channel patterns
settings.where: claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-tag › Claude's access › Channels › Slack (or a workspace) › Advanced › Channels
settings.recommended: Your confidential channel naming patterns, for example *-confidential-*, hr-* and legal-*
settings.why: Claude won't read or respond in a matching channel even if someone invites it, and a workspace can add patterns but not remove the organisation's.

settings.name: Channels Claude can search
settings.where: claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-tag › Claude's access › Channels › Slack (or a workspace or channel) › Advanced › Channels
settings.recommended: All public channels
settings.why: Public channels are open to every member already and private ones are never searched; regulated teams choose Only channels Claude is in.

settings.name: Auto mode allow rules
settings.where: claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-tag › Claude's access › Channels › scope › Advanced › Sessions
settings.recommended: None on the Slack page or workspaces; narrow rules naming tool, action and environment on single channels
settings.why: A rule pre-approves an action in every channel beneath its scope with nobody approving it; the permission checker keeps reviewing everything else.

settings.name: Allowed websites
settings.where: claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-tag › Claude's access › Connectors › connector › connect form
settings.recommended: The service's own API hosts only, with a dedicated service account per tool
settings.why: Agent Proxy attaches the credential only for the listed hosts and the sandbox never holds it, so a prompt-injected request elsewhere goes out without it.

settings.name: Restrict by path or method
settings.where: claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-tag › Connectors › connector › Access from › Edit connection
settings.recommended: GET only, and a path prefix, wherever the channel only needs to read
settings.why: Everyone in a scope can make Claude act with its credentials; a read-only connection can't delete or post even if Claude is told to.

settings.name: Allow all hosts
settings.where: claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-tag › Bundles › bundle › Add a domain (Domain `*`)
settings.default: Not set (Limited access environment plus the hosts you add)
settings.recommended: Not set — add Read-only domain entries one host at a time
settings.why: Sandbox requests reach only hosts a connection, domain entry or environment allows; a `*` entry, or a Full access environment on a scope, opens every host.

settings.name: Federated agent access
settings.where: claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-tag › Federated agent access
settings.recommended: A gateway, AWS role, Google Cloud identity or authorization server for every system that accepts one
settings.why: Claude presents a 10-minute signed token your system checks, so no long-lived key is stored in Claude for those systems.

settings.name: Every repository in (repository grant)
settings.where: claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-tag › Bundles › bundle › Add › Repository
settings.recommended: Not used — grant named repositories to each bundle or channel
settings.why: The grant is every repository in the GitHub App installation, including ones added later; named grants keep a channel to the code it works on.

settings.name: Require two approving reviews
settings.where: GitHub › repository › branch protection rule or ruleset on the branches Claude opens pull requests against
settings.recommended: Two approving reviews, with stale approvals dismissed on new commits
settings.why: Claude authors its pull requests, so the person who asked for the change could otherwise approve and merge it alone.

settings.name: Require human review of every message
settings.where: claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-tag › Personal connectors › Edit
settings.recommended: Off — the sensitive-content check holds flagged results for the requester
settings.why: Results of tasks run on a member's personal connectors are screened before posting; regulated teams turn it on so every result waits for the requester.

settings.name: Additional topics (Sensitive information requiring review)
settings.where: claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-tag › Personal connectors › Edit
settings.recommended: Your own markers — client code names, deal names, board material
settings.why: Personal-connector results touching those topics are held for the requester's review instead of posting to the channel.

settings.name: Inference hooks
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › Data and privacy › Inference hooks
settings.recommended: On, connected to your DLP or AI-security service, enforcing after a monitor-only period
settings.why: Each Claude Tag request, the Slack thread and tool results included, is checked by your own service before inference, so secrets and injected content can be stopped centrally.

settings.name: Spend limit
settings.where: claude.ai/admin-settings/usage/claude-tag (organisation, default and per-channel limits)
settings.recommended: A monthly organisation limit, and a default per-channel limit, sized from the pilot
settings.why: A looping routine or channel stops when its limit is reached instead of drawing on the whole usage balance; a 0 default also stops direct messages from members without a seat.

settings.name: Compliance API (Activity Feed)
settings.where: claude.ai Organization settings › API, then a Compliance Access Key
settings.recommended: On, pulled into your SIEM
settings.why: Bindings, Slack access scopes, connector credentials and proxy rules (ccr_agent_* events) reach the SIEM; Claude Tag transcripts are not in the Compliance API during the beta.
