tools.name: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

variants.name: AgentCore harness (config-only managed loop; CreateHarness / InvokeHarness)
variants.note: GA June 2026. AWS runs the Strands-based loop in a microVM per session; model, prompt, tools, skills, memory and limits are configuration. Built-in shell and file_operations tools are on unless allowedTools restricts them.

variants.name: AgentCore Runtime (bring-your-own agent code on microVMs; InvokeAgentRuntime)
variants.note: The escape hatch: AWS supplies the microVM, identity and endpoints, the loop is your code, and it gets Memory, Gateway, Identity and guardrails only where the code calls them.

variants.name: AgentCore Runtime on Instances (capacity providers; EC2 managed instances in your account)
variants.note: Sessions of up to 14 days on one EC2 instance per session; several agents can share an instance and are not isolated from each other. Data and EBS volumes stay in your account and VPC.

summary: AWS's decomposed agent platform: Runtime (a Firecracker microVM per session, bring-your-own code or the config-only managed harness), Memory (short- and long-term, scoped by actor and session), Gateway (tools from Lambda, OpenAPI, Smithy and MCP servers behind one MCP endpoint with inbound and outbound auth), Identity (a workload identity per agent and a token vault for OAuth tokens and API keys), Policy (Cedar policy engines and Bedrock Guardrails checks evaluated at the gateway), Code Interpreter, Browser, Observability (CloudWatch and X-Ray in your account) and Evaluations, each billed separately and driven over the bedrock-agentcore(-control) APIs with IAM SigV4 or a JWT from your IdP. Inference is Amazon Bedrock by default; the harness can also call OpenAI, Gemini or any LiteLLM provider directly.

Governance is IAM-native: condition keys on the control plane (subnets and security groups, gateway authorizer type, policy engine and mode, target and credential-provider types, memory actor and namespace) let an organisation set floors by SCP that a builder cannot lower, and the Cedar engine is default-deny per tool call. The gaps are boundaries rather than missing features: only traffic through a Gateway is policy-evaluated and guardrail-screened, InvokeHarness callers can override tools, skills, prompt and model per call, the harness runs on the public network with managed memory on (API default) unless configured otherwise, and session IDs are not bound to the caller.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Pay per AgentCore service used (Runtime per-second vCPU and memory, Memory events, records and retrievals, Gateway calls, Browser and Code Interpreter sessions, CloudWatch ingestion); the harness itself has no separate charge. GA; harness GA June 2026.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Harness: Amazon Bedrock (Converse Stream, or Responses / Chat Completions via Bedrock Mantle), OpenAI, Google Gemini or any LiteLLM-compatible provider, switchable per turn and overridable per InvokeHarness call; model fields (modelId, apiBase, additionalParams) pass through unvalidated. Runtime: whatever model the customer's code calls.

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: Everything runs in AWS: prompts, tool inputs and outputs and session files in the microVM (public network unless VPC mode), memory in AgentCore Memory, traces and logs in your CloudWatch. Memory extraction, Policy and Evaluations use cross-region inference inside the geography; a harness configured for OpenAI, Gemini or LiteLLM sends the conversation to that provider.

facts.label: Retention & training
facts.value: MicroVM state is ephemeral and memory-sanitized at session end (idle 900 s, max 8 h by default); session storage persists per runtimeSessionId until the runtime is deleted; Memory events expire per eventExpiryDuration (3–365 days), long-term records until deleted; traces follow your CloudWatch retention. Bedrock content is not used to improve base models or shared with model providers; third-party providers' terms apply to their calls.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Developer Guide (harness, Runtime, Memory, Gateway, Identity, Policy, tools)

facts.label: Compliance scope
facts.value: HIPAA eligible; FedRAMP (Class C and D), SOC 2, ISO 27001/27017/27018/27701 and CSA STAR per the developer guide (the AgentCore FAQ still says FedRAMP is being pursued); reports in AWS Artifact.

facts.label: Network modes
facts.value: networkMode PUBLIC (default) or VPC (ENIs in your subnets via AWSServiceRoleForBedrockAgentCoreNetwork) for harness, Runtime, Code Interpreter and Browser; Code Interpreter also offers SANDBOX. Inbound API calls can use a PrivateLink interface endpoint; private MCP targets are reached via VPC Lattice.

facts.label: Predecessor
facts.value: Amazon Bedrock Agents Classic closed to new customers on 2026-07-30 (maintenance mode, model catalog frozen); AWS recommends migrating to the AgentCore harness.

items.title: Strip the InvokeHarness override surface in the front end
body: InvokeHarness accepts tools, allowedTools, skills, systemPrompt, model, actorId and limits per call, and the harness does not validate additionalParams, apiBase or modelId. Forward only the user's message and derive actorId and runtimeSessionId server-side; lifecycle hooks are the one setting a caller cannot override.

items.title: Set organisation floors by SCP
body: Deny CreateAgentRuntime / UpdateAgentRuntime / CreateCodeInterpreter / CreateBrowser without bedrock-agentcore:subnets, and CreateGateway / UpdateGateway unless bedrock-agentcore:PolicyEngineMode is ENFORCE; restrict CreateGatewayTarget by McpTargetConfigurationType and CredentialProviderType.

riskNotes.note: CreateHarness through the API provisions managed memory when memory is omitted (the CLI defaults to none), and actorId is whatever the caller passes; spans carry model payloads and tool request and response data into CloudWatch, where CVE-2026-15737 showed raw prompts landing in span attributes.

Skills fetched from S3 or Git are injected as trusted input, and callers can override skills per invocation. Bedrock Guardrails' prompt-attack filter does not evaluate toolResult content on the Converse path, so only guardrail policies at the Gateway screen what tools return.

SigV4 callers carry no per-user identity into downstream tools, the gateway service role is shared by every GATEWAY_IAM_ROLE target, and GetWorkloadAccessTokenForUserId trusts a caller-supplied userId. Token passthrough forwards the caller's inbound token to a gateway target unmodified, and invocation is authorised against the runtime ARN, not the session: a shared backend principal can route one user's request into another user's runtimeSessionId, and the credentials it holds, unless the application binds them.

shell and file_operations are available in every harness session unless allowedTools removes them, commands run as root in the microVM, and InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand executes commands without the model at a higher privilege level.
AWS Agent Registry auto-detection catalogs AgentCore Runtimes and Gateways across AWS Organizations member accounts; agents built on other services or outside AWS are registered by hand.

remote_mcp tools are declared by URL in the harness and fetched live; Gateway MCP targets cache the tool catalog until SynchronizeGatewayTargets or pin it with mcpToolSchema, which is the re-gating point for definition changes.

controls.mechanism: ListHarnesses / ListHarnessVersions / ListAgentRuntimes / ListGateways / ListWorkloadIdentities with tags; AWS Agent Registry records (DRAFT → PENDING_APPROVAL → APPROVED via UpdateRegistryRecordStatus) with AWS Organizations auto-detection of Runtimes and Gateways; IAM and SCPs on the create and update actions

steps.title: Turn on organisation-wide auto-detection
body: Enable auto-detection on an organization-scoped registry from the delegated administrator so every AgentCore Runtime and Gateway in member accounts becomes a record with a DETECTED_FROM provenance entry naming its ARN.

steps.title: Curate records through approval
body: Records move DRAFT → PENDING_APPROVAL → APPROVED; route the EventBridge submit event to your review workflow and approve or reject with UpdateRegistryRecordStatus (turn auto-approval off).

steps.title: Restrict who can deploy a definition
body: Grant CreateHarness, UpdateHarness, CreateAgentRuntime, UpdateAgentRuntime and CreateGatewayTarget only to the delivery pipeline's role; the harness actions also require the matching AgentRuntime action on the same ARN.

controls.note: The listable inventory is native (every harness, runtime, version, gateway and workload identity) and the tenant gates creation by IAM and SCP. Registry approval gates discovery, not execution: nothing consults it before InvokeHarness, so "unregistered means denied" is IAM's job. Auto-detection covers Runtimes and Gateways; the docs do not say whether harnesses (Runtimes underneath) appear as their own records. The public-preview registry namespace (bedrock-agentcore) ends on 2026-10-30.

controls.mechanism: Immutable versions created on every UpdateHarness / UpdateAgentRuntime; named endpoints pinned by CreateHarnessEndpoint / UpdateHarnessEndpoint targetVersion (UpdateAgentRuntimeEndpoint for Runtime); A/B tests through an AgentCore Gateway with control and treatment weights scored by online evaluation, then promote or stop

steps.title: Pin production to an endpoint and roll back by pointer
body: Create a production endpoint with targetVersion; DEFAULT follows every update, the named endpoint does not until UpdateHarnessEndpoint moves it, and moving it back to the prior version is the rollback.

steps.title: Canary through an A/B test
body: Run agentcore run ab-test with --control-weight 90 --treatment-weight 10 and a per-variant online evaluation; stop reverts all traffic to control, promote writes the treatment into agentcore.json for the next deploy.

steps.title: Score each version before it moves
body: Attach online evaluation configurations (sampling rate, built-in evaluators such as Builtin.GoalSuccessRate and Builtin.ToolSelectionAccuracy, or custom ones) to the endpoints under test.

controls.note: Versioning, one-step rollback and progressive traffic are native; the evaluation in the promotion path scores but does not block (a person runs promote), evaluators measure quality and safety rather than adversarial behaviour, and no automated rollback on regression is documented. The traffic split applies only to requests routed through a Gateway (one running test per gateway, sticky by session ID); A/B walkthroughs use Runtime endpoints, and a front end that calls InvokeHarness on DEFAULT gets every update at once. Rated native on the architecture rule because versions, endpoints, weighted traffic and an evaluation step all exist, which the first-party runtimes do not offer.

controls.mechanism: AgentCore Gateway outbound authorization per target — OAuth client credentials, authorization code (tokens keyed to user and workload), on-behalf-of token exchange, API key, gateway IAM role or caller IAM credentials — injected by the gateway; SCP keys bedrock-agentcore:CredentialProviderType and CredentialProviderScope on CreateGatewayTarget / UpdateGatewayTarget

steps.title: Put tools behind a gateway with per-target credentials
body: Register each MCP, OpenAPI or Lambda tool as a gateway target with its own credential provider; prefer the token exchange (on-behalf-of) grant so the downstream token carries both user and agent.

steps.title: Authenticate callers with a JWT, not SigV4
body: Set authorizerConfiguration customJWTAuthorizer (discoveryUrl, allowedClients) on the harness; with SigV4 callers the harness propagates no per-user identity and user-scoped vault tokens and on-behalf-of exchange are unavailable.

steps.title: Constrain credential types organisation-wide
body: Deny CreateGatewayTarget and UpdateGatewayTarget unless bedrock-agentcore:CredentialProviderType is on your approved list, keeping JWT_PASSTHROUGH off targets outside the trust boundary.

controls.note: Held outside the agent and injected per destination with per-user scoping on the Gateway path, which meets the architecture rule. Paths outside it: remote_mcp headers on the harness (plain text, or a ${arn:...} token-vault reference the harness resolves at invocation) and Runtime code calling GetResourceOauth2Token or GetResourceApiKey both put the credential inside the session process. The gateway service role is shared by every GATEWAY_IAM_ROLE target and is the upper bound for any caller, and token passthrough forwards the inbound token unmodified.

controls.mechanism: Policy in AgentCore: a Cedar (Dogwood-compatible) policy engine attached to a gateway as policyEngineConfiguration {arn, mode ENFORCE | LOG_ONLY}, default-deny and forbid-wins on every tools/call over principal, tool and context.input, with temporal session rules; SCP keys bedrock-agentcore:PolicyEngineArn and PolicyEngineMode; harness before_tool_call Lambda hooks

steps.title: Attach a policy engine in ENFORCE
body: Create a policy engine and set policyEngineConfiguration arn and mode on CreateGateway or UpdateGateway; run LOG_ONLY first, then ENFORCE, in which anything not permitted is denied.

steps.title: Write per-tool rules over the arguments
body: Permit named actions such as AgentCore::Action::"RefundTool___process_refund" for a principal only when a context.input condition holds (amount < 500), and forbid the rest.

steps.title: Make ENFORCE a floor builders cannot lower
body: By SCP, deny CreateGateway and UpdateGateway unless bedrock-agentcore:PolicyEngineMode is ENFORCE and bedrock-agentcore:PolicyEngineArn is an approved engine.

steps.title: Cover tools the gateway does not see
body: Configure a before_tool_call hook with a Lambda target and failureMode deny; it receives toolName, toolType and toolInput for built-in, remote MCP, gateway and inline tools and can skip the call.

controls.note: Two AWS pages disagree: policy-enforcement-modes says no condition key protects the mode beyond UpdateGateway, while the Gateway condition-keys page and the service authorization reference list bedrock-agentcore:PolicyEngineMode for CreateGateway and UpdateGateway; set the SCP and test that a LOG_ONLY or null update is refused. The deterministic engine sees only gateway traffic: harness shell and file_operations, Browser, Code Interpreter and direct remote_mcp tools are outside it, the before_tool_call hook is the deployer's own Lambda logic, inline_function (custom) tools return to the application, InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand bypasses the loop (IAM is its only gate), and Runtime code reaches the engine only if it routes tools through a gateway.

controls.mechanism: Memory events scoped by actorId + sessionId, long-term namespaces such as /strategy/{memoryStrategyId}/actor/{actorId}/, IAM condition keys bedrock-agentcore:actorId, sessionId and namespace, Cedar FGAC through the Memory gateway connector, eventExpiryDuration, DeleteEvent and DeleteMemoryRecord; harness memory disabled | managedMemoryConfiguration | agentCoreMemoryConfiguration

steps.title: Decide memory on every harness
body: The API provisions managed memory when memory is omitted; set memory {"disabled": {}} or attach a BYO memory (agentCoreMemoryConfiguration) with a customer-managed key and eventExpiryDuration.

steps.title: Scope long-term namespaces per actor
body: Use namespace templates ending in /actor/{actorId}/ with a trailing slash, and restrict callers with the bedrock-agentcore:actorId and namespace condition keys.

steps.title: Bind actorId to the signed-in user
body: Front Memory with a gateway Memory connector and a Cedar policy that permits event access only when the request's actorId equals the JWT sub.

steps.title: Expire and delete
body: Set eventExpiryDuration (3–365 days) and remove poisoned or personal records with DeleteEvent and DeleteMemoryRecord.

controls.note: Scope, disable, expire and delete are all settable. On the harness actorId is an InvokeHarness field, so isolation holds only if the front end derives it from the authenticated user, and the documented execution-role policy grants memory actions with no actor condition. Contents are not validated: AWS puts memory-poisoning prevention on the customer (sanitise with guardrails before CreateEvent). Long-term extraction runs cross-region inside the geography. The CLI creates harnesses without memory; the API does not.

controls.mechanism: AWS Artifact audit reports and the AgentCore compliance-validation page feed the buyer's TPRM platform

evidence.title: Compliance validation for Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
AWS Artifact
AWS services in scope by compliance program

controls.note: A TPRM platform holds the assessment; AWS supplies the evidence. AgentCore is HIPAA eligible and listed for FedRAMP Class C and D, SOC 2, ISO 27001/27017/27018/27701 and CSA STAR on the developer guide, while the AgentCore FAQ still says FedRAMP is being pursued — confirm on services-in-scope. There is no zero data retention mode: retention is what you configure. Memory, Policy and Evaluations use cross-region inference inside the geography, and a harness pointed at OpenAI, Gemini or LiteLLM adds that provider as a subprocessor to assess separately. Re-assess on the 2026 bulletins.

controls.mechanism: A dedicated Firecracker microVM per runtimeSessionId (harness and Runtime) with isolated CPU, memory and filesystem, terminated and memory-sanitized at session end (lifecycleConfiguration idleRuntimeSessionTimeout default 900 s, maxLifetime default 28800 s); Code Interpreter and Browser run their own sessions; Instances run one EC2 instance per session

steps.title: One session ID per user conversation
body: Generate runtimeSessionId server-side from the authenticated user (33+ characters) and never accept it from the client; AgentCore does not enforce session-to-user mapping.

steps.title: Bound the microVM's life
body: Set lifecycleConfiguration idleRuntimeSessionTimeout and maxLifetime on CreateAgentRuntime or UpdateAgentRuntime (harness: idle and lifetime limits) so compute is reclaimed promptly.

steps.title: Keep untrusted agents off shared Instances
body: On the Instances compute type the session, not the agent, is the isolation unit; give agents that are not mutually trusted separate sessions or separate capacity providers.

controls.note: Inside the microVM: shell, file_operations, a custom container and, on Runtime, the customer's whole agent loop. Outside: inference, Gateway, Memory, and Browser and Code Interpreter sessions (their own sandboxes). Commands run as root in the microVM and InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand at a higher privilege; a caller allowed to invoke the runtime ARN can route into any session ID it knows. On Instances the boundary is an EC2 instance in your account shared by co-located agents. Unit 42 showed Code Interpreter SANDBOX mode leaking DNS in 2026; AWS remediated it.

controls.mechanism: networkConfiguration.networkMode PUBLIC (default) | VPC with subnets and security groups on the harness, Runtime, Code Interpreter and Browser; Code Interpreter SANDBOX mode; IAM keys bedrock-agentcore:subnets and securityGroups to force VPC mode; host allowlisting only by the VPC's own firewall and DNS controls

steps.title: Run sessions in VPC mode
body: Create the harness with environment agentCoreRuntimeEnvironment.networkConfiguration networkMode VPC and private subnets and security groups; add VPC endpoints for ECR, S3 and bedrock-runtime instead of a NAT route.

steps.title: Force VPC mode by SCP
body: Deny CreateAgentRuntime, UpdateAgentRuntime, CreateCodeInterpreter and CreateBrowser when bedrock-agentcore:subnets or securityGroups is null or not on the approved list.

steps.title: Close the code interpreter
body: Under AgentCore > Built-in Tools > Code Interpreter > Create, choose Network settings Sandbox (limited external network access) or VPC rather than Public network.

controls.note: Partial on the architecture rule: AgentCore offers a network mode, not a provider-enforced host list. Exact-host allowlisting is the VPC's firewall and DNS filtering — ours to run, as for a self-hosted worker. The harness defaults to the public network, and CreateHarness / UpdateHarness are not among the operations documented to evaluate the subnet condition keys. Paths the mode does not govern: model inference, Gateway targets (egress from the gateway, with its own private endpoints) and the Web Search connector, which is served inside AWS.

controls.mechanism: allowedTools patterns on the harness (@builtin/shell, @server/tool, globs; all tools when omitted); per-target tools at the gateway with Cedar rules over tool and arguments; MCP targets in DEFAULT listing mode cache the catalog until SynchronizeGatewayTargets, or pin it with mcpToolSchema; SCP key bedrock-agentcore:McpTargetConfigurationType

steps.title: Name the tools the agent may select
body: Set allowedTools to the specific entries the agent needs (for example "@builtin/file_operations", "@crm/read_*"), leaving shell out unless required.

steps.title: Admit MCP servers through gateway targets
body: Register servers as gateway targets with a static mcpToolSchema, or review the diff before each SynchronizeGatewayTargets, so a server's new tools stay unavailable until re-approved.

steps.title: Remove direct command execution
body: Grant bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand to nobody who fronts users; allowedTools does not govern it.

controls.note: Per-tool enablement and argument-level permission at the gateway meet the rule. InvokeHarness accepts tools, allowedTools and skills per call and no condition key restricts those fields, so any principal with InvokeHarness can widen the set unless the front end strips them; the next UpdateHarness can undo it unless IAM restricts that action. remote_mcp servers declared by URL are admitted as declared and nothing verifies what they serve; the gateway's cached or static catalog is the only re-gating on definition change.

controls.mechanism: Token vault for OAuth tokens, client credentials and API keys encrypted with an AWS owned or customer managed KMS key; client secrets in Secrets Manager; Private Key JWT client authentication with the key in KMS; SigV4 with short-lived STS role credentials or a JWT for the API; no tunnel — PrivateLink inbound and VPC ENIs or VPC Lattice outbound, authorised by IAM

steps.title: Encrypt the token vault with your key
body: Configure a single-Region symmetric customer managed KMS key (by ARN) for the token vault, and a CMK on the credential providers' Secrets Manager secrets.

steps.title: Replace shared client secrets with Private Key JWT
body: On a CustomOauth2 credential provider, choose Private Key JWT and give the ARN of an asymmetric KMS signing key, so AgentCore Identity signs client assertions in KMS instead of holding a secret.

steps.title: Scope who can read a credential
body: Name exact provider ARNs in GetResourceOauth2Token, GetResourceApiKey and secretsmanager:GetSecretValue statements, and prefer gateway-injected credentials to remote_mcp headers or code retrieval.

controls.note: Partial: the store is encrypted and the API runs on short-lived credentials, but the vault is not write-only. GetResourceOauth2Token and GetResourceApiKey return values to any workload whose role allows them, and the documented harness execution-role policy grants secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on the credential's secret; only gateway-injected credentials never reach the agent's process (the harness docs say agent code never sees model API keys, without saying whether its shell can). Tunnel story: AWS offers no outbound-only tunnel; private MCP servers are reached through VPC mode or gateway private endpoints on VPC Lattice, so there is no tunnel token to rotate.

controls.mechanism: inline_function tools pause the loop (stopReason tool_use) and hand toolUseId and the model's input to the caller, which must return the matching toolResult on the same runtimeSessionId; the harness rejects caller-supplied toolUse blocks; before_tool_call Lambda hooks (allow or deny, timeoutSeconds up to 900); temporal Cedar rules requiring a prior approval action

steps.title: Route consequential actions through inline functions
body: Define the action as an inline_function tool, show the pending toolUseId and input to a person, and send the toolResult only after they approve.

steps.title: Require a recorded approval at the gateway
body: Write a temporal policy that permits the action only if an approval action's response (output approved true) was recorded formerly within 1h in the same policy session for the same resource.

controls.note: Partial: a pause bound to the exact call exists only for inline functions, which the application executes anyway. Built-in, remote MCP and gateway tools have no per-call ask mode; the before_tool_call hook and the temporal policy make the approval the deployer's own Lambda or approval tool, and an after_tool_call event confirms the harness processed a client result, not that the action happened. CVE-2026-18830 (fixed) let a caller dispatch configured tools without the model.

controls.mechanism: Guardrails in Policy in AgentCore at the gateway: BedrockGuardrails::PromptAttack, ContentFilter and SensitiveInformation checks in a when guardrails block — forbid over context.input, suppressOutput over context.output of MCP, HTTP runtime and inference targets — scored by bedrock:InvokeGuardrailChecks with the decision logged

steps.title: Screen what tools return
body: Add a suppressOutput policy whose when guardrails block runs BedrockGuardrails checks over the target response's context.output fields, and a forbid policy with PromptAttack(["PROMPT_INJECTION"]) over context.input.

steps.title: Grant the check and calibrate
body: Give the gateway execution role bedrock:InvokeGuardrailChecks, run the engine in LOG_ONLY to read the scores, then set thresholds (defaults 0.4 prompt attack, 0.2 content and sensitive data).

controls.note: Partial on the input-screening rule: the gateway can classify returned tool content with a block and a logged decision, but the documented output-side checks are ContentFilter and SensitiveInformation; PromptAttack is documented over context.input (what the agent sends), and injection screening of what a tool returns is not shown, so it is not credited until a LOG_ONLY test proves it. It covers gateway targets only, in the Regions the guardrails table lists (not all AgentCore Regions); the docs' output examples use ContentFilter and SensitiveInformation, so test PromptAttack over context.output in LOG_ONLY before relying on it. Not screened: harness built-in tools, direct remote_mcp results, Browser pages, Code Interpreter output and memory retrieval. A guardrailConfig on the model does not help: on Converse it does not evaluate toolResult blocks.

controls.mechanism: AgentCore Observability: harness invocations emit traces, logs and metrics (model calls, tool invocations with payloads, memory operations, shell commands) to CloudWatch and X-Ray in your account, spans in /aws/bedrock-agentcore/runtimes/<id>-<endpoint> (UNIFIED_TRACES_DESTINATION_ENABLED, default for agents created from 2026-07-20) or aws/spans; Runtime via ADOT; CloudTrail management and data events

steps.title: Turn on Transaction Search
body: Enable CloudWatch Transaction Search once per account (CloudWatch > Application Signals > Transaction search); harness traces then flow with no further configuration.

steps.title: Instrument Runtime code
body: Add ADOT with AGENT_OBSERVABILITY_ENABLED=true and AWS_GENAI_CONTENT_EXTRACTION_OPT_OUT=true to keep tool request and response data on spans; without instrumentation a Runtime agent emits no steps.

steps.title: Record data events off-account
body: Create a trail with advanced event selectors for AgentCore data events into an S3 bucket in a separate logging account.

controls.note: Every step lands in our own account, so retention, KMS and SIEM subscription are ours. Not tamper-evident by itself: principals with CloudWatch Logs permissions can alter or delete log groups, so ship to a separate account for non-repudiation. Spans carry prompts and tool data (CVE-2026-15737 was the SDK writing raw prompts to span attributes). Correlation IDs propagate from the harness to Gateway, Memory, Code Interpreter and Browser; a Runtime agent's trace is only as complete as its instrumentation.

controls.mechanism: StopRuntimeSession (terminates the session and its streaming responses at once), StopCodeInterpreterSession / StopBrowserSession; a resource-based policy Deny on the runtime or DeleteHarness / DeleteAgentRuntime; credential revocation by deleting credential providers, Revoke active sessions on the execution role, and a gateway rate limit of 0 for a caller

steps.title: Stop the running session
body: Call StopRuntimeSession with the runtime ARN (for a harness, GetHarness environment.agentCoreRuntimeEnvironment.agentRuntimeArn), qualifier and runtimeSessionId; retry on 409 RetryableConflictException.

steps.title: Refuse new sessions
body: Attach a resource-based policy denying InvokeAgentRuntime on the runtime and its endpoints, or delete the harness (pass deleteManagedMemory=false to keep memory for forensics).

steps.title: Revoke what it held
body: In the IAM console choose the execution role > Revoke sessions > Revoke active sessions, delete its OAuth2 and API key credential providers, and set a rate of 0 on the gateway for its caller (propagates within 30 seconds).

controls.note: Stop, block and revoke are each documented: StopRuntimeSession "instantly terminates" the session and its streaming, and Revoke active sessions denies the role's current credentials immediately. The harness pages do not name StopRuntimeSession; the harness API returns the underlying agentRuntimeArn it takes, so rehearse it on a harness. Deleting a credential provider has no stated propagation time, gateway rate limits fail open on transient errors, ENIs can persist 8 hours after deletion, and nothing cancels work the agent handed to other agents.

controls.mechanism: IAM identity policies and resource-based policies on runtimes (a harness runs on one) and their endpoints, gateways and memory, with explicit Deny winning; inbound customJWTAuthorizer (discoveryUrl, allowedClients) on a harness or gateway; SCP condition keys such as bedrock-agentcore:GatewayAuthorizerType that refuse unauthenticated gateways across member accounts

steps.title: Authorise callers per agent
body: Put a resource-based policy on each runtime and its endpoints that allows InvokeAgentRuntime only to the front end or calling agent that needs it, with a Deny ready for incidents.

steps.title: Authenticate end users at the harness
body: Set authorizerConfiguration customJWTAuthorizer with the firm's IdP discoveryUrl and the front end's allowedClients on CreateHarness / UpdateHarness, so callers present a user token.

steps.title: Refuse unauthenticated gateways
body: In an SCP deny CreateGateway and UpdateGateway unless bedrock-agentcore:GatewayAuthorizerType is CUSTOM_JWT or AWS_IAM.

controls.note: Native on the authorisation rule (as on toolVertexAgentEngine): AWS IAM, resource policies and SCPs administer who may invoke, change or delete each agent and gateway, per resource, with explicit denies that win over grants. Boundary: a caller allowed to call InvokeHarness can override model, additionalParams, skills, tools and allowedTools per call and no condition key restricts those fields, so the front end must strip them; JWT inbound auth proves the caller's identity but which records and tools that user may reach is the agent's and the gateway policy engine's to decide.

controls.mechanism: Harness limits maxIterations (default 75), timeoutSeconds (default 3600) and maxTokens (no default) per invocation; lifecycleConfiguration idleRuntimeSessionTimeout (default 900 s) and maxLifetime (default 28800 s on microVMs); gateway rate limits per caller, target or tool; Runtime service quotas

steps.title: Set the harness limits
body: Set limits maxIterations, timeoutSeconds and a maxTokens budget on CreateHarness / UpdateHarness, and strip per-call limit overrides in the front end.

steps.title: Shorten session lifetimes
body: Set lifecycleConfiguration idleRuntimeSessionTimeout and a maxLifetime no longer than the longest task the agent runs.

steps.title: Rate-limit tools at the gateway
body: Create gateway rate limits with dimension keys for the caller and the tool and a rate entry for each, so one agent cannot exhaust a downstream tool.

controls.note: Native on the resource-consumption rule (unlike toolVertexAgentEngine, which has no per-session budget): the harness stops an invocation at an iteration, wall-clock and token ceiling, the runtime reclaims idle and long-lived sessions, and the gateway bounds tool call rates. Boundaries: limits can be overridden per invocation by any caller allowed to call InvokeHarness; maxTokens is unset by default; a bring-your-own-code Runtime agent gets lifecycle limits and quotas but no iteration or token cap unless its code sets one; maxLifetime ends the instance, and the session can continue on a newly provisioned one; gateway rate limits fail open when the rate-limit service is unavailable and take up to 30 seconds to change. No dollar budget exists in the runtime; spend ceilings are AWS Budgets outside it.

settings.name: customJWTAuthorizer
settings.where: CreateHarness / UpdateHarness › authorizerConfiguration (discoveryUrl, allowedClients)
settings.recommended: The firm's IdP discovery URL and the front end's client ID
settings.why: Callers present a user token, so the end user's identity reaches downstream tools instead of one shared service role.

settings.name: bedrock-agentcore:GatewayAuthorizerType
settings.where: SCP or IAM policy › Deny CreateGateway / UpdateGateway unless the key is CUSTOM_JWT or AWS_IAM
settings.recommended: Deny NONE in every member account
settings.why: No one can create a gateway with No Authorization that forwards any caller, signed or not, to its tools.

settings.name: InvokeHarness overrides (model, additionalParams, skills, allowedTools)
settings.where: The application that calls InvokeHarness › forward only the user's message
settings.default: Callers can override model, additionalParams, skills, tools and allowedTools per call
settings.recommended: Stripped by the front end; actorId and runtimeSessionId derived server-side from the signed-in user
settings.why: A caller cannot widen the agent's tools, load its own skills or redirect inference with signed credentials; no condition key restricts these fields.

settings.name: allowedTools
settings.where: CreateHarness / UpdateHarness › allowedTools
settings.default: All tools, including the built-in shell and file_operations
settings.recommended: The named entries the agent needs (for example "@builtin/file_operations", "@crm/read_*"); shell only where the task requires it
settings.why: The model can select only the tools listed, so a prompt injection cannot reach a shell the use case never needed.

settings.name: bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand
settings.where: IAM identity policies and SCP
settings.recommended: Granted to no principal that fronts users; break-glass role only
settings.why: The API runs commands in the session without the model, outside allowedTools and the gateway policy engine.

settings.name: policyEngineConfiguration › mode
settings.where: CreateGateway / UpdateGateway › policyEngineConfiguration (arn, mode)
settings.recommended: ENFORCE, after a LOG_ONLY period
settings.why: Every tool call through the gateway is denied unless a Cedar policy permits it for that principal and those arguments.

settings.name: bedrock-agentcore:PolicyEngineMode
settings.where: SCP › Deny CreateGateway / UpdateGateway unless the key is ENFORCE (with bedrock-agentcore:PolicyEngineArn on the approved engine)
settings.recommended: ENFORCE required in every member account
settings.why: A builder cannot drop a gateway to LOG_ONLY or detach its engine; the enforcement-modes page says no key protects the mode, so test that the SCP refuses it.

settings.name: before_tool_call › failureMode
settings.where: CreateHarness / UpdateHarness › lifecycle hooks › before_tool_call (Lambda target)
settings.default: No hook; failureMode deny when a hook is set
settings.recommended: A Lambda hook that denies consequential tools outside policy or routes them for approval, failureMode deny
settings.why: Built-in, remote MCP and inline tools the gateway never sees get a check before they run, and callers cannot override hooks per invocation.

settings.name: Inline function tools
settings.where: CreateHarness › tools › inline_function, answered by the application with toolResult on the same runtimeSessionId
settings.recommended: Consequential actions (payments, sends, deletions) defined as inline functions a person approves before the toolResult is returned
settings.why: The loop pauses on the exact call and the model's input, and nothing happens until the application answers it.

settings.name: bedrock-agentcore:CredentialProviderType
settings.where: SCP › Deny CreateGatewayTarget / UpdateGatewayTarget unless the key is on the approved list
settings.recommended: OAUTH, API_KEY and GATEWAY_IAM_ROLE allowed; JWT_PASSTHROUGH denied for targets outside the firm
settings.why: A target outside the trust boundary never receives the caller's own token unmodified.

settings.name: bedrock-agentcore:McpTargetConfigurationType
settings.where: SCP › Deny CreateGatewayTarget / UpdateGatewayTarget for mcpServer outside the platform team's role
settings.recommended: mcpServer targets created only by the platform team's pipeline role
settings.why: A remote MCP server becomes an agent tool only after the team that keeps the registry has reviewed it.

settings.name: ListingMode
settings.where: CreateGatewayTarget › MCP server target › ListingMode
settings.recommended: DEFAULT, with SynchronizeGatewayTargets run only after the server's changed tools are reviewed
settings.why: The gateway serves the catalog it indexed, so a server that changes its tool definitions does not change what agents see until someone re-syncs; DYNAMIC forwards live.

settings.name: networkConfiguration › networkMode
settings.where: CreateHarness / CreateAgentRuntime › environment › agentCoreRuntimeEnvironment.networkConfiguration
settings.recommended: VPC, in private subnets whose egress passes the firm's firewall allowlist, with ECR, S3 and bedrock-runtime endpoints
settings.why: Commands and code in the session reach only the hosts the firm allows, not the open internet.

settings.name: bedrock-agentcore:subnets / bedrock-agentcore:securityGroups
settings.where: SCP › Deny CreateAgentRuntime, UpdateAgentRuntime, CreateCodeInterpreter, CreateBrowser when null or not approved
settings.recommended: Approved subnets and security groups required in every member account
settings.why: A builder cannot launch a runtime, code interpreter or browser on the public network; CreateHarness is not among the documented operations, so check harnesses separately.

settings.name: Network settings (Code Interpreter)
settings.where: AgentCore console › Built-in Tools › Code Interpreter › Create › Network settings
settings.recommended: Sandbox, or VPC where the code must reach private data
settings.why: Model-written code runs with limited external network access instead of on the public internet.

settings.name: memory (harness)
settings.where: CreateHarness / UpdateHarness › memory (disabled, managedMemoryConfiguration or agentCoreMemoryConfiguration)
settings.default: Managed memory provisioned when the field is omitted
settings.recommended: Set explicitly on every harness; managed memory with encryptionKeyArn and eventExpiryDuration 30 where the agent needs to remember, otherwise disabled
settings.why: Conversations are not kept by accident, and what is kept expires on the firm's retention and under its key.

settings.name: Fine-grained access control for Memory
settings.where: AgentCore Gateway › Memory connector target › Cedar policy on actorId
settings.recommended: Event and record access permitted only when the request's actorId equals the token's sub
settings.why: One user's agent cannot read or write another user's memories by passing their actorId.

settings.name: lifecycleConfiguration › idleRuntimeSessionTimeout / maxLifetime
settings.where: CreateAgentRuntime / UpdateAgentRuntime (harness lifecycle limits)
settings.recommended: 900 s idle; maxLifetime the longest task the agent runs, at most 4 hours
settings.why: A session, and the credentials in it, is reclaimed soon after its work ends instead of living for eight hours.

settings.name: maxIterations / timeoutSeconds / maxTokens
settings.where: CreateHarness / UpdateHarness › limits
settings.recommended: A maxTokens budget per invocation and timeoutSeconds 1800; strip per-call overrides in the front end
settings.why: A looping or hijacked agent stops at a cost and time ceiling instead of running for an hour.

settings.name: Rate limits (gateway)
settings.where: AgentCore Gateway › rate limits › dimension keys and rate entries
settings.recommended: A per-caller and per-tool rate on every production gateway
settings.why: One caller or runaway agent cannot exhaust a tool, and a rate of zero blocks a specific caller at once.

settings.name: Customer managed key (token vault)
settings.where: AgentCore Identity › token vault encryption
settings.recommended: A customer managed KMS key
settings.why: The firm controls, audits and can revoke the key that protects every stored OAuth token and API key.

settings.name: Private Key JWT
settings.where: CustomOauth2 credential provider › client authentication › asymmetric KMS signing key ARN
settings.recommended: Private Key JWT wherever the authorisation server supports it
settings.why: AgentCore signs client assertions in KMS, so there is no shared client secret to leak.

settings.name: GetResourceOauth2Token / GetResourceApiKey
settings.where: Execution-role IAM policy › exact credential-provider ARNs
settings.recommended: Each workload's role names only its own providers; gateway-injected credentials preferred to code retrieval
settings.why: A compromised agent can fetch only the credentials it was built to use, not every secret in the vault.

settings.name: Guardrails in policies (PromptAttack, ContentFilter, SensitiveInformation)
settings.where: Policy in AgentCore › forbid and suppressOutput policies with a when guardrails block; gateway role holds bedrock:InvokeGuardrailChecks
settings.recommended: PromptAttack over context.input and ContentFilter and SensitiveInformation over context.output on every production gateway, calibrated in LOG_ONLY
settings.why: What agents send to tools and what tools return are screened with a logged decision; only gateway traffic is covered.

settings.name: Enable Transaction Search
settings.where: CloudWatch console › Application Signals (APM) › Transaction search
settings.recommended: On in every account that runs agents, with log groups subscribed to the SIEM
settings.why: Harness and gateway spans (model calls, tool calls, shell commands) appear with no further setup.

settings.name: AWS_GENAI_CONTENT_EXTRACTION_OPT_OUT
settings.where: Runtime environment variable (ADOT instrumentation)
settings.recommended: Unset, so model payloads and tool data stay off spans
settings.why: Prompts and tool results are not copied into CloudWatch for everyone with log access; set it only on a log group the firm treats as client data.

settings.name: CloudTrail data events (AgentCore Gateway)
settings.where: CloudTrail › trail › advanced event selectors
settings.recommended: On, delivered to an S3 bucket in a separate logging account
settings.why: Each gateway request is recorded where the agent's own account cannot alter it.

settings.name: targetVersion (harness endpoint)
settings.where: CreateHarnessEndpoint / UpdateHarnessEndpoint › targetVersion
settings.recommended: Production callers use a named endpoint pinned to a tested version; rollback moves the pointer back
settings.why: An UpdateHarness reaches users only when someone moves the production endpoint, and moving it back is the rollback.

settings.name: Auto-detection (organization-scoped registry)
settings.where: AWS Agent Registry › delegated administrator › organization-scoped registry
settings.recommended: On, owned by a delegated administrator account
settings.why: Every AgentCore Runtime and Gateway in member accounts is catalogued automatically, so unregistered agents show up.

settings.name: Record approval
settings.where: AWS Agent Registry › create registry › Record approval
settings.recommended: Manual approval (auto-approval off), with the submit event routed to the review workflow
settings.why: A record is discoverable only after a curator approves it, and a detected change returns it to Draft.

settings.name: StopRuntimeSession
settings.where: bedrock-agentcore API › StopRuntimeSession (runtime ARN, qualifier, runtimeSessionId)
settings.recommended: The SOC playbook's first step, rehearsed on a harness
settings.why: Terminates the session and its streaming responses at once, instead of only refusing new ones.

settings.name: Resource-based policy (agent runtime and endpoint)
settings.where: PutResourcePolicy on the runtime and its endpoints › Deny bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntime
settings.recommended: A pre-written Deny statement ready to attach during an incident
settings.why: An explicit deny on the resource refuses every new invocation whatever the callers' own policies allow.

tools.name: Amazon Quick Automate (automation groups, UI agents, custom agents, human-in-the-loop tasks, scheduled and API triggers)

variants.name: UI agent (natural-language browser automation in a managed browser)
variants.note: Navigates websites, clicks, types and reads data in a browser Quick Automate manages, signing in with website credentials saved to the automation group; egress is the public internet unless a VPC connection is associated with the group.

variants.name: Custom agent (tool-calling step; Fast, Pro or Custom mode with a Bedrock model)
variants.note: Uses the automation group's integration actions, Code and Create user task as tools, and can query datasets and knowledge bases in spaces linked to the group; Custom mode bills inference to the account behind the Bedrock integration.

summary: AWS's agentic business-process automation inside Amazon Quick: builders describe a process or upload its documentation, a planning agent drafts the automation, and the visual designer combines actions (browser, Excel, PDF, files, code in a restricted Python environment, integrations), UI agents that operate web applications, custom agents that call integration actions as tools, and human-in-the-loop tasks. Committed versions are deployed with runtime configuration, HITL resolvers and the credentials and connections they run on, then started by schedule or by the StartAutomationJob API. Everything runs in AWS's managed environment; the managed browser reaches the public internet unless the automation group is associated with a VPC connection in the customer's account.

The administrator is the Amazon Quick administrator (Manage Quick) and the automation group Owner: identity through IAM Identity Center, custom permissions profiles (the Automate capability, Deny by Default for AI capabilities, per-connector Create and Update, Share and Use action), automation groups with Viewer, Contributor and Owner roles that hold the integrations, credentials, spaces and datasets an automation may use, IAM on StartAutomationJob, and CloudTrail and CloudWatch for monitoring. AWS states that automated workflows authenticate at service level, are not bounded by an individual user's connector permissions and run unattended, so the review belongs at approval time.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Amazon Quick accounts provisioned through the AWS Management Console (not Free or Plus accounts from aws.com/quick); custom permissions and MCP integrations need an Enterprise subscription; automations and flows consume agent hours.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Custom agents run in fully managed Fast or Pro modes, or Custom mode, which calls a model the customer selects in Amazon Bedrock through a Bedrock runtime integration billed to that account.

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: A vendor-hosted platform: process documents, run data, browser sessions and model calls are processed in AWS. The managed browser and integrations reach target systems from AWS, over the public internet by default or through an ENI in the customer's VPC when a VPC connection is associated with the automation group.

facts.label: Retention & training
facts.value: Quick does not use conversations, files or personal context to train or improve AI models. Customer managed keys cover only participating Automate stores (group and trigger content, validated inbound email); workflow, deployment and run data, execution artifacts and credentials use service-controlled keys.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: Amazon Quick User Guide › Using Amazon Quick automations › Using Amazon Quick Automate; Administering Amazon Quick

facts.label: Compliance scope
facts.value: Quick is a HIPAA Eligible Service (BAA required) and in scope for SOC 1, SOC 2 and SOC 3; confirm Quick Automate on AWS services in scope.

items.title: Where each control lives
body: Manage Quick: Permissions › Custom permissions (Automate, Restrict AI capabilities, connector Create and Update action, Share action, Use action), IP and VPC endpoint restrictions, VPC connections, AWS KMS keys. Automate: Projects › Manage groups (roles, Assets › Actions, Credentials, Spaces, Datasets, VPC connection), Deployments (Release details, Runtime configuration, Tasks, Access), Task center, Monitoring. AWS: IAM Identity Center, IAM policies on quicksight:StartAutomationJob, SCPs on quicksight:Subscribe, CloudTrail, CloudWatch metrics in the QuickSight namespace.

links.title: AI and agent security in Amazon Quick

items.title: Whose authority an automation runs on
body: Deployments select the website credentials and integration connections the automation uses; they are stored encrypted and never shown to authors, but every run uses them, whoever triggered it. AWS's own guidance is that an automated workflow can reach any resource its service-level credential permits, regardless of which user created it, so give each automation group connections to dedicated service accounts scoped at the target system.

riskNotes.note: Automations authenticate at service level and are not bounded by the triggering user's connector permissions; anyone who can start a deployed automation borrows the reach of its connections.

Scheduled and API-triggered automations run unattended; a human-in-the-loop task pauses only where the author placed one, and the custom agent's Create user task tool fires when the agent decides it is stuck.

UI agents read live web pages and custom agents read integration results and knowledge bases; AWS documents its content-safety screening and blocked words for chat agents and flows, not for automations.

Linking a space grants the automation group access to every knowledge base and file in it, and datasets with row-level or column-level security cannot be attached, so retrieval is not trimmed per user.
Any user with Contributor rights in an automation group can build, test and deploy; nothing outside the group's Owner approves a deployment.

controls.mechanism: Custom permissions profile capability Automate (users cannot create, update or run automations); automation group roles Viewer, Contributor and Owner; integrations, credentials, spaces and datasets made available per automation group by its Owner; HITL task resolvers set at deployment; IAM on quicksight:StartAutomationJob scoped to the automation ARN

steps.title: Restrict Automate to builders
body: In Manage Quick › Permissions › Custom permissions create a profile that restricts Automate, assign it at account level, and assign an allow profile to the builders' role.

steps.title: Keep Owner rights with a named few
body: In each automation group give Owner (integrations, credentials, user access) to the process owner and IT, Contributor to trained builders and Viewer to everyone else.

steps.title: Scope who can start an automation by API
body: Grant quicksight:StartAutomationJob only on the specific automation ARN to the calling system's role.

controls.note: Partial on the authorisation rule, the same word as toolAgentforce: the administrator decides who may build, deploy and start automations and which connections a group can use, but AWS documents that automated workflows authenticate at service level rather than as the invoking user, so there is no end-user mode to enforce (toolCopilotStudio is native because it can remove maker credentials). Custom permissions need an Enterprise subscription and an account administrator can change them; an SCP cannot reach them.

controls.mechanism: No agent identity: a deployed automation runs on the website credentials and integration connections selected at deployment, authenticated at service level

evidence.title: Deploying automations — Access (Credentials and Connections)
AI and agent security in Amazon Quick — Autonomy and identity

controls.note: None on the agent-identity rule: toolCopilotStudio mints an Entra Agent ID and toolAgentforce a dedicated agent user, while Quick Automate documents no principal of its own per automation; target systems see whatever account the connection or website credential belongs to. Stand-in: give each automation group's connections a dedicated service account at the target system, named for the automation, so its activity is attributable and revocable there.

controls.mechanism: Projects and automation groups listing every automation with its versions and deployments; Monitoring summary of automations and runs; the analytics dashboard's assets-created and users-by-asset-type views (quicksight:QuickSuiteUsageMetrics); CloudTrail records of automation API calls

steps.title: Read the automation population
body: Use the analytics dashboard (permission quicksight:QuickSuiteUsageMetrics) for automations created and the users building them, and the Monitoring summary for what is deployed and running.

steps.title: Organise by accountable group
body: Create one automation group per business unit or process family so every automation sits under an Owner who answers for it.

controls.note: Partial on the registry rule, the same word as toolAgentforce: the platform's own lists are authoritative for the account, but no owner, approval state or credential mode is documented per automation, the inventory is not exportable as a registry, and nothing denies an unregistered automation. The AWS Agent Registry integration surfaces MCP servers to Quick's chat, agents, apps, Flows and Research, not to Automate.

controls.mechanism: Committed versions (only committed versions deploy; restoring a version keeps the history); Test and production environments in Monitoring; runtime configuration overridden per environment at deployment; export and import between accounts

steps.title: Deploy only committed, tested versions
body: Test the automation end to end, commit the version, and select it in Release details; move a version between accounts with export and import rather than editing production.

steps.title: Promote across accounts
body: Export the tested automation from the development account and import it into production.

controls.note: Partial on the rollout rule: versioning, a test environment and rollback by redeploying an earlier committed version exist, but any Contributor can deploy, no approval step or evaluation gate stands before production, and there is no canary or percentage release.

controls.mechanism: Amazon Quick compliance validation (HIPAA eligible, SOC 1/2/3) and AWS Artifact reports feed the organisation's TPRM platform

evidence.title: Compliance validation for Amazon Quick
AWS services in scope by compliance program

controls.note: External: the assessment, evidence expiry and reassessment trigger live in the TPRM platform, as for every vendor. Re-assess when Custom mode brings a Bedrock model, and for each third-party system the UI agent signs in to.

controls.mechanism: Integrations usable only after an Owner adds them to the automation group (Assets › Add › Actions); custom permissions per connector (Create and Update action, Share action, Use action); custom agents limited to the actions the author selects from the group; Code in a restricted Python environment that is not the path to external systems

steps.title: Add only the integrations a group needs
body: In Projects › Manage groups › Assets › Add › Actions link only the integrations the group's processes use; automations in other groups cannot select them.

steps.title: Restrict connector use by profile
body: In the custom permissions profile, under Connectors, restrict Create and Update action to administrators and Use action for connectors builders should not reach.

controls.note: Partial on the tool-permission rule, the same word as toolAgentforce: tools are admitted per group and per connector, and AWS states MCP tools do not become available until reviewed and turned on, but there is no per-operation scope for an automation, no connector classification or combination rule, and an integration linked to a group is usable by every automation in it.

controls.mechanism: Website credentials and action credentials stored encrypted and supplied at runtime without being shown to authors; Default OAuth app (90-day refresh tokens) or Custom OAuth app for connectors; VPC connections with ENIs in the customer's VPC instead of a relay host; service-controlled keys for Automate credentials

steps.title: Keep secrets in the group's credential store
body: Save website and integration credentials to the automation group and select them under Access at deployment; never put them in runtime configuration or code.

steps.title: Use the firm's own OAuth app
body: Configure connectors used by automations with Custom OAuth app so the client and its revocation are the firm's.

steps.title: Reach private systems through the VPC
body: Create a Quick VPC connection and associate it with the automation group so traffic to private systems leaves through ENIs in the firm's VPC.

controls.note: Partial on the credential rule, the same word as toolCopilotStudio and toolAgentforce: secrets are held by the platform and kept from authors, and private systems are reached through the customer's VPC with no tunnel credential to custody. But website credentials are standing usernames and passwords, rotation is a manual edit, Automate credentials use service-controlled keys rather than the customer's, and no short-lived issuance is documented.

controls.mechanism: Built-in content-safety and prompt-attack screening and blocked words are documented for user requests in chat agents and flows, not for automations, UI agent page reads or custom agent tool results

evidence.title: AI guardrails in Amazon Quick (blocked words apply to chat agents and flows)
AI and agent security in Amazon Quick — Guardrail screening and blocked words

controls.note: None: no screening of web pages, files or tool results entering an automation's agents is documented, and no attach point for the firm's own classifier. Stand-in: keep UI agents on known sites, attach only reviewed knowledge, and place a human-in-the-loop task before any step that acts on what an agent read.

controls.mechanism: Spaces and datasets attached to an automation group only by their owner; knowledge bases with ACL support enforce document permissions on retrieval; datasets with row-level or column-level security cannot be attached; linking a space grants the group access to every knowledge base and file in it

steps.title: Link only purpose-built spaces
body: In Manage groups › Assets › Add › Spaces link a space built for the process, not a team's general space, since the group gains everything in it.

steps.title: Create knowledge bases with ACL support
body: Create knowledge bases with document-level ACLs; the choice is permanent and later retrieval returns nothing rather than unfiltered results when permissions cannot be evaluated.

controls.note: Partial on the retrieval rule, the same word as toolAgentforce: the owner decides what a group may ground on, but an automation reads as the group, not as the person whose case it is working, and the docs do not say which identity ACL enforcement evaluates for a run-as-service automation.

controls.mechanism: Monitoring dashboards (automation summary, runs with version, duration, cases and HITL task counts, and logs); CloudWatch metrics in the QuickSight namespace by AutomationId and AutomationGroupId; CloudTrail management and data events for Quick API calls; AGENT_HOURS_LOGS vended log entries for AUTOMATION

steps.title: Alarm on runs in CloudWatch
body: In CloudWatch › Metrics › QuickSight choose the AutomationId dimension and alarm on failed and StoppedAutomationRunCount runs.

steps.title: Record API activity off-account
body: Send Quick CloudTrail management events, and data events through advanced event selectors, to a separate logging account.

controls.note: Partial on the tracing rule: run status, metrics and API calls reach the firm's account, but the per-step log of what a UI agent saw and did lives in the Quick console, and no export of step-level traces (actions, tool inputs, pages) to a sink the firm runs is documented; CloudTrail records no action inputs or approval decisions.

controls.mechanism: Custom permissions capability Automate (users cannot run automations); IAM deny on quicksight:StartAutomationJob; schedule triggers with end dates; revoking the credentials and connections a deployment uses

steps.title: Refuse new API starts
body: Remove or deny quicksight:StartAutomationJob for the automation's ARN in the calling roles' policies.

steps.title: Withdraw the capability
body: Restrict Automate in the custom permissions profile for the affected users.

controls.note: Partial on the kill-switch rule: levers that block new starts exist, but no administrator stop for a production run in progress is documented (the Automation Job APIs are start and describe only; Stop is a test-run debug control), and whether restricting Automate halts scheduled triggers is not stated. Revoking the target-system credential is the reliable stop.

settings.name: IAM Identity Center
settings.where: Amazon Quick sign-up › identity method (cannot be changed after the account is created)
settings.recommended: IAM Identity Center with the firm's IdP as the identity source, MFA enforced at the IdP
settings.why: Every Quick user signs in through the corporate IdP and its MFA, and leaving the IdP ends their access.

settings.name: quicksight:DirectoryType / quicksight:Edition (quicksight:Subscribe)
settings.where: AWS Organizations SCP › Deny quicksight:Subscribe outside the approved edition and directory type
settings.recommended: Only the firm's approved edition with IAM Identity Center, in approved accounts
settings.why: No team can start a separate Quick subscription, with its own automations and users, outside the governed account.

settings.name: IP and VPC endpoint restrictions
settings.where: Manage QuickSight › Security and Permissions › IP and VPC endpoint restrictions › Rules
settings.recommended: On, allowing the firm's egress ranges and its VPC endpoints
settings.why: The Quick web console, where automations and their credentials are managed, is reachable only from the firm's network paths; the public API needs an IAM source-IP condition as well.

settings.name: Automate (custom permissions)
settings.where: Manage Quick › Permissions › Custom permissions › profile › Capabilities & features › AI capabilities › Automate
settings.recommended: Restricted at account level; allowed on the builders' role
settings.why: Only trained builders can create, update or run automations; restricting it is also how the capability is withdrawn from a user.

settings.name: Restrict AI capabilities (Deny by Default)
settings.where: Manage Quick › Permissions › Custom permissions › profile › Restrict capabilities
settings.default: Allow by default (new capabilities available on release)
settings.recommended: On in the account-level profile, with the capabilities the firm uses allowed explicitly
settings.why: A new AI capability AWS ships, including new agent abilities in Automate, is denied until someone has evaluated it.

settings.name: Viewer, Contributor, and Owner (automation group roles)
settings.where: Automate › Projects › Manage groups › (group) › users
settings.recommended: Owner held by the process owner and IT; Contributor for trained builders; Viewer for everyone else
settings.why: Only Owners decide which systems and credentials a group's automations can use, and only Contributors can deploy.

settings.name: Automation Group › Assets › Actions
settings.where: Automate › Projects › Manage groups › (group) › Assets › Add › Actions
settings.recommended: Only the integrations the group's processes use
settings.why: An automation can call only systems its group has been given, so a builder cannot wire in a connector nobody approved for the process.

settings.name: Create and Update action / Share action / Use action (connector features)
settings.where: Manage Quick › Permissions › Custom permissions › profile › Connectors
settings.recommended: Create and Update action restricted to administrators; Use action restricted for connectors builders should not reach
settings.why: New integrations, MCP servers included, are created by the people who review them, not by any builder.

settings.name: Access (Credentials and Connections)
settings.where: Automate › (automation) › Deploy › Additional settings › Access
settings.recommended: Connections and website credentials of a dedicated service account per automation group, never a builder's own
settings.why: Every run uses these whoever triggers it, so they must be scoped and attributable at the target system.

settings.name: Custom OAuth app
settings.where: Connections › Integrations › (connector) › OAuth Configuration
settings.default: Default OAuth app where the connector supports it
settings.recommended: Custom OAuth app registered by the firm for connectors automations use
settings.why: The OAuth client, its scopes and its revocation belong to the firm, not to the Quick-managed application.

settings.name: VPC connection (automation group)
settings.where: Quick admin tools › create VPC connection, then the automation group page › VPC connection section
settings.recommended: Associated with every group that reaches private systems, with egress through the firm's firewall
settings.why: Browser and integration traffic leaves through ENIs in the firm's VPC, so private systems stay private and egress is the firm's to filter.

settings.name: Automation group › Assets › Spaces / Datasets
settings.where: Automate › Projects › Manage groups › (group) › Assets › Add › Spaces or Datasets
settings.recommended: Only spaces and datasets built for the process; knowledge bases in them created with ACL support
settings.why: Linking a space gives the group every knowledge base and file in it, so the scope of what agents can read is decided here.

settings.name: Tasks (for HITL assignments)
settings.where: Automate › (automation) › Deploy › Additional settings › Tasks
settings.recommended: A named resolver group for every human-in-the-loop task
settings.why: Approvals and exceptions go to people accountable for the process, not to whoever built it.

settings.name: Release details (committed version)
settings.where: Automate › (automation) › Deploy › Release details
settings.recommended: Only versions tested end to end and committed; the previous version kept for redeployment
settings.why: Production runs an immutable version someone tested, and rolling back is redeploying the one before.

settings.name: Export and import automations
settings.where: Automate › (automation) › Export, then Import in the target account
settings.recommended: Builders work in a development account; production receives imports only
settings.why: Nobody edits a production automation in place, so what runs there is what was tested.

settings.name: quicksight:StartAutomationJob
settings.where: IAM policy of the calling role › Resource arn:aws:quicksight:<region>:<account>:automation-group/<group>/automation/<automation>
settings.recommended: Granted per automation ARN to the one system that triggers it; a Deny ready for incidents
settings.why: Only the intended caller can start the automation, and a single policy change refuses new starts.

settings.name: CloudTrail data events (Amazon Quick)
settings.where: CloudTrail › trail › advanced event selectors for Quick resource types, plus management events
settings.recommended: On, delivered to a separate logging account
settings.why: Automation and connector API activity, and changes to custom permissions, are recorded where the Quick account cannot alter them.

settings.name: CloudWatch metrics (QuickSight namespace, AutomationId)
settings.where: CloudWatch › Metrics › QuickSight › AutomationId or AutomationGroupId
settings.recommended: Alarms on failed and StoppedAutomationRunCount runs per production automation
settings.why: An automation that starts failing or being stopped is noticed by operations, not discovered in the console later.

settings.name: AGENT_HOURS_LOGS (vended log)
settings.where: Amazon Quick vended logs › delivery to CloudWatch Logs, Amazon S3 or Firehose
settings.recommended: Delivered to the firm's log store
settings.why: Each automation's consumption is recorded against its resource ARN, a cheap signal of an automation that has started running far more than expected.

settings.name: quicksight:QuickSuiteUsageMetrics (analytics dashboard)
settings.where: IAM permission for the analytics dashboard › Assets created, users by asset type
settings.recommended: Granted to the platform team, who review new automations and their builders monthly
settings.why: New automations and who is building them are visible to the people who keep the inventory; the dashboard can expose query text, so access stays narrow.
