items.title: Identity and device management
body: SAML 2.0 SSO (password auth can be blocked), SCIM provisioning with group sync, and three dashboard roles. MDM policies for macOS and Windows cover Allowed Team IDs (blocks personal-account login on corporate devices), an Allowed Extensions allowlist (Cursor 2.1+) and Workspace Trust enforcement.

links.title: Cursor enterprise identity and access management

items.title: Privacy, model and MCP control
body: Privacy Mode is default-on for Enterprise teams and admins can enforce it so members cannot disable it; model access is set per team and per organisation group, and BYOK API keys can be blocked. MCP servers are governed by a dashboard allowlist with wildcard matching, per-server tool restrictions and per-server network policies; ~/.cursor/permissions.json, distributable via MDM, carries only the terminal and MCP auto-run allowlists and Auto-review hints — admin settings take precedence over the local file and editor settings.

items.title: Agent run-mode policies and audit
body: Enterprise Run Mode policies (Cursor 3.6+) set the terminal posture — Auto-review, Allowlist, or Run Everything — and the docs are candid that the allowlist is best-effort, not a security boundary; hooks can scan prompts, block commands and redact secrets, and .cursorignore is likewise documented as not a boundary. Enterprise audit logs record admin and account events (explicitly not agent responses or generated code), stream to SIEM, and the Admin API exposes members, usage, spend, repo blocklists and model access.

riskNotes.note: Cursor's own mitigation is an LLM classifier (Auto-review) that the docs say can allow a call you would have blocked; the deterministic layer is sandbox.json, hooks and the CLI's permissions.deny (the IDE's permissions.json holds allowlists and classifier hints, not denies). Rules files, AGENTS.md and .cursor/* are instruction surfaces an attacker can reach through a repository (Rules File Backdoor), which is what .cursor Directory Protection and enforced Team Rules are for.

MCPoison (CVE-2025-54136) showed trust bound to an MCP server's name rather than its command; since 1.3 any change to an MCP configuration re-prompts. The Enterprise MCP allowlist matches command and URL patterns, so a pinned pattern is the only provenance check the vendor ships — the org must curate the Team Marketplace itself.

Run Everything mode removes every gate; the Enterprise Run Mode policy is the switch that takes it away from members. Five sandbox-escape advisories in 2026 mean the sandbox is a blast-radius reducer, not a guarantee; keep the fleet on 3.1.2 or later.

.cursorignore is a convenience filter that terminal and MCP tools bypass; beforeReadFile and beforeSubmitPrompt hooks (failClosed, which only an MDM-placed or project hooks.json can set), Read Controls in Workspace mode and the sandbox's protected paths are the controls that hold. ZDR is lost the moment a member uses a personal API key, which Model Access Control can block.

The extension marketplace is a second supply chain inside the IDE: AllowedExtensions, Install Cooldown and ExtensionGalleryServiceUrl decide what can be installed; the .claude/settings.local.json hook escape (CVE-2026-48124) shows sibling-tool config files in a workspace are also executable surface.

controls.mechanism: SSO required for every user on a verified domain once the SAML connection is active (Team Settings → Single Sign-On (SSO); the Organization's Settings on Enterprise); MDM policy AllowedTeamId pins the client to the org's teams; the second factor is the IdP's policy

steps.title: Federate sign-in and verify the domain
body: In Team Settings → Single Sign-On (SSO) (Enterprise org admins use the Organization's Settings) complete SSO-Provider Connection Settings and Domain Verification Settings; once both are active every user on that domain must sign in with SSO, and there is no separate enforcement toggle.

steps.title: Pin managed devices to your teams
body: Set the MDM policy AllowedTeamId (it overrides the cursorAuth.allowedTeamId setting) to the comma-separated list of your team IDs so a sign-in to any other team, including a personal account, is logged out immediately.

steps.title: Close the non-domain door
body: On teams not using SCIM turn on Restrict invites to verified domains in team settings, and revoke invite links, which have a long expiry and admit anyone who holds them.

steps.title: Stop personal API keys skipping the IdP
body: Turn off Allow Personal API Key Creation (Personal API Keys, Team tab under API keys at grok.com/dashboard) so members cannot create or rotate personal Cursor API keys, then revoke the existing ones from Members › View API keys (Enterprise); revoked keys fail immediately.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: Cursor enforces SSO-only sign-in for users on a verified domain (Teams and Enterprise) and AllowedTeamId pins the device client to the org's teams (Enterprise MDM: macOS profile, Windows ADMX, Linux ~/.cursor/policy.json in the user's home directory), so the IdP's MFA policy governs every interactive login. MFA is configured in the IdP, not in Cursor, whose own account layer has no require-second-factor switch. Paths that skip the IdP's MFA: user API keys from Dashboard → API Keys used by the CLI as CURSOR_API_KEY or --api-key (no expiry documented; turning off Allow Personal API Key Creation stops new ones, but existing keys keep working until an admin revokes them from Members › View API keys on Enterprise), Enterprise service-account keys (rotate or archive to revoke), Admin API keys, the CLI's locally stored browser-login credential (lifetime not documented), and invite-link joins with non-domain emails. AllowedTeamId does not reach unmanaged devices.

original.mechanism: Enterprise dashboard SSO (SAML 2.0) and SCIM 2.0; MDM policy AllowedTeamId / cursorAuth.allowedTeamId

steps.title: Turn on SSO and SCIM
body: Configure SAML 2.0 SSO (Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, OneLogin) in the team dashboard and enable SCIM 2.0 provisioning with group sync; both require Enterprise and SCIM requires SSO.

steps.title: Pin corporate devices to your team
body: Set the MDM policy AllowedTeamId to the comma-separated list of authorised team IDs so personal accounts cannot sign in on managed devices; deploy via the shipped .mobileconfig (bundle com.todesktop.230313mzl4w4u92), the ADMX templates or ~/.cursor/policy.json on Linux.

controls.mechanism: Admin-distributed pre-tool hooks: Enterprise Team hooks (dashboard, cloud-synced) or an MDM-placed system hooks.json, with preToolUse / beforeShellExecution / beforeMCPExecution returning permission deny (failClosed only in the MDM-placed file; dashboard hooks take no per-hook options); the Enterprise Run Mode policy removes Run Everything

steps.title: Distribute a deny-capable pre-tool hook
body: In the dashboard's Team hooks (team-content?section=hooks; Enterprise cloud distribution, synced to clients every thirty minutes) add preToolUse, beforeShellExecution and beforeMCPExecution hooks that call your policy service and return permission deny (or exit code 2), and turn on Block until hooks are ready. Dashboard hooks take no per-hook options such as failClosed or matcher, so a crash or timeout there lets the call through.

steps.title: Or place it system-wide by MDM
body: Write hooks.json to /Library/Application Support/Cursor/hooks.json, /etc/cursor/hooks.json or C:\ProgramData\Cursor\hooks.json with failClosed true on each security-critical hook, the only distributed copy that can fail closed; hooks from every source run and any deny wins over ask and allow regardless of source.

steps.title: Remove Run Everything
body: In the web dashboard's team controls limit the modes available to members to Auto-review and Allowlist; team settings take precedence over individual and project configuration.

controls.note: Native on the rule applied to every vendor: an admin-locked pre-tool hook that can deny, evaluated by the harness before shell, file (Read, Write, Delete, Grep), MCP and Task calls, outside the model, in both the IDE and the CLI. The decision logic is the organisation's own hook: Cursor's declarative lists are allowlists that skip approval, and the Auto-review classifier (Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite, with Claude 4.5 Haiku as the fallback) is documented as "not a security boundary", so neither is the policy decision point. Gaps: hooks fail open unless failClosed is set, which only an MDM-placed (or project) hooks.json can do, since dashboard hooks take no per-hook options; preToolUse accepts but does not enforce ask (escalate from beforeShellExecution / beforeMCPExecution instead); Tab completions use separate hooks; cloud distribution is Enterprise-only (Teams can place hooks by MDM only); the decision is exported only as cursor.hook.execution_complete in Enterprise OpenTelemetry Export unless the hook logs it itself; and a user-writable C:\ProgramData\Cursor\hooks.json on Windows (reported January 2026, unresolved) lets a local user replace the system hook.

original.mechanism: Enterprise Run Mode policy (Auto-review / Allowlist / Run Everything); ~/.cursor/permissions.json via MDM; hooks.json beforeShellExecution / beforeMCPExecution with permission deny; CLI permissions.deny

steps.title: Set the Run Mode policy
body: In the Enterprise team dashboard set the run mode to Auto-review (default) or Allowlist and remove Run Everything; team settings take precedence over individual and project configuration.

steps.title: Distribute deterministic deny rules
body: Push ~/.cursor/permissions.json through MDM for terminal-command and MCP allow/deny lists; admin dashboard settings outrank the file, which outranks editor settings.

steps.title: Block at the hook boundary
body: Ship an enterprise hooks.json (/Library/Application Support/Cursor/hooks.json, /etc/cursor/hooks.json, C:\ProgramData\Cursor\hooks.json) with beforeShellExecution and beforeMCPExecution hooks returning permission deny; precedence is Enterprise → Team → Project → User and exit code 2 blocks.

steps.title: Lock the CLI the same way
body: In ~/.cursor/cli-config.json set permissions.allow / permissions.deny with Shell(), Read(), Write(), WebFetch() and Mcp(server:tool) rules; deny wins over allow.

original.note: The docs state the Auto-review classifier can allow a call you would have blocked; only the deny rules, hooks and sandbox are deterministic.

controls.mechanism: Vendor evidence on cursor.com/security and the Trust Center (trust.cursor.com), consumed by the organisation's own TPRM platform

evidence.title: Cursor security page (AIUC-1, ISO 27001 and 42001, SOC 2 Type II, annual pen test)
Cursor Trust Center (reports on request, subprocessors; client-rendered)

controls.note: External by the rule applied to every vendor: Cursor publishes evidence but the assessment, its cadence and the reassessment trigger belong to the organisation's TPRM platform. The security page states AIUC-1, ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and ISO/IEC 42001:2023 certification, a SOC 2 Type II attestation and at-least-annual third-party penetration testing, with certificates and reports available on request at trust.cursor.com; the portal renders client-side, so its document list was not read by automated fetch. Subscribe there for subprocessor and posture-change notices, and re-run the assessment for the 2026-08-15 change of ownership to SpaceX and the sign-in move to accounts.spacex.ai / accounts.x.ai from 2026-09-30.

original.mechanism: Vendor evidence from cursor.com/security and trust.cursor.com consumed by the organisation's own TPRM platform

steps.title: Collect the vendor evidence
body: Pull SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001/42001, AIUC-1, the pen-test report and the sub-processor list from the trust portal; note the 2026-08-15 change of ownership to SpaceX and re-run the assessment.

original.note: Cursor publishes evidence; the assessment cadence and reassessment trigger on ownership change must come from your TPRM tooling.

controls.mechanism: Hooks as the inline attach point for the organisation's DLP: beforeSubmitPrompt and beforeReadFile (block), preToolUse updated_input and postToolUse updated_mcp_tool_output (rewrite); .cursorignore and the Enterprise dashboard's Cursor Ignore Configuration as data minimisation only

steps.title: Inspect prompts and file reads inline
body: Distribute beforeSubmitPrompt (return continue false) and beforeReadFile (receives the file content; return permission deny) hooks that send the text to your DLP API, with failClosed true on beforeReadFile in the MDM-placed hooks.json (dashboard hooks cannot fail closed).

steps.title: Mask what tools send and return
body: Use preToolUse updated_input to strip secrets from outgoing tool arguments and postToolUse updated_mcp_tool_output to replace an MCP result with a redacted copy before the model sees it.

steps.title: Keep secret paths out of context
body: Add .cursorignore patterns (or global ignore patterns in user settings) for .env, key and credential files; Agent, Tab, Inline Edit and @-mentions honour them, terminal and MCP tools do not.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: the hooks are an inline attach point that can block or rewrite, and the detection is the organisation's DLP; Cursor itself detects nothing. Covered once a hook is attached: user prompts (block only), agent file reads (block only), Tab file reads (beforeTabFileRead), outgoing tool arguments and MCP results (rewrite). Not covered: shell command output and web fetch or browser content enter context with no hook that can change them. The file exclusions are data minimisation, which the docs call "not a security boundary". Network or endpoint DLP on *.cursor.sh is the documented external alternative, and SSL inspection of those domains is a documented cause of agent failures. Cloud distribution of hooks is Enterprise; Teams places them by MDM.

original.mechanism: hooks.json beforeSubmitPrompt and beforeReadFile (Enterprise-managed, failClosed); .cursorignore as a convenience filter only

steps.title: Scan prompts and reads with hooks
body: Add beforeSubmitPrompt and beforeReadFile hooks in the enterprise or team hooks.json to scan for sensitive data and block or redact before content reaches the model; set failClosed on critical hooks.

steps.title: Do not rely on .cursorignore
body: Use .cursorignore for secrets and regulated trees, knowing terminal and MCP tools cannot be blocked by it and the docs call it a convenience feature, not a security boundary.

original.note: No vendor-side content inspection or blocking policy exists; the docs point to endpoint DLP, hooks and third-party vendor APIs for centralised policy.

controls.mechanism: Enterprise MCP Configuration (server command/URL allowlist with a per-server Tools list); admin Run Mode policy and allowlists; hooks for argument and path denies; CLI permissions.allow / deny in the user-editable ~/.cursor/cli-config.json

steps.title: Scope MCP servers and their tools
body: In Team Settings > MCP Configuration (Enterprise) add command entries for stdio servers, URL entries for remote servers and a tool allowlist per server, and do not let users configure their own MCP servers outside the admin-defined patterns.

steps.title: Own the auto-run lists
body: Set the Run Mode policy and command and MCP allowlists in the dashboard; admin-controlled lists replace permissions.json and editor entries and make the in-app allowlist editor read-only.

steps.title: Deny by argument and path with hooks
body: For shell arguments and file paths distribute preToolUse, beforeShellExecution and beforeReadFile hooks that deny on your patterns (git push, credential paths), since the IDE has no declarative deny list.

steps.title: Scope the CLI
body: In ~/.cursor/cli-config.json set permissions.allow and permissions.deny with Shell(), Read(), Write(), WebFetch() and Mcp(server:tool) tokens; deny wins over allow.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: admin-lockable scoping exists for MCP servers and tools (Enterprise MCP Configuration; the MCP page describes the Tools list as what may run automatically, the Model and Integration page as what can run) and for which calls skip approval, but the IDE has no declarative per-tool deny with argument or path scoping. That exists only in the CLI's cli-config.json, a user-editable file with no documented admin lock, or in the organisation's own hooks. Bypass modes: Run Everything is removable by the Enterprise Run Mode policy; the CLI's --force / --yolo and approvalMode unrestricted are not documented as bound by that policy (Enterprise can restrict which users may use the CLI). Enforcement sits in the harness, outside the model.

original.mechanism: Enterprise MCP Configuration (server:tool allowlist patterns, per-server tool lists); ~/.cursor/permissions.json via MDM; CLI Mcp(server:tool) rules

steps.title: Allowlist MCP servers and tools
body: In the dashboard's MCP Configuration add command patterns for stdio servers and URL patterns for remote servers, then restrict each server's Tools field; patterns are server:tool, server:*, *:tool or *:*.

steps.title: Scope CLI tools per operation type
body: Use Shell(commandBase), Read(pathOrGlob), Write(pathOrGlob), WebFetch(domain) and Mcp(server:tool) entries in permissions.allow / permissions.deny; project-level .cursor/cli.json carries permissions only.

original.note: server:tool patterns hide MCP tools; permissions.json and CLI rules limit shell and file arguments; Run Mode pre-approves. Run Everything bypasses all of it unless the Enterprise policy removes that mode.

controls.mechanism: OS sandbox for agent terminal commands (macOS Seatbelt; Linux Landlock + seccomp) shaped by sandbox.json with a team-admin layer local files cannot weaken; Agent Sandbox Mode enforceable org-wide on Enterprise; per-server sandbox for stdio MCP servers. Credential paths: Enterprise Read Controls (team read policy, Workspace mode) for the agent's reads and sandboxed commands, read-denies on the agent's own file tools (beforeReadFile hooks, .cursorignore / Enterprise Cursor Ignore Configuration, CLI Read() denies) and the sandbox's filesystem limits on sandboxed commands; nothing holds credentials outside the agent or scopes them per destination

steps.title: Enforce sandboxing org-wide
body: In the Enterprise dashboard's Run Mode controls keep members on Auto-review or Allowlist with sandboxing enabled and remove Run Everything; team settings take precedence over individual and project configuration.

steps.title: Set the team-admin sandbox policy
body: Define the team sandbox rules (networkPolicy, paths, disableTmpWrite); they merge above ~/.cursor/sandbox.json and <workspace>/.cursor/sandbox.json and neither file can weaken them.

steps.title: Sandbox local MCP servers
body: In MCP Configuration give each stdio server the Allowlist or Deny all network mode, never No sandbox.

steps.title: Meet the Linux requirements
body: Ship kernel 6.2+ with Landlock v3 and unprivileged user namespaces, and install the cursor-sandbox-apparmor package for the CLI and remote environments; otherwise Cursor falls back to approval prompts.

steps.title: Narrow reads to the workspace
body: In Team Settings › Security & automation turn on Read Controls and pick Workspace (Enterprise, Cursor 3.23+); reads outside the workspace ask first, searches stay inside it, and sandboxed commands read only the workspace, the Read Allowlist and system paths, with only ~/.ssh/known_hosts from ~/.ssh.

steps.title: Deny the agent's file tools on credential paths
body: Place a beforeReadFile hook with failClosed true in the MDM-distributed hooks.json that denies reads of cloud CLI config, kubeconfig, SSH keys, .env and key files by file_path.

steps.title: Hide them from context
body: List the same patterns in .cursorignore or the global ignore list in user settings; Agent, Tab, Inline Edit and @-mentions honour them, terminal and MCP tools do not.

steps.title: Keep the sandbox's read set narrow
body: Do not add credential directories to additionalReadonlyPaths, additionalReadwritePaths or the Read Allowlist in any sandbox policy, knowing ~/.ssh and SSL certificate paths stay readable under the default System read boundary.

steps.title: Deny them in the CLI
body: Add Read() denies such as Read(.env*) and absolute credential paths to permissions.deny in ~/.cursor/cli-config.json.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: the sandbox is OS-enforced and Enterprise can enforce it org-wide, but it does not fail closed. Commands that need full system access run outside it after an approval, and in Auto-review the classifier rather than a person can clear them; no documented admin setting forbids that escalation, and Linux without Landlock v3 falls back to approval prompts. The Run Modes page documents macOS and Linux only (Cursor's engineering blog says Windows runs the Linux sandbox inside WSL2). Inside: sandboxed terminal commands, workspace write, protected paths (.git/hooks, .git/config, .cursor/*.json, .claude/*.json, .vscode, .cursorignore) write-denied, ~/.ssh readable unless Read Controls is Workspace. Outside: MCP tool calls (the deployment page says they do not run in the local sandbox; a stdio server process gets only its per-server mode, and No sandbox removes it), the extension host, the Cursor process itself, and CLI runs with --sandbox disabled or agent sandbox disable. Six sandbox-escape advisories Feb–Jul 2026 were fixed by 3.1.2; keep the fleet current. Credential paths: the read-denies bind Cursor's own Read tool, not the shell (the docs say terminal and MCP tools cannot honour .cursorignore), and nothing holds credentials outside the agent or injects them only for named destinations. Under the default System read boundary the docs do not list which home-directory paths sandboxed commands can read, and ~/.ssh is readable; Enterprise Read Controls set to Workspace (Cursor 3.23+) limits sandboxed commands to the workspace, the Read Allowlist and system paths (only ~/.ssh/known_hosts from ~/.ssh) and makes the agent ask before reading outside it, but a member's approval or the Read Allowlist opens a path, so it narrows the boundary without making it required. What the agent still inherits: ~/.ssh inside the sandbox under System, and for commands run outside it, MCP servers and the extension host the developer's ssh-agent, git credential helper, cloud CLI configuration and browser profiles; the docs say "there is no security boundary between agents and your user account". Remote Control keeps credentials on the machine by design. The stronger fix is a named product class: a dev container or VM (Cursor's own advice is Cloud Agents in a separate VM) or a secretless broker such as 1Password Environments wired through a hook.

original.mechanism: sandbox.json (type workspace_readwrite / workspace_readonly / insecure_none, additional paths, network policy); Run Mode sandboxing; team-admin policy layer cannot be weakened; CLI --sandbox and sandbox.mode

steps.title: Enable sandboxing in the Run Mode policy
body: Keep Auto-review or Allowlist with sandboxing enabled so non-allowlisted shell commands run in the sandbox that blocks protected files, writes outside approved paths and arbitrary network destinations.

steps.title: Set the sandbox policy
body: Configure ~/.cursor/sandbox.json (and per-repo .cursor/sandbox.json) with type, additionalReadwritePaths, additionalReadonlyPaths, disableTmpWrite and a network policy; merge order is per-user < per-repo < team-admin < hard-coded rules and the upper layers cannot be weakened.

steps.title: Sandbox the CLI
body: Set sandbox.mode and sandbox.networkAccess in ~/.cursor/cli-config.json, or pass --sandbox enabled|disabled in headless runs.

original.note: Six sandbox-escape advisories were published Feb–Jul 2026 (git hooks, .claude hooks, working directory, symlinks, privileged Docker containers, tampered venvs); all fixed by 3.1.2. Treat the sandbox as blast-radius reduction. Inside the boundary: sandboxed commands. Outside: MCP servers set to No sandbox, Browser Controls and the IDE process itself; Run Everything bypasses it entirely unless the team policy removes that mode.

original.mechanism: Not offered for the local agent — it runs with the developer's own identity and credentials
original.note: The local agent and CLI act as the signed-in user with whatever the shell can reach; Remote Control deliberately keeps credentials on the machine. Delegation controls (OIDC federation, Runtime Secrets, service accounts) exist only on Cloud Agents (toolCursorCloudAgents). Put scoped credentials in the developer's environment and use Runtime Secrets where the work can move to a Cloud Agent.

evidence.title: Vendor docs index, reviewed; no setting for this control (2026-09-10)

controls.mechanism: Enterprise .cursor Directory Protection; enforced Team Rules; sandbox write-protection of .cursor/*.json and .claude/*.json; MDM WorkspaceTrustEnabled (project hooks run only in trusted workspaces)

steps.title: Protect the .cursor directory
body: Turn on .cursor Directory Protection in the team dashboard (Enterprise) so agents need approval to modify or delete .cursor/ rules and settings files.

steps.title: Enforce Team Rules
body: Create Team Rules in the dashboard (Teams and Enterprise) and tick Enforce this rule so members cannot disable them; Team Rules take precedence over project and user rules.

steps.title: Require workspace trust
body: Set the MDM policy WorkspaceTrustEnabled to true so users are prompted to trust each new workspace and untrusted workspaces run in restricted mode.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: an admin can lock instruction sources (enforced Team Rules, .cursor Directory Protection, workspace trust) but nothing validates their contents. The local agent has no documented memory store today; its persistent state is instruction files: .cursor/rules, AGENTS.md at the root and in subdirectories, skills, commands, hooks and mcp.json. Gaps: the sandbox leaves .cursor/rules, commands, skills and agents writable, and AGENTS.md sits outside .cursor, where the agent edits workspace files without approval; Directory Protection gates agent edits with an approval, not a validator; rule text is guidance the model weighs (Rules File Backdoor), and the docs say AI guidance should not be your only security control. Nothing expires, validates or rolls back instruction changes beyond git. The Cloud Agent automations' MEMORIES.md belongs to toolCursorCloudAgents.

original.mechanism: Enterprise .cursor Directory Protection; enforced Team Rules; Workspace Trust via MDM

steps.title: Protect the .cursor directory
body: Turn on .cursor Directory Protection in the team dashboard so agents cannot modify project settings (rules, MCP config, hooks) that persist across sessions.

steps.title: Restrict untrusted folders
body: Set the MDM policy WorkspaceTrustEnabled so untrusted folders open in restricted mode with AI features limited.

original.note: Persistent state is project configuration rather than a memory store; there is no expiry, validation or rollback of agent memory.

original.mechanism: Team Rules from the dashboard with Enforce; precedence Team → Project → User; .cursor Directory Protection

steps.title: Enforce team rules
body: Create Team Rules in the dashboard and mark them enforced so members cannot disable them; Team Rules take precedence over project and user rules.

steps.title: Stop agents rewriting instructions
body: Turn on .cursor Directory Protection so the agent cannot modify .cursor/rules, mcp.json or hooks in the project.

original.note: Rules files inside repositories remain untrusted input (Rules File Backdoor); the docs say AI guidance should not be your only security control. Enforce protects the instruction configuration — users cannot disable Team Rules — but rule text is guidance the model weighs, not a runtime action boundary; pair it with hooks and Run Mode policy for anything that must be deterministic.

controls.mechanism: Attach points only: beforeReadFile (deny a file on its content), postToolUse updated_mcp_tool_output (replace an MCP result) and beforeSubmitPrompt (block a prompt) hooks calling the organisation's classifier; Cursor ships no injection classifier on inputs

steps.title: Screen MCP results before the model sees them
body: Distribute a postToolUse hook matched to MCP tools that sends tool_output to your injection classifier and returns updated_mcp_tool_output with flagged content removed, logging the event from the hook.

steps.title: Screen repository files and prompts
body: Add a beforeReadFile hook (failClosed, in the MDM-placed hooks.json) that classifies the file content and returns permission deny for flagged files, and a beforeSubmitPrompt hook that returns continue false on a direct injection.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: post-tool and pre-read hooks are an attach point that can block or replace content before it enters context; the classifier is the organisation's. Not covered: shell command output (afterShellExecution only observes), web fetch and search results, browser page content, and rules or AGENTS.md loaded into context. The Auto-review classifier judges proposed tool calls, not their inputs, and is credited under action policy; Browser Controls (Enterprise origin allowlist for the browser tool) and Workspace Trust are admission, not screening. The alternative that covers the brokered path is an AI gateway or MCP gateway classifier.

original.mechanism: Auto-review LLM classifier on non-allowlisted commands; beforeSubmitPrompt hooks; Browser Controls domain allowlist

steps.title: Keep Auto-review on
body: Auto-review runs allowlisted calls immediately, sandboxes what it can and routes the rest through an LLM classifier; enforce it from the Enterprise Run Mode policy.

steps.title: Limit what the browser tool can read
body: Define the Enterprise Browser Controls allowlist of approved domains so agents visiting other origins are blocked.

original.note: There is no classifier on retrieved content or MCP tool output; the vendor's own language is that the classifier can make mistakes.

controls.mechanism: Team Settings → Models BYOK restriction (Enterprise); Allow Personal API Key Creation off to stop new user API keys; Enterprise service accounts with key rotation and archive; Enterprise Read Controls keeping home-directory credential files out of sandboxed reads; .env* on the default ignore list

steps.title: Block personal provider keys
body: In Team Settings → Models (Enterprise) restrict personal API keys (BYOK) so all usage goes through Cursor's included models and no member-held provider key is used.

steps.title: Use service accounts for automation
body: Create service accounts under Dashboard → Settings → API Keys → Service Accounts (Enterprise), rotate their keys on a schedule and archive an account to revoke all its keys, instead of personal user API keys in CI.

steps.title: Stop new personal Cursor API keys
body: Turn off Allow Personal API Key Creation (Personal API Keys, Team tab under API keys at grok.com/dashboard) and revoke existing keys from Members › View API keys (Enterprise).

steps.title: Watch and revoke user keys
body: Alert on the audit log's user_api_key and team_api_key events (create, revoke; Enterprise) and revoke keys nobody can account for.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: rotation exists only for service-account keys, and it is manual. User API keys (Dashboard → API Keys, used as CURSOR_API_KEY or --api-key) are static and have no documented expiry; an admin can stop new ones with Allow Personal API Key Creation, but existing keys keep working until revoked (Enterprise admins revoke them from Members › View API keys); the CLI's browser-login credential is "securely stored locally" with no storage mechanism or lifetime documented; MCP server secrets sit as env values in mcp.json. The API overview says keys "are unaffected by the original creator's account status", so offboarding must revoke them explicitly. Secrets out of model context: .env* is on the default ignore list and hooks can deny reads, but terminal and MCP tools bypass both; Read Controls in Workspace mode also keeps sandboxed commands away from home-directory credential files.

original.mechanism: Team Settings → Models block on personal API keys; beforeReadFile hooks to redact secret files; Enterprise service-account keys (CURSOR_API_KEY) for the CLI

steps.title: Block personal model keys
body: In Team Settings → Models disable personal API keys so all usage routes through the team's included models and ZDR terms.

steps.title: Use service accounts for headless CLI
body: Create an Enterprise service account (Dashboard → Settings → API Keys → Service Accounts), store its one-time key as CURSOR_API_KEY in CI, rotate or archive it to revoke.

original.note: No vault or just-in-time issuance for the secrets the local agent touches; .env files are ignored by default but not protected from terminal tools.

controls.mechanism: Enterprise MCP Configuration allowlist matching the full stdio command string or the remote URL (with wildcards); Cursor's manual review of marketplace plugins and their updates; admin-curated Team Marketplaces

steps.title: Pin stdio servers to a version and remote servers to a URL
body: In Team Settings → MCP Configuration write command entries that spell out the package version (for example *npx -y @acme/mcp-tool@1.4.2, not @latest or @acme/*) and URL entries for the exact server URL rather than a host wildcard.

steps.title: Distribute only curated servers
body: Publish approved servers through a team marketplace in Dashboard → Plugins & MCPs (admin-only on Enterprise) and keep Allow Local Plugin Imports off.

steps.title: Re-check at call time
body: Add a beforeMCPExecution hook with failClosed true to the MDM-placed hooks.json (dashboard hooks cannot fail closed) that checks mcp_server_name, url or command against your registry and denies anything unknown.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: an allowlist admits servers but pins nothing they serve. Full-command matching that includes a pinned package version is version pinning for stdio servers only; remote servers are matched by URL and stay unpinned, and nothing hashes or re-gates a server's tool definitions when they change (the MCPoison fix in 1.3 re-prompts when the configuration changes, not when a server's tool list does). Cursor manually reviews marketplace plugins and every update before listing, which is vendor-side admission for that channel only. Definition scanning and content-hash pinning need an MCP gateway or registry.

original.mechanism: Enterprise MCP Configuration allowlist by command / URL pattern with per-server network modes; mandatory re-approval of any MCP config change (since 1.3); admin-curated Team Marketplaces

steps.title: Pin approved servers by pattern
body: Add each approved server's command or URL pattern to MCP Configuration and choose its network mode (Allow all, Allowlist, Deny all, No sandbox) for local servers.

steps.title: Curate a Team Marketplace
body: Publish approved MCP servers and plugins through Dashboard → Plugins, set installation mode (Default Off / Default On / Required) and turn off Allow Members to Publish.

original.note: Rated native on the same rule as Copilot CLI, Codex and Cowork: the Enterprise allowlist admits servers by command or URL and Team Marketplaces admit plugins by source. Admission is not integrity — no content-hash pinning of tool definitions or rug-pull detection; the 1.3 fix re-prompts on configuration change, not on a server's own tool-list change.

controls.mechanism: Approval prompts that show the full command or MCP arguments; Enterprise Run Mode policy (remove Run Everything, admin-owned allowlists); Browser, File-Deletion and External-File protections; hooks returning ask

steps.title: Remove Run Everything
body: In the web dashboard's team controls take Run Everything out of the modes available to members; team settings take precedence over individual and project configuration.

steps.title: Own the allowlists
body: Configure the Run Mode controls and allowlists as team admin; admin-controlled allowlists make the in-app editor read-only and hide Add to allowlist, so members cannot widen them.

steps.title: Keep the built-in protections on
body: Leave Browser Protection, File-Deletion Protection and External-File Protection enabled so browser tools, deletions and writes outside the workspace still ask.

steps.title: Escalate named actions to a person
body: Return permission ask from beforeShellExecution or beforeMCPExecution hooks for consequential commands (git push, deploys, database writes); preToolUse does not enforce ask.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: a person sees the exact command or MCP arguments when asked and the Enterprise policy can remove Run Everything, but the default and recommended Auto-review mode lets a model classifier clear non-allowlisted calls (not human approval), Allowlist mode with sandboxing runs supported shell commands in the sandbox without asking, workspace file edits need no approval, and the CLI's --force / --yolo and approvalMode unrestricted are not documented as bound by the team policy. Approval is per call with no identity binding or expiry. A person is forced into the loop only where a hook returns ask.

original.mechanism: Run Modes (Auto-review / Allowlist); MCP tools require approval by default; hooks can force ask/deny

steps.title: Remove Run Everything
body: Configure the Enterprise Run Mode policy so members cannot select Run Everything; Ask Every Time was deprecated in 3.5 in favour of Auto-review.

steps.title: Keep MCP approval prompts
body: Leave MCP tools outside the allowlist so Cursor asks for approval and shows arguments before each call.

controls.mechanism: Team Marketplaces (Dashboard → Plugins & MCPs: Marketplace Access, Required / Default On / Default Off, admin-only edits on Enterprise); MCP Configuration allowlist that blocks unmatched servers; AllowedExtensions for extensions

steps.title: Make the team marketplace the approved list
body: In Dashboard → Plugins & MCPs add team marketplaces (admin-only on Enterprise), restrict Marketplace Access to Organization Groups, set each plugin Required, Default On or Default Off, and keep Allow Local Plugin Imports off.

steps.title: Refuse unlisted servers
body: List approved servers in Team Settings → MCP Configuration (Enterprise); with an allowlist active, servers that do not match an entry are blocked.

steps.title: Refuse unlisted extensions
body: Set AllowedExtensions by MDM or in the dashboard's Security & Identity section to the approved publishers and extension IDs, without the "*" wildcard.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: the MCP allowlist, team marketplaces and AllowedExtensions are consulted at load time and unlisted items are refused, but they are settings lists with no owner, version or approval-state record, and admins can let users run their own MCP servers outside the admin patterns. The Analytics API's MCP adoption endpoints (Enterprise) report which servers and tools members use, not an inventory reconciled against the allowlist; endpoint inventory of ~/.cursor/mcp.json and installed plugins is the external complement.

original.mechanism: Team Marketplaces (Dashboard → Plugins) and the MCP Configuration allowlist as the approved list; Active Sessions in Members

steps.title: Make the marketplace the register
body: Restrict marketplace visibility to Organization Groups via SCIM, set Required for mandated plugins and only allow admins to add marketplaces (Enterprise).

original.note: There is no inventory of what is actually installed on endpoints or reconciliation against the allowlist.

controls.mechanism: Endpoint inventory (EDR/MDM) and SSE/proxy detection of the documented Cursor domains; the product's own contribution is prevention (MDM AllowedTeamId, Protected Git Scopes)

evidence.title: Cursor identity and access management — Allowed Team IDs (prevention, not discovery)
Cursor network configuration — backend and sign-in domains for proxy detection

controls.note: External by the rule applied to every vendor: Cursor offers no discovery of unmanaged use on the organisation's domain. AllowedTeamId logs out personal accounts on managed devices and Protected Git Scopes keeps other Cursor accounts from using the org's repositories with Cloud Agents and Bugbot; both are prevention. Discovery is endpoint inventory of the Cursor app, the agent CLI and ~/.cursor, and proxy detection of *.cursor.sh, *.cursorapi.com, *.cursor-cdn.com, *.cursorvm.com (and the accounts.spacex.ai / accounts.x.ai sign-in hosts from 2026-09-30) from devices without the MDM policy.

original.mechanism: MDM AllowedTeamId to block personal logins; Members → Active Sessions; documented backend domains for proxy detection

steps.title: Block personal accounts on managed devices
body: Deploy AllowedTeamId so only your team IDs can sign in, then watch Active Sessions in the dashboard.

steps.title: Detect unmanaged installs at the proxy
body: Alert on traffic to *.cursor.sh, *.cursorapi.com, *.cursor-cdn.com and *.cursorvm.com from devices without the MDM policy.

original.note: Rated external on the same rule as Claude Code: AllowedTeamId prevents personal logins and Active Sessions lists sanctioned use; neither discovers unsanctioned installs, personal accounts on unmanaged devices or undeclared MCP servers and extensions. Discovery is endpoint inventory of the Cursor binary and ~/.cursor, and proxy detection of the documented backend domains.

controls.mechanism: Enterprise OpenTelemetry Export (Team Settings > OpenTelemetry Export, server-side OTLP/HTTP); Enterprise audit log with SIEM streaming and /teams/audit-logs; hooks for per-call records

steps.title: Export telemetry server-side
body: In Team Settings > OpenTelemetry Export create a destination, test the connection and enable it, keeping the model_usage, tool_calls and skills_hooks_plugins families on.

steps.title: Stream the audit log
body: Ask hi@cursor.com to stream the audit log to your SIEM, a webhook or S3 for login, API key, Privacy Mode, mcp_server_config, team_rule and team_hook events.

steps.title: Or pull it
body: Query /teams/audit-logs with an Admin API key (20 requests per minute per team).

steps.title: Record each tool call with hooks
body: Distribute postToolUse, postToolUseFailure, afterShellExecution and afterMCPExecution hooks that ship the tool, arguments, result and conversation_id to your SIEM.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: the export is admin-configured and runs server-side, so a user cannot turn it off, but for the IDE and CLI it carries per-request model logs keyed by cursor.conversation.id and tool calls only as an aggregate metric (cursor.tool.calls by tool name and status, no conversation id, no arguments); per-call tool events and permission decisions are on the wire for Grok Bot only, and prompt, response and tool I/O content (opt-in) covers Cloud Agents and Grok Bot, not the IDE or CLI. The audit log is control plane only ("we do not log agent responses or generated code content"); the dashboard page calls its records tamper-proof, the export makes no such claim. Hooks give per-call records but run on the endpoint and fail open by default. All three are Enterprise.

original.mechanism: Enterprise Audit Log (dashboard audit-log) with SIEM streaming; Admin API /teams/audit-logs; Team Settings → OpenTelemetry Export

steps.title: Stream the audit log
body: Request streaming to Splunk, Sumo Logic, Datadog, a webhook, S3, Elasticsearch or CloudWatch via hi@cursor.com; logged events cover logins, membership, API keys, Privacy Mode, MCP authentication, team rules, hooks and Cloud Agent environments — not agent responses or generated code.

steps.title: Pull it programmatically
body: Query /teams/audit-logs with an Admin API key (Basic auth, 20 requests per minute).

steps.title: Export activity telemetry
body: In Team Settings → OpenTelemetry Export add an OTLP/HTTP destination for token, tool-call, hook and plugin events; no prompt content is exported.

original.note: Tamper-evidence and the retention period are not stated on the pages fetched.

controls.mechanism: Remove the member (Members → Remove, SCIM unassignment, Enterprise Admin API /teams/remove-member); Allow Personal Machines, the team's Remote Control switch (Dashboard → Cloud Agents → Self-Hosted); Team Settings → Models; no stop for a running local session

steps.title: Remove the member
body: Remove the member from Members (context menu → Remove), or unassign them in your identity provider when the team uses SCIM.

steps.title: Automate it
body: Call POST /teams/remove-member with the userId or email (Enterprise, 50 requests per minute) from your offboarding or incident workflow.

steps.title: Cut remote steering
body: Turn Allow Personal Machines (the team's Remote Control setting) off in Dashboard → Cloud Agents → Self-Hosted so members cannot hand local sessions to Cursor's cloud and steer them from another device.

steps.title: Withdraw a model
body: Remove the model or provider from Team Settings → Models (Enterprise) so members can no longer use it.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: each lever blocks new use from the vendor control plane, none is documented to stop a running local session, and the delay before a removed member's in-flight agent fails is not documented. Active Sessions in the dashboard lets admins monitor and manage sessions; whether ending one stops a running agent is not documented. The agent's tools run on the device, so stopping active work is local: an EDR process kill of Cursor or the agent CLI is the external complement. The API overview says API keys "are unaffected by the original creator's account status", so revoke the member's keys as well; AllowedTeamId keeps a removed user from signing back in with a personal account on managed devices.

original.mechanism: SCIM deprovisioning; Admin API /teams/remove-member; Model Access Control to disable a model; AllowedExtensions to remove an extension

steps.title: Cut a user or model
body: Deprovision through SCIM or call /teams/remove-member (Enterprise); disable a provider or model under Team Settings → Models and Cursor stops routing to it.

original.note: There is no fleet-wide stop for running local agent sessions; Remote Control can be switched off for the team from Dashboard → Cloud Agents → Self-Hosted.

controls.mechanism: Third-party EDR; integration points are the code-signed Cursor.app / Cursor.exe and agent CLI processes, the CURSOR_SANDBOX variable Cursor injects into every sandboxed child process, and hook events carrying the command text and sandbox flag

evidence.title: Cursor endpoint security configuration — process and path exclusions
Cursor Run Modes — environment variables injected into sandboxed processes
Cursor hooks — beforeShellExecution / afterShellExecution payloads

controls.note: External by the rule applied to every vendor: Cursor analyses no process behaviour. The endpoint security page lists process and path exclusions (Cursor.exe, rg.exe, inno_updater.exe, Cursor.app) to avoid startup timeouts; exclude those binaries only, never the agent's child processes, so the EDR still sees what agent commands execute. For correlation, CURSOR_SANDBOX (seatbelt or native) and CURSOR_ORIG_UID mark sandboxed agent children, and hook payloads carry command, cwd, sandbox, conversation_id and user_email for the SIEM.

original.mechanism: Third-party EDR with the documented process exclusions; hooks (preToolUse, beforeShellExecution) as the pre-tool-call boundary EDR can consume

steps.title: Register the exclusions
body: Exclude Cursor.exe, rg.exe and inno_updater.exe (Windows) and Cursor.app (macOS) from scanning to avoid timeouts.

steps.title: Feed hook events to your endpoint tooling
body: Enterprise hooks.json runs at every tool boundary and can forward command and file events to an endpoint agent before execution.

original.note: Sensor scope: the host, where Cursor and its sandboxed commands run; hooks are where the sensor can be consulted, not a sensor themselves. Apply the documented process exclusions rather than exempting the agent's child processes.

controls.mechanism: Sandbox network policy (networkPolicy default deny, allow / deny domains and CIDRs; a team-admin allowlist replaces local lists; private ranges and cloud metadata blocked); per-server network mode for stdio MCP servers; Enterprise Browser Controls origin allowlist

steps.title: Set the team's sandbox networking rules
body: In the web dashboard's team controls configure the sandbox networking rules for terminal commands with only the domains agents need; team settings take precedence over individual and project configuration.

steps.title: Rely on the merge rules
body: A team-admin allowlist replaces the per-user and per-repo lists, networkPolicy.default deny wins over allow and deny patterns always win; add denies for internal domains (RFC 1918, IPv6 private ranges and 169.254.169.254 are blocked by default).

steps.title: Constrain local MCP servers
body: Give each stdio server in MCP Configuration the Allowlist or Deny all network mode, never Allow all or No sandbox.

steps.title: Restrict the browser tool
body: Set Browser Controls (Enterprise) to the allowlist of origins agents may visit.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: the domain allowlist exists and the team-admin layer cannot be weakened by local files, but it binds only sandboxed terminal commands and sandboxed stdio MCP servers, not all agent-executed commands. Bypasses: commands escalated outside the sandbox (after a user approval, or in Auto-review after the classifier allows them), Run Everything if not removed, MCP servers set to Allow all or No sandbox, remote MCP servers (restricted only to their own URL pattern), the extension host, the agent's built-in fetch and search tools, and Cursor's own API traffic. The docs do not say whether the admin policy also locks a member's Allow All network mode (which ignores sandbox.json) or whether denied attempts are logged. The endpoint firewall or SSE is the complement for everything else.

original.mechanism: sandbox.json network policy (default deny, allow/deny patterns, RFC 1918 and metadata blocked); per-server MCP network modes; Browser Controls domain allowlist

steps.title: Default-deny sandbox egress
body: Set networkPolicy.default to deny and list allowed domains, wildcards or CIDRs; private ranges and cloud metadata endpoints are blocked regardless, and the team-admin layer cannot be weakened.

steps.title: Constrain local MCP servers
body: Choose Allowlist or Deny all as the network mode for each stdio server in MCP Configuration.

original.note: Applies to sandboxed commands only; commands that run outside the sandbox (Run Everything, No sandbox MCP servers) reach anything the device can.

controls.mechanism: Cursor's extension marketplace proxy (marketplace.cursorapi.com) scans extensions for malware before serving them; Marketplace Install Cooldown; Enterprise Require Extension Signature Verification; AllowedExtensions version pins; Cursor's manual review of marketplace plugins

steps.title: Delay and verify extension installs
body: In Team settings → Security & automation set Marketplace Install Cooldown (hours) above 0, applied fleet-wide, and on Enterprise turn on Require Extension Signature Verification.

steps.title: Pin approved extensions
body: Set AllowedExtensions by MDM or in the dashboard to approved publishers and extension IDs, pinning versions or a release channel where needed.

steps.title: Force dependency installs through your mirror
body: Make the team-admin sandbox allowlist permit only your scanned package mirror's domains for package managers, so sandboxed installs cannot reach public registries directly.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: Cursor itself scans what it serves on one channel, extensions through its marketplace proxy (automated malware and supply-chain analysis, with a blocklist), and manually reviews marketplace plugins and every update; the cooldown and signature checks are client-side install gates. Outside that boundary: project dependencies and MCP server packages the agent installs through the terminal (npm, pip, npx), plugins from GitHub-imported team marketplaces or local imports, and extensions from a custom ExtensionGalleryServiceUrl. Those need the organisation's package mirror or artifact repository with malware scanning; the sandbox allowlist enforces the route only for sandboxed commands. No model files are loaded on the device, since inference is hosted.

original.mechanism: Not applicable — no model artifacts are loaded on the device
original.note: All inference is on Cursor's hosted providers; which models may be used is governed by Model Access Control. Nothing to scan locally.

evidence.title: Vendor docs index, reviewed for applicability (2026-09-10)

original.mechanism: Not offered
original.note: No manifest or signature of the models, plugins and tools composing a session. Extension installs can require signature verification and an Install Cooldown (security hardening page), and the official marketplace is manually reviewed, but nothing is machine-readable or verified at load.

evidence.title: Vendor docs index, reviewed; no setting for this control (2026-09-10)

settings.name: Single Sign-On (SSO)
settings.where: Team Settings › Single Sign-On (SSO) › SSO-Provider Connection Settings and Domain Verification Settings (Enterprise orgs › Organization's Settings)
settings.recommended: SSO connection active with every corporate domain verified, and MFA enforced on the Cursor app in your IdP
settings.why: Once the connection and domain are active every user on that domain must sign in through the IdP and its MFA; there is no separate enforcement toggle to forget.

settings.name: SCIM
settings.where: Team Settings › SCIM (after SSO), with the Cursor SCIM app in your IdP
settings.recommended: SCIM, driven by the IdP group that grants Cursor
settings.why: Unassigning someone in the IdP removes them from the team, so a leaver's access ends with their account rather than with a ticket.

settings.name: AllowedTeamId
settings.where: MDM policy AllowedTeamId (overrides cursorAuth.allowedTeamId)
settings.recommended: Your Enterprise team IDs, comma-separated
settings.why: A sign-in to any other team, personal accounts without Privacy Mode included, is logged out immediately on managed devices.

settings.name: x-cursor-allowed-tenants
settings.where: TLS-terminating proxy → header on requests to api2.cursor.sh and cursor.com
settings.recommended: v1.orgs=<your organization id>
settings.why: From the corporate network the app, CLI and API keys can only reach your organisation, which covers devices MDM does not; it needs TLS termination on those two hosts.

settings.name: Allow Personal API Key Creation
settings.where: grok.com/dashboard › API keys › Team › Personal API Keys
settings.recommended: Off, with Enterprise service accounts for CI and automation
settings.why: User API keys skip the IdP and its MFA and outlive the member's account; existing keys keep working, so revoke them from Members › View API keys.

settings.name: Privacy Mode
settings.where: Team dashboard › Settings › Privacy Settings (enable, then enforce)
settings.default: On for Enterprise teams, not enforced
settings.recommended: On and enforced
settings.why: Members cannot switch off zero data retention and the no-training commitment for Cursor-routed models.

settings.name: Models with data retention
settings.where: Team dashboard › restricted models (for example Claude Fable 5.1)
settings.default: Not approved (requests to these models fail)
settings.recommended: Not approved
settings.why: Every request stays under Cursor's zero-retention agreements; approving one opts the whole team into provider-side retention of inputs and outputs.

settings.name: Model access control
settings.where: Team Settings › Models › Cursor Models, Other Models and Model Defaults
settings.default: New models are opt-in for Enterprise teams
settings.recommended: The models your AI risk review approved, new models off by default, Claude 4.5 Haiku kept allowed
settings.why: Members use only reviewed models, a model can be withdrawn team-wide in one place, and Auto-review keeps its classifier.

settings.name: Personal API Keys (BYOK)
settings.where: Team Settings › Models › Personal API Keys (BYOK)
settings.recommended: Blocked
settings.why: A member's own OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure or Bedrock key routes code outside Cursor's zero-retention terms and outside the organisation's key custody.

settings.name: Cursor Ignore Configuration
settings.where: Team dashboard › Settings › Cursor Ignore Configuration
settings.recommended: .env*, *.pem, *.key, credentials and secrets directories, and regulated client data trees
settings.why: Agent, Tab and @-mentions stop pulling secret files into context; terminal and MCP tools ignore it, so Read Controls and hooks carry the hard boundary.

settings.name: Repository Blocklist
settings.where: Team dashboard › Settings › Repository Blocklist
settings.recommended: Client repositories not cleared for AI assistance
settings.why: The editor and CLI refuse to index or work in those repositories at all; it does not reach Cloud Agents or Bugbot.

settings.name: Auto Run Configuration
settings.where: Team dashboard › Settings › Auto Run Configuration (team Run Mode controls)
settings.default: Auto-review, Allowlist and Run Everything all available to members
settings.recommended: Auto-review and Allowlist only, sandboxing on; Run Everything removed
settings.why: Members lose the mode that runs every tool call with no prompt, sandbox or classifier; team settings outrank user and project files.

settings.name: terminalAllowlist and mcpAllowlist
settings.where: Team dashboard Run Mode allowlists, or ~/.cursor/permissions.json by MDM
settings.recommended: Admin-owned lists of build and test commands and read-only MCP tools; no git push, curl or publish commands
settings.why: Allowlisted calls skip review entirely; an admin list replaces the file and editor lists and makes the in-app editor read-only.

settings.name: Read Controls
settings.where: Team Settings › Security & automation › Read Controls (with Read Allowlist and Read Control User Extensions)
settings.default: Off (each member's Read Access, which defaults to System)
settings.recommended: On, mode Workspace, with a team Read Allowlist for shared toolchains
settings.why: The agent asks before reading outside the workspace and sandboxed commands lose ~/.ssh, cloud CLI config and other home-directory secrets.

settings.name: Cloud Distribution (team hooks)
settings.where: Web dashboard › Team content › Hooks
settings.recommended: preToolUse, beforeShellExecution and beforeMCPExecution hooks calling your policy service; beforeSubmitPrompt, beforeReadFile and postToolUse hooks calling your DLP and injection screening; post-call hooks logging to the SIEM
settings.why: Your own deny logic runs in the harness before shell, file and MCP calls on every member's machine, synced every thirty minutes, and can block or rewrite prompts, reads and MCP results.

settings.name: failClosed
settings.where: MDM-placed hooks.json → failClosed (/Library/Application Support/Cursor/hooks.json, /etc/cursor/hooks.json, C:\ProgramData\Cursor\hooks.json)
settings.recommended: true on the policy and DLP hooks
settings.why: Dashboard hooks take no per-hook failClosed, so a crashed or timed-out policy hook lets the call through unless the MDM copy fails closed.

settings.name: Block until hooks are ready
settings.where: Web dashboard › Team content › Hooks › hook settings
settings.recommended: On
settings.why: The first prompt after a restart otherwise runs before enterprise, team and project hooks have loaded.

settings.name: MCP Configuration
settings.where: Team dashboard › Settings › MCP Configuration (command and URL allowlist, per-server Tools)
settings.recommended: Approved servers only — stdio entries with a pinned package version, remote servers by exact URL, Tools limited per server
settings.why: A server that matches no entry is blocked, and a version-pinned command stops a silent package swap on stdio servers.

settings.name: Marketplace Access
settings.where: Dashboard › Plugins & MCPs › Team Marketplaces › Marketplace Settings › Marketplace Access, with Plugin Installation per plugin
settings.recommended: The firm's curated team marketplace as the distribution channel, security plugins set to Required
settings.why: Plugins bundle MCP servers, rules and hooks; members get the reviewed set from one place and cannot uninstall the required ones.

settings.name: Allow Members to Publish
settings.where: Dashboard › Plugins & MCPs › Default marketplace › Marketplace Settings
settings.recommended: Off
settings.why: Only admins publish skills to the team marketplace, so an unreviewed personal skill cannot spread to every teammate.

settings.name: Allow Local Plugin Imports
settings.where: Dashboard › Settings › Security & Identity › Marketplace and Plugins
settings.recommended: Off
settings.why: Plugins dropped into ~/.cursor/plugins/local or imported from disk would bypass the curated marketplace.

settings.name: AllowedExtensions
settings.where: MDM policy AllowedExtensions (or dashboard › Security & Identity, which MDM overrides)
settings.recommended: Your approved publishers and extension IDs, version-pinned where it matters, with no "*": true
settings.why: Extensions run with workspace access outside the agent sandbox; anything not listed cannot be installed.

settings.name: Marketplace Install Cooldown (hours) with Require Extension Signature Verification
settings.where: Team settings › Security & automation
settings.recommended: 72 / On
settings.why: A malicious extension version that is pulled within three days never reaches the fleet, and unsigned Open VSX packages are refused.
settings.requires: Teams or Enterprise; signature verification Enterprise

settings.name: .cursor Directory Protection
settings.where: Team dashboard › Settings › .cursor Directory Protection
settings.recommended: On
settings.why: An injected agent needs a person's approval to rewrite .cursor rules, MCP config or hooks that persist into the next session.

settings.name: Enforce this rule
settings.where: Cursor dashboard › Team content › Team Rules › Enforce this rule
settings.default: Not enforced (members can toggle a rule off)
settings.recommended: On for the firm's security and client-data rules
settings.why: Members cannot switch the firm's instructions off, and Team Rules outrank project rules; they steer the model and do not replace hooks.

settings.name: WorkspaceTrustEnabled
settings.where: MDM policy WorkspaceTrustEnabled (overrides security.workspace.trust.enabled)
settings.recommended: true
settings.why: A cloned repository's project hooks and settings run only after the developer trusts the folder.

settings.name: permissions.deny
settings.where: ~/.cursor/cli-config.json → permissions.deny
settings.recommended: Read(.env*), Read(~/.ssh/**), Read(~/.aws/**), Write(**/*.key) and Shell(rm)
settings.why: The CLI agent cannot read key and token files or run the listed commands; the file is user-editable, so pair it with hooks.

settings.name: Sandbox networking rules
settings.where: Web dashboard › team controls › sandbox networking rules (merged above ~/.cursor/sandbox.json and the repo's sandbox.json)
settings.recommended: A team allowlist of your source control, package mirror and approved domains, networkPolicy.default deny
settings.why: Sandboxed commands reach only listed hosts and installs go through the scanned mirror; a team allowlist replaces user and repo lists, which cannot widen it.

settings.name: Network mode (per-server network controls)
settings.where: Team dashboard › MCP Configuration › each stdio server › network mode
settings.recommended: Allowlist, or Deny all for servers that need no network; never No sandbox
settings.why: A local MCP server, which runs outside the agent sandbox, can only reach the destinations its job needs.

settings.name: OpenTelemetry Export
settings.where: Team Settings › OpenTelemetry Export › destination
settings.recommended: A destination at your collector with every family on
settings.why: Model requests, tool-call counts, hook executions and plugin installs reach the SIEM server-side, so a member cannot switch them off.

settings.name: Streaming audit logs
settings.where: Arranged with hi@cursor.com — Splunk HEC, Sumo Logic, HTTPS webhook or S3
settings.recommended: On, to your SIEM
settings.why: Sign-ins, API key creation and revocation, and every settings change land in the SIEM rather than only on the dashboard page.

settings.name: Allow Personal Machines (Remote Control)
settings.where: Cursor Dashboard › Cloud Agents › Self-Hosted
settings.default: Off on Teams and Enterprise until an admin enables it
settings.recommended: Off, unless a team needs to drive local sessions from a phone
settings.why: Stops a local session, with the developer's files and credentials, being steered through Cursor's cloud from another device.
