facts.value: Copilot Chat concepts and Spaces.

items.title: Policies that reach chat on github.com
body: Copilot in the cloud is the feature switch for chat and agent work on github.com and Mobile. Per the supported-surfaces table, Copilot can search the web, Configure models, MCP servers in Copilot, Copilot Memory and content exclusion apply to cloud sandbox sessions; on GitHub Actions-based sessions web search does not apply. Restrict MCP access to registry servers applies to neither, so the MCP allowlist for these sessions is the managed allowedMcpServers list, which cloud sandbox sessions read together with the permissions.* rules. Across a user's organisations the least restrictive setting wins for most policies, including web search and Copilot in the cloud; public-code matching is among the exceptions that follow the most restrictive.

links.title: Enterprise managed settings (client support by key)

items.title: The unified Copilot in the cloud experience (from 2026-10-28)
body: Copilot Chat on github.com, Chat in GitHub Mobile and the cloud agent are one experience under one policy. A session runs in a cloud sandbox (the default: resumable across clients, life-of-account retention, repository and personal MCP servers and connectors) or on GitHub Actions (28-day retention, setup steps, self-hosted runners), chosen at start; policy and managed-settings coverage differs between the two. Repositories opted out of the cloud agent stay opted out.

links.title: Copilot on GitHub.com and GitHub Mobile (comparison of the two experiences)
Managing Copilot in the cloud for your enterprise

riskNotes.note: CamoLeak (2025) turned hidden PR-description comments into silent exfiltration through GitHub's own Camo image proxy; the fix was to stop rendering images in chat. Chat still reads every issue and PR the user can see, and in the new experience acts through its preconfigured GitHub tools and any MCP servers or connectors a user adds in a cloud sandbox session.

Web search and image/PDF attachments widen the inference input beyond repository data; both are policy-controlled (web search) or user-controlled (attachments) rather than inspected. Cloud sandbox sessions keep chat for the life of the account (28 days on GitHub Actions), and Spaces accept uploads and free text that are then shareable to organisation members or publicly.

Spaces and the repositories themselves are the retrieval stores (a repository is indexed automatically once a chat has its context); anyone with editor access to an organisation Space, or push access to a repository, can shape what the model reads.

controls.mechanism: Copilot licences by user, enterprise team (IdP-synced under Enterprise Managed Users) or organization; enterprise Copilot policies set once or delegated to organizations (AI controls > Copilot > Configure features & clients), chat itself under the Copilot in the cloud policy; Copilot connectors and personal MCP servers in cloud sandbox sessions admitted by MCP servers in Copilot and the managed allowedMcpServers list; OAuth app access restrictions and GitHub App installation are GitHub's target-tenant path for other products' GitHub connectors

steps.title: Assign licences by group
body: Enterprise > Billing and licensing > Licensing > Copilot > Manage > Enterprise Teams > Assign licenses; with Enterprise Managed Users sync the team to an IdP group so joining or leaving the group grants or removes Copilot.

steps.title: Set feature policies at enterprise level
body: Enterprise > AI controls > Copilot > Configure features & clients: enable or disable each policy for the enterprise instead of letting organizations decide, because a user seated by several organizations gets the least restrictive setting.

steps.title: As the target tenant, gate other vendors' GitHub connectors
body: Keep OAuth app access restrictions enabled on each organization (the default for new organizations) and approve OAuth apps and GitHub App installations one by one, which decides whether another chat product's GitHub connector can reach organization data.

controls.note: Partial by the D3-APA rule on this drawing: GitHub administers group-based authorization over the chat feature (licences by user, enterprise team or organization; policies per enterprise or delegated per organization, enforced server-side), but the connectors chat can now use in cloud sandbox sessions (Copilot connectors, personal MCP servers) are admitted by an enterprise allowlist, not by a consent the target tenant grants per connector, and inside the product authorization is feature on/off per organization, with per-team variation only through enterprise-team overrides of managed settings. The consent path GitHub does document runs the other way: as the target tenant for other vendors' GitHub connectors (OAuth app access restrictions, bypassed by privileged OAuth apps; GitHub App installation with selected repositories; fine-grained token approval) — the other products' control seen from their side. The enterprise block for Copilot in the cloud is labelled for the cloud agent; GitHub does not say whether it also refuses chat to someone licensed elsewhere who can read the repositories. Policy configuration is not the runtime decision; the decision is GitHub's server-side check of licence and policy on each request.

original.mechanism: Copilot seat assignment (enterprise teams, IdP-synced under EMU), Copilot in GitHub.com policy, SAML SSO

steps.title: Assign seats and enable the feature
body: Grant licences from Enterprise > Billing and licensing > Licensing > Copilot (users, enterprise teams or organisations); enable Copilot in GitHub.com under AI controls > Copilot > Configure features & clients.

steps.title: Confirm the unified policy before 2026-09-28
body: Review the single policy replacing Copilot Chat on github.com, Chat in Mobile and the cloud agent; opting out removes chat on github.com and Mobile.

original.mechanism: Retrieval runs as the user; Space viewers only see sources they have access to; no remediation of over-shared repositories

steps.title: Rely on repository permissions and Space visibility
body: Organisation-owned Spaces grant admin / editor / viewer or No access; viewers only see sources they can already access — fix repository over-sharing first.

original.note: Delegated: retrieval carries the user's own repository permissions, so an over-shared repository is retrievable by everyone who can already see it; nothing here narrows scope below the user's entitlements.

controls.mechanism: Enterprise access restrictions: the sec-GitHub-allowed-enterprise header, injected by the organisation's break-and-inspect proxy on github.com, api.github.com and *.githubcopilot.com, makes GitHub refuse accounts outside the enterprise (Enterprise Managed Users only); Copilot subscription-based network routing by plan endpoint; the web-search policy for GitHub's own egress

steps.title: Enable enterprise access restrictions
body: Enterprise > Settings > Authentication security > Enterprise access restrictions: select "Enable enterprise access restrictions" and copy the header value shown for the enterprise.

steps.title: Inject the header at the proxy
body: Have the TLS-inspecting proxy overwrite sec-GitHub-allowed-enterprise: ENTERPRISE-ID (up to 20 IDs) on all traffic to github.com/*, api.github.com/* and *.githubcopilot.com; other accounts get a 403 and the audit log records business.proxy_security_header_unsatisfied.

steps.title: Route Copilot by plan
body: Allow *.business.githubcopilot.com and/or *.enterprise.githubcopilot.com and block *.individual.githubcopilot.com; GitHub lists Copilot Chat on GitHub and GitHub Mobile among the features this routing affects.

steps.title: Turn web search off where exfiltration risk matters
body: Set Copilot can search the web to disabled at enterprise level; it applies to cloud sandbox sessions (not to sessions on GitHub Actions), and across a user's organizations the least restrictive setting wins.

controls.note: Partial by the D3-OTF rule on this drawing: GitHub honours a documented tenant-restriction header that the organisation's proxy injects and enforces the block server-side (web sign-in, API and OAuth or GitHub App tokens, Copilot endpoints); the organisation's SSE does the injection. Boundary: Enterprise Managed Users only (data-residency enterprises are already separated by their GHE.com subdomain); it needs a break-and-inspect proxy on every path, so devices off the proxy are not covered. Enterprises with personal accounts have no header, only the plan-based endpoint routing, which blocks personal Copilot plans but not a personal GitHub account. A customer proxy does not control GitHub's own egress: web search queries go to Bing from GitHub's side, and a cloud agent session started from chat egresses from GitHub-hosted runners under its own firewall (toolCopilotCloudAgent); keeping web search off is the only chat-side lever.

original.mechanism: No vendor feature; github.com chat traffic is ordinary HTTPS to github.com
original.note: An SSE or CASB can only see the browser session; the model traffic originates from GitHub's side. Tenancy enforcement must rely on SSO and seat assignment.

evidence.title: Vendor docs index, reviewed for the integration point (2026-09-10)

original.mechanism: Web-search policy; image rendering disabled in chat (post-CamoLeak); GitHub MCP server limited to a fixed task set
original.note: The model's reach is GitHub data plus web search; there is no domain allowlist for chat, and the vendor's remaining lever is to keep web search off.

steps.title: Turn web search off where exfiltration risk matters
body: Disable Copilot can search the web; it applies to IDEs and Chat in GitHub.

controls.mechanism: No content inspection in the product; content exclusion (path filter) and the web-search policy are data minimisation; an SSE or browser security product inspecting the github.com and *.githubcopilot.com session is the integration point

evidence.title: Content exclusion for GitHub Copilot (website and Mobile support, public preview)
Asking Copilot questions in GitHub (attachments on by default, no policy)
Copilot network routing (plan endpoints an SSE can see)
Audit log events for agents (Copilot API usage records, EMU and data residency, preview)

controls.note: External by the rule applied to every vendor on this drawing: GitHub detects nothing in chat prompts, attachments, Space uploads or answers, offers no inline hook, and applies no sensitivity labels. Content exclusion (Enterprise > AI controls > Copilot > Content exclusion; public preview on the website and Mobile) keeps named paths out of Copilot's context, and the web-search policy limits what leaves in search queries — path and feature minimisation, not detection. Image and PDF attachments (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WEBP, PDF, HEIC, HEIF) are on for every plan with no policy to turn them off. Integration point: an SSE or browser security product that TLS-inspects the github.com and *.githubcopilot.com session and blocks pastes and uploads before they leave. Copilot Usage Records (request and response bodies, Enterprise Managed Users and data-residency enterprises, preview) would allow detection after the fact, but its documented client list does not name Chat on github.com.

original.mechanism: Content exclusion (honoured by Chat on GitHub and Mobile) and the web-search policy; no inspection of prompts or uploads

steps.title: Exclude sensitive paths at enterprise scope
body: Enterprise > AI controls > Copilot > Content exclusion: fnmatch patterns per repository or "*" — applied to chat on the GitHub website and Mobile, not to third-party agents.

steps.title: Decide on web search
body: Set Copilot can search the web at enterprise level; across a user's organisations it resolves to the least restrictive organisation setting, so an enterprise-level lockdown is the only way to guarantee it is off.

original.note: Content exclusion is a context filter on what the model may read; nothing inspects the prompt, the uploads or the answer for sensitive content.

original.mechanism: No vendor feature; paste and upload controls belong to a browser security product
original.note: Chat accepts JPEG, PNG, GIF, WEBP, PDF, HEIC and HEIF attachments; only a browser control can stop uploads of classified documents.

evidence.title: Vendor docs index, reviewed for the integration point (2026-09-10)

controls.mechanism: No documented screening of the content Chat on github.com reads; GitHub-side content filters on prompts and outputs cover harmful content, and image rendering was disabled after CamoLeak

controls.note: None by the input-screening rule on this drawing: GitHub documents no injection screening of the repository files, issues, pull requests, Space sources, attachments or web results that Chat on github.com reads, nothing an administrator can switch on or tune, and no event. What exists is adjacent: prompts and outputs pass GitHub's content filters for harmful, offensive or off-topic content (a harm filter, not injection classification); hidden characters and HTML comments are filtered only before input reaches the Copilot cloud agent; and disabling image rendering in chat on 2025-08-14 closed the CamoLeak exfiltration channel on the output side. No product class can sit on GitHub's internal retrieval path. What stands in: web search off, the Allow confirmation and rulesets for writes, and GitHub's defences questioned in the vendor assessment.

body: Image rendering in Copilot Chat was disabled on 2025-08-14 to close the Camo exfiltration channel; hidden HTML comments in issues and PRs are filtered before agent prompts.

controls.note: External by rule: the assessment belongs to the organisation's TPRM platform. The GitHub Copilot Trust Center overview lists SOC 1, SOC 2, SOC 3, ISO 27001:2013, CSA STAR Level 2, TISAX and ISO/IEC 42001:2023, with SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 reports, a SOC 3 report, bridge letters, the 2026 ISO/IEC 42001 certificate, a 2026 CAIQ, a PCI DSS attestation and bug-bounty letters, most behind Request access; the overview shows no penetration-test summary. The model-hosting page names the processors chat can route to — OpenAI (OpenAI and GitHub's Azure), Anthropic (Amazon Bedrock, Anthropic, Google Cloud; Claude Fable 5 and 5.1 retained by Anthropic by default unless a ZDR exemption is granted), Google, xAI, Microsoft (Azure AI Foundry) and Moonshot models on Foundry or Fireworks — and web search sends queries to Bing. Re-assess for the Copilot in the cloud experience launched 2026-10-28 (one policy, life-of-account retention in cloud sandboxes, user-added MCP servers and connectors as new processors). Policy state in the UI and the audit log are the read points a TPRM or SSPM tool can use.

original.mechanism: No vendor feature; model-hosting page lists providers and retention terms

steps.title: Record the provider set
body: OpenAI on Azure, Anthropic on AWS / Anthropic / GCP (Claude Fable 5 / 5.1 retain by default), Google, xAI, Moonshot on Foundry / Fireworks.

original.mechanism: Enterprise AI controls tab (features, privacy, models, Memory, MCP), audit log for policy changes
original.note: Switches and evidence of switching are inputs to governance; catalogue, intake, risk decisions and ownership live in the organisation's governance platform. Rated external on the same rule as every other vendor.

steps.title: Manage policies from the AI controls tab
body: Enterprise > AI controls > Copilot > Configure features & clients holds the chat-relevant policies; organisation settings sit under Settings > Code, planning, and automation > Copilot.

original.mechanism: Policy state is visible in the UI and audit log; an SSPM tool reads it via the audit log stream and REST APIs
original.note: Policy state in the UI, the audit log stream and the REST APIs are the inputs; comparison to a baseline and drift detection are the SSPM product's.

evidence.title: Vendor docs index, reviewed for the integration point (2026-09-10)

controls.mechanism: Allow confirmation before each GitHub MCP skill runs in Chat on github.com (create_branch, create_or_update_file, push_files, update_pull_request_branch, merge_pull_request); in Copilot in the cloud sessions, interactive mode with assisted tool approvals, and in cloud sandboxes the managed permissions.ask and disableBypassPermissionsMode keys; branch rulesets and repository roles still gate the resulting writes

steps.title: Gate protected branches with rulesets
body: In a branch ruleset add "Require a pull request before merging" with required approvals and "Restrict updates", and keep the bypass list short, so a push_files or merge_pull_request confirmed in chat meets the same rules as the person.

steps.title: Know what the user confirms
body: The user clicks Allow to confirm each MCP skill action before Chat performs it; GitHub documents no administrator setting to require, extend or remove that confirmation.

steps.title: Require fresh approval in cloud sandbox sessions
body: In managed-settings.json set permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode to "disable" and list the operations that must always prompt under permissions.ask; cloud sandbox sessions honour both, sessions on GitHub Actions do not.

controls.note: Partial by the approval rule on this drawing: a present person confirms each write before it runs. In cloud sandbox sessions the administrator can now remove allow-all and force a fresh prompt for chosen operations through managed settings; sessions on GitHub Actions do not read those keys, assisted approval lets a model clear operations it judges safe, the docs do not say whether the chat prompt shows the exact arguments, and the built-in write tools cannot be switched off one by one. Rulesets and required reviews then approve the result on protected branches — a merge gate approves the output, not the action — while create_branch, create_or_update_file and push_files to an unprotected branch land directly. A cloud agent session started from chat is governed by the cloud agent's own gates (toolCopilotCloudAgent), not this prompt.

original.mechanism: GitHub MCP actions run "at your request" in the conversation; agent hand-offs land in the cloud agent's draft-PR and workflow-approval gates
original.note: The chat page documents no per-action approval prompt for the built-in MCP tasks; the human gate is the conversation itself and, downstream, PR review.

steps.title: Keep the downstream gates
body: Chat can create branches or merge PRs on request and can start cloud agent sessions; branch protections, rulesets and workflow approval remain the enforced approvals.

controls.mechanism: The organization's repository list (visibility, base permissions) is the inventory of what chat can reach; repository custom properties hold an administrator-set classification; no content classification, no oversharing report, no administrator list of Spaces

steps.title: Label repositories by sensitivity
body: Organization Settings > Repository > Custom properties > New property (for example a single select data_sensitivity), then Set values on each repository so rulesets can target them.

controls.note: Partial by the D3-DI rule on this drawing: what chat reaches is the repositories, issues and pull requests the user can already read, and GitHub's repository list with its visibility and base permissions is that inventory; custom properties let administrators record a classification by hand. GitHub classifies nothing in the content, reports neither what Copilot can reach nor over-shared repositories (internal repositories are readable by every enterprise member whatever the base permission), and lists no organization- or user-owned Spaces to administrators; attachments, Space uploads and conversations are not inventoried. Retention is not inventory. A DSPM or data-classification product over the repositories fills the classification half.

original.mechanism: Conversation retention (28 days → life of account from 2026-09-28), Memory export / delete and 28-day expiry, Spaces visibility settings

steps.title: Export or delete Memory when required
body: Organization Settings > Copilot > Access: Export Copilot memories / Delete Copilot memories per user, or Download / Delete user memories in bulk (JSONL, 10 exports per hour).

steps.title: Plan for life-of-account chat retention
body: After 2026-09-28 chat conversations are retained for the life of the account rather than 28 days; treat chat history as a data store in retention policy.

original.note: Retention and Memory export or deletion are lifecycle controls; nothing discovers or classifies sensitive content in conversations or memories — a DSPM product reads the exports to do that.

controls.mechanism: No tunnel and no connector tokens (the built-in GitHub MCP skills run in the user's session); the lifetimes an administrator can bound are the personal access tokens used against the Copilot administration APIs (Enterprise > Policies > Personal access tokens) and the IdP-governed SSO period

steps.title: Cap token lifetimes for automation
body: Enterprise > Policies > Personal access tokens: under "Set maximum lifetimes for personal access tokens" set a limit on the Fine-grained tokens and Tokens (classic) tabs, leave "Exempt administrators" unchecked where possible, and require approval of fine-grained tokens.

controls.note: Partial by the D3-CH rule for products without a tunnel: GitHub offers no tunnel for Chat on github.com (it reaches only GitHub data and Bing) and holds no connector OAuth tokens for the organisation to govern; the GitHub MCP skills act through the user's session, and GitHub does not document the credential they use internally or its lifetime. The credentials around the product are the user's web and GitHub Mobile sessions (SAML SSO re-authentication every 24 hours unless the IdP sets otherwise; Mobile session lifetime not documented) and the tokens automation uses against the Copilot administration APIs (content exclusion, usage records, metrics), which the enterprise can bound — fine-grained tokens default to a 366-day maximum, classic tokens have no expiration requirement unless a lifetime policy is set, and administrators can be exempted from it. Secrets pasted into chat are a redaction matter, not this row.

original.mechanism: Not applicable — chat holds no agent credentials; secret scanning covers repository content, not chat uploads
original.note: Uploaded files and pasted text are not secret-scanned; content exclusion of secret paths is the only vendor lever.

evidence.title: Vendor docs index, reviewed for applicability (2026-09-10)

controls.mechanism: Preconfigured GitHub tools in chat; in Copilot in the cloud sandbox sessions, repository and personal MCP servers and Copilot connectors admitted by the "MCP servers in Copilot" policy and the managed allowedMcpServers / deniedMcpServers lists, with managed permissions.deny / ask / allow rules ("Restrict MCP access to registry servers" is not supported for cloud sessions); each GitHub tool bounded by the user's repository role and rulesets; the "Copilot can search the web" policy for the web tool

steps.title: Decide on web search at enterprise level
body: Set Copilot can search the web for the whole enterprise rather than letting organizations decide; across a user's organizations the least restrictive setting wins.

steps.title: Bound the write skills with rulesets
body: Use "Restrict updates", "Restrict deletions" and "Require a pull request before merging" in branch rulesets so create_branch, push_files, create_or_update_file and merge_pull_request can do no more than the person's role and the ruleset allow.

steps.title: Allowlist MCP servers and connectors for cloud sandbox sessions
body: Keep MCP servers in Copilot enabled and define allowedMcpServers (by serverUrl or serverCommand) in the enterprise's managed-settings.json; connectors are remote MCP servers and are blocked unless their URLs match an entry.

steps.title: Deny operations in cloud sandbox sessions
body: Put Shell(), Read(), Edit() and Domain() selectors under permissions.deny in managed settings; they apply in cloud sandboxes, not in sessions on GitHub Actions.

controls.note: Partial by the tool-permission rule on this drawing. Since the Copilot in the cloud experience (2026-10-28), cloud sandbox sessions accept repository and personal MCP servers and connectors, and the administrator can restrict them with allowedMcpServers (matched on URL or command; the registry restriction is not supported there) and deny or gate operations with managed permissions, varied per enterprise team through overrides. Sessions on GitHub Actions do not read those keys, and allowedMcpServers does not cover servers defined in custom agent profiles. What holds per principal, operation and resource is GitHub's own permission model: each GitHub tool acts with the user's repository role (a session without write access is read-only), and rulesets are enforced server-side outside the model. Switching chat off entirely is the kill-switch row.

original.mechanism: Fixed GitHub MCP server with a limited task set; MCP policy and registry restriction do not apply to Chat in GitHub; web-search policy
original.note: The tool set cannot be narrowed by the customer; only web search can be switched off.

steps.title: Accept the fixed tool set or disable the surface
body: The supported-surfaces table shows MCP servers in Copilot as not applicable to Copilot Chat in GitHub; the built-in GitHub MCP server performs a limited set of tasks at the user's request.

controls.mechanism: Retrieval as the requesting user (Space viewers only see sources they can access); content exclusion at enterprise, organization and repository level, honoured by Chat on the GitHub website and in GitHub Mobile (public preview)

steps.title: Exclude repositories and paths from Copilot
body: Enterprise > AI controls > Copilot > Content exclusion: enter a repository reference followed by fnmatch path patterns, or "*": for patterns that apply in every repository; enterprise rules apply to every Copilot user in the enterprise, organization rules only to users seated by that organization.

steps.title: Fix over-broad permissions before chat surfaces them
body: Organization Settings > Member privileges > Base permissions: set the lowest level members need; internal repositories stay readable by every enterprise member regardless.

steps.title: Share organization Spaces by role
body: In a Space's share dialog set the organization base role to viewer, editor or No access and add named users or teams; viewers still see only the sources they can open.

controls.note: Native by the retrieval rule on this drawing: retrieval runs with the requesting user's own GitHub permissions, and the administrator restricts what is returned with content exclusion, enforced by GitHub server-side for Chat on the GitHub website and in GitHub Mobile. Boundary: content exclusion is in public preview on those two surfaces and matches file paths, so issue, pull-request and discussion text, Space free text and uploads are outside it, and the docs do not say whether a file attached to a Space bypasses an exclusion; organization rules bind only users seated by that organization, repository rules any Copilot user in the enterprise. GitHub offers no oversharing analysis: an over-shared repository answers everyone who can read it. The enterprise block for Copilot in the cloud is labelled for the cloud agent; the docs do not say whether it also refuses chat over those repositories to people licensed elsewhere.

original.mechanism: Retrieval runs as the user; Space viewers only see sources they have access to; no remediation of over-shared repositories

steps.title: Rely on repository permissions and Space visibility
body: Organisation-owned Spaces grant admin / editor / viewer or No access; viewers only see sources they can already access — fix repository over-sharing first.

original.note: Delegated: retrieval carries the user's own repository permissions, so an over-shared repository is retrievable by everyone who can already see it; nothing here narrows scope below the user's entitlements.

controls.mechanism: No inventory of chat's tools with owner and approval state; in cloud sandbox sessions the managed allowedMcpServers list, kept in the enterprise's .github-private repository, admits only listed MCP servers and Copilot connectors and blocks the rest; Copilot Spaces — the corpora users attach on their own authority — have no administrator inventory, owner record, approval state or block

steps.title: Keep the approved servers and connectors in managed settings
body: List each approved MCP server and connector URL under allowedMcpServers in copilot/managed-settings.json in the .github-private repository, so the file is the reviewed record of what cloud sessions may use.

steps.title: Keep a register of organization Spaces
body: Prefer organization-owned Spaces shared by role and record them by process; GitHub offers no administrator list of Spaces.

controls.note: Raised from none to partial by the registry rule on this drawing: the premise of the old rating — a tool set closed by construction — no longer holds, because cloud sandbox sessions now take repository and personal MCP servers and connectors, and an unlisted one is now blocked by allowedMcpServers. It is an admission list, not a registry: it records no owner or approval state and does not verify what a server serves; sessions on GitHub Actions and servers in custom agent profiles are outside it. The gap is still Spaces: anyone with a Copilot licence, including Free, can create one; GitHub states that creation is not blocked under an organization that has Spaces disabled when the user's seat comes from elsewhere, yet no Spaces policy appears on the policy pages fetched; organization-owned Spaces can be hidden from other members with No access. What stands in: a register of organization Spaces and of approved servers kept by process.

original.mechanism: Organisation-owned Spaces with role-based sharing; enterprise custom agents and the Agent apps policy; no registry for Spaces
original.note: Anyone with a Copilot licence, including Free, can create a Space; there is no dedicated Spaces policy on the pages fetched — only visibility settings per Space.

steps.title: Prefer organisation-owned Spaces
body: Create shared Spaces under the organisation so access is admin / editor / viewer by member rather than public or user-by-user.

controls.mechanism: No discovery report of personal or unmanaged accounts; plan-specific Copilot endpoints (*.individual.githubcopilot.com) and personal github.com sign-ins are what an SSE or CASB sees

evidence.title: Copilot subscription-based network routing (plan endpoints)
Restricting access to GitHub.com using a corporate proxy (blocked-attempt audit event)

controls.note: External by the shadow-AI rule on this drawing: GitHub lists no personal or unmanaged accounts on the organisation's domains. An SSE or CASB finds personal-plan Copilot from traffic to *.individual.githubcopilot.com and sign-ins to personal github.com accounts. Credited as prevention only: with Enterprise Managed Users the sec-GitHub-allowed-enterprise header blocks personal accounts on the proxied network, and each block logs business.proxy_security_header_unsatisfied with no actor (IP only when enabled) — a count of attempts, not a list of accounts.

original.mechanism: No vendor feature; personal Copilot accounts on github.com are invisible to the enterprise

evidence.title: Vendor docs index, reviewed for the integration point (2026-09-10)

controls.mechanism: Enterprise audit log (180 days, streamable): Copilot policy, licence and content-exclusion changes (action:copilot) and agent activity (actor:Copilot, actor_is_agent, agent_session_id); Copilot Usage Records Streaming and API (request and response bodies; Enterprise Managed Users and data-residency enterprises, public preview) whose documented clients do not name Chat on github.com; no export of chat conversations

steps.title: Stream the audit log to your SIEM
body: Enterprise > Settings > Audit log > Log streaming: configure a destination, since the audit log keeps only 180 days on GitHub.

steps.title: Watch Copilot configuration and agent sessions
body: Search action:copilot for policy, licence and content-exclusion changes and actor:Copilot for the cloud agent sessions a chat starts; client prompts are not recorded.

steps.title: Turn on Copilot usage records where eligible
body: Enterprise > AI Controls > Copilot: set "Copilot Usage Records Streaming" (and "Copilot Usage Records API") to Enabled everywhere, then test whether chat on github.com records arrive.

controls.note: Partial by the telemetry rule on this drawing: what GitHub exports for this product is the control plane and the agent sessions a chat starts; the audit log "does not include client session data, such as the prompts". No documented export carries Chat on github.com or Mobile conversations: the usage-records endpoint (bodies with user_id and endpoint; Enterprise Managed Users and data residency only; preview) lists the cloud agent on github.com, the CLI and IDEs among its clients but not Chat on github.com, so its coverage of chat must be tested. Whether a GitHub MCP skill run from chat (branch, push, merge) is flagged actor_is_agent or logged as the user's ordinary git and pull_request event is not documented. Capture is not tamper resistance.

original.mechanism: Audit log records policy, licensing and Memory administration events (180 days, streamable); chat prompts are not logged

steps.title: Stream policy and licensing events
body: Filter action:copilot in the enterprise audit log and stream to a SIEM; client and chat prompts are not recorded.

controls.mechanism: The Copilot in the cloud policy disabled at enterprise level (it replaced the Copilot cloud agent, Copilot Chat in GitHub and Copilot Chat in GitHub Mobile policies); licence unassignment (enterprise: immediate; organization: end of billing cycle); the enterprise "Block Copilot cloud agent" toggle under AI controls > Agents > Copilot in the cloud; an empty managed allowedMcpServers list for MCP servers and connectors in cloud sandbox sessions

steps.title: Disable chat at enterprise scope
body: Enterprise > AI controls > Copilot > Configure features & clients: set Copilot in the cloud to Disabled everywhere rather than letting organizations decide; it switches off chat on github.com and Mobile and cloud sessions together.

steps.title: Pull licences where it must be immediate
body: Unassign the licence in the enterprise settings or remove the user from the licensed enterprise team (immediate); organization-level revocation only takes effect at the next billing cycle.

steps.title: Stop hand-offs to the cloud agent
body: Enterprise > AI controls > Agents > Available agents > Copilot in the cloud: toggle "Block Copilot cloud agent in all repositories owned by ENTERPRISE-NAME"; a session already running stops only with Stop session.

controls.note: Downgraded from native to partial on the kill-switch rule: the administrator can switch the surface off enterprise-wide, but the docs do not say what happens to a response or MCP skill action already in flight or how fast a policy change reaches an open chat — delay not documented. Licence removal is immediate only from the enterprise; organization-level revocation, like disabling Copilot for an organization, lasts to the end of the billing cycle, so the policy is the fast lever. Connectors and MCP servers a user added are cut by emptying allowedMcpServers in cloud sandbox sessions. Within one enterprise only an enterprise-level setting is certain (a delegated policy resolves to the least restrictive organization); across enterprises the most restrictive wins. A cloud agent session started from chat keeps running until someone stops it from the session log (toolCopilotCloudAgent). The enterprise block toggle sits under Copilot in the cloud but is labelled for the cloud agent; GitHub does not say whether people licensed elsewhere lose chat over the enterprise's repositories. Stored conversations remain after disable.

original.mechanism: Copilot in GitHub.com policy Disabled everywhere (unified policy from 2026-09-28); seat removal; Memory policy Disabled everywhere with bulk delete

steps.title: Disable at enterprise scope
body: Set Copilot in GitHub.com to Disabled everywhere; across enterprises the most restrictive policy applies, within one enterprise set it at enterprise level.

steps.title: Purge Memory
body: Set Copilot Memory to Disabled everywhere and use Delete user memories in bulk.

original.note: The policy applies at the next request; a hand-off already running in the cloud agent is stopped from that agent's session log, not from the chat policy.

settings.name: Require SAML authentication
settings.where: Enterprise › Settings › Authentication security › SAML single sign-on
settings.recommended: On, with MFA enforced on the GitHub app in your IdP (Enterprise Managed Users sign in through the IdP by design)
settings.why: Chat reads organisation repositories only with a current SSO session, so a leaver's or lapsed account cannot keep asking questions of client code.

settings.name: Assign licenses (Enterprise Teams)
settings.where: Enterprise › Billing and licensing › Licensing › Copilot › Manage › Enterprise Teams › Assign licenses
settings.recommended: Licences assigned to enterprise teams synced from the IdP group that grants Copilot
settings.why: Joining or leaving the IdP group grants or removes the seat, so a leaver loses Copilot with their account rather than with a ticket.

settings.name: Copilot in the cloud
settings.where: Enterprise › AI controls › Copilot › Configure features & clients
settings.recommended: Enabled for selected organizations, chosen at enterprise level
settings.why: This one policy now gates chat on github.com and GitHub Mobile as well as cloud sessions; Disabled everywhere removes them for every seat you license.

settings.name: Enable enterprise access restrictions
settings.where: Enterprise › Settings › Authentication security › Enterprise access restrictions; your proxy injects the sec-GitHub-allowed-enterprise header
settings.recommended: On, with the header injected by your break-and-inspect proxy on github.com, api.github.com and *.githubcopilot.com
settings.why: On the corporate network Copilot works only with accounts your enterprise owns, so client code cannot leave under a personal or another company's licence.

settings.name: Base permissions
settings.where: Organization › Settings › Member privileges › Base permissions
settings.recommended: No permission, with access granted through teams per engagement
settings.why: Chat retrieves as the requesting user, so every repository a member can read by default is one chat will summarise for them; internal repositories stay readable regardless.

settings.name: Custom properties
settings.where: Organization › Settings › Repository › Custom properties
settings.recommended: A required data-classification property (for example public, internal, client-confidential) on every repository
settings.why: Gives you an inventory of which repositories hold client data, which content exclusion and rulesets can then target.

settings.name: Content exclusion
settings.where: Enterprise › AI controls › Copilot › Content exclusion (also organisation and repository Settings › Copilot › Content exclusion)
settings.recommended: Secret and key-material paths ("*.pem", "*.key", "**/.env*", "secrets*") and client-restricted repositories, set at enterprise level
settings.why: Excluded files are not used to answer questions on github.com or in GitHub Mobile; third-party MCP servers are not bound by it.

settings.name: Copilot can search the web
settings.where: Enterprise › AI controls › Copilot › Configure features & clients
settings.recommended: Enabled
settings.why: Web grounding is part of the tool's value; the generated queries leave for the search provider, so regulated teams disable it at enterprise level.

settings.name: MCP servers in Copilot
settings.where: Enterprise › AI controls › MCP
settings.recommended: Enabled everywhere, with allowedMcpServers restricting which servers run
settings.why: Cloud sandbox sessions started from chat can use repository and personal MCP servers and Copilot connectors; Disabled removes all of them, GitHub's advice is to keep it on and restrict it.

settings.name: allowedMcpServers
settings.where: copilot/managed-settings.json in the enterprise's .github-private repository → allowedMcpServers
settings.recommended: Your approved servers matched by serverUrl or serverCommand, plus the connector URLs you allow
settings.why: In cloud sandbox sessions a server or connector not on the list never starts; sessions on GitHub Actions don't read it, and the registry restriction does not apply to cloud sessions.

settings.name: Require a pull request before merging
settings.where: Organization or repository ruleset › Branch rules, targeting the default branch
settings.recommended: On, with at least one approving review
settings.why: Chat's write skills (create or update files, push, merge) still meet the branch's review requirement, so a confirmed chat action cannot land unreviewed code.

settings.name: OAuth app access restrictions
settings.where: Organization › Settings › Third-party access › OAuth app policy
settings.recommended: On; approve each OAuth app on request
settings.why: Another chat product's GitHub connector reaches organisation data only after an owner approves its OAuth app.

settings.name: Require approval of fine-grained personal access tokens
settings.where: Enterprise › Policies › Personal access tokens › Fine-grained tokens
settings.default: Allow organizations to configure approval requirements
settings.recommended: Require approval
settings.why: A token a user pastes into another AI tool reaches organisation repositories only after an owner approves it.

settings.name: Set maximum lifetimes for personal access tokens
settings.where: Enterprise › Policies › Personal access tokens › Fine-grained tokens and Tokens (classic)
settings.default: 366 days for fine-grained tokens; none for classic
settings.recommended: 90 days for both token types
settings.why: Tokens used for Copilot administration and pasted into other AI tools expire instead of living for a year, or for ever with classic tokens.

settings.name: Audit log streaming
settings.where: Enterprise › Settings › Audit log › Log streaming
settings.recommended: On, to your SIEM
settings.why: Copilot policy, licence and content-exclusion changes and agent activity (actor:Copilot) outlive GitHub's 180 days; chat transcripts are not in it.

settings.name: Copilot Usage Records Streaming
settings.where: Enterprise › AI controls › Copilot › Copilot Usage Records Streaming
settings.recommended: Enabled everywhere, into the audit-log stream, readable only by your investigations team
settings.why: Request and response bodies of Copilot API calls reach your SIEM; GitHub's pages do not say chat on github.com is covered, so confirm it in your stream.
settings.requires: Enterprise Managed Users or data residency (public preview)
