tools.name: GitHub Copilot CLI

variants.name: Copilot CLI (GA 2026-02-25)
GitHub Copilot app (desktop, GA 2026-06-17; same managed-settings plane, own policy since 2026-07-27)
Copilot in Windows Terminal (Canary; governed by the Copilot CLI policy)

summary: Copilot CLI is the terminal-native coding agent (plan mode, autopilot, built-in Explore / Task / Code Review / Plan agents, /fleet parallel sessions, hooks, plugins, MCP) and the runtime behind the GitHub Copilot desktop app, the SDK and JetBrains agent mode. It runs on the developer's machine with the developer's GitHub identity; inference goes to the Copilot API by plan, or straight to a provider under local BYOK.

Prompts, file contents and tool output leave the device for the Copilot API; session data (prompts, responses, tools, files changed) is written to ~/.copilot/session-state and synced to the user's GitHub account only where the "Store local sessions in the Cloud" policy is at least "View from cloud" (unconfigured keeps it local for Business and Enterprise seats). Remote steering exposes the session to github.com and GitHub Mobile. Nothing reaches the organisation's audit log except policy changes.

The admin plane is managed-settings.json: server-managed from the .github-private repository (copilot/managed-settings.json, with team overrides), MDM (HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\GitHubCopilot, com.github.copilot) or a root-owned file. It carries deny / ask / allow permissions with Shell, Read, Edit and Domain selectors (GA 2026-09-09), disableBypassPermissionsMode, allowedMcpServers / deniedMcpServers, plugin marketplaces, the MXC local sandbox policy, OpenTelemetry export and remote-control mode.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: All Copilot plans; Business and Enterprise gate it with the Copilot CLI policy (Enterprise > AI controls > Copilot > Configure features & clients > Clients), and the desktop app with its own GitHub Copilot app policy.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Copilot API per plan; enterprise-enabled models only; local BYOK (OpenAI, Azure, Anthropic, Ollama) bypasses GitHub; enterprise BYOK models are served by the Copilot API.

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: Prompts and tool output to the Copilot API; session data synced to the GitHub account only where the "Store local sessions in the Cloud" policy allows it and remoteExport is not false; OTLP telemetry only where the enterprise configures it; remote-steering traffic to github.com.

facts.label: Data retention / training
facts.value: Business and Enterprise prompts are not used for training; model providers run under ZDR except Claude Fable 5 / 5.1 (retain by default, exemption available through end-2026).

facts.label: Sandboxes
facts.value: Local sandbox uses Microsoft eXecution Container (MXC: Seatbelt on macOS 15+, bubblewrap on Linux, a recent Windows 11 build on Windows — GitHub's CLI reference names the Windows backend ProcessContainer, its local-sandboxing page BaseContainer); cloud sandboxes are isolated, ephemeral GitHub-hosted Linux environments with no access setting of their own — the Copilot in the cloud policy (enabled by default) decides whether members can use them.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: Copilot CLI how-tos (install, authenticate, allowing tools, hooks, MCP, plugins, administer for your enterprise).

items.title: Managed settings — delivery and precedence
body: Server-managed: an organisation in the enterprise hosts .github-private with copilot/managed-settings.json (legacy .github/copilot/settings.json still read); copilot/team-mappings.json and copilot/teams/*.json let named teams relax keys the enterprise marks { "overridable": ... }. Clients refresh within about an hour, or on restart. MDM and local-file delivery exist for machines that must not depend on the server channel; the CLI falls back to its cached copy when a fetch fails.

Keys the CLI honours: permissions.deny / ask / allow, permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode, model, enabledPlugins / extraKnownMarketplaces / strictKnownMarketplaces, allowedMcpServers / deniedMcpServers, telemetry.*, remoteControl and sandbox.* — sandbox applies to the CLI and the app (not VS Code), the app ignores telemetry, the cloud agent honours only model and plugin keys.

items.title: Permission model and its escape hatches
body: Read-only operations run without asking; edits, destructive shell commands and URL fetches prompt. Per-repo approvals persist in ~/.copilot/permissions-config.json and allowed URLs in ~/.copilot/settings.json. --allow-all / --yolo, /allow-all, --allow-all-tools and autopilot remove the prompts; deny rules still win. The managed file removes these options with disableBypassPermissionsMode and pins its own deny / ask / allow.

Policy hooks — root-owned, machine-wide, immune to disableAllHooks — run preToolUse (fail-closed on error, fail-open on timeout) and permissionRequest with a permissionDecision of allow, deny or ask; HTTP hooks for those events must be https.

items.title: Local sandbox policy
body: Deny-by-default filesystem: read/write, read-only and denied paths, with automatic grants for the working directory, PATH toolchains and package caches that managed settings can switch off (addCurrentWorkingDirectory, allowDevToolAccess). Network allowOutbound / allowLocalNetwork and an HTTP proxy; auth.git / auth.gh credential injection (formerly gitAuth / ghAuth) and macOS keychainAccess are separate switches. Managed values combine in the most restrictive direction; built-in file tools are software-checked only and remote MCP servers are outside the policy.

links.title: Understanding filesystem policies for local sandboxing

riskNotes.note: Autopilot and --yolo exist by design; CVE-2026-29783 showed the read-only classifier itself could be tricked by bash parameter expansion. disableBypassPermissionsMode plus a managed sandbox is the only configuration where a bad tool call is contained rather than merely prompted.

Repository files, MCP responses and hook output all feed the agent; the vendor's fix for CVE-2026-29783 added parse-time blocking and prompt hardening but no classifier. Domain() deny rules and sandbox allowOutbound=false bound the exfiltration path.

Session transcripts sync to github.com wherever the policy allows it and remote steering publishes them to the agents list; OTLP captureContent can also carry prompts. Decide the "Store local sessions in the Cloud" policy and lockCaptureContent explicitly.

Plugins and MCP servers install by name from marketplaces and npx commands; only strictKnownMarketplaces and the managed allowlist (URL and stdio command match) bound the sources — the registry restriction is name-only and bypassable.

controls.mechanism: GitHub's own second-factor requirement (Enterprise > Settings > Authentication security > "Require two-factor authentication for the enterprise and all of its organizations", optionally "Only allow secure two-factor methods") plus the device-delivered managed key forceLoginOrgs, which pins the CLI to the organization's accounts and refuses personal accounts and BYOK/API-key sign-in

steps.title: Require two-factor authentication for every organization
body: Enterprise > Settings > Authentication security: select "Require two-factor authentication for the enterprise and all of its organizations" and "Only allow secure two-factor methods"; members without 2FA cannot reach organization resources until they enable it. Not available to Enterprise Managed Users, whose second factor is the IdP's.

steps.title: Pin the CLI to your organizations
body: Deliver forceLoginOrgs (an array of organization logins) through MDM (com.github.copilot plist, HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\GitHubCopilot) or a root-owned managed-settings.json: Copilot then runs only for an account in a listed organization, refuses personal accounts, other enterprises and BYOK/API-key authentication, and fails closed if the policy cannot be read.

steps.title: Bound the tokens that skip the second factor
body: Enterprise > Policies > Personal access tokens: set "Set maximum lifetimes for personal access tokens", require approval of fine-grained tokens and restrict classic tokens.

controls.note: Native by the rule applied to every vendor: GitHub's identity layer requires a second factor for every organization member and forceLoginOrgs pins the client to the organization account (MDM or file channel only — the server-managed channel reaches only accounts already signed in, so unmanaged devices are not pinned). With Enterprise Managed Users the 2FA policy is unavailable: MFA is the IdP's and, per GitHub, enforced only at IdP sign-in. Non-interactive paths that skip the second factor once issued: the OAuth token (gho_) kept in the OS keychain, whose lifetime "depend[s] on how the token was created"; fine-grained PATs with the Copilot Requests account permission and GitHub App user tokens (ghu_) read from COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN / GH_TOKEN / GITHUB_TOKEN; and the gh CLI token fallback. forceLoginOrgs still requires those accounts to belong to a listed organization; whether the PAT lifetime and restriction policies govern the Copilot Requests permission is not documented.

original.mechanism: Copilot seat plus the Copilot CLI policy (and the separate GitHub Copilot app policy); OAuth device/browser flow or a fine-grained PAT with the Copilot Requests permission; SAML SSO authorisation per organisation

steps.title: Enable the CLI for the right organisations
body: Enterprise > AI controls > Copilot > Configure features & clients > Clients: set Copilot CLI to Enabled everywhere, Disabled everywhere or Let organizations decide; users still need an assigned seat.

steps.title: Set the desktop app policy separately
body: Since 2026-07-27 the GitHub Copilot app has its own policy under AI Controls > Copilot Clients (default Enabled everywhere); it no longer follows the CLI policy.

steps.title: Constrain how the CLI authenticates
body: OAuth tokens (gho_) and fine-grained PATs (github_pat_, Copilot Requests permission) are accepted; classic PATs are not. Tokens live in the OS keychain with a plaintext fallback at ~/.copilot/config.json; SSO-protected organisations require Authorize at login.

controls.mechanism: managed-settings.json permissions.deny / ask / allow with Shell(), Read(), Edit() / Write() and Domain() selectors; root-owned policy hooks (preToolUse, permissionRequest) in /etc/github-copilot/policy.d/ or HKLM\Software\Policies\GitHub\Copilot

steps.title: Write the managed permission rules
body: Under permissions set deny (blocks from any source), ask (fresh approval every time; bypass, auto-approval, hooks and saved grants cannot satisfy it) and allow (intersection across sources) with Shell(...), Read(...), Edit(...) and Domain(...) selectors; any managed rule makes unmatched operations default to ask.

steps.title: Add a machine-wide policy hook
body: Deploy a root-owned JSON file in /etc/github-copilot/policy.d/ (Windows C:\ProgramData\GitHub\Copilot\policy.d\ or HKLM\Software\Policies\GitHub\Copilot) whose preToolUse hook returns permissionDecision "deny"; errors and exit code 2 deny, timeouts fail open, and disableAllHooks cannot switch policy hooks off.

controls.note: Native by the rule applied to every vendor: admin-delivered, user-proof deny/ask/allow rules over shell commands (including redirection and sed -i writes), file paths and network domains are evaluated before each call, and an admin-locked pre-tool hook can deny any tool, MCP tools included (managed selectors do not name MCP tools). The hook is an integration point whose logic the organisation writes: command hooks fail closed on error but open on timeout, and HTTP preToolUse hooks fail open on any error, so set timeoutSec and prefer command hooks. Remote MCP servers' own actions are outside both; decisions reach telemetry only as hook span events.

original.mechanism: managed-settings.json permissions.deny / ask / allow with Shell(), Read(), Edit(), Domain() selectors (GA 2026-09-09); root-owned policy hooks on preToolUse / permissionRequest

steps.title: Write the managed permission rules
body: Under permissions set deny (blocked from any source), ask (fresh approval every time, bypass cannot satisfy) and allow (intersection across sources) with Shell(...) / Bash(...) / PowerShell(...), Read(path), Edit(path) / Write(path) and Domain(host) selectors; mark team-relaxable keys { "overridable": ... }.

steps.title: Add a machine-wide policy hook
body: Deploy a root-owned policy hook file; a preToolUse hook returning permissionDecision "deny" blocks the call, errors and exit code 2 deny (fail-closed), timeouts fail open — set timeoutSec accordingly. disableAllHooks cannot switch policy hooks off.

original.note: Managed permissions are deterministic; policy hooks are an integration point whose logic the organisation writes and must fail closed. Remote MCP servers' own actions are outside both.

controls.mechanism: No vendor feature; the organisation's TPRM platform assesses GitHub and each model provider from the GitHub Copilot Trust Center and the model-hosting page

evidence.title: GitHub Copilot Trust Center (compliance reports; most documents behind Request access)
Hosting of models for GitHub Copilot (providers and retention terms)

controls.note: External: the organisation's TPRM platform owns the assessment. Rendered in a browser on 2026-09-25 the trust center lists SOC 1, SOC 2 and SOC 3 (SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 reports), ISO 27001:2013, ISO/IEC 42001:2023, CSA STAR Level 2, TISAX, a 2026 CAIQ, a PCI DSS AOC and bug-bounty letters, most behind Request access; no penetration-test summary is listed. Model providers: Azure, AWS Bedrock, Anthropic, Google Cloud, xAI, Azure AI Foundry and Fireworks, with Claude Fable 5 / 5.1 retaining prompts by default (ZDR exemption through end-2026). Local BYOK in the CLI "is not controlled by enterprise policies" and changes the subprocessor set per developer; forceLoginOrgs, which refuses BYOK/API-key sign-in, is the lever that keeps it off managed devices.

original.mechanism: No vendor feature; model-hosting page and provider ZDR terms are the assessment inputs
original.note: Local BYOK changes the subprocessor set per developer — disable it through the "Enable custom models" policy if the vendor assessment did not cover the providers.

steps.title: Record model providers and retention terms
body: Enumerate hosting per model (Azure, AWS Bedrock, Anthropic, GCP, xAI, Fireworks) and the Claude Fable 5 / 5.1 retention exception.

controls.mechanism: Policy hooks that can rewrite or deny prompt and tool traffic (userPromptTransformed, preToolUse modifiedArgs, postToolUse modifiedResult); built-in redaction of GITHUB_TOKEN / COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN values from output and --secret-env-vars; content exclusion and Read() denies as data minimisation

steps.title: Hand prompt and tool traffic to your inspector
body: In a root-owned policy hook, return modifiedTransformedPrompt from userPromptTransformed with secrets masked, and have preToolUse and postToolUse call your DLP service and deny or return modifiedArgs / modifiedResult.

steps.title: Redact named secrets from tool environments
body: Start sessions with --secret-env-vars=VAR,... to redact those variables from shell and MCP server environments; GITHUB_TOKEN and COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN values are redacted from output by default.

steps.title: Keep secret files out of context
body: Set enterprise, organization and repository content-exclusion rules, and test them in the CLI before relying on them: the CLI administration page says they apply ("Excluded files are not used as context"), while the content-exclusion how-to says Copilot CLI does not support content exclusion. Back them with managed Read(...) denies.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: the CLI detects no secrets or PII in prompts or tool traffic itself. It masks two named token values and, per session, variables the user names with --secret-env-vars (a flag, not a managed key), and its policy hooks are an inline attach point that can block or rewrite traffic once the organisation attaches a detector (userPromptSubmitted config-file hooks cannot change the prompt; userPromptTransformed can). Content exclusion and managed Read(...) denies are path filtering, credited as data minimisation; GitHub's own pages contradict each other on content exclusion for the CLI — the CLI administration page, the content-exclusion concept table and the supported-surfaces table say it applies, the content-exclusion how-to says the CLI does not support it — so the Read(...) denies are the dependable half. The model still sees whatever the developer pastes. Local BYOK sends prompts straight to the configured provider.

original.mechanism: Content exclusion applies to the CLI and the app; Read() deny rules and sandbox deniedPaths keep files out of tools; telemetry.captureContent=false with lockCaptureContent
original.note: A context filter and path denies, not inspection: nothing scans the prompt stream for sensitive content, and the model still sees whatever the developer pastes.

steps.title: Deny secret paths to the agent's tools
body: Put Read(**/.env) and similar under permissions.deny; add the same paths to sandbox.userPolicy.filesystem.deniedPaths, which managed values add to rather than replace.

steps.title: Apply content exclusion and lock telemetry content
body: Enterprise and organisation content-exclusion rules apply to the CLI ("Excluded files are not used as context"); set telemetry.captureContent=false and lockCaptureContent=true so exports never carry prompts.

controls.mechanism: No classifier; a policy hook's postToolUse can replace a tool result before the model sees it

steps.title: Screen tool results with a post-tool hook
body: In a root-owned policy hook, have postToolUse send each result to your classifier and return modifiedResult (a replacement textResultForLlm) or a failure when it flags injected instructions; the hook runs for every tool unless a matcher narrows it.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: GitHub ships no classifier for repository files, MCP results or fetched pages; the post-tool hook is an attach point. The CLI's command safety analysis and the parse-time blocking added for CVE-2026-29783 judge proposed shell commands — action policy, not input screening — and web_fetch SSRF protection limits destinations, not content. Folder trust and MCP server trust levels are admission. An AI or MCP gateway classifier on the brokered path is the external complement.

original.mechanism: Vendor-side parse-time blocking of dangerous shell patterns and hardened system prompts (post CVE-2026-29783); userPromptSubmitted / preToolUse hooks; no classifier

steps.title: Keep the CLI current and add hook-based screening
body: Run >= 0.0.423 (the fix blocks ${var@P}-style expansions unconditionally); use policy hooks on userPromptSubmitted and preToolUse to screen or deny suspicious inputs and tool arguments.

original.note: Parse-time blocking detects a class of injected shell commands; the hooks are the attach point for a detector on prompts. Repository files, MCP results and fetched pages are not classified.

controls.mechanism: Managed permissions.deny / ask / allow with argument-scoped Shell(), Read(), Edit() and Domain() selectors; permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode; allowedMcpServers; session flags --deny-tool / --allow-tool / --available-tools with MyMCP(tool) patterns

steps.title: Remove the all-tools switches
body: Set permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode to "disable": --yolo, --allow-all, --allow-all-tools, --allow-all-paths and --allow-all-urls are suppressed at startup and /yolo and /allow-all are blocked.

steps.title: Scope shell, file and domain operations
body: Put Shell(git push *), Read(~/.ssh/**), Edit(//etc/**) and Domain(...) selectors under permissions.deny and permissions.ask; deny from any managed source blocks for every user.

steps.title: Scope MCP tools per session
body: Use --deny-tool / --allow-tool with MyMCP(tool) and --available-tools for scripted runs; deny rules beat allow even under --allow-all.

controls.note: Native by the rule applied to every vendor: admin-lockable deny/ask/allow with argument and path scoping for shell, file and network operations, with the bypass modes removable. MCP tools are scoped at server level by allowedMcpServers; per-tool MCP scoping is a user flag or a policy hook, not a managed selector. A server-managed disableBypassPermissionsMode is cleared by switching to an account that does not set it — deliver it by MDM or pin accounts with forceLoginOrgs; "allow-auto-only" keeps LLM-assisted approval, "disable" removes it.

original.mechanism: permissions.deny / allow selectors, disableBypassPermissionsMode, --available-tools / --excluded-tools, MCP tool-level selectors such as MyMCP(create_issue)

steps.title: Remove the all-tools switches
body: Set permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode to "disable": --yolo, --allow-all and /allow-all are suppressed and autopilot cannot skip approvals.

steps.title: Scope shell, write and MCP tools
body: Use shell(git:*), write(path) and MyMCP(tool) selectors in --allow-tool / --deny-tool or the managed rules; --available-tools restricts the agent to a named set and deny always beats allow, even under --allow-all.

original.note: --excluded-tools hides tools, allow selectors pre-approve, Shell()/Edit()/Read() specifiers limit arguments; MCP tools use MyMCP(tool) selectors. disableBypassPermissionsMode must be set or --allow-all overrides the rules.

controls.mechanism: Managed sandbox floor: sandbox.enabled, failIfUnavailable, allowBypass, sandboxMcpServers, sandboxLspServers and userPolicy.filesystem / network rules (MXC: Seatbelt, bubblewrap and a Windows 11 backend); cloud sandboxes for GitHub-hosted sessions, governed by the Copilot in the cloud policy. Credential paths: deny-by-default sandbox filesystem with managed sandbox.auth.git / sandbox.auth.gh=false (renamed from gitAuth / ghAuth), allowDevToolAccess=false, userPolicy.filesystem.deniedPaths and seatbelt.keychainAccess=false; managed Read() denies for built-in tools

steps.title: Make the local sandbox mandatory
body: Set sandbox.enabled=true, sandbox.failIfUnavailable=true and sandbox.allowBypass=false so --no-sandbox, /sandbox disable and per-command bypass prompts are refused and an unusable backend blocks execution; add sandboxMcpServers=true and sandboxLspServers=true.

steps.title: Narrow the filesystem policy
body: Set sandbox.addCurrentWorkingDirectory and sandbox.allowDevToolAccess as needed and pin sandbox.userPolicy.filesystem readwritePaths / readonlyPaths / deniedPaths; managed path grants only narrow the user's, and managed denied paths add to them.

steps.title: Decide on cloud sandboxes
body: Cloud sandboxes have no access setting of their own and cannot be disabled separately: the Copilot in the cloud policy (enabled by default) decides whether members can start sessions in them from any client, and a cloud sandbox budget limits their spend.

steps.title: Stop token injection into sandboxed commands
body: In the managed sandbox floor set auth.git=false and auth.gh=false so no Git or GitHub CLI credentials are injected into the sandbox; disabled credential injection cannot be re-enabled by the user.

steps.title: Keep credential stores unreachable
body: Set sandbox.allowDevToolAccess=false (package-registry tokens), add the SSH, cloud-CLI and browser-profile directories to sandbox.userPolicy.filesystem.deniedPaths, and keep sandbox.userPolicy.seatbelt.keychainAccess=false on macOS.

steps.title: Use narrow tokens for headless runs
body: For CI or scripted use pass a fine-grained PAT with only the Copilot Requests account permission in COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN rather than the developer's OAuth token.

controls.note: Native by the rule applied to every vendor: an administrator can require an OS-enforced sandbox around agent-run shell commands, searches and local MCP/LSP servers, covering filesystem and network, that the user cannot turn off and that fails closed. Public preview; macOS 15+ (Seatbelt), Linux with bubblewrap 0.5+, and Windows only on recent Windows 11 builds (25H2 with KB5124010 or 26H1 with KB5124006 or later), where support for denied paths, localhost connections and proxying depends on the Windows version. Outside the OS boundary: the CLI process itself, its built-in file tools (a software-only policy check), remote MCP servers and detached background commands, which cannot be sandboxed. The GitHub Copilot app honours the same managed sandbox key. Credential paths: with the managed sandbox required, credential paths are OS-denied to agent commands — the filesystem policy is deny-by-default, gh's stored credentials and the keychain are blocked, and token injection can be locked off. Both the managed-settings and the CLI configuration references now name the injection keys auth.git / auth.gh (renamed from gitAuth / ghAuth) — confirm the effective values with /sandbox policy. Still inherited: environment variables (unless the user passes --secret-env-vars), the unsandboxed CLI process with its own GitHub token and MCP OAuth tokens, remote MCP servers' credentials, built-in file tools (software check only), and whatever a bypassed or detached command reaches; ssh-agent socket access is not documented. On Windows deniedPaths cannot be used. No on-behalf-of exchange: the CLI acts as the signed-in developer.

original.mechanism: managed sandbox.* keys (enabled, failIfUnavailable, allowBypass, sandboxMcpServers, sandboxLspServers, userPolicy.filesystem / network / seatbelt); Cloud sandbox access policy
original.note: Public preview; requires macOS 15+, bubblewrap 0.5+ or recent Windows 11. Remote MCP servers and the built-in file tools sit outside the OS enforcement.

steps.title: Make the local sandbox mandatory
body: Set sandbox.enabled=true, sandbox.failIfUnavailable=true and sandbox.allowBypass=false so /sandbox disable, --no-sandbox and per-command bypass requests are refused; add sandboxMcpServers and sandboxLspServers=true.

steps.title: Narrow the filesystem and network policy
body: Set addCurrentWorkingDirectory and allowDevToolAccess as needed, pin userPolicy.filesystem readwritePaths / readonlyPaths / deniedPaths, and set userPolicy.network.allowOutbound and allowLocalNetwork; verify with /sandbox policy.

steps.title: Decide on cloud sandboxes
body: Enterprise > Policies > Sandboxes > Cloud sandbox access is Disabled by default; choose Let organizations enable or Enabled by default. Cloud sessions run on GitHub-hosted Azure Container Apps Sandboxes and are usage-billed.

original.mechanism: sandbox.gitAuth / ghAuth / sandbox.userPolicy.seatbelt.keychainAccess=false stop the developer's tokens reaching sandboxed commands; fine-grained PATs with only Copilot Requests for automation

steps.title: Stop token injection into sandboxed commands
body: Set sandbox.gitAuth=false and sandbox.ghAuth=false so the GitHub token is not exported into git HTTPS or gh inside the sandbox, and sandbox.userPolicy.seatbelt.keychainAccess=false on macOS.

steps.title: Use narrow tokens for headless runs
body: For CI or scripted use pass COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN / GH_TOKEN as a fine-grained PAT with only the Copilot Requests account permission rather than the developer's OAuth token.

original.note: Covers the developer's git and GitHub tokens and the keychain for sandboxed commands; remote MCP servers and unsandboxed commands still run with whatever the shell can reach. No on-behalf-of exchange — the CLI acts as the signed-in developer.

controls.mechanism: Copilot Memory policy (off by default for Business and Enterprise; repository facts validated against cited code before use; admin export / delete); "Store local sessions in the Cloud" policy; repository instruction files are not admin-lockable

steps.title: Set the Memory policy and keep the delete lever
body: Enterprise > AI controls > Copilot > Configure features & clients > Features > Copilot Memory: choose a policy. Export or delete user preferences per user (Export / Delete Copilot memories) or in bulk from Get usage report; repository admins review and delete repository facts.

steps.title: Decide whether session transcripts leave the device
body: Sessions sync only where the "Store local sessions in the Cloud" policy is at least "View from cloud"; disabled or unconfigured keeps them local, and enabling it does not give admins access.

steps.title: Deny memory writes where Memory stays on
body: The memory permission kind (--deny-tool=memory) blocks storing facts for a session; memory is off in prompt mode unless --enable-memory is passed.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: the administrator can disable Copilot Memory, repository facts are checked against their citations on the current branch before use and expire after 28 days unused, and admins can export or delete memories — but instruction sources cannot be locked: AGENTS.md, .github instruction, skill and hook files load from the checked-out tree, the managed keys include no customization lockdown, and --no-custom-instructions is a user flag. Policy hooks load before repository and user hooks and can observe, not pin, those sources. User preferences are confirmed by the model's judgement, not validated.

original.mechanism: Copilot Memory policy (repository facts and user preferences, 28-day unused expiry, admin export / delete); "Store local sessions in the Cloud" policy and remoteExport
original.note: Memory entries are validated against the current branch before use but there is no quarantine or rollback; an admin can only delete. The CLI uses Memory, the supported-surfaces table notwithstanding — treat the concept page as authoritative for scope.

steps.title: Set the Memory policy and keep the delete lever
body: Enterprise > AI controls > Copilot > Configure features & clients > Features > Copilot Memory: Enabled / Disabled / Let organizations decide. Export or delete a user's memories from Organization Settings > Copilot > Access (Export / Delete Copilot memories) or in bulk from Get usage report.

steps.title: Decide whether session transcripts leave the device

body.Sessions sync to the GitHub account by d: false, and the organisation controls availability with the "Store local sessions in the Cloud" policy. Enabling it does not give admins access to the data.

original.mechanism: Enterprise custom agents, custom instructions, strictKnownMarketplaces; repository .github instruction and hook files remain writable by contributors
original.note: Repository-level instructions, skills and hooks are loaded from the checked-out tree; the CLI loads policy files before repository, user and plugin sources so a policy hook can screen them, but there is no version pin.

steps.title: Prefer enterprise custom agents and policy hooks
body: Publish enterprise custom agents (available to the CLI) and deploy machine-wide policy hooks, which load ahead of repository and user hooks.

controls.mechanism: OS keychain storage (service copilot-cli; plaintext config.json only when storeTokenPlaintext allows it); forceLoginOrgs refuses BYOK/API-key authentication; PAT lifetime policies; no rotation of the OAuth token

steps.title: Keep credentials in the keychain
body: Ensure Keychain Access, Credential Manager or libsecret is available; without one the CLI offers to store the token in plaintext in ~/.copilot/config.json.

steps.title: Forbid static provider keys on managed devices
body: Deliver forceLoginOrgs by MDM or managed-settings.json so BYOK/API-key authentication is refused; storeTokenPlaintext (plaintext tokens in config.json) defaults to false.

steps.title: Cap personal access token lifetime
body: Enterprise > Policies > Personal access tokens: set "Set maximum lifetimes for personal access tokens" and require approval of fine-grained tokens.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: the GitHub token and MCP OAuth tokens and secrets are keychain-backed (file fallbacks when no keychain exists), and forceLoginOrgs lets an admin forbid static provider keys, but the interactive OAuth token is long-lived with no documented rotation, and whether PAT lifetime policies govern the Copilot Requests permission is not documented. Secret values are kept out of model context only for GITHUB_TOKEN / COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN (redacted from output by default) and variables named with --secret-env-vars; environment variables otherwise reach unsandboxed commands and MCP servers.

original.mechanism: OS keychain storage for the GitHub token (plaintext ~/.copilot/config.json fallback); sandbox deniedPaths and Read() deny rules for secret files; no vault integration

steps.title: Keep credentials in the keychain
body: Ensure a keychain (Keychain Access, Credential Manager, libsecret) is available; without one the token is stored in plaintext in ~/.copilot/config.json.

steps.title: Deny secret files to tools and the sandbox
body: Add .env and credential paths to permissions.deny (Read / Edit) and to sandbox.userPolicy.filesystem.deniedPaths.

original.note: Storage only: the GitHub token sits in the keychain or, as a fallback, in plaintext config; nothing issues short-lived credentials for tools. Deny rules keep named secret files out of tools; environment variables remain readable by unsandboxed commands.

controls.mechanism: allowedMcpServers / deniedMcpServers (serverName, serverUrl with wildcards and canonicalisation, exact serverCommand; malformed lists block all); enterprise allowlist fingerprinting of command, arguments and URL; sandboxMcpServers; registry restriction (preview, name-matched)

steps.title: Publish the allowlist and denylist
body: In copilot/managed-settings.json add allowedMcpServers (omit = allow all, [] = block all but built-ins) with serverUrl or serverCommand entries — pin package versions inside serverCommand — and deniedMcpServers (always wins); entries with unresolved variables are blocked.

steps.title: Run local MCP servers inside the sandbox
body: Set sandbox.sandboxMcpServers=true so stdio servers inherit the filesystem and network policy; remote servers do not run in the local sandbox.

steps.title: Treat the registry as discovery only
body: The custom registry (CLI 1.0.11+) enforces "Registry only" by server name/ID, which can be bypassed by editing configuration files.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: an allowlist admits servers but pins nothing they serve. The CLI fingerprints each server's command, arguments and URL and blocks unapproved ones fail-closed, but nothing hashes tool definitions or re-gates a server whose tools change (the tool snapshot cache is replaced by live discovery). Exact serverCommand matching that includes a pinned package version is version pinning for stdio servers only; remote servers stay unpinned, and built-in first-party servers are exempt. An MCP gateway supplies definition scanning and pinning.

original.mechanism: allowedMcpServers / deniedMcpServers (serverName, serverUrl with wildcards and canonicalisation, serverCommand exact match; fail-closed with an empty allowlist); sandboxMcpServers; registry restriction (preview, bypassable)

steps.title: Publish the allowlist and denylist
body: In copilot/managed-settings.json add allowedMcpServers (omit = allow all, [] = block all but built-ins) and deniedMcpServers (always wins); entries with unresolved variables are blocked. Prerequisites: MCP servers in Copilot enabled, registry restriction set to Allow all.

steps.title: Run local MCP servers inside the sandbox
body: Set sandbox.sandboxMcpServers=true so stdio servers inherit the filesystem and network policy; remote servers remain outside it.

steps.title: Treat the registry as discovery only
body: The custom registry (CLI 1.0.11+) shows approved servers but its Registry only mode matches by name/ID and can be bypassed by editing configuration files.

original.note: Admission by identity: allowedMcpServers and deniedMcpServers, fail-closed when empty; the registry restriction is discovery and can be bypassed by editing configuration. Admission is not integrity — nothing pins the tool descriptions a server returns or detects a changed implementation.

controls.mechanism: Managed permissions.ask (fresh approval that bypass, auto-approval, hooks and saved grants cannot satisfy) and permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode "disable"; remoteControl.mode for who may answer prompts remotely

steps.title: Force approval on privileged operations
body: Put Shell(git push *), Edit(/.github/**) and Domain(...) selectors under permissions.ask; each matching call needs a fresh one-time human approval.

steps.title: Remove the modes that skip approval
body: Set permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode to "disable" (not "allow-auto-only", which keeps LLM-assisted approval); deliver it by MDM, since a server-managed value is cleared when the user switches to an account that does not set it.

steps.title: Decide who may answer prompts remotely
body: remoteControl.mode = "disabled" prevents remote control of sessions on the device; "requireSSO" with githubDotComOrganizations limits it to SSO-authorised clients.

controls.note: Native by the rule applied to every vendor: a present person approves each prompted action seeing the exact command, path or URL; the admin can force approval for named shell, file and domain operations and remove bypass, allow-all and LLM-assisted modes (autopilot then auto-denies anything that needs permission). Boundaries: saved "This location" and "Always" approvals and permissionRequest hooks still pre-approve operations that no managed ask names, and MCP tool calls cannot be named in a managed ask (they prompt by default, and users can persist approval). Delegation to the cloud agent (/delegate) ends in a pull request — a merge gate, not action approval.

settings.name: Require SAML authentication
settings.where: Enterprise › Settings › Authentication security › SAML single sign-on
settings.recommended: On, with MFA enforced on the GitHub app in your IdP (Enterprise Managed Users sign in through the IdP by design)
settings.why: Every Copilot sign-in is bound to an IdP session and its MFA, and tokens without a current SSO authorization stop reaching organisation data.

settings.name: Assign licenses (Enterprise Teams)
settings.where: Enterprise › Billing and licensing › Licensing › Copilot › Manage › Enterprise Teams › Assign licenses
settings.recommended: Licences assigned to enterprise teams synced from the IdP group that grants Copilot
settings.why: Joining or leaving the IdP group grants or removes the seat, so a leaver loses Copilot with their account rather than with a ticket.

settings.name: forceLoginOrgs
settings.where: managed-settings.json delivered by MDM (plist, registry or file) → forceLoginOrgs
settings.recommended: ["your-org-login"] — your organisation logins
settings.why: On managed devices the CLI runs only for accounts in your organisations; personal accounts and BYOK or API-key sign-in are refused.

settings.name: Enable enterprise access restrictions
settings.where: Enterprise › Settings › Authentication security › Enterprise access restrictions; your proxy injects the sec-GitHub-allowed-enterprise header
settings.recommended: On, with the header injected by your break-and-inspect proxy on github.com, api.github.com and *.githubcopilot.com
settings.why: On the corporate network Copilot works only with accounts your enterprise owns, so client code cannot leave under a personal or another company's licence.

settings.name: Copilot CLI
settings.where: Enterprise › AI controls › Copilot › Configure features & clients › Clients
settings.recommended: Enabled everywhere, set at enterprise level rather than delegated
settings.why: A delegated policy lets the least restrictive organisation win; Disabled everywhere is the switch that stops the CLI for every seat (the Copilot app has its own policy).

settings.name: storeTokenPlaintext
settings.where: ~/.copilot/settings.json → storeTokenPlaintext
settings.recommended: false — don't enable it
settings.why: The OAuth token stays in the OS keychain; true writes it in plain text to config.json wherever no keychain exists, such as build servers and containers.

settings.name: Set maximum lifetimes for personal access tokens
settings.where: Enterprise › Policies › Personal access tokens › Fine-grained tokens and Tokens (classic)
settings.default: 366 days for fine-grained tokens; none for classic
settings.recommended: 90 days for both token types
settings.why: Tokens developers paste into MCP configs and environment files expire instead of living for a year, or for ever with classic tokens.

settings.name: Content exclusion
settings.where: Enterprise › AI controls › Copilot › Content exclusion (also organisation and repository Settings › Copilot › Content exclusion)
settings.recommended: Secret and key-material paths ("*.pem", "*.key", "**/.env*", "secrets*") and client-restricted repositories, set at enterprise level
settings.why: Excluded files are not used as context; GitHub's pages disagree on whether the CLI honours it, so test it before relying on it and pair it with Read() denies.

settings.name: MCP servers in Copilot
settings.where: Enterprise › AI controls › MCP
settings.recommended: Enabled everywhere, with allowedMcpServers restricting which servers run
settings.why: GitHub's advice is to keep MCP on and restrict it; Disabled blocks every non-default MCP server in the CLI.

settings.name: allowedMcpServers
settings.where: copilot/managed-settings.json in the enterprise's .github-private repository (or MDM) → allowedMcpServers
settings.recommended: Your approved servers matched by serverUrl or serverCommand, not serverName, plus the connector URLs you allow
settings.why: A server not on the list never starts, whichever way the session is started (-p, --acp, --server); the built-in GitHub server is exempt.

settings.name: Restrict MCP access to registry servers
settings.where: Enterprise › AI controls › MCP › MCP Registry URL and Restrict MCP access to registry servers
settings.recommended: Registry only, with a registry listing exactly the servers in allowedMcpServers
settings.why: A second, name-matched layer for discovery; the managed allowedMcpServers list is the boundary, since registry matching is bypassable by editing local config.

settings.name: strictKnownMarketplaces
settings.where: managed-settings.json → strictKnownMarketplaces
settings.recommended: Your organisation's marketplace repositories only
settings.why: Plugins, which bundle agents, hooks and MCP servers, install only from your marketplaces; setting the key also turns off the built-in ones.

settings.name: permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode
settings.where: managed-settings.json → permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode
settings.recommended: "disable"
settings.why: Neutralises --yolo, --allow-all and /allow-all at startup and in session; account switches cannot undo it, and an unrecognised value fails closed.

settings.name: permissions.deny
settings.where: managed-settings.json → permissions.deny
settings.recommended: Deny secret paths: Read(~/.ssh/**), Read(~/.aws/**), Read(./.env*), Edit(//etc/**)
settings.why: Managed deny rules win over every mode, user rule and shell redirection the CLI can parse, so keys never enter the context.

settings.name: permissions.ask
settings.where: managed-settings.json → permissions.ask
settings.recommended: Shell(git push *) and Shell(gh pr merge *)
settings.why: A fresh approval that allow-all, assisted approval, hooks and saved grants cannot satisfy, kept for actions that leave the machine.

settings.name: permissions.defaultMode
settings.where: managed-settings.json → permissions.defaultMode
settings.recommended: "manual" — developers may still pick assisted for a session
settings.why: New sessions start by asking before edits and commands, and this managed default outranks the user's defaultPermissionMode.

settings.name: features.computerUse
settings.where: managed-settings.json → features.computerUse
settings.recommended: false
settings.why: The agent cannot take over the desktop's mouse and keyboard, a reach that the shell, file and domain permission rules do not describe.

settings.name: Policy hooks
settings.where: /etc/github-copilot/policy.d/*.json (Windows: C:\ProgramData\GitHub\Copilot\policy.d or HKLM\Software\Policies\GitHub\Copilot)
settings.recommended: An admin-owned preToolUse hook denying secret-path reads and uploads to unapproved hosts, plus postToolUse logging and redaction
settings.why: Root-owned and machine-wide, loaded before user and repository hooks and immune to disableAllHooks; timeouts fail open, so it is one guard, not the only one.

settings.name: sandbox.enabled with sandbox.failIfUnavailable
settings.where: managed-settings.json → sandbox.enabled, sandbox.failIfUnavailable
settings.recommended: true / true
settings.why: Shell commands run under Seatbelt, Bubblewrap or ProcessContainer, and the CLI blocks model and tool execution if it cannot enforce one; allowBypass stays on for one-off approvals, which regulated teams turn off.

settings.name: sandbox.sandboxMcpServers
settings.where: managed-settings.json → sandbox.sandboxMcpServers
settings.default: On in the user's sandbox settings; not enforced
settings.recommended: true
settings.why: Local MCP servers inherit the sandbox's filesystem and network limits instead of running with the developer's full rights.

settings.name: sandbox.userPolicy.network.allowedHosts
settings.where: managed-settings.json → sandbox.userPolicy.network.allowedHosts
settings.recommended: Your source host, package mirror and approved internal hosts
settings.why: Sandboxed commands reach only listed hosts through the CLI's local proxy, so an injected curl to a paste site fails; Windows relies on programs honouring the proxy.

settings.name: permissions.limitTo
settings.where: managed-settings.json → permissions.limitTo
settings.recommended: Unset — web fetch stays open
settings.why: A closed-world domain list that allow-all cannot widen; regulated teams set it to their approved domains, at the cost of general web research.

settings.name: telemetry
settings.where: managed-settings.json → telemetry (enabled, endpoint, capture)
settings.recommended: enabled true to your OTLP collector, capture.identity true, every content class false
settings.why: Agent turns and tool calls reach your collector attributed to user and machine, without prompts or code in the pipeline.

settings.name: Audit log streaming
settings.where: Enterprise › Settings › Audit log › Log streaming
settings.recommended: On, to your SIEM
settings.why: Policy and licence changes affecting the CLI outlive GitHub's 180 days; local prompts and tool calls are not in the audit log, which is why telemetry is separate.

settings.name: Copilot Usage Records Streaming
settings.where: Enterprise › AI controls › Copilot › Copilot Usage Records Streaming
settings.recommended: Enabled everywhere, into the audit-log stream, readable only by your investigations team
settings.why: Request and response bodies of Copilot API calls reach your SIEM — the only server-side record of what an agent was asked and answered.
settings.requires: Enterprise Managed Users or data residency (public preview)

settings.name: Copilot Memory
settings.where: Enterprise › AI controls › Copilot › Configure features & clients › Features
settings.recommended: Let organizations decide — off unless an organisation opts in
settings.why: Stored preferences are injected into later sessions; repository facts are governed separately under Repository access, and /memory off disables both locally.

settings.name: Store local sessions in the Cloud
settings.where: Enterprise › AI controls › Copilot policies
settings.recommended: Disabled
settings.why: Synced CLI session history sits on GitHub under each user's personal account, where administrators can neither see nor delete it.

settings.name: remoteControl.mode
settings.where: managed-settings.json → remoteControl.mode
settings.recommended: "disabled"
settings.why: Nobody can steer a CLI session on a developer's machine, or answer its approval prompts, from another device; requireSSO is the option for teams that need it.

settings.name: forceRemoteSettingsRefresh
settings.where: managed-settings.json delivered by MDM or file → forceRemoteSettingsRefresh
settings.recommended: true
settings.why: The CLI starts only with current policy instead of a cache up to an hour old, so a tightened allowlist reaches every new session; Copilot is unavailable offline.

tools.name: GitHub Copilot cloud agent

variants.name: Copilot cloud agent (formerly "coding agent") and automations
Copilot code review (agentic; PR approval in public preview since 2026-09-01)
Partner coding agents — Anthropic Claude and OpenAI Codex (public preview)
Agent apps (partner GitHub Apps exposing agents; "Agent apps" policy)
GitHub Agentic Workflows (public preview; markdown compiled to a hardened .lock.yml)

summary: The cloud agent takes an issue, PR comment, chat hand-off or automation trigger and works in a GitHub-hosted cloud sandbox (the default where a client offers the choice) or an ephemeral GitHub Actions environment (59-minute hard limit) on a copilot/ branch, pushing a draft PR that a human must review and merge. Code review, partner agents (Claude, Codex), agent apps and Agentic Workflows run on the same Actions substrate and share its mitigations; automations re-run the agent on schedules and repository events.

Inference runs on the Copilot API against enterprise-enabled models; the runner talks to api.<plan>.githubcopilot.com behind an egress firewall that, by default, allows package registries and certificate authorities only. The GitHub MCP server is wired in with a read-only token scoped to the repository; other MCP servers run with whatever secrets the administrator places in the Agents secret type — and are used without approval prompts.

Governance is enterprise-first: the Copilot in the cloud policy (AI controls > Copilot > Configure features & clients; it replaced the separate cloud agent and Chat in GitHub policies) with Enabled for selected organizations (custom properties via REST), organisation and repository access controls, Actions workflow approval, validation tools (CodeQL, secret scanning, dependency review, Copilot review), runner type and the firewall. Sessions are visible at github.com/copilot/agents and in the audit log as actor:Copilot with agent_session_id.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: All paid Copilot plans; Business and Enterprise require the Copilot in the cloud policy (enabled by default). Billing is AI credits plus compute, with cloud sandbox and GitHub Actions compute drawing on the same monthly allowance; user-level budgets always hard-stop, organisation and enterprise budgets block only with "Stop usage when budget limit is reached" (off by default).

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Copilot API from the Actions runner (api.business / api.enterprise.githubcopilot.com); models per the enterprise Configure models policy; data-resident routing under the "Restrict Copilot to data residency compliant models" policy (+10% credits). Enterprise BYOK does not apply to the cloud agent.

facts.label: Data leaving the environment
facts.value: Repository contents, issue and PR text and tool output go to the Copilot API; outbound network from Bash tools is firewalled; MCP servers and copilot-setup-steps are not firewalled; session logs and commits persist on GitHub.

facts.label: Data retention / training
facts.value: Ephemeral environment destroyed after the session; each agent commit links permanently to its session logs (application card). GitHub does not use Copilot Business or Enterprise customer data to train AI models; provider terms are per model on the model-hosting page (OpenAI and xAI zero retention, Anthropic per its ZDR documentation, Google no training).

facts.label: Copilot in the cloud (from 2026-10-28)
facts.value: The Copilot in the cloud policy replaced the Copilot cloud agent, Copilot Chat in GitHub and Copilot Chat in GitHub Mobile policies, and repository opt-outs carried over. Sessions run in a cloud sandbox by default (cross-repository, resumable across clients, chat kept for the life of the account) or on GitHub Actions (one repository, setup steps and self-hosted runners, 28-day chat retention); policy and managed-settings coverage differs between the two.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: Cloud agent concepts: about, risks and mitigations, MCP, automations, access management.

items.title: Enablement, targeting and repository scope
body: Enterprise > AI controls > Copilot > Configure features & clients > Copilot in the cloud: enabled by default; Enabled for selected organizations (UI, or by custom property through the REST API), Disabled, or let organisations decide. Enabling it also makes cloud sandboxes available, and they cannot be disabled separately. Organisation owners then set Repository access (all or selected repositories); owners and users can opt individual repositories out. Only users with write access can trigger the agent, and automations ignore events from users without write access by default.

Third-party agents and agent apps are separate policies: disabling the cloud agent does not disable Claude or Codex agents, and the "Agent apps" policy gates partner apps installed in the enterprise's organisations. Content exclusion does not apply to third-party agents.

links.title: Enabling the cloud agent in your enterprise
Managing access to the cloud agent

items.title: The environment — setup steps, secrets, runners, firewall
body: .github/workflows/copilot-setup-steps.yml on the default branch (job name copilot-setup-steps; only steps, permissions, runs-on, services, snapshot and timeout-minutes are honoured; 59 minutes maximum) prepares the runner. Secrets and variables come only from the Agents type (repository or organisation Settings > Secrets and variables > Agents); COPILOT_MCP_* entries reach MCP servers only; Actions, Codespaces and Dependabot secrets are never exposed.

The firewall is on by default with a recommended allowlist (OS and language package registries, container registries, certificate authorities, Playwright browser hosts); organisations and repositories add domain or URL rules or disable it. It applies only to processes the agent starts through its Bash tools — not MCP servers, not setup steps. Blocked requests are reported in the PR body or a comment. Runners default to a standard GitHub-hosted runner; organisation owners can set a Runner type and stop repositories overriding it. Larger and self-hosted runners (Ubuntu x64 or Windows 64-bit; ephemeral single-use self-hosted runners recommended) need uploads.github.com, user-images.githubusercontent.com and api.<plan>.githubcopilot.com, and the firewall must be disabled on self-hosted runners.

links.title: Configure secrets and variables for the cloud agent
Configuring runners for the cloud agent in your organization

items.title: Output controls — workflow approval, validation, code review approvals
body: Repository Settings > Copilot > cloud agent: Validation tools (CodeQL, secret scanning, dependency advisories, Copilot code review; on by default) and Actions workflow approval (Require approval for workflow runs; keep it on — the docs warn about auto-running workflows on agent code). The agent cannot mark a PR ready, approve or merge; rulesets add one more approval when the PR is opened under the agent's app identity, and the requesting user cannot approve their own request.

Copilot code review can be authorised to approve PRs (public preview): enterprise "Allow Copilot to approve pull requests" is Disabled everywhere by default, organisations choose whether approvals count toward merge requirements, repositories can limit that to file-path globs.

links.title: Configuring settings for the cloud agent

riskNotes.note: Every trigger is attacker-reachable text (issues, PR bodies, comments, repository files). GitHub strips hidden characters and HTML comments before prompting and ignores non-write-access events for automations, but MCP tools run without approval, so an injection that reaches a write-capable MCP tool acts immediately.

The firewall covers only Bash-spawned processes; MCP servers and copilot-setup-steps have unrestricted egress, and Agents secrets are plain environment variables inside the runner. Put nothing in the Agents secret type that a compromised MCP server should not see.

Automations act under their creator's identity and cannot approve the resulting PRs; partner agents install as GitHub Apps (anthropic code agent, openai code agent) with their own permissions. Rulesets and the extra-approval rule are the boundary, not the agent.

steps.title: Deny by argument with a preToolUse hook

controls.mechanism: Draft pull request reviewed and merged by a person other than the requester; "Approve and run workflows" gate (repository Require approval for workflow runs, on by default); ruleset "Require an additional approval for unattributed Copilot pull requests"; enterprise "Allow Copilot to approve pull requests" (Disabled everywhere by default); no per-action approval inside the session

steps.title: Keep Copilot from approving
body: Enterprise > AI controls > Copilot code review > "Allow Copilot to approve pull requests": keep Disabled everywhere (the default); organisations otherwise decide "Count Copilot approvals toward merge requirements".

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every hosted product: a merge gate approves the output, not the actions. Every tool call, MCP call and network request in the session is pre-approved and has already happened when the reviewer arrives (a preToolUse "ask" is treated as deny because nobody is there to answer). The requester's own approval does not count toward required approvals, and workflows wait for a person. The workflow gate is a repository setting a repository administrator can turn off, not locked at organisation level. The automation "Full control" level for issue changes is, in GitHub's words, a workflow convenience and not a security control. Copilot code review approvals are an AI reviewer and never count as human approval here.

original.mechanism: Human review and merge of draft PRs; Actions workflow approval; ruleset extra approval for agent-opened PRs; code review approval policy off by default
original.note: The human gate is the pull request and the workflow-run approval; tool calls, network access and MCP actions taken while the agent produces the PR are not individually approved.

steps.title: Keep workflow approval on
body: Repository Settings > Copilot > cloud agent > Actions workflow approval: leave Require approval for workflow runs enabled so a user with write access must click Approve and run workflows.

steps.title: Keep the extra approval rule and required checks
body: Rulesets require one more approval when a PR is opened under the agent's app identity (enabled by default); the requester cannot approve, and branch protections apply.

steps.title: Decide whether Copilot may approve PRs
body: Enterprise > AI controls > Copilot code review > "Allow Copilot to approve pull requests" is Disabled everywhere by default; organisations decide whether approvals count toward merge requirements.

controls.mechanism: GitHub strips hidden characters and HTML comments from issue and comment text before prompting; comments from users without write access are never presented; automations ignore events from those users by default; repository postToolUse hooks can replace a tool result (modifiedResult) before the model sees it; no classifier

steps.title: Leave untrusted-event handling at its default
body: When creating an automation keep events from users without write access ignored (the default); the opt-in is per automation, so review automations whose tool set is not read-only.

steps.title: Attach an inspector with a postToolUse hook
body: Commit .github/hooks/*.json with a postToolUse command hook that sends each tool result to your classifier and returns modifiedResult to replace flagged output; hook traffic is subject to the agent firewall.

steps.title: Use Agentic Workflows for event-driven automation that must be hardened
body: Agents run read-only; writes are buffered as safe outputs, scanned by a detection job and executed by a separate job, with @mention neutralisation, size limits and min-integrity filtering of inputs.

controls.note: Rated partial on the input-screening rule. GitHub's hidden-character and HTML-comment filtering normalises one input class and is not admin-configurable; the postToolUse hook is an attach point — repository code, changeable by anyone who can merge to the default branch, that screens nothing until the organisation attaches a classifier, and that fails open on timeout. Repository files, command output and MCP tool results are not screened by GitHub. Putting instruction files, hooks and setup steps under CODEOWNERS with "Require review from Code Owners" (GitHub's own guidance) is a process control, credited here, not screening. Agentic Workflows adds input sanitisation and an AI threat-detection job on outputs; that is a variant, not this agent's default path.

original.mechanism: Hidden-character and HTML-comment stripping before prompting, automations ignore non-write events, a content safety system on prompts and responses; Agentic Workflows sanitise user content and gate writes behind a threat-detection job

body: Agents run read-only; writes are buffered as safe outputs, scanned by a detection job and executed by a separate job — with @mention neutralisation, size limits and min-integrity filtering of inputs.

controls.mechanism: User-level budgets (Bundled AI credits budget, Users scope; always a hard stop); SKU-level "Copilot cloud agent" and organisation or enterprise budgets with "Stop usage when budget limit is reached"; the "AI credits paid usage" policy; GitHub Actions and cloud sandbox budgets; 59-minute hard limit for sessions on GitHub Actions, shorter with timeout-minutes in copilot-setup-steps.yml

GitHub documents the per-request check, not what the session then shows. Organisation, cost-centre and enterprise budgets stop usage only when "Stop usage when budget limit is reached" is selected (off by default). Automations bill to their creator.
