steps.title: Pin the runner at organisation level
body: Organization Settings > Copilot > Cloud > Runner type: Standard GitHub runner, then turn off Allow repositories to customize the runner type so copilot-setup-steps.yml cannot move sessions elsewhere.

steps.title: Keep sessions on fresh machines
body: GitHub recommends GitHub-hosted runners so each session runs on a fresh virtual machine; if you must use self-hosted runners, use ephemeral single-use ones — their isolation is then yours.

steps.title: Know what runs inside the sandbox
body: Hooks run in the ephemeral, non-interactive Linux sandbox the cloud agent provisions for each job, with a constrained network, and anything they write is discarded when the job ends.

controls.note: Native on the hosted D3-EI rule, re-verified: GitHub documents an ephemeral environment per session, destroyed when the session ends, with each session on a fresh virtual machine on GitHub-hosted runners, and an organisation owner can lock the runner type. Inside the boundary: setup steps, the agent's commands, hooks and local MCP server processes. Outside: the model, GitHub's services and remote MCP servers. The guarantee does not hold on self-hosted runners (GitHub recommends ephemeral single-use runners; reuse is possible) and GitHub's single-CPU hosted runners are containers on a shared VM. What crosses sessions: pushed commits, the session log, Copilot Memory and any custom image version saved with the setup job's snapshot key. Cloud sandboxes, the default since the Copilot in the cloud experience, are isolated GitHub-hosted Linux environments with no runner choice; their per-session lifetime is not described on the pages fetched.

original.mechanism: Ephemeral development environment per job powered by GitHub Actions — a non-interactive Linux sandbox with a constrained network, destroyed when the job ends; 59-minute hard limit; optionally on the organisation's own runners

steps.title: Keep the agent on the ephemeral Actions environment
body: Each task runs in its own ephemeral environment on GitHub Actions and ends within 59 minutes, a limit that cannot be extended; if you route it to self-hosted runners (configure-runners), the isolation of that runner is yours.

steps.title: Know what runs inside the sandbox
body: Setup steps, the agent's commands, hooks and MCP server processes all run inside the job's sandbox; the firewall applies to the agent's Bash processes but not to MCP server processes.

original.note: Inside the boundary: commands, setup steps, hooks and MCP servers. Outside: the model and GitHub's own services, reached through the agent's app identity. The boundary is a job, not a session: nothing persists after it ends except what was pushed.

controls.mechanism: Agent firewall on the organisation's Copilot > Internet access tab (Copilot in the cloud section): "Enable firewall" and "Recommended allowlist" (Enabled, Disabled or Let repositories decide), "Allow repository custom rules" and an organisation custom allowlist repositories cannot delete; domain and URL rules; blocked requests reported in the pull request; enforced only on processes the agent starts through its Bash tool

steps.title: Lock the firewall at organisation level
body: Organization Settings > Copilot > Internet access, Copilot in the cloud section: set Enable firewall to Enabled (the default is Let repositories decide) so repositories cannot turn it off.

steps.title: Own the allowlist
body: Set Allow repository custom rules to Disabled, maintain the Organization custom allowlist (domains or URL prefixes), and set Recommended allowlist deliberately — it admits public package and container registries.

controls.note: Partial on the hosted egress rule even though the organisation can now author and lock the list. It is enforced on processes the agent starts through its Bash tool, not around the sandbox: MCP server processes and copilot-setup-steps are outside it (there is no separate setup-phase policy — setup is unfirewalled), GitHub states sophisticated attacks may bypass it, and it operates only inside the environment where Copilot runs (a GitHub-hosted Actions runner or a cloud sandbox, which honours the organisation and repository allowlists) — it must be disabled on self-hosted runners and is not compatible with Windows. GitHub's own hosts and the Copilot API are always allowed. On self-hosted or Azure-private-network runners the organisation's network controls are the egress control.

original.mechanism: Firewall on by default with the recommended allowlist (OS packages, container and language registries, certificate authorities, Playwright hosts); custom allowlist per repository; organisation Settings > Copilot > Internet access can enforce or delegate

steps.title: Enforce the firewall at organisation level
body: Under Settings > Copilot > Internet access keep the firewall enabled and enforce it for every repository, adding only the hosts your builds need; disabling it lets Copilot connect to any host.

original.note: Rated partial on the egress rule: the firewall applies only to processes the agent starts through its Bash tool, not to MCP server processes — including the Playwright MCP server enabled by default — and the vendor states that sophisticated attacks may bypass it. Bound MCP servers through their configuration and tools arrays, and treat the firewall as blast-radius reduction.

controls.mechanism: No git proxy: GITHUB_COPILOT_GIT_TOKEN and GITHUB_COPILOT_API_TOKEN are set in the sandbox, the repository credential limited to the working repository and one branch; Agents secrets and variables reach setup steps and the agent's commands as environment variables, COPILOT_MCP_* values only MCP servers; secret values masked in session logs; Actions, Codespaces and Dependabot secrets never passed

steps.title: Scope Agents secrets to the repositories that need them
body: Organization Settings > Secrets and variables > Agents > New organization secret, Repository access: Selected repositories; repository-level secrets live under the repository's Secrets and variables > Agents.

steps.title: Keep MCP credentials MCP-only
body: Prefix values meant for MCP servers COPILOT_MCP_ so only the MCP configuration receives them; every other Agents secret is an environment variable the agent's commands can read.

steps.title: Keep everything else out of the Agents type
body: Store tokens the agent must not reach as Actions, Codespaces or Dependabot secrets, which it never receives; setup steps get the workflow GITHUB_TOKEN with only the permissions the file declares.

steps.title: Leave the GitHub MCP server on its repository-scoped token
body: Set COPILOT_MCP_GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN only when needed, and then as a fine-grained, read-only token limited to specific repositories.

controls.note: Rated partial on the hosted D3-CTS rule. GitHub does not proxy the repository credential: the hooks reference lists GITHUB_COPILOT_GIT_TOKEN and GITHUB_COPILOT_API_TOKEN among the sandbox's environment variables, so both sit inside the boundary where any command can read them. What bounds them is scope — the working repository, one branch, no merge, and GitHub states the agent cannot run git push itself — and their lifetime is not documented. Agents secrets are not removed after setup: setup steps and every command the agent runs receive them, so the model sees any value a command prints; masking applies to session logs, not the model's context. Only COPILOT_MCP_* values are confined to MCP servers. The strong part is exclusion: no Actions, Codespaces or Dependabot secret reaches the agent. Agentic Workflows (a variant) shows the proxy pattern: the engine key stays in the AWF API proxy sidecar and the agent sees a dummy key.

original.mechanism: Agents secrets and variables (repository or organisation) exposed as environment variables to setup steps and the agent's commands; COPILOT_MCP_ prefix limits a value to MCP servers; no access to Actions, Codespaces or Dependabot secrets; pushes go through the agent's own push path, not git commands

steps.title: Scope secrets to MCP servers with the prefix
body: Store values MCP servers need under COPILOT_MCP_* so they reach only those servers; everything else under Agents secrets is an environment variable every command can read.

steps.title: Keep the agent's own reach narrow
body: The agent cannot run git push itself and can only perform simple push operations; rulesets keep the requester from approving its PR.

original.note: Rated partial because Agents secrets sit inside the execution boundary: any command in the job can read them and print them to the model. The isolation that exists is scope — no other secret types, MCP-only values, and an app identity rather than a person's token. No on-behalf-of exchange: actions carry the agent's app identity with the requesting human as co-author.

original.mechanism: Agents-type secrets and variables (repository / organisation Settings > Secrets and variables > Agents); COPILOT_MCP_* prefix scopes values to MCP servers; no access to Actions, Codespaces or Dependabot secrets

steps.title: Use the Agents secret type only
body: Add secrets under Settings > Secrets and variables > Agents; prefix MCP credentials COPILOT_MCP_ so they are only available to MCP server configuration and never exported as general environment variables.

steps.title: Keep engine credentials out of Agentic Workflow agents
body: In Agentic Workflows the real engine key stays in the AWF API proxy sidecar; the agent container sees only a dummy key — configure ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / OPENAI_API_KEY / GEMINI_API_KEY as repository secrets, not in the workflow body.

original.note: Agents secrets are readable by the setup steps and MCP servers they are scoped to (COPILOT_MCP_*), and by commands the agent runs in the session; the model sees a value if a command prints it. They are stored secrets, not ephemeral issuance.

controls.mechanism: Agents secrets and variables encrypted (LibSodium; list and get return metadata, never the value) and scoped by organisation owners to selected repositories; git and Copilot API tokens set by GitHub in each job's sandbox (lifetime undocumented); OIDC federation available in copilot-setup-steps; no vendor tunnel — private reach is self-hosted or Azure-private-network runners

steps.title: Keep session secrets in the Agents store, scoped
body: Organization Settings > Secrets and variables > Agents > New organization secret with Repository access set to Selected repositories; repository administrators add repository-level Agents secrets.

steps.title: Rotate through the API
body: PUT /orgs/{org}/agents/secrets/{secret_name} with a value encrypted to the key from GET /orgs/{org}/agents/secrets/public-key; list and get endpoints never reveal the encrypted value.

steps.title: Prefer federated credentials in setup steps
body: Grant id-token: write on the copilot-setup-steps job and sign in with OIDC (GitHub's Azure DevOps example uses azure/login) instead of storing a long-lived cloud key as an Agents secret.

controls.note: Rated partial on the hosted D3-CH rule. The store is sound — Agents secrets are encrypted, never returned by the API and scoped per repository — but inside the session they are plain environment variables readable by every command and so by the model (masking covers session logs only), and GitHub documents no expiry or rotation for them; rotation is the organisation's job. The session's own GITHUB_COPILOT_GIT_TOKEN and GITHUB_COPILOT_API_TOKEN are GitHub-issued, but their lifetime is not documented. Tunnel: GitHub offers no tunnel or connector for this product; reach into private networks is through self-hosted runners or larger runners with Azure private networking, so there is no tunnel token to harden, and credentials for internal MCP servers are Agents secrets (COPILOT_MCP_*). A token obtained by OIDC in setup steps is short-lived but also lands in the sandbox.

settings.name: Require SAML authentication
settings.where: Enterprise › Settings › Authentication security › SAML single sign-on
settings.recommended: On, with MFA enforced on the GitHub app in your IdP (Enterprise Managed Users sign in through the IdP by design)
settings.why: Starting or resuming a session on an organisation's repositories needs a current SSO session, so a leaver's or a lapsed account cannot delegate work.

settings.name: Copilot in the cloud
settings.where: Enterprise › AI controls › Copilot › Configure features & clients
settings.recommended: Enabled for selected organizations, chosen at enterprise level
settings.why: Cloud sessions, issue assignment and cloud sandboxes reach only the organisations you chose; Disabled everywhere stops them for every licensed user.

settings.name: Block Copilot cloud agent in all repositories owned by ENTERPRISE-NAME
settings.where: Enterprise › AI controls › Agents › Copilot in the cloud
settings.recommended: Off — the first step of your incident runbook
settings.why: Unlike licence policies it applies to everyone, including users with a personal plan or another enterprise's seat, so it is the true enterprise-wide stop.

settings.name: Repository access
settings.where: Organization › Settings › Copilot › Cloud › Repository access
settings.recommended: Selected repositories — those with rulesets and setup steps reviewed for agents
settings.why: Anyone with Copilot and write access can delegate work to the agent; the agent works only where you have prepared the guardrails.

settings.name: Allow automations
settings.where: Organization › Settings › Copilot › Cloud › Allow automations
settings.recommended: Blocked, then allowed per organisation that needs scheduled or event-driven sessions
settings.why: Automations start sessions unattended, on a schedule, an event or an API call, and are visible only to their creator.

settings.name: Allow Claude coding agent / Allow Codex coding agent
settings.where: Enterprise › AI controls › Agents, then Organization › Settings › Copilot policies
settings.recommended: Off until each vendor has passed your AI vendor assessment
settings.why: Each switch installs a partner GitHub App that works on your repositories with another vendor's model and data path.

settings.name: Agent apps
settings.where: Enterprise › AI controls › Agents (agent apps policy), then each app's organisation installation
settings.recommended: Off; enable only for apps your vendor review has approved
settings.why: An agent app is a partner GitHub App with its own prompt, tools and MCP servers calling back to the partner's systems, billed to your Copilot.

settings.name: Runner type
settings.where: Organization › Settings › Copilot › Cloud › Runner type
settings.recommended: Standard GitHub runner, or a labelled group of ephemeral self-hosted runners where private network access is needed
settings.why: Each Actions session gets a fresh virtual machine, so nothing one session leaves behind is there for the next.

settings.name: Allow repositories to customize the runner type
settings.where: Organization › Settings › Copilot › Cloud
settings.recommended: Disabled
settings.why: A repository's copilot-setup-steps.yml cannot move the agent onto a long-lived or privileged runner.

settings.name: Enable firewall
settings.where: Organization › Settings › Copilot › Internet access › Copilot in the cloud
settings.recommended: Enabled
settings.why: Repository admins cannot switch off the egress filter that stands between an injected instruction and an upload of your code; it covers the agent's Bash tool, not MCP servers or setup steps.

settings.name: Recommended allowlist
settings.where: Organization › Settings › Copilot › Internet access › Copilot in the cloud
settings.recommended: Disabled, with your package mirror in the organization custom allowlist
settings.why: The default list opens every public package and container registry; routing installs through your mirror keeps dependencies scanned and egress narrow.

settings.name: Allow repository custom rules
settings.where: Organization › Settings › Copilot › Internet access
settings.recommended: Disabled; hosts are added to the organisation list on request
settings.why: A repository admin cannot quietly widen where the agent can send data.

settings.name: Organization custom allowlist
settings.where: Organization › Settings › Copilot › Internet access › Organization custom allowlist
settings.recommended: Your package mirror, internal registries and the external hosts your teams have justified
settings.why: One allowlist the organisation maintains, which repositories cannot delete entries from.

settings.name: Require approval for workflow runs
settings.where: Repository › Settings › Copilot › Cloud agent › Policies
settings.recommended: On — don't turn it off
settings.why: Workflows on Copilot's branch wait for someone with write access, so unreviewed agent code cannot reach Actions secrets or a write token.

settings.name: Require an additional approval for unattributed Copilot pull requests
settings.where: Repository or organisation ruleset › Require a pull request before merging
settings.recommended: On — don't clear it
settings.why: A pull request Copilot opens under its own identity still gets two humans: one more approval than the rule asks for.

settings.name: Allow Copilot to approve pull requests
settings.where: Enterprise › AI controls › Copilot › Configure features & clients › Copilot code review
settings.recommended: Disabled everywhere
settings.why: Copilot cannot approve, and so help merge, a pull request that Copilot wrote.

settings.name: Require review from Code Owners
settings.where: Ruleset › Require a pull request before merging, with CODEOWNERS covering .github/copilot, .github/agents, .github/hooks and copilot-setup-steps.yml
settings.recommended: On for the paths that configure agents, MCP servers and setup steps
settings.why: A change to what the agent runs, which MCP servers it gets or which hooks fire needs the owning team's approval.

settings.name: Agents secrets and variables › Repository access
settings.where: Organization › Settings › Secrets and variables › Agents
settings.recommended: Selected repositories, with MCP credentials prefixed COPILOT_MCP_
settings.why: Each credential reaches only the repositories that need it, and COPILOT_MCP_ values reach MCP servers, not the agent's shell; Actions secrets stay out of reach.

settings.name: MCP servers in Copilot
settings.where: Enterprise › AI controls › MCP
settings.recommended: Enabled everywhere, with allowedMcpServers restricting which servers run
settings.why: GitHub's advice is to keep MCP on and restrict it; Disabled leaves the agent only its built-in GitHub and Playwright servers.

settings.name: allowedMcpServers
settings.where: copilot/managed-settings.json in the enterprise's .github-private repository → allowedMcpServers
settings.recommended: Your approved servers matched by serverUrl or serverCommand, not serverName, plus the connector URLs you allow
settings.why: Enforced in cloud sandboxes, not on GitHub Actions or for servers in custom agent profiles, where the firewall is what stops them starting.

settings.name: permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode
settings.where: copilot/managed-settings.json in the enterprise's .github-private repository → permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode
settings.recommended: "disable"
settings.why: Cloud sandbox sessions cannot be switched to allow-all; sessions on GitHub Actions do not read managed settings.

settings.name: permissions.deny
settings.where: copilot/managed-settings.json in the enterprise's .github-private repository → permissions.deny
settings.recommended: Deny secret paths: Read(~/.ssh/**), Read(~/.aws/**), Read(./.env*), Edit(//etc/**)
settings.why: Deny rules hold in cloud sandbox sessions whatever the user or repository sets; GitHub Actions sessions rely on the scoped token and rulesets instead.

settings.name: permissions.ask
settings.where: copilot/managed-settings.json in the enterprise's .github-private repository → permissions.ask
settings.recommended: Shell(git push *) and Shell(gh pr merge *)
settings.why: In cloud sandbox sessions the user is asked afresh before each matching action; assisted approval and allow-all cannot answer for them.

settings.name: Repository-level hook files (.github/hooks/*.json)
settings.where: Repository → .github/hooks/*.json, protected by CODEOWNERS
settings.recommended: A preToolUse deny for secret paths and a postToolUse hook that screens web and MCP results, from your template repository
settings.why: The only place to inspect a tool result before the model reads it in a cloud session; policy hooks are not supported there.

settings.name: Content exclusion
settings.where: Enterprise › AI controls › Copilot › Content exclusion (also organisation and repository Settings › Copilot › Content exclusion)
settings.recommended: Secret and key-material paths ("*.pem", "*.key", "**/.env*", "secrets*") and client-restricted repositories, set at enterprise level
settings.why: Excluded files are not used as context by cloud sessions; it narrows what the agent reads, not what its token can reach.

settings.name: Copilot Memory
settings.where: Enterprise › AI controls › Copilot › Configure features & clients › Features
settings.recommended: Let organizations decide — off unless an organisation opts in
settings.why: Stored preferences are injected into later sessions and administrators can export or delete them; repository facts are governed separately under Repository access.

settings.name: Universal user-level budget
settings.where: Enterprise › Billing and licensing › Budgets and alerts
settings.recommended: A monthly AI-credit cap per user, with individual overrides for power users
settings.why: A runaway or looping session stops at the user's cap; user-level budgets are always a hard stop.

settings.name: Stop usage when budget limit is reached
settings.where: Enterprise › Billing and licensing › Budgets and alerts › (SKU-level budget for Copilot cloud agent)
settings.recommended: On
settings.why: Without it a budget only emails; with it, cloud agent spend stops at the limit you set.

settings.name: Audit log streaming
settings.where: Enterprise › Settings › Audit log › Log streaming
settings.recommended: On, to your SIEM
settings.why: Agent activity (actor:Copilot, agent_session_id) and policy changes outlive GitHub's 180 days and can be alerted on.

settings.name: Copilot Usage Records Streaming
settings.where: Enterprise › AI controls › Copilot › Copilot Usage Records Streaming
settings.recommended: Enabled everywhere, into the audit-log stream, readable only by your investigations team
settings.why: Request and response bodies from cloud sessions reach your SIEM — the record of what the agent was asked, read and answered.
settings.requires: Enterprise Managed Users or data residency (public preview)

settings.name: Validation tools
settings.where: Repository › Settings › Copilot › Cloud agent › Validation tools
settings.recommended: On — don't turn them off
settings.why: The agent's own code is checked for security issues and secrets and reviewed by Copilot code review before its pull request is finished.

summary: Governance runs through the enterprise AI-controls tab and organisation Copilot settings: Feature, Privacy and Models policies set enterprise-first (enable, disable, or let organisations decide), with content exclusion and MCP governance layered on for Business and Enterprise plans.

Inference runs on GitHub's Copilot API (api.*.githubcopilot.com per plan) against models hosted on Azure, AWS Bedrock, Anthropic, GCP, xAI and Fireworks; with local BYOK the prompts go straight from the editor to the chosen provider and bypass GitHub. Prompts, open-file context, tool arguments and (in agent mode) shell output leave the device; the audit log never sees them — only an OpenTelemetry export the enterprise pins in managed settings does.

Two admin planes overlap in VS Code: device policy (Windows registry Software\Policies\Microsoft\VSCode, macOS configuration profiles, /etc/vscode/policy.json) and GitHub's managed-settings.json (MDM key HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\GitHubCopilot / com.github.copilot, then server-managed copilot/managed-settings.json, then a local file). Where both set the same policy the Copilot managed setting wins. JetBrains honours the managed file for MCP, plugins, telemetry and bypass-mode lockout (2026-08-18) and a managed sandbox in preview (2026-09-08); Visual Studio is ADMX-only.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Free, Pro, Pro+, Max; Business and Enterprise carry policies, content exclusion, MCP governance and managed settings.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: GitHub Copilot API by plan (*.business / *.enterprise.githubcopilot.com); OpenAI on Azure, Anthropic on AWS Bedrock / Anthropic / GCP, Gemini on GCP, xAI, Moonshot on Foundry/Fireworks. Data residency (US, EU) is a policy at +10% credits.

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: Prompts, file context and tool outputs to the Copilot API; telemetry to collector.github.com and copilot-telemetry.githubusercontent.com; local BYOK sends prompts directly to the provider; enterprise BYOK stays server-side.

facts.label: Data retention / training
facts.value: Business and Enterprise prompts are not used for training; model providers run under zero-data-retention except Claude Fable 5 / 5.1, which retain by default with a ZDR exemption available through end-2026.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: GitHub Copilot documentation, plus the VS Code enterprise policy reference.

items.title: Enterprise and organisation policy framework
body: Policies gate which Copilot features, agents and models users can access — named policies include MCP servers in Copilot, restricting MCP to registry servers, allowed models, custom models, web search, Copilot Memory and suggestions-matching-public-code (blocked by default for Business seats). Conflict rules matter for design: within one enterprise the least restrictive setting wins across a user's organisations, so a lockdown must be set at the enterprise level to be a lockdown.

items.title: MCP governance and content exclusion
body: The MCP policy gates whether MCP servers run at all across Copilot clients; server allowlisting comes in two strengths — a GitHub-hosted Managed Settings File (GA, matched on name, URL and stdio command, not user-bypassable) and a Custom MCP Registry (preview, name matching only, bypassable by editing local config). Content exclusion (Business and Enterprise) applies at repository, organisation and enterprise scope with fnmatch patterns, but is not honoured by the edit and agent modes of Chat in VS Code and other editors, nor by third-party agents — scope guidance accordingly.

items.title: Audit surface and network posture
body: The organisation audit log records Copilot licensing, settings and policy changes (action:copilot) and the cloud agent's website activity (actor:Copilot) with 180-day retention — it does not capture client-side prompts, so IDE-level telemetry needs its own answer. Proxy and firewall allowlists are documented per-plan, with a /meta API endpoint for the current domain set.

items.title: VS Code device policies and the Copilot managed-settings plane
body: VS Code's ADMX/plist/policy.json set carries the agent lockdown: ChatAgentMode, ChatToolsAutoApprove, ChatToolsTerminalEnableAutoApprove, the deprecated ChatAgentSandbox* policies (Local harness only), ChatAgentNetworkFilter with allowed/denied domains, ChatMCP / ChatAllowedMcpServers / ChatDeniedMcpServers / ChatAllowManagedMcpServersOnly, McpGalleryServiceUrl, ChatPlugins* and ChatStrictMarketplaces, ChatHooks / ChatAllowManagedHooksOnly, Claude3PIntegration / Codex3PIntegration, ChatApprovedAccountOrganizations and the CopilotOtel* export keys. Developer: Policy Diagnostics shows which source won.

The same keys arrive through GitHub's managed-settings.json (permissions deny/ask/allow, disableBypassPermissionsMode, allowedMcpServers, enabledPlugins, telemetry, and the sandbox.* keys that now govern sandboxing in Copilot harness sessions). Precedence in VS Code 1.128+: MDM-delivered managed settings, then server-managed, then the local file — and a Copilot managed setting outranks the equivalent VS Code policy.

links.title: VS Code AI settings for enterprises

riskNotes.note: Three of the four 2025–26 CVEs on this surface are prompt injection turned into code execution (settings-file rewrite in VS Code, shell metacharacters in the JetBrains plugin, consent-prompt bypass in the extension host). The vendor mitigations are approval prompts and the sandbox; the enterprise controls that survive a successful injection are ChatToolsAutoApprove=false, the managed sandbox.enabled key (the ChatAgentSandbox* device policies are deprecated and reach only Local harness sessions) and the network filter.

The registry-based restriction matches on server name only and is bypassable by editing mcp.json; only the managed-settings allowlist (name, URL, stdio command) is a real boundary. Starting a server straight from mcp.json also skips the trust prompt.

Content exclusion is not honoured by edit and agent modes, and the IDE can still surface semantic information from excluded files. Local BYOK moves prompts off GitHub's ZDR contracts onto whatever the developer's provider retains.

Agent Host sessions can run Claude Agent SDK and Codex runtimes inside VS Code; unless Claude3PIntegration / Codex3PIntegration are set to false, a "Copilot" seat is also a third-party agent seat, with its own model and data path.

controls.mechanism: GitHub's own second-factor requirement (Enterprise > Settings > Authentication security > "Require two-factor authentication for the enterprise and all of its organizations", optionally "Only allow secure two-factor methods") plus client pinning in VS Code (ChatApprovedAccountOrganizations) and Visual Studio (ADMX Copilot Settings); the JetBrains, Xcode, Eclipse and Vim plugins cannot be pinned

steps.title: Require two-factor authentication for every organization
body: Enterprise > Settings > Authentication security: select "Require two-factor authentication for the enterprise and all of its organizations" and "Only allow secure two-factor methods"; members without 2FA cannot reach organization resources until they enable it. The policy is not available to Enterprise Managed Users, whose second factor is the IdP's.

steps.title: Pin VS Code to your organizations
body: Set the ChatApprovedAccountOrganizations policy to your organization logins; chat, agents and inline suggestions stay disabled (the policy is fail-closed) until the signed-in GitHub account belongs to one of them and its account-side policy has resolved.

steps.title: Block personal Copilot plans in Visual Studio
body: Deploy the Visual Studio ADMX templates and under Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Visual Studio > Copilot Settings disable Copilot for individual accounts (17.10+) and Copilot Free (17.13+).

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor. GitHub's identity layer can require a second factor for every organization member, but this entity can pin its client to the organization account only in VS Code (ChatApprovedAccountOrganizations, fail-closed) and Visual Studio (ADMX blocks individual and Copilot Free plans); the JetBrains, Xcode, Eclipse and Vim plugins document no account pin, so a personal account works there. VS Code alone meets the native definition. With Enterprise Managed Users the 2FA policy is unavailable: MFA is configured in the IdP and, per GitHub, enforced only at IdP sign-in. Paths that skip the second factor once issued: the OAuth token each editor keeps (lifetime not documented) and fine-grained PATs (Enterprise > Policies > Personal access tokens can cap lifetime and require approval for organization resources; whether that governs the Copilot Requests account permission is not documented). In VS Code, Codex sessions can run on a ChatGPT sign-in (chat.agentHost.allowSignedOutWhenUsable); Codex3PIntegration=false closes that path.

original.mechanism: Enterprise licensing (seat assignment, enterprise teams synced from the IdP) plus the VS Code ChatApprovedAccountOrganizations device policy and Visual Studio ADMX

steps.title: Assign seats through enterprise teams or organisations
body: Enterprise > Billing and licensing > Licensing > Copilot > Manage: assign licences to users or enterprise teams; with Enterprise Managed Users, sync the team to an IdP group so access follows the IdP.

steps.title: Gate VS Code chat to approved GitHub organisations
body: Set the ChatApprovedAccountOrganizations policy to the list of organisation logins; chat, agents and inline suggestions stay off until the signed-in account belongs to one, which forces the organisation's policies to apply before any AI feature works.

steps.title: Block personal Copilot accounts in Visual Studio
body: Deploy the Visual Studio ADMX templates and use Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Visual Studio > Copilot Settings to disable Copilot for individual accounts or Copilot Free.

controls.mechanism: Managed permissions.deny / ask / allow (Shell, Read, Edit, Domain selectors) and machine-wide Copilot Policy Hooks (preToolUse deny) in VS Code Copilot sessions on Agent Host only; Local-harness sessions have ChatToolsEligibleForAutoApproval and Preview PreToolUse hooks (ChatAllowManagedHooksOnly)

steps.title: Pin deny / ask / allow rules in the managed file
body: In copilot/managed-settings.json set permissions.deny, permissions.ask and permissions.allow with Shell(...), Read(...), Edit(...) and Domain(...) selectors; deny from any source wins and a managed ask cannot be satisfied by bypass mode, auto-approval, a hook or a saved grant. VS Code applies these rules only to Copilot sessions that use Agent Host.

steps.title: Deploy a machine-wide policy hook
body: Install a root-owned hook file in /etc/github-copilot/policy.d/ (Windows C:\ProgramData\GitHub\Copilot\policy.d\ or HKLM\Software\Policies\GitHub\Copilot) whose preToolUse hook calls your policy service and returns permissionDecision "deny"; policy hooks load first and disableAllHooks cannot switch them off.

steps.title: Move editor chat onto the harness that runs them
body: Set ChatEditorPreferCopilotHarness=true (VS Code 1.134+) so new editor-chat sessions use the Copilot SDK harness, which loads Policy Hooks, and ChatAllowManagedHooksOnly=true so Local-harness hooks come only from managed sources and policy-enabled plugins.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: the rules cover only some sessions. Inside: VS Code Copilot sessions on Agent Host, where managed deny/ask/allow govern shell, file and domain operations and a Policy Hook can deny any tool, MCP included (command hooks fail closed on error but open on timeout; HTTP preToolUse hooks fail open). Outside: Local-harness sessions (ChatToolsEligibleForAutoApproval only forces a prompt, a false terminal rule "does not block the command", and Local PreToolUse hooks are Preview), Claude and Codex harness sessions (their own permission models), JetBrains (honours only permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode among the permission keys) and Visual Studio, Xcode and Eclipse (no rule engine; Visual Studio can only disable agent mode). Managed selectors do not name MCP tools; only a hook does. VS Code's AI-settings page still warns that the granular permissions are "supported only in GitHub Copilot CLI" while GitHub's reference and the 2026-09-09 changelog list VS Code Agent Host sessions — test before relying on them.

original.mechanism: managed-settings.json permissions.deny / ask / allow (Shell, Read, Edit, Domain selectors; GA 2026-09-09) for VS Code Agent Host sessions, plus PreToolUse hooks

steps.title: Pin deny / ask / allow rules in the managed file
body: Write permissions.deny, permissions.ask and permissions.allow with Shell(...), Read(...), Edit(...) and Domain(...) selectors. Deny wins from any source, ask forces a fresh approval that bypass mode cannot satisfy, and the effective allow list is the intersection of all sources.

steps.title: Confirm the client honours managed permissions
body: Managed permissions are enforced in VS Code sessions that use Agent Host, the Copilot app and the CLI; the reference matrix shows JetBrains honouring only permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode, so JetBrains lockdown relies on that key and the sandbox.

steps.title: Add a PreToolUse hook as a second gate
body: VS Code runs .github/hooks/*.json and ~/.copilot/hooks; a PreToolUse hook returns permissionDecision allow / deny / ask. Set ChatAllowManagedHooksOnly so only enterprise-managed hooks and policy-enabled plugins can register.

original.note: Component-specific: managed permissions and PreToolUse hooks apply to VS Code Agent Host sessions (enterprise-managed settings page); the VS Code enterprise AI settings page governs editor policies and auto-approval, a different scope. JetBrains, Visual Studio and the other plugins have no runtime rule engine. Where the two pages appear to conflict, the enterprise-managed settings reference is the narrower and authoritative one.

controls.mechanism: No vendor feature; the organisation's TPRM platform assesses GitHub and each model provider from the GitHub Copilot Trust Center and the model-hosting page

evidence.title: GitHub Copilot Trust Center (compliance reports; most documents behind Request access)
Hosting of models for GitHub Copilot (providers and retention terms)

controls.note: External: the organisation's TPRM platform owns the assessment. Rendered in a browser on 2026-09-25 the trust center lists SOC 1, SOC 2 and SOC 3 (SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 reports), ISO 27001:2013, ISO/IEC 42001:2023, CSA STAR Level 2, TISAX, a 2026 CAIQ, a PCI DSS AOC and bug-bounty letters, most behind Request access; no penetration-test summary is listed. Treat GitHub plus each model provider as the subprocessor set: OpenAI on Azure, Anthropic models on AWS, Anthropic and Google Cloud (Claude Fable 5 / 5.1 retain prompts and outputs by default outside the ZDR agreement; a ZDR exemption can be requested through end-2026), Google, xAI, and Moonshot models on Azure AI Foundry and Fireworks. The hosting page changes with each model launch; local BYOK moves prompts to whatever provider the developer configures.

original.mechanism: No vendor feature; the assessment inputs are the model-hosting page (providers, ZDR terms) and the Copilot Trust Center
original.note: Treat GitHub plus each model provider (OpenAI on Azure, Anthropic on AWS/GCP/Anthropic, Google, xAI, Moonshot on Foundry/Fireworks) as the subprocessor set; the hosting page is the only first-party list and it changes with every model launch. The trust centre page did not render for automated fetch on 2026-09-10.

steps.title: Record the model-provider set and their retention terms
body: Use the hosting page to enumerate where each model runs and which retain data (Claude Fable 5 / 5.1 retain by default; request the ZDR exemption).

controls.mechanism: No built-in detector; Copilot Policy Hooks in VS Code Copilot sessions on Agent Host can rewrite or deny prompt and tool traffic (userPromptTransformed, preToolUse modifiedArgs, postToolUse modifiedResult); content exclusion as data minimisation

steps.title: Hand prompt and tool traffic to your inspector
body: In a root-owned /etc/github-copilot/policy.d/*.json policy hook, return modifiedTransformedPrompt from userPromptTransformed with secrets masked, and have preToolUse and postToolUse call your DLP service and deny or return modifiedArgs / modifiedResult.

steps.title: Route editor chat through the harness that runs the hooks
body: Set ChatEditorPreferCopilotHarness=true; Local-harness sessions do not load Policy Hooks.

steps.title: Exclude secret-bearing paths
body: Enterprise > AI controls > Copilot > Content exclusion (or the organization's Copilot > Content exclusion): add fnmatch entries such as "*": ["**/.env"]; changes can take up to 30 minutes to reach IDEs that already loaded the settings.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: no Copilot editor detects secrets or PII itself; the Agent Host Copilot harness exposes inline hooks that can block or rewrite prompt and tool content, an attach point that works only once the organisation attaches a detector (userPromptSubmitted config-file hooks cannot change the prompt; userPromptTransformed can). Content exclusion is path filtering, credited as data minimisation: VS Code honours it in chat but not in Edit or Agent mode, Xcode and Eclipse chat do not honour it, symlinks and remote filesystems are exempt, and IDE-provided type information from excluded files can still reach the model. Local-harness, Claude and Codex sessions and the other editors have no such hook; endpoint DLP or an SSE / AI gateway covers them. telemetry.captureContent=false with lockCaptureContent keeps prompts out of the OTel export — data minimisation of telemetry, not redaction.

original.mechanism: Content exclusion (repository / organisation / enterprise) plus telemetry.captureContent=false with lockCaptureContent
original.note: Content exclusion is a context filter, not DLP: it does not apply to edit and agent modes, symlinks or remote filesystems, and IDE-provided type information can still leak. Inline inspection of the prompt stream needs an SSE or endpoint DLP product.

steps.title: Exclude secret-bearing paths at enterprise scope
body: Enterprise > AI controls > Copilot > Content exclusion (or Organization Settings > Copilot > Content exclusion): add fnmatch entries such as "*": ["**/.env"] and per-repository paths; changes propagate within 30 minutes.

steps.title: Keep prompt content out of the telemetry export
body: In managed-settings.json set telemetry.captureContent to false and telemetry.lockCaptureContent to true so users cannot turn content capture on.

controls.mechanism: No classifier; a Copilot Policy Hook's postToolUse can replace a tool result before the model sees it (VS Code Copilot sessions on Agent Host); URL response review and Workspace Trust are human review and admission

steps.title: Screen tool results with a post-tool hook
body: In a policy hook, have postToolUse send each result to your classifier and return modifiedResult (a replacement textResultForLlm) or a failure when it flags injected instructions.

steps.title: Keep fetched content under review
body: Leave chat.tools.urls.autoApprove without approveResponse: true entries so fetched pages are shown for review before they are added to the chat context.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: GitHub ships no injection classifier for tool results, fetched pages or repository files in any editor. The post-tool hook is an attach point in VS Code Copilot sessions on Agent Host only; URL response approval is a person reading content, and Workspace Trust and MCP server trust are admission decisions, not screening. For Local-harness, Claude and Codex sessions and the other editors the answer is external: an AI or MCP gateway classifier on the brokered path. Prompt injection produced code execution on this surface (CVE-2025-53773, CVE-2026-21516).

original.mechanism: VS Code two-step URL approval, Workspace Trust restricted mode, edit review flow; no configurable injection classifier
original.note: Defences are structural (approvals, trust boundaries, sandbox), not detection. Prompt injection has produced RCE on this surface twice (CVE-2025-53773, CVE-2026-21516), so pair these with tool scoping and egress control rather than relying on them.

steps.title: Keep the structural defences on
body: Leave URL fetching on the two-step trust-domain-then-review flow, keep Workspace Trust so untrusted folders open in restricted mode with agents disabled, and require edit review before commits.

controls.mechanism: VS Code policies ChatToolsAutoApprove, ChatToolsEligibleForAutoApproval, ChatAgentExtensionTools, BrowserChatTools, ChatMCP and ChatAgentMode (per tool class); argument-scoped managed permissions in Agent Host Copilot sessions only; Visual Studio "Disable Agent Mode"

steps.title: Remove global auto-approval and pin approval-only tools
body: Set ChatToolsAutoApprove to false and ChatToolsEligibleForAutoApproval to entries such as {"runTask": false, "fetch": false, "runInTerminal": false} so those tools always need a manual approval users cannot switch off.

steps.title: Cut tool classes you do not need
body: ChatAgentExtensionTools=false blocks extension-contributed tools, BrowserChatTools=false removes the integrated-browser tools, ChatMCP=registry or none limits MCP sources, and ChatAgentMode=false removes agents entirely.

steps.title: Scope arguments in Agent Host sessions
body: Use permissions.deny / ask / allow with Shell(git push *), Read(~/.ssh/**), Edit(//etc/**) and Domain(...) selectors; they apply to VS Code Copilot sessions that use Agent Host.

steps.title: Disable agent mode in Visual Studio where needed
body: Visual Studio 17.14.16+ honours Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Visual Studio > Copilot Settings > Disable Agent Mode.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: outside Agent Host the admin controls are per tool class (on/off or approval-required), with no argument or path scoping; the managed Shell/Read/Edit/Domain selectors reach only VS Code Copilot sessions on Agent Host and do not name MCP tools. Bypass is not fully removable: Agents-window worktree sessions always run with Allow all ("can't be changed"), and the Claude harness has a user setting, github.copilot.chat.claudeAgent.allowDangerouslySkipPermissions, that bypasses every check (Claude3PIntegration=false removes the harness). JetBrains honours only permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode; Xcode and Eclipse have no tool policy.

original.mechanism: VS Code policies ChatToolsAutoApprove, ChatToolsEligibleForAutoApproval, ChatAgentExtensionTools, BrowserChatTools, ChatAgentMode; Visual Studio "Disable Agent Mode"; managed permissions

steps.title: Remove global auto-approval and pick eligible tools
body: Set ChatToolsAutoApprove to false (it "disables manual approval completely for all tools in all workspaces") and use ChatToolsEligibleForAutoApproval to name the tools that may ever skip approval.

steps.title: Cut extension and browser tools
body: ChatAgentExtensionTools=false blocks tools contributed by third-party extensions; BrowserChatTools=false removes the integrated browser tool; ChatAgentMode=false removes agent mode entirely.

steps.title: Disable agent mode in Visual Studio where needed
body: Visual Studio 17.14.16+ honours Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Visual Studio > Copilot Settings > Disable Agent Mode.

original.note: VS Code policies hide tool classes and control auto-approval; managed permissions limit arguments for Agent Host sessions; Visual Studio can only disable agent mode. Other editors have no tool-level policy.

controls.mechanism: Copilot harness (Agent Host) sessions in VS Code: the runtime sandbox (macOS Seatbelt, glibc Linux and WSL2 bubblewrap, Windows BaseContainer — Experimental), required by the managed sandbox.enabled, sandbox.failIfUnavailable and sandbox.allowBypass keys (enforcement Preview), with sandboxMcpServers / sandboxLspServers; Local harness sessions keep the deprecated ChatAgentSandboxEnabled / ChatAgentSandboxAllowUnsandboxedCommands / ChatAgentSandboxAllowNetwork device policies (macOS and Linux); JetBrains enterprise-managed sandbox (preview). Credential paths: managed sandbox.userPolicy.filesystem.deniedPaths, sandbox.auth.git / auth.gh and allowDevToolAccess; managed Read(...) denies in Agent Host sessions; otherwise the agent holds the developer's credentials

steps.title: Require the sandbox for Copilot harness sessions
body: In managed-settings.json set sandbox.enabled=true, sandbox.failIfUnavailable=true and sandbox.allowBypass=false; VS Code 1.140 and later then lock the session's sandbox toggle, and clients below the minimum version (VS Code 1.141.0) lose Copilot until they update.

steps.title: Check Windows and the effective policy
body: The Windows sandbox is Experimental; run /sandbox policy in a Copilot harness session to see the effective policy, including organisation-managed restrictions (not available in Local harness sessions).

steps.title: Push the JetBrains sandbox policy from managed settings
body: The JetBrains plugin reads the enterprise-managed sandbox policy (enablement, filesystem and network access, proxy, developer-tool and macOS Keychain access) and locks it under GitHub Copilot > Sandbox — public preview.

steps.title: Sandbox the MCP servers a session starts
body: Set sandbox.sandboxMcpServers=true (and sandboxLspServers) in managed settings so servers the Copilot harness starts run inside the sandbox; the per-server sandbox entry in mcp.json is a user or workspace setting and is not available on Windows.

steps.title: Cover Local harness sessions too
body: Managed sandbox keys do not reach Local harness sessions; for those, the deprecated ChatAgentSandboxEnabled=on and ChatAgentSandboxAllowUnsandboxedCommands=false device policies still apply (macOS and Linux), and ChatTemporaryDefaultToLocalHarness should stay unset because Local does not enforce runtime-only sandbox and permission settings.

steps.title: Deny credential directories explicitly
body: Add the SSH, cloud-CLI and browser-profile directories to sandbox.userPolicy.filesystem.deniedPaths in managed settings (managed denied paths add to the user's), and set sandbox.auth.git / sandbox.auth.gh to false where a task needs no GitHub credentials.

steps.title: Deny credential reads in Agent Host sessions
body: Put Read(~/.ssh/**) and similar selectors under permissions.deny in the managed file; VS Code applies them to Copilot sessions that use Agent Host.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: the sandbox exists but is platform-limited and only partly admin-requirable. For Copilot harness sessions VS Code's own docs say the device policies no longer enforce sandboxing and administrators should require it with Copilot managed settings; GitHub's managed-settings reference lists the sandbox key as supported in VS Code, while VS Code's AI-settings page says the reference does not list it for VS Code — the two vendors' pages disagree, so verify the effective policy with /sandbox policy before relying on it. Managed enforcement is in Preview and the Windows sandbox is Experimental. The ChatAgentSandbox* device policies are deprecated and govern only Local harness sessions (macOS and Linux), which auto-approve sandboxed commands. The boundary is processes the session starts: terminal commands, and MCP and language servers when configured; built-in file tools, extension tools, remote MCP servers, the extension host and the Agent Host process run outside it, and the deprecated chat.agent.sandbox.retryWithAllowNetworkRequests still lets Local harness users retry a blocked command with open network. GitHub's managed-settings reference marks the sandbox key unsupported in JetBrains, while the 2026-09-08 changelog announces a JetBrains managed sandbox in preview. Visual Studio, Xcode and Eclipse have no sandbox; a dev container or VM supplies one. Credential paths: managed deniedPaths, auth.git / auth.gh and allowDevToolAccess bound what sandboxed commands can read in Copilot harness sessions (the old chat.agent.sandbox.fileSystem.mac / .linux settings are deprecated and ignored there); built-in file tools, MCP servers outside the sandbox and extensions are not covered. Not documented: whether environment variables, the ssh-agent socket or the git credential helper reach sandboxed commands. Tool calls carry the signed-in user's GitHub authority with no on-behalf-of exchange. JetBrains' managed sandbox (preview) adds Keychain and developer-tool access switches; Visual Studio, Xcode and Eclipse run with the developer's full credential set, where a dev container or VM is the external fix.

original.mechanism: VS Code ChatAgentSandboxEnabled / AllowNetwork / AllowAutoApprove / AllowUnsandboxedCommands (macOS, Linux, WSL2; preview); JetBrains enterprise-managed sandbox (preview 2026-09-08); per-server MCP sandbox
original.note: Rated partial because the entity spans editors with different support: VS Code (macOS, Linux, WSL2; preview) and JetBrains (preview 2026-09-08) can be required to sandbox, while Visual Studio and the Xcode, Eclipse and Vim plugins have no sandbox at all. Inside the boundary: terminal commands and per-server local MCP; outside: remote MCP servers, the editor's own tools and the model endpoint. The VS Code setting chat.agent.sandbox.retryWithAllowNetworkRequests has no policy, so a sandboxed command can be retried with network unless allowNetwork is also false.

steps.title: Force the VS Code sandbox on and close its exits
body: Set ChatAgentSandboxEnabled=true, ChatAgentSandboxAllowNetwork=false and ChatAgentSandboxAllowUnsandboxedCommands=false; keep ChatAgentSandboxAllowAutoApprove false unless sandboxed commands may run unattended.

steps.title: Sandbox stdio MCP servers
body: In the server entry set sandboxEnabled: true with allowWrite paths and allowedDomains; sandboxed servers can only touch the paths and domains listed.

steps.title: Push the JetBrains sandbox policy from managed settings
body: The JetBrains plugin reads the managed sandbox policy (enablement, filesystem and network access, proxy, dev-tool and Keychain access) under GitHub Copilot > Sandbox — public preview.

original.mechanism: The agent acts with the developer's own GitHub session; org OAuth-app access policy and PAT policies bound what the GitHub MCP server can reach
original.note: There is no on-behalf-of exchange: tool calls carry the signed-in user's authority. The usable boundaries are the organisation's OAuth app access restrictions, fine-grained PAT approval and SSO enforcement on the GitHub MCP server, and the sandbox for local commands.

steps.title: Bound the GitHub MCP server with org access policies
body: Enforce the OAuth app access policy for third-party hosts, require approval of fine-grained PATs and keep SSO enforcement on so tokens must map to a recent SSO login.

controls.mechanism: ChatStrictPluginOnlyCustomization and ChatAllowManagedHooksOnly lock instruction and hook sources; CopilotSessionSync and the "Store local sessions in the Cloud" policy govern session sync; VS Code's local memory tool has no documented policy; Copilot Memory does not apply to IDEs

steps.title: Lock customization sources to managed plugins
body: Set ChatStrictPluginOnlyCustomization=true to block standalone user and workspace skills, agents, hooks, instructions and MCP servers, and ChatAllowManagedHooksOnly=true so hooks come only from managed sources (VS Code 1.132+).

steps.title: Decide whether sessions leave the device
body: Set the CopilotSessionSync policy (chat.sessionSync.enabled) to false to keep session history local.

steps.title: Review and clear local agent memory
body: VS Code's memory tool writes /memories/ (user, auto-loaded into every session up to 200 lines), /memories/repo/ and /memories/session/ locally; use Chat: Show Memory Files and Chat: Clear All Memory Files to inspect and remove them.

steps.title: Confirm Copilot Memory is out of scope for IDEs
body: The supported-surfaces table marks the Copilot Memory policy as not applying to IDEs (it applies to the cloud agent, third-party agents, the CLI and code review).

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: an administrator can lock instruction and hook sources in VS Code (ChatStrictPluginOnlyCustomization, ChatAllowManagedHooksOnly) and keep sessions local, but VS Code's own memory tool writes notes that are loaded into later sessions with no documented policy to disable it and no validation or review of what it stores. Organization instructions and agents are applied only when the developer leaves github.copilot.chat.organizationInstructions.enabled and showOrganizationAndEnterpriseAgents on — user settings, not policy. Repository instruction files are read as trusted context and writable by anyone with push access (the CVE-2025-53773 pattern); nothing version-pins them. Other editors expose no memory or instruction-source control.

original.mechanism: CopilotSessionSync policy (VS Code) and the "Store local sessions in the Cloud" policy; Copilot Memory does not apply to IDEs
original.note: IDE sessions have no persistent agent memory of their own; the exposure is session history synced to github.com and repository custom-instruction files, which the agent reads as trusted context.

steps.title: Decide whether IDE sessions sync to GitHub
body: Set the CopilotSessionSync policy (chat.sessionSync.enabled) to false to keep session history local; at the organisation level the "Store local sessions in the Cloud" policy controls the same sync for Copilot clients.

steps.title: Confirm Memory is out of scope for IDEs
body: The supported-surfaces table lists Copilot Memory as not supported in IDEs, the CLI and the app; the memory policy therefore governs github.com, the cloud agent and code review only.

original.mechanism: Organisation and enterprise custom instructions and custom agents, ChatStrictPluginOnlyCustomization, ChatAllowManagedHooksOnly
original.note: Repository .github instruction files are read as trusted context and are writable by anyone with push access — CVE-2025-53773 exploited exactly that pattern against settings files. The enterprise can force its own instructions but cannot version-pin repository ones.

steps.title: Apply organisation instructions and managed agents
body: Enable github.copilot.chat.organizationInstructions.enabled and showOrganizationAndEnterpriseAgents so organisation-level instructions and custom agents are applied and offered by default.

steps.title: Block user and workspace overrides
body: ChatStrictPluginOnlyCustomization removes standalone user and workspace instructions, agents, skills and hooks; ChatAllowManagedHooksOnly keeps hooks to managed sources.

controls.mechanism: VS Code's secure credential store for MCP server inputs; GitHub PAT policies (maximum lifetime, restrict access); edit approval for secret files (chat.tools.edits.autoApprove); nothing forbids the static keys a developer brings (local BYOK, API keys in MCP env files)

steps.title: Keep MCP secrets out of configuration files
body: Supply MCP API keys as sensitive input parameters rather than literals in mcp.json; VS Code stores sensitive MCP input parameters in its secure credentials store.

steps.title: Cap personal access token lifetime
body: Enterprise > Policies > Personal access tokens: set "Set maximum lifetimes for personal access tokens", require approval of fine-grained tokens, and restrict classic tokens from organization resources.

steps.title: Require approval for edits to secret files
body: Set chat.tools.edits.autoApprove with patterns such as "**/.env": false so those edits need explicit approval (a user setting).

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: MCP inputs sit in an encrypted store and PAT lifetime can be capped, but the editors issue no short-lived credentials to tools, the GitHub sign-in token's lifetime is not documented, and no admin control forbids static keys (local BYOK provider keys, API keys in MCP env files) — the BYOK concept page says local BYOK in IDEs can be disabled by an enterprise or organization policy without naming it. McpEnterpriseManagedAuthIdp (OAuth/OIDC IdP for enterprise-managed MCP authentication) is listed in the VS Code policy reference with a one-line description only. Keeping secrets out of model context relies on content exclusion (not honoured in VS Code Edit or Agent mode) and edit approval; agents read whatever the developer's environment holds.

original.mechanism: chat.tools.edits.autoApprove glob patterns, content exclusion for secret files, GitHub sign-in through the editor's account provider
original.note: No vault integration: agents read whatever the developer's environment holds. The vendor lever is to keep secret files out of context and out of auto-approved edits.

steps.title: Require manual review for edits to secret files
body: Set chat.tools.edits.autoApprove with patterns such as "**/.env": false so those files always need explicit approval.

steps.title: Exclude secret files from context
body: Add **/.env and credential paths to organisation or enterprise content exclusion.

controls.mechanism: managed-settings.json allowedMcpServers / deniedMcpServers (serverName, serverUrl with wildcards, exact serverCommand) with ChatAllowManagedMcpServersOnly; the registry restriction (MCP Registry URL, Registry only; McpGalleryServiceUrl in VS Code) matches names only and is what Visual Studio 2026, Eclipse and Xcode enforce

steps.title: Publish the enterprise MCP allowlist
body: In .github-private copilot/managed-settings.json set allowedMcpServers entries with serverUrl or serverCommand (pin package versions inside serverCommand, e.g. an exact npx package@version) and deniedMcpServers for hard blocks; keep "MCP servers in Copilot" enabled and set "Restrict MCP access to registry servers" to Allow all.

steps.title: Make VS Code ignore user and workspace allowlists
body: Set ChatAllowManagedMcpServersOnly (managed key allowManagedMcpServersOnly, VS Code 1.132+) to true so only the enterprise-managed allowlist can grant access.

steps.title: Treat the registry restriction as discovery
body: "Registry only" enforcement matches server name/ID and "can be bypassed by editing configuration files"; the cloud agent ignores it.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: an allowlist admits servers but pins nothing they serve. Nothing hashes or re-verifies tool definitions: VS Code re-shows its trust dialog when a non-workspace server's configuration changes (workspace servers inherit Workspace Trust even after their configuration changes), not when its tools change. Exact serverCommand matching that includes a pinned package version is version pinning for stdio servers only; remote (serverUrl) servers stay unpinned, and first-party servers such as the built-in GitHub MCP server are exempt from deny rules. The managed allowlist reaches VS Code and JetBrains; Visual Studio, Eclipse and Xcode enforce only the name-matched registry restriction. An MCP gateway supplies definition scanning and pinning.

original.mechanism: managed-settings.json allowedMcpServers / deniedMcpServers (name, URL wildcard, stdio command), ChatAllowManagedMcpServersOnly, McpGalleryServiceUrl registry, Visual Studio 2026 allowlist

steps.title: Publish the enterprise MCP allowlist
body: In .github-private/copilot/managed-settings.json set allowedMcpServers entries with serverName, serverUrl (wildcards allowed) or serverCommand arrays and deniedMcpServers for hard blocks; prerequisite is MCP servers in Copilot enabled and Restrict MCP access to registry servers set to Allow all.

steps.title: Make VS Code ignore user and workspace allowlists
body: Set ChatAllowManagedMcpServersOnly (managed key allowManagedMcpServersOnly) to true and ChatMCP to registry or none; point McpGalleryServiceUrl at a private registry if one exists.

steps.title: Treat the registry restriction as advisory
body: Registry-only enforcement matches on server name/ID and "can be bypassed by editing configuration files"; the cloud agent ignores it. Use it for discovery, not control.

original.note: Admission by identity: allowedMcpServers and deniedMcpServers with ChatAllowManagedMcpServersOnly. Admission is not integrity — nothing pins the tool descriptions a server returns or detects a changed implementation.

steps.title: Remove bypass and Autopilot
body: Set permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode to "disable": VS Code turns off chat.tools.global.autoApprove and it cannot be re-enabled; JetBrains honours the same key.

steps.title: Force approval on the operations that matter
body: Put Shell(git push *), Edit(/.github/workflows/**) and similar selectors under permissions.ask; a managed ask needs a fresh approval every time and cannot be satisfied by bypass, auto-approval, hooks or saved grants (Agent Host Copilot sessions).

steps.title: Remove the auto-approval paths in Local sessions
body: Set ChatToolsTerminalEnableAutoApprove=false and name tools under ChatToolsEligibleForAutoApproval so they always prompt.

steps.title: Kill bypass and Autopilot modes fleet-wide
body: Set permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode to "disable"; VS Code and the app then reject auto-approve settings, the CLI drops --yolo / --allow-all, and JetBrains blocks Bypass Approvals and Autopilot.

steps.title: Force approval on the operations that matter
body: Put Shell(git push*), Edit(**/.env) and similar selectors under permissions.ask; ask entries require a fresh approval every time and cannot be satisfied by saved approvals.

steps.title: Disable terminal auto-approval rules
body: ChatToolsTerminalEnableAutoApprove=false removes the regex-based terminal auto-approval, whose parser has documented gaps around aliases and complex syntax.

controls.mechanism: Enterprise custom agents (AI Controls, REST API), plugin standards (enabledPlugins, strictKnownMarketplaces), MCP Registry URL with "Restrict MCP access to registry servers", ChatStrictPluginOnlyCustomization

steps.title: Publish approved agents centrally

steps.title: Block unregistered customization in VS Code

settings.name: Require SAML authentication
settings.where: Enterprise › Settings › Authentication security › SAML single sign-on
settings.recommended: On, with MFA enforced on the GitHub app in your IdP (Enterprise Managed Users sign in through the IdP by design)
settings.why: Every Copilot sign-in is bound to an IdP session and its MFA, and tokens without a current SSO authorization stop reaching organisation data.

settings.name: Assign licenses (Enterprise Teams)
settings.where: Enterprise › Billing and licensing › Licensing › Copilot › Manage › Enterprise Teams › Assign licenses
settings.recommended: Licences assigned to enterprise teams synced from the IdP group that grants Copilot
settings.why: Joining or leaving the IdP group grants or removes the seat, so a leaver loses Copilot with their account rather than with a ticket.

settings.name: Enable enterprise access restrictions
settings.where: Enterprise › Settings › Authentication security › Enterprise access restrictions; your proxy injects the sec-GitHub-allowed-enterprise header
settings.recommended: On, with the header injected by your break-and-inspect proxy on github.com, api.github.com and *.githubcopilot.com
settings.why: On the corporate network Copilot works only with accounts your enterprise owns, so client code cannot leave under a personal or another company's licence.

settings.name: ChatApprovedAccountOrganizations
settings.where: VS Code device policy (ADMX, macOS profile or /etc/vscode/policy.json) → ChatApprovedAccountOrganizations
settings.recommended: ["your-org-login"] — your organisation logins
settings.why: VS Code's AI features stay off until the signed-in account belongs to one of your organisations (fail-closed); JetBrains, Xcode and Eclipse have no equivalent.

settings.name: Copilot Agent Mode in IDE Chat
settings.where: Enterprise › AI controls › Copilot › Configure features & clients
settings.recommended: Enabled everywhere, set at enterprise level rather than delegated
settings.why: Across a user's organisations the least restrictive value wins, so only the enterprise setting holds — and Disabled everywhere is the switch that stops agent mode in every IDE.

settings.name: Content exclusion
settings.where: Enterprise › AI controls › Copilot › Content exclusion (also organisation and repository Settings › Copilot › Content exclusion)
settings.recommended: Secret and key-material paths ("*.pem", "*.key", "**/.env*", "secrets*") and client-restricted repositories, set at enterprise level
settings.why: Excluded files never inform suggestions or chat answers; VS Code's edit and agent modes and Xcode and Eclipse chat ignore it, so it is minimisation, not a boundary.

settings.name: Copilot can search the web
settings.where: Enterprise › AI controls › Copilot › Configure features & clients
settings.recommended: Enabled
settings.why: Web grounding is part of the tool's value; the generated queries leave for the search provider, so regulated teams disable it at enterprise level.

settings.name: Editor preview features
settings.where: Enterprise › AI controls › Copilot › Configure features & clients
settings.recommended: Disabled everywhere; enabled for a pilot organisation once a preview has been reviewed
settings.why: Copilot connectors, the unified plugin marketplace and GitHub Environments arrive as previews, often before their admin controls; turning the policy off forces them off in VS Code.

settings.name: MCP servers in Copilot
settings.where: Enterprise › AI controls › MCP
settings.recommended: Enabled everywhere, with allowedMcpServers restricting which servers run
settings.why: GitHub's advice is to keep MCP on and restrict it; Disabled blocks every MCP server and connector in the IDEs, GitHub's own included.

settings.name: allowedMcpServers
settings.where: copilot/managed-settings.json in the enterprise's .github-private repository (or MDM) → allowedMcpServers
settings.recommended: Your approved servers matched by serverUrl or serverCommand, not serverName, plus the connector URLs you allow
settings.why: A server or connector not on the list never starts in VS Code or JetBrains; name-only entries are spoofable, so identity is enforced on URL or command.

settings.name: ChatAllowManagedMcpServersOnly
settings.where: VS Code device policy → ChatAllowManagedMcpServersOnly
settings.recommended: true
settings.why: VS Code decides which servers may run from the enterprise-managed allowlist alone, so a developer's own allow entries cannot widen it.

settings.name: Restrict MCP access to registry servers
settings.where: Enterprise › AI controls › MCP › MCP Registry URL and Restrict MCP access to registry servers
settings.recommended: Registry only, with a registry listing exactly the servers in allowedMcpServers
settings.why: The only MCP allowlist Visual Studio, Eclipse and Xcode enforce; it matches names and is bypassable by editing local config, so managed settings stay the boundary where supported.

settings.name: strictKnownMarketplaces
settings.where: managed-settings.json → strictKnownMarketplaces
settings.recommended: Your organisation's marketplace repositories only
settings.why: Plugins, which bundle agents, hooks and MCP servers, install only from your marketplaces; setting the key also turns off the built-in ones.

settings.name: ChatAllowManagedHooksOnly
settings.where: VS Code device policy → ChatAllowManagedHooksOnly
settings.recommended: true
settings.why: A cloned repository's hooks are commands that run on the developer's machine; only enterprise-managed hooks and policy-enabled plugins run.

settings.name: AllowedExtensions
settings.where: VS Code device policy → AllowedExtensions (extensions.allowed)
settings.recommended: Your approved extension list: GitHub Copilot Chat, and no other AI agent until it has been assessed
settings.why: Unvetted AI extensions, and the tools they contribute to agent mode, cannot be installed on managed VS Code.

settings.name: permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode
settings.where: managed-settings.json → permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode
settings.recommended: "disable"
settings.why: Removes Allow all in VS Code and JetBrains and turns chat.tools.global.autoApprove off; a disable from any policy layer cannot be relaxed.

settings.name: ChatToolsAutoApprove
settings.where: VS Code device policy → ChatToolsAutoApprove (chat.tools.global.autoApprove)
settings.recommended: false
settings.why: Global auto-approval is off in every harness, including Local sessions that managed permission rules do not reach.

settings.name: permissions.deny
settings.where: managed-settings.json → permissions.deny
settings.recommended: Deny secret paths: Read(~/.ssh/**), Read(~/.aws/**), Read(./.env*), Edit(//etc/**)
settings.why: Managed deny rules beat every mode and user rule in Copilot harness (Agent Host) sessions; Local harness sessions do not apply them.

settings.name: permissions.ask
settings.where: managed-settings.json → permissions.ask
settings.recommended: Shell(git push *) and Shell(gh pr merge *)
settings.why: A fresh approval that allow-all, assisted approval, hooks and saved grants cannot satisfy, kept for actions that leave the laptop.

settings.name: permissions.defaultMode
settings.where: managed-settings.json → permissions.defaultMode
settings.recommended: "manual" — developers may still pick assisted for a session
settings.why: New Agent Host sessions start by asking before edits and commands, rather than in whatever mode the developer last chose.

settings.name: Copilot Policy Hooks
settings.where: Machine-wide policy hook files, loaded by Copilot harness sessions in VS Code
settings.recommended: An admin-owned preToolUse hook denying secret-path reads and uploads to unapproved hosts, plus postToolUse logging
settings.why: Runs on the host before each tool call whatever the user or repository configures; Local harness sessions don't load it and timeouts fail open.

settings.name: sandbox.enabled with sandbox.failIfUnavailable
settings.where: managed-settings.json → sandbox.enabled, sandbox.failIfUnavailable
settings.recommended: true / true
settings.why: Agent Host terminal commands run in the OS sandbox and are refused if it cannot be enforced; allowBypass stays on for one-off approvals, which regulated teams turn off.

settings.name: sandbox.userPolicy.network.allowedHosts
settings.where: managed-settings.json → sandbox.userPolicy.network.allowedHosts
settings.recommended: Your source host, package mirror and approved internal hosts
settings.why: Sandboxed commands reach only listed hosts, so an injected curl to a paste site fails and installs go through your mirror; Windows relies on programs honouring the proxy.

settings.name: telemetry
settings.where: managed-settings.json → telemetry (enabled, endpoint, capture)
settings.recommended: enabled true to your OTLP collector, capture.identity true, every content class false
settings.why: Each agent turn and tool call reaches your collector attributed to user and machine, without prompts or code in the pipeline; VS Code's CopilotOtel* policies carry the same keys.

settings.name: Audit log streaming
settings.where: Enterprise › Settings › Audit log › Log streaming
settings.recommended: On, to your SIEM
settings.why: Copilot policy, licence, content-exclusion and agent events (action:copilot, actor:Copilot) outlive GitHub's 180 days and can be alerted on; client prompts are not in it.

settings.name: Copilot Usage Records Streaming
settings.where: Enterprise › AI controls › Copilot › Copilot Usage Records Streaming
settings.recommended: Enabled everywhere, into the audit-log stream, readable only by your investigations team
settings.why: Request and response bodies of Copilot API calls reach your SIEM — the only server-side record of what an agent was asked and answered.
settings.requires: Enterprise Managed Users or data residency (public preview)

settings.name: Copilot Memory
settings.where: Enterprise › AI controls › Copilot › Configure features & clients › Features
settings.recommended: Let organizations decide — off unless an organisation opts in
settings.why: Stored preferences are injected into later sessions (in VS Code, Local Agent Host sessions only); repository facts are governed separately under Repository access.

settings.name: Store local sessions in the Cloud
settings.where: Enterprise › AI controls › Copilot policies
settings.recommended: Disabled
settings.why: Synced session transcripts sit on GitHub under each user's personal account, where administrators can neither see nor delete them; VS Code's CopilotSessionSync policy follows it.

settings.name: remoteControl.mode
settings.where: managed-settings.json → remoteControl.mode
settings.recommended: "disabled"
settings.why: Nobody can steer a VS Code session on a developer's laptop, or answer its approval prompts, from another device; requireSSO is the option for teams that need it.

settings.name: forceRemoteSettingsRefresh
settings.where: managed-settings.json delivered by MDM or file → forceRemoteSettingsRefresh
settings.recommended: true
settings.why: VS Code starts Copilot only with current policy, so a tightened allowlist or bypass ban is not served from a stale cache; Copilot is unavailable offline.

settings.name: Set maximum lifetimes for personal access tokens
settings.where: Enterprise › Policies › Personal access tokens › Fine-grained tokens and Tokens (classic)
settings.default: 366 days for fine-grained tokens; none for classic
settings.recommended: 90 days for both token types
settings.why: Tokens developers paste into MCP configs and environment files expire instead of living for a year, or for ever with classic tokens.
