tools.family: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (Vertex AI Agent Engine)
tools.name: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform Agent Runtime (Vertex AI Agent Engine)

variants.name: Agent Runtime (ReasoningEngine resource): our agent code — ADK, LangChain, LangGraph, AG2, LlamaIndex, A2A or any container meeting the runtime contract — with Sessions, Memory Bank and sandboxes
Managed Agents API on Agent Platform (Agents API + Interactions API, Antigravity harness)
variants.note: Pre-GA and not for production or confidential data: a config-only agent (base_agent antigravity-preview-05-2026, global location only) in an isolated Linux sandbox per env_id with network off by default; an interaction's tools and MCP servers replace the agent's for that turn.

summary: Google Cloud's managed agent runtime, renamed on 2026-04-22 from Vertex AI Agent Engine to Agent Runtime on the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (the API resource is still ReasoningEngine on aiplatform.googleapis.com). Our own agent code is deployed from source files, a Dockerfile, an Artifact Registry image or a Developer Connect Git link and served as query and streamQuery endpoints: the loop is ours, while the container, scaling (operations up to 7 days), Agent Platform Sessions, Memory Bank, the Code Execution, Shell and Computer Use sandboxes and telemetry are Google's. The Pre-GA Managed Agents API adds a config-only variant on Google's Antigravity harness.

Governance is Google Cloud's own control plane: a SPIFFE agent identity per agent with certificate-bound tokens, IAM allow, deny and Principal Access Boundary policies on it, Agent Registry as the inventory, Agent Gateway as a default-deny enforcement point for IAM Unified Access Policies, Model Armor and Semantic Governance (Preview), an org-policy constraint that pins agents to approved gateways, Model Armor floor settings over Gemini calls, revisions with percentage traffic split (Preview), OpenTelemetry into our project, VPC-SC, a PSC interface and CMEK. Missing: a runtime approval pause, a documented interrupt of a running query, and egress substitution of third-party credentials — the auth manager hands tokens to the agent's own process.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Google Cloud pay-as-you-go: Agent Compute $0.085 per vCPU-hour after 50 free hours a month and Agent Memory $0.009 per GiB-hour after 100 free GiB-hours, one SKU set for all Scale products (Runtime, Sessions, Memory Bank, sandboxes); model tokens are billed separately. The Managed Agents API is Pre-GA.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Whatever the agent's code calls: Gemini and Model Garden models on Agent Platform (locational, jurisdictional multi-region or global endpoints — a global endpoint may process anywhere and gives no residency guarantee) or an external model. Inference is inside Google, not behind our AI gateway; Model Armor floor settings are the tenant-side screen for Gemini calls.

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: The agent runs in a Google-managed network in a Google-owned tenant project, so its code, environment variables, session events, memories, sandbox files and telemetry sit with Google; a PSC interface routes its egress into our VPC, and an Agent-to-Anywhere gateway TLS-inspects every outbound call.

facts.label: Retention & training
facts.value: No training or fine-tuning on customer data without permission. Stateful by design: Sessions and Memory Bank keep data until TTL or deletion (see the memory row); for zero data retention, don't use sandbox snapshots, and Gemini calls carry abuse-monitoring prompt logging and 24-hour in-memory caching unless the page's conditions are met.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform (Build, Scale, Govern, Optimize); old Agent Engine URLs redirect to /scale

facts.label: Network requirements
facts.value: Public internet by default; a PSC interface (psc_interface_config with a network attachment on a /28 subnet and DNS peering) routes egress into our VPC; with VPC-SC the perimeter blocks public internet unless our VPC provides a proxy; an Agent Gateway binding sends all egress, platform APIs included, through the gateway.

facts.label: Naming
facts.value: 2026-04-22: Vertex AI became part of Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, Agent Engine became Agent Runtime and Agent Builder Sessions became Agent Platform Sessions; SDK 2.0.1 moved vertexai.agent_engines to agentplatform.Client().runtimes.

items.title: Make the gateway a floor, then choose it over revisions
body: A custom org-policy constraint on aiplatform.googleapis.com/ReasoningEngine (CREATE, UPDATE) can require spec.deploymentSpec.agentGatewayConfig.agentToAnywhereConfig.agentGateway to name an approved gateway, and a gateway binding forces identity_type AGENT_IDENTITY. Agent Gateway cannot be attached to agents that use revisions, cannot bind engines created before 2026-04-29, and every agent in a project and region must use the same egress gateway — plan projects around it.

links.title: Route Agent Runtime traffic through Agent Gateway

items.title: Set agent identity at creation and clean up bindings on deletion
body: identity_type AGENT_IDENTITY cannot be patched onto an existing engine. A redeploy creates a new reasoningEngines ID and so a new principal; deleting an agent leaves its IAM bindings as inactive grants. Grant baseline roles to the project principalSet and keep principal:// bindings for sensitive data.

links.title: Use agent identity with Agent Runtime

riskNotes.note: Without agent identity every agent in a project runs as the shared AI Platform Reasoning Engine Service Agent; Unit 42 (2026-03) and XM Cyber (2026-01) showed agent code reading that identity's token from the metadata server to reach buckets, sessions and memories beyond the agent's own.

Agent Registry auto-registers Agent Runtime agents only in their own project; agents in other projects need manual registration, and a non-A2A agent registers without endpoint, identity or skills. Deleting an agent leaves every binding to its principal in IAM policies, so delete-and-recreate pipelines leave orphaned grants.

Memory Bank writes LLM-extracted memories from conversation events and feeds them into later sessions; the docs name memory poisoning and point to Model Armor, which only screens what passes a gateway or a Gemini call.

Agent Registry does not introspect a manually registered MCP server's tools — tool-level policies match the toolspec.json we upload — and Model Armor passes tools/list unscreened, so a changed tool description is not caught.
The default split, trafficSplitAlwaysLatest, sends all traffic to every new revision the moment it exists; set a manual split before shipping.

CMEK does not cover display names, descriptions, service-account emails, class method names or environment variables, and content capture writes prompts, responses and user.id to Cloud Logging or Cloud Storage.

controls.mechanism: reasoningEngines list and get (console Deployments page with an Identity column, gcloud ai reasoning-engines describe), runtimeRevisions list, Agent Registry auto-registration of Agent Runtime agents plus registered MCP servers and endpoints; IAM on aiplatform.reasoningEngines.create / update / delete; custom org-policy constraints on aiplatform.googleapis.com/ReasoningEngine for CREATE and UPDATE

steps.title: Inventory from the platform
body: List agents with reasoningEngines.list (console Agent Platform Deployments page) and each agent's revisions with runtimeRevisions.list; put owner and environment in labels at deploy.

steps.title: Register the rest of the estate
body: SDK-deployed Agent Runtime agents register in Agent Registry automatically, same project only; register agents from other projects, MCP servers (with a toolspec.json) and endpoints with gcloud agent-registry services create.

steps.title: Gate who can deploy
body: Grant aiplatform.reasoningEngines.create, update and delete only to the release pipeline's identity — roles/aiplatform.user carries them — so a definition reaches the runtime only through review.

steps.title: Constrain what may be deployed
body: Apply a custom constraint on aiplatform.googleapis.com/ReasoningEngine with method_types CREATE and UPDATE (the documented example requires an approved Agent Gateway) with gcloud org-policies set-custom-constraint and set-policy.

controls.note: Native on the registry rule (as on toolBedrockAgentcore): a listable inventory of agents, revisions and identities, and the tenant gates create and update by IAM and org policy. Not an approval workflow: registration records, it does not approve, and anyone holding roles/aiplatform.user can deploy (XM Cyber's 2026 finding started from aiplatform.reasoningEngines.update). "Unregistered means denied" holds only for egress through an Agent Gateway. Auto-registration is per project, and a non-A2A agent registers without endpoint or skills. In the Managed Agents API an interaction can replace the agent's tools and MCP servers, so a call can run a configuration the registry never saw.

controls.mechanism: runtimeRevisions (an immutable snapshot on every versioned-field change), trafficConfig trafficSplitManual percentages or trafficSplitAlwaysLatest (the default), a per-revision query path; the Evaluation Service and online monitors beside the release (revisions are Preview, v1beta1)

steps.title: Set a manual split before shipping
body: Govern > Deployments > agent > Revisions > Manage traffic > Split mode Manual (trafficConfig trafficSplitManual) so a new revision starts at 0% instead of taking all traffic under Always latest.

steps.title: Evaluate the candidate revision first
body: Query it on runtimeRevisions/REVISION_ID:query, which bypasses the split, with Evaluation Service cases and simulated users, then raise its percentage.

steps.title: Watch and roll back by pointer
body: Run online monitors over the live traces (scored about every 10 minutes) and set the previous revision back to 100% in trafficSplitManual on regression.

controls.note: Partial: versioning, percentage canary and one-step rollback exist (Preview), but the evaluation is not in the promotion path — the Evaluation Service and online monitors score beside the release, nothing holds a split until they pass, and no automated rollback is documented. Rated partial where toolBedrockAgentcore is native because AgentCore's evaluation step sits in its promote flow; here moving traffic is an ordinary update. The default split sends 100% to each new revision, direct revision queries bypass the split, and an agent bound to Agent Gateway cannot use revisions, so an organisation chooses between the gateway's policy and canary releases. IAM grants, gateway policies and Model Armor templates are not versioned with the agent.

controls.mechanism: Agent Identity auth manager auth providers (3-legged OAuth per end user, 2-legged OAuth, API key) in a Google-managed vault, each gated by IAM on the agent's SPIFFE ID (roles/agentidentity.user on the provider), retrieved by the agent and attached by ADK; certificate-bound Google Cloud tokens (mTLS, DPoP beyond the gateway); Secret Manager references in env_vars

steps.title: Keep third-party credentials in auth providers
body: Create them with gcloud agent-identity auth-providers create (--three-legged-oauth-* for user-delegated access) and grant only this agent's principal roles/agentidentity.user on the provider.

steps.title: Keep Google API tokens bound to the agent
body: Leave the default Context-Aware Access policy on — do not set GOOGLE_API_PREVENT_AGENT_TOKEN_SHARING_FOR_GCP_SERVICES to False — so a token used outside the agent's runtime fails with 401.

controls.note: Partial on the vault rule applied to every vendor (toolBedrockAgentcore is native only on its gateway, which injects outside the agent): scoping is real — per end user (3LO), per agent (IAM on each provider) and, for Google APIs, bound to the agent's certificate — but the auth manager returns the credential to the agent's own process, where ADK sets the header; it is not substituted at egress. Decrypt-at-the-gateway is documented only for Gemini Enterprise connectors behind Agent Gateway. Secret Manager references in env_vars become environment variables of every instance, shared by all its sessions. Model-generated code runs in sandboxes with no ambient credentials; the agent's own function tools run beside the credential.

controls.mechanism: Agent Gateway in Agent-to-Anywhere mode (governedAccessPath AGENT_TO_ANYWHERE) enforcing IAM Unified Access Policies through IAP — default deny, allow and deny rules in CEL over the agent principal, MCP server, tool name and annotations, endpoint host, path and method, iamEnforcementMode DRY_RUN or ENFORCE — plus custom authorization extensions and Semantic Governance (Preview); custom constraint custom.allowlistedEgressAgentGatewaysForAgentEngine; Model Armor floor settings

steps.title: Create an egress gateway that authorises through IAP
body: Console Agent Gateway page > create in Agent-to-Anywhere mode with Access Authorization set to IAP; test with iamEnforcementMode DRY_RUN (denials logged to Cloud Audit Logs), then remove it to enforce.

steps.title: Write per-tool allow and deny rules
body: gcloud iam access-policies create with rules on destination.agent_registry.mcp_server.tool.name and tool.annotations.read_only_hint or destructive_hint, bound with gcloud iam policy-bindings create after turning off constraints/iam.managed.disableAccessPolicyBindings; deny overrides allow.

steps.title: Make the gateway binding mandatory
body: Enforce a custom constraint on aiplatform.googleapis.com/ReasoningEngine requiring agentToAnywhereConfig.agentGateway in an approved list (gcloud org-policies set-policy; up to 15 minutes to take effect).

steps.title: Set the Model Armor floor
body: gcloud model-armor floorsettings update --add-integrated-services=VERTEX_AI and --vertex-ai-enforcement-type=INSPECT_AND_BLOCK on the project; set template-conformance floors at the organisation or folder with the API.

controls.note: Native on the architecture rule: a declarative per-call policy evaluated by the provider at its tool gateway, default-deny, plus tenant floors — the org-policy gateway binding and Model Armor floor settings — that a builder without IAM admin on the gateway project cannot lower. CEL sees principal, destination, MCP method, tool name and annotations, not arguments: argument rules need a custom authorization extension (our service) or Semantic Governance, which is an LLM verdict in Preview, and there is no escalate-to-human outcome. The gateway sees network calls only; on Agent Runtime every tool is our code, so work done inside the agent's process, in sandboxes or by Google-side tools is outside it, and a result our application executes returns unevaluated. Unavailable to engines created before 2026-04-29 and to agents using revisions.

controls.mechanism: Memory Bank scope dictionaries isolating memories per identity; IAM Conditions on aiplatform.googleapis.com/memoryScope and aiplatform.googleapis.com/sessionUserId; memoryViewer / memoryEditor roles and the agent's default agentContextEditor; ttl_config (default_ttl, granular_ttl); memory revisions with rollback and disable_memory_revisions; DeleteMemory; Sessions ttl / expire_time

steps.title: Scope memories and restrict who reads them
body: Generate and retrieve with a per-user scope such as {"user_id": ...} and grant memory roles with a condition on api.getAttribute('aiplatform.googleapis.com/memoryScope', {}); sessions take the same condition on sessionUserId.

steps.title: Make memories expire
body: Set ttl_config.default_ttl (or granular_ttl create_ttl, generate_created_ttl, generate_updated_ttl) on the Memory Bank — without it memories never expire — and a ttl on each session (default 365 days).

steps.title: Audit and roll back
body: Keep revisions on (memory_revision_default_ttl 365 days), list them to see what was extracted, and call client.memory_banks.memories.rollback or delete on poisoned memories.

controls.note: Native on the memory rule: scope, write permission, expiry, rollback and deletion are all settable. Isolation holds only if our application derives scope and user ID from the authenticated user — both are request fields — and the default agentContextEditor role reaches all of that agent's own sessions and memories. Contents are not validated: memories are LLM-extracted and consolidated into later turns, and the docs put memory poisoning on Model Armor, which sees only what a gateway or template routes to it. Sessions and Memory Bank write no Cloud Logging entries of their own; global endpoints may process generation out of region.

controls.mechanism: The organisation's TPRM platform, consuming Google Cloud's compliance reports (Compliance Reports Manager), the services-in-scope and HIPAA covered-products lists, and the Agent Platform ZDR and Access Transparency pages

evidence.title: Google Cloud services in scope by compliance program (Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform: ISO 27001/27017/27018, SOC 1/2/3, PCI DSS, penetration testing; last modified 2026-07-16)
HIPAA covered products (Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, Model Armor listed)
Agent Platform and zero data retention
Access Transparency for Agent Platform (Agent Engine listed)
Google Cloud compliance resource center

controls.note: External: the assessment is the organisation's TPRM process; Google publishes the evidence. The platform is in scope for ISO 27001/27017/27018, SOC 1/2/3 and PCI DSS and on the HIPAA covered-products list, but Agent Runtime, Sessions and Memory Bank are not broken out, so confirm component scope in the reports and the BAA. Access Transparency covers Agent Engine. Pre-GA pieces — the Managed Agents API (no confidential data), revisions, Semantic Governance, agent identity — sit under Pre-GA terms. Re-assess on the platform's cadence: the April 2026 rename moved features between products and SDKs.

controls.mechanism: Agent Runtime containers per deployed agent (min_instances, max_instances, container_concurrency default 9) in a Google-managed network; Agent Platform sandboxes the agent's code creates — Code Execution (no network, state up to 14 days), Shell, Computer Use and custom containers (7 days) — each isolated by container sandboxing; Managed Agents API sandbox per env_id

steps.title: Run generated code in a sandbox, not the runtime
body: Create a Code Execution sandbox (client.sandboxes.create) for model-written code: limited file system, no network, no libraries beyond the preinstalled set.

steps.title: Tie sandbox lifetime to the session
body: Create one sandbox per session with config.ttl and delete it when the session ends (client.sandboxes.delete), pausing idle ones rather than sharing them.

steps.title: Separate trust boundaries by agent and project
body: One instance serves up to container_concurrency sessions at once, so deploy untrusted workloads as separate agents and projects rather than relying on the container between sessions.

controls.note: Partial on the isolation rule (a per-session sandbox, reclaimed after): the sandbox boundary is documented — each isolated from other sandboxes and the host, no ambient credentials — but per-session binding is our code's choice, sandboxes persist 7 to 14 days and can be shared, and the agent's loop and function tools run in runtime containers serving several sessions at once. Rated partial where toolBedrockAgentcore, a microVM per session around the loop, is native. installation_scripts run as root at build. Managed Agents API: one sandbox per env_id, shared by any interaction or agent passing the same env_id, 7-day TTL.

controls.mechanism: Agent Gateway Agent-to-Anywhere binding (agent_gateway_config.agent_to_anywhere_config) routing all agent egress, platform APIs included, through default-deny IAP access policies over registered endpoints or host/path rules; alternatively VPC-SC with PSC interface egress into our VPC; Code Execution without network; Managed Agents API base_environment.network.allowlist (off by default)

steps.title: Bind every agent to an egress gateway
body: Set agent_gateway_config.agent_to_anywhere_config.agent_gateway with identity_type AGENT_IDENTITY at creation (Terraform deployment_spec.agent_gateway_config), after allowlisting the Google API hostnames the agent uses, regional and mTLS variants included, or while policies are DRY_RUN.

steps.title: Allow only named destinations
body: Register endpoints in Agent Registry and grant iap.resources.egressViaIAP per agent principal; avoid base URIs, which admit a whole domain.

steps.title: Or close the perimeter
body: Put aiplatform.googleapis.com in a VPC-SC perimeter and give the agent a psc_interface_config network attachment, so any internet path is our proxy and Cloud NAT.

steps.title: Managed Agents API
body: Leave base_environment.network unset (no network) or list exact domains in network.allowlist; a domain of "*" is unrestricted.

controls.note: Native on the architecture rule: an exact-host (and path) allowlist enforced by Google around the runtime, default-deny, logged, and mandatory by org policy. It covers every outbound call from a bound agent. Not seen: Google-side tools such as Search grounding and url_context, sandboxes (governed by their own template's PSC interface or VPC-SC), and unbound agents — engines created before 2026-04-29 and agents using revisions. Without a gateway or VPC-SC an agent has public internet access. Pages disagree: manage-agent-access says VPC-SC is unsupported with Agent Gateway; the 2026-09-09 release note supports it for gateways created after 2026-09-08 with an ALL_TRAFFIC connectivity template — test before relying on both.

controls.mechanism: IAM Unified Access Policies at Agent Gateway by agent principal, MCP server, tool name and annotations, and endpoint host, path and method; IAM roles, deny policies and Principal Access Boundary on the agent identity for Google Cloud resources; the agent's tool list in its own code

steps.title: Scope tools per agent at the gateway
body: Allow rules naming destination.agent_registry.mcp_server.tool.name for each tool the agent may call (or tool.annotations.read_only_hint == true) and deny rules for destructive tools.

steps.title: Scope Google Cloud resources by the agent's principal
body: Grant roles on specific resources to the principal:// identifier and cap it with a Principal Access Boundary policy.

steps.title: Register MCP servers with their tool specs
body: Upload a toolspec.json when registering a server so tool-level rules have names to match.

controls.note: Native on the permissions rule (as on toolBedrockAgentcore): per-tool enablement and per-principal permission by operation and resource, enforced outside the model at the gateway and in IAM. Arguments are not in the policy language. The policies live in the gateway project and IAM, not in the agent's code, so the next revision cannot widen them — though a redeployed agent gets a new principal and loses per-principal grants. Tools that never leave the agent's process are bounded only by IAM; registration pins nothing a server serves. In the Managed Agents API an interaction's tools list replaces the agent's for that turn.

controls.mechanism: Agent Identity auth manager vault (API keys, OAuth client secrets, user tokens; IAM per auth provider); Secret Manager references for env_vars; auto-rotated 24-hour agent certificates with bound tokens and no service-account keys; iam.managed.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation; CMEK through encryption_spec; no vendor tunnel — private reach is a PSC interface network attachment

steps.title: Keep tool secrets in the auth manager
body: Register API keys and OAuth clients as auth providers (gcloud agent-identity auth-providers create) and grant use per agent principal, rather than putting values in env_vars.

steps.title: Reference Secret Manager for anything the code reads
body: Pass env_vars as {"secret": SECRET_ID, "version": VERSION} (same project only) and grant secretmanager.versions.access to the Agent Platform Service Agent, which fetches them at deployment.

steps.title: Run on short-lived credentials
body: Use agent identity — 24-hour certificates, bound tokens, no long-lived keys — and enforce iam.managed.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation for the pipeline and callers.

controls.note: Partial on the vault rule applied to every vendor (as on toolBedrockAgentcore): custody and lifetime are strong — a Google-managed vault gated per agent principal, 24-hour certificates, bound tokens — but the vault is not write-only: retrieveCredentials returns the value to the agent's process, and Secret Manager values become environment variables of every instance, which CMEK does not cover. Tunnel story: Google offers no outbound-only tunnel; a private MCP server is reached through a PSC interface network attachment in our VPC, which carries no token or TLS key to rotate — the control is who may change the attachment. Our application's own credential for the API is ours to federate.

controls.mechanism: No runtime approval pause. ADK tool confirmation (FunctionTool require_confirmation, request_confirmation, an adk_request_confirmation call answered with the same function_call_id) is experimental and not supported with VertexAiSessionService; an Agent Gateway custom authorization extension can hold a call

steps.title: Build the approval into the agent
body: Wrap consequential tools with require_confirmation so the run pauses on adk_request_confirmation and our front end answers with a FunctionResponse carrying the same function_call_id — on a session service that supports it, which Agent Platform Sessions (VertexAiSessionService) does not.

steps.title: Or hold the call at the gateway
body: Import a custom authorization extension (gcloud service-extensions authz-extensions import) whose service refuses a consequential tool call until our approval service has recorded a person's decision.

controls.note: Partial on the approval rule (as on toolBedrockAgentcore and toolOpenaiAgentsApi): the runtime has no approval primitive, so approval is our code on an attach point. ADK's confirmation binds to the exact call but is experimental and unsupported with the managed Sessions Agent Runtime pairs with, so on the managed stack the gate is our own logic or a gateway extension. Semantic Governance is an LLM verdict and Model Armor a classifier — neither is human approval. The Managed Agents API documents no approval step.

controls.mechanism: Model Armor templates on Agent Gateway — egress: MCP tools/call and prompts/get responses and tool execution errors, A2A v1 SendMessage, OpenAI-compatible LLM payloads; ingress: ADK streamQuery — with prompt-injection and jailbreak, malicious-URI and Sensitive Data Protection filters under INSPECT_AND_BLOCK; floor settings over Gemini generateContent (integrated service VERTEX_AI)

steps.title: Turn Model Armor on at the egress gateway
body: Create templates with pi_and_jailbreak_filter_settings ENABLED and enforcement_type INSPECT_AND_BLOCK, switch on Enable Model Armor on the Agent-to-Anywhere gateway, and grant the Service Extensions service agent roles/modelarmor.calloutUser and roles/modelarmor.user.

steps.title: Screen every Gemini call in the project
body: Floor settings with --add-integrated-services=VERTEX_AI and --vertex-ai-enforcement-type INSPECT_AND_BLOCK apply even when a generateContent call omits modelArmorConfig.

controls.note: Native on the guardrail rule (unlike toolBedrockAgentcore, whose documented output checks omit injection): returned tool content is classified at the gateway with a block and a logged verdict. Inspected: MCP tools/call responses and tool errors, A2A v1 SendMessage, OpenAI-compatible completions. Passed unscreened: tools/list, resources/*, notifications, MCP and A2A streaming (SSE), pre-v1 A2A, plain REST responses to function tools, and anything from an agent without a gateway. The floor covers Gemini generateContent only (not file uploads) and fails open when Model Armor is unreachable or errors; ingress screening covers ADK streamQuery only.

controls.mechanism: OpenTelemetry traces (GOOGLE_CLOUD_AGENT_ENGINE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY, OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN, OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT) to Cloud Trace with prompts and responses in Cloud Logging or Cloud Storage in our project; reasoning_engine_stdout / stderr logs; Agent Gateway telemetry; Cloud Audit Logs for sessions and memories; Log Router sinks

steps.title: Turn telemetry and content capture on
body: Set the three env_vars at deploy, or Deployments > Telemetry configuration > Configure: Enable instrumentation of OpenTelemetry traces and logs, and Enable logging of prompt inputs and response outputs.

steps.title: Enable Data Access audit logs
body: Turn on Data Access logs for aiplatform.googleapis.com: sessions.create, sessionEvents.append, memories.retrieve and related calls are DATA_READ / DATA_WRITE and off by default.

steps.title: Ship it off-platform
body: A Log Router sink to Pub/Sub, BigQuery or a Cloud Storage bucket in a separate project keeps a copy the agent's project cannot alter.

controls.note: Native on the tracing rule: spans for model calls and tool executions, grouped by session, land in our own project and can be exported. Instrumentation is opt-in and emitted by the agent's own framework, so a custom or compromised agent's trace is only as complete as its code; gateway telemetry and audit logs are the independent record. Prompts, responses and user.id are captured only with content capture on; Sessions, Memory Bank and Code Execution write no Cloud Logging entries of their own; Model Armor trace spans are Pre-GA. Not tamper-evident in the project: route to another one.

controls.mechanism: reasoningEngines.delete with force=true (console Deployments > Delete agent), removing the agent with its sessions and memories; IAM deny policy or binding removal on the agent's principal; deny rules in the gateway access policy; removing aiplatform.reasoningEngines.query from callers; sandbox delete

steps.title: Cut the agent off
body: Add an IAM deny policy naming the agent's principal (or a deny rule in the gateway's access policy), then remove its allow bindings and revoke callers' aiplatform.reasoningEngines.query.

steps.title: Decommission
body: client.runtimes.delete(name=..., force=True) or DELETE .../reasoningEngines/ID removes the agent and its child sessions and memories; then delete its sandboxes and the now-inactive IAM bindings.

controls.note: Partial on the kill-switch rule (toolBedrockAgentcore is native on StopRuntimeSession): disable and revoke are documented, but no operation interrupts a running query — Agent Runtime supports operations up to 7 days — and whether delete ends in-flight streams is not documented; IAM propagation time is not stated (delay not documented). Deleting the agent leaves its principal's bindings in place, and nothing cancels work handed to A2A subagents. Managed Agents API: DELETE the agent resource; its environment lasts 7 days after the last interaction.

controls.mechanism: IAM on the ReasoningEngine resource (a narrow invoker role with aiplatform.reasoningEngines.query and .get bound per agent); deploy permissions (reasoningEngines.create / update / delete) held by the release pipeline; IAM deny policies and Principal Access Boundary on agent identities

steps.title: Bind callers per agent
body: Create a custom role with aiplatform.reasoningEngines.query and aiplatform.reasoningEngines.get and bind it on each agent to the front end or calling agent that needs it, instead of a project-wide role.

steps.title: Keep deploy rights with the pipeline
body: Grant reasoningEngines.create, update and delete only to the release pipeline's service account; Agent Platform User (roles/aiplatform.user) includes create, so keep it off people in agent projects.

controls.note: Native on the authorisation rule: Google Cloud IAM administers who may query, deploy, change or delete each agent, per resource, with deny policies that win over grants, and the same IAM governs what the agent's own principal may reach. Boundary: project-level grants (Agent Platform User or Viewer) let any holder query every agent in the project, so per-agent scoping holds only once those are removed; end-user authorisation inside a session is the agent code's.

controls.mechanism: Per-agent max_instances (default 100, range 1–1000), resource_limits (default 4 vCPU, 4 GiB) and container_concurrency (default 9); sandbox config.ttl; project quotas

steps.title: Cap the agent's scale-out
body: Set max_instances in the runtimes.create / update config to the agent's expected load (e.g. 10) and keep resource_limits at the default unless the agent needs more.

steps.title: Expire sandboxes
body: Set config.ttl when creating a sandbox so it is removed when the TTL expires, even if the agent never calls delete().

controls.note: Partial on the resource-consumption rule: the deployer caps how many containers an agent can scale to and how large each is, and sandboxes can be made to expire, but there is no per-session or per-user budget for model tokens, tool calls or run time — a single query may run for up to 7 days — and model spend is bounded only by project quotas and billing alerts outside the runtime.

settings.name: identity_type=AGENT_IDENTITY
settings.where: runtimes.create / update config → identity_type
settings.default: The default identity (the Agent Platform service agent), unless a custom service_account is set
settings.recommended: AGENT_IDENTITY on every agent
settings.why: Each agent gets its own SPIFFE principal with certificate-bound tokens, so its grants, denials and log entries are its own rather than a shared service account's.

settings.name: GOOGLE_API_PREVENT_AGENT_TOKEN_SHARING_FOR_GCP_SERVICES
settings.where: runtimes.create config → env_vars
settings.default: Unset (the Google-managed Context-Aware Access policy binds tokens to the runtime)
settings.recommended: Unset — never False
settings.why: Keeps the agent's tokens unusable outside its own runtime, so a token lifted from logs or a tool response can't be replayed.

settings.name: Custom role with aiplatform.reasoningEngines.query and aiplatform.reasoningEngines.get
settings.where: IAM policy on the agent resource (gcloud beta ai reasoning-engines add-iam-policy-binding)
settings.default: Any principal with Agent Platform User or Viewer on the project can query
settings.recommended: A narrow invoker role bound on each agent to the front end or calling agent that needs it, not project-wide
settings.why: Only the named application or agent can query this agent; a project-wide user role lets any principal in the project drive every agent.

settings.name: aiplatform.reasoningEngines.create / update / delete
settings.where: IAM roles on the agent project
settings.default: Included in Agent Platform User (roles/aiplatform.user) as well as Admin and Editor
settings.recommended: Held only by the release pipeline's service account and a named few administrators; people get a role without create, update or delete
settings.why: Agent Platform User can deploy agents, so a broad user grant lets anyone ship an unreviewed agent; the pipeline then evaluates and records every revision.

settings.name: IAM deny policy on agent identities
settings.where: IAM deny policy for principalSet://agents.global.org-ORGANIZATION_ID.system.id.goog/*
settings.recommended: Deny reasoningEngines.create, .delete and .update, and IAM role changes, to all agent identities
settings.why: An agent steered by injected content can't deploy, alter or remove other agents or grant itself access; a per-agent deny is the fastest cut-off.

settings.name: Principal Access Boundary
settings.where: Organization › IAM › principalAccessBoundaryPolicies, bound to the agent principal set
settings.recommended: A boundary limiting agent identities to the agent's own projects
settings.why: A role granted by mistake elsewhere in the organisation still can't be used by an agent outside its boundary.

settings.name: Secret Manager references in env_vars
settings.where: runtimes.create config → env_vars → {"secret", "version"}
settings.recommended: Every credential the agent's code reads referenced from Secret Manager, never a literal
settings.why: Keys stay in Secret Manager under IAM and audit instead of in the deployment spec, its revisions and the pipeline's logs.

settings.name: Auth providers (auth manager)
settings.where: Agent Identity auth manager → auth provider per tool (3-legged OAuth, 2-legged OAuth or API key)
settings.recommended: One provider per third-party tool, 3-legged OAuth where the tool acts for a user, each granted only to the agents that call it
settings.why: Third-party tokens sit in a Google-managed vault gated by IAM on the agent's identity, not in code or environment variables.

settings.name: encryption_spec (Customer-managed encryption keys)
settings.where: runtimes.create config → encryption_spec.kms_key_name
settings.recommended: Google-managed keys; a Cloud KMS key only where a client contract requires key custody
settings.why: Data at rest is encrypted either way; CMEK adds revocable key custody at the cost of key operations.

settings.name: Memory Bank ttl_config (default_ttl)
settings.where: Memory Bank configuration → ttl_config.default_ttl or granular_ttl
settings.recommended: default_ttl of 30 days, longer only where the agent's purpose needs it
settings.why: Memories, including anything an injected session wrote, expire instead of steering the agent indefinitely.

settings.name: IAM Conditions on aiplatform.googleapis.com/memoryScope
settings.where: IAM binding of roles/aiplatform.memoryViewer or memoryEditor with a condition on the memoryScope API attribute
settings.recommended: Memory roles conditioned on the caller's own scope
settings.why: One user's memories can't be read or rewritten through another user's session.

settings.name: agent_gateway_config (agent_to_anywhere_config)
settings.where: runtimes.create config → agent_gateway_config.agent_to_anywhere_config.agent_gateway
settings.recommended: Bound to your Agent-to-Anywhere gateway on every agent, with identity_type AGENT_IDENTITY
settings.why: All of the agent's outbound calls, platform APIs included, pass the gateway's access policies and Model Armor.

settings.name: Restrict Agent Runtime to approved Agent Gateways (custom constraint)
settings.where: Organization policy → custom.allowlistedEgressAgentGatewaysForAgentEngine on aiplatform.googleapis.com/ReasoningEngine
settings.recommended: Enforced at the organisation, listing your approved gateways
settings.why: A deploy or update that omits the gateway, or names an unapproved one, is refused, so no agent ships with ungoverned egress.

settings.name: Access Authorization (Audit-only / Enforce policies)
settings.where: Agent Gateway › Governed Access Path Agent-to-Anywhere › Access Authorization; or iamEnforcementMode in the IAP authorization extension
settings.recommended: Enforce policies, after an Audit-only period on new gateways; failOpen false
settings.why: Requests with no explicit allow are blocked; in Audit-only the gateway lets everything through and only logs.

settings.name: IAM Unified Access Policies
settings.where: Google Cloud console › Policies, or gcloud / Terraform, bound to the gateway project
settings.recommended: Allow rules per agent for its MCP servers, tools and endpoints; deny rules on destructive tools
settings.why: Each agent reaches only the servers, tools and hosts it was approved for, decided at the gateway rather than in the agent's code.

settings.name: Model Armor templates on Agent Gateway
settings.where: Agent Gateway › Client-to-Agent and Agent-to-Anywhere template settings
settings.recommended: Prompt-injection and jailbreak, malicious-URI and sensitive-data filters on both directions, blocking
settings.why: Tool and MCP responses and user requests carrying injected instructions are screened at the gateway before the agent acts on them.

settings.name: Model Armor floor settings — Agent Platform (Inspect and block violations)
settings.where: Model Armor › Floor settings › Agent Platform, at the project
settings.recommended: Inspect and block violations on agent projects, after an Inspect only period
settings.why: Every Gemini call in the project is screened even when an agent isn't bound to a gateway.

settings.name: require_confirmation (ADK Tool Confirmation)
settings.where: Agent code → FunctionTool(..., require_confirmation=True)
settings.recommended: True on tools that send, pay, delete or change permissions
settings.why: The agent stops and waits for the user before a consequential tool runs; the feature is experimental, so test it on your session service.

settings.name: psc_interface_config
settings.where: runtimes.create config → psc_interface_config.network_attachment
settings.default: Not set (egress from Google's managed network)
settings.recommended: Your network attachment where agents reach private systems or run inside VPC Service Controls
settings.why: The agent's private traffic enters your VPC, where your firewall and proxy rules apply; it's required for internet access under VPC-SC.

settings.name: config.ttl (Agent Platform sandboxes)
settings.where: client.sandboxes.create → config.ttl
settings.default: Execution state kept up to 14 days (Code Execution)
settings.recommended: The session's expected length
settings.why: Generated code runs in a sandbox with no network, and its state and files are removed when the task ends, not two weeks later.

settings.name: base_environment.network.allowlist (Managed Agents API)
settings.where: Agents API → agent base_environment → network.allowlist
settings.recommended: Disabled, or named domains only — never "*"
settings.why: The managed harness's sandbox reaches only the hosts you list, so an injected instruction can't send data anywhere it likes.

settings.name: max_instances
settings.where: runtimes.create config → max_instances (with resource_limits and container_concurrency)
settings.recommended: Sized to expected load per agent (e.g. 10), with resource_limits left at the default
settings.why: A looping or abused agent can't scale to a hundred containers and run up compute and model spend before anyone notices.

settings.name: traffic_config (trafficSplitManual)
settings.where: runtimes.update config → traffic_config.trafficSplitManual
settings.recommended: trafficSplitManual — a new revision takes a small share first
settings.why: A bad revision reaches a slice of traffic and is rolled back by moving the split, not by redeploying.

settings.name: Agent Registry management boundary
settings.where: Agent Registry governance project → management boundary over the folder or organisation
settings.recommended: A boundary covering every project that deploys agents
settings.why: Agents deployed in any project appear in one inventory, so none runs unregistered.

settings.name: GOOGLE_CLOUD_AGENT_ENGINE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY
settings.where: runtimes.create config → env_vars
settings.recommended: "true" on every agent, routed to your SIEM through a log sink
settings.why: Traces, logs and metrics of each run and tool call land in your project without prompt or response text.

settings.name: OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT
settings.where: runtimes.create config → env_vars
settings.recommended: Off; EVENT_ONLY on agents whose investigations or evaluations need the text, with notice to users
settings.why: Prompts, responses and user IDs stay out of logs unless a team has a reason to keep them.

settings.name: Data Access audit logs (aiplatform.googleapis.com)
settings.where: Google Cloud console › IAM & Admin › Audit Logs › Agent Platform API
settings.default: Disabled (Data Access logs aren't written unless enabled)
settings.recommended: DATA_READ and DATA_WRITE on for agent projects, routed to your SIEM
settings.why: Records which principal queried, read sessions or changed memories, alongside the Admin Activity record of deploys and deletes.

advisories.title: Unit 42 "Double Agents": code in a deployed Agent Engine agent read the Reasoning Engine service agent's credentials from the metadata server and reached consumer buckets and Google-owned Artifact Registry images (no CVE; Google updated its docs and recommends a custom service account)

XM Cyber: a user with aiplatform.reasoningEngines.update deploys a tool that reads the Reasoning Engine service agent token from metadata, reaching memories, sessions, storage and logging (no CVE; Google: working as intended)

tools.name: Gemini in Chrome (with Chrome auto browse)

variants.name: Gemini in Chrome side panel (chat with tab context, desktop and iOS)
Chrome auto browse (multi-step tasks in the user's tabs, desktop)
variants.note: Experimental; US, English, 18+; for managed users only on the Workspace editions the admin article lists and only where GeminiActOnWebSettings allows it. Gemini Spark can drive it only when GeminiSparkSettings is 0.

summary: Gemini built into Google Chrome: a side panel that answers with the content of the current tab (shared by default) and up to ten more tabs the user adds, and Chrome auto browse, where Gemini plans and runs multi-step tasks in the user's own browser — clicking, filling forms and, with the user's permission, signing in through Google Password Manager — with the same sites and sessions the user has. Inference is Google's; prompts, page content of shared tabs and auto browse actions leave the browser for the Gemini app service, and a task may finish in a remote browser in Google's cloud if the device goes away.

For a Workspace account it is part of the Gemini app core service, so it needs both the Admin console's Gemini app service status and Chrome's GeminiSettings policy on. Administrators shape it with Chrome Enterprise policies — GeminiSettings (on or off), GenAiDefaultSettings (whether Google may use the data to improve models), GeminiActOnWebSettings with GeminiActOnWebAllowedForURLs / BlockedForURLs (where auto browse may act) and GeminiSparkSettings — and with the Gemini app's conversation history, temporary chat, sharing and connected-apps settings, Vault, and Chrome Enterprise Premium DLP, which can single out transfers made by auto browse. The confirmation and take-over prompts are vendor-chosen; no policy adds an action class or forces a confirmation.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Core service with enterprise data protections on most Workspace Business, Enterprise, Essentials, Frontline, Nonprofit and Education editions; auto browse for managed users only on Business Standard and Plus, Enterprise Standard and Plus, AI Ultra Access, AI Expanded Access, Google AI Pro for Education and Gemini Education Premium. Users without a qualifying edition get it only under consumer terms if the admin grants that. Automatically blocked for customers who signed a HIPAA BAA.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Google's Gemini app service; no customer model, region or gateway choice. Auto browse uses the local Chrome or, when the device is unavailable, a remote browser in Google's cloud.

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: Prompts, page content of the current tab (shared by default) and of any tab the user adds, and for auto browse the pages visited and the information Gemini shares with sites to complete a task (name, contact details, files, preferences); Gemini may read a shared Workspace page directly from the user's Workspace account.

facts.label: Retention & training
facts.value: Workspace editions: prompts, tab context and responses are not used to train models or human reviewed outside the domain without permission; chats are kept per the Gemini conversation history setting (3, 18 or 36 months, default 18) and Vault rules, and sites auto browse visited are marked in Chrome history. GenAiDefaultSettings 0 lets Google use data to improve models for users outside that protection; 1 is the default for Admin-console-managed enterprise users.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: Chrome Enterprise and Education Help "Gemini in Chrome" (admin), Chrome Help "Use Gemini in Chrome" and "auto browse", the Chrome Enterprise policy list, and Workspace Admin Help Generative AI > Gemini app.

facts.label: Compliance scope
facts.value: The Workspace Gemini app page states Gemini in Chrome does not yet support HIPAA BAA, SOC 1/2/3, ISO/IEC 27001, 27017, 27018, 27701, 9001, 42001, FedRAMP High or BSI C5:2020.

items.title: Two switches and a default
body: Gemini in Chrome needs both the Admin console's Gemini app service (Generative AI > Gemini app > Service status) and Chrome's GeminiSettings (Devices > Chrome > Settings > Generative AI > Gemini integrations). Unset, GeminiSettings follows GenAiDefaultSettings, where 0 or 1 allow the feature and 2 blocks it; GenAiDefaultSettings can only be set in the Admin console. GeminiSettings alone turns Gemini in Chrome off while leaving the Gemini web and mobile apps on.

items.title: Where auto browse may act
body: GeminiActOnWebSettings 1 stops Gemini acting on web pages; GeminiActOnWebAllowedForURLs and GeminiActOnWebBlockedForURLs take URL patterns, URLs on neither list follow GeminiActOnWebSettings, and a URL on both is allowed. So an allowlist is GeminiActOnWebSettings 1 plus the allowed list, with the blocklist kept free of overlap. The policies govern acting, not reading: a tab the user shares is still read. GeminiSparkSettings (default 1) separately keeps the Gemini Spark agent from driving auto browse.

riskNotes.note: Google's own auto browse page lists injected instructions that post private data to a public site or forward Gmail to an outside service; its safeguards (prohibited-task recognition, site and action restriction to the task) are vendor-internal and "don't guarantee protection against all risks".
Auto browse acts in every site the user is signed into and can sign in to more through Google Password Manager with the user's permission; it has no identity of its own, so a site sees the user.

CVE-2026-0628 (Unit 42, fixed in Chrome 143.0.7499.192 on 2026-01-06) let a low-privilege extension inject code into the Gemini panel's WebView and inherit its file, screenshot, camera and microphone access; extension policy is part of this product's boundary.
The current tab is shared by default when a chat starts, and auto browse "may share your personal info with those sites"; only Chrome Enterprise Premium DLP inspects what leaves.

A personal Google account signed in to Chrome gets consumer Gemini in Chrome, auto browse included on Google AI Pro or Ultra, outside every Workspace setting; Chrome sign-in restriction is the boundary.

controls.mechanism: Google Workspace / Cloud Identity 2-Step Verification enforcement on the accounts signed in to Chrome; RestrictSigninToPattern and AllowedDomainsForApps (which injects X-GoogApps-Allowed-Domains) bind Chrome and Google services to corporate accounts

steps.title: Enforce 2-Step Verification
body: In the Google Admin console go to Security > Authentication > 2-step verification and set Enforcement to On for the organizational units that use Gemini, or enforce MFA in the federated IdP.

steps.title: Restrict Chrome sign-in to corporate accounts
body: Set RestrictSigninToPattern to a regular expression matching your domains, so a personal Google account cannot become the browser's primary account on managed browsers.

steps.title: Restrict Google services to your domains
body: Set AllowedDomainsForApps to your Workspace domains; Chrome then adds the X-GoogApps-Allowed-Domains header and refuses other Google accounts, consumer accounts included.

controls.note: Native on the MFA rule applied to Gemini CLI: Google's own account layer enforces the second factor for every member, and managed Chrome can be bound to corporate accounts. Boundaries: 2SV covers interactive sign-in; a long-lived Chrome session is not re-challenged before Gemini acts; an enforcement date or new-user enrollment period allows password-only sign-in until it ends; the sign-in policies hold only on managed browsers — an unmanaged browser with a personal account gets consumer Gemini in Chrome. Auto browse signing in to third-party sites uses those sites' own authentication, not this factor.

controls.mechanism: GeminiActOnWebSettings with GeminiActOnWebAllowedForURLs / GeminiActOnWebBlockedForURLs; GeminiSparkSettings; the Gemini app's Apps settings (Workspace apps, Other Google apps)

steps.title: Deny auto browse by default
body: Set GeminiActOnWebSettings to 1 for every organizational unit, so Gemini cannot act on any web page unless a URL is explicitly allowed.

steps.title: Allow named sites for the pilot
body: For the pilot organizational unit set GeminiActOnWebAllowedForURLs to the approved sites, and keep GeminiActOnWebBlockedForURLs free of overlap (a URL on both lists is allowed).

steps.title: Scope the apps Gemini can reach
body: In Admin console > Generative AI > Gemini app > Apps, keep Workspace apps on and turn Other Google apps (Maps, YouTube, Flights, Hotels) off.

controls.note: Partial on the rule applied to Claude in Chrome: the admin sets per-site act/don't-act lists Chrome enforces over the user, but a permitted site is fully actionable (no read-only tier, no per-action scope) and the lists govern acting, not reading a tab the user shares. The policy is delivered by Chrome management and holds only on managed browsers and accounts; a task that moves to the remote cloud browser is not documented as bound by the device's policies.

controls.mechanism: Vendor-chosen confirmations and take-over steps in auto browse; GeminiSparkSettings 1 keeps the autonomous Gemini Spark agent from driving Chrome

steps.title: Keep Gemini Spark off Chrome
body: Leave GeminiSparkSettings at 1 so the Gemini Spark agent cannot connect to Chrome and run auto browse without a person starting the task.

controls.note: Partial on the human-approval rule: a present user reviews the plan, then is asked to confirm sending communications, modifying data, submitting forms, scheduling events and visiting highly sensitive financial or health sites, and must take over to finalise payments, accept terms or create accounts. The set is vendor-chosen and phrased as "aims to ask"; no policy adds an action class or forces a confirmation, and "Let Gemini browse for you" is a user setting. Google states the user is responsible for Gemini's actions, including purchases.

controls.mechanism: Google Password Manager sign-in on the user's per-site permission (passwords not shared with Gemini); GeminiActOnWebBlockedForURLs and the allowlist keep auto browse off the sessions of unlisted sites

steps.title: Keep auto browse off high-value sessions
body: List banking, payroll, HR and admin-console domains in GeminiActOnWebBlockedForURLs so Gemini never acts in those signed-in sessions.

controls.note: Partial on the rule applied to Claude in Chrome: the vendor keeps passwords away from the model and asks per site before signing in, and the admin site lists deny the agent the sessions of listed sites, but auto browse otherwise uses every cookie in the profile and there is no policy that stops Gemini using saved passwords (PasswordManagerEnabled stops only new saves). No dedicated profile is provisioned by the product.

controls.mechanism: Vendor-internal prohibited-task recognition and site-and-action restriction; Safe Browsing required for auto browse (SafeBrowsingProtectionLevel)

steps.title: Keep Safe Browsing mandatory
body: Set SafeBrowsingProtectionLevel to 1 (Standard) as a mandatory policy; auto browse needs Safe Browsing on and known-malicious pages are blocked before Gemini reads them.

controls.note: Partial on the input-screening rule: Google documents vendor-internal defences against injected instructions (prohibited-task recognition, restricting actions to sites relevant to the task) that no administrator can tune or see verdicts from, and Safe Browsing screens only known-bad URLs. No Model Armor or inline hook is documented for Gemini in Chrome.

controls.mechanism: Gemini conversation history (on/off, 3/18/36-month retention); Allow temporary chats and Allow users to delete conversations

steps.title: Bound what Gemini remembers
body: In Admin console > Generative AI > Gemini app > Gemini conversation history keep history on and set Conversation retention to 3 months.

controls.note: Partial on the disable-only rule applied to Claude in Chrome: the admin can turn conversation history off or shorten it, but nothing scopes which pages may inform what auto browse "reviews" from earlier chats and shared details, or treats remembered content as untrusted. Turning history off also turns off Workspace apps in Gemini.

controls.mechanism: Chrome Enterprise Premium data protection rules with the Source Chrome context "Gemini in Chrome (auto browse)"; Chrome history marks sites auto browse visited

steps.title: Single out agent transfers
body: In a Chrome data protection rule, add the condition Source Chrome context = Gemini in Chrome (auto browse), with audit or block on uploads and pastes, so transfers the agent makes are recorded apart from the user's.

controls.note: Partial on the browser-activity rule: the vendor's own premium browser control can tell agent-originated content transfers apart and report them, but no export of every navigation, click and form entry auto browse made is documented, Chrome history is local to the profile, and the remote cloud browser's activity is outside it. Needs Chrome Enterprise Premium and Chrome Enterprise connectors.

controls.mechanism: Admin-set Gemini app Apps toggles (Workspace apps, Classroom app, Other Google apps) and GeminiSparkSettings over what Gemini in Chrome may connect to; browser enrolment in Chrome Enterprise Core for which managed browsers have it

steps.title: Fix the connected-app set
body: In Admin console > Generative AI > Gemini app > Apps, choose which app families Gemini may use; treat that page and GeminiSparkSettings as the record of what the browser agent can reach.

controls.note: Partial on the registry rule: the admin decides which app families and which agent (Spark) may connect, per organizational unit, and Chrome Enterprise Core lists the managed browsers, but there is no record per user of auto browse use, connected-app grants or sites signed in to; those are the user's own Gemini and Chrome settings.

controls.mechanism: SSE / CASB and browser management reporting; integration points are Chrome sign-in state on managed browsers and the X-GoogApps-Allowed-Domains header

evidence.title: Gemini in Chrome admin article (no report of personal-account use)
AllowedDomainsForApps

controls.note: External on the discovery rule: no Google page documents a report of staff using consumer Gemini in Chrome or auto browse under personal accounts; RestrictSigninToPattern and AllowedDomainsForApps prevent it on managed browsers rather than discover it. Use the SSE's generative-AI category and browser inventory for unmanaged browsers.

controls.mechanism: Gemini Apps Activity per user; Google Vault retention, hold, search and export of Gemini app prompts and responses

steps.title: Retain and export Gemini app conversations
body: In vault.google.com create a default retention rule for Gemini app with a retention period that matches your records policy, then search and export through Vault.

controls.note: Partial on the tracing rule: prompts and responses are retrievable centrally through Vault (Gemini in Chrome is part of the Gemini app service; the Vault page does not name Chrome, so confirm coverage), but auto browse's own steps — sites visited, clicks, form entries — are recorded only in the user's Chrome history with a Gemini icon, not in an export. Media files are not retained by Vault. The Gemini for Workspace log events page does not say it covers Gemini in Chrome.

controls.mechanism: Chrome Enterprise Premium real-time DLP rules on paste and upload, with the Gemini in Chrome (auto browse) context condition

steps.title: Block sensitive data the agent sends
body: Create Chrome data protection rules for your detectors (credentials, national IDs, client account numbers) with action Block on upload and paste, including the Gemini in Chrome (auto browse) context.

controls.note: Partial on the redaction rule: the vendor's premium browser DLP blocks matched content leaving through paste and upload, auto browse included, but it does not inspect the tab content Gemini reads when the user shares a tab, nothing masks a value, and it needs a Chrome Enterprise Premium licence. Workspace "DLP for Gemini" is a Drive control and does not apply to Gemini in Chrome.

controls.mechanism: GeminiActOnWebSettings 1 with GeminiActOnWebAllowedForURLs — an admin-set list of sites auto browse may act on, enforced by Chrome for the agent separately from the user's browsing

steps.title: Default-deny with an allowlist
body: Set GeminiActOnWebSettings to 1 and list approved sites in GeminiActOnWebAllowedForURLs; Gemini then acts only on those URLs, whatever the user asks.

steps.title: Block the sites that must never be driven
body: Add banking, payroll and admin-console URL patterns to GeminiActOnWebBlockedForURLs, without overlapping the allowlist.

controls.note: Native on the rule applied to Claude in Chrome: an admin-set allowlist of the sites the agent may work on, enforced by the browser for the agent and separable from the user's own browsing, with dynamic refresh. Boundaries: it governs acting on pages, not which sites a shared tab's content is read from; requests an allowed page makes itself are the page's; a task continued in Google's remote browser is not documented as bound by device policy; URL patterns follow the URLBlocklist format.

controls.mechanism: Admin-delivered site lists (GeminiActOnWeb*) the user cannot override; vendor-fixed prohibited and confirm-first action classes

steps.title: Deliver the site policy centrally
body: Set GeminiActOnWebSettings and its URL lists in Admin console > Devices > Chrome > Settings (or by MDM as mandatory policy) so users cannot change them.

controls.note: Partial on the rule applied to Claude in Chrome: site lists are admin-delivered and non-overridable, but the blocked and confirm-first action classes are vendor-chosen (no admin can add one), the user can turn browsing on or off for themselves within what policy allows, and judging "instructions from web content" is left to Google's classifiers.

controls.mechanism: The organisation's TPRM platform, consuming the Workspace Gemini app page's compliance statement and the Generative AI in Google Workspace Privacy Hub

evidence.title: Turn the Gemini App on or off — Gemini in Chrome compliance scope
Gemini in Chrome (admin) — data usage

controls.note: External on the rule applied to every vendor: the assessment lives in the organisation's TPRM process. Google states Gemini in Chrome does not yet support SOC 1/2/3, the ISO/IEC 27001 family, ISO 42001, FedRAMP High, BSI C5 or a HIPAA BAA — the main finding for a firm that relies on those reports. Reassess when auto browse leaves its experimental stage or the compliance list changes.

controls.mechanism: GeminiSettings 1 or GeminiActOnWebSettings 1 (dynamic refresh) per organizational unit; Gemini app Service status off in the Admin console

steps.title: Switch auto browse or Gemini off
body: Set GeminiActOnWebSettings to 1 to stop actuation, or GeminiSettings to 1 to remove Gemini in Chrome, for the affected organizational unit; changes take minutes and up to 24 hours.

controls.note: Partial on the kill-switch rule: both switches are reachable without the user and refresh dynamically, but no page says a task already running stops, propagation can take up to 24 hours, and a task Gemini moved to the remote cloud browser is not documented as reached by device policy. The user's own Stop and Take over task end a task immediately.

settings.name: 2-Step Verification — Enforcement
settings.where: Google Admin console › Security › Authentication › 2-step verification › Enforcement
settings.recommended: On for every organizational unit that uses Gemini, or MFA enforced in your federated IdP
settings.why: The account Chrome is signed in with — and so the sessions Gemini acts in — needs a second factor at sign-in.

settings.name: RestrictSigninToPattern
settings.where: Admin console › Devices › Chrome › Settings, or MDM → RestrictSigninToPattern
settings.recommended: A pattern matching your corporate domains, e.g. .*@example\.com
settings.why: A personal Google account can't become the managed browser's primary account and bring consumer Gemini in Chrome with it.

settings.name: AllowedDomainsForApps
settings.where: Admin console › Devices › Chrome › Settings, or MDM → AllowedDomainsForApps
settings.recommended: Your Workspace domains
settings.why: Chrome adds X-GoogApps-Allowed-Domains, so Google services, Gemini included, refuse consumer and other organisations' accounts on managed browsers.

settings.name: Gemini app — Service status
settings.where: Admin console › Generative AI › Gemini app › Service status
settings.recommended: On for the organizational units licensed and trained for Gemini
settings.why: Gemini in Chrome is part of the Gemini app; turning the service off for a unit removes it there with the web and mobile apps.

settings.name: GeminiSettings (Gemini integrations)
settings.where: Admin console › Devices › Chrome › Settings › Generative AI › Gemini integrations, or MDM → GeminiSettings
settings.recommended: 0 (Allow Gemini integrations) for Gemini-enabled units, set explicitly; 1 elsewhere
settings.why: The Chrome-side switch for Gemini in Chrome alone, refreshed without a restart — the fastest way to remove it from a unit.

settings.name: GenAiDefaultSettings
settings.where: Admin console › Devices › Chrome › Settings › Generative AI (Admin console only)
settings.recommended: 1 (Allow GenAI features without improving AI models)
settings.why: Chrome's generative AI features stay on without Google using prompts, inputs or outputs to improve its models; regulated teams set 2.

settings.name: GeminiActOnWebSettings
settings.where: Admin console › Devices › Chrome › Settings, or MDM → GeminiActOnWebSettings
settings.default: 0 / unset allows (the admin article says off by default for managed users) — set it explicitly
settings.recommended: 1 (Disallow), with approved sites in GeminiActOnWebAllowedForURLs for the pilot unit
settings.why: Auto browse can't act on any page that isn't explicitly allowed, so an injected page can't send it into the user's other signed-in sessions.

settings.name: GeminiActOnWebAllowedForURLs
settings.where: Admin console › Devices › Chrome › Settings, or MDM → GeminiActOnWebAllowedForURLs
settings.recommended: The internal apps and approved SaaS a pilot team uses auto browse on, widened as the pilot shows the need
settings.why: Gemini acts only on listed sites while GeminiActOnWebSettings is 1; reading a shared tab is unaffected.

settings.name: GeminiActOnWebBlockedForURLs
settings.where: Admin console › Devices › Chrome › Settings, or MDM → GeminiActOnWebBlockedForURLs
settings.recommended: Banking and payment sites, HR and payroll systems and your admin consoles — none of them also on the allowlist
settings.why: Gemini never acts in those signed-in sessions; a URL on both lists is allowed, so keep them disjoint.

settings.name: GeminiSparkSettings
settings.where: Admin console › Devices › Chrome › Settings, or MDM → GeminiSparkSettings
settings.why: The autonomous Gemini Spark agent can't drive Chrome auto browse in the user's live session; Google's own warning cites credential risk and lost context-aware signals.

settings.name: SafeBrowsingProtectionLevel
settings.where: Admin console › Devices › Chrome › Settings, or MDM → SafeBrowsingProtectionLevel (mandatory)
settings.recommended: 1 (Standard), mandatory
settings.why: Auto browse requires Safe Browsing, and known-malicious pages are blocked before Gemini reads or acts on them; Enhanced shares more browsing data with Google.

settings.name: Apps — Workspace apps / Other Google apps
settings.where: Admin console › Generative AI › Gemini app › Apps
settings.recommended: Workspace apps on; Other Google apps off
settings.why: Gemini can use the user's Gmail, Drive and Calendar under Workspace terms; Maps, YouTube, Flights and Hotels run under consumer Google terms.

settings.name: Gemini conversation history — Conversation retention
settings.where: Admin console › Generative AI › Gemini app › Gemini conversation history
settings.recommended: On, 3 months (the shortest offered)
settings.why: Chats, tab content shared into them included, are deleted after 3 months; turning history off would also switch off Workspace apps in Gemini.

settings.name: Allow temporary chats
settings.where: Admin console › Generative AI › Gemini app › Gemini conversation history
settings.default: On (without Vault for Gemini); Off (with Vault for Gemini)
settings.recommended: Off, unless a Vault retention rule covers the Gemini app
settings.why: Without Vault, Gemini logs nothing for a temporary chat, so there is no record of what a user asked or shared from a tab.

settings.name: Vault default retention rule — Gemini app
settings.where: vault.google.com › Retention › Gemini app
settings.recommended: A retention period matching your records policy for the Gemini-enabled units
settings.why: Prompts and responses can be held, searched and exported centrally even after users delete chats; Vault doesn't keep media files.

settings.name: Allow conversation sharing via link
settings.where: Admin console › Generative AI › Gemini app › Sharing › Conversation sharing
settings.recommended: Off
settings.why: A chat holding client page content can't be published to anyone with the link; Drive sharing (on by default) follows your Drive external-sharing settings.

settings.name: Chrome data protection rule — Source Chrome context "Gemini in Chrome (auto browse)"
settings.where: Admin console › Security › Access and data control › Data protection › rule with the Source Chrome context condition
settings.recommended: Audit every auto browse upload and paste; block your sensitive detectors (credentials, national IDs, client account numbers)
settings.why: Content the agent sends to a site is inspected and recorded separately from the user's own transfers.
settings.requires: Chrome Enterprise Premium, with Chrome Enterprise connectors on
