tools.name: Gemini CLI

variants.name: Gemini CLI (npm @google/gemini-cli, v0.61.0 stable 2026-09-23)

summary: Google's open-source terminal coding agent (Apache-2.0, npm @google/gemini-cli): a ReAct loop over built-in file, shell, web-fetch and search tools, MCP servers, hooks, extensions, sub-agents and skills, driven by a present developer. Inference is remote — Gemini via the Code Assist service (Google Workspace account with a Gemini Code Assist Standard or Enterprise licence and a Google Cloud project), a Gemini API key, or Vertex AI; the developer runs the harness on their own machine.

Prompts, file contents and tool output leave the device for the chosen Google endpoint; session transcripts, checkpoints and the shadow-git history stay under ~/.gemini. Usage statistics go to Google unless privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled is false; OpenTelemetry export is off unless telemetry.enabled is set, and logPrompts decides whether prompt text rides along.

Two admin planes. Locally, a root-owned system settings.json (/etc/gemini-cli, C:\ProgramData\gemini-cli, /Library/Application Support/GeminiCli) takes final precedence over user and workspace settings and carries tools.core, mcp.allowed, tools.sandbox, security.auth.enforcedType, security.disableYoloMode and telemetry.*; admin-tier policy TOML files under the same directory outrank every other policy tier. Remotely, the Enterprise Admin Controls page describes a Management Console (strict mode, extensions, MCP on/off, an MCP allowlist that strips local command/args/env, required MCP servers, unmanaged capabilities) that the client enforces and users cannot override — the console itself is reached through a go-link that resolves only to geminicli.com, so its location and licence gating could not be verified.

The consumer path is closing: the vendor's authentication page states that Gemini CLI was replaced by Antigravity CLI on 2026-06-18 for unpaid-tier and Google One users, and the Code Assist for individuals notice says Login with Google no longer serves the CLI for individual, Google AI Pro and Ultra tiers. Organisations stay on Code Assist Standard/Enterprise, an API key or Vertex AI.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Gemini Code Assist Standard (1,500 requests/user/day) and Enterprise (2,000) include the CLI, with quota shared with Code Assist agent mode; Gemini API key (unpaid 250/day Flash-only, or paid) and Vertex AI (express or pay-as-you-go) are the other paths. The quota page still lists the free Google-account tier, but the authentication page says that tier moved to Antigravity CLI on 2026-06-18.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Remote only: Code Assist API for licensed Workspace/Cloud accounts (needs GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT and the Gemini for Cloud API), Gemini API with GEMINI_API_KEY, or Vertex AI with ADC / service-account JSON / GOOGLE_API_KEY. GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL (API-key auth) and GOOGLE_VERTEX_BASE_URL (Vertex auth) redirect those calls through an organisation proxy; the Code Assist path has no documented base-URL override.

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: Prompts, context files, tool output and file contents to the model endpoint; anonymous usage statistics to Google (privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled, default true); OTLP telemetry to a local collector or Google Cloud Logging/Trace/Monitoring only when telemetry.enabled is set, with telemetry.logPrompts governing prompt text.

facts.label: Retention & training
facts.value: Code Assist Standard/Enterprise: stateless service, prompts and responses are not stored in Google Cloud unless the admin turns on logging to a Cloud Logging bucket; "Google doesn't use your data to train our models without your permission". API-key and Vertex paths fall under the Gemini API (unpaid/paid) and Google Cloud terms respectively.

facts.label: Enterprise admin planes
facts.value: System settings.json and admin policy TOML on the machine (GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH overrides the path); Management Console controls (strict mode, extensions, MCP allowlist and required servers, unmanaged capabilities) enforced by the client and non-overridable locally.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: geminicli.com/docs — Enterprise configuration, Settings reference, Policy engine, Sandboxing, Trusted folders, Hooks, MCP servers, Extensions, Telemetry, Terms & privacy.

items.title: Settings precedence and the system override file
body: Settings merge in the order system defaults (system-defaults.json), user (~/.gemini/settings.json), workspace (.gemini/settings.json), then the system override (settings.json in /etc/gemini-cli, C:\ProgramData\gemini-cli or /Library/Application Support/GeminiCli), which wins; arrays such as includeDirectories and objects such as mcpServers are merged rather than replaced. Environment variables and command-line flags sit above the files. GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH and GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_DEFAULTS_PATH relocate the system files, so pin them or the directory ACLs with MDM.

items.title: Policy engine tiers
body: Tool calls are decided by TOML rules (toolName, mcpName, argsPattern, commandPrefix / commandRegex, decision allow / deny / ask_user, priority 0-999, modes, interactive). Tiers are default 1, extension 2, workspace 3 (currently disabled), user 4, admin 5; admin rules in the system policies directory always outrank user rules, and a global deny removes the tool from the model's context. ask_user is treated as deny in headless runs. Out of the box, read-only tools are allowed and write tools and run_shell_command ask; yolo mode adds a high-priority allow-all rule.

items.title: Management Console controls
body: The Enterprise Admin Controls page lists Strict Mode (blocks yolo mode), an Extensions toggle, an MCP toggle, an MCP allowlist (locally configured servers not in the list are ignored, and the client clears command, args, env and cwd so only remote servers survive), Required MCP Servers (injected, overriding same-named local entries, with authProviderType / targetServiceAccount / oauth fields) and Unmanaged Capabilities (currently Agent Skills). All are described as enforced globally and immutable locally. The page's console link (goo.gle/manage-gemini-cli) redirected to the geminicli.com home page on 2026-09-10, so treat the delivery path as unverified.

riskNotes.note: GEMINI.md context files are loaded from the repository, its parents and any directory a tool touches; the first public exploit (Tracebit, 2025-07) hid instructions in a README.md the CLI pulled into context and chained a payload behind an allowlisted grep. Trusted folders keep workspace settings (and with them project hooks), .env files, MCP servers and custom commands off until the user trusts the folder; the page does not list GEMINI.md context loading among them, and nothing classifies the content.

--yolo and per-session "always allow" remain user choices unless the admin sets security.disableYoloMode / security.disableAlwaysAllow or Strict Mode; GHSA-wpqr-6v78-jr5g (CVSS 10.0) showed yolo mode ignoring the tool allowlist and headless runs trusting the workspace automatically.

Extensions install from any GitHub URL or local path and bundle MCP servers, hooks, commands, sub-agents and skills; only the admin extensions toggle and the MCP allowlist bound the source, and neither pins content.

API keys live in plaintext in .gemini/.env or shell profiles; telemetry.logPrompts defaults to true on the telemetry page, the settings reference states no default and the enterprise page recommends false, so set it explicitly in the system file.

controls.mechanism: Google Workspace / Cloud Identity 2-Step Verification enforcement (Admin console > Security > Authentication > 2-step verification > Enforcement) on the accounts holding Gemini Code Assist Standard/Enterprise licences; security.auth.enforcedType "oauth-personal" in the system settings.json pins the CLI to Sign in with Google; the X-GeminiCodeAssist-Allowed-Domains header pins the account domain

steps.title: Enforce 2-Step Verification on the licensed accounts
body: In the Google Admin console go to Security > Authentication > 2-step verification, select the organizational unit or group that holds Code Assist users, check Allow users to turn on 2-Step Verification and set Enforcement to On; keep the New user enrollment period short and leave Allow user to trust the device unchecked.

steps.title: Pin the CLI to Google sign-in
body: In the system settings.json (/etc/gemini-cli, C:\ProgramData\gemini-cli or /Library/Application Support/GeminiCli) set security.auth.enforcedType to "oauth-personal"; a user configured for another method is prompted to switch, and non-interactive runs exit with an error.

steps.title: Pin the account domain
body: On the organisation's TLS-inspecting proxy inject X-GeminiCodeAssist-Allowed-Domains with the organisation's domains into requests to https://cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com, so the Code Assist backend rejects any other Google account.

controls.note: Rated native: the vendor's own account layer can require the second factor for every org member, and the client can be pinned to that account. 2SV is enforced by Google sign-in for Google-managed Workspace or Cloud Identity accounts; where the organisation federates to a third-party IdP the second factor is that IdP's policy instead. It covers interactive Sign in with Google only. Paths that skip it: the locally cached OAuth credential reused by later and headless runs (its lifetime is not documented on the authentication page), GEMINI_API_KEY, Google Cloud API keys and Vertex service-account JSON keys. enforcedType makes the CLI refuse those, but it lives in a local file that a user with local administrator rights, or one who re-points GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH without the enterprise page's wrapper script, can bypass; the domain header binds only traffic that crosses the organisation's proxy. Consumer Login with Google stopped serving the CLI on 2026-06-18, so a personal account is refused by the service itself. A 2SV enforcement date or new-user enrollment period allows password-only sign-in until it ends.

original.mechanism: Google account sign-in gated by a Gemini Code Assist licence and Google Cloud project IAM; security.auth.enforcedType in the system settings file

steps.title: Force the organisation's auth path
body: In the system settings.json set security.auth.enforcedType (the enterprise page's example is "oauth-personal") so a mismatched cached credential triggers re-authentication rather than silently using an API key.

steps.title: Licence and project
body: Company, school and Workspace accounts need a Gemini Code Assist licence, GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT set, the Gemini for Cloud API enabled and IAM access on that project; without them Sign in with Google does not serve the CLI.

controls.mechanism: Admin-tier policy engine TOML in the system policies directory (toolName, mcpName, argsPattern, commandPrefix / commandRegex, subagent; decision allow / deny / ask_user); hooks.BeforeTool in the system settings as an organisation-written attach point

steps.title: Ship admin policies
body: Place [[rule]] TOML files in /etc/gemini-cli/policies (macOS /Library/Application Support/GeminiCli/policies, Windows C:\ProgramData\gemini-cli\policies), root-owned and not writable by group or others or the CLI ignores them; match shell calls with commandPrefix or commandRegex, MCP tools with mcpName, arguments with argsPattern, and set decision "deny" with a denyMessage.

steps.title: Add a BeforeTool gate
body: A hooks.BeforeTool command in the system settings receives tool_name and tool_input and blocks the call with decision "deny" or exit code 2; treat it as defence in depth behind the admin policy tier.

controls.note: Native: admin policies are declarative rules over tool name, arguments and target, evaluated by the harness before every built-in, MCP and sub-agent tool call, and the admin tier outranks extension, user and default rules (yolo's allow-all is a default-tier rule); supplemental --admin-policy and adminPolicyPaths files are ignored once the standard directory holds TOML. The decision is logged in the gemini_cli.tool_call telemetry event when telemetry is on. Boundary: enforced by the CLI on the device, per machine rather than per user principal; the enterprise page warns that a user with local administrator rights can circumvent its controls; an underscore in an MCP server name makes mcpName rules fail silently; a remote server's own downstream actions are outside it. Hooks are not admin-locked (project and user hooks rank above system hooks, /hooks disable-all turns them off, and non-JSON output is treated as allow). security.enableConseca (off by default) adds an LLM-generated per-prompt policy, non-deterministic and credited as a supplement only. The workspace policy tier is currently non-functional; the page gives the admin tier base 5 in its table and 4 in its text.

original.mechanism: Admin-tier policy engine TOML plus BeforeTool hooks in the system settings file

steps.title: Ship admin policies
body: Place [[rule]] files in /etc/gemini-cli/policies (or the macOS / Windows equivalents): admin tier 5 outranks user and workspace tiers; use commandPrefix / commandRegex for shell, mcpName for servers, decision deny with denyMessage.

steps.title: Add a BeforeTool gate
body: A hooks.BeforeTool command in the system settings receives tool_name and tool_input and blocks with {"decision": "deny"} or exit code 2. The hooks page ranks project and user settings above system settings for hooks, so treat the admin policy tier as the enforced layer and the hook as defence in depth.

original.note: The policy engine TOML is deterministic and admin-tiered; BeforeTool hooks are an integration point whose logic the organisation writes. Sub-agents and MCP tools pass through the same engine; a remote server's own actions are outside it.

controls.mechanism: The organisation's TPRM platform, consuming Google Cloud's Gemini certifications page and the Code Assist security, privacy and compliance page

evidence.title: Certifications and security for Gemini products in Google Cloud (SOC 1/2/3, ISO 27001/27017/27018/ 27701, ISO 42001 listed)
Security, privacy and compliance for Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise
Gemini CLI terms and privacy notices by authentication path

controls.note: External: the assessment is the organisation's TPRM process; Google publishes the evidence. The certifications page lists BSI C5, CSA STAR, HIPAA, HITRUST CSF, ISO 27001/27017/27018/27701, ISO 42001, PCI-DSS v4.0.1 and SOC 1/2/3 as compliant for Gemini products in Google Cloud (not for Code Assist on GitHub). The Code Assist Standard/Enterprise page describes a stateless service, no training on customer data without permission and VPC Service Controls, and the Code Assist Gemini CLI page says those practices apply to the CLI for Standard and Enterprise users. API-key (Gemini API unpaid or paid) and Vertex paths carry different terms, listed on the CLI's Terms and Privacy page, so assess the path the organisation enforces.

original.mechanism: Google Cloud terms and the Code Assist security, privacy and compliance page consumed by the organisation's TPRM platform
original.note: The CLI is covered by the Gemini Code Assist Standard/Enterprise commitments (stateless service, no training without permission, VPC Service Controls) when used with that licence; the API-key and Vertex paths carry different terms, listed on the CLI's Terms and Privacy page.

steps.title: Record which terms apply
body: Match the auth path the organisation enforces to its terms row on the Terms and Privacy page and file the Code Assist compliance page as the vendor evidence.

controls.mechanism: hooks.BeforeModel / AfterModel in the system settings as the attach point for an organisation inspector; security.environmentVariableRedaction for secret-named variables in tool environments; no vendor DLP

steps.title: Wire an inspection hook
body: Configure hooks.BeforeModel in the system settings to pass llm_request to the organisation's DLP inspector and return decision "deny" (or exit code 2) to abort the turn, or hookSpecificOutput.llm_request to rewrite it; add hooks.AfterModel to replace response chunks with hookSpecificOutput.llm_response.

steps.title: Redact secrets from tool environments
body: Set security.environmentVariableRedaction.enabled to true in the system settings (off by default) so secret-named and secret-valued variables are withheld from shell commands, and add names to security.environmentVariableRedaction.blocked.

controls.note: Partial on the rule applied to every vendor: BeforeModel is an inline hook that can hand prompt content to an organisation inspector and block; Gemini CLI itself detects nothing in prompts or tool traffic. Boundary: hooks run on the device and are not admin-locked (project and user hooks rank above system hooks, /hooks disable-all switches them off, non-JSON output is treated as allow). Environment redaction masks secrets in child-process environments (stdio MCP servers get it by default unless a variable is declared in the server's env block), not in content sent to the model. .geminiignore and context.fileFiltering keep files out of context — data minimisation, not detection. The inline alternative is an AI gateway at GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL / GOOGLE_VERTEX_BASE_URL (API-key and Vertex auth only; the Code Assist path has no documented base-URL override) or endpoint DLP.

original.mechanism: BeforeModel / AfterModel hooks for redaction; no vendor DLP
original.note: Hooks can rewrite the outbound request and filter the response, and inherited environment variables matching TOKEN / SECRET / PASSWORD / KEY patterns are redacted before MCP servers see them; content inspection of prompts and uploads is the organisation's own hook or a proxy at GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL.

steps.title: Wire a redaction hook
body: Configure hooks.BeforeModel and hooks.AfterModel commands in the system settings file to inspect and redact the request and response payloads.

controls.mechanism: hooks.AfterTool (a deny replaces the tool result the model sees) and hooks.BeforeModel as attach points for an organisation classifier; no vendor injection screening

steps.title: Screen tool results
body: Register a hooks.AfterTool command in the system settings that sends tool_response to the organisation's injection classifier; decision "deny" (or exit code 2) hides the real output and the reason text replaces the result sent back to the model.

steps.title: Screen the assembled request
body: A hooks.BeforeModel command receives llm_request, including context files, fetched pages and MCP results already in the conversation, and can return decision "deny" to abort the turn.

controls.note: Partial on the rule applied to every vendor: a post-tool hook that can block or replace output before the model sees it is an attach point; nothing classifies content until the organisation attaches a classifier. No injection or jailbreak classifier is documented. security.enableConseca judges proposed tool calls (credited under action policy); web_fetch's block on private and internal addresses and the policy engine's redirection check constrain actions; trusted folders and project-hook fingerprinting are admission. None of these screens content. Hooks are user-disableable and fail open (see the redaction row). GEMINI.md files load from the workspace, its ancestors and any directory a tool touches; treat them, MCP responses and fetched pages as untrusted. The external alternative is an AI gateway or MCP gateway classifier on the brokered path.

original.mechanism: Not offered; structural mitigations only

steps.title: Attach a detector in hooks
body: Register a BeforeModel hook in the system settings file that sends the assembled prompt (GEMINI.md context, MCP results, fetched pages) to your classifier and rejects on a hit; without it nothing detects an injected instruction.

original.note: Rated like Copilot CLI and the Copilot SDK: no injection or jailbreak classifier is documented, but BeforeModel and AfterModel hooks are the attach point for one, and the post-2025-07 shell-command validation blocks a class of injected commands. Trusted folders and ask_user policies contain; they do not detect. Treat every GEMINI.md, MCP response and fetched page as untrusted.

evidence.title: Vendor docs index, reviewed; no setting for this control (2026-09-10)

controls.mechanism: Admin-tier policy engine TOML (toolName, mcpName, argsPattern, commandPrefix / commandRegex, subagent); tools.core and per-server includeTools / excludeTools with mcp.allowed in the system settings; security.disableYoloMode and security.disableAlwaysAllow

steps.title: Scope tools in the admin tier
body: In /etc/gemini-cli/policies (or the macOS / Windows equivalent) write deny, ask_user or allow rules by toolName with argsPattern on the arguments or commandPrefix for shell commands, and mcpName plus toolName for MCP tools; admin rules outrank user, extension and default rules.

steps.title: Narrow the tool surface
body: In the system settings.json set tools.core to the permitted built-ins (for example ReadFileTool, GlobTool, ShellTool(ls)), define approved mcpServers with includeTools and list their names in mcp.allowed.

steps.title: Remove the bypass modes
body: Set security.disableYoloMode and security.disableAlwaysAllow to true in the system settings and keep security.enablePermanentToolApproval false.

controls.note: Native: admin-delivered rules over tool, arguments and target, enforced by the CLI outside the model, with yolo and "Always allow" removable by the administrator. Boundary: rules bind the machine, not the user principal (the subagent field scopes by calling sub-agent). tools.core and mcp.allowed live in the system settings file, which environment variables and command-line flags outrank: GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH can re-point it unless the enterprise page's wrapper script pins it, and --allowed-mcp-server-names and --allowed-tools are session flags whose interaction with mcp.allowed and admin rules is not documented. The admin policy directory is checked for root ownership and is not affected by that variable. tools.exclude is deprecated in favour of deny rules. The enterprise page warns that a user with local administrator rights can circumvent all of it.

original.mechanism: tools.core allowlist, tools.confirmationRequired, per-server includeTools / excludeTools, mcp.allowed / mcp.excluded in the system settings file

steps.title: Allowlist built-in tools
body: Set tools.core in the system settings (for example ReadFileTool, GlobTool, ShellTool(ls)); tools.exclude is deprecated in favour of the allowlist.

steps.title: Scope MCP tools
body: Define mcpServers centrally and set mcp.allowed to the same names, or users can add their own; trim each server with includeTools / excludeTools and keep trust unset so calls still confirm.

steps.title: Keep confirmation on specific tools
body: tools.confirmationRequired forces approval for named tools even when tools.allowed would skip it.

original.note: tools.core hides built-ins, includeTools/excludeTools hide MCP tools, confirmationRequired gates; argument limits come from the policy engine TOML, not these lists. YOLO mode must be disabled or it pre-approves everything.

controls.mechanism: tools.sandbox (docker / podman / runsc / lxc / sandbox-exec) or security.toolSandboxing in the system settings; SEATBELT_PROFILE on macOS; tools.sandboxNetworkAccess and tools.sandboxAllowedPaths. Credential paths: the same sandbox confining agent commands to the workspace; default redaction of secret-named variables for stdio MCP servers; security.environmentVariableRedaction for shell commands; GEMINI_CLI_HOME for shared runners

steps.title: Set a container sandbox
body: In the system settings.json set tools.sandbox to "docker", "podman" or "runsc" (gVisor, Linux), or to an object with command and image pointing at a hardened image in the organisation's registry.

steps.title: Choose a restrictive macOS profile
body: With sandbox-exec, set SEATBELT_PROFILE to a restrictive-* or strict-* profile in the environment the organisation's wrapper exports; the default permissive-open allows broad reads and network.

steps.title: Keep network and mounts closed
body: Leave tools.sandboxNetworkAccess false and tools.sandboxAllowedPaths empty in the system settings.

steps.title: Keep credential paths outside the sandbox
body: Run tools in the sandbox (by default it only has access to the current project workspace) and do not mount ~/.ssh, cloud CLI configuration or browser profiles through SANDBOX_MOUNTS; on macOS use a strict-* SEATBELT_PROFILE, which restricts reads as well as writes.

steps.title: Redact secrets from shell environments
body: Set security.environmentVariableRedaction.enabled to true in the system settings (off by default) and list extra names under security.environmentVariableRedaction.blocked.

steps.title: Scope what MCP servers receive
body: Stdio MCP servers get secret-named host variables (*TOKEN*, *SECRET*, *KEY*, *CREDENTIAL*) stripped by default; declare in each server's env block only the variables it needs, because declared variables skip redaction.

steps.title: Isolate shared runners
body: Set GEMINI_CLI_HOME per job so credentials, trust decisions and history do not leak between users on a shared machine.

controls.note: Partial: the sandbox is OS- or container-enforced but an administrator cannot require it. The sandbox page ranks the -s flag and the GEMINI_SANDBOX environment variable above the settings file, and GEMINI_SANDBOX accepts false, so a user can run unsandboxed; sandbox expansion requests let the user widen filesystem or network access per command; the Management Console has no sandbox control. A wrapper that exports GEMINI_SANDBOX and SEATBELT_PROFILE (the pattern the enterprise page uses for the settings path) raises the bar but is not enforcement. Inside the boundary in full-process mode: the CLI and the tools it spawns, with the workspace mounted at the same path. With security.toolSandboxing only individual tool executions are isolated and the CLI process stays on the host. Outside: remote MCP servers, the model endpoint and every unsandboxed run. Docker or Podman must be installed on each machine; Seatbelt is macOS-only, gVisor and LXC Linux-only, and the Windows native sandbox leaves persistent Low integrity labels. Credential paths: the product can keep credential paths out of sandboxed commands and strip secrets from child environments, but none of it is admin-requirable (the sandbox yields to -s and GEMINI_SANDBOX, as above) and there is no credential broker. Unsandboxed, run_shell_command inherits the developer's full credential set: the ssh-agent socket, the git credential helper, gcloud application-default credentials, ~/.aws, kube configurations and browser profiles; environment redaction removes variables, not files or sockets. Required MCP servers can authenticate with google_credentials or service_account_impersonation instead of a user token. The configuration reference names the redaction keys both security.environmentVariableRedaction.* and security.allowedEnvironmentVariables / blockedEnvironmentVariables; the settings table uses the former.

original.mechanism: tools.sandbox (docker / podman / sandbox-exec), Seatbelt profiles, tools.sandboxNetworkAccess

steps.title: Enforce a container sandbox
body: Set tools.sandbox to "docker" or "podman" in the system settings so tool execution runs in ghcr.io/google/gemini-cli (or a custom image via tools.sandbox.image) with the workspace mounted at the same path.

steps.title: Pick a macOS profile
body: On macOS the default Seatbelt profile is permissive-open; choose restrictive-* or strict-* and a *-proxied variant via SEATBELT_PROFILE when network must go through a proxy.

original.note: Inside the boundary: the CLI process and the tools it spawns, in docker, podman or a Seatbelt profile. Outside: remote MCP servers and the model endpoint. Docker and podman need the runtime installed on every developer machine; Seatbelt is macOS only.

original.mechanism: Per-user cached OAuth credential; Vertex AI service accounts; MCP OAuth per server; GEMINI_CLI_HOME for job isolation
original.note: The agent runs with the developer's Google identity and whatever shell credentials it inherits; required MCP servers can carry targetServiceAccount / authProviderType, and shared runners can point GEMINI_CLI_HOME at a per-job directory, but there is no on-behalf-of exchange for the agent itself.

steps.title: Isolate shared runners
body: Set GEMINI_CLI_HOME per job so credentials, trust decisions and history do not leak between users on a shared machine.

controls.mechanism: security.folderTrust.enabled; experimental.autoMemory (off, inbox review); admin policy rules over write_file / replace on memory files; general.checkpointing.enabled; context.fileName

steps.title: Require folder trust
body: Set security.folderTrust.enabled to true in the system settings; untrusted folders then skip workspace settings, .env files, MCP servers, custom commands and extension management. Do not ship GEMINI_CLI_TRUST_WORKSPACE=true or --skip-trust outside CI.

steps.title: Keep auto memory off
body: Set experimental.autoMemory to false in the system settings; when on, it drafts .patch candidates from past sessions into a /memory inbox that the user must approve.

steps.title: Gate memory-file writes
body: The agent saves memories by editing Markdown memory files with write_file or replace; add an admin-tier rule for toolName ["write_file", "replace"] with an argsPattern matching those files and decision ask_user or deny.

steps.title: Make edits revertible
body: Set general.checkpointing.enabled to true so a shadow Git snapshot is taken before each file modification and /restore can roll it back.

controls.note: Partial: agent-written memory can be switched off, its writes gated and reverted, but instruction sources cannot be locked and no content is validated. ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md is user-writable; project GEMINI.md files load from the workspace, its ancestors and, just in time, any directory a tool touches, with @file imports; context.fileName fixes the file names, not their contents; GEMINI_SYSTEM_MD replaces the whole built-in system prompt from any file (including through a trusted project's .gemini/.env) with no admin lock. Project hooks are fingerprinted and re-prompt when their command changes. The settings reference lists security.folderTrust.enabled as default true while the Trusted Folders page says the feature is disabled by default, so set it explicitly. Session transcripts persist under ~/.gemini/tmp; general.sessionRetention.* bounds them.

original.mechanism: Trusted folders gate context and .env loading; auto memory is experimental, off by default and approval-gated; checkpointing snapshots before edits
original.note: The settings reference lists security.folderTrust.enabled as default true while the Trusted Folders page says the feature is disabled by default; set it explicitly. The global ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md is user-writable and no admin lock is documented.

steps.title: Require folder trust
body: Set security.folderTrust.enabled to true in the system settings; untrusted folders then skip workspace settings, .env, MCP servers, extensions, custom commands and automatic context loading. Do not ship GEMINI_CLI_TRUST_WORKSPACE=true or --skip-trust outside CI.

steps.title: Keep auto memory off
body: Leave experimental.autoMemory false; when enabled it mines ~/.gemini/tmp/<project>/chats and proposes memory and skill updates that still need user approval.

original.mechanism: GEMINI.md hierarchy with context.fileName; GEMINI_SYSTEM_MD full replacement; trusted folders gate project context
original.note: GEMINI_SYSTEM_MD replaces the entire built-in prompt from any file and has no documented admin lock; project GEMINI.md files load from the workspace and any directory a tool touches, subject only to folder trust.

steps.title: Fix the context file names
body: Set context.fileName in the system settings to the reviewed file names the organisation uses and require folder trust so untrusted clones do not inject context.

controls.mechanism: Sign in with Google (cached, refreshable OAuth) forced with security.auth.enforcedType; $VAR / ${VAR} substitution in settings; admin-required MCP servers with google_credentials or service_account_impersonation; the system keychain only for extension settings marked sensitive

steps.title: Refuse static keys
body: Set security.auth.enforcedType to "oauth-personal" in the system settings.json so users on an API key or other method are prompted to switch to Google sign-in and non-interactive runs exit.

steps.title: Keep literals out of settings
body: Reference secrets as $VAR_NAME or ${VAR_NAME} in mcpServers env and headers so no settings file carries a literal token.

steps.title: Use Google credentials for corporate servers
body: Define Required MCP Servers with authProviderType google_credentials or service_account_impersonation (targetServiceAccount) instead of static headers.

controls.note: Partial: one credential path can be forced and it is short-lived, but storage is not hardened. The authentication page says Google sign-in credentials are cached locally without naming a keychain; MCP OAuth tokens sit in ~/.gemini/mcp-oauth-tokens.json; GEMINI_API_KEY, GOOGLE_API_KEY and service-account key paths come from the environment, shell profiles or plaintext .gemini/.env files. Only extension settings marked sensitive go to the system keychain. enforcedType is a local file setting with the bypasses listed under D3-MFA. Secret-named variables are withheld from stdio MCP servers by default and from shell commands when security.environmentVariableRedaction.enabled is on, which keeps them out of tool output the model reads; values declared in a server's env block pass through. The Required MCP Servers console location could not be verified.

original.mechanism: ${VAR} substitution in settings for MCP headers and env; automatic redaction of secret-named inherited variables
original.note: API keys are read from GEMINI_API_KEY / GOOGLE_API_KEY, shell profiles or a plaintext .gemini/.env; nothing vaults them, and variables declared explicitly in a server's env block (or by an extension) are trusted and skip the automatic redaction. Prefer Sign in with Google (cached OAuth) or Vertex ADC over long-lived keys.

steps.title: Reference secrets, do not inline them
body: Use "$VAR_NAME" / "${VAR_NAME}" substitution in mcpServers env and headers so the system settings file carries no literal tokens.

controls.mechanism: mcp.allowed / mcp.excluded with system-defined mcpServers (admin-owned command arrays) and per-server includeTools / excludeTools; the Management Console MCP allowlist; security.allowedExtensions and security.blockGitExtensions for extension-bundled servers

steps.title: Allowlist and define servers centrally
body: In the system settings define each approved server in mcpServers, with the package version written into the command for stdio servers, and list the names in mcp.allowed; without mcp.allowed users can add their own servers.

steps.title: Use the console allowlist where available
body: The Management Console MCP Servers allowlist ignores unlisted local servers, takes url, type and trust from the admin entry and clears local command, args, env and cwd, so only listed remote servers connect.

steps.title: Bound extension-bundled servers
body: Set security.allowedExtensions to regex patterns for approved extension sources, or security.blockGitExtensions to true, in the system settings.

controls.note: Partial on the rule applied to every vendor: an allowlist admits servers but pins nothing they serve. Gemini CLI does no tool-definition scanning, content hashing or re-verification after an update; its schema processing only strips properties for API compatibility. Because the system file's same-named definition wins, the admin's command array is authoritative, which pins a version for stdio servers only when the admin writes one into the command; remote servers, including everything on the console allowlist, are unpinned. Enforced by the CLI on the device, with the settings-file bypasses under AML.M0028; the console Extensions and MCP toggles switch whole features off. The console's location could not be verified (goo.gle/manage-gemini-cli resolves to the geminicli.com home page). v0.59.0 fixed an SSRF in MCP OAuth metadata discovery.

Admission is not integrity — no content-hash pinning or tool-definition scanning is documented. v0.59.0 fixed SSRF in MCP OAuth metadata discovery.

steps.title: Bound extensions

steps.title: Require approval on named actions

steps.title: Remove the bypasses
body: In the system settings set security.disableYoloMode and security.disableAlwaysAllow to true, keep security.enablePermanentToolApproval false, and list consequential tools in tools.confirmationRequired, which takes precedence over allowed tools and tools.core.

steps.title: Strict Mode
body: Where the Management Console is in use, Strict Mode (enabled by default) prevents yolo mode and cannot be overridden locally.

controls.note: Native: a present person approves each gated call in a confirmation dialog, an administrator can force ask_user on named actions, and yolo, "Always allow" and permanent approvals can be removed; in headless runs ask_user is treated as deny, so nothing is approved silently. Residual paths: auto_edit mode auto-approves edit tools unless an admin ask_user rule for write_file / replace outranks it; an MCP server with trust true skips confirmations (required servers default to trust true, and only system-defined or console servers put that flag under the administrator's control); --allowed-tools skips the dialog for listed tools but yields to tools.confirmationRequired. Approval is per call and has no expiry or identity binding beyond the local session.

On the network, SSE/CASB can match the User-Agent prefix GeminiCLI with its surface tag (terminal, vscode, zed). steps.title: Turn on Code Assist logging

steps.title: Enable Data Access audit logs

controls.note: Partial: the per-event export has the right content (tool calls with arguments and decision, approval mode switches, hook calls, ConSeca verdicts, correlated by session.id) but the user can turn it off: the telemetry page says environment variables override settings, and GEMINI_TELEMETRY_ENABLED set to anything but true or 1 disables it; GEMINI_TELEMETRY_OTLP_ENDPOINT and GEMINI_TELEMETRY_LOG_PROMPTS override likewise. The server-side records cannot be switched off by the user but cover only the Code Assist sign-in path and model traffic, not local tool decisions; the Code Assist logging pages state that recording is limited to interactions within an IDE while their sample entries carry client_name cloudcode_cli, so CLI coverage is unconfirmed. steps.title: Export telemetry centrally

steps.title: Turn on Code Assist logging

steps.title: Cut the licensed path
body: In Admin for Gemini select Manage Gemini Code Assist > Manage Subscription > License Management > Manage Automatic License Assignment, select the user and Unassign License (needs consumerprocurement.licensePools.unassign on the billing account); with automatic assignment on, remove the user's Gemini for Google Cloud User role on the project instead.

steps.title: Close the unlicensed paths
body: Set security.auth.enforcedType in the system settings so an API key cannot replace the revoked licence.

controls.note: Partial: an administrator can block new work from the Google control plane, but nothing documented stops a running session. Unassigning the licence or removing IAM fails later Code Assist calls; the delay is not documented, and cached OAuth tokens and in-flight turns are not addressed. With automatic licence assignment on, individual licences cannot be removed and a user with the required roles is reassigned on next use, so the IAM role is the lever. Management Console toggles (MCP, Extensions, Strict Mode) block features, not sessions; Turn off Code Assist only stops subscription renewal. API-key and Vertex paths are outside the licence. An EDR kill of the gemini process is the external complement.

original.mechanism: Licence and IAM revocation on the Google Cloud project; console MCP / extensions toggles; system settings tools.core
original.note: Removing the Code Assist licence or project IAM stops Sign in with Google sessions, but a developer with a Gemini API key keeps working unless security.auth.enforcedType and network egress rules deny that path.

steps.title: Cut the licensed path

evidence.title: Telemetry reference, gemini_cli.tool_call events (function_name, function_args, decision)
Sandboxing, container and sandbox-exec process model

controls.note: External: Gemini CLI does no process analysis of its own; EDR is the product class. EDR sees the node process running the npm package @google/gemini-cli (binary gemini), the shells it spawns for run_shell_command, stdio MCP server processes and, when sandboxed, the docker or podman container from ghcr.io/google/gemini-cli or the sandbox-exec wrapper. There is no processWrapper or launcher key; the enterprise page's wrapper script on PATH is the nearest launcher point. Correlate EDR events with the OTel gemini_cli.tool_call records (command text in function_args, session.id, user.email). A hooks.BeforeTool command can call a local EDR agent and deny on its verdict, an attach point that the user can disable.

original.mechanism: EDR around the process; BeforeTool hooks as the pre-tool-call integration point
original.note: Hooks in the system settings can call an endpoint agent before every tool call and deny on its verdict; otherwise watch for the sandbox container, writes under ~/.gemini and child processes of the gemini binary.

steps.title: Allowlist destinations in the proxy

None of it is admin-lockable: SEATBELT_PROFILE, GEMINI_SANDBOX_PROXY_COMMAND and GEMINI_SANDBOX are environment variables and the sandbox yields to them (see D3-EI). settings.name: 2-Step Verification — Enforcement
settings.where: Google Admin console › Security › Authentication › 2-step verification › Enforcement
settings.recommended: On for the organizational unit or group holding Code Assist licences, or MFA enforced in your federated IdP
settings.why: Interactive Sign in with Google for the CLI needs a second factor; a cached OAuth credential and API keys still skip it.

settings.name: security.auth.enforcedType
settings.where: System settings.json → security.auth.enforcedType
settings.recommended: "oauth-personal" (Sign in with Google on the licensed corporate account)
settings.why: The CLI refuses a personal Gemini API key or a Vertex service-account key; non-interactive runs with another method exit.

settings.name: X-GeminiCodeAssist-Allowed-Domains
settings.where: Corporate TLS-inspecting proxy → header on requests to cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com
settings.recommended: Your Workspace domains, injected for every managed device
settings.why: The Code Assist backend rejects any Google account outside your domains, so a personal account can't serve the CLI on the corporate network.

settings.name: X-GoogApps-Allowed-Domains
settings.where: Corporate TLS-inspecting proxy → header on requests to google.com
settings.recommended: Your Workspace domains
settings.why: Google sign-in on the corporate network accepts only corporate accounts, which the enterprise page names as the CLI's domain restriction.

settings.name: Enable Automatic License Assignment
settings.where: Google Cloud console › Admin for Gemini › Manage Gemini Code Assist › Manage Subscription › License Management
settings.recommended: Off — licences assigned to the group that grants Code Assist
settings.why: Under automatic assignment you can't remove one user's licence, so the licensed path can't be cut for a single person or leaver.
settings.requires: Gemini Code Assist Standard or Enterprise

settings.name: GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH
settings.where: Wrapper script ahead of the real binary on PATH (e.g. /usr/local/bin/gemini), or the system PowerShell profile
settings.recommended: Exported by the wrapper to your managed system settings.json
settings.why: Stops a user pointing the variable at their own file and loading the CLI without the organisation's overrides.

settings.name: privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled
settings.where: System settings.json → privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled
settings.recommended: false
settings.why: Usage statistics stop going to Google from managed devices, as the enterprise page's example configuration sets.

settings.name: general.sessionRetention.maxAge
settings.where: System settings.json → general.sessionRetention (enabled, maxAge)
settings.recommended: Enabled, "30d" — don't raise it
settings.why: Chat history under ~/.gemini holds client code and prompts; a longer period keeps more of it on every laptop.

settings.name: security.environmentVariableRedaction.enabled
settings.where: System settings.json → security.environmentVariableRedaction (enabled, blocked)
settings.recommended: true, with your vault and cloud token variable names in blocked
settings.why: Variables that look like secrets are redacted before commands and tools see them, so a token in the shell doesn't reach the model.

settings.name: hooks.BeforeModel
settings.where: System settings.json → hooks.BeforeModel
settings.recommended: Your DLP or AI-security inspector, returning decision "deny" on a match
settings.why: The assembled request is checked before it leaves for Google; a deny or exit code 2 aborts the turn. Project and user hooks rank above system hooks.

settings.name: hooks.AfterTool
settings.where: System settings.json → hooks.AfterTool
settings.recommended: Your injection classifier over web-fetch and MCP results
settings.why: A deny replaces the tool result the model would have read, so injected instructions in a fetched page or server response never reach it.

settings.name: experimental.autoMemory
settings.where: System settings.json → experimental.autoMemory
settings.recommended: false
settings.why: Keeps the background agent from writing durable memories from sessions that may have read injected content.

settings.name: security.folderTrust.enabled
settings.where: System settings.json → security.folderTrust.enabled
settings.default: true in the settings reference; the Trusted folders page says disabled by default — set it explicitly
settings.recommended: true
settings.why: An untrusted folder's workspace settings, .env files, MCP servers and auto-approvals don't load until the developer trusts it.

settings.name: System-wide policies (Admin)
settings.where: /etc/gemini-cli/policies/*.toml (macOS /Library/Application Support/GeminiCli/policies, Windows C:\ProgramData\gemini-cli\policies)
settings.default: None (default tier — read-only tools allowed, writes and shell ask)
settings.recommended: Root-owned rules that deny reads of secret paths and destructive shell prefixes, and ask_user before push or deploy commands
settings.why: Admin-tier rules outrank user, extension and default rules, so a developer's allow can't reopen what the organisation denied.

settings.name: security.disableYoloMode
settings.where: System settings.json → security.disableYoloMode
settings.recommended: true
settings.why: Removes --yolo, the one switch that runs every tool without a prompt, even when the flag is passed.

settings.name: Strict Mode
settings.where: Gemini CLI Management Console › Strict Mode
settings.recommended: Enabled
settings.why: Blocks yolo mode from the console, where a local administrator can't undo it.
settings.requires: Gemini Code Assist Standard or Enterprise

settings.name: security.disableAlwaysAllow
settings.where: System settings.json → security.disableAlwaysAllow
settings.recommended: false
settings.why: Developers can approve a repeated tool for the session; regulated teams set true so every call is confirmed.

settings.name: security.enablePermanentToolApproval
settings.where: System settings.json → security.enablePermanentToolApproval
settings.recommended: false
settings.why: An approval doesn't persist into future sessions and repositories, so it can't outlive the context it was given in.

settings.name: tools.sandbox
settings.where: System settings.json → tools.sandbox
settings.recommended: true — Seatbelt on macOS, Docker or Podman elsewhere
settings.why: Shell commands and file writes run confined to the project; the -s flag and GEMINI_SANDBOX take precedence over the file, so check for them.

settings.name: tools.sandboxNetworkAccess
settings.where: System settings.json → tools.sandboxNetworkAccess
settings.recommended: false
settings.why: Sandboxed commands get no network unless the developer approves an expansion; the CLI's own web fetch is unaffected.

settings.name: GEMINI_SANDBOX_PROXY_COMMAND
settings.where: Environment variable set by MDM, with SEATBELT_PROFILE=permissive-proxied on macOS
settings.recommended: Your allowlisting proxy script listing the package mirror and source hosts
settings.why: Network from the sandbox goes only to the domains the organisation lists, so an injected command can't reach an attacker's host.

settings.name: agents.browser.allowedDomains
settings.where: System settings.json → agents.browser.allowedDomains
settings.recommended: The default, plus your own source and documentation hosts
settings.why: The browser agent navigates only to listed domains instead of anywhere a page or prompt points it.

settings.name: agents.browser.confirmSensitiveActions
settings.where: System settings.json → agents.browser.confirmSensitiveActions
settings.recommended: true
settings.why: The browser agent asks before filling forms or running page scripts in a signed-in session.

settings.name: agents.browser.blockFileUploads
settings.where: System settings.json → agents.browser.blockFileUploads
settings.recommended: true
settings.why: The browser agent can't upload a local file to a website, a direct exfiltration path.

settings.name: MCP (Enabled/Disabled)
settings.where: Gemini CLI Management Console › MCP
settings.recommended: Enabled, with the console allowlist populated
settings.why: MCP stays usable for approved servers only; with the toggle off nobody can use any server.
settings.requires: Gemini Code Assist Standard or Enterprise

settings.name: MCP Servers (preview)
settings.where: Gemini CLI Management Console › MCP › MCP Servers
settings.recommended: Your approved remote servers, each with includeTools
settings.why: Locally configured servers not on the list are ignored and local command, args and env are cleared, so only the approved endpoints run.
settings.requires: Gemini Code Assist Standard or Enterprise

settings.name: Required MCP Servers (preview)
settings.where: Gemini CLI Management Console › MCP › Required MCP Servers
settings.recommended: Your corporate servers, with authProviderType google_credentials or service_account_impersonation
settings.why: Corporate servers authenticate with the user's Google credential instead of a static token pasted into local settings.
settings.requires: Gemini Code Assist Standard or Enterprise

settings.name: mcp.allowed
settings.where: System settings.json → mcp.allowed, with each server defined under mcpServers
settings.default: Unset (any server a user defines runs)
settings.recommended: Names of your approved servers, each defined in the system file with includeTools
settings.why: A server a user or repository adds is blocked, and a same-named one is overridden by the system definition.

settings.name: Extensions (Enabled/Disabled)
settings.where: Gemini CLI Management Console › Extensions
settings.recommended: Enabled, bounded by security.allowedExtensions
settings.why: Approved extensions stay usable; the console has no extension allowlist, so regulated teams leave it disabled.
settings.requires: Gemini Code Assist Standard or Enterprise

settings.name: security.allowedExtensions
settings.where: System settings.json → security.allowedExtensions
settings.recommended: Regex patterns for your approved extension repositories
settings.why: Extensions bundle MCP servers, hooks and commands; only those from your listed sources install or load.

settings.name: Unmanaged Capabilities
settings.where: Gemini CLI Management Console › Unmanaged Capabilities
settings.recommended: Disabled
settings.why: Agent Skills load instructions and scripts no admin control lists; ship approved skills inside allowlisted extensions instead.
settings.requires: Gemini Code Assist Standard or Enterprise

settings.name: telemetry.enabled
settings.where: System settings.json → telemetry (enabled, target, otlpEndpoint)
settings.recommended: true, exporting to your OTLP collector or target gcp in your project
settings.why: Each tool call, its decision and the API requests reach your SIEM; without it the only record is on the laptop.

settings.name: telemetry.logPrompts
settings.where: System settings.json → telemetry.logPrompts
settings.default: true (telemetry page); the settings reference states no default
settings.recommended: false
settings.why: Prompt text stays out of the telemetry stream while tool calls are still recorded, as the enterprise page recommends.

settings.name: Enable Data Access audit logs (cloudaicompanion API)
settings.where: Google Cloud console › IAM & Admin › Audit Logs › cloudaicompanion.googleapis.com
settings.recommended: DATA_READ and DATA_WRITE on in the Code Assist project, routed to your SIEM
settings.why: A server-side record of which principal called the Code Assist backend that the developer can't switch off; the page doesn't list CLI requests, so confirm they appear.
settings.requires: Gemini Code Assist Standard or Enterprise

summary: Google Cloud's employee assistant: chat and enterprise search grounded in connected data stores (Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Jira, Confluence, ServiceNow, BigQuery and many more, federated live or ingested into the app's index), web grounding, actions that create or send in connected systems, and an Agent Gallery of Google-made, employee-made and registered custom agents. Inference is Google's (Gemini, and Anthropic Claude models when the admin enables them), in global, US, EU or selected in-country locations; the app and its data stores live in the customer's Google Cloud project.

Administration is Google Cloud's: Discovery Engine IAM roles (project, app and data-store level), licences, the app's Configurations (Feature Management, Assistant, Observability), managed org-policy constraints that restrict connector data sources, egress domains and custom MCP data stores, Model Armor templates on prompts, responses and data-store content, Sensitive Data Protection content policies on ingestion and uploads, VPC Service Controls, CMEK and Access Transparency, and Cloud Logging for usage audit logs and OpenTelemetry traces. Retrieval honours source ACLs through the configured identity provider. Actions present a draft the user edits and sends; no admin setting forces or removes that step.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Business (1–500 users, administered from the Workspace Admin console), Standard, Plus, Pay-as-you-go and Frontline editions; seat licences are per project and location and assigned manually or automatically on first sign-in. Sensitive Data Protection content policies are not available on Business.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Gemini models chosen per app (some GA models cannot be turned off) and, if enabled, Claude Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 billed per token; app locations global, us, eu or in-country, with a warning before a model is routed to the global endpoint from an unsupported in-country region. Web grounding uses Google Search or the data-residency-compliant Enterprise web search.

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: Prompts, uploads and conversation content go to the Gemini Enterprise app in Google Cloud; federated connectors query the source live, ingestion connectors copy content into the app's index; third-party connectors call public endpoints outside Google, restricted by the egress-FQDN constraint and VPC firewall rules.

facts.label: Retention & training
facts.value: Assistant chat sessions are deleted after the admin's chat history retention period (1, 30, 60, 90, 120 or 180 days; default 60, counted from creation); user-requested deletions complete within 60 days. Prompt and response text reaches Cloud Logging only if the admin enables it. The training term is not stated on the admin pages read — confirm it in the Google Cloud service terms.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs — Administrator guide (apps, feature management, identity, licences, connectors, agents, Model Armor, Sensitive Data Protection, VPC-SC, CMEK, observability, audit logging) and the release notes.

facts.label: Compliance scope
facts.value: Standard and Plus editions list HIPAA, FedRAMP, ISO 27001/27017/27018/27701, SOC 1/2/3, PCI DSS and BSI C5:2020 among their certifications; CMEK (US and EU multi-regions only) and Access Transparency are not supported in the global location.

items.title: Who can reach which app
body: Project-level Gemini Enterprise User (roles/discoveryengine.agentspaceUser) opens every app in the project and overrides app-level policy. To scope users to one app, grant Gemini Enterprise Restricted User at the project and Gemini Enterprise User on the app; to scope data stores as well, bind both the app and the data store, since a user needs both to get answers from it.

links.title: Granular access controls for apps and data stores

items.title: Org-policy constraints on connectors
body: Three managed constraints shape what admins can connect: discoveryengine.managed.allowedDataSources (Restrict allowed data sources for data connectors), discoveryengine.managed.allowedEgressFqdns (Restrict egress domains for data connectors) and a constraint that blocks custom MCP data stores by default. Under VPC Service Controls, new data stores are blocked until the sources and egress domains are listed.

riskNotes.note: Include cross-domain documents lets users search Drive documents from outside the organisation, which the vendor flags as raising prompt-injection exposure; Model Armor screens data-store content with the user-prompt template only when the admin enables it.

Actions run with each user's own authorisation of the connected service (one Google connection covers both Calendar and Gmail), so a prompt-injected draft is sent with the user's authority once they click Send.
Ingestion connectors copy source content into the app's index; Sensitive Data Protection content policies can refuse matched content at ingestion, but nothing validates the rest.
Employee-made agents start Private and are visible to admins with discoveryengine.agents.manage, but with agent sharing without admin approval on they reach colleagues without review.

controls.mechanism: AllowedDomainsForApps / X-GoogApps-Allowed-Domains on managed Chrome or the proxy, binding Google sign-in to corporate domains; VPC Service Controls perimeter around the app; the allowed-egress-FQDN constraint for connector traffic

steps.title: Pin Google sign-in to your domains
body: Set the Chrome policy AllowedDomainsForApps (or inject X-GoogApps-Allowed-Domains at the proxy) with your Workspace domains, so other Google accounts are refused on managed devices and the network.

steps.title: Put the app inside a perimeter
body: Add the Gemini Enterprise project to a VPC Service Controls perimeter with Access Context Manager levels for your corporate network and devices.

steps.title: List the egress domains connectors may reach
body: Enforce discoveryengine.managed.allowedEgressFqdns with the FQDNs of each approved third-party connector's instance, authorisation and token URLs.

controls.note: Partial on the browser-pin rule applied to every vendor: Google honours a domain-allowlist header the organisation's managed browser or proxy injects and enforces it server-side at sign-in, and VPC-SC with access levels keeps the API surface to approved contexts. Boundaries: the header binds only traffic through managed Chrome or the proxy; with Workforce Identity Federation sign-in the third-party IdP's conditional access is the pin; a separate Gemini Enterprise project created by staff is not refused by the header.

controls.mechanism: Model Armor templates (with Sensitive Data Protection filters) on user prompts and responses; Sensitive Data Protection content policies on connectors and on files uploaded to the assistant

steps.title: Screen prompts and responses
body: In Gemini Enterprise > (app) > Configurations > Assistant, click Enable Model Armor and enter the resource names of templates for user prompts and response outputs, with Inspect and block.

steps.title: Refuse sensitive content at ingestion and upload
body: Create a Sensitive Data Protection content policy and apply it to each connector and to assistant uploads, so matched content is not indexed and violating files are not uploaded.

controls.note: Native on the redaction rule applied to Microsoft 365 Copilot: a vendor tenant control inspects prompts and responses for sensitive data types and blocks the turn server-side, and content policies keep matched source content out of the index. Boundaries: block only — Model Armor "does not remove or alter PII or mask sensitive data"; content policies need Standard edition or higher and don't apply to the older type of data store; federated sources are screened at serving, not ingestion.

controls.mechanism: Model Armor on the app: prompt-injection and jailbreak, malicious-URI and responsible-AI filters on user prompts, responses and out-of-the-box data-store content; Allow user interactions during Model Armor processing failure toggle

steps.title: Turn Model Armor on for the app
body: Enable Model Armor under Configurations > Assistant with templates whose enforcement type is Inspect and block (the console default); data-store content is screened with the user-prompt template.

controls.note: Native on the input-screening rule: an administrator-configured classifier screens prompts and retrieved content and blocks the turn, and its verdicts are in our Model Armor logs. Boundaries: "out-of-the-box data stores" are named, so custom MCP data stores and registered custom agents are not stated to be screened; latency rises; with the failure toggle on (the mode that keeps the service up), interactions pass unscreened while Model Armor is unavailable.

controls.mechanism: Actions create a draft (calendar event, email) that the user edits and sends; per-service authorisation before the first action

steps.title: Enable only reviewed actions
body: In Gemini Enterprise > Data Stores > (data store) > Actions enable only the actions a team needs; each produces a draft the user must send.

controls.note: Partial on the human-approval rule: a present person sees and sends each Google action's draft, but the admin can neither require approval for an action class nor see that it was given, and registered custom agents carry their own approval behaviour. Approval is per draft, not per tool call.

controls.mechanism: The app's Data Stores list (source, federation or ingestion, owner); Sensitive Data Protection content policies inspecting ingested content

steps.title: Inspect what is ingested
body: Apply a Sensitive Data Protection content policy to each ingestion connector, so content is inspected for your information types as it is indexed.

controls.note: Partial on the inventory rule applied to ChatGPT: the product lists every connected source and can inspect ingested content against detectors, but it does not inventory or classify the content behind federated sources or report oversharing; Google Cloud Sensitive Data Protection discovery or the source's own DSPM supplies that.

controls.mechanism: Connector OAuth and service credentials held by the app (re-authenticate per data store); per-user action authorisation; Workforce Identity Pool admin roles restricted; CMEK for the app and connectors

steps.title: Restrict who can change identity mappings
body: Grant IAM Workforce Identity Pool Admin and Workforce Pool Editor only to named administrators, through Privileged Access Manager, and alert on attribute-mapping changes.

controls.note: Partial on the credential rule: connector and user tokens are held by the service rather than the model, and the admin re-authenticates a data store's credential, but no page documents rotation, expiry or scope review of stored connector credentials, and a mis-set workforce pool mapping lets one user impersonate another.

controls.mechanism: Admin-created data stores with per-action enablement; allowedDataSources constraint; custom MCP data stores blocked by default; app- and data-store-level IAM

steps.title: Enable actions one by one
body: In Data Stores > (data store) > Actions select only the actions to enable; disable the rest.

steps.title: Restrict connector types
body: Enforce discoveryengine.managed.allowedDataSources with the approved source values (for example jira, box), leaving custom_mcp out except in projects that need it.

controls.note: Native on the tool-permission rule applied to ChatGPT: only admins create data stores, each action is enabled individually, and org-policy constraints refuse unapproved source types and custom MCP servers, enforced server-side. Boundaries: a custom MCP data store admits the tools its server ships; registered custom agents' own tools are outside these lists.

controls.mechanism: The app's Agents page (every Google-made, employee-made and custom agent with state Private, Enabled, Suspended or Disabled, owner and identity); Agent Registry import for A2A agents and MCP servers; skill and agent sharing approval

steps.title: Review the agent inventory
body: In Gemini Enterprise > (app) > Agents review each agent's state, owner and identity; register custom A2A agents and MCP servers through Agent Registry.

steps.title: Keep sharing reviewed
body: In Feature Management leave Enable skill sharing without admin approval and Enable agent sharing without admin approval off, so new shares queue for an admin.

controls.note: Native on the registry rule: the platform keeps an authoritative list of every agent in the app with owner, state and identity, and the admin approves sharing and can disable any agent. Boundaries: approval covers the first share only; a registered custom agent's SPIFFE ID shows only if its publisher published it.

controls.mechanism: Usage audit logs and OpenTelemetry traces in Cloud Logging and Trace (Configurations > Observability, optional prompt and response logging); Cloud Audit Logs for discoveryengine.googleapis.com

steps.title: Turn observability on
body: In Configurations > Observability turn on Enable instrumentation of OpenTelemetry traces and logs; decide Enable logging of prompt inputs and response outputs per your policy.

steps.title: Enable Data Access audit logs
body: Enable Data Access audit logs for discoveryengine.googleapis.com and route them to your SIEM.

controls.note: Native on the telemetry rule: interactions, the sources used for grounding and the actions triggered are exported to our project's logging, where a sink sends them on. Limits: sensitive fields are logged only with prompt logging on (otherwise <elided>); Workflow Builder and Deep Research agents have their own per-agent toggle.

controls.mechanism: SSE / CASB generative-AI category and Google Cloud organisation inventory (projects with the Discovery Engine API enabled)

evidence.title: Gemini Enterprise security overview (no report of unmanaged use)

controls.note: External on the discovery rule: Gemini Enterprise reports on the apps in our projects, not on staff using consumer Gemini or a Gemini Enterprise app in a project outside the organisation. Use Cloud Asset Inventory for discoveryengine.googleapis.com across the organisation and the SSE for the rest.

controls.mechanism: ACL-respecting retrieval through the configured identity provider (Google Identity or Workforce Identity Federation); app- and data-store-level IAM; the Include cross-domain documents toggle

steps.title: Configure the identity provider
body: Configure Google Identity (or Workforce Identity Federation for Microsoft 365 ingestion) so the app identifies each user and checks source permissions on every result.

steps.title: Scope data stores to the people who need them
body: Bind users to specific apps and data stores with resource-level IAM, and don't grant project-level predefined roles, which override them.

controls.note: Native on the retrieval rule applied to every vendor: retrieval honours source ACLs for the requesting user and the administrator decides which apps and data stores a user can reach. Limits: an ingested source's ACLs are as fresh as the last sync; changing identity provider loses chat history.

controls.mechanism: Discovery Engine IAM (Gemini Enterprise Admin, User and Restricted User; app- and data-store-level bindings); licence assignment

steps.title: Scope users to apps
body: Grant Gemini Enterprise Restricted User at the project and Gemini Enterprise User on each app.

steps.title: Assign licences deliberately
body: In Gemini Enterprise > Manage users, assign licences to named users rather than Assign licenses automatically.

controls.note: Native on the authorisation rule: IAM administers who uses which app, data store and admin function, and licences gate access per user. Project-level predefined roles override resource-level bindings.

controls.mechanism: Agent state Disabled or Suspended; Feature Management toggles; removing app IAM or licences; disabling the Discovery Engine API (destructive)

steps.title: Disable a misbehaving agent
body: In Agents set the agent to Disabled (hidden, unusable) or Suspended (visible with a notice); users can no longer interact with it.

controls.note: Partial on the kill-switch rule: the admin can stop an agent or a feature org-wide without the user, but no delay is documented and, for workflows, Google states runs already in progress continue to completion. Disabling the Discovery Engine API turns everything off but may delete the app's resources.

controls.mechanism: The organisation's TPRM platform, consuming the Gemini Enterprise compliance and security controls page and Google Cloud's compliance reports

evidence.title: Compliance certifications and security controls for Gemini Enterprise

controls.note: External on the rule applied to every vendor. Note for the assessment: CMEK and Access Transparency are not available in the global location, and partner (Claude) models are an additional processor path when enabled.

settings.name: Identity provider (Google Identity or Workforce Identity Federation)
settings.where: Gemini Enterprise identity configuration — Google Identity, or a Workforce Identity Federation pool
settings.recommended: Google Identity federated to your corporate IdP (SAML or OIDC); Workforce Identity Federation only for Microsoft 365 ingestion
settings.why: Every answer is checked against source permissions for an identified user; changing provider later loses users' chat history.

settings.name: Gemini Enterprise Restricted User / Gemini Enterprise User on the app
settings.where: IAM — roles/discoveryengine.agentspaceRestrictedUser at the project, roles/discoveryengine.agentspaceUser on each app
settings.default: Project-level User role opens every app in the project
settings.recommended: Restricted User at the project, User granted per app to the groups that need it
settings.why: An HR or deal-team app isn't reachable by everyone holding a licence in the same project.

settings.name: Assign licenses automatically
settings.where: Google Cloud console › Gemini Enterprise › Manage users
settings.recommended: Off — licences assigned to named users from your IdP group
settings.why: Automatic assignment licenses anyone with project access on first sign-in; manual assignment keeps the user list an access decision.

settings.name: IAM Workforce Identity Pool Admin / Workforce Pool Editor holders
settings.where: IAM — roles/iam.workforcePoolAdmin and roles/iam.workforcePoolEditor, through Privileged Access Manager
settings.recommended: A named few, as time-bound Privileged Access Manager entitlements, with mapping changes alerted in the SIEM
settings.why: Whoever edits attribute mappings can make one user appear as another and read their documents.

settings.name: AllowedDomainsForApps (X-GoogApps-Allowed-Domains)
settings.where: Chrome policy on managed browsers, or the header injected by your proxy
settings.recommended: Your Workspace domains
settings.why: Google sign-in on managed devices and the corporate network accepts only corporate accounts.

settings.name: VPC Service Controls perimeter
settings.where: Access Context Manager › perimeter around the Gemini Enterprise project
settings.recommended: The project inside a perimeter with access levels for your corporate network and managed devices
settings.why: The app's APIs and connected data can't be reached or copied from outside approved contexts; new data stores then need the source and egress constraints set.

settings.name: Restrict egress domains for data connectors (discoveryengine.managed.allowedEgressFqdns)
settings.where: Organization Policies › discoveryengine.managed.allowedEgressFqdns
settings.recommended: Enforced, listing each approved connector's instance, authorisation and token domains
settings.why: A connector can't be pointed at an arbitrary host to pull data in or send it out.

settings.name: Restrict allowed data sources for data connectors (discoveryengine.managed.allowedDataSources)
settings.where: Organization Policies › discoveryengine.managed.allowedDataSources
settings.recommended: Enforced, listing the connector types your firm has approved
settings.why: An admin can't add a data store for an unreviewed SaaS source, so the connected estate stays the reviewed one.

settings.name: Custom MCP data store constraint
settings.where: Organization Policies › managed constraint blocking custom MCP data stores (override per project)
settings.recommended: Blocked, overridden only for projects whose MCP servers are registered and reviewed
settings.why: An MCP server's tools reach the assistant only after someone has approved the server.

settings.name: Actions (Enable actions / Disable actions)
settings.where: Google Cloud console › Gemini Enterprise › Data Stores › (data store) › Actions
settings.recommended: Only the actions a team needs — read and draft-creating actions first; delete actions off
settings.why: Each write the assistant can make in a connected system is one an admin chose; the user still sends each draft.

settings.name: Enable Model Armor
settings.where: Google Cloud console › Gemini Enterprise › (app) › Configurations › Assistant
settings.recommended: On, with Inspect and block templates for user prompts and response outputs, including Sensitive Data Protection filters
settings.why: Injected instructions in prompts or retrieved content, malicious URLs and sensitive data in responses are blocked before the user sees them.

settings.name: Allow user interactions during Model Armor processing failure
settings.where: Google Cloud console › Gemini Enterprise › (app) › Configurations › Assistant
settings.recommended: On
settings.why: The assistant keeps working through a screening outage; regulated teams turn it off so nothing passes unscreened.

settings.name: Sensitive Data Protection content policies
settings.where: Sensitive Data Protection › content policy, applied to each connector and to assistant uploads
settings.recommended: A policy for your detectors (credentials, national IDs, client account numbers) on every ingestion connector and on uploads
settings.why: Matched content is never indexed and violating files never reach the assistant.

settings.name: Include cross-domain documents
settings.where: Google Cloud console › Gemini Enterprise › (app) › Configurations › Feature Management
settings.recommended: Off
settings.why: Drive documents from outside the organisation stay out of results, which the vendor names as a prompt-injection path.

settings.name: Enable web grounding
settings.where: Google Cloud console › Gemini Enterprise › (app) › Configurations › Assistant
settings.recommended: On — Enterprise web search (Data Residency compliant)
settings.why: Web answers stay available without sending generated queries to the standard Google Search index; regulated teams turn grounding off.

settings.name: Chat history retention period
settings.where: Google Cloud console › Gemini Enterprise › (app) › Configurations › Assistant
settings.recommended: 30 days
settings.why: Conversations holding client material are deleted sooner; tell users, since age counts from creation, not last use.

settings.name: Enable session sharing
settings.where: Google Cloud console › Gemini Enterprise › (app) › Configurations › Feature Management
settings.recommended: On
settings.why: Colleagues can share conversations inside the organisation; anyone shared with sees every prompt and response in it, generated content included.

settings.name: Enable skill sharing without admin approval
settings.where: Google Cloud console › Gemini Enterprise › (app) › Configurations › Feature Management
settings.recommended: Off
settings.why: A custom skill reaches colleagues only after an admin approves the share request.

settings.name: Agent state (Enabled / Suspended / Disabled)
settings.where: Google Cloud console › Gemini Enterprise › (app) › Agents
settings.recommended: Disabled is your incident runbook's first step for a misbehaving agent
settings.why: Stops one agent for everyone without touching the assistant; runs already in progress are not documented to stop.

settings.name: Enable instrumentation of OpenTelemetry traces and logs
settings.where: Google Cloud console › Gemini Enterprise › (app) › Configurations › Observability
settings.recommended: On, with a log sink to your SIEM
settings.why: Each request, the sources used and the actions it triggered are traced in your project instead of nowhere.

settings.name: Enable logging of prompt inputs and response outputs
settings.where: Google Cloud console › Gemini Enterprise › (app) › Configurations › Observability
settings.recommended: Off; turned on for an investigation, with log access restricted
settings.why: Usage audit logs still record who did what with prompt text elided; turning it on puts full prompts, PII included, into Cloud Logging.

settings.name: Data Access audit logs (discoveryengine.googleapis.com)
settings.where: Google Cloud console › IAM & Admin › Audit Logs › Discovery Engine API
settings.recommended: DATA_READ and DATA_WRITE on for the Gemini Enterprise project, routed to your SIEM
settings.why: A server-side record of every search, answer and data-store read by principal, beside the admin-activity record of configuration changes.
