tools.name: Gemini Enterprise Workflow Builder (chat agents and workflows)

variants.name: Chat agents (conversational, single or multi-step)
Workflows (steps, triggers, schedules, human-in-the-loop steps, MCP steps)

summary: The no-code / low-code builder inside the Gemini Enterprise web app (GA 2026-09-03): employees create chat agents and workflows from natural language or a visual editor, wire them to the app's connectors, MCP servers and other agents, simulate them, version them, schedule them or start them from connector events, and share them with colleagues or groups. Agents run in Google's service under the Gemini Enterprise app; scheduled and event-triggered runs use the author's delegated user credentials, which expire every 14 days.

Governance is the Gemini Enterprise app's: the Feature Management toggles (Enable chat agents, Enable workflows, agent sharing with or without admin approval, sharing with groups), the connectors, actions and MCP data stores the administrator provisions (the only tools an agent can use), the Agents page with its Enabled / Suspended / Disabled states, per-agent observability, and Model Armor on the app. There is no separate agent identity, no approval gate on new versions after the first share, and turning a workflow off lets in-progress runs finish.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Part of the Gemini Enterprise editions administered in the Google Cloud console; schedules are multi-region only.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Gemini agent steps run on the app's Gemini models in Google's service; MCP and connector steps call the systems the administrator connected.

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: Workflow definitions, run inputs and outputs and connector data stay in the Gemini Enterprise app; connector and MCP steps send data to those systems with the running user's (or, for schedules, the author's) authorisation.

facts.label: Retention & training
facts.value: As for the Gemini Enterprise app; workflow runs are listed in the Runs tab, and per-agent observability decides whether traces and prompt text reach Cloud Logging.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/workflow-builder — create, share, publish, versions, triggers, human-in-the-loop steps, MCP servers, quotas and known issues.

facts.label: Execution identity
facts.value: Scheduled agents execute using the author's delegated user credentials, valid 14 days and refreshed manually; shared users run with their own authorisation to data stores and connectors.

riskNotes.note: A scheduled or event-triggered workflow acts with its author's delegated credentials, so its output, shared with others, can carry data only the author could read.

By default workflow owners share with any user in the organisation without admin approval; only the initial share is ever reviewed, so a later version changes what colleagues run without a second look.
Mutative connector actions (create, send, delete) and MCP tools in a Gemini agent step are chosen by the model at runtime; approval steps exist only where the author adds them.
Event triggers start workflows from new emails, calendar events or files, so outside content reaches a Gemini agent step without a person in the loop.

controls.mechanism: Feature Management toggles (Enable chat agents, Enable workflows, Enable agent sharing, Enable agent sharing without admin approval, Enable End Users to share with Groups); IAM allow policies on each shared agent; app-level IAM

steps.title: Turn the builder on for the right app
body: In Gemini Enterprise > (app) > Configurations > Feature Management turn on Enable chat agents and Enable workflows only in apps whose users are cleared to build agents.

steps.title: Require review of shares
body: Keep Enable agent sharing without admin approval off so first shares queue for an app administrator.

controls.note: Native on the authorisation rule applied to Copilot Studio: the administrator decides who may build, whether sharing needs approval and whether groups can be targets, and each share is an IAM allow policy (up to 1,500 members). Boundary: approval covers the first share only.

controls.mechanism: No agent identity for employee-made agents; runs use the running user's or, for schedules, the author's delegated credentials

evidence.title: Workflow Builder quotas and limits — credential validity window
Agents overview — agent identity (SPIFFE ID for registered custom agents only)

controls.note: None on the agent-identity rule applied to Copilot Studio: an employee-made agent has no principal of its own — interactive runs authenticate as the user and scheduled runs as the author, with delegated credentials that expire after 14 days. Downstream systems see a person, not the agent. Where a workflow needs its own identity, build it as an Agent Runtime agent with agent identity and register it in the app.

controls.mechanism: The app's Agents page listing employee-made agents with owner and state; admin approval of first shares; administrators can transfer ownership

steps.title: Review employee-made agents
body: In Gemini Enterprise > (app) > Agents review employee-made agents by state and owner; Private agents are visible to holders of discoveryengine.agents.manage.

controls.note: Native on the registry rule: the platform keeps an authoritative list of every employee-made agent with owner and state, and admins approve sharing, transfer ownership and disable agents.

controls.mechanism: Draft and live versions, version history and restore, simulation in the Preview tab; admin approval of the initial share

steps.title: Gate the first release
body: Keep Enable agent sharing without admin approval off so a workflow's first share is reviewed before it reaches colleagues.

controls.note: Partial on the rollout rule applied to Copilot Studio. Met: versioning with a draft separate from the live version, simulation before turning on, restore of an earlier version. Not met: "subsequent workflow revisions don't need re-approval", so an author can turn on any new version for everyone already shared with; there is no percentage rollout.

controls.mechanism: Agents can use only the connectors, actions and MCP data stores the administrator provisioned; per-action enablement on data stores; allowedDataSources and the custom MCP constraint

steps.title: Provision only approved tools
body: Enable on each data store only the actions agents may call, and keep custom MCP data stores blocked except for reviewed servers.

controls.note: Native on the tool-permission rule applied to Copilot Studio: the actions and tools available to any agent "are limited to the data connectors, tools, and permissions provisioned by the Gemini Enterprise administrator", enforced by the service; an author cannot add a tool the admin didn't provision. Boundary: an MCP connector admits every tool its server ships.

controls.mechanism: Delegated OAuth per user, with author credentials for schedules valid 14 days; admin-registered OAuth client and scopes for custom MCP servers

steps.title: Narrow MCP OAuth scopes
body: When registering Gemini Enterprise as an OAuth client for a custom MCP server, grant only the scopes its tools need.

controls.note: Partial on the credential rule applied to Copilot Studio: credentials are held by the service and expire (14 days for schedules), but the agent borrows a person's authority rather than holding a scoped credential of its own, and no rotation or scope review is documented beyond the manual refresh.

controls.mechanism: Model Armor on the Gemini Enterprise app (Configurations > Assistant)

steps.title: Turn Model Armor on for the app
body: Enable Model Armor with Inspect and block templates on the app the builder runs in.

controls.note: Partial on the input-screening rule: Model Armor is admin-configured for the app, but its page names the assistant's prompts and responses and out-of-the-box data-store content, not Workflow Builder agent steps, event-trigger payloads or MCP tool results; confirm coverage in the Model Armor logs before relying on it.

controls.mechanism: Shared agents read data stores and connectors with each user's own authorisation; source ACLs preserved; app- and data-store-level IAM

steps.title: Scope data stores
body: Bind users to the apps and data stores they need with resource-level IAM; shared agents then return only what each user can read.

controls.note: Native on the retrieval rule applied to Copilot Studio: a shared agent run by a user retrieves with that user's permissions and ACLs are preserved. Boundary: scheduled and event-triggered runs use the author's credentials, so their outputs carry the author's view of the data.

controls.mechanism: Per-agent observability toggle (OpenTelemetry traces and logs, optional prompt logging) for Workflow Builder agents; the Runs tab

steps.title: Turn observability on per agent
body: In Gemini Enterprise > (app) > Agents > (agent) > Configuration turn on Enable instrumentation of OpenTelemetry traces and logs for each shared or scheduled agent.

controls.note: Partial on the tracing rule applied to Copilot Studio: traces land in our project when enabled, but the toggle is per agent, not an app-wide default, so a new agent is untraced until someone turns it on.

controls.mechanism: Agent state Disabled or Suspended; turning a workflow off (removes schedules and triggers); Enable chat agents / Enable workflows off

steps.title: Disable the agent
body: In Agents set the agent to Disabled; for a workflow, also turn its live version off so no new run starts.

controls.note: Partial on the kill-switch rule: the admin can stop new use and new runs without the author, but Google states that runs already in progress, simulations included, continue until they complete.

controls.mechanism: The organisation's TPRM platform, consuming the Gemini Enterprise compliance page

evidence.title: Compliance certifications and security controls for Gemini Enterprise

controls.note: External on the rule applied to every vendor; assessed with toolGeminiEnterprise, since Workflow Builder is a feature of the same app and service.

settings.name: Enable chat agents
settings.where: Google Cloud console › Gemini Enterprise › (app) › Configurations › Feature Management
settings.recommended: On in apps whose users are cleared to build agents
settings.why: Who can build conversational agents on the firm's connected data is a per-app decision; off removes building and use of custom chat agents.

settings.name: Enable workflows
settings.where: Google Cloud console › Gemini Enterprise › (app) › Configurations › Feature Management
settings.recommended: On in apps whose users are cleared to build agents
settings.why: Workflows run on schedules and connector events with the author's credentials; enabling them is the decision to allow unattended automation.

settings.name: Enable agent sharing
settings.where: Google Cloud console › Gemini Enterprise › (app) › Configurations › Feature Management
settings.recommended: On
settings.why: Useful agents can reach colleagues inside the organisation through a reviewed share.

settings.name: Enable agent sharing without admin approval
settings.where: Google Cloud console › Gemini Enterprise › (app) › Configurations › Feature Management
settings.default: Workflow owners can share with any user without approval (per the share-workflows page)
settings.recommended: Off — first shares go to an app administrator for review
settings.why: An agent reaches colleagues only after someone accountable has seen what it does; later versions still need no re-approval.

settings.name: Enable End Users to share with Groups
settings.where: Google Cloud console › Gemini Enterprise › (app) › Configurations › Feature Management
settings.recommended: On, with admin approval kept on
settings.why: Group shares stay manageable and under IAM's 1,500-member limit per policy; approval still applies.

settings.name: Enable instrumentation of OpenTelemetry traces and logs (agent level)
settings.where: Google Cloud console › Gemini Enterprise › (app) › Agents › (agent) › Configuration
settings.recommended: On for every shared, scheduled or event-triggered agent; prompt logging off
settings.why: Each run's steps and tool calls are traced in your project; the toggle is per agent, so add it to the share-approval checklist.

settings.name: Agent state (Enabled / Suspended / Disabled)
settings.where: Google Cloud console › Gemini Enterprise › (app) › Agents
settings.recommended: Disabled is your incident runbook's first step for a misbehaving employee-made agent
settings.why: Users can no longer run it; turn its workflow version off as well, and note in-progress runs continue to completion.

settings.name: Actions (Enable actions / Disable actions)
settings.where: Google Cloud console › Gemini Enterprise › Data Stores › (data store) › Actions
settings.recommended: Only the actions agents need; delete and permission-changing actions off
settings.why: Mutative steps a workflow's model can choose are limited to the ones an admin enabled.

settings.name: Custom MCP data store constraint
settings.where: Organization Policies › managed constraint blocking custom MCP data stores (override per project)
settings.recommended: Blocked, overridden only for projects whose MCP servers are registered and reviewed
settings.why: MCP tools that a Gemini agent step can call at runtime come only from servers someone has approved.

settings.name: OAuth scopes for the Gemini Enterprise client app (custom MCP server)
settings.where: Your identity provider › OAuth client registered for https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/oauth-redirect
settings.recommended: Only the scopes the server's approved tools need
settings.why: Agents calling the server on a user's behalf can't use more of that user's authority than the tools require.

settings.name: Enable Model Armor
settings.where: Google Cloud console › Gemini Enterprise › (app) › Configurations › Assistant
settings.recommended: On, with Inspect and block templates
settings.why: Prompts and responses in the app are screened for injection and malicious URLs; check the logs for Workflow Builder steps before relying on it there.

settings.name: Resource-level IAM on apps and data stores
settings.where: IAM bindings on the app and on each data store, with no broad project-level predefined roles
settings.default: Project-level roles apply to every app and data store
settings.recommended: Users bound to the apps and data stores their work needs
settings.why: A shared agent returns only what each user is entitled to; project-level roles would override the scoping.

tools.name: LM Studio

variants.name: LM Studio desktop app
variants.note: GUI for search, download, chat and the local server (Developer tab > Start server). With "run the LLM server on login" checked, closing the app leaves the server running from the system tray.

variants.name: llmster (headless daemon)
variants.note: The desktop app's core without the GUI, installed per user by install.sh / install.ps1 and started with lms daemon up; the docs' Linux startup task is a systemd unit at /etc/systemd/system/lmstudio.service running ~/.lmstudio/bin/lms as the named user.

variants.name: lms CLI
variants.note: Ships with either the app or llmster and drives both (lms get / import / load / server start / log stream); ls, load and ps accept --host to operate a reachable remote instance.

summary: Element Labs' desktop application for running open-weights models on the user's own machine (LM Studio 0.4.27, 2026-10-29): a GUI over the llama.cpp engine (GGUF) and, on Apple Silicon, Apple MLX, with a local server that speaks OpenAI-compatible /v1, Anthropic-compatible /v1/messages and a native REST /api/v1, on port 1234 by default. The same core ships headless as llmster, driven by the lms CLI. Models are downloaded from Hugging Face (Discover tab, lms get, or the REST download endpoint) straight into ~/.lmstudio/models.

Inference stays on the device. What leaves it, per the App Privacy Policy: update checks, anonymised model search and download requests, engine (runtime) downloads, LM Link discovery through the LM Studio Hub with traffic between the user's devices over Tailscale, and — only if bought and used — Cloud Services (cloud models, web search) processed under zero data retention.

The admission settings are per-user app toggles in Developer > Server Settings: Serve on Local Network (the CLI binds 127.0.0.1 by default), Require Authentication with API tokens (off by default, 0.4.0+), Enable CORS (off by default), Just in Time Model Loading, and two MCP-over-API switches. No managed or locked settings file, MDM key or admin console for them is documented at any tier; only the bind has a non-GUI channel (lms server start --bind, LMS_SERVER_HOST). The Enterprise and Teams page sells the Bionic agent, not runtime policy.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: The LM Studio app, llmster and lms are free, proprietary software under the App Terms. The pricing page now sells Bionic (Free; Bionic+ $20 and Pro $100 USD/month for US-hosted cloud models); teams get "centralized billing ... using inference credits" through an organisation, with team subscription plans "coming soon". The Enterprise and Teams page is a contact form for Bionic (ZDR cloud, own infrastructure or edge). No SSO, admin console, policy or MDM control for the runtime is documented at any tier; the changelog's "enterprise internal network model endpoint" mode (0.4.20, API key support 0.4.21) has no documentation page.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Local engines only: llama.cpp for GGUF (macOS, Windows, Linux), MLX on Apple Silicon, and the Splash engine on M3+ Macs (0.4.25); engines are packaged as hot-swappable runtime extension packs. Callers use http://localhost:1234 — /v1/models, /v1/responses, /v1/chat/completions, /v1/embeddings, /v1/completions, /v1/messages and /api/v1/*. With LM Link on, a request for a model held on another linked device is routed there over Tailscale through the same localhost call.

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: Local chats, attached documents and API traffic stay on the machine. Update checks send app version, OS and IP; model search and download reach huggingface.co (or LM Studio's Hugging Face proxy option, 0.3.9) and LM Studio receives anonymised search queries; engine downloads and LM Link discovery (through the LM Studio Hub) also go out. Cloud Services (cloud models, web search) send the request only when purchased and used. An API caller can also make the runtime connect out: POST /api/v1/models/download fetches any Hugging Face URL, and "Allow per-request MCPs" lets a request name a remote MCP server.

facts.label: Retention & training
facts.value: No telemetry or user-specific tracking in local use; prompts and responses are not retained; Cloud Services requests are processed transiently under ZDR and not used for training (App Privacy Policy, effective June 2026). Conversations are stored locally as JSON in ~/.lmstudio/conversations (%USERPROFILE%\.lmstudio\conversations on Windows).

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: lmstudio.ai/docs/app and lmstudio.ai/docs/developer (full text at lmstudio.ai/llms-full.txt)

facts.label: Offline operation
facts.value: Chat, document chat (RAG) and the local server work fully offline once a model is on disk. Model search, downloads, the Discover catalog, runtime downloads and app update checks need connectivity; updates are offered, not forced (notification to update now or later).

facts.label: Model storage
facts.value: ~/.lmstudio/models/<publisher>/<model>/<file> by default, preserving the Hugging Face layout; the directory is changed in My Models. lms import moves (or --copy / --hard-link / --symbolic-link) a GGUF from elsewhere into that layout; no checksum is documented on download or import.

facts.label: MCP
facts.value: The app is an MCP client (0.3.17+) configured in mcp.json (Program tab > Install > Edit mcp.json); the chat UI asks before each tool call with allow-once or always-allow, managed in App Settings > Tools & Integrations. Through the API, "Allow calling servers from mcp.json" (requires Require Authentication) and "Allow per-request MCPs" (ephemeral remote servers) are server switches (defaults not documented), narrowed per request by allowed_tools; no human confirmation is documented for API calls.

facts.label: LM Link
facts.value: Signed-in devices (LM Studio account) form a Tailscale-based network and use each other's models as if local, through localhost:1234. Off switch: Settings > LM Link > Enable LM Link off, or lms link disable for llmster. Whether Require Authentication applies to requests arriving over LM Link is not documented.

facts.label: Vendor ownership
facts.value: Element Labs, Inc. (Delaware); privacy@lmstudio.ai; bugs reported at lmstudio-ai/lmstudio-bug-tracker

items.title: Server baseline for a managed device
body: Developer > Server Settings: Require Authentication on (create one token per consuming application under Manage Tokens; clients send Authorization: Bearer or x-api-key), Serve on Local Network off, Enable CORS off, Allow per-request MCPs off, Allow calling servers from mcp.json off unless an application needs it, Just in Time Model Loading off on shared machines.

These are per-user app settings; no managed settings file or MDM key is documented, so device management can only launch the server with lms server start --bind 127.0.0.1 (no --cors) or set LMS_SERVER_HOST=127.0.0.1, and must detect drift in the rest. Turn LM Link off (Settings > LM Link, or lms link disable) where the machine should serve only itself.

items.title: Model supply chain
body: Discover, lms get and POST /api/v1/models/download pull from Hugging Face directly into the loadable models directory — there is no quarantine step and no documented digest check. For a promotion flow, fetch and scan outside LM Studio, then bring approved GGUFs in with lms import --user-repo <org>/<repo> --copy, and point My Models at a directory only the promotion job can write.

Loaders are limited to GGUF (llama.cpp) and MLX safetensors; the GGUF chat template still runs on every request, and since 0.4.17 a template override can be set per model in My Models > Load Parameters > Advanced > Chat Template.

riskNotes.note: No pickle loader ships: GGUF goes to llama.cpp and MLX models load with trust_remote_code off in the open-source MLX engine. The remaining classes are the GGUF parser (native code in fast-moving engine packs) and the embedded Jinja chat template, which runs on every request; answering Pillar Security on 2025-06-20, LM Studio put template vetting on users. A per-model Chat Template override (0.4.17) replaces the embedded one for models the organisation has reviewed.

Any Hugging Face URL is accepted by Discover, lms get and the REST download endpoint; the publisher name becomes the directory name and no digest verification is documented, so the file on disk is whatever the hub (or LM Studio's Hugging Face proxy) served.

With Just in Time Model Loading on, any caller can make the runtime load any downloaded model into memory; batching is per model (Max Concurrent Predictions, default 4) with nothing per caller, and the API is unauthenticated by default. LM Link adds every signed-in device of the account as a caller.

A proprietary desktop app plus llama.cpp / MLX engine packs that update separately from the app, an in-app updater (Linux AppImage and .deb since 0.4.22) and lms daemon update (stable or --beta, no version pinning). The vendor publishes no advisories: 0.4.16 lists only "Security hardening".

The local API can send work off the machine: LM Link routes a localhost request to a model on another device, an API caller with "Allow per-request MCPs" on can make the runtime call any remote MCP server, and the privacy policy's paid Cloud Services send prompts to LM Studio's ZDR cloud.

What is served can be changed through the API itself — /api/v1/models/download, /load and /unload — by any local process while Require Authentication is off, and by anyone on the network once Serve on Local Network is on; a file swapped in ~/.lmstudio/models is served on the next load with no check.

Model files, including any organisation adapters placed beside them, sit under ~/.lmstudio/models with the user's permissions, and LM Link exposes the loaded models to every device on the account's link.

controls.mechanism: Loader surface limited to GGUF (llama.cpp engine) and MLX safetensors — no pickle loader, MLX engine trust_remote_code off by default; no digest check, content scan or quarantine documented; lms import lets a scanned file be promoted from outside

steps.title: Point the runtime at promoted storage only
body: In My Models set the models directory to a location only the promotion job can write, so in-app downloads cannot land beside approved files unreviewed.

steps.title: Promote scanned files with lms import
body: After the model scanner passes a GGUF in quarantine, run lms import <file> --user-repo <org>/<repo> --copy (with --dry-run first) instead of downloading it in the app.

steps.title: Close the API download path
body: Turn on Require Authentication in Developer > Server Settings so POST /api/v1/models/download, which accepts catalog ids and any Hugging Face URL, needs an API token.

controls.note: Partial by the drawing's rule (native needs verification before load; partial covers safe formats without it). The pickle and remote-code axis is closed by construction: the only engines are llama.cpp for GGUF and MLX for safetensors, and the open-source MLX engine loads with trust_remote_code=False and vendors model-specific code instead. Nothing inspects a file before load: no digest check on download or import is documented, no content scan ships, and Discover, lms get and the REST download endpoint write straight into the loadable directory, so fetch and promotion collapse. The GGUF chat template executes on every request, past any static scan (LM Studio's 2025-06-20 reply to Pillar Security put vetting on users), and the GGUF parser is itself native code. Format and content inspection at quarantine is an external model scanner in the artifact repository or promotion pipeline.

controls.mechanism: Require Authentication with named API tokens (off by default) as caller identity; loopback bind by default (Serve on Local Network; lms server start --bind, LMS_SERVER_HOST) and Enable CORS (off by default) around it; no Host or Origin validation documented; per-user app settings with no managed channel except the bind

steps.title: Require API tokens
body: In Developer > Server Settings turn on Require Authentication and create tokens under Manage Tokens; every REST, SDK and /v1/messages request then needs Authorization: Bearer or x-api-key.

steps.title: Pin the bind to loopback from device management
body: Leave Serve on Local Network off, and launch managed servers with lms server start --bind 127.0.0.1 or set LMS_SERVER_HOST=127.0.0.1, the only non-GUI channel for these settings.

steps.title: Keep CORS and the MCP switches off
body: Leave Enable CORS off (never pass --cors) and keep Allow per-request MCPs and Allow calling servers from mcp.json off unless an authenticated application needs them.

steps.title: Turn off LM Link where the machine serves only itself
body: Set Settings > LM Link > Enable LM Link off in the app, or run lms link disable for llmster.

evidence.title: LM Studio docs — Authentication (API tokens, off by default)
LM Studio docs — lms server start (--bind, LMS_SERVER_HOST)
LM Link FAQ (account-linked devices use each other's models)

controls.note: Partial by the drawing's rule: callers can be authenticated, but not in a way the organisation can require. Require Authentication makes every REST, SDK and Anthropic-compatible request carry a bearer token (Developer > Server Settings; tokens from Manage Tokens; Authorization: Bearer or x-api-key), so one named token per application identifies the caller; it has been off by default since it arrived in 0.4.0, tokens have editable permissions whose names are not documented, and the docs do not say /v1 OpenAI-compatible calls are covered. Loopback default: yes — --bind defaults to 127.0.0.1 and the docs warn that any other bind needs authentication. Host and Origin validation: not documented — CORS off only stops a page reading replies, and DNS rebinding is not addressed. Delivery is the weak point: Require Authentication, CORS and Serve on Local Network are per-user app toggles with no documented managed or locked settings file, so the device's user can undo them and device management can only pin the bind and detect drift. Where the token must be the only path, put an authenticating reverse proxy or gateway in front, give it the only token and publish only the proxy. The LM Studio account sign-in (lms login, used for LM Link and the Hub) is not a gate on the local API; LM Link lets devices on the same account reach this machine's models over Tailscale, and whether Require Authentication applies to them is not documented, so turn LM Link off where the proxy must be the only path. lms ls / load / ps --host operate any instance they can reach.

controls.mechanism: No content classification in the runtime; prompt-preprocessor plugins see only chat-UI user input, not API traffic or model output

evidence.title: LM Studio docs — Prompt Preprocessors (called when the user hits Send)
LM Studio docs — OpenAI-compatible endpoints

controls.note: External: LM Studio ships no harm-category, denied-topic or policy classifier on either direction, and the API returns raw model output. Prompt preprocessors (plugins) run when a user presses Send in the chat window, see only the current user message and never the response, and are not documented for server requests, so they are not an attach point on the api->runtime path. The class is an AI gateway or guardrail model served beside it: bind LM Studio to 127.0.0.1, turn on Require Authentication and give the gateway the only token so callers cannot bypass it. Whatever refusal behaviour the weights carry is the whole in-product defence.

controls.mechanism: Per-model Max Concurrent Predictions (default 4), per-load context length and the JIT loading switches; API tokens name a caller but carry no documented rate limit or quota

steps.title: Cap concurrent predictions per model
body: In the model loader turn on Manually choose model load parameters and Show advanced settings, and set Max Concurrent Predictions (default 4) for each model the server exposes.

steps.title: Stop callers loading models on demand
body: In Developer > Server Settings turn Just in Time Model Loading off, or keep Auto Unload Unused JIT Models and Only Keep Last JIT Loaded Model on, so a caller cannot fill memory with models.

steps.title: Issue one token per consuming application
body: With Require Authentication on, create a named token per application under Manage Tokens so a runaway caller can be identified and its token deleted.

controls.note: Partial by the drawing's rule (global concurrency, queue and context limits that are not per caller). Max Concurrent Predictions batches up to N requests per loaded model and queues the rest (lms ps --json reports the queue), and the context length bounds one request, but no limit attaches to a token, a process or a device: one caller can hold every slot. With JIT loading on, any caller can force a model load; LM Link adds the account's other devices as callers. Per-caller rates and quotas are gateway rate limiting in front of a loopback-bound server (external).

controls.mechanism: Model files under ~/.lmstudio/models (or the My Models directory) with the user's file permissions; not content-addressed, no digest on download or load; Require Authentication gates only the REST download / load / unload endpoints

evidence.title: LM Studio docs — models directory layout and lms import
LM Studio docs — REST download endpoint (no verification documented)

controls.note: External on the drawing's rule (partial needs at least a digest on download or content-addressed storage, which is what puts toolOllama's sha256 blob store at partial). Files are stored by publisher/model/file name as served by Hugging Face, readable and replaceable by any process running as the user, and nothing checks them at load, so a swapped or altered GGUF is served on the next load without notice. Restrictive permissions and swap detection are OS controls and file-integrity monitoring on the models directory; the product's contribution is the My Models directory setting (point it at storage the user cannot write) and Require Authentication, which keeps unauthenticated API callers from downloading, loading or unloading models but does nothing for the files themselves.

controls.mechanism: The decision lives in the organisation's GRC / AI governance register; LM Studio publishes a privacy policy and terms but no security policy, assurance report or advisory feed, and has no model-source allowlist setting

evidence.title: LM Studio Desktop App Privacy Policy (effective June 2026)
LM Studio App Terms of Use
lmstudio-bug-tracker (no security policy file or published advisories)
LM Studio Enterprise and Teams page (Bionic contact form)

controls.note: External: whether local inference may run, from which sources and on which machines is recorded in the organisation's GRC, AI governance or TPRM platform. Vendor evidence for that record is thin: the App Privacy Policy and App Terms; no SOC 2 or ISO report, no trust or security page (lmstudio.ai/security resolves to a Hub profile), no SECURITY.md or advisories in the lmstudio-ai repositories, and fixes described only as "Security hardening" in the changelog. No device setting enforces a source decision: Discover, lms get and the REST download endpoint accept any Hugging Face URL, and the Hugging Face proxy option reroutes rather than restricts. Enforcement is the models-directory location, Require Authentication on the download endpoint, egress rules to huggingface.co at the device firewall or proxy, and application allow/deny through MDM.

controls.mechanism: EDR over the LM Studio app and llmster processes; integration points are port 1234, ~/.lmstudio/bin/lms, the documented systemd unit, lms log stream and lms ps --json

evidence.title: LM Studio docs — llmster Linux startup task (systemd unit, binary path, port)
LM Studio docs — lms log stream
LM Studio docs — lms daemon update

controls.note: External: process behaviour, vulnerable-version discovery and containment belong to the EDR. Points it can key on: the server on TCP 1234 (curl http://localhost:1234/v1/models answers with no token by default), ~/.lmstudio/bin/lms and the llmster daemon it starts (lms daemon up, lms daemon status --json), the desktop app kept in the tray by "run the LLM server on login", and /etc/systemd/system/lmstudio.service where the docs' Linux startup task is used. lms log stream --source server --json streams server logs and --source model the exact model input and output (no on-disk log path is documented); lms ps --json lists loaded models and queued requests. Version tracking must cover the app, llmster (lms daemon update, stable or --beta) and the llama.cpp / MLX engine packs, which update separately.

controls.mechanism: Local lists only (lms ls --json, GET /api/v1/models) with publisher, key, format, quantization and size — no digest, source URL or revision; no fleet inventory

evidence.title: LM Studio docs — GET /api/v1/models response fields
LM Studio docs — lms ls

controls.note: External on the drawing's rule (partial needs a local list with digests and source that fleet tooling can collect, as toolOllama's does; native a fleet inventory). LM Studio's lists — lms ls --json (or --host for a reachable instance) and GET /api/v1/models — give publisher, key, format (gguf/mlx), quantization, size_bytes and variants, but no hash, source URL or hub revision, and nothing aggregates across machines. An AI BOM needs MDM or EDR inventory scripts that hash files under ~/.lmstudio/models/<publisher>/<model>/ and record the source; the directory layout preserves the Hugging Face repository name, not its revision.

controls.mechanism: EDR / MDM software inventory and network scanning; LM Studio reports nothing to an organisation

evidence.title: LM Studio docs — headless mode and llmster install
LM Studio docs — Serve on Local Network
LM Studio Desktop App Privacy Policy (no telemetry)

controls.note: External: nothing in the product registers an install with the organisation — local use carries no telemetry, and the Team organisation offers credit billing, not a device list. Signals for endpoint and network discovery: the LM Studio app install, the per-user ~/.lmstudio tree (models, bin/lms, conversations, hub), llmster installed per user by curl -fsSL https://lmstudio.ai/install.sh | bash or irm https://lmstudio.ai/install.ps1 | iex, a listener on TCP 1234 (routable when Serve on Local Network or --bind 0.0.0.0 is set) answering GET /v1/models, and LM Link's Tailscale traffic to other devices.

controls.mechanism: No security evaluation ships; an evaluation harness or red-team tool calls the local API before a model is promoted into the models directory

evidence.title: LM Studio docs — OpenAI-compatible endpoints (harness target)
LM Studio docs — lms log stream (exact model input and output)

controls.note: External: LM Studio has no backdoor, leakage or adversarial test suite and no gate on what loads — any downloaded model is loadable, and JIT-loadable by any API caller. Evaluation harnesses and red-team tooling run against the OpenAI-compatible endpoint in a staging copy before a model is promoted; lms log stream --source model --filter input,output shows the exact templated prompt, which exposes chat-template behaviour to the evaluator. Catalog curation (staff picks, lmstudio-community uploads) is not an evaluation.

controls.mechanism: No checksum or signature is documented on download (Discover, lms get, POST /api/v1/models/download), on lms import or at load; verification is a promotion job that hashes the file before it enters the models directory, and file-integrity monitoring over that directory

evidence.title: LM Studio docs — Download a model (REST; no verification documented)
LM Studio docs — lms import (moves or copies a file into the models layout)
LM Studio docs — Changing the models directory

controls.note: External on this drawing's rule (partial needs at least a digest check on download, as toolOllama's pull has; toolVllm pins hub revisions). LM Studio writes what Hugging Face served straight into the loadable directory and never hashes it, and lms import trusts the file it is given. The organisation's job hashes (or verifies the model-signing bundle of) each approved GGUF in quarantine, imports it with lms import --copy into a models directory only that job can write, and file-integrity monitoring re-hashes the directory against the approved list.

settings.name: Require Authentication
settings.where: Developer › Server Settings › Require Authentication; tokens under Manage Tokens
settings.recommended: On, with one named API token per consuming application
settings.why: Every REST and SDK request must carry a token, so a stray local process or web page cannot load, download or call models, and a runaway caller can be found and its token deleted.

settings.name: Serve on Local Network
settings.where: Developer › Server Settings › Serve on Local Network
settings.recommended: Off
settings.why: Keeps the API on localhost so other devices on the network cannot call it; a shared server goes behind an authenticating proxy instead.

settings.name: --bind / LMS_SERVER_HOST
settings.where: lms server start --bind 127.0.0.1, or LMS_SERVER_HOST in the environment of the managed start script
settings.recommended: 127.0.0.1, set explicitly by the managed launch
settings.why: The one setting device management can deliver; the docs warn that any other bind exposes the server beyond localhost.

settings.name: Enable CORS
settings.where: Developer › Server Settings › Enable CORS (lms server start --cors)
settings.recommended: Off
settings.why: Web pages open in the user's browser cannot read replies from the local API.

settings.name: Allow per-request MCPs
settings.where: Developer › Server Settings › Allow per-request MCPs
settings.recommended: Off
settings.why: An API caller cannot name an arbitrary remote MCP server for the runtime to call, which would carry the conversation off the machine.

settings.name: Allow calling servers from mcp.json
settings.where: Developer › Server Settings › Allow calling servers from mcp.json (requires Require Authentication)
settings.recommended: Off unless an authenticated application needs those tools
settings.why: API callers cannot use the user's own MCP servers, which the page warns may reach the file system or private data.

settings.name: mcp.json
settings.where: Program tab › Install › Edit mcp.json
settings.recommended: Only MCP servers the organisation has approved
settings.why: The page says some MCP servers can run arbitrary code and reach local files and the network; never install them from untrusted sources.

settings.name: Tool call confirmations
settings.where: Tool call confirmation dialog in chat › allow once / always allow
settings.default: Confirmation shown for every tool call
settings.recommended: Allow once — no "always allow" for tools that write files or reach the network
settings.why: The user reviews, and can edit, each tool call's arguments before it runs; an always-allowed tool runs unseen.

settings.name: Enable LM Link
settings.where: Settings › LM Link › Enable LM Link (on llmster, lms link disable)
settings.recommended: Off
settings.why: Every device signed in to the same LM Studio account could otherwise use this machine's models over Tailscale, and the docs do not say Require Authentication applies to them.

settings.name: Just in Time Model Loading
settings.where: Developer › Server Settings › Just in Time Model Loading, Auto Unload Unused JIT Models, Only Keep Last JIT Loaded Model
settings.recommended: On, with Auto Unload Unused JIT Models and Only Keep Last JIT Loaded Model on

tools.name: Meta Muse

variants.name: Muse app (iOS and Android) and muse.ai
Muse in WhatsApp
variants.note: Message Muse like a contact; AI glasses are announced, not shipped.

variants.name: Muse for Small Business
variants.note: Business connectors (Facebook Pages, Instagram professional accounts, Meta ad accounts, Shopify, Stripe and others) on the same personal agent; no team or admin features described.

summary: Meta's personal agent, running on a dedicated cloud VM per person (Muse Secure VM) with its own browser, file system and terminal. It keeps memory and goals across conversations, works on a schedule and on events after the app is closed, and messages the person when something changes or an approval is needed.

A separate host-side agent, Sentinel, is the sole permission authority for connector actions and all network egress; Muse proposes, Sentinel allows, denies or asks the person. Credentials live on the VM and the agent sees only surrogate tokens. It is a consumer product with no organisation plan.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Free for most use, with paid subscriptions for more. Rolling out in the US (the small-business post also names Canada) on iOS, Android, muse.ai and WhatsApp.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Meta operates the VM and runs Muse Spark. Security services (Sentinel, credential store, privilege separation) run outside the agent's container on the same VM.

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: Connector data, files, memory and credentials are held on the person's cloud VM. Device connectors such as Apple Health or Android SMS are granted in device settings.

facts.label: Retention & training
facts.value: No retention period is stated; VM data is continuously backed up. Training is on by default and turned off with Help improve our AI models in Settings > Data controls. Not shared with Meta's ad systems.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: Meta Help Center articles on Muse data and connectors; Meta's Muse safety post.

facts.label: Bug bounty
facts.value: Public bounty up to $300,000, including prompt injection affecting one user.

items.title: Decide whether work accounts may connect to it
body: Muse has no organisation plan, so the enterprise lever is at the services it connects to. Use the identity provider's or each SaaS admin console's third-party app consent controls to decide whether Muse may reach work mail, calendars and drives from a personal Meta account.

items.title: Custom connectors are unreviewed code
body: Muse can write its own connector for any service with an API or CLI and store the credentials it needs. Meta does not review custom connectors, and their sandboxing is not described.

riskNotes.note: A personal Muse with standing access to a work mailbox or ad account is invisible to every admin console.
Pages, mail and files it reads on schedule can steer later work; Sentinel's tainted-egress rule limits what leaves afterwards.
Custom connectors that Muse writes itself are not reviewed by Meta.
Disconnecting or deleting does not remove what Muse already learned; ask it to forget or reset.

controls.mechanism: No organisation plan or admin switch; the connected services' third-party app consent controls decide what it can reach.

evidence.title: Muse announcement (consumer availability)
How Muse works with Connectors

controls.note: External: Muse is tied to a personal Meta account and no organisation can turn it on or off. Govern it at the destination — OAuth app approval in Google Workspace, Microsoft 365 and other SaaS — and in acceptable-use policy for personal AI agents.

controls.mechanism: Settings > Connectors per connector; many connectors can be set to retrieve only; Sentinel applies the person's connector policy (allowed, denied or ask) with read and write separated where the service allows.

steps.title: Connect read-only where possible
body: In Settings > Connectors, connect only what Muse needs, choose retrieve-only access where offered, and disconnect anything unused.

controls.note: Partial on the consumer rule: the person sets it and no organisation can require it. Custom connectors Muse writes itself are unreviewed, and disconnecting does not remove what it already learned.

controls.mechanism: Sentinel asks the person in a client approval dialog (not the chat) before consequential connector actions, data leaving the VM and each purchase; grants can be one-time, session, task, time-bounded or perpetual.

steps.title: Keep approvals narrow
body: In Settings, keep Muse asking before important actions, and grant approvals one-time or per task rather than perpetual.

controls.note: Partial on the consumer rule, though it is the strongest gate on this drawing: the dialog answers straight to Sentinel, out of the model's reach. Read-only, previously allowed and low-risk actions proceed unprompted, a perpetual grant removes the gate, and no organisation sets the policy.

controls.mechanism: Sign-in is the person's own Meta account; no organisation SSO or MFA policy applies.

evidence.title: Muse announcement (consumer availability)

controls.note: None for an organisation: Muse has no business tenancy, so no SSO, conditional access or MFA requirement reaches it. Any second factor is the person's own Meta account setting.

controls.mechanism: Credentials, OAuth tokens included, stay in a credential service on the VM outside the agent's container; the agent sees surrogate tokens, and browser logins go from the client straight to that store.

evidence.title: Credentials and tokens

controls.note: None on the consumer rule (lowered from partial 2026-10-30): the credential store outside the agent's container is a vendor design nobody can configure or audit, so nothing in the product delivers it as a setting, and the signed-in browser session still carries the account's authority. What stands in is the connected services' own token controls — OAuth consent, scopes and revocation in each service.

controls.mechanism: Sentinel swaps real credentials in at the network boundary only after authorising the request to that destination; purchases use single-use cards bound to one merchant, amount and time window.

evidence.title: Surrogate tokens and single-use cards

controls.note: None on the consumer rule (lowered from partial 2026-10-30): recipient binding is documented, which is more than the other products on this drawing show, but it is a vendor design with no setting the person or an organisation can make or an event either can check. What stands in is the person's purchase approvals and the connected services' own scopes.

controls.mechanism: Memory.md, Soul.md and Identity.md are readable and editable; a forget skill; Reset Muse; VM data is continuously backed up.

steps.title: Review and edit its memory
body: Tap the Assistant icon > Identity > Memory and edit or delete entries in Memory.md; ask Muse to forget a topic, or use Settings > Data controls > Reset Muse to start clean.

controls.note: Partial on the consumer rule. Memory is inspectable, but nothing validates what Muse writes to it, and Meta says it may still remember information learned from items you delete.

controls.mechanism: Free and paid tiers are announced; their limits are not documented.

evidence.title: Muse announcement (pricing)

controls.note: Unknown: Meta documents no per-task time, spend or step limit and no tier limits. Payments are bounded per purchase by single-use cards, which is not a workload limit.

controls.mechanism: Sentinel checks all egress at layers 4 and 7 (host, resolved and final IP, port, method, path), blocks SSRF to private addresses and known malicious sites, and removes auto-allow once a process has read user data.

evidence.title: Sentinel egress control

controls.note: Partial: the enforcement point is real and covers the whole VM, but the policy is Meta's plus the person's approvals; there is no destination allowlist an organisation writes or sees.

controls.mechanism: An ensemble of classifiers screens files and tool outputs; external content is labelled untrusted; the browser agent reads an accessibility tree with JavaScript and DevTools disabled; the email connector filters one-time codes and reset links.

evidence.title: Prompt-injection defences

controls.note: None on the consumer rule (lowered from partial 2026-10-30): the classifier ensemble is documented in detail but vendor-internal, with no setting, threshold or detection event anyone can see, so no settings row can deliver it. What stands in is the person's approval of consequential actions.

controls.mechanism: No organisation view of who runs Muse; discover it from OAuth grants in the connected services.

evidence.title: How Muse works with Connectors

controls.note: External: a SaaS-management or OAuth-grant review is the only way to find work accounts connected to a personal Muse. Custom connectors it writes appear in no registry at all.

controls.mechanism: The organisation's third-party risk process consumes Meta's published security design.

evidence.title: How we built safety into Muse
Muse privacy policy

controls.note: External. Record that Muse is a consumer service with no business terms or DPA, that the VM is readable by Meta until the announced Confidential VM ships, and that training is on by default.

controls.mechanism: The avatar opens a full activity log of completed and planned actions and the permissions approved; data download from Data controls.

steps.title: Read the activity log
body: Tap the Muse avatar for its activity log and approved permissions; use Settings > Data controls > Download your Muse data for a copy.

controls.note: Partial on the consumer rule: a person-facing log with an export, but no organisation feed and no documented step-level detail of what the browser read.

controls.mechanism: Reset Muse erases chat history, files and active tasks; connectors can be disconnected in Settings > Connectors.

steps.title: Stop and wipe
body: Settings > Data controls > Reset Muse erases chat history, files and active tasks and cannot be undone; disconnect connectors in Settings > Connectors to cut future access.

controls.note: Partial: the only documented stop is destructive, its cessation delay is not stated, and no non-destructive pause appears in Meta's pages. No organisation can trigger it.

settings.name: Connectors
settings.where: Muse › Settings › Connectors
settings.default: None connected (Facebook, Instagram and Threads connect automatically through a shared Accounts Center)
settings.recommended: Only what Muse needs, retrieve-only where offered, and no work account the employer has not approved
settings.why: Each connector is standing access Muse uses on a schedule; read-only stops actions, and disconnecting cuts future access but not what it already learned.

settings.name: approval settings
settings.where: Muse › Settings (Meta's pages name no label for it)
settings.default: Asks before important actions such as sending an email or making a purchase; ordinary browsing allowed
settings.recommended: The default or more cautious, with grants given one-time or per task, never perpetual
settings.why: Sentinel asks you, outside the model's reach, before consequential actions and data leaving the VM; a perpetual grant removes that gate.

settings.name: Memory
settings.where: Assistant icon › Identity › Memory (Memory.md; also Soul and Identity)
settings.default: Written by Muse as it learns
settings.recommended: Reviewed after any work-related task; entries from untrusted mail or pages deleted
settings.why: What Muse remembers steers every later task, and nothing validates what it writes there.

settings.name: Help improve our AI models
settings.where: Muse › Settings › Data controls › Help improve our AI models
settings.recommended: Off
settings.why: Chats, files and connector data stop being used to train Meta's models; turning it off also covers past interactions.

settings.name: activity log
settings.where: Tap the Muse avatar (activity log and the permissions you've approved)
settings.recommended: Reviewed weekly, with standing permissions trimmed there
settings.why: It is the only record of what Muse did and was allowed to do; no organisation feed exists.

settings.name: Reset Muse
settings.where: Muse › Settings › Data controls › Reset Muse
settings.recommended: The stop for a compromised Muse, after Download your Muse data and with its OAuth grants revoked at each service
settings.why: It deletes all Muse data and cannot be undone; access tokens held by connected services end only when revoked there.
