tools.name: Microsoft Copilot in Edge (Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat in the Edge for Business side pane, browsing with Copilot)

variants.name: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat in the Edge side pane (Entra profile)
variants.note: Chat with enterprise data protection that can read the current page, browsing history and video transcript when EdgeEntraCopilotPageContext allows it; summarised page content may be retained under enterprise data protection.

variants.name: Browsing with Copilot (preview; Microsoft 365 Copilot licence; tenants outside the EEA)
variants.note: Copilot browses sites on the user's behalf to complete multi-step workflows, only on domains in BrowsingWithCopilotAllowList and never on BrowsingWithCopilotBlockList; it asks the user for authentication steps and final saving and submitting actions.

variants.name: Cowork actions in Edge (Edge 152 and later)
variants.note: Lets Microsoft 365 Copilot Cowork take actions on the user's behalf in Edge; governed by CopilotCoworkToolActionsEnabled, which does not apply to Microsoft account profiles.

summary: Copilot built into Microsoft Edge for Business: on a profile signed in with a Microsoft Entra account the side pane is Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat with enterprise data protection, which can use the open page, browsing history and video transcripts as context, and with a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence it can browse sites for the user (browsing with Copilot, preview) and let Cowork act in the browser. Inference runs in Microsoft's cloud under Microsoft 365 Copilot; Edge decides what browsing context to send based on the query and the policy, and Copilot acts inside the user's own signed-in browser session.

The administrator is the Microsoft 365 or Intune administrator: Edge policies delivered by Group Policy, Intune or the Edge management service (Microsoft 365 admin center › Settings › Microsoft Edge › Configuration policies › Copilot tab) switch Copilot off (EdgeCopilotEnabled), control page access (EdgeEntraCopilotPageContext, CopilotPageContext, CopilotOnSensitiveContentEnabled), allow and block the sites Copilot may browse (AllowBrowsingWithCopilot, BrowsingWithCopilotAllowList and BlockList) and Cowork actions (CopilotCoworkToolActionsEnabled). Interactions are audited in Microsoft Purview as CopilotInteraction with AppHost Edge; Purview DLP and Defender for Cloud Apps act in the Edge for Business work profile.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat in Edge for any Entra user; browsing with Copilot needs a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence and is a preview open to tenants outside the European Economic Area; Commercial Journeys (Get things done) needs Microsoft 365 Copilot Premium or higher.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat under enterprise data protection when signed in with an Entra account; the side pane is hosted on edge://commercial-copilot-chat and cr.m365copilotapp.svc.cloud.microsoft, which Microsoft says to govern by policy rather than block. Edge can also download a local foundational model for on-device inference (GenAILocalFoundationalModelSettings).

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: For queries that need no browsing context Edge sends the URL, page title, query and conversation history; with permission to use page information it sends the browsing context of the session. Pages protected by DLP policies are not read unless CopilotOnSensitiveContentEnabled opens a protected session. Browsing history of tenant-approved work sites is shared with Microsoft 365 Copilot Search unless ShareBrowsingHistoryWithCopilotSearchAllowed is disabled.

facts.label: Retention & training
facts.value: Enterprise data protection applies to prompts and responses on an Entra profile; summarised page content (not the full page) may be retained and processed under it. Copilot memory follows Microsoft 365 Copilot (Enhanced personalization on by default; Purview retention does not apply to memories).

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: Microsoft Edge Browser Policy Documentation (Copilot and Generative AI sections) and Copilot Chat in Edge (learn.microsoft.com/copilot/edge)

facts.label: Admin planes
facts.value: Edge policies by Group Policy (ADMX), Intune or macOS preferences; the Edge management service Copilot tab (Access to browser context, Copilot icon in the toolbar, Copilot search box, AI-generated text and editing, Copilot new tab page, Browsing with Copilot), assigned to all users or Entra groups and downloaded within up to 90 minutes; Microsoft Purview (Audit, DLP); Defender for Cloud Apps.

items.title: Where each control lives
body: Edge policies (Administrative Templates/Microsoft Edge, or the Edge management service Copilot tab): EdgeCopilotEnabled, Microsoft365CopilotChatIconEnabled, EdgeEntraCopilotPageContext, CopilotPageContext, CopilotOnSensitiveContentEnabled, AllowBrowsingWithCopilot, BrowsingWithCopilotAllowList, BrowsingWithCopilotBlockList, CopilotCoworkToolActionsEnabled, ShareBrowsingHistoryWithCopilotSearchAllowed, BrowserSignin, RestrictSigninToPattern. Microsoft Purview: Audit (CopilotInteraction, AppHost Edge), DLP. Microsoft 365 admin center: Enhanced personalization for Copilot memory, Copilot usage report.

links.title: Enable browsing with Copilot in the Edge management service

items.title: Policies apply only to Entra profiles
body: The page-context, browsing and Cowork policies state that they apply to profiles signed in with a Microsoft Entra account and not to Microsoft account profiles. Pair them with BrowserSignin and RestrictSigninToPattern so managed devices run Copilot only in the work profile.

riskNotes.note: Browsing with Copilot and page summarisation read web pages into the model; Microsoft 365 Copilot's cross-prompt-injection classifier is vendor-run and surfaces only as XPIADetected in the audit record, and the allow list bounds which sites the agent acts on, not what an allowed page says.

Copilot acts inside the user's own signed-in Edge session with no identity of its own, so an allowed site sees the user; Copilot asks the user for authentication steps rather than handling credentials.

Copilot on a personal Microsoft account profile is outside every Entra-profile policy; without RestrictSigninToPattern a user can sign a managed Edge into a personal account and use consumer Copilot Mode beside the work profile.
Page access is on by default outside the EU (EdgeEntraCopilotPageContext unset), and browsing history of tenant-approved sites is shared with Microsoft 365 Copilot Search by default.

Browsing with Copilot confirms authentication and final saving or submitting with the user, but which steps count is Microsoft's choice; Cowork actions in Edge are a user setting unless the policy pins them.

controls.mechanism: Browsing with Copilot requests user input for steps requiring authentication and for final saving and submitting actions (vendor-defined); CopilotCoworkToolActionsEnabled decides whether Cowork may take actions on the user's behalf in Edge; AllowBrowsingWithCopilot can pin browsing on or off

steps.title: Keep Cowork actions behind a decision
body: Set CopilotCoworkToolActionsEnabled to Disabled for everyone outside a pilot group so Cowork cannot act in the browser and users cannot turn it on in Settings.

steps.title: Pilot browsing with Copilot to a group
body: Assign the Browse with Copilot configuration to an Entra group in the Edge management service rather than to All users.

controls.note: Partial on the rule applied to Claude in Chrome: a present user confirms named consequential classes (authentication, final save and submit), but the set is vendor-chosen and no administrator setting adds a class or requires per-action approval; the docs do not say how a send or a purchase that is not a "final submit" is treated. Cowork actions are all-or-nothing per policy.

controls.mechanism: BrowsingWithCopilotAllowList and BrowsingWithCopilotBlockList (origins; block wins; users cannot modify); EdgeEntraCopilotPageContext and CopilotPageContext for read access to page content, browsing history and video transcripts; CopilotCoworkToolActionsEnabled for Cowork actions

steps.title: List the sites Copilot may browse
body: Set BrowsingWithCopilotAllowList to the work sites the pilot needs (or use the curated commonly used sites toggle) and BrowsingWithCopilotBlockList to client portals, banking and HR systems.

steps.title: Decide page access explicitly
body: Set EdgeEntraCopilotPageContext to Enabled or Disabled rather than leaving the regional default.

controls.note: Partial on the rule applied to Claude in Chrome: per-origin allow and block lists the user cannot override, but no read-only tier on an allowed site and no per-operation scope; page context is a single switch for page content, history and transcripts. Paths are ignored in the patterns, so a site is allowed or blocked whole.

controls.mechanism: Copilot acts in the user's Entra profile session; browsing with Copilot asks the user for steps requiring authentication; the allow list bounds the signed-in origins it can act on

steps.title: Bound the sessions Copilot can use
body: Keep BrowsingWithCopilotAllowList to named work sites so Copilot acts only in those sessions.

controls.note: Partial on the rule applied to Claude in Chrome: the allow list denies the agent the sessions of unlisted origins and authentication is handed back to the user, but on an allowed origin Copilot acts with the user's full session and cookies; there is no agent identity or on-behalf-of exchange, and nothing documented keeps Edge's saved passwords from a page Copilot fills.

controls.mechanism: Microsoft 365 Copilot's jailbreak and cross-prompt-injection (XPIA) classifiers, vendor-run, recorded as JailbreakDetected and XPIADetected on the CopilotInteraction audit record (AppHost Edge)

steps.title: Alert on detected injection
body: Stream CopilotInteraction records with AppHost Edge to the SIEM and alert on XPIADetected and JailbreakDetected.

controls.note: Partial on the rule applied to every vendor: the screening is vendor-internal and not admin-tunable, and its verdict reaches the organisation only after the fact through audit. The Edge pages do not say whether pages read during browsing with Copilot are screened before the agent acts on them.

controls.mechanism: Copilot memory of Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat governed by Enhanced personalization (admin, disable-only; on by default); eDiscovery search and Graph deletion of memories

steps.title: Decide whether memory is on
body: Leave Enhanced personalization on for the firm or turn it off for groups that handle client data that must not persist between chats.

controls.note: Partial on the disable-only rule applied to Claude in Chrome: memory can be switched off and searched or deleted by an administrator, but administrators cannot restrict what is added to memory, Purview retention does not apply to it, and nothing treats remembered page content as untrusted. The memory page does not name Edge; the side pane is Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, so the control is inherited.

controls.mechanism: Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps session policies and Purview DLP enforced in the Edge for Business work profile (in-browser protection) observe the user's session, in which Copilot's browsing runs

evidence.title: In-browser protection with Microsoft Edge for Business (Defender for Cloud Apps)
Enable browsing with Copilot (no activity log of browsing steps documented)

controls.note: External: session analysis is a CASB/SSE product's (Defender for Cloud Apps, separately licensed), and the integration point is the Edge for Business work profile, where in-browser protection applies its session policies without a proxy. Edge documents no log of the pages browsing with Copilot visited or the actions it took, so the agent's activity is seen only as the user's session.

controls.mechanism: Copilot is part of the browser, not an extension; the browser estate and its policy state are reported by device management (Intune, edge://policy), and agents reachable from the side pane are registered in the Microsoft 365 admin center (toolM365Copilot)

evidence.title: Configure Microsoft Copilot settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center (Copilot in Edge links to Edge configuration policies)
Microsoft Edge management service Copilot features

controls.note: External by the rule applied to Claude in Chrome: inventory of where the capability is enabled is the device-management product's, keyed on the configuration policy assignment; there is nothing to admit by id because Copilot ships in the browser. The agents and connectors Copilot Chat can call are the Microsoft 365 admin center's registry, assessed on toolM365Copilot.

controls.mechanism: BrowserSignin (Force) and RestrictSigninToPattern keep managed Edge profiles on work accounts, which the Copilot policies govern; the Microsoft 365 Copilot usage report lists Copilot use in Microsoft Edge per user; Purview DLP in Edge for Business acts on unmanaged AI apps

steps.title: Keep managed browsers on work accounts
body: Set BrowserSignin to Force and RestrictSigninToPattern to the firm's domains so personal Microsoft accounts cannot be signed in.

steps.title: Read Copilot use in Edge
body: Review the Microsoft 365 Copilot usage report's Microsoft Edge entries for who uses Copilot in the browser.

controls.note: Partial: the vendor lists governed use and the browser can be held to work accounts, but consumer Copilot on a personal profile or an unmanaged device is invisible to these reports; discovering other AI tools used through Edge is Purview's and Defender for Cloud Apps' (external).

controls.mechanism: Microsoft Purview Audit CopilotInteraction records for Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat in the Edge sidebar (AppHost Edge), with the resources accessed and classifier verdicts

steps.title: Stream Edge Copilot interactions
body: In Purview Audit filter CopilotInteraction on AppHost Edge and collect the records for the SIEM.

controls.note: Partial on the tracing rule: chat interactions in the side pane land in the organisation's audit log, but the Edge pages document no record of the steps browsing with Copilot or Cowork took in the browser (pages visited, clicks, form entries), so the action trail is the target sites' own logs.

controls.mechanism: Copilot cannot read page content on pages protected by DLP policies; CopilotOnSensitiveContentEnabled opens a protected session (not saved to history, no copy or download) for such pages; Purview DLP on the Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat location; EdgeEntraCopilotPageContext to stop page access

steps.title: Keep DLP-protected pages out of Copilot
body: Leave CopilotOnSensitiveContentEnabled unconfigured or disabled so Edge keeps Copilot away from content your DLP policies protect.

steps.title: Refuse prompts carrying sensitive data
body: Create a Purview DLP policy on the Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat location with Content contains > Sensitive information types and Restrict Copilot from processing content.

controls.note: Partial: DLP keeps protected pages and prompts carrying sensitive types away from Copilot, but nothing masks a value in place; an unprotected page containing client data is sent whole once page access is on.

controls.mechanism: BrowsingWithCopilotAllowList and BrowsingWithCopilotBlockList restrict the origins browsing with Copilot can act on, enforced by Edge for the agent and separable from the user's own browsing; with no allow list the feature is unavailable

steps.title: Allow only listed sites
body: Configure BrowsingWithCopilotAllowList with the approved origins and BrowsingWithCopilotBlockList for exceptions; leaving the allow list empty disables browsing with Copilot.

controls.note: Native by the rule applied to Claude in Chrome: an administrator-set list of sites the agent may work on, enforced by the browser and not changeable by the user. Boundaries: only HTTP and HTTPS origins, paths ignored; whether a navigation from an allowed page to an unlisted one is stopped before the request leaves is not documented; the side pane's web search and Cowork actions are not documented to follow these lists.

controls.mechanism: Copilot Chat with enterprise data protection requires an Entra sign-in to the Edge profile, whose MFA is Microsoft Entra Conditional Access; BrowserSignin and RestrictSigninToPattern hold the browser to work accounts

steps.title: Force a work sign-in
body: Set BrowserSignin to Force (2) and RestrictSigninToPattern to the firm's account pattern; enforce MFA for the Microsoft 365 apps in Conditional Access.

controls.note: Partial on the MFA rule applied to every vendor: Edge documents no second factor of its own, so the factor is whatever Entra enforces, and the tenant binding keeps Copilot off personal accounts.

controls.mechanism: Administrator-delivered allow and block lists the user cannot modify; vendor-fixed confirmation of authentication and final save or submit; Cowork actions on or off by policy

steps.title: Block sites where an action would be consequential
body: Add banking, HR, payment and client-portal origins to BrowsingWithCopilotBlockList, which takes precedence over the allow list.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to Claude in Chrome: the site lists are admin-delivered and non-overridable, but no administrator can add an action class or a rule over what Copilot types or submits.

controls.mechanism: Microsoft 365 Copilot compliance offerings and the Service Trust Portal feed the organisation's TPRM platform; the Edge privacy statement describes what Edge sends to Copilot

evidence.title: Microsoft Edge privacy — data and consent used by Copilot in Microsoft Edge
Get started with the Microsoft Service Trust Portal

controls.note: External: the assessment, evidence expiry and reassessment trigger live in the TPRM platform, as for every vendor; Copilot in Edge runs on Microsoft 365 Copilot, assessed with toolM365Copilot. Reassess when browsing with Copilot leaves preview and when Cowork actions are enabled.

controls.mechanism: EdgeCopilotEnabled disabled (users cannot use Copilot in Edge); AllowBrowsingWithCopilot disabled; CopilotCoworkToolActionsEnabled disabled; all support dynamic policy refresh; Edge management service changes download within up to 90 minutes

steps.title: Turn browsing off
body: Set AllowBrowsingWithCopilot to Disabled for the affected group; Edge applies it on policy refresh without a restart.

steps.title: Turn Copilot off
body: Set EdgeCopilotEnabled to Disabled; users cannot use Copilot in Microsoft Edge.

controls.note: Partial on the kill-switch rule: the switches reach every managed browser without the user, but delivery through the Edge management service can take up to 90 minutes and the docs do not say that a browsing task already running stops when the policy refreshes.

settings.name: BrowserSignin
settings.where: Edge policy › BrowserSignin
settings.default: Users decide whether to sign in
settings.recommended: Force users to sign-in to use the browser (2)
settings.why: Every managed Edge runs on a signed-in profile, so Copilot is always the governed Entra-profile version.

settings.name: RestrictSigninToPattern
settings.where: Edge policy › RestrictSigninToPattern
settings.recommended: The firm's account pattern (for example .*@firm\.com)
settings.why: A personal Microsoft account cannot be signed in to a managed Edge, which would bring consumer Copilot outside every policy.

settings.name: EdgeCopilotEnabled
settings.where: Edge policy › EdgeCopilotEnabled
settings.default: Eligible users can use Copilot and turn it off
settings.recommended: Not configured; Disabled is the incident switch
settings.why: Copilot stays available, and one policy removes it from every managed browser on refresh when something goes wrong.

settings.name: Microsoft365CopilotChatIconEnabled
settings.where: Edge policy, or Edge management service › Copilot tab › Copilot icon in the toolbar
settings.recommended: Enabled
settings.why: Staff use the governed Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat in the side pane rather than a consumer AI site; browsing with Copilot also requires it.

settings.name: EdgeEntraCopilotPageContext
settings.where: Edge policy, or Edge management service › Copilot tab › Access to browser context
settings.default: Enabled outside the EU, disabled in the EU; users can change it
settings.recommended: Enabled, set explicitly so users cannot switch it
settings.why: Page summarisation is much of the value and stays under enterprise data protection; DLP-protected pages remain excluded, and regulated teams disable it by group.

settings.name: CopilotPageContext
settings.where: Edge policy › CopilotPageContext
settings.default: Enabled outside the EU, disabled in the EU; users can change it
settings.recommended: Disabled
settings.why: The side-pane Copilot this policy covers (not Copilot with enterprise data protection, which EdgeEntraCopilotPageContext governs) cannot read work pages.

settings.name: CopilotOnSensitiveContentEnabled
settings.where: Edge policy › CopilotOnSensitiveContentEnabled
settings.recommended: Disabled
settings.why: Copilot is kept away from page content the firm's DLP policies protect, rather than reasoning over it in a protected session.

settings.name: ShareBrowsingHistoryWithCopilotSearchAllowed
settings.where: Edge policy › ShareBrowsingHistoryWithCopilotSearchAllowed
settings.default: Shared; users can turn it off
settings.recommended: Enabled
settings.why: Only tenant-approved work sites are shared to improve Microsoft 365 Copilot Search; regulated teams disable it so browsing history stays on the device.

settings.name: AllowBrowsingWithCopilot
settings.where: Edge policy, or Edge management service › Copilot tab › Browse with Copilot
settings.default: Off; users can turn it on
settings.recommended: Enabled for a pilot group only; Disabled for everyone else
settings.why: Copilot acting on sites in users' own sessions reaches only the people the firm is piloting it with, and the policy is the off switch.
settings.requires: Microsoft 365 Copilot licence; preview outside the EEA

settings.name: BrowsingWithCopilotAllowList
settings.where: Edge policy, or Edge management service › Browse with Copilot › Allowed sites
settings.recommended: The work sites the pilot needs; the curated commonly used sites list only after review
settings.why: Copilot can browse and act only on origins the firm listed, and users cannot add any.

settings.name: BrowsingWithCopilotBlockList
settings.where: Edge policy, or Edge management service › Browse with Copilot › Blocked sites
settings.recommended: Banking, payment, HR and client-portal origins
settings.why: Sites where an agent action would move money or client data are excluded even if a broad allow list covers them.

settings.name: CopilotCoworkToolActionsEnabled
settings.where: Edge policy › CopilotCoworkToolActionsEnabled
settings.recommended: Disabled outside the Cowork pilot group
settings.why: Cowork cannot take actions in the browser for people who have not been through the pilot, and users cannot switch it on themselves.

settings.name: BuiltInAIAPIsEnabled
settings.where: Edge policy › BuiltInAIAPIsEnabled
settings.recommended: Allowed
settings.why: Websites can use the browser's on-device language model APIs; nothing leaves the device through them, so regulated teams disable them only to remove the surface.

settings.name: Enhanced personalization
settings.where: Microsoft Copilot enhanced personalization control (tenant or per user), or Microsoft Graph enhancedPersonalizationSetting
settings.recommended: On; off for groups whose client data must not persist between chats
settings.why: Copilot memory follows the firm's choice per group; administrators can search and delete memories but cannot restrict what is remembered.

settings.name: DLP for Microsoft 365 Copilot — Restrict Copilot from processing content › Processing prompts
settings.where: Microsoft Purview › Data loss prevention › Policies › location "Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat"
settings.recommended: On, for the firm's sensitive information types (credentials, national IDs, client account numbers)
settings.why: A prompt in the Edge side pane carrying a sensitive type is refused before Copilot processes it.

settings.name: Audit — CopilotInteraction (AppHost Edge)
settings.where: Microsoft Purview › Audit › CopilotInteraction, filtered on AppHost Edge
settings.recommended: On, streamed to the SIEM; alert on XPIADetected and JailbreakDetected
settings.why: Side-pane interactions, the resources they touched and the injection verdicts are searchable and alertable outside the browser.

settings.name: In-browser protection (session policies)
settings.where: Defender for Cloud Apps session policies, enforced in the Edge for Business work profile
settings.recommended: On for the firm's sanctioned cloud apps, monitoring upload, download and copy-paste
settings.why: The sessions Copilot acts in are monitored and constrained in the browser itself, which is where the agent's actions happen.

tools.name: Microsoft Copilot Studio (agents, knowledge, tools and connectors, autonomous triggers, computer use)

variants.name: Agents on the standard harness (topics, generative orchestration, agent flows)
variants.note: The harness most governance pages are written for (Entra Agent ID, tools, connectors, computer use); publishes to Teams and Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Direct Line websites, WhatsApp, Facebook and Dynamics 365 Customer Service.

variants.name: Agents on the GitHub Copilot harness (goal-driven, multi-step, files, skills, memory, sandbox)
variants.note: A Copilot Studio runtime, not the GitHub Copilot service; customer data is not sent to GitHub Copilot and Copilot Studio's privacy, compliance and residency commitments apply. Runs each task in a sandbox governed by Copilot Studio.

variants.name: Agents on the Copilot chat harness (extend Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat)
variants.note: Published to internal teams only; billed by consumption or included in the Microsoft 365 Copilot licence. Conversation transcripts are not written to Dataverse for Microsoft 365 Copilot agents.

summary: Microsoft's low-code agent builder: makers author agents from instructions, knowledge sources (SharePoint, OneDrive, uploaded files, public websites, Dataverse, connectors), tools (Power Platform connectors, agent flows, MCP servers, REST APIs, prompts, computer use) and event triggers, then publish them to Teams and Microsoft 365 Copilot, SharePoint, websites and messaging channels. Agents run in Microsoft's cloud on Azure OpenAI models by default, with Anthropic, Mistral and xAI models available per environment once an administrator allows them; connectors reach third-party services from Microsoft's cloud, and on-premises systems through the on-premises data gateway.

The administrator is the Power Platform administrator: data policies and advanced connector policies, environment and environment-group settings (Product > Features > Copilot Studio agents), Managed Environments sharing limits, Manage > Inventory with Block and the quarantine API, Security > Threat detection and Security > Identity and access > Agent access channels. Each new agent gets a Microsoft Entra Agent ID; maker and user activity is audited in Microsoft Purview; conversation transcripts land in the environment's Dataverse.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Standalone Copilot Studio subscription (any supported channel, premium connectors, Copilot Credits); Copilot Studio for Microsoft Teams plan in select Microsoft 365 subscriptions (classic orchestration, Teams only); the Copilot chat harness is billed by consumption or included in Microsoft 365 Copilot. The free trial cannot publish.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Generative AI features draw on Azure OpenAI Service and Bing Search. External models (Anthropic, Mistral, xAI) need access allowed in the Microsoft 365 admin center and then Enable External Models per environment or environment group; Anthropic is a Microsoft subprocessor under the DPA since 2026-01-07 but is excluded from the EU Data Boundary, and xAI is US-only.

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: A vendor-hosted platform: prompts, knowledge, tool calls and model calls are processed in Microsoft's cloud. In some geographies outside the United States, generative AI features move data across regional boundaries once a Global or Power Platform administrator allows it; Bing-powered features fall under the Microsoft Services Agreement and Privacy Statement. A configured external threat-detection provider receives the prompt, recent history, prior tool outputs and proposed tool inputs.

facts.label: Retention & training
facts.value: Transcripts are saved to the environment's Dataverse (a bulk-delete job removes them after 30 days unless changed) and held in Copilot Studio storage for up to 28 days; administrators can stop saving per environment or environment group. Purview retention covers interactions under Microsoft Copilot Experiences. The tenant setting Data sharing for Dynamics 365 Copilot and Power Platform Copilot AI Features (human review and model improvement) is disabled by default.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio (Security and governance overview)

facts.label: Admin planes
facts.value: Power Platform admin center (Security > Data and privacy > Data policy; environment Settings > Product > Features > Copilot Studio agents; Managed Environments; Manage > Inventory and Manage > Copilot Studio; Security > Threat detection; Security > Identity and access > Agent access channels; Tenant settings), Microsoft Entra admin center (agent identities), Microsoft Purview (Audit, DSPM for AI, DLP) and the Teams or Microsoft 365 admin center for org-catalogue approval.

facts.label: Network requirements
facts.value: The on-premises data gateway opens outbound connections to Azure Service Bus on TCP 443 (default), 5671, 5672 and 9350-9354; no inbound port is required.

items.title: Where each control lives
body: Power Platform admin center: Security > Data and privacy > Data policy (Copilot Studio connectors for authentication, knowledge, HTTP, skills, triggers and channels; Configure connector > Connector actions and Connector endpoints); environment Settings > Product > Features > Copilot Studio agents (Control maker credential options, transcript settings, Enable External Models); Edit Managed Environments > Manage sharing; Manage > Inventory (Block, Download); Security > Threat detection > Additional threat detection; Security > Identity and access > Agent access channels; Copilot > Settings (Connected Agents Copilot Studio); Settings > Tenant settings (Publish Copilots with AI features, Environment routing); Manage > Data (preview) for gateways. Microsoft Entra admin center: agent identities. Microsoft Purview: Audit, DSPM for AI, DLP on the Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat location.

links.title: Security and governance in Copilot Studio

items.title: Whose credentials a tool runs on
body: Each tool's Authentication is End user (the default for connectors and flows) or Maker-provided; computer use defaults to Maker-provided. The automatic security scan warns the maker before publishing when Maker-provided is chosen, the inventory records connectionProvider Maker or User per connector operation, and Control maker credential options lets the administrator remove the Maker-provided choice per environment or environment group, at the cost of autonomous and scheduled runs, which then fail.

links.title: Automatic security scan in Copilot Studio

riskNotes.note: Both End-user and Maker-provided credentials are enabled by default, and computer use defaults to the maker's. A tool on maker credentials lends the maker's access to every consumer; the inventory's connectionProvider field finds them and Control maker credential options removes the choice.

Any licensed user can build in the default environment unless environment routing sends makers to personal developer environments; the inventory lists drafts and Agent Builder agents but not classic chatbots.

Knowledge sources, connector and MCP results and web pages re-enter the orchestrator. Built-in UPIA and XPIA blocking is vendor-run and always on; the admin-configured external threat detection (preview) sees proposed tool calls only and allows them by default if it does not answer within one second.

No authentication lets anyone with the link chat with the agent unless a data policy blocks Chat without Microsoft Entra ID authentication in Copilot Studio; locally uploaded knowledge files are served to anyone who can use the agent, whatever the source file's permissions.

Event triggers and computer use act with no person present; Ask the end user before running is off by default on every tool, and computer use can operate on any website or application unless the maker turns on access control.
SharePoint and OneDrive files and folders added through Upload files are synchronised into a Dataverse index, so whoever can write the folder writes what every agent grounded on it reads.

Anthropic models sit outside the EU Data Boundary, Bing-powered features fall under the Microsoft Services Agreement, and an external threat-detection provider receives conversation and tool data under its own terms.

controls.mechanism: Data policy blocking the connector Chat without Microsoft Entra ID authentication in Copilot Studio (No authentication becomes unavailable and Require users to sign in cannot be turned off); environment or environment-group setting Product > Features > Copilot Studio agents > Control maker credential options (End-user credentials / Maker-provided credentials); Managed Environments agent sharing rules (Let people grant Viewer permissions, Only share with individuals, Limit number of viewers; bot-limitSharingMode, bot-maxLimitUserSharing, bot-authoringSharingDisabled); Agent access channels (preview)

steps.title: Require authentication on every channel
body: In Security > Data and privacy > Data policy, in a policy scoped to all environments, block Chat without Microsoft Entra ID authentication in Copilot Studio so only Authenticate with Microsoft or Authenticate manually can be published.

steps.title: Remove maker-provided credentials
body: In Manage > Environment groups (or Environments) > Settings > Product > Features > Copilot Studio agents, set Control maker credential options to End-user credentials only.

steps.title: Limit who an agent can be shared with
body: In Edit Managed Environments > Manage sharing, clear Let people grant Viewer permissions when agents are shared, or select Only share with individuals and set Limit number of viewers.

steps.title: Restrict the publishing channels
body: In Security > Identity and access > Agent access channels, clear the channels an environment group may not publish to (preview; published agents on a blocked channel fail at runtime).

controls.note: Native on the authorisation rule: the administrator can enforce authentication on every channel, remove maker credentials (the confused-deputy case) and cap who may use or co-author an agent, tenant-wide through data-policy scope and environment groups. Defaults to change: new agents start on Authenticate with Microsoft, but makers may pick No authentication until the data policy blocks it; both credential modes are allowed by default, and computer use defaults to maker credentials. Costs and gaps: with maker credentials removed, scheduled and autonomous runs fail for lack of a live user; sharing rules need Managed Environments, apply only to new shares (non-compliant agents can only be unshared) and take up to an hour; Generic OAuth agents cannot restrict which users chat. Policy administration is not the enforcement path: Entra and the connector runtime enforce it.

controls.mechanism: A Microsoft Entra Agent ID created automatically for every new agent since May 2026 (no opt-out), a child of the Microsoft-owned Microsoft Copilot Studio agent identity blueprint, with the owner as sponsor, connector API permissions attached at publish (Operations.Execute.All or per-operation scopes) and deletion with the agent; legacy agents keep app registrations until migrated (Actions > Recommendations > Migrate Copilot Studio agents to Microsoft Entra Agent ID, preview)

steps.title: Find each agent's identity
body: Read the GUID at agent Settings > Advanced > Metadata > Entra Agent ID, or the entraAgentId field in the inventory, and review the identity, its sponsor and its API permissions in the Entra admin center.

steps.title: Migrate legacy app-registration agents
body: In Actions > Recommendations open Migrate Copilot Studio agents to Microsoft Entra Agent ID for enhanced agent governance, migrate a pilot batch, and validate before the next.

steps.title: Put Conditional Access on connector scopes
body: Target the connector permissions on agent identities with Conditional Access (network location, device compliance, risk); today it is evaluated only when the agent runs in Microsoft Teams.

steps.title: Give agent access an expiry
body: Assign agent identities access through Entra ID Governance access packages with an end date so access lapses unless the sponsor extends it.

controls.note: Partial on the agent-identity rule, the same word as toolM365Copilot: a directory principal is minted per agent, inventoried with a sponsor and deleted with the agent, and no one in the tenant can mint tokens for it. But what the agent does in connected systems is authenticated as the end user or the maker through the Power Platform connection, not as the agent identity; Conditional Access on the agent identity is evaluated only in Teams (other channels use the existing connector authentication flow); custom connectors, MCP servers and REST API tools add no permissions to it; agents created before May 2026 run on app registrations until migrated; Agent Builder agents have no identity. Disabling the agent identity as a revocation path is not documented; deleting the agent is.

controls.mechanism: Power Platform inventory (Manage > Inventory and Manage > Copilot Studio; Power Platform API inventory, Azure Resource Graph, Power Platform for Admins V2 connector): every Copilot Studio and Agent Builder agent, drafts included, with ownerId, createdBy, environment, lastPublishedAt, authentication, channels, sharedWithViewers (entireTenant), entraAgentId, isQuarantined, and powerPlatformConnectors[].operations[] with connectionProvider (Maker or User) and connectionIdSharedByMaker; Block in the command bar and the quarantine API

steps.title: Query the inventory for maker-credential agents
body: In Manage > Inventory filter Copilot Studio agents, add the Connectors column, and query powerPlatformConnectors operations where connectionProvider is Maker through Azure Resource Graph or the inventory API; export to CSV for reconciliation.

steps.title: Find public and tenant-wide agents
body: Filter on authentication None and sharedWithViewers.entireTenant true, and on owners who have left, to reassign or block.

steps.title: Block what should not run
body: Select a published agent in Manage > Inventory or Manage > Copilot Studio and choose Block; unblock once remediated.

controls.note: Native on the registry rule: the platform itself keeps an authoritative, queryable record of every agent with owner, channels, authentication mode and, per connector operation, whether it runs on the maker's or the user's connection, and the administrator can block or quarantine from it. Limits: most configuration fields are preview; capabilities reflect the published version only; detailed capability data covers Power Platform connectors and a web-search flag, not HTTP nodes, REST API tools, computer use or other knowledge sources; at most 200 resources of each type per agent; changes appear within 15 to 20 minutes; classic chatbots are listed separately. The inventory records agents after the fact rather than admitting them, so the publication gate is a separate row.

controls.mechanism: Solutions as the versioned unit; Power Platform pipelines with delegated deployments (approval before deploying as a service principal or pipeline owner), stages the same exported artifact must pass in order, and redeploy of previous solution versions; Settings > Tenant settings > Environment routing to personal developer environments and Publish Copilots with AI features; Submit for admin approval to list an agent in the org catalogue of Teams and Microsoft 365

steps.title: Route makers out of the default environment
body: Turn on Environment routing in Settings > Tenant settings so makers land in managed personal developer environments governed by environment-group rules.

steps.title: Promote through an approved pipeline
body: Build a pipeline (development, test, production) in the Deployment Pipeline Configuration app with delegated deployments so a named approver releases each stage.

steps.title: Keep a way back
body: Turn on the pipeline setting that allows redeploying previous solution versions from the run history.

steps.title: Approve org-wide listing
body: Review agents submitted with Show to everyone in my org in the Teams admin center Manage apps page before they appear in Built for your org.

controls.note: Partial on the rollout rule. Met: versioning (solutions, managed layers), a promotion gate a person approves (delegated deployments) that cannot skip a stage, and rollback by redeploying an earlier version. Not met: nothing forces a maker to use the pipeline, since anyone with maker rights in an environment can publish straight to its channels; the org-catalogue approval covers the listing and its details only, and content changes republish without re-approval; no canary or percentage release, and no evaluation gate. Publish Copilots with AI features is an all-or-nothing switch. Pipeline targets must be Managed Environments.

controls.mechanism: Built-in user prompt-injection (UPIA) and cross-domain prompt-injection (XPIA) blocking on every published agent, always on, with blocked-message counts in the maker's Protection status and Security analytics; admin-configured external threat detection (preview) at Security > Threat detection > Additional threat detection per environment (Microsoft Defender or a partner webhook) that allows or blocks each proposed tool call, with Set error behavior; content moderation level set per agent by the maker

steps.title: Connect runtime threat detection
body: Register the Entra app with the provider's federated credential, then in Security > Threat detection > Additional threat detection select the environment, choose Set up and Allow Copilot Studio to share data with a threat detection provider.

steps.title: Fail closed
body: Change Set error behavior from Allow the agent to respond to Block the query, so a provider timeout (one second) or error blocks the tool call.

steps.title: Review blocked prompt attacks
body: Ask makers to review Protection status > See details > Security analytics (Reason for block) for their agents.

controls.note: Partial on the input-screening rule: the injection classifiers that screen prompts and knowledge are vendor-internal, always on and not admin-tunable, and their detections surface in a per-agent maker view rather than an administrator event stream. External threat detection is an attach point where a Defender or partner classifier can block, but it judges proposed tool calls (with the prompt, history and prior tool outputs as context) rather than screening each knowledge chunk before context assembly; it is preview, generative orchestration only, set per environment or environment group with no tenant-wide, PowerShell or API setting (new environments start without it), and allows the call by default when the provider is slow. Content moderation is a maker setting. On this drawing the pin sits on our gateway, which screens the grounding it returns.

controls.mechanism: Copilot Studio compliance offerings (HIPAA BAA, HITRUST, FedRAMP, SOC, ISO, PCI DSS, CSA STAR) and the Service Trust Portal audit reports feed the organisation's TPRM platform; external-model and threat-detection provider terms assessed separately

evidence.title: Copilot Studio compliance offerings
Get started with the Microsoft Service Trust Portal
Allow external language models (Anthropic subprocessor, EU Data Boundary and FedRAMP exclusions)

controls.note: External: the assessment, evidence expiry and reassessment trigger live in the organisation's TPRM platform, as for every vendor. Copilot Studio is an Online Service covered by HIPAA (BAA), HITRUST, FedRAMP, SOC, ISO, PCI DSS and CSA STAR, but Anthropic models are outside the EU Data Boundary, FedRAMP and PCI DSS, xAI is US-only, and an external threat-detection provider handles data under its own terms. Re-assess when external models are enabled, when a threat-detection provider is connected and when harnesses change. The Service Trust Portal renders client-side and was not read.

controls.mechanism: Power Platform data policies (Security > Data and privacy > Data policy): every connector classified Business, Non-business or Blocked, connectors in different groups cannot be combined, Copilot Studio connectors for HTTP, skills, event triggers (Microsoft Copilot Studio), knowledge and channels; Configure connector > Connector actions (per-action allow or deny, default for new actions); Connector endpoints (preview); advanced connector policies (default-deny allowlist, MCP server-level blocking); enforced in real time with the Publish button unavailable on violation; exemptions no longer supported

steps.title: Classify connectors tenant-wide
body: In Security > Data and privacy > Data policy create a policy with Add all environments, move each connector to Business, Non-business or Blocked, and block HTTP, Skills with Copilot Studio and the Microsoft Copilot Studio (event triggers) connector where they are not needed.

steps.title: Allow only the actions you need
body: On a blockable connector choose Configure connector > Connector actions, deny write actions you do not accept, and set Default connector action settings to block new actions.

steps.title: Pin connectors to known endpoints
body: Use Configure connector > Connector endpoints on HTTP and the SharePoint and public-website knowledge connectors to allow only approved URLs (preview).

steps.title: Move to default-deny
body: In an environment group's Rules tab add Advanced connector policies with only the approved certified and MCP connectors; new connectors are blocked automatically.

controls.note: Native on the tool-permission rule: a tenant policy classifies connectors, refuses violating combinations at authoring and publish and again at runtime, and restricts individual operations and endpoints; blocking a connector also blocks MCP tools that rely on it, and tools on end-user credentials keep the caller's authority. Limits: in classic data policies new connectors land in Non-business by default, so unclassified is blocked only under advanced connector policies; ACP does not cover custom connectors, HTTP or the Copilot Studio virtual connectors and is runtime-only in Copilot Studio until its design-time enforcement ships; action control excludes custom and unblockable connectors and handles triggers only in PowerShell; endpoint filtering is preview; scoping is per environment, not per user; computer use's website and app allowlist is a maker setting, off by default.

controls.mechanism: On-premises data gateway: data-source credentials encrypted with asymmetric encryption before storage in the gateway cloud service and decrypted only on the gateway host; outbound-only relay; administrator-assigned recovery key; Manage > Data (preview) for gateway users, members, clusters and Manage gateway installers; maker OAuth connections held in the Power Platform connection store; computer-use stored credentials in internal storage or the customer's Azure Key Vault

steps.title: Restrict who can install gateways
body: In Manage > Data (preview) turn on Tenant administration and use Manage gateway installers to name the users allowed to register gateways.

steps.title: Control gateway use and remove members
body: Use Manage users on each gateway cluster to limit Can use and Can use + share (and the data-source types they may create), and Remove members or clusters that should no longer relay.

steps.title: Hold the recovery key
body: Keep the recovery key assigned at install where administrators can find it; it is required to restore, migrate or take over the gateway.

steps.title: Keep computer-use passwords in your vault
body: Under the computer use tool's Stored credentials choose the Azure Key Vault option (subscription, resource group, vault and secret name) instead of internal storage.

controls.note: Partial on the credential rule, the same word as toolM365Copilot: Microsoft ships the gateway, the relayed credential is encrypted to the host and never reaches the model, nothing is opened inbound, and gateway access and installation are administrator-controlled. But the gateway uses one stored standing credential per data source for every caller, rotation is a manual edit of that connection, no short-lived issuance or rotation of the gateway key pair is documented, and maker OAuth connections sit in Microsoft's connection store with lifetimes set by the target service and no documented bulk revocation; removing the Maker-provided choice (D3-APA) stops their use rather than revoking them. The gateway can also carry standard connectors straight to on-premises sources, bypassing our gateway (a recorded deviation).

controls.mechanism: SharePoint and OneDrive knowledge retrieved on behalf of the signed-in user (Authenticate with Microsoft by default) with sensitivity-label permission trimming; synced Upload files > SharePoint/OneDrive items check the user's permission before answering; connector tools default to end-user credentials; administrator control of attachable sources through data-policy knowledge connectors (documents, SharePoint and OneDrive, public websites), Connector endpoints filtering and Control maker credential options

steps.title: Stop uploads that bypass source permissions
body: Block Knowledge source with documents in Copilot Studio in the data policy; locally uploaded files are answered to anyone who can use the agent.

steps.title: Allow only governed sites as knowledge
body: On Knowledge source with SharePoint and OneDrive in Copilot Studio and on the public-websites connector use Configure connector > Connector endpoints to allow only approved site URLs (preview).

steps.title: Keep every read on the user's entitlement
body: Set Control maker credential options to End-user credentials so connector knowledge and tools run as the invoking user.

steps.title: Keep labelled SharePoint content out of agents
body: In the Purview portal create a DLP policy on the Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat location with Content contains > Sensitivity labels and Prevent Copilot from processing content; Microsoft applies it to Copilot Studio agents grounded on SharePoint in Teams, SharePoint and Microsoft 365 Copilot.

controls.note: Native on the retrieval rule, the same word as toolM365Copilot: SharePoint, OneDrive and synced knowledge is retrieved with the invoking user's permissions and label trimming, and the administrator decides which source types and sites makers may attach and can remove maker credentials. Outside it: locally uploaded documents are not identity-scoped (block the connector), public websites are public, content already overshared in SharePoint is returned (remediate with the DSPM and SharePoint Advanced Management reports on toolM365Copilot), No-authentication agents cannot use SharePoint, encrypted files are not grounded at all, and endpoint filtering is preview. Restricted SharePoint Search, where still on, blocks SharePoint knowledge. The Purview label rule keeps labelled SharePoint content out of agents in Teams, SharePoint and Microsoft 365 Copilot; files a maker uploads, public websites and connector payloads are not inspected, so what may be uploaded is decided before publication.

controls.mechanism: Purview unified audit log: maker events (BotCreate, BotUpdateOperation-BotPublish, -BotShare, -BotAuthUpdate, BotComponentUpdate, AIPluginOperationUpdate, BotDelete) and CopilotInteraction per user turn with the channel in AppHost and the transcript thread ID, readable through the Office 365 Management Activity API; conversation transcripts in the environment's Dataverse ConversationTranscript table (Content JSON of every activity; node-level nodeTraceData only with the maker's enhanced-transcripts toggle); per-agent Application Insights set by the maker; Entra sign-in logs for agent identities

steps.title: Keep transcripts in Dataverse
body: In the environment group rule Accessing transcripts from conversations in Copilot Studio agents (or environment Settings > Product > Features > Copilot Studio agents) keep Allow conversation transcripts and their associated metadata to be saved in Dataverse on.

steps.title: Retain and export transcripts
body: Cancel the Bulk Delete Conversation Transcript Records Older Than 1 Month job, create one with your retention, and ingest the ConversationTranscript table into your store.

steps.title: Stream maker and usage audit events
body: Filter Copilot Studio activities in Purview Audit and collect them through the Office 365 Management Activity API for the SIEM.

controls.note: Partial on the tracing rule: run and maker records land where we can query them (our Dataverse, Purview, the Management Activity API), but per-step capture of tool and connector calls with arguments is not documented as part of the default transcript; node-level trace and Application Insights are maker toggles per agent that the administrator cannot floor. Transcripts are not written for Dataverse for Teams environments, developer environments or Microsoft 365 Copilot agents; SharePoint-grounded answers are REDACTED; records are written after 30 minutes of inactivity; audit records carry the transcript thread ID, not the text; some channels are excluded from logging, and non-Microsoft channels need Purview pay-as-you-go billing. Capture is not tamper resistance: the SIEM copy is the record.

controls.mechanism: Block on a published agent in Manage > Inventory or Manage > Copilot Studio (reversible); Power Platform API POST .../copilotstudio/environments/{EnvironmentId}/bots/{BotId}/api/botQuarantine/SetAsQuarantined; org-wide levers: data-policy blocks on channels and connectors (enforced in real time), Agent access channels (preview), Publish Copilots with AI features, Control maker credential options; deleting an agent deletes its Entra Agent ID

steps.title: Block one agent
body: In Manage > Inventory select the published agent and choose Block; makers can still test it, but no other channel can use it.

steps.title: Quarantine by API
body: As an AI, Power Platform or Global administrator call botQuarantine/SetAsQuarantined with a token carrying CopilotStudio.AdminActions.Invoke, and check isBotQuarantined.

steps.title: Cut maker-credential connections
body: Set Control maker credential options to End-user credentials on the environment group; every tool switches to end-user sign-in immediately.

steps.title: Close channels org-wide
body: Clear channels in Agent access channels, or block the channel connectors in the data policy; agents already published there fail at runtime.

controls.note: Partial on the kill-switch rule: the administrator can block or quarantine a specific agent and close channels or connectors for all agents, but whether a conversation or autonomous run already in progress stops is not documented, no delay is published for block or quarantine (the maker-credential switch may take a minute to propagate), and revoking the OAuth connections a maker authorised is not a documented bulk action; the maker-credential switch stops their use for tools. Quarantine and block do not cover classic chatbots. Deleting the agent removes its Entra Agent ID.

settings.name: Copilot Studio authors
settings.where: Power Platform admin center › Manage › Tenant settings › Copilot Studio authors
settings.recommended: An Entra security group of makers who have taken the firm's agent-building training
settings.why: Only people the firm has trained and can name build agents, instead of every licensed user.

settings.name: Security group (environment)
settings.where: Power Platform admin center › Manage › Environments › (environment) › Edit › Security group
settings.recommended: The Entra group for the team that owns the environment, on every production and sandbox environment
settings.why: Removing someone from the group disables them in the environment, so leavers and other teams cannot reach its agents or data; the default and developer environments cannot take a group.

settings.name: Chat without Microsoft Entra ID authentication in Copilot Studio
settings.where: Power Platform admin center › Security › Data and privacy › Data policy › (tenant-wide policy) › connector
settings.default: Not blocked (makers can pick No authentication)
settings.recommended: Blocked, in a policy scoped to Add all environments
settings.why: Makers can no longer publish an agent anyone with the link can chat with; only Authenticate with Microsoft or Authenticate manually remain.

settings.name: Control maker credential options
settings.where: Power Platform admin center › Manage › Environment groups › (group) › Settings › Product › Features › Copilot Studio agents
settings.default: End-user credentials and Maker-provided credentials both allowed
settings.recommended: End-user credentials only, except an environment group set aside for reviewed autonomous agents
settings.why: A tool can no longer lend its maker's access to every user of the agent; scheduled and autonomous agents fail without maker credentials, hence the separate group.

settings.name: Only share with individuals (no security groups) › Limit number of viewers who can access each agent
settings.where: Power Platform admin center › Manage › Environments › (managed environment) › Edit Managed Environments › Manage sharing › Agent sharing rules
settings.recommended: On with a limit of 20 viewers in the personal-developer environment group; production groups, which publish through pipelines, leave it off
settings.why: An in-progress agent, possibly on maker credentials, cannot be shared to the whole firm before it has been through review; rules apply to new shares and take up to an hour.

settings.name: Direct Line channels in Copilot Studio, Facebook channel in Copilot Studio, WhatsApp channel in Copilot Studio
settings.where: Power Platform admin center › Security › Data and privacy › Data policy › (tenant-wide policy) › connectors
settings.default: Allowed (Direct Line channels allowed by default)
settings.recommended: Blocked tenant-wide, with an excluded environment for approved public-facing agents
settings.why: Agents reach only Teams, Microsoft 365 and SharePoint unless a public agent has been approved for a website or messaging channel.

settings.name: Agent access channels
settings.where: Power Platform admin center › Security › Identity and access › Agent access channels › (environment group)
settings.recommended: Teams + Microsoft 365 and SharePoint only on every environment group except the public-agent one
settings.why: Channels cannot be added by editing agent code, and a channel closed later makes agents already published there fail at runtime (preview).

settings.name: Data policy (Business, Non-business, Blocked)
settings.where: Power Platform admin center › Security › Data and privacy › Data policy › New Policy › Assign connectors › Define scope › Add all environments
settings.default: No tenant policy; new connectors land in the default group (Non-business)
settings.recommended: Tenant-wide policy with the firm's systems in Business, consumer storage and social connectors Blocked, and the default group set to Blocked
settings.why: Connectors in different groups cannot be combined, so an agent reading client data cannot also post it to a consumer service, and a new connector stays unusable until reviewed.

settings.name: Connector actions › Default connector action settings
settings.where: Data policy › (blockable connector) › Configure connector › Connector actions
settings.recommended: Block for new actions; deny delete and send actions the firm's agents do not need on each Business connector
settings.why: An agent can call only the operations someone approved, and an action the vendor adds later is blocked until reviewed; custom and unblockable connectors are out of scope.

settings.name: Advanced connector policies
settings.where: Power Platform admin center › Manage › Environment groups › (group) › Rules › Advanced connector policies
settings.recommended: On in mixed mode on production environment groups, listing only the approved certified and MCP connectors
settings.why: Default-deny means a connector or MCP server nobody approved is blocked automatically; custom, HTTP and Copilot Studio virtual connectors still need the classic policy.

settings.name: HTTP › Connector endpoints
settings.where: Data policy › HTTP › Configure connector › Connector endpoints
settings.recommended: Allow the firm's approved API hosts, then * Deny
settings.why: An HTTP request node can reach only listed hosts, closing the arbitrary-URL exfiltration path; dynamically built URLs are not evaluated (preview).

settings.name: Knowledge source with documents in Copilot Studio
settings.where: Data policy › (tenant-wide policy) › connector
settings.recommended: Blocked in production environment groups; makers ground on SharePoint, which keeps the user's permissions
settings.why: A file a maker uploads is answered to anyone who can use the agent, whatever its source permissions were.

settings.name: Microsoft Copilot Studio (event triggers)
settings.where: Data policy › (tenant-wide policy) › connector
settings.recommended: Blocked tenant-wide; allowed only in the environment group for reviewed autonomous agents
settings.why: Agents that act on an event with nobody present exist only where someone reviewed what they can reach.

settings.name: Hosted browser in computer use
settings.where: Power Platform admin center › Manage › Tenant settings › Hosted browser in computer use
settings.recommended: Off until a computer-use pilot has an owner and an access-control allow list
settings.why: Computer use can act on any website, by default on the maker's stored credentials, from a Microsoft-hosted machine.

settings.name: Allow Copilot Studio to share data with a threat detection provider
settings.where: Power Platform admin center › Security › Threat detection › Additional threat detection › (environment) › Set up
settings.recommended: On with Microsoft Defender for every environment that holds production agents
settings.why: Each proposed tool call is checked by a classifier the firm runs before it executes; there is no tenant-wide switch, so new environments need it too (preview).

settings.name: Set error behavior
settings.where: Additional threat detection › (environment) › Set error behavior
settings.recommended: Block the query
settings.why: A provider that is slow (over one second) or down blocks the tool call instead of letting it run unscreened.

settings.name: DLP policy scoped to the Microsoft 365 Copilot location (sensitivity labels)
settings.where: Microsoft Purview › Data loss prevention › Policies › location "Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat" › Content contains › Sensitivity labels
settings.recommended: Exclude the firm's highest label (e.g. Highly Confidential – client restricted) from processing
settings.why: Agents grounded on SharePoint in Teams, SharePoint and Microsoft 365 Copilot do not use labelled content in their answers.

settings.name: Allow conversation transcripts and their associated metadata to be saved in Dataverse (required for enhanced reporting)
settings.where: Power Platform admin center › Manage › Environment groups › (group) › Rules › Accessing transcripts from conversations in Copilot Studio agents
settings.recommended: On
settings.why: Every conversation lands in the firm's own Dataverse where it can be exported; turning it off removes the record of what agents said and did.

settings.name: Allow agent owners and editors to see session transcripts from conversation interactions in their agents
settings.where: Same environment-group rule › Accessing transcripts from conversations in Copilot Studio agents
settings.recommended: Off in production environment groups
settings.why: Makers stop reading and downloading what colleagues typed to their agents, often client data; the security team still reads transcripts in Dataverse.

settings.name: Bulk Delete Conversation Transcript Records Older Than 1 Month
settings.where: Power Apps › Settings › Advanced settings › Settings › Data Management › Bulk Record Deletion › Recurring Bulk Deletion System Jobs
settings.recommended: Keep the 30-day job; export the ConversationTranscript table to the SIEM before it runs
settings.why: Thirty days in Dataverse is the baseline retention, and the exported copy is the record investigations use.

settings.name: Audit (Copilot Studio activities)
settings.where: Microsoft Purview › Audit; collected through the Office 365 Management API
settings.default: Administrative activities enabled on all tenants
settings.recommended: On, streamed to the SIEM; alert on BotUpdateOperation-BotAuthUpdate and BotUpdateOperation-BotShare
settings.why: Maker changes to an agent's authentication and sharing, and every user interaction, are searchable outside the platform.

settings.name: Inventory
settings.where: Power Platform admin center › Manage › Inventory (Copilot Studio agents), or the Power Platform inventory API
settings.recommended: Reviewed monthly for agents on maker credentials, with No authentication, shared tenant-wide or owned by leavers
settings.why: Every agent, drafts included, is listed with owner, channels and per-connector credential mode, so the risky ones can be found before they are used.

settings.name: Block
settings.where: Power Platform admin center › Manage › Inventory › (published agent) › Block
settings.recommended: The incident runbook's first step for a misbehaving agent
settings.why: Stops one agent on every channel except the maker's test chat, reversibly, without touching other agents.

settings.name: SetAsQuarantined
settings.where: Power Platform API › POST copilotstudio/environments/{EnvironmentId}/bots/{BotId}/api/botQuarantine/SetAsQuarantined
settings.recommended: Wired into the SOAR playbook, with an app registration holding CopilotStudio.AdminActions.Invoke
settings.why: The SOC can isolate an agent from an alert without opening the admin center; classic chatbots are not covered.

settings.name: Migrate Copilot Studio agents to Microsoft Entra Agent ID for enhanced agent governance
settings.where: Power Platform admin center › Actions › Recommendations
settings.default: Agents created before May 2026 keep app registrations
settings.recommended: Migrate every legacy agent, a pilot batch first
settings.why: Each agent gets a directory identity with a sponsor and its connector scopes visible in Entra, instead of an app registration nobody reviews (preview).

settings.name: Microsoft Entra Conditional Access (agent identity connector scopes)
settings.where: Microsoft Entra admin center › Conditional Access › policy targeting the connector permissions on Copilot Studio agent identities
settings.recommended: Require a compliant network location and block high-risk agent sign-ins for connectors that write
settings.why: Token issuance for a connector can be refused by Entra; today it is evaluated only when the agent runs in Teams.

settings.name: Environment routing
settings.where: Power Platform admin center › Manage › Tenant settings › Environment routing
settings.recommended: On for new and existing makers, routed into a governed personal-developer environment group
settings.why: Makers build in their own managed environment under group rules instead of the shared default environment everyone can see.

settings.name: Is delegated deployment
settings.where: Pipelines host › Deployment Pipeline Configuration › (production stage) › Is delegated deployment
settings.recommended: On for the production stage, as a service principal, with an approval step in the OnApprovalStarted flow
settings.why: An agent reaches production only after a named approver releases it, deployed as a service identity rather than the maker.

settings.name: Bing search
settings.where: Power Platform admin center › Manage › Environments › (environment) › Generative AI features › Edit
settings.recommended: Selected
settings.why: Web grounding is much of an agent's value; Bing-powered features fall under the Microsoft Services Agreement, so regulated teams leave it clear.

settings.name: Enable External Models (Power Platform Anthropic, Power Platform Mistral AI, Power Platform XAI)
settings.where: Microsoft 365 admin center (provider) then Power Platform admin center › Environment groups › (group) › Rules
settings.recommended: Only the providers the firm's vendor assessment approved; Anthropic off where EU Data Boundary commitments apply
settings.why: An agent's prompts reach a model provider only after the firm has assessed it; Anthropic is outside the EU Data Boundary and xAI is US-only.

settings.name: Data sharing for Dynamics 365 Copilot and Power Platform Copilot AI Features
settings.where: Power Platform admin center › Manage › Tenant settings
settings.recommended: Disabled
settings.why: Microsoft does not capture or human-review the firm's prompts and outputs to improve its models.

settings.name: Restrict Users in your organization from installing gateways
settings.where: Power Platform admin center › Manage › Data (preview) › On-premises data gateways › Manage gateway installers
settings.default: Off (anyone in the organisation can install a gateway)
settings.recommended: On, with named gateway administrators as the only installers
settings.why: Nobody can stand up a relay from an on-premises system to Microsoft's cloud, holding that system's credential, without IT knowing.
