tools.name: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Microsoft Copilot app, Copilot Chat, in-app Copilot, agents and connectors)

variants.name: Microsoft Copilot app and Copilot Chat (web, desktop, mobile; copilot.cloud.microsoft)
variants.note: Copilot Chat (Basic) is included for Entra users with a qualifying Microsoft 365 subscription and is web-grounded; Graph-grounded chat needs the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on licence.

variants.name: Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and Teams
variants.note: Built into the apps, not an add-in; the Multiple account access to Copilot for work documents policy decides whether a personal Copilot subscription can act on work files.

variants.name: Researcher and Analyst
variants.note: Part of the core Copilot Chat experience and outside agent-related settings; availability is controlled only by blocking the agent tenant-wide.

variants.name: Agents from the Agent Store and Copilot connectors (synced and federated MCP connectors)
Copilot Cowork (agentic tasks in Microsoft's cloud, usage-based billing)
variants.note: Access is granted only by a spending policy that selects Cowork (Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration); the Cowork entry under Agents > All agents no longer controls access. Where Cowork drives the person's local Edge browser, that local reach is the agentic browser drawing's (toolCopilotEdge), not this SaaS record's.

summary: Microsoft's work-grounded assistant, renamed Microsoft Copilot (and Copilot Chat to Microsoft Copilot Chat) during 2026 with no change to its security, compliance or privacy terms: the Copilot app and Copilot Chat, Copilot inside Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and Teams, the Researcher and Analyst reasoning agents, agents from the Agent Store, Copilot connectors, and the Cowork agentic system. Inference runs inside the Microsoft 365 service boundary on Microsoft-hosted models, with OpenAI and Anthropic as subprocessors; grounding reads Microsoft Graph content with the signed-in user's permissions, and web grounding sends a generated query to Bing outside the DPA and EU Data Boundary.

The admin planes are the tenant's own: Microsoft Entra (Conditional Access, tenant restrictions v2, agent identities), the Microsoft 365 admin center (Copilot > Settings, Agents > All agents, Copilot connectors > Your connections), Microsoft Purview (DLP location "Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat", sensitivity labels, DSPM, audit, retention, eDiscovery), the SharePoint admin center (SharePoint Advanced Management), Cloud Policy (Allow web search in Copilot) and Defender. Interaction content is stored in the user's mailbox and exported through a Graph API; CopilotInteraction audit records stream through the Office 365 Management Activity API.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Copilot Chat (Basic): web-grounded, no extra cost with a qualifying Microsoft 365 subscription. Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) add-on: Graph and Work IQ grounding and the full in-app experience; Cowork is billed by usage on top. Microsoft 365 E7 bundles E5, Microsoft Copilot, Agent 365 and the Entra Suite.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Microsoft-hosted models plus OpenAI and Anthropic as subprocessors (admin toggle at Copilot > Settings > Data access > AI providers for other large language models). LLM calls go to the closest region and may overflow to other regions at peak; EU traffic stays in the EU Data Boundary, except Anthropic models, which are currently excluded from it.

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: Prompts, grounding content and responses are processed in the Microsoft 365 service boundary. With web search on, a generated query (the whole prompt only when it is very short; no user or tenant identifiers) goes to Bing, where the DPA, HIPAA and the EU Data Boundary do not apply.

facts.label: Retention & training
facts.value: Prompts, responses and Graph data are not used to train foundation models; Azure OpenAI abuse monitoring is opted out. Interaction history is stored with the organisation's Microsoft 365 content, deletable by users in My Account and governed by Purview retention policies (location Microsoft Copilot experiences).

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot (Copilot documentation hub; Copilot controls overview)

facts.label: Network requirements
facts.value: Allow *.cloud.microsoft (primary URL copilot.cloud.microsoft); Microsoft does not support managing Copilot Chat through domain, URL or IP blocking.

facts.label: Data residency
facts.value: A covered workload in the Product Terms data-residency commitments since 2024-03-01, including Advanced Data Residency and Multi-Geo.

items.title: Where each control lives
body: Microsoft 365 admin center: Copilot > Settings (User access, Data access, Copilot actions), Copilot > Overview > Security (the Copilot security dashboard), Agents > All agents (Registry, Requests, Block, Delete), Agents > Settings (Allowed agent types, User access, Sharing, Agent management rules) and Copilot connectors > Your connections. Purview portal: Data Loss Prevention, DSPM, Audit, eDiscovery, Data Lifecycle Management. SharePoint admin center: Active sites (Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot), Reports > Data access governance, Advanced Management. Entra admin center: Conditional Access, Cross-tenant access settings, Agent identities.

links.title: Manage Microsoft Copilot settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center
Security for Microsoft Copilot (security dashboard, Security Dashboard for AI)

items.title: Prompt-injection defence in depth
body: Microsoft runs jailbreak and cross-prompt-injection (XPIA) classifiers on inputs before model execution and sanitises hidden Unicode in pasted prompts; detections surface as JailbreakDetected and XPIADetected in CopilotInteraction audit records and as Defender alerts. The customer-side levers are source controls: DLP exclusion of external email from grounding, Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 prompt-injection detection on inbound mail, web-grounding domain exclusion and the web search policy.

links.title: Microsoft Copilot prompt defense in depth

riskNotes.note: Every mail, file, chat and connector result Copilot grounds on is model input. MSRC has published a run of server-side-fixed Critical command-injection disclosures (CVE-2025-32711, the EchoLeak zero-click chain; CVE-2026-26129, -26164, -42824); the XPIA classifiers that answer them are vendor-run and may not cover every scenario.

Copilot grounds on whatever the user's permissions already reach, so a prompt can pull far more of SharePoint, OneDrive and Teams than the question needed; web-grounding queries leave the DPA and the EU Data Boundary.

Agent Builder agents can be shared with named colleagues without admin approval; a personal Copilot subscription can act on work documents unless Multiple account access to Copilot for work documents is disabled; consumer Copilot with a personal Microsoft account is outside the tenant. Shared agents become ownerless when their creator is deleted, and per-user connector OAuth grants have no admin-visible expiry.
Federated connectors gain write, update and delete tools from early October 2026 and Cowork automated tasks run without a person present; both let users persist approval.

controls.mechanism: Tenant restrictions v2 in Entra ID > External Identities > Cross-tenant access settings, enforced by Entra when the sec-Restrict-Tenant-Access-Policy: <TenantId>:<policyGuid> header reaches login.live.com, login.microsoft.com, login.microsoftonline.com and login.windows.net (proxy injection, authentication plane only) or through universal tenant restrictions (Global Secure Access) or Windows GPO

steps.title: Block external tenants and personal Microsoft accounts
body: In Entra ID > External Identities > Cross-tenant access settings set the default tenant restrictions to block external accounts and apps, and add a policy for the Microsoft account tenant so personal-account sign-ins are refused.

steps.title: Signal the policy on every sign-in
body: Have the proxy insert sec-Restrict-Tenant-Access-Policy with your tenant ID and the cross-tenant access policy ID on the four Microsoft sign-in domains, or use universal tenant restrictions in Global Secure Access to tag traffic without a proxy.

controls.note: Partial on the browser-pin rule: Microsoft documents a tenant-restriction header that the organisation's proxy or SSE injects and Entra enforces server-side, so personal tenants and personal Microsoft accounts are refused at sign-in. Proxy injection covers only the authentication plane (Windows GPO and Global Secure Access add data-plane coverage), and anonymous resources are not blocked. Microsoft does not support managing Copilot Chat by domain, URL or IP blocking. A customer proxy does not control Microsoft's own egress: Bing web grounding, federated connector calls and Cowork's hosted environment leave from Microsoft's cloud; the vendor-side levers there are the Allow web search in Copilot policy and web-grounding domain exclusion (up to 1,000 sites).

controls.mechanism: Microsoft Purview DLP policy on the "Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat" location: Content contains > Sensitive information types with Prevent Copilot from processing content > Processing prompts (preview) or > Performing Web Searches, and Content contains > Sensitivity labels to keep labelled files and email out of grounding; encrypting labels without the EXTRACT usage right withhold content; Endpoint DLP blocks paste into web Copilot Chat

steps.title: Block prompts that carry sensitive information
body: In the Purview portal go to Data Loss Prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Custom > Custom policy, turn on the Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat location, and add Content contains > Sensitive information types with Prevent Copilot from processing content > Processing prompts (and > Performing Web Searches to keep those prompts off Bing).

steps.title: Keep labelled items out of responses
body: In a separate rule of the same location add Content contains > Sensitivity labels with Prevent Copilot from processing content, so labelled files and email are cited but not read.

steps.title: Withhold EXTRACT on encrypting labels
body: Configure encrypting sensitivity labels so groups that must not get Copilot answers lack the EXTRACT usage right; Copilot returns encrypted content only with VIEW and EXTRACT.

steps.title: Block paste into web Copilot Chat
body: Use Endpoint DLP to block paste of sensitive content and files by sensitivity label into the web version of Copilot Chat on onboarded devices.

controls.note: Native on the redaction rule: a vendor tenant control inspects typed prompts for sensitive information types and blocks the turn, and excludes labelled items from grounding, server-side. Boundaries: block only, no masking; the prompt block is in preview and rolling out; DLP does not scan files uploaded into a prompt, only the typed text; no response-side inspection is documented (labels are displayed and inherited, not enforced on output); SIT and label conditions cannot share a rule; the label rule covers files and email sent on or after 2025-01-01, not calendar invites, and in Word, Excel and PowerPoint is evaluated at file open; policy changes take up to four hours; evaluations that time out are deferred (DLPEvaluationDeferred in the audit record), so watch that field.

controls.mechanism: Service Trust Portal audit reports and whitepapers, and the Copilot privacy page's compliance statement, feed the organisation's TPRM platform

evidence.title: Get started with the Microsoft Service Trust Portal (ISO/IEC, SOC 1-3, GDPR, FedRAMP, PCI, CSA STAR)
Data, Privacy, and Security for Microsoft Copilot (compliance offerings, subprocessors, EUDB)

controls.note: External: the assessment, its evidence expiry and the reassessment trigger live in the organisation's TPRM platform. The Service Trust Portal publishes the ISO/IEC, SOC 1-3, GDPR, FedRAMP, PCI and CSA STAR material behind an Entra sign-in and NDA; the privacy page states GDPR, ISO 27001, HIPAA and ISO 42001 coverage for Copilot, points to a Copilot & Copilot Chat Risk Assessment Quickstart, and names OpenAI and Anthropic as subprocessors with Anthropic excluded from the EU Data Boundary. Re-assess on model and subprocessor changes; the portal itself renders client-side and was not read.

controls.mechanism: Federated connector write, update and delete tools (rolling out from early October 2026) show a confirmation card with the action parameters and default to Needs approval per tool, with Allow once, Allow for conversation or Always allow; Cowork asks before an automated task sends email, posts or changes a shared system, and users can pre-authorise; no admin setting forces approval

steps.title: Review which connectors can write
body: In the Microsoft 365 admin center open Copilot connectors > Your connections, select a federated connector and read its Tools section (coming soon); disable or scope connectors whose write tools you do not accept.

steps.title: Tell users how to reset approvals
body: Users set the connector's Write/Delete tools back to Needs approval in Copilot Settings > Sources; a publisher change to a tool resets it to Needs approval.

steps.title: Limit who can run Cowork
body: Grant Cowork only through a spending policy scoped to a security group at Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration; users outside every Cowork policy cannot start tasks.

controls.note: Partial on the human-approval rule: a present person approves each write seeing its parameters, but users can persist Always allow per tool or pre-authorise Cowork automated tasks, and the administrator can neither require approval nor remove Always allow. Read tools never prompt. Actions run with the user's own permissions in the target system. Agents with their own actions (Copilot Studio, API plugins) carry their publisher's confirmation behaviour, which this row does not cover.

controls.mechanism: Vendor-run jailbreak and cross-prompt-injection (XPIA) classifiers screen inputs before model execution, always on and not configurable, logged as JailbreakDetected and XPIADetected in CopilotInteraction audit records and raised as Defender alerts; admin-set source controls: DLP Email is received from > External users (preview), Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 prompt-injection detection on inbound mail, web-grounding domain exclusion

steps.title: Watch the classifier signals
body: In the Purview portal Audit search, filter the CopilotInteraction operation and alert on AccessedResources.XPIADetected and Messages.JailbreakDetected; SecOps sees the same detections in the Defender portal.

steps.title: Keep external email out of grounding
body: Add a rule to the Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat DLP location with Email is received from > External users and Prevent Copilot from processing content.

steps.title: Screen inbound mail for injection
body: With Defender for Office 365 Plan 2, inbound messages carrying prompt injection get the High confidence phishing verdict with detection technology Prompt injection protection; route that verdict to quarantine in your anti-spam policy.

steps.title: Narrow web grounding
body: Run ConfigureTenantDomainExclusions.ps1 (Search Administrator) to exclude up to 1,000 sites from web grounding, or disable web search with the Allow web search in Copilot policy.

controls.note: Partial on the input-screening rule: screening of retrieved content is vendor-internal, documented but not configurable ("may not be available in all Microsoft Copilot scenarios"), and a detection is an audit event, not an admin quarantine. The switches the administrator does own act on sources rather than classifying content: the external-email rule reads sender metadata only; Defender for Office 365 covers inbound mail only and a focused set of intents (URL exfiltration, system-prompt and tool discovery). SharePoint files, Teams chats, Copilot connector content and federated MCP results have no admin-tunable screening.

controls.mechanism: Purview DSPM data risk assessments (default weekly assessment of the top 100 SharePoint sites by usage, custom and item-level assessments) with sensitive-information classification and oversharing counts; SharePoint Advanced Management data access governance reports and the Content Management Assessment

steps.title: Run data risk assessments
body: In the Purview portal open Solutions > DSPM > Discover > Data risk assessments, review the default weekly assessment and create custom assessments for the sites and users Copilot will serve.

steps.title: Run the data access governance reports
body: In the SharePoint admin center open Reports > Data access governance and run Site permissions across your organization and Sensitivity labels applied to files, then the Sharing links and 'Everyone except external users' activity reports.

steps.title: Start the Content Management Assessment
body: In the SharePoint admin center select Advanced Management > Start assessment and rerun it every 30 days to track oversharing, inactive and ownerless sites.

controls.note: Native on the inventory rule: the vendor inventories and classifies what Copilot can reach in SharePoint and OneDrive and reports the oversharing. Limits: the default assessment covers the top 100 sites by usage; 200,000 items per location; item-level scanning is SharePoint only and at most 10 sites; Exchange mailboxes, Teams chats, synced Copilot connector content and federated sources are not in the oversharing assessments; results lag by days. DSPM needs Purview licensing; SharePoint Advanced Management features come with Copilot licences, and E5 alone gets only part of the reports.

controls.mechanism: No customer-run tunnel for MCP servers; the Microsoft Graph connector agent (on-premises, outbound port 443) authenticates with an Entra app registration's client secret (expiry chosen at creation) or certificate; connectors such as ServiceNow offer Microsoft Entra ID OpenID Connect federated auth with no stored secret; federated connector OAuth tokens are held by Microsoft per user; Entra sessions are bounded by sign-in frequency and revoked with Revoke-MgUserSignInSession

steps.title: Prefer secretless connector auth
body: Where the connector offers it, choose Microsoft Entra ID OpenID Connect (Federated Auth) so the connector authenticates to the source without storing or rotating a client secret.

steps.title: Bound the connector agent's credential
body: Configure the Graph connector agent with a certificate, or a client secret created under App registration > Certificates and secrets with a short expiry, and rotate it there.

steps.title: Revoke a user's tokens
body: Run Revoke-MgUserSignInSession to invalidate the user's refresh tokens; access tokens last up to an hour unless the app supports continuous access evaluation.

controls.note: Partial on the credential rule for a product without an MCP tunnel: the Entra-issued credentials (connector agent app, Graph export apps, user sessions) are scoped, expiring and rotatable by the administrator, and connector tokens never reach the model; but the per-user OAuth tokens federated connectors hold for third-party services are in Microsoft's custody with lifetime set by the third party and no admin rotation or revocation documented, and some synced connectors still accept Basic authentication with a stored password. The Graph connector agent is an indexing agent for synced connectors, not a tunnel; its app credential is the load-bearing secret on that path.

controls.mechanism: Agents > Settings > Allowed agent types (built by Microsoft / your organization / external publishers; also governs default federated connectors), Agents > Settings > User access, per-agent publish and install audiences, and per-connector allowed-user scope and staged rollout to Entra groups at Copilot connectors > Your connections; write, update and delete tools are not enabled separately

steps.title: Switch connectors to allowlist mode
body: At Agents > Settings > Allowed agent types clear the Microsoft-published and third-party options so federated connectors, including future ones, are off until an administrator enables each one.

steps.title: Scope each connector to groups
body: At Copilot connectors > Your connections enable a connector and use Add staging to limit it to specific Microsoft Entra ID groups.

steps.title: Scope agent access
body: At Agents > Settings > User access choose Specific users/groups, and publish each agent to named groups rather than everyone.

controls.note: Partial on the tool-permission rule: an admin-locked allowlist of connectors and agents with group scoping, but no per-tool or read/write scoping: a connector admitted for reads admits the write, update and delete tools its publisher ships (from early October 2026), and the admin Tools list is view-only. Actions keep the caller's authority (the user's own permissions at the source). Researcher and Analyst sit outside agent settings. The Set-FederatedConnectorToggle cmdlet is retired; its state is honoured only until 2026-10-20.

controls.mechanism: Microsoft 365 admin center Agents > All agents > Registry (every agent available to the tenant, with publisher type, owner, channel, platform, status and risk signals; Export; Agents without owners), Requests (Pending review / update / activate; Publish to store or Reject submission), Block, and Copilot connectors > Your connections; Allowed agent types for allowlist mode

steps.title: Review and export the registry
body: At Agents > All agents > Registry filter by publisher type, platform and status, export to CSV, and work the Agents without owners card.

steps.title: Approve before anything is published
body: At Agents > All agents > Requests review each agent's data sources, tools and permissions, then Publish to store to a named audience or Reject submission; updates wait as Pending update.

steps.title: Close the default-allow paths
body: Restrict Agents > Settings > Allowed agent types and Sharing (Specific users), and Block any agent in the registry that should not run.

steps.title: Give agent access an expiry
body: Assign agent identities access through access packages with an end date (policy "For users, service principals, and agent identities" > All agents) so access lapses unless the sponsor extends it, and run Reassign ownerless agents created with Agent Builder to manager at Agents > Settings > Agent management rules.

controls.note: Native on the registry rule: an authoritative record of every agent and connector in the tenant with owner and approval state, and admin enforcement (approval queue, allowed types, block). Gaps to watch: Agent Builder agents can still be shared with named individuals without approval (Sharing set to No users keeps direct sharing, and the control covers only Agent Builder agents); they appear in the registry and can be blocked, but are not pre-approved. Microsoft-published federated connectors are on until Allowed agent types is changed. Registry risk signals need E7 or Agent 365; Cowork plugins are managed on their own page. The grants that carry Copilot into third-party systems are per-user OAuth consents the administrator cannot list or expire per grant; disabling a connector for everyone is the only admin lever.

controls.mechanism: CopilotInteraction records in the unified audit log (Audit Standard; auditing on by default for new tenants) with AppHost, AgentId, AISystemPlugin (BingWebSearch), AccessedResources (SensitivityLabelId, PolicyDetails, XPIADetected) and Messages (JailbreakDetected), streamed through the Office 365 Management Activity API (Audit.General, record type 261); prompt and response text through the Graph getAllEnterpriseInteractions API

steps.title: Stream the audit records to the SIEM
body: Subscribe to the Audit.General content type in the Office 365 Management Activity API and parse record type 261 (CopilotInteraction) with the Copilot schema.

steps.title: Export prompts and responses
body: Grant an app AiEnterpriseInteraction.Read.All and call GET /copilot/users/{id}/interactionHistory/getAllEnterpriseInteractions per user, or subscribe to aiInteraction change notifications.

steps.title: Confirm auditing and search it
body: In the Purview portal Audit, filter Activities - operation names on CopilotInteraction; web queries appear as AISystemPlugin.Id BingWebSearch.

controls.note: Native on the telemetry rule: programmatic export of interaction events (with the files, sites, plugins, agents and policy decisions involved) and of conversation content, for fusion with the gateway's record. Limits: audit records carry references, not prompt text, so content comes from the Graph export API, which needs a Copilot licence, has no delta and does not return Copilot Studio agent interactions; capture is not tamper resistance, so the SIEM copy is the record of truth.

controls.mechanism: Nothing in Copilot lists personal accounts or unsanctioned assistants; Microsoft's own SSE/CASB products (Defender for Cloud Apps cloud app catalog, Generative AI category; Global Secure Access shadow AI discovery) and Purview DSPM browser and endpoint signals do the discovery

evidence.title: Manage generative AI apps for your organization (DSPM for AI, Defender for Cloud Apps)
Shadow AI discovery in Global Secure Access
Multiple account access to Microsoft Copilot for work and school documents

controls.note: External on the discovery rule: Copilot does not report personal Microsoft accounts on the organisation's domains or other AI tools staff use; the integration points are Defender for Cloud Apps (Cloud apps > Cloud app catalog, Category Generative AI, tag Unsanctioned), Global Secure Access and the Purview browser extension; the Security Dashboard for AI aggregates their findings (third-party AI apps, shadow agents) but is Microsoft's security stack around Copilot, not Copilot. The Agent Registry's Unmanaged agents count covers agents inside the tenant only. Prevention, credited here only: tenant restrictions v2 refusing the Microsoft account tenant, and the Cloud Policy setting Multiple account access to Copilot for work documents set to Disabled so personal Copilot subscriptions cannot act on work files.

controls.mechanism: Grounding through Microsoft Graph and the Semantic Index with the signed-in user's permissions, synced connector items carrying source ACLs, federated connectors calling as the user; admin corpus scoping with Restricted Content Discovery (Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot, Set-SPOSite -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch), the DLP sensitivity-label exclusion and connector allowed-user scope

steps.title: Pull sensitive sites out of Copilot
body: In the SharePoint admin center open Sites > Active sites > the site > Settings and turn on Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot, or run Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true; report with Start-SPORestrictedContentDiscoverabilityReport.

steps.title: Exclude labelled content from grounding
body: Add a Content contains > Sensitivity labels rule to the Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat DLP location with Prevent Copilot from processing content.

steps.title: Limit connectors to the groups that need them
body: Scope each Copilot connector at Copilot connectors > Your connections to specific Entra ID groups with Add staging.

controls.note: Native on the retrieval rule: retrieval runs with the requesting user's entitlements at the source, and the administrator can restrict which sites, labels and connectors are returned. Limits: Restricted Content Discovery changes no permissions, still lets users reach content they own or recently used, does not apply to OneDrive and takes time to propagate on large sites; Restricted SharePoint Search is retiring (no new enablement from 2026-07-31) and was never a security boundary; synced connectors are only as tight as the ACLs they map; what is already overshared is returned until permissions are fixed (see D3-DI).

controls.mechanism: Group-based authorisation administered in the Microsoft 365 admin center (Copilot licence assignment, Agents > Settings > User access, per-agent publish and install audiences, connector allowed-user scope, AI Administrator role); consent paths documented: Review permissions > Grant admin consent when an agent is published or installed, and connector apps registered in the target system (for example ServiceNow System OAuth > Application Registry with Microsoft Entra ID OpenID Connect)

steps.title: Decide who gets Copilot and agents
body: At Agents > Settings > User access choose Specific users/groups, and publish or install each agent to named groups.

steps.title: Grant admin consent deliberately
body: When installing or publishing an agent, read the Review permissions pane before selecting Grant admin consent and Accept.

steps.title: Register the connector in the target system
body: For a synced connector, register the app in the target (ServiceNow: System OAuth > Application Registry, OIDC provider Microsoft Entra ID) and limit its scope there.

controls.note: Native on the authorisation rule: the console administers group-scoped authorisation over Copilot, agents and connectors, and Microsoft documents the consent path for agent permissions and per-connector target registration. The target tenant's consent (ServiceNow, Google, HubSpot) is that tenant's control; federated connectors authenticate each user into the third party, and whether its admin must approve the app is the third party's setting, not documented per connector by Microsoft. Policy administration is not the enforcement path: Entra and the source system enforce.

controls.mechanism: Block access to Copilot Chat for all users or groups; remove Microsoft 365 Copilot licences; Agents > All agents > Block per agent (Researcher and Analyst only tenant-wide); disable the agent type used by connectors or set a connector to No users (up to 10 minutes); drop users from Cowork spending policies; Revoke-MgUserSignInSession per user

steps.title: Block an agent for the whole organisation
body: At Agents > All agents select the agent, choose Block > Block agent and Save; delete it for a 30-day soft delete, or Permanently delete.

steps.title: Block Copilot Chat
body: Block access to Copilot Chat for all users or selected groups, and set Custom link for blocked Microsoft Copilot app under Copilot > Settings to explain why.

steps.title: Cut every connector
body: Disable the agent type used by Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors in Allowed agent types; each connector's allowed-user scope becomes No users within about ten minutes.

steps.title: Revoke a user's sessions
body: Run Revoke-MgUserSignInSession for the user; access tokens already issued last up to an hour unless the app supports continuous access evaluation.

controls.note: Partial on the kill-switch rule: the administrator can switch Copilot, agents and connectors off org-wide, but the docs do not say that work already running stops (Cowork automated tasks, a Researcher run, an agent mid-task), the delay for agent and Chat blocks is not documented (connector changes take up to 10 minutes), third-party OAuth grants are not revoked in bulk by any documented action, and blocking a SharePoint or Foundry agent affects only Copilot Chat. Session revocation leaves issued access tokens alive for up to an hour.

settings.name: User access
settings.where: Microsoft 365 admin center › Agents › Settings › User access
settings.recommended: Specific groups — the Entra groups licensed for Copilot
settings.why: Who can use agents, plugins and connectors is a group decision you can audit, not everyone by default.

settings.name: Tenant restrictions v2
settings.where: Microsoft Entra admin center › External Identities › Cross-tenant access settings › Tenant restrictions
settings.recommended: Block external tenants and personal Microsoft accounts, signalled by your proxy or Global Secure Access
settings.why: Staff on managed devices cannot sign in to Copilot with a personal or another organisation's account and take client data with them.

settings.name: DLP for Microsoft 365 Copilot — Restrict Copilot from processing content › Processing prompts
settings.where: Microsoft Purview › Data loss prevention › Policies › location "Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat"
settings.recommended: On, for your sensitive information types (credentials, national IDs, client account numbers)
settings.why: A prompt carrying a sensitive information type is refused before Copilot processes it.

settings.name: DLP for Microsoft 365 Copilot — Content contains › Sensitivity labels
settings.where: Microsoft Purview › Data loss prevention › Policies › location "Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat"
settings.recommended: Exclude your highest label (e.g. Highly Confidential – client restricted) from processing
settings.why: Labelled files and mail can still be cited but their content never enters a Copilot answer.

settings.name: Restricted Content Discovery
settings.where: SharePoint admin center, or Set-SPOSite -Identity <site> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true
settings.recommended: On for sites the oversharing reports flag, until their permissions are fixed
settings.why: An overshared site stops surfacing in Copilot answers and org-wide search while its access is cleaned up.

settings.name: Data risk assessments (DSPM)
settings.where: Microsoft Purview › Data Security Posture Management › Data risk assessments
settings.default: Default assessment of the most-used SharePoint sites
settings.recommended: Default assessment on, plus a custom one over client-engagement sites
settings.why: Finds the sensitive content Copilot can already reach before a user's question does.

settings.name: Data access governance reports
settings.where: SharePoint admin center › Reports › Data access governance
settings.recommended: Run monthly; feed the results to Restricted Content Discovery and site owners
settings.why: Shows sites shared with everyone or with many guests — the oversharing Copilot amplifies.

settings.name: Allow web search in Copilot
settings.where: Cloud Policy service for Microsoft 365 › Allow web search in Copilot
settings.recommended: Enabled
settings.why: Web grounding is much of Copilot's value; generated queries go to Bing outside the Microsoft 365 boundary, so regulated teams turn it off by group.

settings.name: Agent and plugin access
settings.where: Microsoft 365 admin center › Agents › Settings › Agent and plugin access
settings.recommended: Microsoft and your organisation allowed; external publishers off, with approved ones enabled one by one
settings.why: Third-party agents, plugins, connectors and MCP servers reach Copilot only after someone has approved them.

settings.name: Agent requests (review before publishing)
settings.where: Microsoft 365 admin center › Agents › Requests
settings.recommended: Review every request; publish only agents with an owner and a stated data scope
settings.why: The registry stays a list of agents someone is accountable for, not everything anyone built.

settings.name: Connector staged rollout
settings.where: Microsoft 365 admin center › Copilot connectors › Your connections › (connector) › staged rollout
settings.default: New connectors available to all users
settings.recommended: Each connector staged to the groups that need it
settings.why: A connector that can write to a system of record reaches only the people whose job needs it.

settings.name: Cowork spending policy scope
settings.where: Microsoft 365 admin center › Copilot › Cost Management › Configuration › spending policy
settings.recommended: Specific groups — a pilot group first
settings.why: Cowork runs multi-step tasks that send mail and change shared files; it reaches only the people you scope in.

settings.name: Microsoft Graph connector agent — authentication
settings.where: Entra app registration › Certificates and secrets, selected in the connector agent
settings.recommended: Certificate, rotated before expiry
settings.why: The on-premises connector agent holds a credential to your tenant; a certificate is harder to lift than a pasted secret.

settings.name: Prompt injection protection
settings.where: Microsoft Defender portal › Email & collaboration (Defender for Office 365 Plan 2)
settings.recommended: On
settings.why: Inbound mail carrying instructions aimed at an AI assistant is detected before Copilot reads it.

settings.name: Audit — CopilotInteraction records
settings.where: Microsoft Purview › Audit; streamed through the Office 365 Management Activity API
settings.recommended: On, streamed to your SIEM; alert on JailbreakDetected and XPIADetected
settings.why: Every Copilot and agent interaction, the resources it touched and the classifier verdicts are in one record type you can search and alert on.

settings.name: Block agent
settings.where: Microsoft 365 admin center › Agents › All agents › (agent) › Block
settings.recommended: Your incident runbook's first step for a misbehaving agent
settings.why: Stops one agent for the whole organisation without removing anyone's Copilot.

tools.name: MLflow Tracking Server and Model Registry

variants.name: MLflow Tracking Server with Model Registry (`mlflow server`)
variants.note: One process serves the UI, the tracking and registry REST APIs and, by default, proxied artifact access (--serve-artifacts with --artifacts-destination). Metadata goes to --backend-store-uri (SQLite mlflow.db by default, PostgreSQL or MySQL in production); users and grants to a separate auth database. Listens on 127.0.0.1:5000 unless started with --host.

variants.name: MLflow Python client (mlflow, MlflowClient) in the training job and the promotion pipeline
variants.note: The library the job uses to log runs, datasets and models (MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI, MLFLOW_TRACKING_USERNAME / MLFLOW_TRACKING_PASSWORD or MLFLOW_TRACKING_AUTH), and the promoter uses to copy versions and move aliases. Everything it records is what the calling code chose to log.

summary: Open-source (Apache-2.0) experiment tracking server and Model Registry, self-hosted by the organisation; current release 3.17.2 (2026-10-21). It is the registry-and-promotion tier of this drawing: the training job logs runs, input datasets and the candidate model to it, the registry holds numbered versions of each registered model with aliases (champion), tags, descriptions, signatures and the link back to the run, and consumers load `models:/<name>@<alias>`. Model stages (Staging/Production/Archived) are deprecated since 2.9.0 in favour of aliases and tags.

Nothing is trained or served here: inference runs wherever the model is loaded. Metadata stays in the operator's database and artifact bytes in the operator's object store; what leaves is anonymised usage telemetry to mlflow-telemetry.io (on by default since 3.2.0), webhook POSTs the operator configures, and, for PEFT adapters, a base-model download from the Hugging Face hub at load time.

Every control is a server flag, environment variable or basic_auth.ini key the operator sets. Authentication is off by default (`--app-name basic-auth` turns it on), the shipped default_permission is READ for every authenticated user, and there is no approval workflow, signing or audit log in open-source MLflow; creating a model version, moving an alias and transitioning a stage all need the same EDIT grant on the registered model.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Free and open source (Apache-2.0) on PyPI as mlflow (3.17.2, 2026-10-21) and mlflow-skinny. Managed MLflow is sold by Amazon SageMaker AI (MLflow Apps and Tracking Servers, MLflow 3.10 on Apps) and Databricks; those are out of scope here.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: None in this role. Clients call the REST API at MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI; models registered here are loaded and run by whatever consumes them (`mlflow.pyfunc.load_model("models:/<name>@<alias>")`, a serving tier).

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: Self-hosted: run metadata to the backend store and artifacts to the artifact store the operator configures. Anonymised usage telemetry (SDK and Python versions, event names, flavors; no parameters, models or usernames) goes to mlflow-telemetry.io by default since 3.2.0; MLFLOW_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=true or DO_NOT_TRACK=true on the server disables UI telemetry globally. Webhooks POST registry events to HTTPS endpoints the operator lists.

facts.label: Retention & training
facts.value: The vendor receives no training data or models. Deleted runs keep metadata and artifacts until `mlflow gc` removes them; deleting a registered model or model version is irrevocable for the registry entry, but the run's artifacts are not removed with it.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: mlflow.org/docs/latest (machine-readable index at /docs/latest/llms.txt; every page has a .md variant)

facts.label: Network defaults
facts.value: Binds 127.0.0.1:5000. Since 3.5.0 the uvicorn server's security middleware validates Host (--allowed-hosts / MLFLOW_SERVER_ALLOWED_HOSTS, default localhost and private IPs) and CORS origins (--cors-allowed-origins, default localhost:*) and sets X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN; it does not run under --gunicorn-opts or --waitress-opts. TLS is left to a reverse proxy.

facts.label: Authentication
facts.value: Built-in basic-auth app (username and password, 12-character minimum, no default admin password since the GHSA-gq3w-7jj3-x7gr fix); role-based grants from 3.13.0 (per-resource legacy APIs removed). SSO through the third-party mlflow-oidc-auth plugin or a reverse proxy; custom schemes through authorization_function.

facts.label: Security reporting
facts.value: SECURITY.md: GitHub private vulnerability reporting only; reports through bounty platforms such as huntr are no longer accepted. Only the latest version is supported; backports are at the maintainers' option.

items.title: Baseline for a self-hosted registry server
body: Run 3.15.0 or later (3.17.2 current): 35 GitHub advisories were published for mlflow in 2025–26, nine critical, several of them authentication bypasses on servers with basic-auth enabled.

Start with `--app-name basic-auth`, MLFLOW_FLASK_SERVER_SECRET_KEY set to a stable secret, the admin password from MLFLOW_AUTH_ADMIN_PASSWORD, and a basic_auth.ini (MLFLOW_AUTH_CONFIG_PATH) with default_permission = NO_PERMISSIONS and database_uri on the central database.
Expose it only as `--host 0.0.0.0 --allowed-hosts <fqdn> --cors-allowed-origins <origin>` behind a TLS-terminating reverse proxy; never set --disable-security-middleware.

Keep artifact access proxied (--artifacts-destination, no --default-artifact-root) so the storage credential lives only on the server, set MLFLOW_CREATE_MODEL_VERSION_SOURCE_VALIDATION_REGEX to the proxied prefix, set MLFLOW_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=true, and leave server job execution (MLFLOW_SERVER_ENABLE_JOB_EXECUTION) off unless it is needed.
On every process that loads registered models set MLFLOW_ALLOW_PICKLE_DESERIALIZATION=false and log scikit-learn and LightGBM models with serialization_format="skops".

links.title: MLflow Tracking Server — Secure Tracking Server, Model Version Source Validation
MLflow — Authentication with username and password

riskNotes.note: Anyone holding EDIT on a registered model can create a version in it, and any authenticated user can create a new registered model and becomes its MANAGE owner, so which adapters are admitted is decided by which registered model consumers load from. A PEFT adapter is logged with source_model_name and source_model_revision (the Hugging Face repo and commit) and the base weights are downloaded on the fly at load; nothing in the registry checks that the base is an approved one.

Many flavors save with pickle or cloudpickle and MLFLOW_ALLOW_PICKLE_DESERIALIZATION defaults to true, so loading a registered model can execute code. The statsmodels flavor ignored the switch until 3.15.0 (GHSA-gqvg-gmmx-x4hm), and CVE-2025-15379 injected shell commands from a model's python_env.yaml when it was served with env_manager=LOCAL (fixed 3.8.1).

The registry server has its own steady CVE stream: 35 GitHub Advisory Database entries published 2025–26, nine critical — a hard-coded default admin password (CVE-2026-2635), unauthenticated directory-traversal RCE in the artifact handler (CVE-2026-2033), FastAPI routes left outside basic-auth (CVE-2026-2652, CVE-2026-0545) and a full-read SSRF through webhook redirects (CVE-2026-64849).

With proxied artifact access the server holds one storage credential that is "an assumed role of access to all artifacts", so anyone who reaches the server with a grant — or the bucket with that credential — reads every candidate; the shipped default_permission is READ. Before 3.11.0rc1 the multipart-upload endpoints skipped per-resource checks entirely (CVE-2026-2651), and S3 presigned download URLs (3.15.0+) work for whoever holds them until they expire.

Evaluation datasets and results are ordinary runs and datasets in an experiment; anyone with EDIT on that experiment can log metrics to it or replace its datasets, so benchmark custody depends on keeping the evaluation experiment out of the trainers' grants.

A model version records a source URI, not a signature; any caller with EDIT can register a version from any source unless MLFLOW_CREATE_MODEL_VERSION_SOURCE_VALIDATION_REGEX restricts it (bypassed with a prompt tag before 3.10.0, CVE-2026-2614), and a PEFT version pulls its base from the hub by commit at every load.

controls.mechanism: Not applicable — MLflow records which dataset a run read (source, digest, schema, profile) but screens and filters nothing; sanitisation belongs to the curation stage

evidence.title: MLflow Dataset Tracking (mlflow.data — source, digest, schema, profile; no screening)
MLflow documentation index (no dataset screening or filtering feature)

controls.note: Not applicable: the objective belongs to the curation & filtering stage — the quality, safety and sensitive-content filter jobs between the content origins and the versioned corpus — which the data platform runs, not the registry. A dataset profile (row and element counts, column statistics) describes a dataset; it detects no poisoned, mislabelled or restricted example, and neither the tracking server nor the registry refuses a run or a version whose inputs were never screened. What MLflow can add downstream is the record: the curation job logs its screened output with mlflow.log_input so runs cite that version (AML.M0025).

controls.mechanism: mlflow.data Dataset objects (source, digest, schema, profile) attached to runs with mlflow.log_input(dataset, context="training" | "validation" | "evaluation"), stored by the tracking server and shown per run; a MetaDataset records source and schema for data MLflow does not hold

steps.title: Log every input dataset on the run
body: In the training job build each input with mlflow.data.from_pandas / from_huggingface / from_spark (or MetaDataset for a remote corpus) and call mlflow.log_input(dataset, context="training"), repeating for "validation" and "evaluation", so the run records the dataset's source, digest, schema and profile.

steps.title: Point the source at an immutable version
body: Pass source= as a versioned address — an object version, a Delta table version, a Hugging Face revision — because mlflow.data.get_source() and a reload read whatever that address serves later.

steps.title: Log the curation output the same way
body: Have the curation job create its own run and log_input the assembled corpus version with context="training", so the corpus version, its source and its digest exist before any training run cites them.

controls.note: Native on this drawing's rule (dataset tracking records source and digest per run). Boundary: dataset-level and per run, written by the job's own client — the server stores what the job reports and requires nothing, so a run with no logged inputs is accepted and can still be registered. Per-example source and licence at ingest (the pin's curation-stage record) stays with the curation pipeline; MLflow holds a pointer and a fingerprint. The digest is identification, not integrity: for pandas and numpy data it is a truncated MD5 over the first 10,000 rows plus shape and column names, and a MetaDataset's covers only name, source and schema (mlflow/data source); CVE-2026-10803 (predictable collisions from deterministic sampling) is fixed in 3.10.1. Cryptographic integrity of the corpus and its modification history belong to the data store's versioning.

controls.mechanism: basic-auth app (`mlflow server --app-name basic-auth`) with role grants (3.13.0+) of READ / USE / EDIT / MANAGE / NO_PERMISSIONS per experiment and registered model, enforced by the server on REST calls and on proxied artifact reads; default_permission in basic_auth.ini sets the floor

steps.title: Turn authentication on
body: Start the server with `--app-name basic-auth`, MLFLOW_FLASK_SERVER_SECRET_KEY set, the admin password in MLFLOW_AUTH_ADMIN_PASSWORD, and database_uri in the file named by MLFLOW_AUTH_CONFIG_PATH pointing at a central database.

steps.title: Deny by default
body: Set default_permission = NO_PERMISSIONS in that basic_auth.ini; the shipped value READ lets every authenticated user read every experiment, run artifact and registered model.

steps.title: Grant reads per experiment and model
body: In /admin → Roles (or AuthServiceClient create_role, add_role_permission, assign_role) grant READ on the specific experiment and registered model to the people and services that need the candidates, never a (experiment, *, READ) wildcard.

steps.title: Keep artifact bytes behind the server
body: Run with --artifacts-destination and proxied access (the default --serve-artifacts, no --default-artifact-root) and give the storage credential only to the server, so every artifact read passes the per-experiment check.

controls.note: Partial on this drawing's rule: server-enforced read scoping per experiment and registered model exists but is off by default, and neither pin sits wholly inside MLflow. Candidate store: with proxied access the basic-auth app checks the experiment id in each /mlflow-artifacts path (list, download, upload, delete, multipart) and model-version artifact downloads against the caller's grant (mlflow/server/auth source); but the server's storage credential is "an assumed role of access to all artifacts", so anyone reaching the bucket directly, or holding an S3 presigned URL (3.15.0+, MLFLOW_PRESIGNED_DOWNLOAD_URL_TTL_SECONDS, default 300), bypasses it, and with --no-serve-artifacts the storage IAM is the only control. Reads are not logged per user (open source has no audit log); the storage access log or a proxy records them (external). Corpus: MLflow holds dataset metadata, not the corpus, so who may read it is cloud IAM on the corpus store. Identity is MLflow's own user store (or the mlflow-oidc-auth plugin or a reverse proxy) and is not carried through to storage. Authorization gaps fixed recently: CVE-2026-2651 (multipart upload, 3.11.0rc1), CVE-2026-2734 (model-version enumeration, 3.10.0), CVE-2026-8147 (trace endpoints, 3.13.0).

controls.mechanism: A model-file scanner and a scanning package mirror (artifact repository / package firewall) in front of the job; MLflow analyses no file. MLflow's integration points: MLFLOW_CREATE_MODEL_VERSION_SOURCE_VALIDATION_REGEX, the model_version.created webhook, and MLFLOW_ALLOW_PICKLE_DESERIALIZATION=false at loaders

evidence.title: MLflow Tracking Server — Model Version Source Validation (regex on the source URI)
MLflow Webhooks — model_version.created (experimental, SQL backend only)
MLflow — Pickle-free models (MLFLOW_ALLOW_PICKLE_DESERIALIZATION, default true)

controls.note: External: the pin is format and content inspection gating admission of base checkpoints and dependencies to the private mirror, and MLflow is neither the mirror nor a scanner. Integration points: have the scanner write cleared artifacts to one prefix and set MLFLOW_CREATE_MODEL_VERSION_SOURCE_VALIDATION_REGEX on the server so the registry refuses versions sourced elsewhere (a regex on the URI, not a check of the bytes; CVE-2026-2614 bypassed it with a prompt tag before 3.10.0); the model_version.created webhook can start a scan, but it fires after registration and asynchronously, so it can only tag or delete. At load time MLFLOW_ALLOW_PICKLE_DESERIALIZATION=false refuses pickle and cloudpickle models (default true; ignored by the statsmodels flavor before 3.15.0) — a loader format policy, not file analysis. A PEFT version downloads its base weights from the Hugging Face hub at load unless that host is reachable only through the mirror.

controls.mechanism: OpenSSF Model Signing (`model_signing sign`, sigstore/model-transparency) run by the promotion pipeline under an identity the job never holds, with the signature bundle stored outside the job's reach and referenced from the release version's tags; MLflow signs and verifies nothing

evidence.title: MLflow model format — MLmodel fields (flavors, run_id, signature, input_example; no signature of the artifact)
sigstore/model-transparency — model_signing sign / verify (Sigstore keyless, private key, certificate, PKCS#11)
OpenSSF Model Signing

steps.title: Split candidate and release registered models
body: In /admin → Roles grant the training job's user EDIT on its experiment and on dev.<team>.<model> only, and a promoter group EDIT on prod.<team>.<model>, so the job can never write the model that is signed.

steps.title: Promote by copy, as the promoter
body: The promoter runs client.copy_model_version(src_model_uri="models:/dev.<team>.<model>@candidate", dst_name="prod.<team>.<model>"), then signs the copied version; the copy needs READ on the source and EDIT on the destination.

controls.note: External: open-source MLflow has no artifact signing, no signature field on a model version and no verification when `models:/` URIs are loaded (docs index; the MLmodel "signature" is the input/output schema, not a cryptographic signature). Integration point: after copy_model_version to the release model, the promotion pipeline downloads the version's artifacts, runs `model_signing sign <dir>` with a Sigstore identity, key or PKCS#11 token the training job never holds, stores the bundle (model.sig) where the job cannot write, and records its location and digest with set_model_version_tag. The serving tier must run `model_signing verify` before loading, since MLflow's loaders will not. For a PEFT version the signature covers the adapter only; the base weights fetched by source_model_revision need their own pinning. MLflow separates credentials by resource, not action — creating a version, setting an alias and transitioning a stage all need EDIT on one registered model — so the job is kept from the release only by the split above, and there is no approval step: the human decision needs a gate around the promoter credential (a CI job with required reviewers, a change ticket). Sign the digest the evaluator tested, and check it matches the copied version's bytes before signing.

controls.mechanism: mlflow.models.evaluate and mlflow.genai.evaluate (built-in and custom scorers, plugin evaluators such as Giskard) logging results to a run, and mlflow.validate_evaluation_results(..., validation_thresholds=...) raising ModelValidationFailedException in the deployer's pipeline; the server never blocks promotion on results

steps.title: Evaluate the candidate in a protected experiment
body: Run mlflow.models.evaluate(model=..., data=..., model_type=...) — or mlflow.genai.evaluate(data=..., predict_fn=..., scorers=[Safety(), Correctness(), Guidelines(...)]) for a tuned LLM — logging to an evaluation experiment on which the trainers hold no EDIT grant.

steps.title: Fail the pipeline on thresholds
body: Call mlflow.validate_evaluation_results(candidate_result=..., baseline_result=..., validation_thresholds={"<metric>": MetricThreshold(threshold=..., greater_is_better=True)}) and run the promotion step only when no ModelValidationFailedException is raised.

steps.title: Add safety judges for tuned LLMs
body: Pass the predefined LLM judges (Safety, Guidelines, Correctness, RetrievalGroundedness) as scorers to mlflow.genai.evaluate; they need a judge model configured.

controls.note: Partial on this drawing's rule: the harness and a threshold check ship, but the check runs in the deployer's pipeline and the registry accepts an alias on a version with no evaluation or a failed one — native would need the server to block promotion on results. Backdoor probing (trigger-phrase hunting) and memorisation or extraction testing are not built-in evaluators; they are custom metrics or scorers, or a plugin, the deployer supplies. The GenAI judges are models grading a model. Benchmark custody depends on RBAC: anyone with EDIT on the evaluation experiment can log metrics or swap its datasets. Validation moved out of mlflow.models.evaluate into validate_evaluation_results in 2.18.0.

controls.mechanism: Storage-side encryption with organisation-held keys (cloud KMS, bucket default encryption) under the artifact store and the backend database; MLflow only passes MLFLOW_S3_UPLOAD_EXTRA_ARGS (for example ServerSideEncryption aws:kms with SSEKMSKeyId) through to S3 uploads

evidence.title: MLflow Artifact Stores — Passing extra arguments to S3 upload (MLFLOW_S3_UPLOAD_EXTRA_ARGS), bucket ownership verification
MLflow Tracking Server — Authentication and Encryption (TLS via reverse proxy)

controls.note: External: MLflow does not encrypt artifacts or metadata at rest and holds no keys. It passes MLFLOW_S3_UPLOAD_EXTRA_ARGS='{"ServerSideEncryption": "aws:kms", "SSEKMSKeyId": "<key>"}' to S3 uploads made by the process that sets it — the server with proxied access, every client without — so enforce it with the bucket's default encryption and a bucket policy that denies other keys; MLFLOW_S3_EXPECTED_BUCKET_OWNER guards against a recreated bucket. Checkpoints the job writes outside MLflow and the backend database (PostgreSQL or MySQL) are encrypted by their own stores. In transit the server speaks plain HTTP and the docs put TLS at a reverse proxy or VPN. Key custody, rotation and revocation are the KMS's.

controls.mechanism: Model version records (run_id, source, logged-model id) plus the run's parameters, tags and input datasets and the MLmodel file (flavors, signature, input_example, mlflow_version, time_created, run_id, with requirements.txt, python_env.yaml and conda.yaml; source_model_name and source_model_revision for transformers and PEFT models), written automatically when the job logs and registers the model

steps.title: Log and register from inside the run
body: Log the candidate with mlflow.<flavor>.log_model(..., registered_model_name="dev.<team>.<model>") in the same run that called log_input, so the version links to the run, its datasets and the MLmodel file.

steps.title: Record the base model for adapters
body: Log PEFT adapters with mlflow.transformers.log_model so MLmodel carries source_model_name and source_model_revision (the Hugging Face repository and commit hash) of the base.

steps.title: Accept versions only from tracked artifacts
body: Set MLFLOW_CREATE_MODEL_VERSION_SOURCE_VALIDATION_REGEX="^mlflow-artifacts:/.*$" on the server so a version cannot be registered from a path outside the tracked artifact store.

steps.title: Walk lineage in both directions
body: From a version read run_id and the run's dataset inputs; from a suspect run set find every version with client.search_model_versions("run_id IN ('<id>', ...)").

steps.title: Keep the backend store central and durable
body: Start the server with --backend-store-uri on a managed PostgreSQL or MySQL database (not the default SQLite mlflow.db) with its own backup and access logging, and restrict run deletion (can_delete needs MANAGE) and who may run mlflow gc.

controls.note: Native on this drawing's rule (versions linked to runs, datasets, signatures and source). Boundary: this is MLflow's own lineage graph, not an exportable AI BOM — no CycloneDX or SPDX output. Everything in it is what the job's client logged and nothing is signed (AML.M0013): the run's user comes from the client (MLFLOW_TRACKING_USERNAME or the OS user), not the authenticated caller. A signature is optional in open source (only Unity Catalog requires one); datasets hang off the run, not the version; the base of a full fine-tune is recorded only if the job logs it (the transformers flavor records it); and a version can be registered from a model saved outside MLflow unless the source regex forbids it. Open source keeps no audit log of user actions, so who promoted or withdrew what comes from an authenticating proxy's access log. Withdrawing a version a lineage query names (alias rollback, delete_model_version) takes effect on each consumer's next resolution only; copies already loaded keep serving until the serving tier reloads them.

controls.mechanism: Registered-model and model-version descriptions (Markdown), tags (validation_status and the like), aliases, the MLmodel signature and input example, and run lineage per version; no approval state enforced on promotion and no model-card generation

steps.title: Describe the model and each version
body: Set descriptions with client.update_registered_model(name, description=...) and client.update_model_version(name, version, description=...), or edit them in the registry UI.

steps.title: Log a signature and input example with every model
body: Pass signature= or input_example= to mlflow.<flavor>.log_model so MLmodel records the input and output schema that travels in the artifact directory.

steps.title: Record approval state as a version tag
body: Set client.set_model_version_tag(name, version, "validation_status", "approved") from the evaluation pipeline — a label the promoter's pipeline must check, not a gate the server enforces.

controls.note: Partial on this drawing's rule (documentation without a gate). The capability's gate — a version without a current card and an approval record is not eligible for promotion — is not in open-source MLflow: set_registered_model_alias accepts any version whatever its tags, description or signature, and a signature is optional (only Unity Catalog requires it). There is no model-card generator. The MLmodel file travels inside the artifact; descriptions, tags and approval labels live in the registry database and do not follow the bytes when they are copied elsewhere. The gate is the promoter pipeline refusing to call set_registered_model_alias without the tag and a current description; a model_version_alias.created webhook can flag a release that skipped it, after the fact.

controls.mechanism: Not applicable — deny-by-default egress from the training job is the compute platform's network policy; the tracking server is one destination on that allowlist

evidence.title: MLflow Tracking Server — proxied versus direct artifact access (what the job must reach)
MLflow Webhooks — URL validation and SSRF protection (the server's own egress)

controls.note: Not applicable: the pin bounds the training job and is absorbed by the compute platform (the drawing's recorded deviation). MLflow's contribution is shaping the allowlist: with proxied artifact access (the default) the job needs only the tracking server's URL, and with --no-serve-artifacts it also needs the bucket. The server's own outbound traffic — webhooks (HTTPS only, private addresses refused unless MLFLOW_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE_IPS=true; redirect bypass fixed in 3.15.0, CVE-2026-64849) and telemetry to mlflow-telemetry.io (MLFLOW_DISABLE_TELEMETRY) — belongs to the egress policy of wherever the server runs.

controls.mechanism: A dedicated MLflow user per training job (basic-auth, MLFLOW_TRACKING_USERNAME and MLFLOW_TRACKING_PASSWORD in the job) whose role grants reach only its experiment and candidate model; or MLFLOW_TRACKING_AUTH=kubernetes sending the pod's service-account token to a proxy or authorization_function that verifies it

steps.title: Create a user for the job identity
body: Create the job's user in /admin → Users or with POST 2.0/mlflow/users/create, and hand its password to the job as MLFLOW_TRACKING_USERNAME / MLFLOW_TRACKING_PASSWORD from the secret store.

steps.title: Keep it away from the release model
body: Assign that user a role holding only (experiment, <id>, EDIT) and EDIT on the candidate registered model, with no grant on the release model the promoter uses.

steps.title: Use the pod's workload identity instead of a password
body: Set MLFLOW_TRACKING_AUTH=kubernetes in the job so each request carries the pod's service-account token, with the server behind kube-rbac-proxy or a custom authorization_function that validates it.

controls.note: Partial on this drawing's rule: MLflow can hold separate users for run logging and promotion and enforces their grants, but its own identity is a username and static password (12-character minimum; no token issuance or expiry documented), shared by every run of the job unless rotated per run. The Kubernetes provider only attaches the service-account token on the client — validating it (kube-rbac-proxy, a custom authorization_function, the mlflow-oidc-auth plugin) happens outside MLflow. Scoping the run to the dataset version an approved spec names is cloud IAM on the corpus store (external): MLflow does not mediate corpus reads. Admin users bypass every grant. Managed variant: SageMaker AI authenticates callers with IAM roles.

controls.mechanism: Not applicable — RL and agentic rollouts execute model output inside the training job's environment, contained by the compute platform; MLflow runs none of it

evidence.title: MLflow documentation index (tracking, registry and evaluation; no rollout execution)
MLflow — Pickle-free models (the loader-side execution risk, rated under other drawings)

controls.note: Not applicable: the pin bounds the training job's rollouts and is absorbed by the compute platform's execution environment (the drawing's recorded deviation). MLflow's own code-execution surfaces — loading pickle-based flavors, building a serving environment from a model's python_env.yaml (CVE-2025-15379) and the server's optional job execution (MLFLOW_SERVER_ENABLE_JOB_EXECUTION, CVE-2026-0545) — sit with the loaders and the server host, recorded in this entry's risk notes and items, not with this pin.

settings.name: --app-name basic-auth
settings.where: mlflow server --app-name basic-auth
settings.default: Off (no authentication; every visitor can read and write everything)
settings.recommended: On
settings.why: Every request to the UI, REST API and proxied artifacts needs a login and passes the per-experiment and per-model checks.

settings.name: authorization_function
settings.where: basic_auth.ini (file named by MLFLOW_AUTH_CONFIG_PATH) → authorization_function = module:function
settings.default: HTTP basic auth against MLflow's own user store
settings.recommended: A function that validates the corporate IdP's token (or the authenticating proxy's identity), so people sign in with SSO
settings.why: People use the firm's SSO and MFA instead of a static MLflow password, and leavers lose access with their IdP account; service jobs keep their own users.

settings.name: default_permission
settings.where: basic_auth.ini → default_permission
settings.recommended: NO_PERMISSIONS
settings.why: An authenticated user reads only the experiments, run artifacts and registered models a role grants, not every candidate model.

settings.name: database_uri
settings.where: basic_auth.ini → database_uri
settings.recommended: The central, backed-up database
settings.why: Users and grants survive a server rebuild and are not reset to an empty store that recreates the admin user.

settings.name: MLFLOW_AUTH_ADMIN_PASSWORD
settings.where: Server environment → MLFLOW_AUTH_ADMIN_PASSWORD (and MLFLOW_AUTH_ADMIN_USERNAME), from the secret store
settings.default: None shipped (earlier releases' password1234 is now refused)
settings.recommended: A generated secret held in the vault; admin rights for a named few
settings.why: Admin users bypass every grant and can create users and change permissions, so the account starts with a secret nobody guesses.

settings.name: MLFLOW_FLASK_SERVER_SECRET_KEY
settings.where: Server environment → MLFLOW_FLASK_SERVER_SECRET_KEY, from the secret store
settings.recommended: A stable random secret, the same on every replica
settings.why: The basic-auth app's CSRF protection rests on it, so a guessable or per-restart key weakens browser sessions.

settings.name: Roles
settings.where: /admin › Roles (or AuthServiceClient create_role, add_role_permission, assign_role)
settings.recommended: Per-experiment and per-model roles — each training job EDIT on its experiment and dev.<team>.<model>, the promoter EDIT on prod.<team>.<model>
settings.why: The training job can never write the release model, and only named people and services read the candidates; no wildcard READ grants.

settings.name: MLFLOW_RBAC_SEED_DEFAULT_ROLES
settings.where: Server environment → MLFLOW_RBAC_SEED_DEFAULT_ROLES (with --enable-workspaces)
settings.default: On (each new workspace gets admin and user roles; user is USE on every resource)
settings.recommended: Off
settings.why: A workspace member does not automatically read and use every model in the workspace; the docs say no lesser per-resource grant can take that back.

settings.name: MLFLOW_TRACKING_USERNAME / MLFLOW_TRACKING_PASSWORD
settings.where: Training-job environment, injected from the secret store
settings.recommended: One MLflow user per training job, never a person's or the admin's login
settings.why: What each job logged and registered is attributable, and its grants reach only its own experiment and candidate model.

settings.name: MLFLOW_TRACKING_AUTH
settings.where: Training-job environment → MLFLOW_TRACKING_AUTH=kubernetes, server behind kube-rbac-proxy or a custom auth plugin
settings.recommended: kubernetes for jobs running in the cluster
settings.why: Each request carries the pod's service-account token instead of a static password; MLflow only attaches it, so the proxy must validate it.

settings.name: --host
settings.where: mlflow server --host
settings.recommended: 0.0.0.0 only with --allowed-hosts and --cors-allowed-origins set, behind a TLS-terminating proxy
settings.why: The server speaks plain HTTP and has no TLS of its own, so it is reached only through the proxy that encrypts and logs access.

settings.name: --allowed-hosts / MLFLOW_SERVER_ALLOWED_HOSTS
settings.where: mlflow server --allowed-hosts, or MLFLOW_SERVER_ALLOWED_HOSTS
settings.recommended: The server's own hostnames only
settings.why: DNS-rebinding pages in a user's browser cannot reach the API under another name; never "*".

settings.name: --cors-allowed-origins / MLFLOW_SERVER_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS
settings.where: mlflow server --cors-allowed-origins, or MLFLOW_SERVER_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS
settings.recommended: The exact origins of the firm's notebook and tooling front ends
settings.why: Other web apps a user visits cannot call the registry with the user's session.

settings.name: --disable-security-middleware
settings.where: mlflow server --disable-security-middleware, or MLFLOW_SERVER_DISABLE_SECURITY_MIDDLEWARE
settings.recommended: false — and serve with uvicorn, not --gunicorn-opts or --waitress-opts
settings.why: Host, CORS and X-Frame-Options protection stay on; the middleware does not run under the other server options at all.

settings.name: --artifacts-destination (proxied artifact access)
settings.where: mlflow server --artifacts-destination <bucket> (default --serve-artifacts; no --default-artifact-root, no --no-serve-artifacts)
settings.default: Proxied, to ./mlartifacts on the server's disk
settings.recommended: Proxied, to the organisation's bucket, with the storage credential held only by the server
settings.why: Every artifact read and write passes the server's grant check and jobs never hold bucket credentials; the docs warn the server's credential reaches every artifact, so lock down the bucket itself.

settings.name: MLFLOW_CREATE_MODEL_VERSION_SOURCE_VALIDATION_REGEX
settings.where: Tracking-server environment → MLFLOW_CREATE_MODEL_VERSION_SOURCE_VALIDATION_REGEX
settings.recommended: "^mlflow-artifacts:/.*$" (or the scanner's cleared prefix)
settings.why: A model version cannot be registered from a path outside the tracked, proxied store, so every version links to a run's logged artifacts.

settings.name: --backend-store-uri
settings.where: mlflow server --backend-store-uri
settings.recommended: A managed PostgreSQL or MySQL database with backups and access logging
settings.why: Run, dataset and version lineage lives in this database, so it must outlast the server and record who touched it.

settings.name: MLFLOW_S3_UPLOAD_EXTRA_ARGS
settings.where: Server environment (and any client uploading directly) → MLFLOW_S3_UPLOAD_EXTRA_ARGS
settings.recommended: {"ServerSideEncryption": "aws:kms", "SSEKMSKeyId": "<organisation key>"}, backed by bucket default encryption
settings.why: Model and dataset artifacts are encrypted under a key the organisation holds and can revoke; the bucket policy enforces it for writers that skip the variable.

settings.name: MLFLOW_S3_EXPECTED_BUCKET_OWNER
settings.where: Server environment → MLFLOW_S3_EXPECTED_BUCKET_OWNER
settings.recommended: The AWS account id that owns the artifact bucket
settings.why: If the bucket is deleted and recreated by another account, MLflow refuses to write models into it.

settings.name: MLFLOW_ALLOW_PICKLE_DESERIALIZATION
settings.where: Environment of every process that loads registered models → MLFLOW_ALLOW_PICKLE_DESERIALIZATION
settings.recommended: false
settings.why: Loading a pickle or cloudpickle model raises an error instead of running whatever code the file carries.

settings.name: serialization_format="skops"
settings.where: mlflow.sklearn.log_model(..., serialization_format="skops") in the training job
settings.recommended: "skops" for scikit-learn models, and the pickle-free option for each other flavor
settings.why: Models are saved in a format that loads without arbitrary code execution, so the loader switch above can stay off.

settings.name: mlflow.log_input
settings.where: Training job → mlflow.log_input(dataset, context="training" | "validation" | "evaluation")
settings.recommended: Every input dataset logged on the run, with source set to an immutable version
settings.why: Each model version can be traced to the dataset versions, digests and schemas that trained and evaluated it.

settings.name: signature
settings.where: mlflow.<flavor>.log_model(..., signature=..., input_example=...)
settings.default: Optional (inferred from an input example or type hints when one is given)
settings.recommended: Logged with every model
settings.why: The version records its input and output schema in MLmodel, which travels with the artifact.

settings.name: mlflow.validate_evaluation_results
settings.where: Promotion pipeline → mlflow.validate_evaluation_results(candidate_result=..., baseline_result=..., validation_thresholds=...)
settings.default: Not called (the registry accepts any version)
settings.recommended: Called on every candidate, with promotion run only when no ModelValidationFailedException is raised
settings.why: A candidate that fails its thresholds is never aliased for release; the server itself would not block it.

settings.name: validation_status (model version tag)
settings.where: client.set_model_version_tag(name, version, "validation_status", "approved") from the evaluation pipeline
settings.recommended: Set by the evaluation pipeline only, and checked by the promoter before it moves an alias
settings.why: Each release version carries its approval state; it is a label the promoter must enforce, not a server gate.

settings.name: set_registered_model_alias
settings.where: client.set_registered_model_alias(name, "champion", version), run by the promoter user only
settings.default: Anyone with EDIT on the registered model
settings.recommended: Called only by the promoter pipeline, after the validation_status tag and a current description are present
settings.why: Consumers loading models:/<name>@champion get a version that passed the gate; the alias moves are the release record.

settings.name: model_version_alias.created
settings.where: Webhook on model_version_alias.created (and model_version.created), HTTPS endpoint with an HMAC secret
settings.recommended: Subscribed by the release-monitoring service, which flags any alias move the promoter did not make
settings.why: The organisation sees every release and new candidate as it happens; open-source MLflow keeps no audit log of its own.

settings.name: MLFLOW_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE_IPS
settings.where: Server environment → MLFLOW_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE_IPS
settings.recommended: false
settings.why: A webhook URL cannot point the server at internal addresses; the docs say not to enable it in production.

settings.name: MLFLOW_DISABLE_TELEMETRY
settings.where: Server and client environment → MLFLOW_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=true (or DO_NOT_TRACK=true)
settings.recommended: true
settings.why: Usage events about the registry and its clients stay inside the organisation; on the server it also turns UI telemetry off globally.
