tools.name: OpenAI Agents SDK

variants.name: openai-agents (Python)
@openai/agents (TypeScript: agents-core, agents-openai, agents-extensions)

summary: An open-source library (Python and TypeScript, MIT) that runs the agent loop inside the customer's own process: agents with instructions, typed function tools, handoffs and agents-as-tools, input, output and tool guardrails, tool approvals that pause a run as serialisable RunState, sessions for conversation history, MCP servers (local or hosted), and sandbox agents that run shell and file tools in Unix-local, Docker or hosted-provider sandboxes. Inference goes to the OpenAI Responses API by default (or Chat Completions and other providers through adapters) with the key or client the application supplies.

Every control is a parameter or a function the deployer writes: max_turns (default 10), needs_approval and require_approval, guardrail functions, is_enabled and MCP tool filters, trace processors. Tracing is on by default and ships each run to OpenAI's Traces dashboard with model inputs, outputs and tool arguments included unless trace_include_sensitive_data is turned off or the processors are replaced; tracing is unavailable to Zero Data Retention organisations. Nothing is hosted by the SDK itself: storage, identity, egress and isolation are the application's.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Free, MIT-licensed packages (pip install openai-agents, npm install @openai/agents); model calls, hosted tools and containers bill to the OpenAI API organisation at API rates.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: OpenAI Responses API by default with OPENAI_API_KEY (or set_default_openai_key / set_default_openai_client, OPENAI_BASE_URL); set_default_openai_api switches to Chat Completions; other providers through a ModelProvider, a Model instance per agent, or the Any-LLM / LiteLLM adapters.

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: Instructions, history and tool results to the model provider; traces to OpenAI's backend by default (generation inputs and outputs and function-call inputs and outputs unless trace_include_sensitive_data is False); session history wherever the chosen session store lives (OpenAIConversationsSession keeps it in OpenAI's Conversations API); hosted tools and hosted containers run at OpenAI.

facts.label: Retention & training
facts.value: API data is not used for training by default; /v1/responses keeps abuse-monitoring logs up to 30 days and is ZDR-eligible; /v1/conversations (OpenAIConversationsSession) keeps items until deleted and is not ZDR-eligible; tracing is unavailable to ZDR organisations and trace retention is not documented on the tracing pages.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: openai.github.io/openai-agents-python and openai.github.io/openai-agents-js, with platform guides at developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents

facts.label: Security policy
facts.value: Reports go through OpenAI's Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure Policy; SECURITY.md states that tool implementations run with the host application's privileges and that the application must authorise them and isolate untrusted execution.

items.title: Keep traces in your own store
body: Tracing starts on and exports to OpenAI. Install your collector's processor with set_trace_processors (which replaces the OpenAI exporter) before the first run, and set trace_include_sensitive_data to False unless that store is approved for prompts and tool arguments.

items.title: Choose a sandbox client that isolates
body: UnixLocalSandboxClient adds no OS-level confinement on Linux and no network isolation on macOS; use Docker with network_mode "none", a hosted sandbox client, or external isolation for commands influenced by untrusted input.

riskNotes.note: Input guardrails run only on the first agent and by default in parallel with it, so the model can already have called tools when a tripwire fires; results of hosted tools (web search, file search, hosted MCP) reach the model inside the Responses call with no SDK hook.
Approval is opt-in per tool: function tools run unapproved unless needs_approval is set, and local ShellTool and ApplyPatchTool default to needs_approval=False on a host the SDK does not sandbox.
Tracing defaults to on, to OpenAI, with model and tool payloads included; serialised RunState carries the application context and approval state, so secrets placed in context travel with it.
max_turns defaults to 10 model calls per run and max_turns=None removes it; usage is counted on the run context but no token or cost ceiling stops a run.
Each run calls list_tools() on every MCP server, so a server can add or redefine tools between runs unless a static tool_filter narrows the list; cache_tools_list is a latency cache, not a pin.

controls.mechanism: The run context (Runner.run(..., context=...)) carrying the caller's grant to every tool, FunctionTool.is_enabled, Handoff.is_enabled, MCP tool_filter, needs_approval callables and guardrails; who may start, resume or cancel a run is the application's endpoint

steps.title: Bind the grant at ingress
body: Pass the principal the run acts for and its grant (a service principal's scope or the on-behalf-of token from the message) as the context object to Runner.run(..., context=...); tools, hooks and guardrails read it from RunContextWrapper.context.

steps.title: Gate capabilities on the grant
body: Return False from FunctionTool.is_enabled, Handoff.is_enabled or a callable MCP tool_filter when the context's grant does not cover the capability; the runner re-evaluates is_enabled before invoking a local function tool.

steps.title: Rebuild the context on resume
body: Resume a parked run with the authenticated caller's context, not the serialised one — in TypeScript RunState.fromStringWithContext(agent, state, context, { contextStrategy: 'replace' }).

controls.note: Partial on this drawing's rule for D3-APA (a run context carrying the caller's grant is an attach point). The SDK carries the grant to every callback but decides nothing with it: it has no listener, is_enabled "controls visibility and dispatch; it does not replace authorization that depends on the tool arguments or the resource", and the grant is whatever the application places in context. Who may start, resume or cancel a run — including whether the event that resumes a parked proposal carries an authorised approver — is the application's endpoint behind its IdP or API gateway. Serialised RunState includes the context and approval state (TypeScript's default contextStrategy 'merge' merges the serialised approvals), so where it is stored is part of the trust boundary.

controls.mechanism: Agent.tools, handoffs and mcp_servers declared per agent in application code; a call to an unlisted function tool raises ModelBehaviorError by default (tool_not_found_behavior); MCP tool lists fetched from each server on every run and narrowed by create_static_tool_filter

steps.title: Declare each agent's catalogue in reviewed code
body: Give every Agent an explicit tools and handoffs list and keep RunConfig.tool_not_found_behavior at its default, so a model-named tool that is not on the current agent raises ModelBehaviorError.

steps.title: Fix each MCP server's tool list
body: Set tool_filter=create_static_tool_filter(allowed_tool_names=[...]) (TypeScript createMCPToolStaticFilter) on every MCP server so tools a server adds later are not exposed.

steps.title: Label runs for reconciliation
body: Set RunConfig workflow_name, group_id and trace_metadata (owner, release) on each run so traces can be reconciled against the organisation's registry.

controls.note: Partial by this drawing's rule (tools declared per agent in code; admission is code review). There is no registry with owner, version or approval state and nothing consults one before a tool is offered; the catalogue is whatever the process constructs. MCP tool definitions arrive from the server on each run, so a server adds tools unless a static filter narrows them, and HostedMCPTool servers list their tools inside the Responses API. set_default_openai_harness only adds an agent_harness_id to trace metadata — a label, not an admission check. Change gating is the organisation's pipeline.

controls.mechanism: None in the SDK; an evaluation platform in CI runs the agent against a protected test set before a model, instruction or tool change ships

evidence.title: Testing — deterministic, provider-neutral utilities; model behaviour needs real providers (2026-09-25)
Evaluate agent workflows — trace grading and eval runs on the OpenAI Platform (2026-09-25)
Evals platform deprecation — read-only 2026-10-31, shutdown 2026-11-30 (2026-09-25)

controls.note: External (evaluation or red-team platform in CI), as for the Claude Agent SDK and Codex SDK: the SDK's testing utilities (ScriptedModel, provider-neutral fakes) make no model requests and test the orchestration the application owns — the page says to use real providers for behaviour owned by the model — so they cannot validate a model or prompt change. OpenAI's trace grading and Evals run on the platform and gate nothing; the Evals platform becomes read-only on 2026-10-31 and shuts down on 2026-11-30. Integration point: run the agent headless in CI against the evaluation platform's suite with a pinned model and output_type, and gate the release on its result.

controls.mechanism: @function_tool / tool() schemas generated from Pydantic or Zod types with strict_mode True by default, arguments validated (Field constraints included) before the function runs; per-agent tools lists and is_enabled; create_static_tool_filter on MCP servers

steps.title: Type and constrain every action
body: Declare each action with @function_tool (TypeScript tool({ parameters: z.object(...) })) using constrained types such as Field(ge=, le=, pattern=) and leave strict_mode True; arguments that fail validation never reach the function.

steps.title: Give each agent only its own actions
body: Set Agent.tools per agent and use is_enabled for request-scoped exposure; a specialist reached by handoff runs with its own tools, not the triage agent's.

steps.title: Allowlist tools from MCP servers
body: Set tool_filter=create_static_tool_filter(allowed_tool_names=[...]) on each MCP server; the allow-list is applied first and blocked_tool_names removes from what remains.

steps.title: Validate in hand-built tools
body: In a hand-built FunctionTool, validate the raw JSON string on_invoke_tool receives (for example model_validate_json) before acting on it.

controls.note: Native on this drawing's rule for AML.M0028 (typed schemas strictly validated by the SDK before execution, plus per-agent tool lists): the decorator path builds a strict JSON schema and re-validates the parsed arguments with Pydantic, so a malformed or out-of-range call is refused outside the model. Outside that boundary: hand-built FunctionTool receives raw JSON; MCP tool schemas are converted to strict best-effort and validated by the server; hosted tools and local shell, apply-patch and computer tools take free-form arguments; is_enabled governs visibility, not authorisation. Every tool runs with the process's authority unless the tool reads the caller's grant from context, and a declared blast radius or compensating transaction is the tool author's, not an SDK concept. The multi-agent drawing's SDK rows are partial on that drawing's per-hop rule, which this drawing does not apply.

controls.mechanism: needs_approval (True or an async callable over context, parsed arguments and call ID) on function tools, Agent.as_tool, ShellTool and ApplyPatchTool; require_approval on local and hosted MCP servers; the run pauses with RunResult.interruptions (ToolApprovalItem with agent.name, tool_name, arguments) and resumes after state.approve or state.reject for that call ID

steps.title: Key approval to consequence
body: Set needs_approval on each consequential tool to an async callable that returns True above the irreversibility or value threshold (TypeScript needsApproval), or True to always ask.

steps.title: Park the run and resume on a decision
body: Store result.to_state() with state.to_json() (TypeScript result.state.toString()), show the approver each interruption's agent, tool_name and arguments, and resume with Runner.run(agent, state) only after state.approve or state.reject.

steps.title: Gate MCP and shell actions too
body: Set require_approval on MCPServerStdio, MCPServerSse and MCPServerStreamableHttp, tool_config require_approval "always" on HostedMCPTool, and needs_approval=True on local ShellTool and ApplyPatchTool (default False).

steps.title: Keep decisions per call
body: Do not pass always_approve=True for consequential tools; it approves every later call to that tool for the rest of the run and survives serialisation.

controls.note: Native on the same rule as the Claude Agent SDK's canUseTool: a built-in primitive holds the exact call (per call ID, with its arguments) until the application records a decision, callable rules fail closed on malformed arguments, and nested, handed-off and agent-as-tool approvals surface on the outer run. The deployer supplies the approver, the UI, authentication, expiry and the rule that the requester never approves — the SDK records no approver identity. Boundaries: approval is opt-in per tool; hosted tools, hosted-container shell (which must not set needs_approval) and handoffs have none; on_approval and on_approval_request callbacks decide in code and are not human approval; always_approve is sticky for the run; the serialised RunState carries the approval state, so its storage must be tamper-protected.

controls.mechanism: Tool input guardrails (@tool_input_guardrail with ToolContext tool_name, tool_call_id, tool_arguments) returning reject_content or raising a tripwire, per function tool or server-wide on local MCP servers; needs_approval callables as the escalate path; no declarative policy language

steps.title: Decide every function-tool call in a guardrail
body: Attach tool_input_guardrails to each function tool (TypeScript inputGuardrails on tool()) that checks the context's principal, the tool and its arguments and returns ToolGuardrailFunctionOutput.reject_content(...) or raises a tripwire.

steps.title: Apply it to MCP tools
body: Pass tool_input_guardrails on MCPServerStdio, MCPServerSse or MCPServerStreamableHttp so the SDK attaches it to every tool the server exposes after filtering.

steps.title: Decide before the approval prompt
body: Set RunConfig.tool_execution=ToolExecutionConfig(pre_approval_tool_input_guardrails=True) so the policy runs before an approval interruption and again after approval.

controls.note: Partial by this drawing's rule (tool guardrail functions the deployer writes). The guardrail runs outside the model, per call, before the function executes, and deny, allow and escalate (via needs_approval) are all expressible — but the rules are the deployer's code and the decision is recorded only as a guardrail span. Not covered: handoffs, Agent.as_tool, hosted tools (WebSearchTool, FileSearchTool, HostedMCPTool, CodeInterpreterTool, ImageGenerationTool) and built-in execution tools (ComputerTool, ShellTool, ApplyPatchTool, LocalShellTool), which bypass the guardrail pipeline. A hosted MCP server can be pointed at an MCP gateway that decides per call. The intersection of requester grant and agent identity is the application's to compute: an MCP server receives whatever token the application put in its headers, function tools run with the process's credentials, and the app context is shared by every agent in a run, nested Agent.as_tool runs included.

controls.mechanism: No agent identity in the SDK; the process authenticates to OpenAI with OPENAI_API_KEY, set_default_openai_key or a client from set_default_openai_client, or per agent with a Model instance on its own AsyncOpenAI client; a project service account through workload identity federation is the revocable workload identity

steps.title: Federate a workload identity per agent workload
body: In Organization Settings > Security > Workload Identity Provider map each agent workload's OIDC, SPIFFE or X.509 identity to its own project service account with only the permissions it needs.

steps.title: Give an agent its own model client
body: Pass the agent a Model instance on its own client (the models guide shows OpenAIChatCompletionsModel(model=..., openai_client=AsyncOpenAI())) instead of the process default.

steps.title: Give an agent its own tool credential
body: Construct that agent's MCP servers with headers carrying a token minted for the agent, and list them only in its mcp_servers.

controls.note: Partial by this drawing's rule (the SDK neither mints nor authenticates agent identities). Agent.name labels spans and approvals but is not a principal; handed-off and nested agents run in the same process and environment, and nested Agent.as_tool runs share the app context by default. Per-agent model clients and MCP credentials are configurable, but minting, rotating and revoking them is the application's; the federated identity is per workload and revocable in the platform (disable the service account or its mapping).

controls.mechanism: The requester's token carried in the run context to function tools, per MCP server in headers, per call in _meta through tool_meta_resolver, and per HostedMCPTool connector in authorization; no OAuth flow, on-behalf-of exchange or built-in identity passthrough

steps.title: Carry the requester's token to each data tool
body: Put the account-scoped access token from your own OAuth or on-behalf-of flow in the run context and use it inside each function tool's data call.

steps.title: Scope each MCP call to the account
body: Construct the MCP server per request with the requester's token in headers, and set tool_meta_resolver to put the account or tenant ID into each call's _meta.

steps.title: Pass the user's grant to hosted connectors
body: For a HostedMCPTool connector, set tool_config authorization to the requesting user's access token for that run.

controls.note: Partial on the same rule as the Claude Agent SDK's per-query MCP headers (a per-call context attach point): retrieval runs with the requester's entitlements only when the application obtains and passes that token, and the docs say MCP servers must authorise their own protected operations. The SDK runs no OAuth flow or token exchange; FileSearchTool reads OpenAI vector stores with the project key, sandbox mounts read with the mount's credentials, and function tools use whatever the application gives them. Oversharing analysis of the sources is outside the SDK.

controls.mechanism: @input_guardrail on the starting agent (run_in_parallel=False to block before the model), tool_output_guardrails on function tools and local MCP servers, and RunConfig.call_model_input_filter, as attach points for the deployer's classifier; none ships

steps.title: Classify the payload before the loop
body: Attach an input guardrail that runs your injection classifier to the starting agent with run_in_parallel=False (TypeScript runInParallel: false), so a tripwire stops the run before any model call or tool.

steps.title: Screen returned content before it re-enters context
body: Attach tool_output_guardrails to each data-returning function tool, and server-wide on local MCP servers, returning reject_content to replace a flagged result before the model sees it.

steps.title: Filter the assembled input
body: Set RunConfig.call_model_input_filter to inspect and strip the prepared input, session history included, immediately before each model call.

controls.note: Partial by this drawing's rule: the guardrails are attach points and no injection classifier ships. Returned content can be screened before it re-enters context for function tools and local MCP tools only; hosted tools' results (web search, file search, hosted MCP, code interpreter) are read by the model inside the Responses call, and shell, apply-patch and computer outputs bypass the pipeline. Input guardrails run only for the first agent and by default in parallel, so the model may already have spent tokens and run tools when one trips; handoff inputs are not screened.

controls.mechanism: Session stores keyed by a session_id the application chooses (SQLiteSession, RedisSession, SQLAlchemySession, MongoDBSession, DaprSession, OpenAIConversationsSession) with clear_session(); EncryptedSession with per-session derived keys and ttl; sandbox Memory() separated by MemoryLayoutConfig

steps.title: Key each session to one case
body: Construct the session with the case ID (for example SQLAlchemySession(case_id, engine=...)), never reuse it for another case, and call clear_session() when the case closes.

steps.title: Encrypt and expire case history
body: Wrap the store in EncryptedSession(session_id, underlying_session, encryption_key, ttl=...) with the master key from your secret manager; items past ttl are skipped on read.

steps.title: Separate sandbox memory by case or tenant
body: Give Memory() a MemoryLayoutConfig per case or tenant (memories_dir, sessions_dir), and use Memory(generate=None) for agents that must not write memory.

controls.note: Partial by this drawing's rule (session objects the deployer scopes): the boundary is the session_id and layout the application picks — a run reads whatever session it is handed, and TypeScript tenant routing is a RunContextAwareSession the deployer writes. Nothing validates what a turn writes: tool results persist in history, and sandbox memory consolidates lessons across every conversation sharing a layout, with live updates to MEMORY.md on by default. ttl skips expired items rather than deleting them; deletion is clear_session() or the store's own TTL (Dapr).

controls.mechanism: OPENAI_API_KEY by default, or set_default_openai_key / set_default_openai_client; a short-lived access token from workload identity federation passed to the client; set_tracing_export_api_key for a separate tracing key; UnixLocalSandboxClient inherit_host_environment=False; credentials scoped per MCP server (headers), per HostedMCPTool (authorization) and per hosted-shell domain (network_policy.domain_secrets)

steps.title: Replace the standing key with federation
body: Map the workload to a project service account under Organization Settings > Security > Workload Identity Provider and exchange its identity token for a short-lived access token, renewing before expires_at.

steps.title: Hand the brokered credential to the SDK
body: Build an AsyncOpenAI client with that token and install it with set_default_openai_client(client, use_for_tracing=False), then set_tracing_export_api_key for the tracing credential.

steps.title: Keep host secrets out of sandbox commands
body: Create UnixLocalSandboxClient(inherit_host_environment=False) with a host_environment_allowlist, so commands do not inherit the process's keys.

steps.title: Scope each tool credential to one server
body: Put each tool credential in that MCP server's headers (an Authorization header, never the URL) rather than the process environment.

steps.title: Bind sandbox secrets to their domain
body: In a hosted-shell allowlist use network_policy.domain_secrets so a secret is injected only for its domain.

controls.note: Partial by this drawing's rule: the SDK takes whatever key or client the application gives it — by default a standing OPENAI_API_KEY from the environment — and brokers nothing per workload or per step. Federation gives an expiring token with no refresh token, so renewal is the application's code, and whether the default tracing exporter accepts a federated token is not documented (it needs an API key of its own when the model client is not used for tracing). The docs warn that RunContextWrapper.context travels with serialised RunState; TypeScript omits the tracing key from serialised state by default.

controls.mechanism: max_turns (default 10; None disables) raising MaxTurnsExceeded; function-tool timeout and max_function_tool_concurrency; ModelSettings.timeout per model call; usage counted on RunContextWrapper.usage with no budget that stops the run

steps.title: Cap turns on every run
body: Pass max_turns to Runner.run (TypeScript maxTurns) and never None; the run ends with MaxTurnsExceeded or the error_handlers "max_turns" output.

steps.title: Bound tool fan-out and time
body: Set RunConfig.tool_execution=ToolExecutionConfig(max_function_tool_concurrency=N) and @function_tool(timeout=...) on slow tools.

steps.title: Enforce a token budget in a hook
body: In RunHooks.on_llm_end read context.usage and stop the run (raise, or cancel a streamed run) when it passes the run's allowance.

controls.note: Partial by this drawing's rule (max_turns only; no token or cost budget ships). The turn limit counts model calls per run and is on by default; usage (requests, tokens) is tracked but only a hook the deployer writes can act on it, hosted tool and container charges are not in it, and no wall-clock deadline covers the whole run (ModelSettings.timeout bounds one model call; TypeScript can pass AbortSignal.timeout as signal). Quotas and cost ceilings "on the crossing" belong to the AI gateway or the project's budget.

controls.mechanism: Hosted-container ShellTool environment network_policy (disabled or allowlist with allowed_domains, within the org allow list); DockerSandboxClientOptions network_mode "none"; no network control for UnixLocalSandboxClient, function tools or local MCP servers

steps.title: Allowlist the hosted shell
body: Configure ShellTool(environment={"type": "container_auto", "network_policy": {"type": "allowlist", "allowed_domains": [...]}}) with only the package mirror and the hosts the task needs; hosted containers have no outbound access by default.

steps.title: Cut networking in Docker sandboxes
body: Set DockerSandboxClientOptions(network_mode="none") (TypeScript networkMode: 'none'), the only explicit mode supported.

steps.title: Bound the host at the network
body: Run the application, its function tools, local MCP servers and any Unix-local sandbox in a subnet or namespace whose egress proxy allows only the AI gateway and the package mirror.

controls.note: Partial on the same finding as the Claude Agent SDK: a domain allowlist exists only for the OpenAI-hosted container shell, enforced by OpenAI within the org allow list set in the dashboard. Docker sandboxes are on or off, Unix-local adds no network isolation, and the hosted sandbox provider clients document no allowlist. In-process function tools (the local tools this pin sits on), local MCP servers and local ShellTool leave through the host network, which is the deployer's to restrict.

controls.mechanism: Built-in tracing, on by default: a trace per run with agent, generation (model input and output), function (tool arguments and results), guardrail and handoff spans, correlated by trace_id and group_id; add_trace_processor / set_trace_processors route spans to the customer's store; trace_include_sensitive_data controls payload capture

steps.title: Send traces to your own store
body: Call set_trace_processors([...]) (TypeScript setTraceProcessors) with your collector's processor — a listed integration or your own exporter — before the first run; add_trace_processor keeps the OpenAI exporter as well.

steps.title: Decide what payload is captured
body: Set trace_include_sensitive_data (OPENAI_AGENTS_TRACE_INCLUDE_SENSITIVE_DATA), True by default, to False where the store is not approved for prompts and tool arguments, or redact inside your own exporter.

steps.title: Correlate runs to the case and principal
body: Set RunConfig group_id to the case ID and trace_metadata to the principal and agent release on each run.

steps.title: Flush before workers exit
body: Call flush_traces() after each job's trace closes so batched spans are exported before a worker is recycled.

controls.note: Native on the rule applied to the Claude Agent SDK: every model call, function-tool call with arguments and results, guardrail and handoff is a span, the whole run is one trace, and a processor sends it to the customer's store. Defaults: on in server runtimes (TypeScript turns it off in browsers and under NODE_ENV=test), exported to OpenAI's Traces dashboard with payloads included, and unavailable to ZDR organisations. No first-party OTLP exporter is documented — export elsewhere uses a third-party processor or the deployer's own. Limits: hosted-tool work appears only inside generation output, session and memory reads and writes are not spans, identity is whatever metadata the application adds, and a processor is an in-process observer, so append-only retention is the collector's.

controls.mechanism: RunResultStreaming.cancel() (immediately or mode "after_turn"); TypeScript signal: AbortSignal on run(); revoking the API key or disabling the workload identity mapping; clear_session() and sandbox session teardown by the application

steps.title: Cancel the running run
body: Call result.cancel() on a streamed run (TypeScript: abort the AbortSignal passed as signal) and keep consuming stream_events() until it finishes.

steps.title: Revoke what it authenticates with
body: Disable the service account's workload identity mapping or revoke the project key the process uses so later model calls fail.

steps.title: Discard what it stored
body: Discard any parked RunState, call clear_session() on its session, and close its sandbox session.

controls.note: Partial by this drawing's rule (in-process cancellation only): the stop is a call by the process that holds the result handle; no runtime or remote cancel exists, and the Python docs document cancel() for streamed runs only. Whether an in-flight function tool, local shell command, MCP call or hosted container stops is not documented. A parked RunState can be resumed by whoever holds it, so quarantine means discarding it. Revoking the key or mapping refuses later model requests only (delay not documented); quarantine from peers and secure deletion are the deployer's steps.

evidence.title: Tools — FileSearchTool retrieves from OpenAI Vector Stores as a hosted tool (2026-09-25)
Agents SDK documentation index, reviewed for applicability (2026-09-25)

controls.note: Not applicable: the SDK has no retrieval corpus or index of its own. FileSearchTool queries OpenAI Vector Stores inside the Responses API, and anything else is a store the application attaches through a function tool or MCP server; ingest trust, per-tenant index isolation and grounding checks belong to that store or the OpenAI API's vector stores. Sandbox memory is covered on AML.M0031.

controls.mechanism: MCP servers declared in code per agent; create_static_tool_filter allowlist or a callable tool_filter that sees each tool definition; require_approval; list_tools() on every run unless cache_tools_list (a latency cache cleared by invalidate_tools_cache()); no hashing or pinning of definitions

steps.title: Admit only named tools
body: Set tool_filter=create_static_tool_filter(allowed_tool_names=[...]) on every MCP server.

steps.title: Refuse redefined tools in a callable filter
body: Pass a callable tool_filter that hashes the name, description and input schema of the tool object it receives and returns False when they differ from the approved value; leave cache_tools_list off.

steps.title: Require approval on write tools
body: Set require_approval with a per-tool map on local servers and "always" on HostedMCPTool for tools that change records.

controls.note: Partial by core rule 1: declared servers and a tool allowlist admit tools by name but verify nothing a server serves, and the docs describe no hashing, pinning or re-approval when a definition changes. A callable tool_filter is the attach point where the deployer can pin definition hashes; it runs for local servers only — HostedMCPTool definitions are listed inside the Responses API. Stdio server versions are whatever command the application starts.

controls.mechanism: None in the SDK; admission scanning at the package mirror or artifact repository the sandbox image and the hosted-shell allowlist point at

evidence.title: Sandbox clients — image choice, Unix-local host execution, hosted providers (2026-09-25)
Tools — hosted shell skills and network_policy allowlist (2026-09-25)

controls.note: External (package firewall or artifact-repository scanning at the mirror): the SDK scans nothing it loads or its agents install — skills load from local directories or skill references, stdio MCP servers start from the command the application gives, and packages a sandbox shell installs come from whatever registry the network allows. Integration points: point the sandbox image's package managers at the scanning mirror and allow only its host in the hosted-shell allowlist and the egress proxy; pin the SDK in the lockfile. No model weights load in the SDK.

controls.mechanism: Sandbox agents run their shell and file tools through the sandbox client the application picks: UnixLocalSandboxClient (no OS-level confinement on Linux; sandbox-exec filesystem restrictions without network isolation on macOS), DockerSandboxClient (a container, network_mode "none") or a hosted provider client (Blaxel, Cloudflare, Daytona, E2B, Modal, Vercel); hosted shell (container_auto) in an OpenAI-provisioned container; function tools, local MCP servers and local ShellTool run in the application's own process

steps.title: Run sandbox agents in Docker or a hosted provider
body: Pass DockerSandboxClient (or a hosted provider client) in SandboxRunConfig for any agent whose commands follow untrusted input; keep UnixLocalSandboxClient for trusted local development.

steps.title: Withhold the host environment from Unix-local
body: Where Unix-local runs inside external isolation, set inherit_host_environment=False so commands get only the default variable allowlist, not the application's keys.

steps.title: Keep one-off commands off the host
body: Use ShellTool(environment={"type": "container_auto"}) so commands run in an OpenAI-provisioned container; a local ShellTool runs on the host, so set needs_approval=True on it.

controls.note: Partial on the core sandbox rule (as on toolClaudeAgentSdk and toolCodexSdk): the SDK offers isolation backends, but nothing is isolated unless the deployer picks one, and the local client is not a boundary (on Linux, commands reach whatever the host process can). Inside a Docker or hosted sandbox: the sandbox agent's shell and file tools. Outside: the agent loop, every function tool, local MCP servers and local ShellTool / ApplyPatchTool, which run with the application's privileges and are the deployer's to isolate. A Docker sandbox's boundary is its image, mounts and network; a hosted provider's is that provider's to document.

settings.name: Workload Identity Provider and service account mapping
settings.where: OpenAI Platform › Organization Settings › Security › Workload Identity Provider, then the client built with set_default_openai_client(...)
settings.recommended: One mapping per agent workload to its own project service account, the short-lived token passed through set_default_openai_client
settings.why: No long-lived API key sits in the deployment, each agent workload is a separate revocable principal, and removing the mapping stops its model calls.

settings.name: context with is_enabled
settings.where: Runner.run(agent, input, context=...); FunctionTool / Handoff is_enabled callables reading RunContextWrapper.context
settings.default: No context; every declared tool enabled
settings.recommended: The authenticated caller and its grant as the run context, with is_enabled returning False for tools that grant does not cover
settings.why: The model is never offered a tool, handoff or data source the requesting principal is not entitled to, and each data tool calls with that principal's token.

settings.name: set_trace_processors
settings.where: set_trace_processors([...]) at application start-up (TypeScript setTraceProcessors)
settings.default: Default processor exporting every trace to OpenAI's Traces dashboard
settings.recommended: Your own exporter to the firm's collector, installed before the first run
settings.why: Traces with prompts and tool arguments go to your store under your retention; add_trace_processor would keep the OpenAI exporter as well.

settings.name: trace_include_sensitive_data
settings.where: RunConfig.trace_include_sensitive_data, or OPENAI_AGENTS_TRACE_INCLUDE_SENSITIVE_DATA
settings.recommended: False, unless the trace store is approved for prompts and tool arguments
settings.why: Generation and function spans keep their structure without model inputs, outputs or tool payloads, so client material stays out of trace storage.

settings.name: OPENAI_AGENTS_DISABLE_TRACING / set_tracing_disabled / RunConfig.tracing_disabled
settings.where: Environment variable, set_tracing_disabled(True) at start-up, or RunConfig per run
settings.recommended: Leave tracing on, exported to your own processor
settings.why: Disabling it loses the per-run record of model calls, tools, guardrails and handoffs; the docs state tracing is unavailable to organisations under Zero Data Retention.

settings.name: OPENAI_AGENTS_DONT_LOG_MODEL_DATA / OPENAI_AGENTS_DONT_LOG_TOOL_DATA
settings.where: Environment variables of the application process
settings.recommended: 1 — don't set 0 in production
settings.why: Debug logs and diagnostic exceptions do not carry model or tool inputs and outputs into the application's log pipeline.

settings.name: EncryptedSession (ttl)
settings.where: EncryptedSession(session_id, underlying_session, encryption_key, ttl=...)
settings.recommended: One session per case, encrypted with a key from your secret manager, ttl matched to the case's retention
settings.why: Conversation history in the store is unreadable without the key, expired items are skipped, and one case's history never seeds another's run.

settings.name: needs_approval
settings.where: @function_tool(needs_approval=...), Agent.as_tool(..., needs_approval=...) (TypeScript needsApproval)
settings.recommended: True, or a callable over the arguments, on every tool that changes records, moves money or sends data out
settings.why: The run pauses with the tool name and arguments for a person to approve or reject that call; don't pass always_approve=True for these tools.

settings.name: needs_approval (ShellTool, ApplyPatchTool)
settings.where: ShellTool(..., needs_approval=True), ApplyPatchTool(..., needs_approval=True)
settings.recommended: True
settings.why: Local shell commands and file edits run on a host the SDK does not sandbox, so each one waits for a decision.

settings.name: require_approval
settings.where: MCPServerStdio / MCPServerSse / MCPServerStreamableHttp(require_approval=...); HostedMCPTool tool_config require_approval
settings.recommended: A per-tool map approving write tools, "always" on hosted MCP connectors that change data
settings.why: An MCP call that writes or sends pauses for a person, the same as a function tool.

settings.name: tool_input_guardrails
settings.where: @function_tool(tool_input_guardrails=[...]), or on a local MCP server for every tool it exposes
settings.recommended: A policy guardrail on every consequential tool that checks principal, tool and arguments
settings.why: A call the policy forbids is skipped or rejected deterministically before it executes; hosted and built-in shell tools do not use this pipeline.

settings.name: pre_approval_tool_input_guardrails
settings.where: RunConfig(tool_execution=ToolExecutionConfig(pre_approval_tool_input_guardrails=True))
settings.recommended: True
settings.why: A call the policy would reject never reaches an approver, who might otherwise approve it; it is checked again after approval.

settings.name: run_in_parallel
settings.where: @input_guardrail(run_in_parallel=False) on the starting agent (TypeScript runInParallel: false)
settings.recommended: False on the injection and policy guardrails
settings.why: The run stops before any model call or tool executes when the guardrail trips, instead of after the agent may already have acted.

settings.name: tool_output_guardrails
settings.where: @function_tool(tool_output_guardrails=[...]), or on a local MCP server
settings.recommended: Your injection classifier on every tool that returns external content
settings.why: A tool result carrying injected instructions is replaced before the model reasons over it.

settings.name: create_static_tool_filter
settings.where: MCP server tool_filter=create_static_tool_filter(allowed_tool_names=[...]) (TypeScript createMCPToolStaticFilter)
settings.default: Unset (every tool the server lists, re-fetched each run)
settings.recommended: The approved tool names for each server
settings.why: Tools a server adds or renames between runs are never exposed to the agent.

settings.name: tool_not_found_behavior
settings.where: RunConfig.tool_not_found_behavior
settings.recommended: Leave at the default
settings.why: A model-emitted call to a tool the current agent does not have ends the run rather than being fed back for the model to retry around.

settings.name: strict_mode
settings.where: @function_tool(strict_mode=...)
settings.recommended: True — don't relax it
settings.why: Arguments must match the tool's JSON schema and constrained types, so malformed or out-of-range values never reach the function.

settings.name: max_turns
settings.where: Runner.run(..., max_turns=...) (TypeScript maxTurns)
settings.recommended: An explicit number sized to the workflow — never None
settings.why: A looping run ends with MaxTurnsExceeded instead of consuming model calls and tool actions without bound.

settings.name: max_function_tool_concurrency and timeout
settings.where: RunConfig(tool_execution=ToolExecutionConfig(max_function_tool_concurrency=N)); @function_tool(timeout=...)
settings.recommended: A concurrency cap and a timeout on every tool that calls a remote system
settings.why: One turn cannot start an unbounded burst of calls against a downstream system or hang on a slow one.

settings.name: UnixLocalSandboxClient / DockerSandboxClient
settings.where: The sandbox client the application constructs for sandbox agents (or a hosted provider client)
settings.recommended: Docker or a hosted sandbox client for any agent whose commands follow untrusted input
settings.why: UnixLocalSandboxClient adds no OS-level confinement on Linux and no network isolation on macOS, so it is not a boundary.

settings.name: inherit_host_environment
settings.where: UnixLocalSandboxClient(inherit_host_environment=False, host_environment_allowlist=...)
settings.recommended: False
settings.why: Sandbox commands get only a short allowlist of variables, not the application's API keys and tokens.

settings.name: network_mode
settings.where: DockerSandboxClientOptions(network_mode="none") (TypeScript networkMode)
settings.recommended: "none" for sandboxes that need no network
settings.why: Commands in the container cannot reach the internet or internal hosts to exfiltrate data.

settings.name: network_policy
settings.where: ShellTool(environment={"type": "container_auto", "network_policy": {...}})
settings.recommended: "allowlist" with your package mirror and the task's hosts, secrets bound with domain_secrets
settings.why: The hosted container reaches only listed domains, and each secret is injected only for its own domain.

settings.name: cancel()
settings.where: RunResultStreaming.cancel() (or mode="after_turn"); TypeScript run(..., { signal }) with an AbortSignal
settings.recommended: Wired to an operator stop control and a run-time ceiling
settings.why: A run that misbehaves stops at once or after its current turn, without killing the process.
