tools.name: ChatGPT Enterprise (chatgpt.com)

variants.name: ChatGPT web (chatgpt.com)
ChatGPT Work Cloud (hosted tasks in OpenAI's cloud)
ChatGPT desktop and mobile apps as chat clients (the same synced chats)
variants.note: Cloud Work conversations sync across web, mobile and desktop, and the desktop app shows chats started on web and mobile. What the desktop app executes or reaches locally is the endpoint record toolChatgptDesktop.

summary: ChatGPT Enterprise in the browser at chatgpt.com: Chat, Work Cloud (hosted multi-step tasks), projects, plugins and connected apps, Workspace Agents and GPTs, administered from the Admin Console (admin.openai.com) and workspace settings. The desktop and mobile apps show the same synced chats, so as chat clients they are this record; the desktop app's local reach — Work Local, Allow local computer access, Computer Use, the built-in browser and browser extension acting on the machine, and the requirements.toml and MDM keys that govern them — is the endpoint record toolChatgptDesktop.

Inference is at OpenAI. Chat and Work Cloud run entirely on OpenAI infrastructure (Work Cloud in VM-backed sandboxes with a hosted browser whose cookies stay separate from the device); the cloud environment does not inherit local files, applications, browser sessions or private-network access.

Enterprise administration is role-based (Owner, Admin, Member, Analytics Viewer plus custom roles whose grants add up, so On in any assigned role grants access), provisioned by SCIM, with plugins and apps off by default on Enterprise and Edu (new workspaces start with a vendor-selected set of apps enabled), per-connection action controls, a GPT actions domain allowlist, access-token lifetime limits, service accounts, and a Compliance API whose records live 30 days at source.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Business, Enterprise and Edu carry the admin controls; apps and plugins default on for Business and off for Enterprise and Edu, except that new Enterprise and Edu workspaces start with a vendor-selected set of apps enabled.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Work Cloud runs the Codex harness in an isolated OpenAI environment; the web cannot access local files, apps or tabs.

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: What a member types, uploads, attaches from Library or a project, or reaches through a connected app; the cloud environment inherits nothing else from the device. Excerpts, screenshots and browser content sent by local work are the endpoint record's (toolChatgptDesktop).

facts.label: Retention & training
facts.value: Conversations follow workspace retention settings with deletion scheduled within 30 days; Compliance Logs Platform keeps 30 days; connected-app data follows the source system.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/chatgpt-work-overview (links every admin page)

items.title: Workspace controls over connectors, apps and memory
body: On Enterprise and Edu workspaces, new plugins and apps are disabled by default (new workspaces start with a vendor-selected set of apps enabled) and enabled per role, with per-app configuration for real-time access, actions, approvals and domain restrictions — one control set that applies across web, mobile, desktop and Codex. Memory and record mode are workspace-level toggles (record off by default), and the Compliance Logs Platform exports immutable audit, authentication and usage events with 30-day source retention, so longer retention requires continuous export.

links.title: Admin controls, security, and compliance for plugins and apps
OpenAI Compliance Platform for Enterprise and Edu customers

items.title: Keeping the endpoint out of the web product
body: For cloud-only Work without cross-device sync, enable Work Cloud and leave Work Local off for the role; Allow local computer access sits under Work Cloud and is a separate opt-in, and turning it off interrupts running turns. Both are tenant switches, so they appear on the endpoint record (toolChatgptDesktop) as well.

links.title: ChatGPT Work cloud security — access and permissions
Roles and workspace permissions — local computer access with Work Cloud

riskNotes.note: Shared connections retrieve with the connected account's permissions, which the vendor warns may be broader than the individual user's; file excerpts and screenshots from local work are the endpoint record's (toolChatgptDesktop).

The hosted cloud browser and connected apps feed arbitrary content to the model; OpenAI's screening (MCP content monitoring, link-generation controls, a sign-in review model) is vendor-internal and not admin-tunable, and a Lockdown Mode role cuts exfiltration paths without screening content.
Agent-owned and shared connected accounts act for whoever triggers the task; action control (read-only or a custom set) is the bound.

controls.mechanism: Admin Console > Permissions custom roles (Default / On / Off; grants combine additively) over Work, plugins and apps, developer mode, agents and GPTs; target-tenant admin consent for connector apps (Admin > Plugins > Configure Microsoft permissions to Entra organisation-wide consent, Google Workspace scope authorisation)

steps.title: Model feature access as custom roles
body: Workspace owners keep Work, plugins, custom MCP plugins, agent building or publishing and GPT sharing off in the workspace default and grant them through custom roles (Permissions & roles > Custom roles) assigned to SCIM groups; grants are additive, so Off in one role does not remove access another assigned role grants.

steps.title: Grant Microsoft permissions through Entra admin consent
body: In Admin > Plugins select Configure Microsoft permissions, keep only the permissions you intend to grant, then have an Entra administrator grant organisation-wide consent to the verified ChatGPT / OpenAI, L.L.C. application; actions stay off until enabled in ChatGPT.

steps.title: Authorise Google scopes in Google Workspace
body: Have the Google Workspace administrator authorise the Drive, Docs, Sheets and Slides scopes (and domain-wide delegation for administrator-managed sync), or turn off the actions whose scopes you will not grant.

steps.title: Require SSO for the workspace
body: In Admin Console (admin.openai.com) open Global settings > Access > Single Sign-On and, after testing the connection, set the ChatGPT product policy (or the workspace override) to Required; Required applies to members whose email is on a verified domain the policy covers.

steps.title: Verify every sign-in domain
body: Under Global settings > Access > Domains add each exact domain and subdomain, publish the DNS TXT record, select Check Domain, then use Manage eligibility to scope it to the intended workspaces.

controls.note: Native by the rule applied to every vendor: the console administers role- and group-based authorisation over connectors, agents and features (custom roles on SCIM-synced groups, whose grants add up), and OpenAI documents the target-tenant consent path for its connector apps — Entra organisation-wide consent to the verified ChatGPT / OpenAI, L.L.C. application for Outlook, Teams and SharePoint, Google Workspace scope authorisation and domain-wide delegation, and Slack admin approval for the ChatGPT Agents app. The target-tenant consent itself is the other tenant's control (Entra, Google Workspace, Slack, GitHub organisation approval); OpenAI does not publish the Entra app ID, so confirm the app identity on the consent screen. Custom roles are Enterprise, Edu and Healthcare only and take about five minutes to apply. Policy administration is not the runtime decision, which OpenAI makes per request. Required SSO sends verified-domain members through the IdP, but invited members from other domains may still use another permitted sign-in method; domain claiming (a separate request to OpenAI) also blocks corporate app connections from personal or other workspaces.

original.mechanism: SCIM provisioning, workspace roles and custom roles (Permissions & roles), access-token expiration limit
original.note: SAML/OIDC setup lives in the Help Center, which returned 403 today; the roles model is verified.

steps.title: Provision from the IdP
body: SCIM provisions membership and groups (manually managed or IdP managed); group membership alone grants no feature permission.

steps.title: Assign roles with deny-wins semantics
body: Owner, Admin, Member, Analytics Viewer and custom roles carry Default / On / Off per feature; an explicit Off in any role blocks access.

steps.title: Bound token lifetime
body: Owners set "Access token expiration limit" in Permissions & roles.

original.mechanism: Connected-service permissions govern retrieval; source-system permission mapping
original.note: Shared connections use the connected account's permissions, potentially broader than the user's.

steps.title: Test with a least-privileged account
body: A member can use an MCP server only when the plugin is available to their role and they have access to the connected service; verify with an account holding only intended permissions.

controls.mechanism: ChatGPT-Allowed-Workspace-Id header injected on https://chatgpt.com/* by the organisation's SASE or TLS-inspecting proxy and enforced by OpenAI; workspace IP allowlisting (inbound)

steps.title: Inject the allowed-workspace header
body: Have the SASE or proxy add ChatGPT-Allowed-Workspace-Id with the workspace UUID(s), comma-separated without spaces, to requests for https://chatgpt.com/*; OpenAI filters out every other workspace, personal ones included, and returns 403 when none remain.

steps.title: Block logged-out use and cover the apps
body: Block URLs starting https://chatgpt.com/backend-anon/, and add the proxy's certificates to the desktop and mobile apps' pin list by MDM (the apps pin certificates), or block desktop.chatgpt.com, ios.chat.openai.com and android.chat.openai.com outright.

steps.title: Restrict where the workspace is reachable from
body: Workspace Settings > Identity & access > Access Restrictions, add IP ranges for Workspace and Compliance API, then toggle Activate IP Allowlist (changes take 5-15 minutes).

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: OpenAI honours a documented allowed-workspace header that the organisation's proxy injects and enforces the block server-side; the SSE only admits the destination, and a pinned session to the approved tenant is not readable. It holds only on traffic the proxy sees and can decrypt — the desktop and mobile apps pin certificates, so devices without the MDM pin exception are outside it. A customer proxy does not control OpenAI's own egress: Work Cloud code and shell (public internet toggle and managed allowlist), the cloud browser, deep research, agent mode and connector calls leave from OpenAI infrastructure; the vendor-side levers are the Work network setting and a Lockdown Mode role (live browsing, agent mode, deep research and file downloads off; Codex unaffected). IP allowlisting limits inbound access to the workspace and Compliance API, not outbound traffic. The desktop app's local runtime — its workspace pin, command networking and desktop-app destination rules — is the endpoint record toolChatgptDesktop.

original.mechanism: Tenancy pinning in product (allowed_chatgpt_workspaces for the desktop app, IP access restrictions referenced); inline inspection is a third-party SSE
original.note: Comparable to Claude chat: the vendor pins tenancy (allowed_chatgpt_workspaces) and offers workspace IP access restrictions, and the inline inspection is the customer's SSE; rated partial for the same reason.

steps.title: Pin the desktop app to the workspace
body: allowed_chatgpt_workspaces in requirements.toml restricts sign-in to listed workspace UUIDs.

original.mechanism: "Allow public internet access" for Work Cloud code/shell (managed allowlist when off); [experimental_network] for Work Local

steps.title: Turn off public internet for cloud code and shell
body: When disabled, commands reach only required hostnames from a managed allowlist; this controls destinations, not commands.

steps.title: Allowlist domains for local commands
body: [experimental_network] with managed_allowed_domains_only = true; browser tools and MCP are outside it.

original.note: Work Cloud code and shell follow the managed allowlist when public internet access is off; Work Local commands follow [experimental_network]. Browser, computer use and connector traffic are outside both and need a network-layer control.

controls.mechanism: SharePoint app Safety & Security Controls > Excluded sensitivity labels without encryption (label-based restriction); no in-product inspection of prompts, uploads or responses in Chat or Work

steps.title: Exclude labelled SharePoint files
body: In the SharePoint app's Safety & Security Controls enter each non-encrypting Microsoft Purview label GUID under Excluded sensitivity labels without encryption; files with encrypting labels are already excluded.

steps.title: Inspect prompts at the endpoint or browser
body: Apply endpoint, browser or SSE DLP inline to chatgpt.com; the desktop and mobile apps need the proxy certificate added to their pin list by MDM before SSL inspection works.

steps.title: Scan conversations after the fact
body: Have a workspace owner create an Admin key with Conversation messages and app-log access and feed the Compliance Logs Platform to a DLP partner such as Microsoft Purview, Netskope, Cyberhaven, Forcepoint or Palo Alto Networks.

controls.note: Partial only by the label-restriction clause of the rule applied to every vendor: the SharePoint sensitivity-label exclusion, enforced by OpenAI, keeps labelled files out of SharePoint app results (supported Office, PDF and MP4 files; TXT and CSV are treated as unlabelled; OneDrive is separate). Nothing in Chat or Work detects identifiers, secrets or classified content in what an employee types or uploads, in connector payloads or in responses, and nothing masks them; Prisma AIRS external guardrails scan Codex prompts only. The pin's objective — classification before material leaves the person — is met by endpoint or browser DLP inline; Compliance Logs Platform partners scan conversations after they reach OpenAI (detection after the fact, 30-day source window). Action controls and parameter constraints limit where data can go but inspect nothing; the desktop app's local minimisation keys (deny_read, allow_appshots) are on toolChatgptDesktop.

original.mechanism: Action control per connection and requirements.toml deny_read / allow_appshots
original.note: In-product controls limit what agents can reach and screenshot; nothing inspects prompt or upload content.

steps.title: Limit what connections may do
body: Action control allows read-only, all or a custom set of actions per connection.

steps.title: Stop screenshots and secret reads on the desktop
body: allow_appshots = false and [permissions.filesystem] deny_read in requirements.toml.

original.mechanism: Managed browser controls for the built-in browser (origins, uploads, downloads, developer access; browser_use flags)
original.note: Covers the agent's browser, not the employee's browser session on chatgpt.com. Rated partial for the managed agent browser only; the employee's own browser on chatgpt.com is secured by the organisation's browser tooling, which is external here as for every other chat SaaS.

steps.title: Restrict the built-in browser
body: Set [features] browser_use and browser_use_full_cdp_access = false, or use the managed browser controls to restrict origins, uploads, downloads and developer access.

controls.mechanism: Vendor-operated screening of returned content (online and offline monitoring of MCP content for prompt injection, policy screening of MCP prompts, known-malicious-domain blocking, link-generation controls, a cloud-browser sign-in review model); none of it is admin-configurable

steps.title: Verify the vendor's returned-content defenses
body: Assess the app and MCP safeguards the App security whitepaper describes (injection monitoring, malicious-domain blocking, link-generation controls) and record that no admin toggle, threshold or detection event exists for them.

steps.title: Limit untrusted MCP sources
body: In Permissions & roles grant Upload plugins with custom MCP servers and Create plugins with MCPs only to vetted builders; only admins and owners can publish a custom app.

steps.title: Put high-risk groups in a Lockdown Mode role
body: Designate a custom role as a Lockdown Mode role and assign the groups that handle sensitive data, which turns off live browsing, agent mode and deep research; it limits exfiltration and does not screen content.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: OpenAI documents vendor-internal screening of returned content — online and offline monitoring for prompt injection originating from MCP servers, policy screening of MCP prompts, blocking of known malicious domains, link-generation controls against URL-based exfiltration and a review model on cloud-browser sign-in pages — but none of it can be switched on, tuned or set to block by the admin, and no detection event is a documented Compliance Logs Platform type. Lockdown Mode cuts outbound paths and, per the vendor, does not prevent prompt injections from appearing in the content ChatGPT processes; Auto approve and Important actions classify actions, not input; the frozen tool snapshot of custom MCP apps guards definitions, not results; Prisma AIRS (Codex only) screens prompts, not tool results. Records read through the organisation's own MCP tier can be classified by its gateway (the drawing's second pin).

original.mechanism: Sign-in review model in the built-in browser, automated risk checks on Auto approve, safety review pauses

steps.title: Know what the vendor checks
body: A review model checks sign-in requests for phishing or deception; the feature is tested against prompt injection.

original.note: Vendor-operated review on browser sign-in and Auto approve actions; page and file content the assistant reads is not classified for injected instructions, and nothing is customer-tunable.

controls.mechanism: Vendor evidence from the OpenAI Trust Portal and the App security and Workspace agents security papers, consumed by the organisation's TPRM platform

evidence.title: OpenAI Trust Portal (SafeBase) — SOC 2 Type 2, SOC 3, ISO/IEC 27001/27017/27018/27701 and 42001, CSA STAR, PCI DSS, FedRAMP 20x, pentest report, subprocessors and DPA (2026-09-25)
App security whitepaper (June 2026)
Workspace agents security overview

controls.note: External by the rule applied to every vendor: the assessment runs in the organisation's TPRM platform. The portal describes itself as covering ChatGPT Enterprise and Edu and lists SOC 2 Type 2 (the 2026 report covers 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2026 and needs an authenticated account), SOC 3, ISO/IEC 27001, 27017, 27018, 27701 and 42001, CSA STAR, PCI DSS, TX-RAMP, FedRAMP 20x, a pentest report, data-flow diagram, CAIQ and HECVAT, the subprocessor list and the DPA; most reports require an access request. Re-assess on the vendor's release clock: new Enterprise workspaces start with a vendor-selected set of apps enabled, Work is on by default for the default role on eligible workspaces, and custom GPTs retire for Enterprise on 2026-12-11 in favour of plugins. Custom MCP servers and third-party apps sit outside OpenAI's trust boundary and need their own assessment.

original.mechanism: Trust portal evidence (SOC 2 Type 2 scope names ChatGPT Enterprise, Edu and Team)

steps.title: Collect evidence
body: SOC 2 / SOC 3 reports, pen-test reports, subprocessor list and DPA are on the trust portal.

original.mechanism: Workspace analytics, Analytics API and the GPT management dashboard feed an external system of record

evidence.title: Vendor docs index, reviewed for the integration point (2026-09-10)

original.mechanism: Compliance API, Analytics API and Admin API consumed by an SSPM product
original.note: Compliance, Analytics and Admin APIs are the inputs; comparison to a baseline and drift detection are the SSPM product's.

evidence.title: Vendor docs index, reviewed for the integration point (2026-09-10)

controls.mechanism: Workspace settings > General > Plugin permissions (workspace default) and per-app Permissions in Admin Console > Plugins (Always ask, Any changes, Important actions, Never ask); Workspace Agent write approvals set by each agent's builder

steps.title: Set the workspace default to ask before changes
body: In Workspace settings > General > Settings > Plugin permissions select Always ask or Allow read actions; the workspace-wide selector does not offer Allow all actions.

steps.title: Keep write-capable apps off Never ask
body: In Admin Console > Plugins open each included app's Permissions control and choose Any changes or Always ask; never select Never ask for an app that can write.

steps.title: Restrict who publishes agents that write
body: In Permissions & roles grant Enable agent publishing and Enable agent publishing with agent-owned connections only to reviewed builders, because each agent's builder sets its write approvals.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: a person approves app actions on a card that shows the app and the proposed action, the admin decides when ChatGPT asks (workspace default plus a per-app override), and managed-workspace members are not offered Always allow as a persistent approval for app actions. Below native because the requirement is set per app, not per action; the per-app options are now Always ask, Any changes (reads proceed, changes need confirmation), Important actions (ChatGPT judges which actions to ask about — an automated reviewer) and Never ask, and an authorised write can run without a prompt when the configured policy allows it; the workspace-wide selector's current options could not be re-read (Help Center 403 on 2026-10-30); Workspace Agents' write approvals (Always ask by default, or Never ask or Custom) are set by the builder, not the admin, and scheduled or event-triggered runs execute without the requester present; cloud-browser website access has an Auto approve risk check, though admins can remove Always allow workspace-wide. Approvals saved on the device (Computer Use, the local browser, Apple Messages) and the keys that stop them are the endpoint record toolChatgptDesktop. Some risky actions are denied rather than prompted. Binding an approval to the exact arguments, and voiding it if they change, is not documented.

original.mechanism: App permissions (when ChatGPT asks before using a connection), website approval levels, per-app computer-use approval

steps.title: Require confirmation on connections
body: App permissions decide when ChatGPT asks before using a connection; start with read actions.

steps.title: Limit website approval levels
body: Always ask, Auto approve, Always allow; administrators can limit which levels users may select.

steps.title: Keep computer use per-app
body: ChatGPT asks before using each application; "Always allow" is per app and listed under Always-allowed apps.

controls.mechanism: Administrator-managed sync source selection (SharePoint sites or folders, Google Drive shared drives or folders), the Admin > Plugins app list and public-catalog CSV export; classification and oversharing analysis by DSPM partners reading the Compliance Platform

steps.title: Choose exactly what is indexed
body: When setting up Indexed search for an app in Admin > Plugins, select the specific sites, folders or shared drives to include rather than all supported content.

steps.title: Export the app catalogue for review
body: In Admin > Plugins select Public, then Export CSV (public-plugins-security-review.csv) to list each plugin with its MCP servers and skills.

steps.title: Classify what sits behind the connectors
body: Feed the Compliance Platform to a DSPM partner such as Varonis, Concentric AI, Microsoft Purview or Teleskope and run oversharing analysis in the source system before enabling sync.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: the product lists the connected sources — which apps are enabled and which sites, folders or drives the administrator-managed index covers — but does not inventory or classify the content behind them or report oversharing; the assistant surfaces whatever the source permissions already allow. Live, non-synced connections retrieve on demand from anything the user's account can reach, so the index scope does not bound them. Retention settings and the Compliance API's 30-day window are lifecycle controls, not inventory. DSPM products (Compliance Platform partners) or the source system's own data-security tooling classify content and find the oversharing.

original.mechanism: Workspace retention settings, Compliance API 30-day window, HIPAA configuration

steps.title: Set retention and export
body: Conversations follow workspace settings with deletion within 30 days; export compliance records before the 30-day source window lapses.

steps.title: Apply the regulated-workspace profile where PHI is possible
body: Keep [mcp_servers] empty by default, restrict sign-in with allowed_login_methods, and do not use Codex cloud with PHI.

original.note: Retention and the Compliance API window are lifecycle controls; discovery, classification and exposure assessment of workspace content are the customer's DSPM product reading the Compliance API.

controls.mechanism: OpenAI-held connector OAuth tokens (encrypted, never in model context), workspace Admin keys (scoped, expiry 30-365 days or Never, revocable) and the Access token expiration limit for Codex and Workspace Agent tokens; no tunnel in this product

steps.title: Scope and expire Admin keys
body: In Admin Console open the workspace's Credentials > Admin keys, choose Custom permissions and a 30, 60, 90-day or custom expiration up to 365 days instead of the Never default, and revoke keys no longer used.

steps.title: Cap access-token lifetime
body: In Permissions & roles set Access token expiration limit; revoke tokens at chatgpt.com/admin/access-tokens.

steps.title: Revoke connector credentials in bulk
body: Disable the app in Admin > Plugins to trigger revocation and deletion of its stored tokens; the admin cannot rotate or expire them individually.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: connector refresh credentials are held by OpenAI, encrypted at rest (AES-256 under Azure Key Vault keys, EKM-capable), minted into short-lived access tokens per call and never placed in prompts, per the App security whitepaper; the admin can revoke them only in bulk by disabling an app and cannot bound their lifetime or rotation. Admin keys are scoped and revocable, but an owner can still create one with no expiry and existing expirations cannot be changed; the access-token expiration limit bounds new Codex and Workspace Agent tokens only. This product has no tunnel of its own: the drawing's tunnel credential belongs to Secure MCP Tunnel (toolOpenaiMcpTunnel) and is rated there. mTLS to custom MCP servers uses an OpenAI-managed client certificate.

original.mechanism: Access-token expiration limit, service-account token lifetime (maximum one year), federation

steps.title: Bound and rotate tokens
body: Tokens require an expiry at creation; owners set the workspace-wide limit; treat tokens as automation secrets.

original.note: Token lifetime limits bound how long a stored credential works; nothing issues per-request credentials. Connector tokens are held by OpenAI and never shown to the model.

controls.mechanism: Permissions & roles > Custom roles > Plugins & connected data (apps per role), Admin > Plugins app Actions (read, write and individual actions; New actions set to Disable new actions), admin-only publishing of custom MCP apps with a frozen tool snapshot, GPT actions domain allowlist

steps.title: Allow apps per role
body: In Workspace settings > Permissions & roles > Custom roles open the role, turn on Allow members to use plugins under Plugins & connected data and use Select to choose its apps.

steps.title: Scope each app's actions
body: In Admin Console > Plugins open the app's Tools (or Actions), enable only the Read or Write actions needed and set New tools (or New actions) to disable new actions so later actions wait for admin review.

steps.title: Gate custom MCP servers
body: Grant Upload plugins with custom MCP servers and Create plugins with MCPs only to vetted builders; only admins and owners publish, choosing actions with Configure Actions and groups with Configure Access, and tool changes need Refresh and republish.

steps.title: Constrain GPT actions until GPTs retire
body: In Workspace settings > GPTs > Actions allow only approved domains; with no domains listed, custom GPT actions cannot execute.

controls.note: Native by the rule applied to every vendor: the admin allowlists apps (off by default apart from the vendor-selected set in new workspaces), assigns them per role and scopes each app's read, write and individual actions, enforced server-side by OpenAI across Chat, Work, deep research and plugins; custom MCP servers need an admin to publish them. Action scoping is per app for the whole workspace, not per role; Workspace Agent builders can narrow further with per-agent actions and Connector Action Constraints but cannot exceed what the admin enabled. Argument-level limits are SharePoint site-collection lists and the parameter constraints the App security whitepaper describes; otherwise the connector's own OAuth scope bounds the call. MCP servers configured locally in the desktop app follow requirements.toml, not these workspace controls (toolChatgptDesktop). Custom GPTs retire for Enterprise on 2026-12-11.

original.mechanism: Admin > Plugins availability per role, action control per connection, GPT actions domain allowlist

steps.title: Enable plugins per role
body: Plugins are off by default on Enterprise and Edu; limit availability to a role or pilot group in Admin > Plugins.

steps.title: Restrict GPT actions to approved domains
body: If no domains are allowed, custom GPT actions cannot execute (Administration > Workspace access, policy, and models > GPTs and Sharing).

original.note: Plugin availability hides tools per role; action control per connection gates; the GPT actions domain allowlist limits destinations. No argument-level scoping inside a connector beyond its own authorisation.

controls.mechanism: Retrieval with each user's provider permissions (live OAuth apps; administrator-managed index with replicated ACLs), SharePoint app Safety & Security Controls site-collection allowlist or deny list, administrator-managed sync source selection

steps.title: Restrict SharePoint to approved site collections
body: In the SharePoint app's Safety & Security Controls choose Access mode Allowed sites and add the site-collection GUIDs (UI, CSV or the Admin API with an Apps-write Admin key); the rule covers search, browsing, retrieval and actions.

steps.title: Scope the administrator-managed index
body: When setting up Indexed search select the SharePoint sites or folders or Google Drive shared drives or folders to include; each member retrieves only what their provider permissions allow.

steps.title: Keep shared agents on the caller's identity
body: Grant Enable agent publishing with agent-owned connections only to reviewed builders so published agents authenticate each end user rather than a shared account.

controls.note: Native by the rule applied to every vendor: retrieval runs with the requesting user's provider permissions — live apps call the source with the user's OAuth grant, and the administrator-managed index replicates source ACLs and filters results per member — and the admin restricts what may be returned (SharePoint site-collection allow or deny lists, enforced by OpenAI before results reach the model; sync source selection). Boundaries: the site controls need enabling for the workspace and cover whole site collections, not subsites, folders or OneDrive; index scope does not restrict a separately enabled live connection; permission changes reach the index only on refresh; administrator-managed SharePoint sync reads ACLs with a broad Microsoft grant (Sites.FullControl.All); for other apps the connector's OAuth scope is the only corpus bound; agent-owned or shared connections retrieve with the connected account's permissions, which the vendor warns can exceed the requester's. Oversharing analysis of indexed repositories is not provided (see D3-DI).

original.mechanism: Connected-service permissions govern retrieval; source-system permission mapping
original.note: Shared connections use the connected account's permissions, potentially broader than the user's.

steps.title: Test with a least-privileged account
body: A member can use an MCP server only when the plugin is available to their role and they have access to the connected service; verify with an account holding only intended permissions.

controls.mechanism: Admin > Plugins catalogue (apps off by default; admin-published custom MCP apps pinned to a tool snapshot) and the Stateful Compliance API List Workspace Plugins, List Workspace Agents and List GPTs

steps.title: Pull the inventory by API
body: With an Admin key call List Workspace Plugins (creator, marketplace, version, installation policy, status), List Workspace Agents (owner, status; draft-only agents excluded) and List GPTs.

steps.title: Keep the connector catalogue in allowlist mode
body: Leave new apps disabled, enable each one deliberately in Admin > Plugins, and publish custom MCP apps only after review; an approved app keeps its tool snapshot until an admin refreshes it.

steps.title: Limit third-party GPTs and agent publishing
body: In Permissions & roles allow only owner-approved third-party GPTs and grant Enable agent publishing only to reviewed builders.

steps.title: Record owner and approval yourself
body: For each connected service record the business owner, approved actions, authentication method and removal contact, as the Plugin controls guide instructs.

steps.title: Build the grant inventory from the log
body: Pull APP_AUTH_LOG (link or unlink, link_id, actor) from the Compliance Logs Platform with an Admin key holding the Apps Auth log scope and keep the grant inventory in the identity-governance tool.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: enforcement exists — apps are off by default on Enterprise and Edu (new workspaces start with a vendor-selected set enabled), only admins publish custom MCP apps and a published app stays on its approved tool snapshot, and third-party GPTs can be limited to owner-approved ones — and the Admin API lists workspace plugins, agents and GPTs with creator or owner. Missing is an owner-and-approval record on the same entry: public-directory apps carry the developer's name, not an organisational owner (the vendor tells admins to keep that record themselves), and Workspace Agents and custom GPTs carry an owner and a publication status but no admin approval — a member holding the building and publishing permissions ships one without review. Draft-only agents are absent from the API list, and nothing reconciles connectors found outside the workspace. Custom GPTs retire for Enterprise on 2026-12-11. Connector grants are per-user OAuth links held by OpenAI: no console or API lists each user's live grants, so that inventory is rebuilt from APP_AUTH_LOG link and unlink events.

original.mechanism: Admin > Plugins (marketplace import and sync) and the GPT management dashboard

steps.title: Manage the plugin catalogue
body: Import a GitHub marketplace, sync daily, mark plugins Available or Installed per role, and flag "No longer in source".

steps.title: Inventory GPTs
body: The dashboard shows builder, custom actions, who can access, activity and ownership for every workspace GPT.

controls.mechanism: Nothing in the product lists personal accounts on verified domains; SSE or CASB discovery of chatgpt.com use, with the allowed-workspace header, domain claiming and automatic account creation as prevention and enrolment

evidence.title: Corporate Network Controls in ChatGPT Enterprise (header, backend-anon blocking) (2026-09-25)
Onboarding employees with existing ChatGPT accounts (automatic account creation) (2026-09-25)
Verifying your domain for OpenAI identity (domain claiming is a separate request) (2026-09-25)

controls.note: External by the rule applied to every vendor: no page documents a report of personal or unmanaged ChatGPT accounts on the organisation's verified domains. Automatic account creation invites verified-domain users into the workspace when they sign in (enrolment, not discovery); domain claiming, by request to OpenAI, blocks corporate app connections from personal or other workspaces; the ChatGPT-Allowed-Workspace-Id header refuses other workspaces and anonymous use on managed networks — prevention, credited here only. Finding personal accounts, other AI chat tenants and unsanctioned connectors is the SSE or CASB's job (chatgpt.com, backend-anon and the app hostnames in proxy logs); finding unmanaged desktop-app installs is the endpoint record's (toolChatgptDesktop).

original.mechanism: None in product beyond workspace pinning of the desktop app

evidence.title: Vendor docs index, reviewed for the integration point (2026-09-10)

controls.mechanism: Compliance Logs Platform (immutable JSONL: conversation messages, APP_LOG request and response, APP_AUTH_LOG, audit, auth, Workspace Agent and Codex events) pulled with a workspace Admin key; 30-day source retention

steps.title: Create an Admin key for log export
body: In Admin Console open the workspace's Credentials > Admin keys; a workspace owner grants Conversation messages plus the audit, authentication and app log categories.

steps.title: Collect continuously
body: Run download_compliance_files.sh or .ps1 (or the List Files and Download File endpoints) per event type into the SIEM before the 30-day source window lapses.

steps.title: Pin the collector's addresses
body: IP allowlisting is always enforced for Compliance API keys; add the collector's egress IPs under Identity & access > Access Restrictions.

controls.note: Native by the rule applied to every vendor: the Compliance Logs Platform exports conversation messages and connector and tool events — APP_LOG records the request payload and normalised response of each app call, APP_AUTH_LOG each link and unlink, and Workspace Agent logs carry run, connector-call, trigger and memory events — as immutable JSONL files with a p99 target under 30 minutes, ready to fuse with the organisation's gateway record. Boundaries: 30 days at source with no backfill; the vendor says the export does not establish a complete trail for every hosted shell command, browser interaction, file operation or approval; Work Local, Computer Use and browser-extension actions are not fully recorded (local OpenTelemetry is a separate opt-in path, on toolChatgptDesktop); app-log coverage varies by app. Capture only: tamper resistance and retention beyond 30 days are the receiving store's.

original.mechanism: Compliance API (30-day source retention) and workspace analytics
original.note: Not every local file operation, screenshot or Chrome-extension action appears in the Compliance API.

steps.title: Export continuously
body: Use COMPLIANCE_API_KEY against the Admin API; the source window does not replace your retention policy.

controls.mechanism: Permissions & roles Off for Work Cloud, Work Local and Enable agents; app Disable in Admin > Plugins; Unpublish or Delete Workspace Agent and Delete User Automation on the Admin API; access-token and service-account revocation

steps.title: Turn the agent surfaces off
body: In Admin Console > Permissions set Work Cloud, Work Local and Enable agents to Off in the workspace default and in every role that grants them — grants are additive, so one remaining On keeps access — and turn off Allow local computer access, which interrupts currently running turns and keeps the desktop app's local reach (toolChatgptDesktop) out of cloud tasks.

steps.title: Revoke connector access in bulk
body: In Admin > Plugins select Disable on each affected app; turning an app off triggers revocation of its stored tokens.

steps.title: Stop agents and scheduled tasks
body: Call Unpublish Workspace Agent or Delete Workspace Agent and Delete User Automation on the Admin API, or use the agent area of the admin console.

steps.title: Revoke automation credentials
body: Revoke tokens at chatgpt.com/admin/access-tokens and disable service accounts, which revokes all of their tokens.

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: the admin can switch the agent surfaces off org-wide, revoke connector grants in bulk by disabling apps, unpublish or delete agents and delete scheduled tasks; turning off Allow local computer access is documented to interrupt currently running turns, but no page says a Work Cloud task, agent run or deep research already in progress stops. Documented timings are custom-role changes in about five minutes, IdP sync every 30 to 40 minutes (it cannot be forced), IP allowlist 5 to 15 minutes, and a Work network change after the current command finishes; the delay for stopping running work is not documented. Removing local Codex permission suspends tokens without revoking them, and per-user grant revocation is the user's action. Measure the stop before relying on it.

original.mechanism: Role Off for Work Local / Work Cloud / plugins, token revocation, service-account disable

steps.title: Turn surfaces off by role
body: Work Cloud and Work Local are distinct toggles in Permissions & roles; plugins can be made unavailable in Admin > Plugins.

steps.title: Revoke credentials
body: Owners and admins revoke any token; disabling a service account revokes all of its tokens.

original.note: Role and token changes apply at the next request; an in-flight request completes. The docs state no propagation delay, so measure it before relying on it.

settings.name: SSO
settings.where: Global Admin Console (admin.openai.com) › SSO and related identity settings, after domain verification
settings.recommended: Required for every verified domain, with MFA enforced on the ChatGPT app in your IdP
settings.why: ChatGPT has no workspace-wide MFA switch, so the IdP's sign-in policy is the only place staff MFA is enforced.

settings.name: Enable Directory Sync
settings.where: Workspace settings › Identity & access › Enable Directory Sync (Use SCIM only for this workspace, or the tenant-level connection)
settings.recommended: On, with membership and groups driven by the IdP groups that grant ChatGPT
settings.why: Removing someone in the IdP removes their workspace membership, so a leaver's access ends with their account rather than with a ticket.

settings.name: Automatic Account Creation
settings.where: Workspace administration (eligible email domains)
settings.recommended: Off where SCIM is on
settings.why: Accounts it creates may sit outside SCIM, so removing someone from the IdP group can leave their workspace access in place.

settings.name: Verified-domain restrictions (domain claiming)
settings.where: Requested from your OpenAI account team for each corporate domain; verifying a domain alone does not activate it
settings.recommended: Active for every corporate email domain
settings.why: Staff cannot connect corporate SharePoint, Gmail or Slack accounts to a personal or other unapproved ChatGPT workspace.

settings.name: Work Cloud
settings.where: Admin Console › Permissions › Workspace default and custom roles › Work Cloud
settings.default: On for the default role on eligible Enterprise and Edu workspaces
settings.recommended: Off in the workspace default; On through a custom role for the groups being rolled out
settings.why: Hosted multi-step tasks act through connected apps; grants add up across roles, so a deliberate group is the only reliable scope.

settings.name: Use Work locally (or Allow members to use Codex and Work Locally)
settings.where: Admin Console › Permissions › Work Local (or the combined Codex and Work Local section)
settings.recommended: Off in the workspace default; On only through a custom role for groups whose devices carry the toolChatgptDesktop baseline
settings.why: Keeps the desktop app's local Work out of the web rollout; with Work Cloud on and Work Local off, Work stays in OpenAI's cloud without cross-device sync.

settings.name: Allow local computer access
settings.where: Admin Console › Permissions › Work Cloud › Allow local computer access
settings.recommended: Off until the Agent security Global baseline is reviewed; then On for Work Local groups only
settings.why: Cloud-orchestrated tasks reach the connected computer's files and tools; turning it off interrupts running turns, so it doubles as a stop.

settings.name: Use a browser
settings.where: Admin Console › Permissions › Workspace default › Workspace capabilities › Let agents use cloud computers (labelled Cloud browser use on some pages); shared with dots and team automations
settings.recommended: On
settings.why: Hosted browsing is much of Work's value and runs in a separate session without the user's sign-ins; regulated teams turn it off by role or use a Lockdown Mode role.

settings.name: Allow network access
settings.where: Admin Console › Permissions › Workspace default › Workspace capabilities › Let agents use cloud computers (labelled Cloud network access on some pages)
settings.recommended: Off — cloud code and shell reach only the managed destination allowlist
settings.why: Code a task writes cannot send data to arbitrary hosts from OpenAI's infrastructure; the browser, web search and apps are separate paths.

settings.name: Use password manager
settings.where: Admin Console › Permissions › Workspace default › Workspace capabilities › Use password manager
settings.recommended: Off
settings.why: Keeps the password manager out of the in-app and cloud browsers an agent drives; members sign in through the secure hosted sign-in flow instead.

settings.name: Use plugins
settings.where: Admin Console › Permissions & roles › (role) › Use plugins (Allow members to use plugins)
settings.recommended: On for the roles that need the approved plugins
settings.why: The general plugin permission is the first gate before any app's data or actions reach a member.

settings.name: Upload plugins with custom MCP servers / Create plugins with MCPs
settings.where: Admin Console › Permissions & roles › (role)
settings.recommended: Off except for a named group of reviewed plugin builders
settings.why: A custom MCP server is outside OpenAI's trust boundary and feeds unscreened content to the model; only vetted builders can add one.

settings.name: Publish plugins to workspace
settings.where: Admin Console › Permissions & roles › (role)
settings.recommended: The plugin maintainers only
settings.why: Only plugins someone has reviewed and owns reach the workspace directory.

settings.name: Installation settings (Available for installation, Installed for workspace, Customize by role, Disable)
settings.where: Admin Console › Plugins › (plugin) or bulk Edit
settings.default: New Enterprise and Edu workspaces start with a vendor-selected set of apps enabled
settings.recommended: Disable for every plugin not approved; Available for installation or Customize by role for approved ones
settings.why: The catalogue stays an allowlist; a role-level Off does not remove access another role grants, so review every role.

settings.name: App access
settings.where: Admin Console › Plugins › (app) › App access
settings.recommended: The groups whose work needs the app
settings.why: Installing a plugin grants no app; each app reaches only the people chosen here, then the connected account's permissions.

settings.name: Tools (or Actions)
settings.where: Admin Console › Plugins › (app) › Tools — Read actions, Write actions, or individual actions
settings.recommended: Read actions only, with individual write actions added where a workflow needs them
settings.why: A summarising workflow cannot create, share or delete records in the connected system.

settings.name: New tools (or New actions)
settings.where: Admin Console › Plugins › (app) › New tools
settings.default: New read actions enabled automatically when Read actions is selected
settings.recommended: Disable new actions
settings.why: An action the developer adds later waits for an admin to review it instead of appearing for every member.

settings.name: Permissions (Always ask, Any changes, Important actions, Never ask)
settings.where: Admin Console › Plugins › (app) › Permissions
settings.recommended: Any changes
settings.why: Reads proceed and every write needs the member's confirmation; regulated teams choose Always ask.

settings.name: Safety & Security Controls
settings.where: Admin Console › Plugins › (app, e.g. SharePoint) › Safety & Security Controls
settings.default: No content restriction beyond the source system's permissions
settings.recommended: On for SharePoint — approved site collections only, and your most sensitive non-encrypting labels excluded
settings.why: Content a member could open in the source still stays out of ChatGPT when it is in a restricted site or carries an excluded label.

settings.name: Manage Domains (domain restriction)
settings.where: Workspace App Settings › (app) dropdown › Manage Domains
settings.recommended: Your corporate domains, set when the app is enabled
settings.why: Supported apps (Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, GitHub, Slack) link and call only organisation-approved identities and domains.

settings.name: Admin-managed Sync
settings.where: The app's Admin-managed Sync setup › scope of synced sites, folders or shared drives
settings.recommended: Off until the source's oversharing is reviewed; then only the sites, folders or shared drives the workspace needs
settings.why: An index replicates source permissions as they are, so overshared content becomes answerable to everyone it is shared with.

settings.name: Workspace connections
settings.where: Admin Console › Workspace connections › + (app), then grant access to users, teams or service accounts
settings.recommended: A dedicated company account with only the resources the team task needs, granted to named teams
settings.why: A shared connection acts with its own account's permissions, which can exceed the requesting member's.

settings.name: Domains (GPT actions)
settings.where: Workspace GPT settings › Domains
settings.recommended: Only the approved API domains your GPTs call; none if no GPT uses custom actions
settings.why: With no domains allowed, custom GPT actions cannot execute, so a GPT cannot post data to an arbitrary API.

settings.name: Lockdown Mode
settings.where: Admin Console › Permissions › Lockdown Mode roles, where available
settings.recommended: A Lockdown Mode role for the groups handling the most sensitive client matters, not the whole workspace
settings.why: Cuts the outbound paths injected content could use to exfiltrate data and applies even when an ordinary role grants access; it screens nothing.

settings.name: Access token expiration limit
settings.where: Workspace settings › Permissions & roles › Access tokens (or the Codex and Work Local section)
settings.recommended: 90 days
settings.why: Codex and Workspace Agents tokens a member creates stop working within a bounded window; existing tokens keep theirs.

settings.name: Admin keys (Compliance Logs Platform)
settings.where: Admin Console › (workspace) › Credentials › Admin keys, read by the download_compliance_files script or the Admin API
settings.default: No key; records kept 30 days at source
settings.recommended: One key for the SIEM collector with Conversation messages and the audit, auth and app log categories, pulled continuously
settings.why: Prompts, responses and app calls reach your SIEM before the 30-day source window lapses; there is no backfill.
