tools.name: opencode

variants.name: opencode TUI and CLI (npm opencode-ai, v1.18.32 2026-09-21)
opencode serve / opencode web (headless HTTP server and browser UI)
OpenCode Desktop (beta)
OpenCode IDE extension (VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf, VSCodium; sst-dev.opencode)
OpenCode GitHub agent (anomalyco/opencode/github action on the customer's runners)

summary: Anomaly's (formerly SST) open-source terminal coding agent (MIT, npm opencode-ai): a TUI over a local client/server core whose HTTP API also serves the web UI, the desktop app, the IDE extension, ACP editors and the SDK. Built-in build and plan agents plus subagents drive bash, edit, write, read, grep, glob, webfetch, websearch, task and skill tools, MCP servers, plugins, custom tools and skills. Inference is whatever provider the developer connects — any models.dev provider with a pasted key, a local model server, or the vendor's optional Zen and Go gateways.

Prompts, file contents and tool output go straight to the chosen provider; the vendor states it stores no code or context. The exception is session sharing (config key share: manual, auto or disabled), which syncs the conversation to opencode.ai and publishes a public link; its docs page was removed (opencode.ai/docs/share/ answered 404 on 2026-10-30) and the key is documented only in the config schema, while the Enterprise page recommends disabling the share pages. Provider keys pasted with /connect sit in ~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json.

No vendor control plane governs the harness. A managed tier — opencode.json in /etc/opencode, /Library/Application Support/opencode or %ProgramData%\opencode, and the ai.opencode.managed macOS preference domain via MDM — outranks remote, global, project and inline config for the keys it sets. It is not a lock: OPENCODE_PERMISSION is merged after it in the current source, command-line flags beat the server settings, --auto approves every prompt, and a cloned repository's .opencode/ agents and plugins load without a trust prompt. The vendor's SECURITY.md says opencode does not sandbox the agent and that the permission system is a UX feature, not security isolation.

Enterprise controls are bolt-on: OpenCode Enterprise sells a central config with SSO and internal-gateway-only routing (no public reference), and OpenCode Zen team workspaces (beta) give admins member, API-key, model-access and monthly-spend controls over Zen traffic only.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Free and open source. Optional OpenCode Zen (pay-per-request gateway; team workspaces free during beta) and OpenCode Go ($10/month open-model subscription). OpenCode Enterprise is per-seat and sales-led (central config, SSO, internal AI gateway); no tokens are charged when the organisation's own gateway is used.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Remote or local, bring your own key: /connect or opencode auth login for any models.dev provider, environment variables or a project .env file; provider.<id>.options.baseURL points a provider at a proxy or gateway; enabled_providers / disabled_providers restrict which providers load (experimental.policies with provider.use is OpenCode 2 only and not enforced in OpenCode 1).

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: Prompts, context files and tool output to the model provider; the model catalogue from models.dev (OPENCODE_DISABLE_MODELS_FETCH); an update check at startup (autoupdate; nothing is installed automatically); npm plugin installs with Bun at startup; LSP server downloads (OPENCODE_DISABLE_LSP_DOWNLOAD); full conversations to opencode.ai when shared (share manual, auto or disabled in the config schema).

facts.label: Retention & training
facts.value: The vendor stores no code or context; shared conversations stay public until /unshare deletes them. Locally, session data sits under ~/.local/share/opencode/project/ and the last ten log files under ~/.local/share/opencode/log/. Training and retention are the provider's terms; Zen models are US-hosted with zero retention except named free models (used for training) and OpenAI and Anthropic (30 days).

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: opencode.ai/docs — Config, Permissions, Policies, Agents, Enterprise, Server, Web, Share, Network, MCP servers, Plugins, Rules, Troubleshooting, GitHub.

facts.label: Managed configuration
facts.value: opencode.json or opencode.jsonc in /Library/Application Support/opencode/, /etc/opencode/ or %ProgramData%\opencode (root/admin-writable), and a .mobileconfig with PayloadType ai.opencode.managed on macOS; highest priority, merged key by key; opencode debug config shows the resolved result.

facts.label: Security model
facts.value: No sandbox; the permission system is a UX feature; the server is unauthenticated unless OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD is set; malicious config files, MCP server behaviour and opted-in server access are out of scope for vulnerability reports.

facts.label: Distribution
facts.value: curl install script (to $OPENCODE_INSTALL_DIR, $XDG_BIN_DIR, ~/bin or ~/.opencode/bin), npm, Bun, pnpm, Yarn, Homebrew (anomalyco/tap/opencode or opencode), Scoop, Chocolatey, Arch, Mise and the ghcr.io/anomalyco/opencode image; the IDE extension installs itself when opencode runs in an IDE terminal. npm opencode-ai 1.18.32 carries registry signatures and no provenance attestation.

items.title: Config tiers and what the managed tier does not hold
body: Sources merge in order: remote .well-known/opencode defaults, ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json, OPENCODE_CONFIG, the project's opencode.json (found by walking up to the git root), .opencode directories, OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT, the managed files, then macOS managed preferences. Later sources override earlier ones only for the keys they set; instructions arrays are concatenated.

Outside the managed tier's reach: OPENCODE_PERMISSION (merged into permission after the managed files in packages/opencode/src/config/config.ts), --auto and the TUI's auto-approve toggle, --hostname / --port / --mdns (flags beat config), repository agents under .opencode/agents/ (agent rules outrank global rules) and repository plugins under .opencode/plugins/, which execute on load.

items.title: Server mode
body: opencode serve listens on 127.0.0.1:4096 by default, opencode web on 127.0.0.1 with a random port; --hostname 0.0.0.0 or --mdns exposes it to the network. The API can post prompts, run /session/:id/shell, answer permission requests and abort sessions. OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD (and OPENCODE_SERVER_USERNAME) turns on HTTP basic auth; there is no config key for it.

riskNotes.note: The local HTTP server is the harness's control surface (shell, PTY, file read, upgrade endpoints). CVE-2026-22812 (no authentication and permissive CORS), CVE-2026-22813 (web-UI XSS reaching /pty) and GHSA-632h-h47v-g4x4 (cross-site /global/upgrade installing an arbitrary npm package) each turned a web page into code execution. Password auth remains opt-in.

A cloned repository's .opencode/plugins/ run as code at startup with no trust prompt, and its opencode.json can add MCP servers and npm plugins that Bun installs on launch; SECURITY.md treats malicious config files as out of scope. The harness checks for updates at startup but installs one only when the developer runs /update or opencode upgrade.

Every permission defaults to allow except doom_loop and external_directory, there is no sandbox, and --auto approves every prompt that is not an explicit deny; the organisation cannot remove auto mode.

/share uploads the full conversation to opencode.ai and publishes it at a public link until unshared; share "auto" shares every session. Set share "disabled" in the managed file. Pasted keys sit in auth.json.

AGENTS.md (or CLAUDE.md) is read from the working directory upward, instructions accepts remote URLs, and a repository's .opencode/ adds agents, commands and skills — all without a trust prompt and with no content screening.
CVE-2026-22813: the web UI rendered model output as unsanitised HTML with no CSP, so a manipulated response ran script on the local API origin; fixed in 1.1.10.
With steps unset an agent iterates until the model stops or the user interrupts; the doom_loop guard asks after three identical calls, and --auto approves that prompt unless doom_loop is deny.

controls.mechanism: permission rules (allow / ask / deny per tool, with wildcard patterns over bash commands, file paths, subagent and skill names and MCP tool names; last match wins) in the managed opencode.json or the ai.opencode.managed plist, agent.<name>.permission for the built-in agents, and a managed npm plugin's tool.execute.before hook as an organisation-written attach point; the serve API kept on loopback (server.hostname "127.0.0.1", server.mdns false) behind OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD

steps.title: Ship the rules in the managed tier
body: Put a permission block in /etc/opencode/opencode.json, /Library/Application Support/opencode/opencode.json or %ProgramData%\opencode\opencode.json (or the ai.opencode.managed .mobileconfig): a catch-all "*" first, then deny patterns such as bash {"*": "ask", "rm *": "deny", "git push *": "deny"}.

steps.title: Cover every tool key
body: Write rules for read, edit, glob, grep, bash, task, skill, webfetch, websearch and external_directory, and "<server>_*" patterns for MCP tools; the last matching rule wins.

steps.title: Pin the agents as well
body: Repeat the rules under agent.build.permission, agent.plan.permission and any organisation agent in the managed file, because agent rules take precedence over the global block.

steps.title: Add a policy hook
body: List the organisation's npm plugin in the managed plugin array; its tool.execute.before hook receives each call's tool name and arguments and blocks the call by throwing.

steps.title: Keep the server on loopback
body: In the managed opencode.json (or the ai.opencode.managed plist) set server.hostname to "127.0.0.1" and server.mdns to false, so prompts and permission answers reach the serve API only from the device itself.

steps.title: Require the shared secret on every server launch
body: Set OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD (and OPENCODE_SERVER_USERNAME) in the environment of every process that runs opencode serve or opencode web, including launch scripts and the desktop and IDE clients that attach to it; without it the server answers unauthenticated.

controls.note: Partial on the drawing's tier rule: deterministic allow/ask/deny rules over tool name and arguments are evaluated by the harness before each built-in, custom and MCP tool call, and the managed tier outranks every other config file for the keys it sets, but the organisation cannot make them non-overridable. OPENCODE_PERMISSION (the CLI page's "inlined json permissions config") is merged after the managed tier in the current source, so a developer's environment rewrites any rule; agent rules outrank global rules and a repository can add a new agent under .opencode/agents/ with its own permission block; repository plugins load without a prompt and a plugin tool replaces a built-in of the same name; --auto turns every ask into allow. Bash patterns match parsed command text. The vendor's SECURITY.md calls the permission system a UX feature, not isolation. experimental.policies is not enforced in OpenCode 1 (the policies page, re-read 2026-10-30, says it requires OpenCode 2). Remote steering: the serve API admits any caller holding the basic-auth secret (anyone, if unset) to post prompts, run /session/:id/shell and answer permission requests; the password is an environment variable with no config key, and --hostname 0.0.0.0 or --mdns on the command line overrides a managed loopback hostname; GitHub comment triggers are permission-checked against the commenter (the GitHub page notes scheduled runs have no user to check).

controls.mechanism: A managed npm plugin's tool.execute.before (block by throwing) and tool.execute.after (rewrite the output) hooks as the attach point for an organisation inspector; permission.read patterns as minimisation; provider baseURL to route model traffic through an inspecting AI gateway; no vendor detection

steps.title: Wire an inspection plugin
body: Add the organisation's npm plugin to the managed plugin array; its tool.execute.before hook blocks calls whose arguments carry sensitive data and tool.execute.after replaces the tool output before the model reads it.

steps.title: Route model traffic through the gateway
body: Set provider.<id>.options.baseURL to the organisation's inspecting AI gateway and list only that provider in enabled_providers in the managed file.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: the tool-path hooks can block or mask, but opencode detects nothing itself; the inspector is organisation code running in-process on the device, alongside any plugins a repository ships. Content that enters without a tool call (the typed prompt, AGENTS.md, instruction files and URLs) is reachable only through the undocumented experimental.chat.messages.transform hook. The read rule's .env handling keeps named files out — minimisation, not detection; the permissions page says .env files are denied by default while the current source asks, so set the rule explicitly. The inline alternative is an AI gateway at the provider baseURL, or endpoint DLP. share "disabled" in the managed file stops whole conversations leaving for opencode.ai.

controls.mechanism: agent.<name>.steps (maximum agentic iterations) and subagent_depth in the managed opencode.json; the doom_loop permission (the same call repeated three times); OpenCode Zen workspace and per-member monthly usage limits for Zen traffic only

steps.title: Cap iterations per agent
body: In the managed file set agent.build.steps (and plan, general and every organisation agent); at the limit the agent is told to stop and summarise its work.

steps.title: Stop repeated calls and deep delegation
body: Set permission.doom_loop to "deny" (the default ask is approved by --auto) and subagent_depth to 1 or 0 in the managed file.

steps.title: Cap spend on the Zen path
body: As a Zen workspace admin set a monthly usage limit for the workspace and for each member, and turn auto-reload off.

controls.note: Partial: the harness limits one kind (iterations, per agent) and a cost ceiling exists only on the vendor's optional Zen gateway; there is no per-run token or cost budget. steps is unset by default — the agent iterates until the model stops or the user interrupts — and binds only the agents the managed file names; a repository's .opencode/agents/ definitions carry their own. Zen limits are monthly, stop Zen requests only, and auto-reload can charge past them; workspaces are beta. With a bring-your-own key the provider invoice or the organisation's gateway budget is the only meter, which is the drawing's pin. compaction and tool_output thresholds bound context size, not spend.

controls.mechanism: permission per tool (read, edit, glob, grep, bash, task, skill, webfetch, websearch, lsp and MCP tool-name patterns) with path and command patterns, external_directory for paths outside the working directory, agent.<name>.permission and subagent_depth, delivered in the managed opencode.json or the ai.opencode.managed plist

steps.title: Deliver grants in the managed tier
body: Place the permission block in the managed opencode.json (or the MDM plist) so user, project and inline config cannot override those keys, and check the result with opencode debug config.

steps.title: Scope to the working tree
body: Set external_directory {"*": "deny"} with explicit allows, edit patterns for the paths a task may change, and "<server>_*": "deny" for MCP servers a role must not use.

steps.title: Narrow per agent
body: Give each managed agent its own permission block (for example plan with edit deny) and set task rules for the subagents it may launch.

controls.note: Partial on the tier rule (Claude Code and Gemini CLI are native because their rules are admin-locked): per-tool grants with path and command patterns exist and the harness enforces them outside the model, but OPENCODE_PERMISSION, repository-defined agents and repository plugins can widen them, and --auto turns ask into allow (see action policy). Limits: bash patterns match command text and the vendor says the permission system is not isolation; the config schema gives webfetch and websearch a single action (no per-URL rule), although the permissions page says webfetch matches the URL; MCP tools are scoped by name, not arguments; every tool runs with the developer's own authority.

controls.mechanism: A VM or dev container the organisation supplies (the ghcr.io/anomalyco/opencode image is an install option); opencode ships no sandbox. Credential paths: kept out only by that boundary (no credential mounts); managed external_directory and read deny rules and a plugin's shell.env hook are the product's contributions

evidence.title: opencode SECURITY.md (No Sandbox)
opencode docs index (Docker install)
Permissions (external_directory, read defaults)
Plugins (shell.env)

controls.note: External: the vendor's SECURITY.md says opencode does not sandbox the agent, that the permission system is not designed to provide isolation, and that true isolation means running it in a Docker container or VM. Integration points: the ghcr.io/anomalyco/opencode image (docker run -it --rm on the docs index), an organisation dev container with only the workspace mounted, and managed external_directory deny rules as a tool-argument filter inside it. Otherwise every tool, MCP server, plugin and LSP server runs as the developer on the host. Credential paths: with no sandbox, bash inherits the developer's ssh-agent socket, git credential helper, ~/.aws, kube and cloud CLI configuration and browser profiles. Contributions: managed external_directory {"*": "deny"} and read deny patterns stop the file tools (and bash commands whose parsed arguments name those paths) reaching outside the workspace, and a managed plugin's shell.env hook can override variables in every shell execution; both are filters the vendor says are not isolation, and neither covers MCP servers or plugins. Routing models through a gateway key keeps upstream provider keys off the device; git, cloud CLIs and MCP servers still act as the developer.

controls.mechanism: edit ask/deny rules on AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, opencode.json and .opencode/** and snapshot true (per-session undo and revert) in the managed opencode.json; managed instructions added to every session; OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE; no agent-written memory store

steps.title: Gate writes to instruction and config files
body: In the managed permission block set edit patterns such as "**/AGENTS.md", "**/CLAUDE.md", "**/opencode.json" and ".opencode/**" to "ask" or "deny".

steps.title: Keep agent edits revertible
body: Set snapshot to true in the managed file so every change the agent makes can be undone or reverted from the session.

steps.title: Publish organisation rules centrally
body: List the organisation's rule files or URL in the managed instructions array; they load in every session next to the repository's AGENTS.md.

steps.title: Drop the Claude Code fallbacks
body: Export OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE=1 in the launch environment so ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md and .claude/skills are not read.

controls.note: Partial: writes can be gated and reverted, but instruction sources cannot be locked and nothing validates content. opencode has no agent-written memory; its persistent state is instruction files and session history under ~/.local/share/opencode/project/. AGENTS.md (or CLAUDE.md when none exists) loads from the working directory upward, ~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md and ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md load globally, instructions accepts globs and remote URLs, and a repository's .opencode/ adds agents, commands, skills, tools and plugins — none behind a trust prompt. Managed instructions are concatenated with the repository's, not substituted; OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE is an environment variable only. Edit rules cover the edit, write and patch tools, not bash, and yield to OPENCODE_PERMISSION; snapshots use an internal git repository.

controls.mechanism: A managed npm plugin's tool.execute.after hook (rewrites the output the model receives) as the attach point for an organisation classifier; no vendor screening

steps.title: Screen tool results
body: In the organisation's managed plugin, have tool.execute.after send read, webfetch, websearch, grep and MCP output to the classifier and replace flagged output before the model reads it.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: a post-tool hook that can replace output is an attach point; nothing is classified until the organisation attaches a classifier, and opencode documents no injection screening. The plugins page lists tool.execute.after; its writable output comes from the @opencode-ai/plugin types. AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, remote instruction URLs and skills enter context without a tool call, and repository plugins run alongside the organisation's. The external alternative is an AI gateway or MCP gateway classifier on the brokered path.

controls.mechanism: {env:VAR} and {file:path} substitution for provider apiKey; keys pasted with /connect or opencode auth login stored in ~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json; MCP OAuth tokens in ~/.local/share/opencode/mcp-auth.json; provider credential chains (AWS profiles and web identity for Bedrock, Azure CLI Entra ID); managed enabled_providers limited to the organisation's gateway provider

steps.title: Reference credentials, don't paste them
body: In the managed file set provider.<gateway>.options.apiKey to "{env:VAR}" or "{file:path}" pointing at a short-lived token the organisation's credential helper writes.

steps.title: Make other providers' keys inert
body: Set enabled_providers to the gateway's provider ID in the managed file so keys for any other provider are not loaded (experimental.policies is not enforced in OpenCode 1).

steps.title: Prefer short-lived cloud credentials
body: For Bedrock use the AWS credential chain (aws sso login profiles, EKS IRSA) rather than AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK, and for Azure choose Microsoft Entra ID (Azure CLI) in /connect.

controls.note: Partial: references and short-lived provider chains exist, but storage is not hardened and plaintext keys cannot be forbidden. /connect and opencode auth login write keys to auth.json (a 0600 file in the current source; no keychain), keys are also read from environment variables and a project's .env file, and a Bedrock bearer token outranks the AWS credential chain. enabled_providers makes keys for other providers inert but does not stop a developer pasting the gateway key itself. The Enterprise page's SSO-issued gateway credentials come with the sales-led central config and have no public reference. Keeping secrets away from agent commands is under D3-EI.

controls.mechanism: opencode-ai installed at a fixed version from the organisation's mirror (updates are never installed automatically); managed mcp.<name> definitions (command arrays naming a pinned package version, remote url) that outrank same-named project entries; a managed plugin list of pinned npm packages

steps.title: Pin the harness version
body: Install opencode-ai at a fixed version from the organisation's package mirror or artifact repository; the config page says updates are never installed automatically, and autoupdate false also stops the update check and notice.

steps.title: Define tool servers centrally
body: Define approved servers under mcp in the managed file, with local commands naming an exact package version (for example ["npx", "-y", "pkg@1.2.3"]).

controls.note: Partial by the rule applied to every vendor: definitions admit servers and pin nothing they serve. opencode hashes and re-verifies nothing: tool definitions refresh with the server, remote servers are unpinned, and a repository's opencode.json can add servers under new names or enable ones the .well-known defaults disable. The update channel only notifies: the config page (re-read 2026-10-30) says updates are never installed automatically and run only through /update or opencode upgrade, which a developer can still run on demand; the server's /global/upgrade endpoint installed arbitrary packages before 1.18.22 (GHSA-632h-h47v-g4x4). npm plugins install with Bun at every startup and the plugins page shows only unversioned specs. npm opencode-ai 1.18.32 has registry signatures but no provenance attestation.

controls.mechanism: permission "ask" rules in the managed opencode.json (once / always for the session / reject); doom_loop and external_directory ask by default; no key removes --auto or the TUI auto-approve toggle

steps.title: Deliver ask rules in the managed tier
body: In the managed opencode.json (or MDM plist) set "ask" for consequential actions, for example bash {"git push *": "ask", "npm publish *": "ask"} and edit "ask".

steps.title: Deny what must never run unattended
body: Use "deny" rather than "ask" for irreversible actions, because auto mode still enforces explicit deny rules.

controls.note: Partial on the tier rule (non-overridable approval): a present developer approves each matched call in a once / always / reject prompt, but the organisation cannot stop the switch to auto — --auto on opencode and opencode run, and the TUI's "Enable auto-approve permissions", approve every ask that is not an explicit deny, and no config key removes them (the current source also accepts --yolo and --dangerously-skip-permissions). "always" approves matching patterns for the rest of the session; OPENCODE_PERMISSION and repository agents can turn ask into allow; any serve client holding the basic-auth secret can answer POST /session/:id/permissions/:permissionID from another device; defaults allow almost everything. Rated below Claude Code and Gemini CLI (native), whose administrators can remove the bypass modes.

controls.mechanism: Managed mcp definitions plus a managed permission allowlist over tool names ("*": "deny" first, then "<server>_*": "allow" for approved servers); remote defaults from the organisation's .well-known/opencode endpoint; no registry

steps.title: Keep approved servers in the managed file
body: Define each approved MCP server under mcp in the managed opencode.json, which outranks project and user entries of the same name.

steps.title: Allow only listed servers' tools
body: In the managed permission block deny "*" first and then allow the built-in tools and each approved server's "<server>_*" pattern; MCP tools are named with the server as prefix.

controls.note: Partial by the rule: the nearest thing to an allowlist is a name-pattern permission list in a tier the developer can override (OPENCODE_PERMISSION, repository agents), with no owner, version or approval record. It admits tools by name, so a repository server whose name matches an allowed prefix passes. The .well-known/opencode remote config is organisation-hosted but supplies defaults every other tier overrides, not an enforced list. Plugins, custom tools and skills from npm or the repository sit outside any list, and plugins execute on load before any permission is consulted. An MCP gateway is the enforced registry; reconciliation against discovered installs is the governance platform's job.

controls.mechanism: Local logs (~/.local/share/opencode/log/, last ten files, --log-level) and session storage under ~/.local/share/opencode/project/; a managed plugin subscribing to tool.execute.before / after, permission.asked / replied and session events to ship records; experimental.openTelemetry (AI SDK spans) in the config schema only

steps.title: Ship tool and approval events
body: Have the organisation's managed plugin forward tool.execute.before and tool.execute.after (tool, arguments, session) and permission.replied events to the SIEM.

steps.title: Collect the local logs
body: Point the endpoint log agent at ~/.local/share/opencode/log/ (the ten most recent files are kept) and raise the level with --log-level where needed.

controls.note: Partial: the product writes local logs and session history the developer can delete, and export is organisation-written plugin code running in a process the developer controls, so capture is not tamper-resistant. No telemetry or OpenTelemetry export is documented; experimental.openTelemetry appears only in the config schema (AI SDK spans for model calls, not tool decisions) with no documented exporter setting. There is no vendor console and the vendor stores nothing unless /share is used. The gateway tap the drawing pins is the complete record for model traffic; local tool execution is visible only to the plugin or EDR.

controls.mechanism: EDR / MDM software inventory and SSE/CASB; the opencode binary and package names, config and data directories, the IDE extension ID and the default serve port are the integration points

evidence.title: opencode docs index (install methods)
Troubleshooting (storage locations)
IDE extension

controls.note: External: opencode has no account plane that reports installs (the Zen console sees only Zen keys). Find installs with EDR or MDM inventory: the opencode binary (~/.opencode/bin by default from the install script), npm opencode-ai, Homebrew anomalyco/tap/opencode or opencode, Scoop and Chocolatey opencode, the ghcr.io/anomalyco/opencode image, OpenCode Desktop, the VS Code extension sst-dev.opencode (installed automatically when opencode runs in an IDE terminal), and ~/.config/opencode, ~/.local/share/opencode and ~/.cache/opencode. On the network, SSE/CASB sees models.dev catalogue fetches, opncd.ai shares and Zen or Go traffic to opencode.ai; in repositories, the opencode-agent GitHub App and workflows using anomalyco/opencode/github.

controls.mechanism: EDR on the endpoint; the opencode process tree, its HTTP listener and a managed plugin's tool events are the integration points

evidence.title: Server (default port and endpoints)
Plugins (tool events)

controls.note: External (EDR): opencode analyses no process behaviour. EDR sees the opencode process and the shells it spawns for bash, stdio MCP server processes (often npx), downloaded LSP servers, Bun installs of plugins at startup, and the listener — 127.0.0.1:4096 by default for serve, a random port for web, 0.0.0.0 with --hostname or --mdns (advertised as opencode.local). There is no process-wrapper key; a launcher script on PATH is the nearest point. Correlate EDR events with a managed plugin's tool.execute.before records (command text, session ID).

controls.mechanism: Credential revocation at the organisation's AI gateway (on the Zen path, an admin removes the member or API key) plus an EDR process kill; POST /session/:id/abort is local to the device's server

evidence.title: Server (POST /session/:id/abort)
Zen (team roles and API keys)

controls.note: External: opencode offers no organisation-reachable stop. The server's POST /session/:id/abort stops a running session but only through the device's own listener. Revoking the key at the organisation's gateway — or, on Zen, an admin removing the member or API key (beta team workspaces) — fails the session's next model request; the delay is not documented and tool calls already dispatched complete. Keys pasted into auth.json must be rotated at each provider. An EDR kill of the opencode process tree is the stop for local work; no live policy refresh is documented, so managed config changes apply at the next start.

controls.mechanism: permission.webfetch and permission.websearch "deny" in the managed file (on/off for the fetch tools); managed enabled_providers with provider baseURL pinning model traffic to the organisation's gateway; share "disabled"; HTTPS_PROXY honoured

steps.title: Pin model traffic to the gateway
body: In the managed file set enabled_providers to the gateway's provider ID and its provider.<id>.options.baseURL to the gateway URL.

steps.title: Turn off the fetch tools
body: Set permission.webfetch and permission.websearch to "deny" in the managed file where browsing is not needed.

steps.title: Disable share uploads
body: Set share to "disabled" in the managed file so no conversation is synced to opencode.ai.

steps.title: Send the rest through the proxy
body: Export HTTPS_PROXY with NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1 (the TUI talks to its local server) and NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS for the organisation's CA.

controls.note: Partial on the drawing's rule for on/off controls: the harness's own named egress (model calls, the two fetch tools, share uploads) can be pinned or switched off from the managed tier, but there is no destination allowlist. bash (curl, git, package managers), MCP servers, plugins, LSP downloads and npm plugin installs reach the network with the host's routes; bash deny patterns match command text only; HTTPS_PROXY is an environment variable the developer controls and is routing until direct egress is blocked. The config schema gives webfetch no per-URL rule. The endpoint egress allowlist enforced by device management is the control the drawing pins.

controls.mechanism: Package mirror / artifact repository with malware scanning; integration points are the private npm registry in ~/.npmrc (honoured for plugin installs), the managed plugin array and installing opencode-ai itself from the mirror

evidence.title: Enterprise (private npm registry FAQ)
Plugins (npm install with Bun at startup)

controls.note: External: opencode scans nothing it downloads or installs. npm plugins install with Bun at startup (a .opencode/package.json triggers bun install too), stdio MCP servers commonly launch through npx, LSP servers download automatically unless OPENCODE_DISABLE_LSP_DOWNLOAD is set, and agent commands install packages at will. The enterprise page documents private registries (Artifactory, Nexus) through ~/.npmrc, the integration point for admission scanning at the mirror. No model files are loaded unless the developer points a provider at a local model server.

settings.name: Managed settings
settings.where: /Library/Application Support/opencode/, /etc/opencode/ or %ProgramData%\opencode → opencode.json; macOS ai.opencode.managed profile
settings.recommended: The keys below in a root-owned managed file on every developer device
settings.why: Managed keys win over remote, global, project and inline config, so a cloned repository's opencode.json cannot loosen them.

settings.name: permission.bash
settings.where: managed opencode.json → permission.bash
settings.recommended: "*": "ask", with "allow" for read-only commands (git status *, ls *) and "deny" for rm -rf * and git push --force *
settings.why: Every other shell command waits for approval, and deny rules hold even under --auto.

settings.name: permission.edit
settings.where: managed opencode.json → permission.edit
settings.recommended: "*": "ask", with "deny" for opencode.json, AGENTS.md and .opencode/**
settings.why: Each write shows for approval, and the agent cannot rewrite its own config, instructions or plugins.

settings.name: permission.read
settings.where: managed opencode.json → permission.read
settings.recommended: "allow", with "deny" for *.env and *.env.* (*.env.example allowed)
settings.why: Project secrets never enter the context, even when a developer runs --auto, which turns the default ask into allow.

settings.name: permission.external_directory
settings.where: managed opencode.json → permission.external_directory
settings.recommended: "ask" — no allow entries for the home directory
settings.why: Any tool touching a path outside the working directory, ~/.ssh and ~/.aws included, needs a click; allowed paths inherit read allow.

settings.name: permission.doom_loop
settings.where: managed opencode.json → permission.doom_loop
settings.recommended: "deny"
settings.why: The same call repeated three times with identical input is stopped outright, which --auto cannot approve.

settings.name: permission.webfetch
settings.where: managed opencode.json → permission.webfetch (and permission.websearch)
settings.recommended: "allow"
settings.why: Web fetch is why people use the tool; it is one switch for all URLs, so regulated teams set "deny" and fetch through approved MCP servers instead.

settings.name: steps
settings.where: managed opencode.json → agent.build.steps (and agent.plan.steps)
settings.default: Unset (the agent iterates until the model stops or the user interrupts)
settings.recommended: A ceiling such as 100
settings.why: At the limit the agent must summarise and stop, so a runaway loop ends without someone watching it.

settings.name: subagent_depth
settings.where: managed opencode.json → subagent_depth
settings.why: Subagents cannot launch further subagents, which bounds fan-out and the tool authority each run inherits.

settings.name: enabled_providers
settings.where: managed opencode.json → enabled_providers
settings.recommended: The organisation gateway's provider id only
settings.why: Keys for any other provider, from /connect, the environment or a project .env, are not loaded, so prompts go only where the organisation inspects them.

settings.name: baseURL
settings.where: managed opencode.json → provider.<id>.options.baseURL
settings.recommended: The organisation's AI gateway URL
settings.why: Model traffic passes the gateway's DLP, injection screening and budgets before any provider sees it.

settings.name: apiKey
settings.where: managed opencode.json → provider.<id>.options.apiKey
settings.recommended: "{env:VAR}" or "{file:path}" pointing at a short-lived gateway token the credential helper writes
settings.why: No long-lived key is written into config or auth.json; a developer can still paste a key, so the gateway should reject long-lived ones.

settings.name: mcp
settings.where: managed opencode.json → mcp.<name>
settings.recommended: The approved servers, local commands naming an exact package version
settings.why: Managed definitions outrank same-named project entries, so a repository cannot repoint an approved server; it can still add servers under new names.

settings.name: plugin
settings.where: managed opencode.json → plugin
settings.recommended: The organisation's audit and inspection plugin and approved packages at pinned versions, from the private npm registry
settings.why: Its tool.execute.before and after hooks are where tool calls are logged and inspected; repository .opencode/plugins still load without a prompt.

settings.name: share
settings.where: managed opencode.json → share
settings.recommended: "disabled"
settings.why: No session is uploaded to opencode.ai and published at a public link; the vendor's enterprise page also recommends disabling the share pages.

settings.name: snapshot
settings.where: managed opencode.json → snapshot
settings.recommended: true
settings.why: Agent edits, to instruction and config files included, can be undone and reverted within the session.

settings.name: server.hostname
settings.where: managed opencode.json → server.hostname (and server.mdns)
settings.default: 127.0.0.1 (0.0.0.0 when mdns is on and no hostname is set); mdns false
settings.recommended: 127.0.0.1, mdns false
settings.why: The local server can post prompts and run shell commands, so it stays off the network; --hostname on the command line still overrides it.

settings.name: OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD
settings.where: environment variable OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD for opencode serve and opencode web
settings.recommended: A random per-launch secret set by the wrapper that starts the server
settings.why: A web page or local process cannot drive the server's shell and PTY endpoints without it, the path behind CVE-2026-22812.

settings.name: --auto
settings.where: opencode --auto, opencode run --auto, or the TUI's Enable auto-approve permissions
settings.recommended: Not used; the deny rules above cover what must never run
settings.why: Auto mode approves every request that is not an explicit deny, and no config key removes it.

advisories.title: GHSA-632h-h47v-g4x4: cross-site /global/upgrade request on opencode serve installs an arbitrary npm package for npm-managed installs (CVSS 7.5); opencode-ai >= 1.14.30, fixed 1.18.22
CVE-2026-22813 (GHSA-c83v-7274-4vgp): web-UI XSS via the server URL override lets a website run commands through the /pty endpoints (critical); fixed 1.1.10
CVE-2026-22812 (GHSA-vxw4-wv6m-9hhh): unauthenticated HTTP server with permissive CORS allows any local process or website to execute commands (CVSS 8.8); fixed 1.0.216

tools.name: Salesforce Agentforce (agents built in Agentforce Builder, with subagents, actions, Data Library grounding and channels)

variants.name: New Agentforce Builder (Agentforce Studio app; Canvas and Script views, Agent Script)
variants.note: Lives outside Setup and is reachable by any user with the Manage AI Agents permission, which grants org-wide management, activation and deactivation of every agent.

variants.name: Legacy Agentforce Builder (Setup > Agentforce Agents)
variants.note: The original visual subagent editor; filters on subagents and actions and the Agent Access tab are documented here first.

summary: Salesforce's CRM-embedded agent builder: makers assemble agents from subagents (formerly topics), instructions and actions (flows, Apex, prompt templates, MCP tools, MuleSoft API Catalog APIs), ground them on CRM records, Data 360 and Agentforce Data Libraries (Knowledge, uploaded files), and deploy them to Lightning Experience, Slack, Enhanced Chat and messaging, email, voice and the Agent API. Agents run in Salesforce's cloud through the Einstein generative AI platform, which calls OpenAI or Azure OpenAI, Anthropic on Amazon Bedrock, Gemini on Vertex AI or Salesforce-hosted models under zero-data-retention agreements; Einstein Trust Layer data masking is disabled for agents, so grounding reaches the model unmasked.

The administrator is the Salesforce org administrator in Setup: Einstein Setup (Turn on Einstein, Configure Model Providers, Enable In-Region Model Requests Only), Einstein Trust Layer (Safety & Security), Einstein Audit, Analytics, and Monitoring Setup (Audit and Feedback, Agentforce Session Tracing), Agentforce Registry and Agentforce Gateway policies, Named and External Credentials, permission sets (Enabled Agent Access, Manage AI Agents) and the agent user. Who an agent runs as is fixed by its type: Employee agents act as the logged-in user, Service agents as a dedicated agent user.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited and Developer Editions; required add-on licences vary by agent type (Agentforce Gateway needs Foundations or Agentforce 1 Editions). Priced by consumption (Flex Credits per agent action), hybrid per-user licensing, or business metrics; Session Tracing, Audit and Feedback and Data Libraries also consume Data 360 credits.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Einstein generative AI platform routes to OpenAI or Azure OpenAI, Anthropic on Amazon Bedrock and Gemini on Vertex AI in the region of the org's Data 360 instance, falling back to other regions unless Enable In-Region Model Requests Only is on in Einstein Setup; Salesforce-hosted models keep data inside the Salesforce trust boundary. Providers are toggled at Einstein Setup > Configure Model Providers.

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: Agent turns carry CRM, Data 360 and Data Library grounding to the model provider unmasked (Trust Layer masking is disabled for agents, including prompt templates called through agent actions). Actions call external systems from Salesforce's cloud through named credentials, Agentforce Registry MCP servers or MuleSoft API connections.

facts.label: Retention & training
facts.value: Third-party LLMs retain nothing and do not train on it (zero data retention; no human review at the provider unless Salesforce grants it for suspected abuse). Audit and Feedback and Session Tracing data are stored in a Data 360 data space in the org until deleted; enhanced event logs are kept seven days; Salesforce notes that agents may store data.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: help.salesforce.com "Agentforce and Einstein Generative AI"; Agentforce Developer Guide (developer.salesforce.com/docs/ai/agentforce)

facts.label: Run-as identity by agent type
facts.value: Employee agents (Lightning Experience, mobile, Slack, Experience Cloud) run as the logged-in user. Service agents (Enhanced Chat, messaging channels) run as the agent user (EinsteinServiceAgent User) unless credential-based user verification is on for Enhanced Chat on an Experience Cloud site. Lead Nurturing agents run as the EinsteinSDRAgent User. Flow actions add their own run context (user, system with sharing, system without sharing).

facts.label: Agent API
facts.value: REST sessions against an agent through an external client app with the client credentials flow; every call runs as the app's Run As user. Not supported for Agentforce (Default).

facts.label: Pro-code shell (Agentforce DX)
facts.value: Salesforce CLI and VS Code commands author, preview, test, retrieve, deploy, activate and deactivate the same agent metadata (Bot, BotVersion, GenAiPlannerBundle, GenAiPlugin, GenAiFunction, AiAuthoringBundle); no admin surface of its own.

facts.label: Agentforce platform toggle
facts.value: Salesforce plans to turn on the Agentforce platform for all orgs with Agentforce access in August 2026 and remove the Agentforce toggle from the Agentforce Agents Setup page.

items.title: Where each control lives
body: Setup: Einstein Setup (Turn on Einstein, Configure Model Providers, Enable In-Region Model Requests Only), Einstein Trust Layer (Data Masking and Safety & Security tabs), Einstein Audit, Analytics, and Monitoring Setup (Audit and Feedback, Agentforce Session Tracing), Agentforce Registry (MCP servers, tools, policies), Policies (Agentforce Gateway Policy Builder), Agentforce Data Library, Named Credentials and External Credentials, External Client Apps Manager, Users (agent users), Permission Sets (Enabled Agent Access, Manage AI Agents), View Setup Audit Trail. Agentforce Studio app: Agents list, Agentforce Builder (Agent Access, Script view config block), Testing Center.

items.title: What the Trust Layer does and does not do for agents
body: For agents the Trust Layer contributes zero data retention with external providers, secure data retrieval with the running user's permissions, system policies and beta prompt-injection scoring, toxicity scoring, and the Data 360 audit trail. Pattern-based and field-based data masking is disabled for agents; it still applies to prompt templates used directly in embedded features.

riskNotes.note: Agentforce never lends the maker's credentials, but it lends shared service identities instead: Service agents answer unidentified customers as the agent user, the Agent API runs as one Run As user, and MCP servers accept only OAuth client credentials, so every consumer inherits that identity's reach. Flow actions in system context without sharing reach all objects regardless of who asked.

Agentforce Studio is in the App Launcher for every user by default, and Manage AI Agents grants org-wide management and activation of all agents; the agent record carries no documented owner field, so an agent outlives its builder unless someone queries BotDefinition.

Public-write objects are an instruction channel: ForcedLeak (2025) and SalesBleed (2026) both planted instructions in Web-to-Lead submissions that an internal user's agent later read, and exfiltrated CRM data through URL rendering; both were fixed server-side in Trusted URLs enforcement. Prompt injection detection is beta and scores rather than blocks.

Trust Layer masking is off for agents, and a Service agent published to an unauthenticated channel answers with everything its agent user can read; session-trace and audit data in Data 360 hold PII and are readable by System Administrators under the default Allow All data-space policy.

Grounding leaves unmasked for OpenAI or Azure OpenAI, Anthropic on Bedrock or Gemini on Vertex under zero-data-retention terms, and requests fall back to another region unless Enable In-Region Model Requests Only is on.

controls.mechanism: Agent type fixes whose authority an agent uses (Employee agents: the logged-in user; Service agents: the agent user unless credential-based user verification is on; Agent API: the external client app's Run As user); Enabled Agent Access on permission sets or profiles scopes who may use each Employee agent; the Manage AI Agents permission scopes who may build and activate

steps.title: Scope who may use each Employee agent
body: In Agentforce Builder open the agent, go to Settings > Agent Access and add only the permission sets that should reach it (or edit Enabled Agent Access on the permission set in Setup); on Experience Cloud sites use a permission set, not the shared profile.

steps.title: Keep each Service agent user least-privilege
body: In Setup > Users find the EinsteinServiceAgent User (Einstein Agent User profile) and grant only the objects its actions need on the [Agent_Name]_Permissions permission set; only administrators can view or edit agent users.

steps.title: Require verification before private actions
body: In the agent's Context panel > Filters create a filter on verification variables and apply it to every subagent and action that acts for a customer; on Enhanced Chat deployed to an Experience Cloud site turn on credential-based user verification so the agent runs as the logged-in site user.

steps.title: Limit the builder permission
body: Assign Manage AI Agents only to people who need org-wide management of all agents, and control who sees the Agentforce Studio app through its profile assignments.

controls.note: Partial on the authorisation rule; toolCopilotStudio is native because a tenant data policy can force authentication on every channel and remove maker credentials. Agentforce never runs an agent on the maker's credentials: Employee agents run as the invoking user (profile, permission sets, field-level security, sharing), and the administrator scopes who may use each Employee agent. But nothing org-wide forces end-user authentication: Service agents on messaging channels answer unidentified users as the agent user by design, credential-based user verification exists only for Enhanced Chat on Experience Cloud sites, and verification filters are set per agent by whoever holds Manage AI Agents. The agent user, the Agent API Run As user and MCP servers (OAuth 2.0 client credentials only; user-level authentication unsupported) are shared service identities every consumer inherits; they are administrator-owned rather than maker-owned, which bounds but does not remove the confused-deputy case.

controls.mechanism: Service and Lead Nurturing agents run as a dedicated agent user (a User record with the Einstein Agent licence, Einstein Agent User profile and an [Agent_Name]_Permissions permission set) created or selected when the agent is made; Employee agents have no principal of their own

steps.title: Mint one agent user per Service agent
body: When creating each Service agent create a new agent user rather than selecting an existing one, set its first name to the agent's name, and keep a Users list view filtered on the Einstein Agent User profile.

steps.title: Bind permissions to that principal only
body: Grant the agent's access on its own [Agent_Name]_Permissions permission set (associated with the Einstein Agent licence and profile), never on a set shared with people.

steps.title: Reassign the agent user after every deployment
body: Deployed agent metadata carries the source org's username; set the target org's agent user by string replacement on a draft, or create a new version of a committed agent and assign it there.

controls.note: Partial on the agent-identity rule, the same word as toolCopilotStudio. A Service agent can have its own principal in the org's directory, whose permission sets and sharing attach to that one agent and which only administrators can edit. But one agent user can be selected for several agents; Employee agents, the internal default, have no identity of their own and act entirely as the invoking user; the agent user is not an identity in the corporate IdP, so conditional access, ownership transfer and token issuance for it are not documented; the BotDefinition Id is a record key, not a principal. MuleSoft Agent Fabric's Trusted Agent Identity (announced GA 2026-04-15) is a gateway feature of another product and is not assessed here.

controls.mechanism: The org's agent metadata as inventory: the Agents list in Agentforce Studio (and Setup > Agentforce Agents), the BotDefinition object, and Metadata API retrieval of every agent and version (Bot, BotVersion, GenAiPlannerBundle, GenAiPlugin, GenAiFunction) with its actions and run-as username; Setup > Agentforce Registry for MCP servers with a per-tool allowlist and risk score

steps.title: Query the agent population
body: Query the BotDefinition object with SOQL for the agent list, and retrieve every agent and version with a package.xml member of * to read each agent's actions and agent username.

steps.title: Retrieve the definitions as source
body: Retrieve with Salesforce CLI using a manifest member of MyAgent#* (all versions) into a DX project so the inventory is diffable in version control.

steps.title: Register and allowlist MCP servers
body: In Setup > Agentforce Registry > New register each MCP server, read its risk score, and allowlist only the tools you trust; agents can call only allowlisted tools.

controls.note: Partial on the registry rule; toolCopilotStudio is native because its inventory carries owner and per-connector credential mode with block and quarantine. Every Agentforce agent is org metadata, so the platform's list is authoritative for this org and queryable, and an MCP server must be registered, scanned for tool poisoning and allowlisted per tool before an agent can call it. Missing: no documented owner, approval-state or credential-mode field on the agent record (run-as follows from agent type and the agent username in metadata; a named credential's principal type sits on the external credential, not the agent); MCP registrations are not packaged between orgs; the enforcement lever is deactivation, not a registry that denies unregistered agents; the risk score is advisory. Agents in other orgs and vendors are outside it (MuleSoft Agent Fabric's registry is the cross-platform product).

controls.mechanism: Agent versions (commit an immutable snapshot, create drafts, compare, one active version), Testing Center batch tests in a sandbox, sandbox-to-production promotion through Metadata API and Salesforce CLI, Enabled Agent Access for a limited first audience, and Activate/Deactivate of a committed version as release and rollback

steps.title: Test in a sandbox
body: Run Testing Center suites (generated from subagents, actions and knowledge, or uploaded) in a sandbox only, because test runs can modify CRM data.

steps.title: Promote by metadata, not by editing production
body: Retrieve the committed version (MyAgent#2) from the sandbox and deploy it to production with Salesforce CLI, keeping the DX project in version control as the source of truth.

steps.title: Release to a pilot audience first
body: On an Employee agent's Agent Access page add only a pilot permission set before widening access.

steps.title: Roll back by activating the prior version
body: In Agentforce Builder select the earlier committed version from the header and click Activate; the current version is deactivated automatically.

controls.note: Partial on the rollout rule, the same word as toolCopilotStudio. Met: versioning (committed versions are immutable metadata snapshots; drafts and compare), promotion through metadata so production can be kept deploy-only, a limited first audience for Employee agents, and rollback by activating an earlier committed version. Not met: no approval step; anyone holding Manage AI Agents can commit and activate any agent directly in production, so the gate exists only where the administrator withholds that permission in production; Testing Center scores do not block activation; no canary or percentage release, and none for Service agents on public channels. MCP registrations are not packaged and the agent user must be reassigned in the target org.

controls.mechanism: Setup > Einstein Trust Layer > Safety & Security > prompt injection detection (Beta), an org-level toggle whose scores are logged to the audit trail in Data 360; built-in system policies (always on); MCP Risk Score on tool descriptions at registration

steps.title: Turn on prompt injection detection
body: From Setup open Einstein Trust Layer, click Safety & Security, accept the beta service terms and turn on prompt injection detection (needs View Setup and Customize Application).

steps.title: Collect the detections as events
body: In Einstein Audit, Analytics, and Monitoring Setup turn Audit and Feedback on and alert on prompt injection scores from the Data 360 DMOs.

steps.title: Screen MCP tool descriptions before allowlisting
body: Refuse tools with a High (red) risk score or with the bidirectional, invisible or mixed-script characters warning shown during registration.

evidence.title: Set Up Einstein Trust Layer prompt injection detection (Salesforce Help; client-rendered, not readable 2026-10-30)
Agentforce Developer Guide — Trust Layer (no injection-detection setting listed)

controls.note: Unknown since 2026-10-30: the earlier partial rating rested on the Safety & Security prompt injection detection toggle, read in a browser on 2026-09-25. On 2026-10-30 help.salesforce.com returned only its loading shell to automated fetch, and no developer.salesforce.com or Trailhead page names the toggle, so the setting could not be re-verified and the settings table carries no row for it. Re-read the Help page in a browser; if the toggle is unchanged, restore partial and add the row. The earlier finding, kept for that re-check: the administrator can switch on an org-wide classifier that covers direct injection and injection arriving indirectly through data sources included in the prompt (role-play, rule changes, prompt leakage, encoding, privacy and malicious-code attacks), but it is beta and documented as scoring and logging to the audit trail, not blocking or stripping the flagged content, so the model still reasons over it. System policies are always on and not configurable. The MCP risk score scans tool descriptions once, at registration, and is a recommendation. Trusted URLs enforcement, the server-side fix for ForcedLeak and SalesBleed, limits where output may send data, not what enters context. Grounding that crosses our tier is screened at our gateway.

controls.mechanism: Trust and Compliance Documentation (Einstein Platform SPARC, Data 360 SPARC, Infrastructure & Sub-processors) and the compliance portal feed the organisation's TPRM platform

evidence.title: Salesforce Trust and Compliance Documentation (Einstein Platform SPARC, Data 360 SPARC, I&S)
Salesforce Compliance portal (certifications and reports, login required)
Einstein Trust Layer (zero data retention with model providers)

controls.note: External: the assessment, evidence expiry and reassessment trigger live in the organisation's TPRM platform, as for every vendor. Salesforce publishes per-service Trust and Compliance Documentation, the Einstein Platform SPARC (2026-07-24, covering the Employee, Service and SDR agents), the Data 360 SPARC and the Infrastructure & Sub-processors list (both 2026-09-22); certification reports sit behind a login on compliance.salesforce.com and were not read. Model subprocessors are OpenAI or Azure OpenAI, Anthropic on Amazon Bedrock and Gemini on Vertex AI under zero-data-retention agreements. Re-assess when a model provider is enabled, when MCP servers or MuleSoft APIs are connected, and after disclosures of the ForcedLeak and SalesBleed class.

controls.mechanism: Agentforce Gateway policies (Setup > Policies > Policy Builder): MCP Attribute-Based Access Control allows or blocks MCP tools by name for target agents and Restrictive Access limits HTTP methods and paths on MuleSoft API Catalog connections; the Agentforce Registry tool allowlist; the agent user's object and field permissions; subagent and action filters

steps.title: Allowlist tools per MCP server
body: In Setup > Agentforce Registry open the server, go to Tools > Edit Tools and keep only the tools agents need.

steps.title: Restrict tools per agent at the gateway
body: Create a policy from the MCP Attribute-Based Access Control template that allows or blocks named tools, then on the Agents tab choose Specific agents (select at least one, or it is not enforced).

steps.title: Restrict API methods and paths
body: For API connections apply a Restrictive Access policy listing the HTTP methods and paths agents may not call, with a Quota Management policy per agent.

steps.title: Bound CRM operations by the running user
body: Grant a Service agent's agent user only the object permissions its actions need on [Agent_Name]_Permissions; Employee agents inherit the invoking user's.

controls.note: Partial on the tool-permission rule; toolCopilotStudio is native because its data policies classify every connector and refuse a confidential-plus-exfiltration combination at publish. Agentforce has real per-principal, per-operation restriction enforced outside the model: tool allowlists per MCP server, per-agent allow and block of MCP tools and HTTP method and path limits on API connections at Agentforce Gateway, and CRM object and field access bounded by the running user. It has no connector classification and no combination rule, so nothing stops an agent that reads confidential CRM data from also holding an action that sends data out. Gateway policies apply only to committed or active agents, not drafts. Flow actions running in system context without sharing reach all objects whatever the running user holds.

controls.mechanism: No on-premises data gateway: private systems are reached through Named Credentials with External Credentials (tokens encrypted in the User External Credential object; principals linked to permission sets and checked at run time), over Private Connect (AWS PrivateLink, add-on) or a public endpoint; MCP registration creates the named credential, external credential and permission set itself

steps.title: Put every connection behind an external credential
body: In Setup > Named Credentials create an external credential for the authentication protocol and a named credential for the endpoint, and grant the principal through a dedicated permission set.

steps.title: Keep private traffic off the internet
body: For systems in AWS, set up a Private Connect outbound connection from the org to the VPC and point the named credential at it.

steps.title: Revoke centrally
body: Remove the permission set that links the external credential principal to the agent user (or edit the external credential's secret); callouts are refused at run time without redeploying anything.

controls.note: Partial on the credential rule, the same word as toolCopilotStudio. Salesforce offers no on-premises data gateway or relay host: the drawing's tunnel is either Private Connect (a Salesforce-managed PrivateLink to our AWS VPC; AWS only) or an internet-facing endpoint of ours, so no connection credential is cached on a host we run and the whole custody question sits with Salesforce. There, external credentials keep authentication out of Apex and flow definitions, store tokens encrypted per user, and admit a callout only when the running user holds the principal's permission set, so a connection is revocable centrally. Not documented on the pages read: rotation schedules or short-lived issuance for client secrets; MCP servers support OAuth 2.0 client credentials only, one standing secret per server. A relay we place ourselves is our custody, not Salesforce's.

controls.mechanism: Secure data retrieval grounds prompts with the running user's profile, permissions, field-level security and sharing (the invoking user for Employee agents, the agent user for Service agents); Agentforce Data Library setup requires Data Cloud admin and System Administrator permissions, and Knowledge libraries index only published articles, optionally public ones or selected data categories

steps.title: Keep grounding sources an administrator decision
body: Assign Data Cloud admin and System Administrator only to administrators, so makers cannot create or edit Agentforce Data Libraries.

steps.title: Scope Knowledge libraries
body: Under Knowledge Settings enable Use Public Knowledge Articles or Filter by Knowledge Data Categories so only articles meant for the agent's audience are indexed.

steps.title: Run reads as the invoker where possible
body: Use Employee agents for internal users and credential-based user verification for Enhanced Chat on Experience Cloud sites; otherwise the agent user's grants decide every read.

controls.note: Partial on the retrieval rule; toolCopilotStudio is native because its SharePoint grounding is documented as trimmed to the invoking user. Agentforce meets the administrator half (makers cannot create Data Libraries; Knowledge libraries are limited to published articles with public-only and data-category filters) and the identity half for CRM and Data 360 grounding reached by Employee agents, which run as the logged-in user. Not met: Service agents read with the agent user's grants rather than the customer's; the Data Library index (Knowledge, uploaded files) is not documented as trimmed per invoker; flows in system context without sharing reach all objects. Oversharing remediation in the indexed sources is ours. Nothing inspects knowledge a maker uploads: Einstein Trust Layer data masking is documented as disabled for agents, so what may be uploaded is decided before publication, and file_upload mode disabled in an agent's Script view config block refuses consumer uploads.

controls.mechanism: Einstein Audit, Analytics, and Monitoring Setup: Agentforce Session Tracing (turn-by-turn interactions, reasoning-engine executions, actions, prompt and gateway inputs and outputs, errors) and Audit and Feedback stream to DMOs in a Data 360 data space; AiAgentSessionLog adds Tool, LLM, Retrieval, Guardrail, Auth and Delegation events; per-agent enhanced event logs keep seven days

steps.title: Turn on Session Tracing org-wide
body: From Setup open Einstein Audit, Analytics, and Monitoring Setup, turn Agentforce Session Tracing on and select the target data space (Standard Data Model 1.130 or later).

steps.title: Turn on Audit and Feedback
body: On the same page turn Audit and Feedback on to store prompts, responses and trust-layer scores in Data 360.

steps.title: Query the trace model
body: Build detections on the AIAgentSession, AIAgentInteraction, AIAgentInteractionStep, AIAgentInteractionMessage and AiAgentSessionLog DMOs, joined on session and trace ids.

steps.title: Protect the trace data
body: Apply data-space permissions and Data 360 Dynamic Data Masking, and delete or narrow the default Allow All policy that lets System Administrators query every DMO.

controls.note: Partial on the tracing rule, the same word as toolCopilotStudio for the opposite gap. The run half is complete: an administrator-set, org-wide switch captures every agent's sessions per step, including actions, prompt and model-gateway inputs and outputs, errors and delegation between agents, into our own Data 360 data space within minutes, queryable and correlated by trace id. The maker half is missing: Setup Audit Trail lists permission-set, profile and user changes (so Agent Access grants are audited) but not agent, subagent or action edits, and no maker event for committing or activating an agent is documented; committed versions in metadata are the only history. Data stays in Data 360 unless we export it; tracing is off by default in orgs with more than one data space and consumes Data 360 credits.

controls.mechanism: Deactivate on the agent in Agentforce Builder (or the Salesforce CLI agent deactivate command) takes it out of service and interrupts ongoing conversations; Einstein Setup > Configure Model Providers turns providers off org-wide (up to ten minutes); connections are cut per MCP tool allowlist, Gateway block policy or external credential principal

steps.title: Deactivate the agent
body: From the Agents page of Agentforce Studio open the agent and click Deactivate (or run the Salesforce CLI agent deactivate command from a pipeline); ongoing conversations are interrupted.

steps.title: Cut its tools
body: In Setup > Agentforce Registry remove the agent's MCP tools from the allowlist, or apply a Gateway MCP Attribute-Based Access Control policy that blocks them for that agent.

steps.title: Revoke its credentials
body: Remove the permission set that grants the external credential principal to the agent user so its named-credential callouts fail.

steps.title: Stop generative AI org-wide
body: In Einstein Setup > Configure Model Providers turn off the providers; affected agents stop within up to ten minutes, along with every other generative AI feature on them.

controls.note: Partial on the kill-switch rule, the same word as toolCopilotStudio for a different gap. The per-agent stop is documented in full: deactivation interrupts ongoing conversations at once (the agent returns the system error message, and an Enhanced Chat window stays open without the agent), and the CLI can do it. Missing is a documented org-wide agent stop: the Agentforce toggle is being removed from the Agentforce Agents page from August 2026, and the remaining lever, turning off model providers, "can stop" agents after up to ten minutes and takes every other generative AI feature with it. Revocation is per connection with no bulk revoke, Employee agents hold no credential of their own, and cancellation of flows or Apex already dispatched by an action is not documented. Every holder of Manage AI Agents can deactivate and reactivate any agent.

settings.name: Agent Access (Enabled Agents)
settings.where: Setup › Permission Sets › (permission set) › Apps › Agent Access › Enabled Agents
settings.default: No one, administrators included, can use an Employee agent until granted
settings.recommended: One permission set per Employee agent, assigned to the groups whose work needs it, a pilot group first
settings.why: Who can use each internal agent is a grant someone made and can audit, and a new agent reaches a small group before everyone.

settings.name: default_agent_user
settings.where: Agent Script › access block › default_agent_user (the agent user created in Setup › Users)
settings.recommended: A dedicated agent user for each Service agent, holding only that agent's permission sets
settings.why: A Service agent answers customers with its own principal's access, not a shared user's, and its grants can be reviewed on their own.

settings.name: Agent user (target org)
settings.where: Target org › Setup › Users › agent user › permission sets deployed with the agent
settings.recommended: Created in each target org and given only the deployed permission sets
settings.why: The agent in production runs with the access tested in the sandbox, not with whatever a reused user already had.

settings.name: available when
settings.where: Agent Script › subagent and action definitions › available when (verification variables)
settings.recommended: Every subagent and action that reads or changes a customer's records gated on a verified flag
settings.why: The model cannot call an action, however it is talked to, until the customer has been verified; prompt instructions alone can be argued around.

settings.name: file_upload › mode
settings.where: Agent Script › config block › file_upload
settings.recommended: error, with a message, on every agent with no file use case
settings.why: Customers cannot hand an agent files it then reads and reasons over when nobody designed it to take them.

settings.name: runtime › thought_chunks
settings.where: Agent Script › config block › runtime
settings.recommended: False on customer-facing channels
settings.why: The agent's internal reasoning, which can carry instructions and retrieved data, is not streamed to the customer.

settings.name: Agentforce Registry
settings.where: Setup › Agentforce Registry › register server › select the tools available in Agentforce
settings.recommended: Every external MCP server registered by an administrator, with only the tools agents need selected
settings.why: Agents reach only servers and tools someone has registered and chosen, and a server-side change prompts a re-review of the registration.

settings.name: Authentication protocol (OAuth 2.0, external (named) credentials, or No Authentication)
settings.where: Agentforce Registry › register server › authentication
settings.recommended: External (named) credentials or OAuth 2.0; never No Authentication
settings.why: The secret for each server lives in Salesforce's credential store, not in the agent, and an unauthenticated server cannot be registered by habit.

settings.name: Add to Allowlist
settings.where: Setup › API Catalog › MCP Server › (server) › discovered tools
settings.recommended: Only the tools an agent script uses
settings.why: MuleSoft and Salesforce MCP tools become usable in Agent Script only after an administrator allowlists them.

settings.name: Agentforce Gateway (MCP usage policies)
settings.where: Setup › Agentforce Gateway › policies for specific agents and tools
settings.recommended: A per-agent tool policy and a call quota on every MCP server in use
settings.why: Which agent may call which server tool, and how often, is enforced at the gateway rather than left to the prompt.

settings.name: Run As (Username)
settings.where: Setup › External Client Apps Manager › (Agent API app) › Policy › OAuth Flows and External Client App Enhancements
settings.recommended: A dedicated API Only user per integration, with only the agent's permissions
settings.why: Every Agent API call runs as this user, so a leaked app credential reaches one narrowly scoped identity, not an administrator.

settings.name: Consumer Key and Secret
settings.where: External Client Apps Manager › (Agent API app) › Settings › OAuth Settings
settings.recommended: Held in the calling system's secret store and rotated on a schedule; one app per integration
settings.why: The client-credentials secret is the whole of the Agent API's authentication, so it is never shared between systems or kept in code.

settings.name: Commit Version
settings.where: Agentforce Builder › Commit Version (or sf agent publish authoring-bundle), then deploy by metadata
settings.recommended: Versions committed in a sandbox and deployed to production by metadata from version control
settings.why: Production receives only immutable, tested versions, and the previous version is there to reactivate.

settings.name: Agentforce Testing Center
settings.where: Agentforce Testing Center (or sf agent test create and run) in the development org
settings.recommended: A test suite per agent, including manipulation and off-scope attempts, run on every version before deployment
settings.why: A version that starts obeying injected instructions or reaching for restricted actions is caught before customers see it.

settings.name: Agentforce Session Tracing
settings.where: Setup › Einstein Audit, Analytics, and Monitoring Setup
settings.recommended: On
settings.why: Every turn, model call and action an agent takes is recorded in the firm's Data 360 for investigation.

settings.name: Audit and Feedback
settings.where: Setup › Einstein Audit, Analytics, and Monitoring Setup
settings.recommended: On
settings.why: Prompts, responses and feedback are kept with the session trace, so a conversation can be reconstructed end to end.

settings.name: Agentforce Session Trace OTel API
settings.where: GET /services/data/v66.0/einstein/audit/otel/{session-id}, polled by an OTLP collector
settings.recommended: Polled into the SIEM within the 72-hour window
settings.why: Agent traces leave Salesforce for the firm's own monitoring, where they can be correlated and retained (beta, one session per call).

settings.name: enable_enhanced_event_logs
settings.where: Agent Script › config block
settings.recommended: True
settings.why: Conversation-level logs for debugging and monitoring are kept for each agent.

settings.name: Deactivate
settings.where: Agentforce Builder › Deactivate, or sf agent deactivate
settings.recommended: The incident runbook's first step, scripted with the CLI
settings.why: Deactivation ends the agent's open interactions and makes it unreachable on every connection.
