tools.name: Vercel AI SDK

variants.name: ai (AI SDK Core: generateText, streamText, ToolLoopAgent)
@ai-sdk/react and the other UI hooks (AI SDK UI: useChat)
@ai-sdk/mcp (MCP client)
@ai-sdk/otel (OpenTelemetry integration)
@ai-sdk/policy-opa (policy-based tool approvals)

summary: An open-source TypeScript toolkit (Apache-2.0) that runs the agent loop inside the customer's own server code: generateText / streamText and ToolLoopAgent call a model, execute the tools declared on that call in the application process, and loop until a stop condition; useChat streams the conversation to a React (or Vue, Svelte) front end. Nothing is hosted by Vercel unless the application routes model calls through AI Gateway, which plain model strings do by default.

Its controls are call options the deployer sets: toolApproval (manual approval, automatic allow or deny, or an OPA policy through @ai-sdk/policy-opa) with experimental_toolApprovalSecret to sign approvals, activeTools and prepareStep, stopWhen and timeout, language-model middleware as the guardrail attach point, OpenTelemetry spans through @ai-sdk/otel, and an MCP client with OAuth and tool-definition fingerprinting. Authentication, chat persistence, rate limiting, sandboxing and egress are the application's or its platform's.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Free, open-source library (Apache-2.0, vercel/ai); no Vercel plan is needed. Model usage is billed by the chosen provider, or by Vercel when routed through AI Gateway (a separate product; request-level ZDR only on Pro and Enterprise).

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: Plain model strings resolve through the global default provider, which is Vercel AI Gateway (ai-gateway.vercel.sh) unless globalThis.AI_SDK_DEFAULT_PROVIDER is set; provider packages (@ai-sdk/openai, @ai-sdk/anthropic and others) call the provider directly with its own key.

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: From the customer's server: prompts, files, tool definitions and tool results to the model provider or AI Gateway. In the standard useChat pattern the browser sends the whole message history to the route every turn. Telemetry goes only to integrations the application registers, with inputs and outputs recorded by default.

facts.label: Retention & training
facts.value: The SDK stores nothing; chat history, memory and traces live where the application puts them. Model-side retention is the provider's terms; through AI Gateway, providerOptions.gateway zeroDataRetention and disallowPromptTraining restrict routing to providers with those agreements with Vercel (the training filter is not applied to BYOK credentials).

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: ai-sdk.dev/docs (llms.txt, a search endpoint and a .md variant of every page); AI SDK 7, ai 7.0.157 on npm on 2026-10-29.

facts.label: Version 7 changes that move controls
facts.value: toolApproval on the call or agent replaces the deprecated needsApproval on tools (kept for WorkflowAgent); experimental_telemetry became telemetry and OpenTelemetry moved to @ai-sdk/otel, opt-out once registered; stepCountIs became isStepCount.

facts.label: Separate Vercel products the docs wire in
facts.value: AI Gateway (default provider, OIDC authentication, quotaEntityId quotas, ZDR routing); Vercel Workflow for WorkflowAgent (durable runs and approvals that survive suspension, no default step limit); Vercel Sandbox as one isolation provider behind Experimental_SandboxSession. Each control that depends on them needs that product.

riskNotes.note: In the default useChat pattern the server rebuilds the conversation from client-sent messages, so without experimental_toolApprovalSecret a client can fabricate an approval for any schema-valid input; tools with an execute function and no toolApproval run as soon as the model calls them.

ToolLoopAgent stops at isStepCount(20) by default, generateText and streamText at one step; isLoopFinished() removes the cap and WorkflowAgent has none, so a durable run loops until the model stops calling tools.

mcpClient.tools() returns whatever the server serves on each call and the SDK uses it unchanged unless the application compares fingerprintTools digests against a stored baseline with detectToolDrift.

useChat hands the application typed parts and renders nothing; the docs' chatbot examples put model file URLs straight into img src, and Streamdown, the companion renderer, allows every image and link prefix until configured.
Once an OpenTelemetry integration is registered every call records inputs and outputs by default, and approval metadata keeps the original tool input including fields a schema transform removed.
Tools run in the application process; Experimental_SandboxSession is only an interface and does not sandbox the tool, and code mode's QuickJS sandbox leaves every provided tool executing on the host.

controls.mechanism: Tools declared per call in the tools map (ToolLoopAgent, generateText, streamText) with activeTools; opaCapabilityMiddleware dropping tools that an OPA policy does not list before the model sees them; wrapMcpTools with default 'denied' over discovered MCP tools; mcpClient.tools({ schemas }) pulling only named tools

steps.title: Serve the admitted tool list from policy
body: Wrap the model with wrapLanguageModel({ model, middleware: opaCapabilityMiddleware({ client, path: 'agent/tools/allowed' }) }) and keep the registry's admitted tool names in the OPA data; an evaluator error leaves the model with no tools.

steps.title: Refuse discovered tools the registry has not admitted
body: Pass MCP tools through wrapMcpTools(await mcpClient.tools(), opaPolicy({ client, path }), { default: 'denied' }) so any tool the policy does not name is denied at dispatch.

steps.title: Pull only the MCP tools you named
body: Call mcpClient.tools({ schemas: { ... } }) with an entry per admitted tool; the client then pulls only the explicitly defined tools.

controls.note: Partial by this drawing's rule (tools declared in code per call; native only with an enforced registry): the SDK admits exactly the tools each call declares and can consult an OPA-served list per call, fail closed, which is where a registry plugs in, but it keeps no record of owner, version or approval state and reconciles nothing. Agents built on the SDK are not inventoried anywhere, provider-executed tools are declared in the same map, and a tool list is whatever the application's code assembles.

controls.mechanism: None in the SDK; an evaluation or red-team platform in the deployer's CI drives generateText or the ToolLoopAgent headless; experimental_evaluate is a runtime LLM-judge API, not a release gate

evidence.title: Evaluation (experimental_evaluate, an evaluation-model API for choice, score and boolean questions)
Navigating the library (no test harness or release gate among the packages)

controls.note: External (an evaluation or red-team platform in CI): the SDK ships nothing that tests a model, prompt or tool change and blocks its release. experimental_evaluate asks an evaluation model named questions about one state and returns uncalibrated estimates; it can score outputs inside a test the platform runs, but the test set, its protection and the promotion decision are the platform's. Integration point: run the agent headless in CI with a pinned model id and gate on the results and the telemetry spans.

controls.mechanism: toolApproval status 'user-approval' (per tool, per input, or one GenericToolApprovalFunction) on ToolLoopAgent, generateText or streamText; the call returns a tool-approval-request (approvalId, toolCallId, input) instead of executing; useChat shows the part in state 'approval-requested' and addToolApprovalResponse answers it; experimental_toolApprovalSecret HMAC-signs the request to the tool name, tool call ID and input

steps.title: Mark consequential tools for approval
body: Set toolApproval: { <tool>: 'user-approval' } on the ToolLoopAgent or streamText call, or a function that returns 'user-approval' from the input and runtimeContext; the agent returns a tool-approval-request instead of running the tool.

steps.title: Show the exact call in the thread
body: Render tool parts with state 'approval-requested' (tool name, input, approval.requestReason) and answer with addToolApprovalResponse({ id: part.approval.id, approved }), with sendAutomaticallyWhen set to lastAssistantMessageIsCompleteWithApprovalResponses.

steps.title: Sign approvals on the server
body: Pass experimental_toolApprovalSecret (at least 32 random bytes, the same value on every instance) so a fabricated or altered approval fails with AI_InvalidToolApprovalSignatureError before the tool runs.

controls.note: Native by this drawing's rule: a built-in primitive pauses the SDK-executed call, surfaces it in the UI stream and runs it only on an approval that, with the secret set, is bound to that call ID, tool and arguments, failing closed. The deployer supplies the approver's authentication and UI. Boundaries: without the secret the history is client-controlled and the docs say a crafted approval bypasses the person; the signature does not bind the approver, the conversation or an expiry, and single use is not documented; subagent tools cannot use toolApproval and provider-executed tools never ask; automatic 'approved' statuses and policy decisions are not human approval; the secret option is experimental.

controls.mechanism: callOptionsSchema and prepareCall on ToolLoopAgent, or runtimeContext on generateText / streamText, carrying the authenticated user's role and tenant into toolApproval; @ai-sdk/policy-opa Rego policies (opaPolicy, httpPolicyClient bundles with IdP group data, shadow rollout, opa test); the grant itself is the application's authentication

steps.title: Carry the user's grant into every call
body: Define callOptionsSchema on the ToolLoopAgent and return toolApproval from prepareCall using the role and tenant read from the server-side session, never from the request body.

steps.title: Administer tool authorisation as policy code
body: Write .rego rules over input.tool.name, input.args and input.runtimeContext, test them with opa test, deploy through shadow(opaPolicy(...), { enforce: false }) and switch to enforce: true.

steps.title: Update entitlements without a deploy
body: Point httpPolicyClient({ url }) at an OPA server whose bundles carry role-to-permission mappings and IdP group memberships.

controls.note: Partial on the rule for this drawing (the deployer's auth; name the SDK hooks): the SDK carries per-request user context into a policy it evaluates on every tool call and ships the package to author, test and roll out that policy, but it authenticates nobody and issues no delegated grant. Session identity, scope and expiry come from the application's auth layer or IdP; runtimeContext holds whatever the route puts there, and the message-persistence guide states it does not cover authorization.

controls.mechanism: activeTools per call and per step (prepareStep); inputSchema validation of every call before execute (InvalidToolInputError) and strict: true for provider-side strict tool calling; toolApproval or opaPolicy deciding by runtimeContext principal, tool name and arguments; toolsContext giving each tool only its own contextSchema-validated context

steps.title: Expose only the user's tools on each call
body: Set activeTools on generateText or streamText, or return activeTools from prepareStep, computed from the authenticated user's entitlements.

steps.title: Validate every argument
body: Give each tool a bounded inputSchema (enums, limits); calls that fail it raise InvalidToolInputError before execute, and strict: true asks supporting providers to generate only valid calls.

steps.title: Decide per principal, operation and resource
body: Pass toolApproval: opaPolicy({ client, path }) with default decision := { "decision": "deny" } so a call the user's role may not make is denied before dispatch.

steps.title: Run tools on the user's credential
body: Pass the user's token in toolsContext for the tool that needs it, declared with contextSchema, instead of a service key read inside execute.

controls.note: Native by this drawing's rule: per-call tool selection and schema validation are enforced by the SDK outside the model (a call to a tool outside the step's active set fails as NoSuchToolError in the generateText source), and the policy package decides per principal, operation and resource, failing closed on evaluator errors. Boundaries: activeTools defaults to every tool and an unmatched policy rule allows; the principal is whatever the route puts in runtimeContext; subagent and provider-executed tools are outside toolApproval; dispatcher tools (bash, HTTP, MCP proxy) need their own argument rules; the user's authority reaches a downstream system only if the tool uses the credential passed in toolsContext.

controls.mechanism: The AI Gateway provider authenticating the deployment with the Vercel OIDC token (no API key) on Vercel deployments; direct provider packages reading static API keys; an OAuthClientProvider as authProvider on each createMCPClient HTTP or SSE transport

steps.title: Authenticate model calls with the deployment's OIDC identity
body: On a Vercel deployment use the gateway provider and leave AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY and apiKey unset; any API key present is used instead of OIDC, even if invalid.

steps.title: Register the agent as its own OAuth client at each tool server
body: Pass an authProvider to createMCPClient({ transport: { type: 'http', url, authProvider } }) and implement validateAuthorizationServerURL to allow only trusted authorization servers.

controls.note: Partial by the rule for this drawing: the SDK authenticates with whatever the host supplies. The OIDC token is issued by the Vercel platform to the project and needs AI Gateway, so every route and agent in the deployment shares it (local tokens expire after 12 hours); direct providers use standing keys; an MCP OAuth client registration is whatever the application's authProvider holds. No agent principal distinct from the application is minted, and issuance, rotation and revocation are the platform's or the IdP's.

controls.mechanism: Vercel OIDC for the AI Gateway credential (obtained and refreshed automatically on deployments); toolsContext with contextSchema so tool secrets never enter the prompt and are left out of telemetry unless includeToolsContext names them; MCP authProvider OAuth tokens in the application's storage; env on Experimental_SandboxSession.run instead of secrets inlined in commands

steps.title: Drop the standing model key
body: Route model calls through the AI Gateway provider on Vercel with OIDC and remove AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY and provider API keys from the deployment's environment.

steps.title: Keep tool secrets out of the prompt and traces
body: Declare contextSchema on the tool, pass the secret in toolsContext, and leave it out of telemetry.includeToolsContext, which excludes every property not set to true.

steps.title: Use OAuth rather than static MCP bearer headers
body: Configure authProvider on the MCP transport instead of headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer ...' } so tokens are obtained and refreshed through the OAuth flow.

controls.note: Partial by the rule for this drawing (native only with short-lived or OIDC credentials supported by configuration): only the model credential can be short-lived, and only through AI Gateway on Vercel. Provider keys, tool keys, MCP headers and OAuth tokens are whatever the application holds and stores; nothing brokers a user-scoped credential per call. toolsContext keeps values out of the model's context, but every tool shares the process, and a secret a tool returns lands in spans because recordInputs and recordOutputs default to true.

controls.mechanism: Stateless calls (the model sees only the messages the route passes); a chat id with server-side storage per the persistence guide (prepareSendMessagesRequest sending only the last message, server-side message ids); validateUIMessages on stored and incoming history; memory tools or providers the deployer chooses

steps.title: Keep the thread on the server
body: In DefaultChatTransport set prepareSendMessagesRequest to send only the last message and the chat id, and load the rest from your store after checking that the signed-in user owns that chat id.

steps.title: Validate history before the model reads it
body: Run validateUIMessages with the tools map on the loaded and incoming messages before convertToModelMessages, and reject the turn on a validation error.

steps.title: Key long-term memory to the authenticated user
body: If you add a memory tool or provider, pass the user id from runtimeContext or toolsContext to its reads and writes, never an id taken from the model's tool input.

controls.note: Partial by the rule for this drawing (chat persistence is the deployer's store): a call reads only the messages it is given, but in the default useChat pattern the client sends the whole history each turn and can rewrite earlier turns, tool results included, unless the route loads history server-side. Chat-id ownership checks are the application's. validateUIMessages checks shape and tool schemas, not provenance. Memory tools write wherever their execute function writes, and memory providers (Letta, Mem0, Supermemory, Hindsight) scope data on their own services.

controls.mechanism: None in the SDK; the data source, retrieval service or an MCP server authorised with the user's OAuth token applies the entitlements; the SDK passes per-request credentials in toolsContext or per-transport authProvider

evidence.title: Runtime and Tool Context (per-tool credentials passed per request)
Model Context Protocol (headers or authProvider per transport)

controls.note: External (the data source or retrieval service enforcing the requesting user's entitlements): by this drawing's rule, external unless the SDK ships retrieval with identity passthrough, and it does not. Retrieval is a tool the application writes, run with whatever credential it is given. Integration points: put the user's token in that tool's toolsContext on each request, or build one MCP client per user with an authProvider holding that user's OAuth grant. Oversharing analysis of the sources is outside the SDK.

evidence.title: Embeddings (vectors only; the data store for retrieval is the application's)
Navigating the library (reviewed for applicability, 2026-09-25)

controls.note: Not applicable: the SDK ships embed, embedMany and rerank calls but no corpus, vector store or index, so there is nothing of its own to trust-tier, isolate per tenant or screen at ingest. The store an application attaches (a vector database, a search service, an MCP server) owns index scoping, ingest screening and grounding checks; record them on that store.

controls.mechanism: LanguageModelV4Middleware through wrapLanguageModel: transformParams sees each step's prompt (user turns, file parts, tool results) before the provider call and can throw or strip; no injection classifier ships

steps.title: Screen every step's prompt
body: Wrap the model with wrapLanguageModel({ model, middleware }) whose transformParams sends user, file and tool-result parts in params.prompt to your injection classifier and throws or strips on a hit.

steps.title: Use the wrapped model everywhere
body: Pass only the wrapped model to ToolLoopAgent and to any model returned from prepareStep, so no step reaches an unwrapped model.

controls.note: Partial by this drawing's rule (middleware with a classifier attached; native only with a shipped classifier): middleware is the attach point and the classifier is the deployer's. Because the loop calls the model once per step, transformParams sees tool results before the next step, so returned record content is covered as well as user turns and uploads (file parts the classifier must decode). The policy-package docs call semantic filtering best-effort. A model left unwrapped, or switched in by prepareStep, bypasses it.

controls.mechanism: None in ai or @ai-sdk/react (useChat returns typed parts and the application renders them); the companion AI Elements MessageResponse component and Streamdown renderer, with rehype-sanitize on by default and allowedImagePrefixes, allowedLinkPrefixes, allowedProtocols and allowDataImages permissive by default

steps.title: Render model text through a hardened renderer
body: Render text parts with Streamdown or AI Elements MessageResponse and set allowedImagePrefixes and allowedLinkPrefixes to your own origins, allowedProtocols to https and allowDataImages to false.

steps.title: Drop raw HTML
body: Set skipHtml on Streamdown so raw HTML in model output is ignored rather than sanitised.

steps.title: Do not auto-load model-supplied URLs
body: Render file and source-url parts only from an origin allowlist instead of placing part.url straight into img src or href as the chatbot guide's examples do.

controls.note: Partial by this drawing's rule (an optional sanitiser): the AI SDK's own UI layer renders nothing, so encoding is the application's renderer. The companion components can close the image-exfiltration path the pin names, but they are optional (AI Elements is a shadcn registry copied into the application, Streamdown a separate package), and Streamdown allows every image, link, protocol and data image until configured; it does strip dangerous raw HTML by default. The SDK's chatbot guide and markdown cookbook use plain img and react-markdown. Content-security policy is the application's.

controls.mechanism: Language-model middleware (transformParams, wrapGenerate, wrapStream) as the attach point for a detector that masks or blocks; telemetry recordInputs / recordOutputs (on by default) and includeRuntimeContext / includeToolsContext (off by default) as minimisation; pruneMessages in prepareStep

steps.title: Mask what reaches the model and the user
body: In a middleware, run your PII and secret detector in transformParams over the prompt and in wrapGenerate / wrapStream over output text, buffering each text block before masking as the docs' guardrail example does.

steps.title: Keep content out of traces
body: Set telemetry: { recordInputs: false, recordOutputs: false } on calls that handle sensitive content.

steps.title: Trim what the session carries forward
body: Return messages: pruneMessages({ messages, toolCalls: 'before-last-3-messages', reasoning: 'all' }) from prepareStep so old tool results stop riding along.

controls.note: Partial by the rule, as for the Claude Agent SDK: middleware can block or mask, but no detector ships and nothing is inspected until one is attached; the telemetry switches and pruning are minimisation. The middleware sees model traffic only: tool results streamed to the UI and history the application persists keep raw values unless it redacts them, and approval metadata keeps the original tool input, including fields a schema transform removed. Recording is on by default once telemetry is registered.

controls.mechanism: None in the SDK; a rate limit in the route handler before streamText (the docs' example uses Upstash Ratelimit) or at the edge (Vercel WAF rate limiting); AI Gateway providerOptions.gateway.quotaEntityId for per-entity quota

evidence.title: Rate Limiting (route-handler pattern with Upstash Ratelimit)
Vercel WAF rate limiting (counting keys and limits by plan)
AI Gateway provider (quotaEntityId, user and tags)

controls.note: External (edge WAF, API gateway or a rate-limit store in the route): the SDK counts nothing per user or session. Integration points: the chat route before streamText or agent.stream, keyed on the authenticated user rather than the IP the docs' example uses; Vercel WAF rate limiting (IP and JA4 keys on Hobby and Pro, header keys on Enterprise, counters per region); AI Gateway quotaEntityId, which needs that product. Volume inside one turn is AML.M0036.

controls.mechanism: registerTelemetry(new OpenTelemetry()) from @ai-sdk/otel: an invoke_agent root span, a chat span per step with gen_ai.input.messages, gen_ai.output.messages, gen_ai.tool.definitions and usage, and an execute_tool span per tool with gen_ai.tool.call.id, arguments and result; telemetry.functionId and includeRuntimeContext for correlation; exported by the application's OpenTelemetry provider

steps.title: Register the integration once
body: Install @ai-sdk/otel and call registerTelemetry(new OpenTelemetry()) at startup (in Next.js, instrumentation.ts beside registerOTel) with an exporter to your collector.

steps.title: Correlate runs to users and chats
body: Pass runtimeContext { userId, chatId, requestId }, list those keys in telemetry.includeRuntimeContext, and set telemetry.functionId per agent.

steps.title: Record policy decisions and approvals
body: Wrap the policy in shadow(opaPolicy(...), { enforce: true, onDecision }) to log each decision, and keep tool-approval-response messages with the stored chat.

controls.note: Native by this drawing's rule: once registered, every generateText, streamText and ToolLoopAgent call traces the turn, each model step and each tool execution with arguments and results, on by default and exported to the customer's collector. Limits: nothing is emitted until an integration is registered, and telemetry { isEnabled: false } opts a call out; v6 code that relied on experimental_telemetry emits nothing after the v7 upgrade until @ai-sdk/otel is added; approvals and policy decisions are not telemetry events; useChat stop and approve clicks are not traced; integration errors are swallowed. Emission is not tamper resistance or detection.

controls.mechanism: abortSignal on generateText, streamText and agent calls (forwarding req.signal); useChat stop(); "supportsCancellation" in vercel.json on Vercel; timeout.totalMs; onAbort for cleanup; tools receive the abortSignal in their execute options

steps.title: Wire cancellation end to end
body: Forward req.signal as abortSignal in the chat route and, on Vercel, add "supportsCancellation": true for that function in vercel.json so useChat's stop() ends the model request.

steps.title: Stop a live run from the server
body: Keep an AbortController per active chat and abort it from an operator action; persist partial steps and release resources in onAbort.

controls.note: Partial by the rule for this drawing (abort signals per request; native only with a documented stop of live sessions): an abort ends the in-flight model call, and tools stop only if their code honours the signal they receive. There is no SDK-level list of live runs and no stop that reaches every instance; a client stop needs the platform to propagate the disconnect. Revoking the provider or AI Gateway key refuses only later requests (delay not documented), and WorkflowAgent runs on Vercel Workflow, whose cancellation is that product's.

controls.mechanism: toolApproval evaluated before every SDK-executed tool call, including @ai-sdk/policy-opa opaPolicy over tool name, arguments, messages and runtimeContext (allow, deny, requires-approval; fail closed on evaluator errors); experimental_toolApprovalSecret binding an approval to tool name, call ID and input

steps.title: Decide every call in policy
body: Pass toolApproval: opaPolicy({ client, path: 'agent/call/decision' }) with default decision := { "decision": "deny" }, allow for read-only tools and requires-approval for mutating ones.

steps.title: Cover discovered and dispatcher tools
body: Wrap MCP tools with wrapMcpTools(..., { default: 'denied' }) and give bash, HTTP and proxy tools a toInput that reduces their input to the action being taken.

steps.title: Bind approvals to the call
body: Set experimental_toolApprovalSecret so an approval replayed with a different tool, call ID or input is rejected before execution.

steps.title: Log every decision
body: Wrap the policy in shadow(..., { enforce: true, onDecision }), or use OPA decision logs from the HTTP backend.

controls.note: Partial by this drawing's rule (native needs built-in enforcement of an approval bound to the action, its arguments and the session): the SDK ships the policy decision point and binds approvals to the tool, call ID and arguments, but not to the session or user, and with client-held history the docs do not say a signed approval is single-use or confined to its conversation. The session leg is the application's server-side history. Unmatched rules allow unless defaulted to deny, optionalOpaPolicy allows all when no policy loads, subagent and provider-executed tools are outside toolApproval, and an approved tool does whatever its code does.

controls.mechanism: stopWhen: isStepCount(n) (ToolLoopAgent default 20, generateText and streamText default 1, WorkflowAgent none); timeout { totalMs, stepMs, toolMs, <tool>Ms }; maxOutputTokens per call or per step; a custom StopCondition over steps[].usage for a token or cost ceiling

steps.title: Cap steps
body: Set stopWhen: isStepCount(n) on every agent and streamText call, and never isLoopFinished() on a user-facing route.

steps.title: Cap wall-clock and tool time
body: Set timeout: { totalMs, stepMs, toolMs } on the call; a tool that overruns returns a tool-error.

steps.title: Cap tokens per turn
body: Set maxOutputTokens and add a StopCondition that sums steps[].usage input and output tokens and returns true at the turn's budget.

controls.note: Partial by this drawing's rule (native needs step-count and token limits that end a turn): the step count, wall clock and per-step output ceiling are enforced by the SDK, but a token or spend ceiling that ends the turn is a StopCondition the deployer writes (the docs' budgetExceeded example), checked only between steps. Input tokens grow with every step unless pruned, WorkflowAgent has no default step limit, and AI Gateway's quotaEntityId is a separate product's quota.

controls.mechanism: None in the SDK (no token exchange); headers or an authProvider per createMCPClient transport, redirect 'error' by default, validateAuthorizationServerURL and callbackIssuer checks; the MCP client forwards whatever token the application sets

evidence.title: Model Context Protocol (transports, OAuth authorization server and issuer validation)
createMCPClient reference (headers, authProvider, redirect defaults to 'error')

controls.note: External (an MCP or API gateway that exchanges the user's token for a narrowed one): by this drawing's rule, external unless the SDK performs token exchange, and it does not. The MCP client sends the headers or OAuth token configured for one transport to that one server, refuses redirects unless redirect is set to 'follow', and can allowlist authorization servers. A user's upstream token placed in headers is forwarded as-is, so passthrough is prevented only by what the application puts there.

controls.mechanism: fingerprintTools and detectToolDrift digests of each MCP tool's description, resolved input schema and title against a stored baseline; mcpClient.tools({ schemas }) with client-side input schemas; wrapMcpTools default 'denied' for tools the policy does not name

steps.title: Pin the reviewed definitions
body: At review time persist fingerprintTools(await mcpClient.tools()); before each call compare the current digests with detectToolDrift and withhold the tools when changed or added is non-empty.

steps.title: Pull only reviewed tools with your own schemas
body: Pass schemas to mcpClient.tools() so only the named tools load, validated against input schemas you define.

steps.title: Refuse unlisted tools at dispatch
body: Wrap discovered tools with wrapMcpTools(tools, opaPolicy(...), { default: 'denied' }).

controls.note: Partial by core rule 1: the SDK ships the content hash and the diff, but the baseline store and the refusal are the application's code (the docs say core does not persist baselines or block calls), so nothing is refused until the deployer writes the check. A behaviour or endpoint swap behind an unchanged definition is invisible to it, nothing scans descriptions statically, server annotations such as readOnlyHint are untrusted hints, and a stdio server runs whatever command the application gives.

controls.mechanism: None in the SDK; tools run in the application process on its network; Experimental_SandboxSession is an interface whose isolation is the provider's; code mode's QuickJS sandbox has no fetch but its tools run on the host

evidence.title: Experimental_SandboxSession (does not sandbox the tool itself)
Code Mode (isolation and tool access)
Tool Calling (the SDK forwards a sandbox but does not create or isolate one)

controls.note: External (an egress proxy or firewall on the function's network, or a sandbox provider with a network policy): the SDK docs configure no outbound allowlist anywhere. Vercel Sandbox is named only as one isolation option, and its network policy is that product's. Integration points: route command tools through experimental_sandbox to an isolation provider with a domain allowlist, give MCP transports a custom fetch that goes through the egress proxy, and restrict the hosting platform's outbound network.

controls.mechanism: None in the SDK; admission scanning at the npm mirror or artifact repository the build and any npx-launched stdio MCP server resolve packages from

evidence.title: Navigating the library (ai and @ai-sdk/* packages installed from npm)
Model Context Protocol (stdio servers start from a command the application gives)

controls.note: External (package firewall or artifact-repository scanning at the mirror): the SDK scans nothing it loads. The ai and @ai-sdk/* packages, community providers and memory providers, and stdio MCP servers started with npx all come from whichever registry the build or host reaches. Integration points: point the npm registry at the scanning mirror, pin versions in the lockfile, and allow only the mirror on the egress path. No model weights load; inference is remote.

controls.mechanism: @ai-sdk/code-mode (experimental) runs model-generated JavaScript in a fresh QuickJS context per invocation, with no Node globals, file system, module loader, fetch or eval, under executionPolicy limits; the experimental_sandbox option hands an Experimental_SandboxSession (an isolation provider the deployer chooses) to tools that delegate commands to it

steps.title: Run generated code only through code mode
body: Expose model-written programs through codeModeTool with an executionPolicy (timeoutMs, cpuTimeoutMs, memoryLimitBytes, maxBridgeRequests) instead of evaluating them in the application process.

steps.title: Delegate command tools to an isolation provider
body: Pass experimental_sandbox with a provider-backed Experimental_SandboxSession and have every command or file tool call its run, readFile and writeFile methods rather than the host's.

controls.note: Partial on the core sandbox rule (an optional boundary the deployer must choose, as for toolClaudeAgentSdk, toolCopilotSdk and toolCodexSdk): code mode confines generated code to QuickJS with no network or file access of its own, but it is experimental, Node 22+ only, and "tools execute in your host application, outside the QuickJS sandbox", so every capability a provided tool exposes is available to the program. The sandbox option is only an interface: "Passing an experimental sandbox does not sandbox the tool itself", and the isolation — its own file system, network policy and teardown — is the provider's (Vercel Sandbox is one). A tool that does not delegate runs in the application process. Added 2026-10-30: the pin had no row.

settings.name: AI_SDK_DEFAULT_PROVIDER
settings.where: globalThis.AI_SDK_DEFAULT_PROVIDER = <provider> at application start-up
settings.default: Vercel AI Gateway (plain model strings route there)
settings.recommended: The organisation's approved provider or gateway, set explicitly
settings.why: A bare model string cannot send prompts to a provider nobody approved; it otherwise routes through AI Gateway.

settings.name: OIDC Authentication (Vercel Deployments)
settings.where: AI Gateway provider — the deployment's Vercel OIDC token, or apiKey / AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY elsewhere
settings.recommended: OIDC on Vercel deployments, with no AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY set; a vault-held key elsewhere
settings.why: The model credential is short-lived and refreshed by the platform instead of a standing key in the environment.

settings.name: disallowPromptTraining
settings.where: providerOptions.gateway.disallowPromptTraining
settings.recommended: true
settings.why: Requests route only to providers with a no-training agreement with Vercel; the filter is not applied to BYOK credentials, whose own terms must say so.

settings.name: zeroDataRetention
settings.where: providerOptions.gateway.zeroDataRetention
settings.recommended: true on routes that handle work for clients whose contracts require zero retention; otherwise off
settings.why: Those requests go only to providers with ZDR agreements and fail rather than fall back to one without.
settings.requires: Vercel AI Gateway; request-level ZDR on Pro or Enterprise

settings.name: runtimeContext
settings.where: generateText / streamText runtimeContext, or ToolLoopAgent prepareCall, filled by the route from its authentication
settings.recommended: The authenticated user, role and tenant from the application's session, never from the request body
settings.why: Tool approvals and policies decide on a principal the server verified, not one the client claimed.

settings.name: toolsContext with contextSchema
settings.where: toolsContext on the call or agent; contextSchema on each tool
settings.recommended: Each tool's credential (ideally the user's own token) passed in its validated context, never in the prompt or tool description
settings.why: Secrets never enter the model's context, and each tool receives only its own credential.

settings.name: authProvider
settings.where: createMCPClient({ transport: { type: 'http', url, authProvider } })
settings.recommended: An OAuthClientProvider holding the requesting user's grant, one client per user
settings.why: The MCP server sees the user's own delegated access instead of a shared service key.

settings.name: redirect
settings.where: createMCPClient HTTP transport → redirect
settings.recommended: 'error'
settings.why: A server cannot redirect the client, and the token it sends, to another host; the default exists to prevent SSRF.

settings.name: toolApproval
settings.where: toolApproval on ToolLoopAgent, generateText or streamText (per tool, per input, or one function)
settings.default: None — tools with an execute function run as soon as the model calls them
settings.recommended: 'user-approval' for tools that write, send, delete or spend; automatic for read-only tools
settings.why: A person approves each consequential call before it runs, answered with addToolApprovalResponse.

settings.name: experimental_toolApprovalSecret
settings.where: experimental_toolApprovalSecret on the agent or call, from the secret store
settings.recommended: Set, wherever history comes from the client
settings.why: An approval is bound to the tool, call id and input, so a client cannot fabricate one in the history it sends; experimental.

settings.name: opaPolicy
settings.where: @ai-sdk/policy-opa opaPolicy({ client, path }) as toolApproval
settings.recommended: opaPolicy (fails closed), not optionalOpaPolicy, with the organisation's Rego policy
settings.why: Every tool call is decided by a reviewed policy over principal, tool and arguments; optionalOpaPolicy approves everything when no policy loads.

settings.name: wrapMcpTools default
settings.where: wrapMcpTools(tools, approval, { default })
settings.recommended: 'denied'
settings.why: A discovered MCP tool the policy does not name is rejected rather than offered for approval, so the policy is an allowlist.

settings.name: opaCapabilityMiddleware
settings.where: wrapLanguageModel({ model, middleware: opaCapabilityMiddleware({ client, path }) })
settings.recommended: On, with the same policy as toolApproval
settings.why: Tools the policy does not allow are removed before the model is told they exist; it fails closed.

settings.name: activeTools
settings.where: activeTools on the call, or returned per step from prepareStep
settings.recommended: Only the tools the step needs
settings.why: The SDK rejects a call to a tool outside the active set, so a steered model cannot reach the rest.

settings.name: schemas
settings.where: mcpClient.tools({ schemas: { <tool>: { inputSchema } } })
settings.default: Schema discovery (every tool the server lists, with its own schemas)
settings.recommended: Named tools with schemas the application defines
settings.why: Only reviewed tools load, validated against the application's schema rather than whatever the server serves.

settings.name: fingerprintTools / detectToolDrift
settings.where: fingerprintTools(await mcpClient.tools()) stored at review; detectToolDrift before each use
settings.default: Not used (the SDK keeps no baseline and blocks nothing)
settings.recommended: Baseline stored at review, tools withheld when any digest changed or a tool was added
settings.why: A server that rewrites a tool's description or schema after review is caught before the model sees it.

settings.name: stopWhen
settings.where: stopWhen: isStepCount(n) on ToolLoopAgent, generateText or streamText
settings.default: isStepCount(20) on ToolLoopAgent; one step on generateText and streamText
settings.recommended: isStepCount(20) or lower — never isLoopFinished() on user-facing routes
settings.why: A loop the model keeps feeding ends at a known step count; isLoopFinished() removes the cap.

settings.name: timeout
settings.where: timeout { totalMs, stepMs, toolMs, <tool>Ms } on generateText, streamText or the agent
settings.recommended: totalMs and toolMs set for every agent route
settings.why: A hung tool or a long run is cut off by wall clock instead of running until the platform kills the function.

settings.name: maxOutputTokens
settings.where: maxOutputTokens on the call, or per step from prepareStep
settings.recommended: Set per route
settings.why: Bounds what one step can generate and bill; a token or cost ceiling for the whole turn is a StopCondition the deployer writes.

settings.name: abortSignal
settings.where: abortSignal: req.signal on streamText and agent calls; tools honour the signal in their execute options
settings.recommended: The request's signal forwarded on every call, and honoured by every long-running tool
settings.why: A user's stop or a dropped connection ends the in-flight model call and the tools that listen, instead of running on unseen.

settings.name: wrapLanguageModel (transformParams)
settings.where: wrapLanguageModel({ model, middleware }) with transformParams calling the organisation's screening service
settings.recommended: Every model the application uses wrapped with input-screening and DLP middleware that blocks or masks
settings.why: Each step's prompt, tool results included, is screened before the provider call; a model left unwrapped, or switched in by prepareStep, bypasses it.

settings.name: prepareSendMessagesRequest
settings.where: useChat transport → prepareSendMessagesRequest sending only the last message and the chat id
settings.default: The whole message history sent from the browser every turn
settings.recommended: Last message only, with history loaded server-side by chat id after an ownership check
settings.why: A client cannot rewrite earlier turns or tool results that the model will trust.

settings.name: validateUIMessages
settings.where: validateUIMessages({ messages, tools, ... }) on the server before each call
settings.recommended: Called on stored and incoming messages
settings.why: Malformed tool calls, metadata or data parts are rejected before they reach the model; it checks shape, not provenance.

settings.name: registerTelemetry
settings.where: registerTelemetry(new OpenTelemetry()) from @ai-sdk/otel at start-up, exporting to the organisation's collector
settings.default: Nothing emitted until an integration is registered
settings.recommended: Registered, exporting to the firm's OpenTelemetry collector
settings.why: Every turn, model step and tool execution leaves a span in the organisation's store; v6 experimental_telemetry code emits nothing after the v7 upgrade.

settings.name: recordInputs / recordOutputs
settings.where: telemetry { recordInputs, recordOutputs } on each call or agent
settings.recommended: false, unless the trace store is approved for prompts and tool results
settings.why: Spans keep their structure and tool names without client material or secrets a tool returned.

settings.name: includeRuntimeContext / includeToolsContext
settings.where: telemetry { includeRuntimeContext, includeToolsContext }
settings.recommended: Only non-secret identifiers (user and tenant id) named for correlation; never credentials
settings.why: Traces can be tied to a principal without copying tokens from the context into span attributes.

settings.name: functionId
settings.where: telemetry { functionId } on each call or agent
settings.recommended: A stable id per agent and route
settings.why: Investigators can find every span from one agent; isEnabled false on a call would opt it out of tracing.

settings.name: executionPolicy
settings.where: @ai-sdk/code-mode codeModeTool({ executionPolicy: { timeoutMs, cpuTimeoutMs, memoryLimitBytes, maxBridgeRequests } })
settings.default: Built-in limits for runtime, memory, source, results and tool calls
settings.recommended: Code mode for any model-written program, with limits set explicitly per route
settings.why: Generated code runs in a fresh QuickJS context with no file system, network or eval and stops at its limits; the tools it calls still run on the host.

settings.name: experimental_sandbox
settings.where: experimental_sandbox option on generateText, streamText or ToolLoopAgent, with command tools delegating to it
settings.default: Unset (tools run in the application process)
settings.recommended: A provider-backed sandbox session with its own network policy, used by every command and file tool
settings.why: Commands and file writes the model asks for land in the isolation provider, not on the application host; passing it alone sandboxes nothing.

settings.name: allowedImagePrefixes / allowedLinkPrefixes / allowDataImages
settings.where: Streamdown (or AI Elements MessageResponse) props
settings.default: ["*"] for images and links; data images allowed
settings.recommended: The organisation's own origins, and allowDataImages false
settings.why: Model output cannot render an image or link that carries conversation data to an attacker's server.
