tools.name: vLLM

variants.name: vllm serve (pip package, OpenAI-compatible server)
variants.note: `vllm serve <model>` starts the HTTP server on port 8000; every control in this entry is one of its flags or an environment variable of the process. With --host unset the listener binds every interface (source: `args.host or ""`; the docs' own logs show "Uvicorn running on http://0.0.0.0:8000").

variants.name: vllm/vllm-openai container image
variants.note: The documented `docker run` publishes -p 8000:8000 on every host interface, passes HF_TOKEN in the environment and mounts ~/.cache/huggingface; the Kubernetes guide's example deployment passes --trust-remote-code, so review copied manifests.

variants.name: Multi-node serving (Ray or multiprocessing backend)
variants.note: Tensor and pipeline parallel across nodes over Ray (run_cluster.sh with VLLM_HOST_IP per node) or the mp backend (--nnodes, --node-rank, --master-addr, --headless workers). Traffic between nodes is unencrypted and unauthenticated; the page says to put VLLM_HOST_IP on a private network segment.

summary: Open-source (Apache-2.0) inference and serving engine from the vllm-project: `vllm serve` loads a model from a Hugging Face Hub id or a local path onto the operator's accelerators and publishes an OpenAI-compatible HTTP API (plus Anthropic /v1/messages, Cohere /v2 and a SageMaker /invocations route) on port 8000, with continuous batching, automatic prefix caching, LoRA adapters and tensor, pipeline, data and expert parallelism across GPUs and nodes. Current release v0.32.0 (2026-10-18, PyPI).

Inference runs entirely on infrastructure the organisation operates; no prompt goes to the project. Outbound traffic is model and tokenizer downloads from the Hub (HF_TOKEN for gated models), media URLs the server fetches for multimodal requests, anonymous usage statistics (on by default; VLLM_NO_USAGE_STATS=1 or DO_NOT_TRACK=1 turns them off), and whatever logs, metrics and OTLP traces the operator exports.

Every control is a `vllm serve` flag or an environment variable of the server process, and the security guide states the trust model plainly: --api-key is opt-in and covers only the /v1, /v2, /inference and /cohere prefixes, so /invocations, /pooling, /classify, /score, /rerank, /tokenize and the operational routes stay unauthenticated; inter-node channels are "insecure by default"; and the recommended front is a reverse proxy that allowlists endpoints.

facts.label: Plans
facts.value: Free and open source (Apache-2.0). No paid tier, licence key or vendor console — the operator runs and configures everything.

facts.label: Inference & routing
facts.value: On accelerators the operator provisions. One base model per `vllm serve` process, under one or more --served-model-name aliases, with named LoRA adapters beside it; spreading traffic across instances is a router or gateway in front (the docs' Nginx example load-balances vllm0:8000 and vllm1:8000).

facts.label: Data leaving the device
facts.value: Hub downloads of weights, tokenizer and (with --trust-remote-code) model code unless a local path is served; media URLs fetched for multimodal requests (limit with --allowed-media-domains); anonymous usage statistics — hardware, model architecture, vLLM version, parallelism and quantization settings — unless VLLM_NO_USAGE_STATS=1, DO_NOT_TRACK=1 or ~/.config/vllm/do_not_track is set.

facts.label: Retention & training
facts.value: No vendor retention or training: prompts never reach the project. Request logging is off by default (--enable-log-requests); KV and prefix cache live in accelerator memory for the life of the process; compile and asset caches persist under VLLM_CACHE_ROOT (~/.cache/vllm); usage statistics are also kept in ~/.config/vllm/usage_stats.json.

facts.label: Docs index
facts.value: docs.vllm.ai/en/stable (no llms.txt; /en/latest is the developer preview)

facts.label: Security guide
facts.value: The product's own threat model: inter-node communication, firewall guidance, the --api-key path limits and unauthenticated endpoint list, dynamic LoRA loading, endpoint plugins, gRPC, cache-directory trust, FIPS, Ray environment propagation, prefix-cache salting and multimodal uuid collisions.

facts.label: Vulnerability disclosure
facts.value: Private reports through the GitHub advisory form; CRITICAL and HIGH fixes are built in a private fork and shared with a prenotification group of organisations that ship or run vLLM; a CVE is requested when the patch merges and the advisory is published when the fix ships. 83 repository advisories were published January 2025 – September 2026 (5 critical, 19 high).

facts.label: Release cadence
facts.value: About every two weeks (v0.25.0 on 2026-07-11 through v0.32.0 on 2026-10-18), each with its own advisory fixes; the container image vllm/vllm-openai tracks the releases.

items.title: The reverse-proxy endpoint allowlist the security guide recommends
body: vLLM cannot unpublish a route, and --api-key covers only /v1, /v2, /inference and /cohere, so the guide's primary control is a reverse proxy (nginx, Envoy or a Kubernetes Gateway) that allowlists only the endpoints end users need, blocks everything else — /invocations, /pooling, /classify, /score, /rerank, /tokenize, /detokenize, /load, /metrics, /scale_elastic_ep and any operational route — and adds authentication, rate limiting and logging.
Expose /metrics only to the monitoring network, and keep --grpc-port and the distributed ports off the proxy entirely.

links.title: vLLM security guide — API key authentication limitations
vLLM — Using Nginx (upstream across vLLM containers)

riskNotes.note: Prefix caching is on by default and shared by every request without a cache_salt, and time-to-first-token reveals a prefix hit (CVE-2025-46570). Beyond the cache, CVE-2026-73558 showed an activation-kernel integer overflow copying one user's output into another's response in the same batch (fixed 0.27.0), and /invocations serves the same inference as /v1 without the API key.

The default --load-format auto falls back to PyTorch .bin files (torch.load with weights_only=True), and trust_remote_code=False has been bypassed by model code three times in 2026 (auto_map dynamic modules, hardcoded trust_remote_code=True, LlavaOnevision2). Cache directories are loaded without integrity checks in formats that execute code, and client-supplied prompt_embeds were a deserialization path (CVE-2025-62164).

With --enable-lora and VLLM_ALLOW_RUNTIME_LORA_UPDATING=True, POST /v1/load_lora_adapter loads weights from any lora_path the server can read and load_inplace swaps an adapter under an existing name; the lora_hf_hub_resolver plugin loads adapters named in requests from the listed Hub repositories. All of it skips storage promotion; the guide says not to enable it for untrusted clients.

/update_weights, /init_weight_transfer_engine and /pause are listed by the guide as unauthenticated routes on any generating model (the v0.30.0 source registers them only in dev mode), and --revision pins did not reach every nested artifact until 0.22.0 (CVE-2026-47155) and 0.28.0 (FunAudioChat, Tarsier2).

83 repository advisories in 2025–26, including critical RCEs over the multi-node and KV-transfer channels (Mooncake, PyNcclPipe), in video processing (CVE-2026-22778) and an --api-key bypass through the Host header (CVE-2026-48746); the image also carries PyTorch, CUDA and transformers with their own streams.

The request queue is unbounded unless --max-num-queued-reqs is set, n defaults to a 16384 ceiling, and dozens of 2025–26 advisories are engine-killing requests or decompression bombs any API caller can send.
The guide documents the prefix-cache timing channel (ROC AUC 0.99 at 8-token prefixes) and offers cache_salt for it; co-batching on shared accelerators has no engine-level partition.

controls.mechanism: --revision (with --code-revision and --tokenizer-revision) pins a Hugging Face Hub branch, tag or commit for hub-sourced loads; no signature or digest is verified at load, and a local-path load checks nothing

steps.title: Pin hub loads to a reviewed commit
body: Pass --revision <commit sha>, and set --code-revision and --tokenizer-revision to the same reviewed commit rather than a branch name, so the Hub resolves the files of that commit.

steps.title: Run a release that propagates the pin
body: Run v0.28.0 or later: the pins reach dynamic modules, GGUF files, image processors, side weights and subfolder artifacts only since 0.22.0 (CVE-2026-47155), and FunAudioChat and Tarsier2 since 0.28.0 (GHSA-hhv2-872h-628q).

controls.note: Partial on this drawing's rule — pinned revisions, no verification. A Hub commit fixes which files are fetched, but vLLM checks no signature, promotion-record digest or OpenSSF Model Signing bundle before loading. On this drawing the runtime loads from Storage by path (`vllm serve /models/<release>`), where the revision flags do not apply and nothing is checked; the security guide adds that cache directories are "loaded without cryptographic integrity verification, including formats that support arbitrary code execution". Verify-at-load is external: an init container or admission step that runs the model-signing verifier (or re-hashes against the promotion record) over the mounted path before `vllm serve` starts, with the volume read-only to the server.

controls.mechanism: GET /v1/models (id, root = the hub id or path served, parent for LoRA adapters, max_model_len), GET /version, the system_fingerprint on responses (--fingerprint-mode full by default) and the model_name label on Prometheus /metrics; no revision, digest or format

steps.title: Collect the served models from each instance
body: Have the inventory job call GET /v1/models on every instance (with the --api-key bearer) and record id, root and, for adapters, parent — the LoRA page shows the response shape.

steps.title: Record the engine build
body: Keep --fingerprint-mode at its default full, so each response's system_fingerprint carries vllm-<version>, the parallelism degrees and an 8-character config hash.

steps.title: Scrape the model label
body: Scrape /metrics, whose series carry model_name from --served-model-name (the first name when several are given), so monitoring knows which name serves on which instance.

controls.note: Partial on this drawing's rule: the engine exposes what is serving for an inventory to collect, but not what an AI BOM needs — root is the hub id or path passed to `vllm serve`, with no commit, digest, format, licence or scan result, and --served-model-name can present any alias. The revision and path live in the deployment manifest; publisher, format and the scan that cleared the artifact come from the promotion pipeline and a registry or AI-BOM tool (external). Calibrated against the local runtimes: toolOllama is partial with digests, toolLmStudio external with neither digest nor source; vLLM names the source but no digest. /server_info, which returns the full configuration, exists only under VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1.

controls.mechanism: --enable-log-requests (INFO: request id, parameters and LoRA request; DEBUG via VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL: prompt text and token ids), --enable-log-outputs (output text at INFO), --max-log-len truncation, --otlp-traces-endpoint (a span per request with request id, token counts, sampling parameters and latencies, no prompt text) and Prometheus /metrics; no redaction

steps.title: Turn on request logging at INFO
body: Start with --enable-log-requests and VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=INFO, so each request's id, parameters and LoRA adapter are logged without prompt text; DEBUG adds prompts and token ids.

steps.title: Decide on completion capture
body: Add --enable-log-outputs only where completions must be kept (it logs output text at INFO and needs --enable-log-requests), and bound logged prompt text with --max-log-len.

steps.title: Export traces
body: Set --otlp-traces-endpoint, with OTEL_SERVICE_NAME and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_PROTOCOL, so the server emits a span per request carrying metadata about it, in the caller's trace.

steps.title: Return the request id
body: Add --enable-request-id-headers so responses carry X-Request-Id for the gateway to join its record to the engine's log line.

controls.note: Partial on this drawing's rule (native needs content capture with privacy controls; logging without redaction is partial). Content capture is all-or-nothing by log level — prompts only at DEBUG, completions as raw text with --enable-log-outputs, truncation the only privacy control — and logs go to the process's stdout for the platform to ship; nothing makes them tamper-resistant. vLLM's own span carries request metadata, not content (the OTel example records the prompt only in its client span). The engine records no caller identity: --api-key admits a bearer without naming a tenant. The privacy-conscious record of every request and completion belongs at the gateway, the crossing every caller shares; the engine's logs, spans and metrics are the correlated inner half.

controls.mechanism: --load-format safetensors limits loading to *.safetensors (the default auto falls back to PyTorch .bin, read with torch.load weights_only=True); --trust-remote-code off by default; no content scanning

steps.title: Load safetensors only
body: Set --load-format safetensors; the default auto "will try to load the weights in the safetensors format and fall back to the pytorch bin format if safetensors format is not available".

steps.title: Keep remote code off
body: Never pass --trust-remote-code (default False), and remove it from copied examples such as the Kubernetes guide's deployment, so Python shipped in a model repository is not imported.

steps.title: Run a release with the remote-code fixes
body: Run v0.28.0 or later: model code bypassed trust_remote_code=False through auto_map (CVE-2026-22807, fixed 0.14.0), hardcoded trust_remote_code=True (CVE-2026-27893, 0.18.0) and LlavaOnevision2 (CVE-2026-90553, 0.28.0).

controls.note: Partial on this drawing's rule — the engine refuses unsafe formats only when configured to. --load-format safetensors and --trust-remote-code left off close the pickle and remote-code axes, but the default auto falls back to .bin (loaded with weights_only=True, whose restricted unpickler was bypassable before PyTorch 2.6 — PyTorch's CVE-2025-32434, carried as vLLM advisory GHSA-ggpf-24jw-3fcw), and the pt and npcache formats remain selectable. The off switch itself was bypassed three times in 2026, and the chat template shipped with the model runs on every request. Nothing inspects content: format and content scanning as a blocking gate on ingest is a model scanner in the promotion pipeline (external), with vLLM serving only the scanned, promoted path.

controls.mechanism: An AI gateway's weighted route or the serving platform's traffic split between vLLM instances or adapter names; vLLM serves one base model per process and has no split, gate or rollback. Evaluation: An evaluation or red-team harness run against the candidate on a staging `vllm serve` instance before promotion; vLLM ships no safety or adversarial evaluation

evidence.title: vLLM serve CLI — --served-model-name aliases, --enable-lora, --lora-modules, --max-loras
vLLM LoRA adapters — static --lora-modules, runtime loading behind VLLM_ALLOW_RUNTIME_LORA_UPDATING
vLLM — Using Nginx (the router in front of several vLLM containers)
vLLM documentation index (benchmarking measures throughput and latency; no model evaluation)

controls.note: External on this drawing's rule. What vLLM offers: one base model per `vllm serve` process under one or more --served-model-name aliases, and several named LoRA adapters beside it (--enable-lora --lora-modules name=path), so a candidate and the previous version can serve side by side as separate instances or adapter names. It has no promotion gate, weighting, canary or automatic rollback, and a new base version means a new instance. The split is the gateway's weighted route or the platform's traffic split; rollback is re-pointing the route at the instance still serving the previous promoted artifact. Runtime adapter swaps (VLLM_ALLOW_RUNTIME_LORA_UPDATING, load_inplace) bypass any gate and stay off. Evaluation: External: vLLM measures performance (`vllm bench`), not behaviour — nothing tests a model for backdoor triggers, leakage or adversarial influence, and any path or hub id passed to `vllm serve` is servable. Integration point: a staging instance started with the candidate's exact serving flags (load format, chat template, LoRA set, quantization) behind the OpenAI-compatible /v1 API that evaluation harnesses call; the approval record gates promotion in the pipeline, not in vLLM.

controls.mechanism: --api-key / VLLM_API_KEY (one or more static bearer keys, checked only under /v1, /v2, /inference and /cohere) and optional client-certificate TLS on the HTTP listener (--ssl-ca-certs with --ssl-cert-reqs 2); no per-tenant identity

steps.title: Require a key on the API prefixes
body: Set --api-key (or VLLM_API_KEY from a secret) to a key only the gateway holds; the flag accepts several keys and admits any one of them.

steps.title: Require the gateway's client certificate
body: Serve TLS with --ssl-keyfile and --ssl-certfile and require client certificates with --ssl-ca-certs <CA bundle> and --ssl-cert-reqs 2 (ssl.CERT_REQUIRED), so only workloads holding a certificate from that CA complete the handshake on the HTTP port.

steps.title: Run a release with the authentication fixes
body: Run v0.22.0 or later: CVE-2026-48746 let a crafted Host header skip the --api-key check on direct exposure, and CVE-2025-59425 (fixed 0.11.0) made the key comparison timing-dependent.

controls.note: Partial on this drawing's rule — a shared key is not per-tenant identity. The key authenticates a bearer, not a tenant: nothing maps a key to a caller for quota, cache scope or attribution, and routes outside the four prefixes (/invocations, /pooling, /classify, /score, /rerank, /tokenize and the operational routes) ignore it. Client-certificate TLS authenticates the calling workload on every route of the HTTP port, but any certificate the CA issued is admitted and vLLM authorises nothing per identity; the gRPC port (--grpc-port) has no authentication or encryption at all. Workload identity per calling tenant is the gateway's or service mesh's (external), with vLLM's key or client certificate authenticating the gateway.

controls.mechanism: Server-wide admission limits: --max-num-queued-reqs (in-flight cap, HTTP 503 beyond it; unbounded when unset), --max-num-seqs and --max-num-batched-tokens per iteration, --max-model-len, VLLM_MAX_N_SEQUENCES (n per request, default 16384) and the media size limits; --scheduling-policy priority; nothing per tenant

steps.title: Bound the queue
body: Set --max-num-queued-reqs so requests beyond the in-flight limit are rejected with HTTP 503 instead of joining an otherwise unbounded queue; size it about data_parallel_size × max_num_seqs plus the depth you accept.

steps.title: Cap per-request fan-out
body: Set VLLM_MAX_N_SEQUENCES to what the workload needs (the guide suggests 64 or 128 for public-facing deployments) instead of the 16384 default.

steps.title: Bound context and batch
body: Set --max-model-len, --max-num-seqs and --max-num-batched-tokens explicitly for the accelerators serving the model.

steps.title: Let the gateway order tenants
body: Start with --scheduling-policy priority, so requests are handled by the priority each carries (lower first) instead of first-come-first-served, and have the gateway set it per tenant.

controls.note: Partial on this drawing's rule — engine-level limits, not per tenant. vLLM has no caller identity to meter, so one tenant can fill the queue for all, and priority scheduling orders requests without capping anyone. The guide itself points rate limiting and request-body validation at the reverse proxy. Per-tenant quotas enforced at admission are the AI gateway's (external). The limits do not replace patching: dozens of 2025–26 advisories are requests that kill the engine or exhaust memory.

controls.mechanism: A guardrail service or AI gateway on both legs, optionally calling a guard model served by a second vLLM instance; vLLM returns raw completions and ships no classifier

evidence.title: vLLM security guide (no content-safety or guardrail setting)
vLLM serve CLI — --middleware (deployer-written ASGI middleware by import path)

controls.note: External on this drawing's rule (a guard model served beside the engine is external). vLLM has no harm-category, denied-topic or injection classifier on either leg; structured outputs constrain format, not content. --middleware loads deployer-written ASGI middleware into the API server — an in-process attach point, not a shipped guardrail. Integration point: the gateway calls the guard model and the generator in turn and blocks, substitutes or annotates on a fail, and the reverse proxy's endpoint allowlist keeps callers off vLLM's own routes, including /invocations, which reaches the same inference.

controls.mechanism: Platform process isolation between serving instances (separate OS users or containers per instance, the guide's advice), with hardware-enforced memory protection from the host; vLLM documents no hardware isolation of its own and batches every tenant of an instance together

evidence.title: vLLM security guide (process-level isolation only — separate OS users or containers, /proc hidepid)
GHSA-7m6h-x95x-82q5 / CVE-2026-73558 — cross-user data leak within one inference batch

controls.note: External: vLLM runs on whatever hardware it is scheduled onto and documents no confidential-computing, attestation or accelerator-partitioning mode. Within one instance, continuous batching puts every tenant's requests through the same forward pass on the same accelerators, and CVE-2026-73558 showed a kernel integer overflow copying one user's output into another's response in the same batch (fixed 0.27.0). The guide's isolation advice is process-level (separate OS users or containers, /proc hidepid=2), not hardware. Integration point: one `vllm serve` instance per sensitivity tier in its own process boundary, with the gateway routing each tenant only to its instance. Process isolation separates memory, not accelerator timing; dedicated GPU nodes or confidential GPU VMs for a tier are a separate deployment decision.

controls.mechanism: GitHub repository security advisories with CVEs and patched version ranges, a prenotification group for organisations that ship or run vLLM, releases about every two weeks, and GET /version plus the system_fingerprint for enumerating running versions

steps.title: Ingest the advisory feed
body: Feed the repository's security advisories (GHSA ids with CVEs and patched ranges for the pip package vllm) into the vulnerability management tool, and track the release notes.

steps.title: Apply for prenotification
body: If the organisation runs a substantial internal deployment or has an established security team, email the vulnerability management team to join the group notified privately before CRITICAL, HIGH or MODERATE fixes are released.

steps.title: Enumerate running versions
body: Collect GET /version from every instance (an unauthenticated utility endpoint) so each advisory maps to the instances it affects.

controls.note: Partial on this drawing's rule — the project publishes the stream; tracking and patching are the operator's. 83 repository advisories were published January 2025 – September 2026 (5 critical, 19 high), with patched version ranges; MODERATE and LOW fixes are developed as public pull requests before the advisory appears. The feed does not cover PyTorch, CUDA, transformers and the other dependencies in the wheel and the vllm/vllm-openai image (the Dockerfile itself had a dependency-confusion advisory, CVE-2026-54232). Continuous posture over which versions and flags serve where is external vulnerability management or CSPM scanning of the images and nodes.

controls.mechanism: The storage platform's access control and encryption on the weights; vLLM opens the path, --download-dir, Hub cache or object store it is given with whatever credentials its environment holds, and tensorizer can decrypt weights serialized with an encryption keyfile

evidence.title: vLLM serve CLI — --load-format, --download-dir, --hf-token
vLLM Tensorizer loading (S3/HTTP sources, tensor encryption)
vLLM security guide — Ray environment propagation (ray_non_carry_over_env_vars.json)

controls.note: External on this drawing's rule: vLLM holds no access policy over stored weights; the files are protected by the volume's permissions and the storage platform's IAM and encryption. Engine-side contributions: --load-format tensorizer loads tensors serialized with encryption when given the keyfile, and loads from S3 or HTTP endpoints. With RayExecutorV2 every driver environment variable, HF_TOKEN and cloud storage keys included, is copied to workers unless listed in $VLLM_CONFIG_ROOT/ray_non_carry_over_env_vars.json. Nothing re-verifies weights at load (see AML.M0014). Same rule as toolLmStudio (external: neither content-addressed nor digest-checked), not toolOllama's partial.

controls.mechanism: Safe defaults on the riskiest surfaces (VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE, VLLM_ALLOW_RUNTIME_LORA_UPDATING, --trust-remote-code, --grpc-port, profiler, --enable-tokenizer-info-endpoint and endpoint plugins all off) but unsafe defaults elsewhere (no --api-key, all-interface bind, shared prefix cache, unauthenticated /invocations and /scale_elastic_ep) and no flag that removes a route; per-request cache_salt, mixed into the hash of the first KV block so only requests with the same salt share cached prefixes, or --no-enable-prefix-caching

steps.title: Keep the runtime-update surfaces off
body: Never set VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 (it adds /collective_rpc, /sleep, /reset_prefix_cache and /server_info) and leave VLLM_ALLOW_RUNTIME_LORA_UPDATING unset so /v1/load_lora_adapter does not exist; serve adapters with --lora-modules at start.

steps.title: Close the optional listeners
body: Leave --grpc-port, --profiler-config and --enable-tokenizer-info-endpoint unset, and set VLLM_PLUGINS to the exact reviewed plugin names so no endpoint plugin can shadow a /v1 route.

steps.title: Tighten the unsafe defaults
body: Leave --allowed-origins at its default [] (cross-origin browser access off; it was ['*'] in earlier releases) or list exact origins, set --disable-fastapi-docs, --allowed-media-domains with VLLM_MEDIA_URL_ALLOW_REDIRECTS=0, and keep --allowed-local-media-path empty.

steps.title: Make the cache directory private
body: Point VLLM_CACHE_ROOT at a directory only the service account can write and never mount it from shared or untrusted storage, because compile and kernel caches load without integrity checks.

steps.title: Salt every request per tenant
body: Have the gateway set cache_salt on every request to a random per-tenant secret (the guide suggests 256 bits, e.g. 43 base64 characters), overwriting any value the caller sent; or start with --no-enable-prefix-caching where tenants must share no cache at all.

steps.title: Keep collision-resistant block hashes
body: Leave --prefix-caching-hash-algo at sha256 (or sha256_cbor) rather than the faster xxhash options.

steps.title: Do not accept caller media ids
body: Strip or regenerate the uuid field on multimodal content parts at the gateway, because two callers presenting the same uuid share one processor and encoder cache entry.

controls.note: Partial on this drawing's rule — the dangerous surfaces are opt-in, but several defaults are unsafe and vLLM has no switch to unpublish a route: /invocations (the same inference as /v1), /pooling, /classify, /score, /rerank, /tokenize and /scale_elastic_ep stay reachable without the key, so the guide's answer is a reverse proxy that allowlists endpoints (external). The vendor's sources disagree on /pause, /resume, /abort_requests, /update_weights and /init_weight_transfer_engine: the guide lists them as unauthenticated whenever the model supports generation, while the v0.30.0 router registers them only under VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE; treat them as reachable and block them at the proxy. Cache isolation is a salt the engine enforces but does not require ("cache_salt is opt-in and not passed by default"): it holds only while the gateway salts every request and callers cannot reach vLLM directly, a tenant that learns another's salt shares its cache, and it does not cover the multimodal caches keyed by caller-supplied uuid. The cache configuration is exported as vllm:cache_config_info on /metrics for drift review.

controls.mechanism: Platform network policy or firewalls around the serving plane; vLLM's integration points are its documented listeners — the API --host/--port (8000; all interfaces when --host is unset), --grpc-port, VLLM_HOST_IP, --kv-ip/--kv-port (default 127.0.0.1:14579), data_parallel_master_ip/port (127.0.0.1:29500), --data-parallel-address and --data-parallel-rpc-port, --master-addr for the mp backend, the Ray cluster, and torch.distributed's TCPStore on all interfaces

evidence.title: vLLM security guide — inter-node communication; firewall configuration guidance
vLLM parallelism and scaling — multi-node over Ray or mp; VLLM_HOST_IP warning
vLLM serve CLI — --host, --port, --data-parallel-address, --data-parallel-rpc-port

controls.note: External on this drawing's rule (the recorded deviation absorbs it into platform network policy). The guide: all inter-node communication is "insecure by default"; PyTorch Distributed has no authorisation, sends messages unencrypted and accepts connections from anywhere; and the multi-node page warns the exchanged format "can be exploited to execute arbitrary code" — the class behind CVE-2025-30165, CVE-2025-47277 and CVE-2025-32444. vLLM can pin which address a channel uses but authenticates none, and the TCPStore listens on every interface even on one host. Integration point: a dedicated serving-plane network or Kubernetes NetworkPolicy admitting only the gateway to the API port and only peer pods to the distributed ports, Ray client and dashboard ports never exposed, and an mTLS sidecar or IPsec where encryption in transit is required.

settings.name: --api-key
settings.where: vllm serve --api-key, or VLLM_API_KEY from the platform's secret store
settings.recommended: A key held only by the gateway in front, from a secret
settings.why: Callers that reach the port without the gateway are refused on /v1, /v2 and /inference; the CLI help warns /invocations and the other routes stay open, so the proxy allowlist still matters.

settings.name: --ssl-cert-reqs / --ssl-ca-certs
settings.where: vllm serve --ssl-keyfile --ssl-certfile --ssl-ca-certs <CA bundle> --ssl-cert-reqs 2
settings.recommended: 2 (required), with the CA that issues the gateway's certificate, where no service mesh provides mTLS
settings.why: Only workloads holding a certificate from that CA complete the handshake, which covers every route on the HTTP port, not just the key-checked prefixes.

settings.name: --host
settings.where: vllm serve --host
settings.recommended: The address only the reverse proxy reaches (127.0.0.1 beside it, or the pod address behind NetworkPolicy)
settings.why: The server's own routes, many unauthenticated, are reachable only through the proxy that allowlists endpoints.

settings.name: --allowed-origins
settings.where: vllm serve --allowed-origins
settings.recommended: [] — leave unset
settings.why: A web page in a user's browser cannot read responses from the API; copied examples that pass * reopen it.

settings.name: --disable-fastapi-docs
settings.where: vllm serve --disable-fastapi-docs
settings.default: False (OpenAPI schema, Swagger UI and ReDoc served)
settings.recommended: True
settings.why: The server stops publishing a map of every route, including the unauthenticated ones, to whoever reaches it.

settings.name: --grpc-port
settings.where: vllm serve --grpc-port (with VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1)
settings.recommended: Unset
settings.why: The security guide says the gRPC interface has no authentication or encryption and binds the same host as HTTP.

settings.name: VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE
settings.where: Server environment → VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE
settings.recommended: 0 — never set in production
settings.why: Dev mode adds /server_info, /collective_rpc, /sleep and /reset_prefix_cache, which the guide says should never be enabled in production.

settings.name: --enable-tokenizer-info-endpoint
settings.where: vllm serve --enable-tokenizer-info-endpoint
settings.recommended: False
settings.why: Keeps /tokenizer_info, which can expose chat templates and tokenizer configuration, unpublished.

settings.name: VLLM_PLUGINS
settings.where: Server environment → VLLM_PLUGINS (comma-separated plugin names)
settings.default: Unset (every installed general plugin loads; endpoint plugins load none)
settings.recommended: The exact reviewed plugin names; never lora_hf_hub_resolver
settings.why: An installed package cannot load code into the server or add a route by being on the image, and requests cannot pull adapters from the Hub.

settings.name: --trust-remote-code
settings.where: vllm serve --trust-remote-code / --no-trust-remote-code
settings.recommended: False — remove it from copied manifests
settings.why: Python shipped in a model repository is not imported into the server; the Kubernetes guide's example passes it, so check deployments.

settings.name: --load-format
settings.where: vllm serve --load-format
settings.recommended: safetensors
settings.why: The engine refuses pickle-based weight files instead of falling back to them when a repository ships no safetensors.

settings.name: --revision / --code-revision / --tokenizer-revision
settings.where: vllm serve --revision <commit> --code-revision <commit> --tokenizer-revision <commit>
settings.recommended: The reviewed commit sha for all three, on hub-sourced loads
settings.why: A push to the model repository's branch cannot change what the next restart loads, and the manifest records exactly which commit serves.

settings.name: --hf-token / HF_TOKEN
settings.where: vllm serve --hf-token, or HF_TOKEN from the platform's secret store
settings.default: Unset (or the token from hf auth login in ~/.cache/huggingface/token)
settings.recommended: A read-only, fine-grained token scoped to the approved repositories, from a secret
settings.why: A leaked server token can read only what the server may load, and cannot push to or read the organisation's other repositories.

settings.name: ray_non_carry_over_env_vars.json
settings.where: $VLLM_CONFIG_ROOT/ray_non_carry_over_env_vars.json (default ~/.config/vllm/)
settings.default: Absent (driver environment copied to Ray workers)
settings.recommended: Lists HF_TOKEN and every cloud storage key
settings.why: Tokens and storage credentials in the driver's environment are not copied to every Ray worker, where other processes could read them.

settings.name: VLLM_CACHE_ROOT
settings.where: Server environment → VLLM_CACHE_ROOT
settings.recommended: A directory only the service account can write, never on shared storage
settings.why: Compile and kernel caches load without integrity checks in formats that can execute code, so a writable cache is a code path into the server.

settings.name: VLLM_ALLOW_RUNTIME_LORA_UPDATING
settings.where: Server environment → VLLM_ALLOW_RUNTIME_LORA_UPDATING (with --enable-lora)
settings.recommended: Unset — serve adapters named at start with --lora-modules
settings.why: /v1/load_lora_adapter does not exist, so a caller cannot load weights from any path the server can read; the LoRA page says not to use it in production.

settings.name: --allowed-local-media-path
settings.where: vllm serve --allowed-local-media-path
settings.recommended: "" — leave empty
settings.why: API requests cannot read images or videos from the server's file system, which the flag's own help calls a security risk.

settings.name: --allowed-media-domains
settings.where: vllm serve --allowed-media-domains
settings.recommended: The domains the application's media come from
settings.why: A multimodal request cannot make the server fetch from internal addresses or arbitrary hosts.

settings.name: VLLM_MEDIA_URL_ALLOW_REDIRECTS
settings.where: Server environment → VLLM_MEDIA_URL_ALLOW_REDIRECTS
settings.why: An allowed domain cannot redirect the server's media fetch to a host outside the list.

settings.name: cache_salt
settings.where: Request body → cache_salt, set by the gateway on every request
settings.default: Not passed (prefix cache shared by every request)
settings.recommended: A random per-tenant secret of about 256 bits, overwriting any caller value
settings.why: Only requests with the same salt share cached prefixes, closing the timing channel that reveals another tenant's prompt; --no-enable-prefix-caching where tenants may share nothing.

settings.name: --prefix-caching-hash-algo
settings.where: vllm serve --prefix-caching-hash-algo
settings.recommended: sha256
settings.why: Keeps prefix-cache block hashes collision-resistant; the xxhash options trade that for speed.

settings.name: --max-num-queued-reqs
settings.where: vllm serve --max-num-queued-reqs
settings.recommended: Set — about data_parallel_size × max_num_seqs plus the queue depth you accept
settings.why: Requests beyond the limit get HTTP 503 instead of joining an unbounded queue; per-tenant quotas still belong to the gateway.

settings.name: VLLM_MAX_N_SEQUENCES
settings.where: Server environment → VLLM_MAX_N_SEQUENCES
settings.why: One request cannot ask for thousands of completions and stall the engine for everyone; the guide suggests 64 or 128 for public-facing deployments.

settings.name: --max-model-len
settings.where: vllm serve --max-model-len
settings.recommended: Set explicitly for the accelerators serving the model
settings.why: Bounds the context one request can occupy, so a caller cannot claim the model's full window on hardware sized for less.

settings.name: --enable-log-requests
settings.where: vllm serve --enable-log-requests, with VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=INFO
settings.recommended: True at INFO (request id, parameters, LoRA adapter; no prompt text)
settings.why: Each request leaves a log line the gateway's record can be joined to; DEBUG would add prompt text, so keep INFO.

settings.name: --enable-log-outputs
settings.where: vllm serve --enable-log-outputs (requires --enable-log-requests)
settings.recommended: False — capture completions at the gateway, with its redaction
settings.why: Output text would otherwise go to the process log unredacted; turn it on only where a log store is approved for completions, bounded with --max-log-len.

settings.name: --otlp-traces-endpoint
settings.where: vllm serve --otlp-traces-endpoint, with OTEL_SERVICE_NAME
settings.recommended: The organisation's OpenTelemetry collector
settings.why: Each request produces a span with ids, token counts and latencies, without prompt text, in the caller's trace.

settings.name: --enable-request-id-headers
settings.where: vllm serve --enable-request-id-headers
settings.recommended: True
settings.why: Responses carry X-Request-Id, so the gateway's record and the engine's log line can be matched in an investigation.

settings.name: --fingerprint-mode
settings.where: vllm serve --fingerprint-mode
settings.default: full (vllm-<version>, parallelism and a config hash)
settings.recommended: full
settings.why: Every response names the engine version and configuration, so inventory and vulnerability tracking know what each instance runs.

settings.name: VLLM_NO_USAGE_STATS / DO_NOT_TRACK
settings.where: Server environment → VLLM_NO_USAGE_STATS=1 or DO_NOT_TRACK=1, or ~/.config/vllm/do_not_track
settings.default: Usage statistics sent to the project
settings.recommended: VLLM_NO_USAGE_STATS=1
settings.why: Hardware, model architecture and configuration details of the serving estate stay inside the organisation.

settings.name: VLLM_HOST_IP
settings.where: Server environment → VLLM_HOST_IP on every node (with --kv-ip and the data-parallel addresses)
settings.recommended: An address on the isolated serving-plane network
settings.why: Inter-node traffic, which the guide says is insecure by default and can carry code execution, stays off networks other workloads share.

settings.name: Prenotification policy
settings.where: vllm-project security advisories feed into vulnerability management; prenotification requested from the vulnerability management team
settings.recommended: Feed ingested, and prenotification requested where the deployment qualifies
settings.why: Critical and high fixes reach the operator when the patch ships, and before it for prenotified organisations.

toolingAttribution: Authored in this repository. Facts are distilled from each vendor's own documentation, fetched and verified on the asOf date recorded per entry; nothing here is recalled from model memory. Verify against the vendor's current pages before enforcing.

settings.name: Assigned users
settings.where: IAM Identity Center › Applications › (the application your Cognito user pool federates to) › Assigned users
settings.recommended: Assigned to the groups that use the app, never to individual users
settings.why: Only assigned groups can sign in to the application at all, so access is a group decision and leavers lose it with their group.

settings.name: Resource binding
settings.where: Amazon Cognito › User pool › Resource servers; clients send resource= on the authorize request
settings.recommended: A resource server per published service, named by its canonical URI, and every user grant bound to it
settings.why: An access token names the one server it is for, so a token minted for another service is refused here. User grants only — client-credentials tokens cannot be bound.

settings.name: Machine-to-machine application (client credentials grant)
settings.where: Amazon Cognito › User pool › App clients; custom scopes on the resource server
settings.recommended: One app client per autonomous workload, custom scopes narrower than a delegated user's, client secret held in Secrets Manager and rotated
settings.why: A workload with no user behind it gets its own identity and a narrow grant, never a borrowed human session. Cognito authenticates these clients with a secret, not private_key_jwt.

settings.name: Access token expiration
settings.where: Amazon Cognito › User pool › App clients › (app client) › Token expiration; token revocation and refresh token rotation on
settings.default: One hour; token revocation on for new app clients
settings.recommended: 15 minutes, with token revocation and refresh token rotation on
settings.why: A revoked token stays valid wherever a JWT is verified locally, so a short lifetime is what makes revocation reach tokens already issued.

settings.name: authenticate-cognito action (OnUnauthenticatedRequest)
settings.where: Application Load Balancer › HTTPS listener › rule actions
settings.default: OnUnauthenticatedRequest = authenticate (once an authenticate action exists)
settings.recommended: authenticate-cognito on every rule, OnUnauthenticatedRequest = deny for the API paths
settings.why: The load balancer rejects every unauthenticated request before your code runs and hands the app the signed-in user's claims.

settings.name: customJWTAuthorizer (Inbound JWT authorization)
settings.where: AgentCore Runtime › (agent runtime) › Inbound Auth
settings.recommended: JWT from your Cognito user pool, allowedAudience set to this runtime's own resource and allowedClients to the clients admitted to it
settings.why: Each session runs as the user whose token opened it, and a token minted for any other audience is refused before the code runs.

settings.name: Resource-based policy on the agent runtime
settings.where: AgentCore Runtime › (agent runtime and its endpoint) › Resource-based policy
settings.default: No resource-based policy (any principal with InvokeAgentRuntime in the account)
settings.recommended: InvokeAgentRuntime allowed only for the ingress function's role, everything else denied
settings.why: A run starts only from the trigger that binds its authority — a queue message or schedule — and nobody can start the agent sideways with their own credentials.

settings.name: Resource-based policy (aws:SourceArn)
settings.where: Lambda › (workflow function alias) › Configuration › Permissions › Resource-based policy statements
settings.default: No statements (only identities in the account with lambda:InvokeFunction)
settings.recommended: One statement per trigger — the EventBridge rule or SQS mapping by its source ARN — and no others
settings.why: A workflow starts only from the trigger that binds its grant, so nobody starts a days-long run sideways on their own authority.

settings.name: Execution role and workload identity
settings.where: AgentCore Runtime › (agent runtime) › Permissions; AgentCore Identity › Agent identity directory
settings.default: Workload identity created automatically; execution role as you scope it
settings.recommended: One runtime per agent, its execution role granted only the gateway, memory and model actions it calls
settings.why: The agent authenticates with platform-issued, expiring credentials under its own identity — no key in its configuration to steal or share.

settings.name: Workload identity per agent
settings.where: AgentCore Identity › Agent identity directory (CreateWorkloadIdentity); one OAuth client per agent in your user pool
settings.default: None for agents hosted outside AgentCore Runtime
settings.recommended: One workload identity and client per agent — supervisor and each specialist — with tokens fetched at step time from the token vault
settings.why: Each agent in the graph is attributable and revocable on its own, and holds a short-lived token for its step rather than a credential for the process's life.

settings.name: Automatic rotation
settings.where: AWS Secrets Manager › (secret) › Rotation configuration
settings.recommended: On for every upstream credential the service holds, one secret per upstream, read only by that service's role
settings.why: A credential stolen from the service is scoped to one upstream and stops working at the next rotation.

settings.name: EKS Pod Identity association
settings.where: Amazon EKS › (cluster) › Access › Pod Identity associations (namespace and service account to IAM role)
settings.recommended: One association per workload, its role granted only the bucket prefixes and APIs that workload needs
settings.why: Each workload reads with its own short-lived credentials, so the serving tier can read weights and nothing else can.

settings.name: Execution role (RoleArn) per training job
settings.where: SageMaker AI › CreateTrainingJob RoleArn; IAM role per pipeline stage
settings.default: Whatever role the job is given
settings.recommended: A role per run, reading only the dataset version its approved spec names and writing only its own candidate prefix; no kms:Sign, no registry write
settings.why: The job that produced a candidate cannot also approve or sign it, which is the separation the promotion gate rests on.

settings.name: Sign (asymmetric SIGN_VERIFY KMS key)
settings.where: AWS KMS › asymmetric key with KeyUsage SIGN_VERIFY; key policy granting kms:Sign to the promotion role only
settings.recommended: Each promoted release's digest manifest signed at promotion, after the human approval, by an identity the training job never holds
settings.why: A signature proves the release passed the gate, and the serving tier verifies it with the public key alone.

settings.name: OAuth2 credential provider (client credentials grant)
settings.where: AgentCore Identity › Outbound Auth › one credential provider per peer platform, its secret in the token vault
settings.recommended: One provider per peer registration, our agent's own client and key at each peer, rotated by its owner
settings.why: Our agent presents a distinct, revocable identity to each peer, and the harness never sees the secret behind it.

settings.name: Deny bedrock:CallWithBearerToken
settings.where: AWS Organizations › Service control policies (or the IAM identities that call Bedrock)
settings.default: Amazon Bedrock API keys usable by any identity allowed to create them
settings.recommended: Denied organisation-wide, with bedrock-mantle:CallWithBearerToken
settings.why: Model calls need SigV4 credentials from a role; a Bedrock API key copied from a config file opens nothing.

settings.name: CUSTOM_JWT inbound authorizer
settings.where: AgentCore Gateway › (gateway) › Inbound Auth; SCP on bedrock-agentcore:GatewayAuthorizerType
settings.default: Chosen at creation; NONE is allowed
settings.recommended: CUSTOM_JWT with allowedAudience = this gateway, allowedClients = the agents and clients admitted to it, allowedScopes per tool; NONE denied by SCP
settings.why: The gateway verifies who is calling, for which user and for which audience, before any model or tool call goes through — and no gateway can be created open.

settings.name: OAuth (token exchange) — on-behalf-of
settings.where: AgentCore Identity › OAuth credential provider (TOKEN_EXCHANGE); AgentCore Gateway › target › Outbound Auth
settings.default: Chosen per target; token passthrough and no authorization are available
settings.recommended: Token exchange on every target that acts as the user; token passthrough not used
settings.why: The gateway swaps the user's token for one scoped to that tool, carrying user and agent both, so the inbound token is never forwarded or reused.

settings.name: Short-term memory (raw event) expiration (eventExpiryDuration)
settings.where: AgentCore Memory › (memory) › Short-term memory (raw event) expiration
settings.recommended: 30 days, events keyed by actorId and sessionId
settings.why: Conversation state ages out instead of accumulating client material, and each read is scoped to one user's session.

settings.name: Tenant-scoped data access
settings.where: Your service code — tenant taken from the validated token, applied to every query and every upstream call
settings.default: The protocol has no tenant; nothing is isolated
settings.recommended: Every handler resolves the tenant from the token and scopes reads and writes to it, with per-tenant credentials or row filters
settings.why: One tenant's call cannot read or change another's records, whatever the arguments say.

settings.name: Manual metadata filtering
settings.where: Bedrock Knowledge Bases › Retrieve / RetrieveAndGenerate › retrievalConfiguration filter, set by your tool code
settings.default: No filter (every chunk the knowledge base holds is retrievable)
settings.recommended: Every query filtered on the asking user's tenant and access-group metadata
settings.why: Retrieval returns only chunks tagged for the asking user, so the index cannot become a way round the source system's permissions.

settings.name: Contextual grounding check
settings.where: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails › (guardrail) › Contextual grounding check
settings.recommended: Grounding and relevance on for answers built from retrieval
settings.why: An answer that strays from — or was steered away from — its sources is flagged before the user acts on it.

settings.name: Sensitive information filters (Mask)
settings.where: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails › (guardrail) › Sensitive information filters, called with ApplyGuardrail before a turn or step result is stored
settings.recommended: Mask the PII types your firm handles before anything is written to memory or a journal
settings.why: Personal data a user pasted is not kept in the thread for every later turn — and every later reader — to see. It checks text only, not tool-call arguments.

settings.name: DurableConfig (RetentionPeriodInDays, KMSKeyArn)
settings.where: Lambda › (workflow function) › durable configuration, set at creation
settings.recommended: History retained 14 days, encrypted under your customer managed KMS key
settings.why: Checkpoints hold every step's payload; your key decides who can read the journal, and it does not outlive the debugging window.

settings.name: Bucket policy
settings.where: Amazon S3 › (dataset, candidate and model artifact buckets) › Permissions › Bucket policy; S3 Block Public Access on
settings.default: Access as the account's IAM policies allow
settings.recommended: Each bucket written by the one pipeline role that owns it and read only by the roles that need it, everything else denied
settings.why: Datasets and weights are written by one identity and read by the few that need them, so copying or replacing them takes a role nobody else holds.

settings.name: GuardDuty Malware Protection for S3
settings.where: Amazon GuardDuty › Malware Protection for S3 › protected bucket (the ingest prefix)
settings.recommended: On for every bucket where external artifacts land, with untagged or infected objects blocked from promotion
settings.why: A file carrying known malware is flagged before anything can promote or load it. Pickle and format inspection is a step you add in the same promotion pipeline.

settings.name: Verify the release digest at load
settings.where: Your loader — an init container that checks the artifact's SHA-256 checksum and Model Signing signature against the registry record before the server starts
settings.default: The server loads whatever files are at the path
settings.recommended: Load refused unless the digest matches the approved release and its signature verifies
settings.why: A file swapped in storage, digest and all, does not load, because the approved digest lives in the registry outside the bucket's write path.

settings.name: Taint accelerated nodes
settings.where: Amazon EKS › GPU node groups or Karpenter NodePools › taints, with tolerations only on that tier's serving pods
settings.default: Any pod can schedule on any node
settings.recommended: A tainted GPU node pool per sensitivity tier; no GPU sharing across tiers
settings.why: One tier's model and cache never share an accelerator or host with another tier's, so a process escape does not reach their memory.

settings.name: Detecting PII entities
settings.where: Amazon Comprehend PII detection, called from the curation processing job beside your quality and safety filters
settings.recommended: Every internal record scanned and redacted before it is written to a dataset version
settings.why: Restricted personal data is removed while it is still a deletion, not something the model has already memorised.

settings.name: Amazon SageMaker ML Lineage Tracking
settings.where: SageMaker AI › lineage entities for datasets, processing jobs, training jobs and model packages
settings.default: Created automatically for SageMaker jobs and pipelines; external sources as you record them
settings.recommended: Every dataset version, its sources and licences, and every run recorded as lineage, external sources included
settings.why: A poisoning or licence problem found later can be traced to the runs and releases it touched.

settings.name: ML storage volume and output encryption (KMS key)
settings.where: SageMaker AI › CreateTrainingJob ResourceConfig VolumeKmsKeyId and OutputDataConfig KmsKeyId; inter-container traffic encryption on
settings.recommended: Your customer managed key on every training volume, checkpoint and output, with inter-container traffic encryption for multi-node runs
settings.why: The checkpoints and candidates a run writes are readable only by principals your key policy names.

settings.name: Guardrails in policies — PromptAttack
settings.where: Policy in AgentCore › policy engine on the gateway › forbid (context.input) and suppressOutput (context.output) policies
settings.recommended: JAILBREAK and PROMPT_INJECTION checked on every request and on every tool and model response
settings.why: Injected instructions in the user's turn, a tool result or a fetched page are refused or withheld at the gateway before the model reads them.

settings.name: Guardrails in policies — ContentFilter and SensitiveInformation
settings.where: Policy in AgentCore › policy engine on the gateway › forbid on context.input and suppressOutput on context.output
settings.recommended: Harmful-content and sensitive-information checks on every request and response that crosses the gateway
settings.why: A completion, task payload or artifact that breaks content policy or carries personal data is refused or withheld at the crossing — the policy no provider applies for you.

settings.name: Policy engine enforcement mode
settings.where: AgentCore Gateway › policyEngineConfiguration.mode; bedrock-agentcore:UpdateGateway held by the platform team only
settings.recommended: ENFORCE, with Cedar policies per agent, tool and argument; new policies proved in LOG_ONLY first
settings.why: Every tool call is decided outside the loop on who is calling, which tool and with what — and whoever can flip the gateway to LOG_ONLY is a short list.

settings.name: Gateway rate limits
settings.where: AgentCore Gateway › Rate limits (dimension keys on JWT claims or IAM identity)
settings.recommended: Tokens per minute on inference targets and calls per minute on tools, per agent and per user
settings.why: A looping turn or a retrying client hits a ceiling at the gateway before it runs up cost or action volume. Rate limits fail open, so they are a brake, not a boundary.

settings.name: mcpToolSchema (static tool schema)
settings.where: AgentCore Gateway › MCP server target › CreateGatewayTarget / UpdateGatewayTarget
settings.default: DEFAULT listing mode (tools fetched from the server at create, update and SynchronizeGatewayTargets)
settings.recommended: Static mcpToolSchema from the reviewed release on every MCP server target
settings.why: The gateway serves the definitions you reviewed, not whatever the server now advertises, so a changed description changes nothing until a reviewed update.

settings.name: REQUEST interceptor
settings.where: AgentCore Gateway › Interceptors (a Lambda function); its execution role limited to that function
settings.recommended: tools/list and tools/call checked against the presenting token's scopes on every request
settings.why: A tool the caller's token does not cover is never listed to its model and cannot be called.

settings.name: Hash-pinned tool definitions at load
settings.where: Your service code — definitions loaded from the approved AWS Agent Registry record or release, checked against the recorded hash
settings.default: Definitions load from whatever is deployed
settings.recommended: Refuse to serve any definition whose hash differs from the one recorded at review
settings.why: An edit to a description that skipped review never reaches a caller's model. The registry checks schema only, so the consumer-side check is yours.

settings.name: Auto-approval
settings.where: AWS Agent Registry › (registry) › Record approval
settings.recommended: Off — a curator approves every MCP server, agent and skill record; only approved records become gateway targets
settings.why: The list of tools an agent may be given is a governed registry with an owner per record, not whatever someone wired in.

settings.name: AgentCardSignature verification and hash pin
settings.where: Your gateway interceptor — every peer card's JWS checked against the key pinned at admission, its hash against the approved registry record, on admission and each task
settings.recommended: Refuse any task to or from a peer whose card signature fails or whose card changed since its record was approved
settings.why: A tampered or silently changed card cannot redirect our tasks or widen a peer's skills; a change is a new approval, not a surprise.

settings.name: Peer platform assessment
settings.where: Your third-party risk process, before the agreement and the federation are signed off
settings.recommended: Assessed before federation and yearly — assertion handling, tenant isolation, card signing, audit export, task cancellation
settings.why: The questions A2A leaves to the implementation are answered in the contract before our users' identity travels there.

settings.name: Interrupts (human in the loop)
settings.where: Your agent code — Strands Agents BeforeToolCallEvent hook raising an interrupt on consequential tools
settings.recommended: Approval before every consequential write — in the thread when the user is present, from an operator queue when nobody is
settings.why: A person confirms each consequential action, with its arguments, before it happens — and never the requester approving their own remedy.

settings.name: Callback (wait for an external approval)
settings.where: Your workflow code — durable execution SDK callback on consequential steps; only the approval service may call SendDurableExecutionCallbackSuccess
settings.recommended: Consequential writes suspend on a callback that only the operator approval service can complete, with the action and its arguments in the payload
settings.why: The step resumes only on an approval for this exact action, possibly days later, and the agent cannot approve itself.

settings.name: --api-key (VLLM_API_KEY)
settings.where: vLLM server arguments on the serving pods; the key in Secrets Manager, presented by the gateway's API-key outbound auth
settings.default: No authentication; runtime LoRA updating off unless VLLM_ALLOW_RUNTIME_LORA_UPDATING is set
settings.recommended: Set, with VLLM_ALLOW_RUNTIME_LORA_UPDATING unset, --trust-remote-code off and --load-format safetensors
settings.why: Only the gateway can call the server, and no caller can load an adapter or remote code into it. The key covers /v1-style paths only, so the network policy still matters.

settings.name: cache_salt
settings.where: AgentCore Gateway REQUEST interceptor, setting the field on every inference request
settings.default: Prefix cache shared across every caller of the server
settings.recommended: A secret per-tenant salt on every request, overwriting any the caller sent
settings.why: One tenant cannot probe another's cached prompts through timing; the vLLM guide is clear it is mitigation, not an isolation boundary.

settings.name: Sanitise rendered model output
settings.where: Your front-end code
settings.recommended: Render as text or sanitised markdown; strip HTML, block external images, set a Content Security Policy
settings.why: A model-written image link or script cannot carry the conversation to an attacker the moment it renders.

settings.name: Network settings — Sandbox mode
settings.where: AgentCore Code Interpreter › custom code interpreter › Network settings
settings.default: The system code interpreter (aws.codeinterpreter.v1) uses the most restrictive settings; custom ones choose Sandbox, Public or VPC
settings.recommended: Sandbox
settings.why: Code the agent writes runs in an isolated session reaching only Amazon S3; where it must install packages, VPC mode in a subnet routed only to CodeArtifact is the alternative, never Public.

settings.name: weightedRoute (gateway rules)
settings.where: AgentCore Gateway › Rules › model routing on the inference target
settings.default: Requests route to the model they name
settings.recommended: A newly promoted model version takes a small weighted share, with the previous version kept as the fallback leg
settings.why: A new checkpoint serves a slice of traffic before it serves everyone, and rollback is a weight change rather than a re-download.

settings.name: Condition step (evaluation gate)
settings.where: SageMaker Pipelines › evaluation step, then a condition step in front of RegisterModel
settings.default: Registration does not depend on evaluation
settings.recommended: Capability, safety, backdoor and memorisation results must pass thresholds before the candidate is registered; benchmark data in a bucket the run's authors cannot write
settings.why: A candidate that fails evaluation never reaches the registry, so promotion is blocked rather than advised.

settings.name: Isolated sessions (dedicated microVM per session)
settings.where: AgentCore Runtime › microVM compute type; a new runtimeSessionId per rollout, maxLifetime set to the task's budget
settings.default: microVM per session; sessions end after 15 minutes idle or 8 hours
settings.recommended: microVM compute (not Instances), one fresh session per rollout, stopped when the episode ends
settings.why: Each rollout runs in its own microVM with isolated CPU, memory and filesystem, terminated and sanitised afterwards, so nothing it did persists or reaches another rollout.

settings.name: Repository policy (codeartifact:ReadFromRepository)
settings.where: AWS CodeArtifact › (repository) › Repository policy; rollout roles in IAM
settings.default: Access as the account's IAM policies allow
settings.recommended: Rollout and agent roles may read only; PublishPackageVersion held by build pipelines alone
settings.why: A rollout can install from the mirror but never write to it, so the package cache cannot become a message board between rollouts.

settings.name: Containment red team before each run
settings.where: Your run checklist — agents attacking the sandbox, host network and platform services, within the AWS penetration testing policy
settings.recommended: Required before any run that widens tools or egress; findings block the run until fixed
settings.why: Escape routes through platform services are found by the red team, not by the model being trained.

settings.name: A/B testing (target-based)
settings.where: AgentCore Gateway › A/B test scored by online evaluation; runtime endpoints pinned to versions
settings.default: The DEFAULT endpoint follows the latest runtime version
settings.recommended: Production endpoint pinned to a version; a new agent, prompt or model version takes a small traffic share after its batch evaluation passes
settings.why: A change that behaves badly reaches a few sessions and rolls back by repointing an endpoint, not by redeploying.

settings.name: Batch evaluation
settings.where: AgentCore Evaluations › batch evaluation job, run from your release pipeline
settings.recommended: A passing batch evaluation against a curated session set before any agent, prompt or model version is published to the alias the triggers invoke
settings.why: A change is scored on known scenarios before it runs unattended, which is the last point at which anyone is watching.

settings.name: Amazon Inspector Code Security
settings.where: Amazon Inspector › Code Security › scan configuration on your repositories
settings.recommended: On for every service repository, scanning source, dependencies and infrastructure as code on each change
settings.why: Handler code and its dependencies are tested and enumerated like any published application's, before and after release.

settings.name: Enhanced scanning
settings.where: Amazon ECR › Private registry › Scanning configuration (Amazon Inspector)
settings.recommended: Enhanced, continuous scanning on every repository the workload pulls from
settings.why: Every image actually deployed is matched against new CVEs as they are published, not only when it was pushed.

settings.name: Package origin controls
settings.where: AWS CodeArtifact › (repository) › (package) › Origin controls
settings.default: Set by how the first version arrives (internal packages get Upstream BLOCK)
settings.recommended: Keep the defaults; Upstream BLOCK on every internal package name, installs only through the repository with its external connection
settings.why: The agent's tools install from your repository, and a public package cannot shadow an internal one. Malware scanning of what is ingested is not a CodeArtifact feature — run it where packages are promoted.

settings.name: networkMode VPC
settings.where: AgentCore Runtime › (agent runtime) › Network configuration; SCP on bedrock-agentcore:subnets
settings.recommended: VPC, private subnets and security groups that reach only the services the workload needs, enforced for every runtime by the subnets condition key
settings.why: The harness and its tools leave only through your VPC's routes and firewall, never straight to the internet or sideways to another workload.

settings.name: VPC configuration (lambda:SubnetIds)
settings.where: Lambda › (function) › Configuration › VPC; SCP on lambda:VpcIds and lambda:SubnetIds
settings.default: Not attached to a VPC (public internet access)
settings.recommended: Private subnets routed through Network Firewall, enforced for agent functions by the condition keys
settings.why: The harness and its in-process tools leave only through your routes and firewall, never straight to the internet.

settings.name: Stateful domain list rule group (Allow)
settings.where: AWS Network Firewall › Firewall policy › Stateful rule groups; private subnet route tables to the firewall endpoint
settings.default: Direct outbound through a NAT gateway
settings.recommended: All outbound from agent subnets through Network Firewall, with an allowlist of the hosts the tools need
settings.why: The agent and its tools reach only the hosts you list; anything else is dropped and logged.

settings.name: Block private and metadata addresses on outbound fetches
settings.where: Your authorization service code — client metadata document fetches; its subnet egress through Network Firewall
settings.default: Fetches go wherever the client's URL resolves
settings.recommended: HTTPS only, resolved address checked against private, link-local and 169.254.169.254 ranges before connecting, IMDSv2 required
settings.why: A client that names an internal URL as its identifier cannot turn the authorization server into a proxy into your network.

settings.name: ClusterNetworkPolicy (admin network policy)
settings.where: Amazon EKS with the VPC CNI network policy agent › cluster-wide policy on the serving namespaces
settings.recommended: Deny by default; serving pods reached only by the gateway's VPC egress, inter-node ports open only between that model's own pods
settings.why: The serving plane's unauthenticated job and inter-node channels are reachable from nothing but themselves.

settings.name: EnableNetworkIsolation
settings.where: SageMaker AI › CreateTrainingJob (and CreateModel); VpcConfig with private subnets and an S3 gateway endpoint
settings.recommended: true
settings.why: The training container makes no outbound calls at all; SageMaker stages the corpus, base and candidate in and out for it.

settings.name: Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall
settings.where: Amazon Route 53 › Resolver › DNS Firewall rule groups associated with the sandbox VPC
settings.recommended: Allow list of the offline web, mirror and platform endpoints; every other name blocked
settings.why: DNS resolves only to the run's own list, which closes the tunnel-out-through-DNS path that a firewall on TCP alone leaves open.

settings.name: Interface VPC endpoints (AWS PrivateLink)
settings.where: Amazon VPC › Endpoints — bedrock-runtime, bedrock-agentcore and the stores the agent uses, each with an endpoint policy
settings.default: Calls leave over public AWS endpoints
settings.recommended: An interface endpoint per service, endpoint policy limited to your accounts
settings.why: Model, gateway and memory calls stay on the AWS network from your VPC, and the endpoint policy refuses use from outside your organisation.

settings.name: Rate-based rule statement
settings.where: AWS WAF web ACL on the load balancer, CloudFront distribution or AgentCore Gateway
settings.recommended: Per-client rate limit on every public endpoint
settings.why: A runaway client or scripted abuse is throttled at the edge, before it spends tokens or triggers actions.

settings.name: AgentCore Observability (CloudWatch Transaction Search)
settings.where: CloudWatch › Application Signals › Transaction search; agent code instrumented with OpenTelemetry (ADOT)
settings.default: Transaction Search off; agent code not instrumented
settings.recommended: On, tracing every agent turn, tool call and gateway hop, logs exported to your SIEM
settings.why: Each tool call, its arguments and its result are traceable per user and session when something goes wrong.

settings.name: Model invocation logging
settings.where: Amazon Bedrock › Settings › Model invocation logging (S3 or CloudWatch Logs)
settings.recommended: Enabled to an S3 bucket in the log archive account
settings.why: Every prompt and completion is kept off the agent's write path, so the record of what the model was told survives the session.

settings.name: CloudTrail data events
settings.where: AWS CloudTrail › organisation trail › Data events (AgentCore, Bedrock, SageMaker and S3 resource types)
settings.recommended: Logged for the resource types the workload uses, to the log archive account
settings.why: Who invoked which gateway, runtime, model or object is recorded by AWS, append-only and out of the workload's reach.

settings.name: RESPONSE interceptor
settings.where: AgentCore Gateway › Interceptors (a Lambda function writing to the log archive bucket)
settings.recommended: Every request and completion written with its tenant identity, sensitive fields masked, to an archive the serving tier cannot write
settings.why: The record of what was asked and answered comes from the crossing every caller shares, not from the callers' own logs.

settings.name: Model approval status
settings.where: Amazon SageMaker Model Registry › model package group › version › Update status
settings.default: Set at registration (PendingManualApproval, Approved or Rejected)
settings.recommended: Registered as PendingManualApproval; Approved only by a separate approver after evaluation, and the deployment records which version serves where
settings.why: The question "what is running, and who cleared it" has an answer in one place, and nothing unapproved reaches a server.

settings.name: Amazon SageMaker Model Cards
settings.where: SageMaker AI › Model Cards, attached to the model package in Model Registry
settings.recommended: A card for every registered version — intended use, training data, evaluation results — required before approval
settings.why: What the artifact is and what it was trained on travel with it to whoever deploys it.

settings.name: StopRuntimeSession
settings.where: AgentCore Runtime data plane API, called from your incident runbook
settings.default: Sessions run until they end or idle out
settings.recommended: The runbook's first step stops every live session of the agent
settings.why: Live conversations, and any streaming response mid-action, end at once without a deploy.

settings.name: StopDurableExecution
settings.where: Lambda API, called from your incident runbook for every running or suspended execution
settings.default: Executions run until they complete or time out (up to a year)
settings.recommended: The runbook's first step stops every execution of the workflow, suspended ones included
settings.why: A workflow halfway through a multi-day run — or parked waiting on a callback — moves to STOPPED and cannot be resumed.

settings.name: Deprecate (registry record)
settings.where: AWS Agent Registry › record › Deprecate; then the peer's Cognito app client and gateway target removed
settings.recommended: The peer cut-off runbook: deprecate its card's record, delete its app client, forbid its principal in the policy engine, cancel the tasks delegated to it
settings.why: A peer is cut off in one sequence at the registry, the token issuer and the gateway, without a deploy; deprecation is terminal.

settings.name: Revoke active sessions
settings.where: IAM › Roles › (the agent's execution role) › Revoke sessions
settings.default: Role sessions valid until they expire
settings.recommended: Part of the incident runbook, followed by a deny policy until the incident closes
settings.why: AWSRevokeOlderSessions denies every credential the agent already holds within about 30 seconds, without redeploying anything.
